docs.title: 4. Exact Source Evidence Remains Separate from Semantic Interpretation
docs.text:
Importing a rich format must preserve enough exact evidence to answer what external bytes or members were observed.

Conceptually:

exact external evidence
  -> parser/adapter
  -> canonical semantic knowledge
  -> derived interpretation

These classes are not interchangeable.

For example, a DOCX parser may understand paragraphs and tables while preserving unknown package parts. A PDF extractor may derive text regions while retaining exact PDF bytes. A CAD adapter may recognize ordinary entities while retaining unsupported proxy/custom data. A QGIS adapter may understand known project XML while preserving plugin-specific extension content.

Exact evidence supports:

  • reproducibility;
  • audit and provenance;
  • round-trip preservation;
  • conflict explanation;
  • adapter upgrades;
  • re-import with improved interpretation;
  • preservation of unsupported content.

Exact evidence does not automatically become canonical semantic meaning.

docs.title: 5. Compound Physical Membership
docs.text:
A logical artifact may own several physical members.

Conceptually:

Artifact A
  member M1 -> path/part/blob
  member M2 -> path/part/blob
  member M3 -> path/part/blob

Membership and ordering are semantic structure owned by the artifact revision, not implicit assumptions reconstructed from directory enumeration each time.

Examples:

ShapefileDataset
  roads.shp
  roads.shx
  roads.dbf
  roads.prj

OpenXmlPackage
  [Content_Types].xml
  word/document.xml
  word/styles.xml
  word/_rels/document.xml.rels
  ...

Scanning may initially discover independent paths. Classification/import may then group them into one logical artifact according to deterministic adapter rules.

One physical file must not be forced to equal one semantic project root object.

docs.title: 6. Logical Parts Inside Containers
docs.text:
Archive/database formats expose addressable logical parts that need not materialize as ordinary files.

Examples include:

XLSX package part
DOCX relationship part
GeoPackage layer/table
QGZ project member
embedded image/object

A logical part may have stable semantic identity and exact revision history even when its physical representation remains inside one container.

Consumers should navigate semantic objects and logical parts rather than requiring extraction to temporary files as the canonical access model.

Temporary extraction may be used internally by an adapter or validator, but it remains an implementation mechanism.

docs.title: 7. Opaque Preservation Is First-Class
docs.text:
Scriberig must not require complete understanding before safely editing a partially understood artifact.

A domain may classify content as:

understood canonical semantic structure
understood derived structure
projection-only representation state
opaque preserved canonical extension content
exact external evidence

Opaque preserved content is content that Scriberig cannot currently interpret semantically but must retain because dropping or rewriting it could damage the artifact or erase author/tool intent.

Examples may include:

  • unknown OOXML extension elements;
  • embedded/custom package parts;
  • application-specific CAD records;
  • QGIS plugin extension XML;
  • unsupported style/metadata records;
  • future-version fields unknown to the current adapter.

An unrelated semantic edit must preserve opaque content unless the requested operation explicitly replaces/removes the owning structure or the adapter can prove that preservation is impossible.

When preservation cannot be guaranteed, the projection/edit capability must degrade explicitly rather than silently losing content.

docs.title: 8. Round-Trip Fidelity Is a Capability, Not an Assumption
docs.text:
A format being parseable does not imply it is safely editable.

Projection/domain capability discovery must be able to distinguish states equivalent to:

InspectOnly
ReadOnlyDerived
LosslessEditable
LossAwareEditable
EditableWithOpaquePreservation
RestrictedExternalProviderEdit
Unsupported

Exact names belong in Level 2.

Capability is evaluated for the exact adapter/version, artifact, projection kind, resolved style, and preservation policy when those affect correctness.

For example:

  • a simple XLSX workbook may be editable while an unsupported macro/signature mode is not;
  • a DOCX may be semantically editable while exact page layout remains derived/read-only;
  • DXF may be editable while native DWG support depends on an optional provider;
  • a QGIS project may be editable while one referenced remote layer is read-only;
  • a lossy user projection remains governed by Level-1 024 loss-aware reconciliation rules.

docs.title: 9. Scalable Semantic Collections
docs.text:
Spreadsheets and geospatial datasets may contain millions of meaningful elements. The universal knowledge model must preserve semantic addressability without requiring every element to be eagerly expanded into heavyweight graph records.

Introduce a scalable collection concept or equivalent implementation strategy with these semantics:

semantic collection
  stable owner and collection identity
  exact snapshot/revision binding
  deterministic paging/range access
  stable member handles
  query/index support
  local semantic mutation
  exact changed-set reporting

Possible physical implementations may use:

  • sparse ranges;
  • persistent indexed tables;
  • database-backed rows;
  • columnar batches;
  • R-tree/spatial indexes;
  • compressed geometry stores;
  • adapter-owned immutable blocks.

Physical representation is an implementation detail as long as universal operations preserve snapshot exactness, stable semantic handles, history, provenance, and change semantics.

The system must avoid designs where importing five million GIS features requires putting five million objects into model context or rendering an enormous tree.

docs.title: 10. Progressive Disclosure for Large Artifacts
docs.text:
Large domains should expose coarse-to-fine navigation.

Examples:

Workbook
  -> worksheets
  -> used regions/tables
  -> bounded range
  -> cell

GeoDataset
  -> layers
  -> schema/extent/count
  -> spatial/query result page
  -> feature

Drawing
  -> layouts/layers/blocks
  -> bounded entity query
  -> drawing entity

The agent, TUI, web editor, CLI, and API all consume the same semantic handles and pagination/query semantics.

A huge collection must not become a huge static capability list or one giant serialized object.

docs.title: 11. Non-Text Projection Anchors
docs.text:
Text line/column is only one projection coordinate system.

Rich domains need typed projection anchors such as:

SpreadsheetAnchor
  sheet + row/column or range

DocumentLayoutAnchor
  page/region when layout exists

DrawingAnchor
  model/layout space + geometric bounds

MapAnchor
  CRS + geometry/bounding box + layer

PackagePartAnchor
  part identity + adapter-specific location

Projection anchors remain non-canonical bridges back to semantic identity.

Selections in a grid, canvas, map, page view, or drawing viewport should resolve to semantic entity/revision handles in the same way a source range resolves to a function or expression.

docs.title: 12. Spreadsheet Domain Family
docs.text:
Spreadsheets are a semantic domain family independent of XLSX as one external representation.

A general spreadsheet vocabulary may include:

Workbook
Worksheet
Row
Column
Cell
Range
Table
Formula
DefinedName
CellStyle
ValidationRule
Chart
ExternalLink

Important rules:

  1. cell/range identity must not be reduced to display text;
  2. formulas preserve authored expressions while parsed references may be canonical or derived according to the domain model;
  3. cached formula results are not automatically authoritative calculations;
  4. row/column insertion and movement use semantic operations that update dependent references according to domain rules;
  5. worksheet data uses scalable/sparse collection mechanics;
  6. formatting/style is separated from value/formula semantics where the format permits that distinction;
  7. XLSX is an adapter/projection/package implementation, not the spreadsheet schema itself.

docs.title: 13. Rich Document Domain Family
docs.text:
Markdown and Word-like documents should share semantic concepts where they genuinely overlap without forcing identical representation.

A common rich-document vocabulary may include:

Document
Section
Paragraph
Inline/Run
List
Table
TableRow
TableCell
Image
Link

Format-specific extensions may include:

WordStyle
Field
Bookmark
Footnote
Endnote
HeaderFooter
Comment
TrackedChange
ContentControl
DrawingObject

Pagination, exact line breaking, font substitution, and similar layout facts are normally derived projection knowledge unless a domain explicitly promotes them.

DOCX is a compound-package adapter over the rich-document domain and its format-specific extensions.

docs.title: 14. CAD Drawing Domain Family
docs.text:
CAD semantics should be modeled independently from any one interchange/storage format.

A useful common vocabulary may include:

Drawing
DrawingSpace
Layout
Viewport
Layer
BlockDefinition
BlockReference
Line
Polyline
Arc
Circle
Text
Dimension
Hatch
Style
ExternalReference

Domain-specific geometry and object types may extend this list.

DXF and DWG are separate adapters over the CAD domain.

External persistent identifiers such as native drawing handles are reconciliation/provenance evidence. They must not replace Scriberig EntityId.

Initial editable CAD capability should favor formats/adapters whose preservation and licensing constraints can be validated. Native/proprietary integrations may be optional provider boundaries rather than dependencies of the reusable semantic platform.

docs.title: 15. Geospatial Data and QGIS Are Distinct Domains
docs.text:
A QGIS project is not the same thing as the data layers it references.

The geospatial data domain may contain:

GeoDataset
GeoLayer
Feature
Geometry
Field
CoordinateReferenceSystem
SpatialIndex
RasterResource

The QGIS project domain may contain:

QgisProject
LayerGroup
LayerReference
RendererStyle
LabelingConfiguration
Join
Relation
Layout
MapItem
ProjectSetting

The domains connect through references such as:

QgisLayerReference --references--> GeoLayer

A GeoLayer may be backed by GeoPackage, Shapefile, GeoJSON, PostGIS, a remote service, raster data, CAD, or another provider.

The QGIS project owns composition/configuration; it does not absorb ownership of every referenced dataset.

docs.title: 16. Spatial Operations Extend Universal Query
docs.text:
Geospatial semantics require domain-specific queries such as:

features intersecting geometry/bbox
features within geometry
nearest features
features matching attribute predicate
layer extent
CRS transformation

These extend the universal query and operation model. They do not create an independent GIS persistence/query architecture.

Results remain snapshot-bound, paged, capability-scoped, and represented by stable semantic handles.

docs.title: 17. Cross-Domain Relations Are Normal
docs.text:
Rich project artifacts frequently reference each other.

Examples:

WordParagraph --references--> SpreadsheetRange
QgisLayerReference --references--> GeoLayer
CADExternalReference --references--> ExternalArtifact
SpreadsheetCell --references--> ProjectDecision
SessionBranch --touches--> GeoFeature
ReportTable --derived_from--> SpreadsheetRange

Cross-domain references use the universal graph and must not require copying another domain's canonical content.

Changes to one referenced object should invalidate/recompute only declared dependent derived knowledge and projections.

docs.title: 18. Semantic Operations Remain the Editing Primitive
docs.text:
Once a domain is understood, ordinary editing is performed through semantic operations.

Examples include:

spreadsheet.set_cell
spreadsheet.set_formula
spreadsheet.insert_rows
spreadsheet.rename_sheet

document.replace_paragraph
document.insert_table_row
document.accept_tracked_change

cad.move_entity
cad.change_layer
cad.insert_polyline
cad.update_text

geo.set_attribute
geo.replace_geometry
geo.insert_feature
geo.delete_feature

qgis.reorder_layer
qgis.change_renderer
qgis.update_layout_item

Every such operation produces candidate semantic state and flows through migration, validation, review/policy, promotion, and materialization.

A model must not normally edit XLSX ZIP members, DOCX XML, DWG bytes, SQLite tables, QGIS XML, or Shapefile sidecars directly when a semantic adapter exists.

docs.title: 19. Compound Materialization Is Atomic at the Artifact Boundary
docs.text:
Materialization may update one file, many coordinated files, or one container.

The system must provide artifact-level materialization semantics equivalent to:

candidate semantic state
  -> render all affected artifact members
  -> validate complete candidate artifact set
  -> stage outputs
  -> verify expected external baseline
  -> atomically replace/promote as far as platform permits
  -> record effect receipts and exact new synchronization baseline

For multi-file artifacts, a partial successful write must not be reported as a successful materialization.

Recovery must be explicit when the operating system cannot provide one primitive covering every member.

docs.title: 20. Validation Is Domain-Specific but Evidence-Bound
docs.text:
Validators may include:

  • package structural validation;
  • reopening the produced XLSX/DOCX with an independent parser;
  • formula/reference checks;
  • CAD parser/reopen checks;
  • geometry validity;
  • CRS/schema consistency;
  • QGIS project reference resolution;
  • GDAL/QGIS/native-provider diagnostics;
  • external application/provider validation where configured.

Validation evidence binds to the exact candidate artifact state it checked.

External tools may run in isolated candidate workspaces, but shell/process execution remains a runtime mechanism rather than the semantic editing API.

docs.title: 21. Product Surfaces and RPI TUI Boundary
docs.text:
The browser editor is expected to provide richer interactive projections such as:

  • spreadsheet grids;
  • rich-document editing;
  • CAD canvases;
  • map canvases;
  • layer/style inspectors.

The TUI should provide semantic navigation, bounded tabular/textual inspection, operation invocation, candidate review, history, diagnostics, and suitable previews.

The TUI is not required to recreate Excel, Word, AutoCAD, or QGIS as terminal widgets.

Under the active RPI adoption work:

  • upstream RPI/RPI-TUI owns commodity terminal controls/runtime/theme;
  • Scriberig owns semantic selections, domain projections, semantic operations, candidate review, and domain capability contracts;
  • TUI-specific presentation state must not become domain state.

CLI, web, TUI, agents, server, and third-party clients consume the same application/protocol semantics.

docs.title: 22. Licensing and Optional Native Providers
docs.text:
A semantic domain must not be coupled to one parser/library/provider whose license would unintentionally redefine the reusable platform's licensing boundary.

Where a format requires proprietary, copyleft-incompatible, native, or separately distributed technology, the architecture should support an optional adapter/provider boundary.

Provider identity, adapter version, fidelity, supported operations, and validation capabilities must be discoverable.

Absence of an optional provider degrades that format's capability explicitly; it does not make the semantic schema unavailable to other adapters.

docs.title: 23. Required Golden Workflows
docs.text: The implementation should eventually prove at least these product workflows through shared application semantics.

docs.title: 23.1 XLSX
docs.text:
open workbook
inspect sheets and used ranges
inspect formula/value
set one cell/formula semantically
review candidate
validate
promote
materialize XLSX
reopen and verify

docs.title: 23.2 DOCX
docs.text:
open document
navigate section/paragraph/table
replace paragraph or table cell semantically
preserve unrelated/opaque package content
review/validate/promote
materialize DOCX
reopen and verify

docs.title: 23.3 CAD
docs.text:
open drawing
navigate layer/block/entity
change one supported entity semantically
preserve unsupported records when required
review/validate/promote
materialize supported CAD representation

docs.title: 23.4 QGIS/geospatial
docs.text:
open QGIS project
resolve referenced editable layer
find feature by semantic/spatial/attribute query
change one attribute or geometry
review/validate/promote
materialize dataset
refresh project view without changing unrelated project configuration

docs.title: 24. Conformance Requirements
docs.text:
The completed architecture must prove all of the following:

  1. one logical artifact may have one, many, or container-internal physical members;
  2. exact source evidence remains inspectable independently of semantic interpretation;
  3. unknown preserved content survives unrelated edits when the adapter advertises preservation;
  4. format capability declares editability/fidelity instead of assuming parse implies write safety;
  5. large grids/layers can be queried and paged without eager full expansion;
  6. non-text selections resolve to semantic handles rather than becoming canonical coordinate identities;
  7. spreadsheet operations update semantic formulas/references according to domain rules;
  8. rich-document edits preserve format-specific structures not targeted by the operation;
  9. CAD external handles remain evidence, not Scriberig identity;
  10. QGIS project composition and geospatial datasets remain distinct but linked domains;
  11. spatial queries remain snapshot-bound and use the shared query model;
  12. compound materialization cannot silently leave a successful partial artifact;
  13. all edits flow through candidate/migration/validation/promotion;
  14. TUI/web/CLI/server/agents consume shared semantics;
  15. optional native/provider integrations do not become hidden mandatory dependencies of the universal platform.

docs.title: 25. Lower-Level Implementation
docs.text:
Concrete crate ownership, types, package selection, adapter libraries, task order, fixtures, protocol changes, browser components, TUI projections, and focused validation commands are defined in:

  • design/level-2/035. rich project artifacts office cad and geospatial implementation plan.md;
  • Level-3 tasks beginning with 154.

docs.title: Derived Knowledge Runtime and Cache Design
1. Purpose
docs.text:
This document translates design/level-1/008. derived knowledge caching and incrementality.md into a reusable Rust subsystem.

The subsystem owns the domain-independent mechanics required to:

  • describe derivations from exact immutable inputs;
  • build stable derivation keys;
  • record exact object and scope dependencies;
  • store and retrieve immutable derived results;
  • choose among multiple compatible results;
  • model freshness for external observations;
  • model retention without accidentally pinning canonical history;
  • find derived results affected by semantic changes;
  • explain reuse and recomputation decisions;
  • expose derived-state events separately from canonical snapshot events;
  • let domain adapters register meaningful derivations without implementing private cache systems.

This design does not make derived state canonical. Cache population, eviction, index rebuilds, and preferred-result changes must not advance canonical snapshots.

Concrete SQL schemas, distributed cache protocols, model-provider integrations, compiler integrations, HTTP payloads, UI components, and domain-specific derivation algorithms are outside this design.

docs.title: 2. Architectural Position
docs.text:
The universal graph design already defines a generic derived artifact and explicitly does not implement a cache. This design continues from that boundary.

The dependency direction is conceptually:

shared core identities/provenance
          |
          v
universal graph derived-artifact model
          |
          v
scriberig-derive
          |
          +----> domain adapters register derivations
          +----> app/runtime consume derivation services
          +----> protocol adapters translate derivation events

The repository-wide workspace design currently uses the scriberig-* crate naming convention. Some earlier persistence designs use the provisional sr-* prefix.

Implementation must inspect the actual workspace and use its canonical naming convention. There must be exactly one derivation/cache crate. If the workspace has standardized on sr-*, create or extend sr-derive rather than creating a competing scriberig-derive crate.

For the remainder of this design, scriberig-derive means that one canonical derivation crate.

The derivation crate may depend on:

  • the shared core identity/provenance crate;
  • the universal graph crate;
  • narrowly required storage abstractions if they already exist as backend-independent traits.

It must not depend on:

  • an agent runtime;
  • a model provider;
  • a concrete SQLite driver;
  • HTTP or WebSocket frameworks;
  • CLI, TUI, or web UI crates;
  • Markdown-, Rust-, PDF-, or session-specific code.

docs.title: 3. Files Prescribed by This Design
docs.text:
Create one reusable derivation crate if it does not already exist.

Target layout:

crates/scriberig-derive/
├── Cargo.toml
├── src/
│   ├── lib.rs
│   ├── profile.rs
│   ├── key.rs
│   ├── dependency.rs
│   ├── result.rs
│   ├── repository.rs
│   ├── selection.rs
│   ├── freshness.rs
│   ├── retention.rs
│   ├── invalidation.rs
│   ├── explain.rs
│   ├── event.rs
│   └── registry.rs
└── tests/
    └── derived_knowledge.rs

If equivalent modules already exist in the canonical workspace, extend them rather than creating parallel implementations.

Update the root workspace manifest only as required to register the one derivation crate.

Do not create domain adapter files, server endpoints, agent tools, or UI files as part of this design.

docs.title: 4. Reuse Existing Universal Types
docs.text:
Do not redefine concepts already owned by lower layers.

Reuse existing equivalents of:

EntityId
RevisionId
SnapshotId
StyleId or exact style revision reference when present
EntityRevisionRef
Provenance
DerivedArtifact

If DerivedArtifact has not yet been implemented in the universal graph crate, that is a prerequisite. The derivation crate must not create a second incompatible graph artifact model merely to proceed.

The derivation layer adds cache/derivation semantics around those universal objects.

docs.title: 5. Derivation Profiles
docs.text:
profile.rs defines exact derivation semantics.

A derivation profile identifies what computation is being requested, independently of one invocation.

Examples include:

function-summary/v1
markdown-section-description/v2
rust-pretty-print-ir/v3
symbol-reference-index/v1
semantic-diff/v2
agent-context-fragment/v4

A profile must be versionable. Changing behavior that can change the meaning or output compatibility of a derivation must produce a distinct profile/version identity.

A profile may carry:

  • stable kind/name;
  • exact version or revision identity;
  • optional producer/implementation identity;
  • configuration identity when that configuration affects semantics;
  • scheduling hints such as eager or lazy preference.

Do not use a mutable string such as "current" as the exact cache identity.

Human-facing aliases may resolve to an exact profile, but exact reuse uses the resolved profile identity.

docs.title: 6. Derivation Keys
docs.text:
key.rs defines the lookup identity for a derivation request.

A DerivationKey must encode every input whose change can alter result meaning.

Conceptually:

DerivationKey {
    profile,
    direct_dependencies,
    scope_dependencies,
    configuration_dependencies,
    freshness_input_if_required,
}

The representation must be deterministic.

Two keys compare equal only when they describe the same compatible derivation request.

Do not key exact reuse only by EntityId.

Do not automatically include the global snapshot in every key. Include it only when the derivation genuinely depends on whole-scope state.

docs.title: 7. Dependency Model
docs.text:
dependency.rs defines domain-independent dependencies.

The dependency model must distinguish at least:

docs.title: 7.1 Exact revision dependencies
docs.text:
The result depends on one exact immutable entity revision.

Entity F @ Revision R7

docs.title: 7.2 Snapshot dependencies
docs.text:
The result depends on the complete canonical state represented by a snapshot or explicitly scoped snapshot.

Use this for genuinely global derivations or conservative early implementations.

docs.title: 7.3 Collection or scope dependencies
docs.text:
The result asserts completeness or absence over a collection/scope.

Examples:

all callers of F
all implementations of trait T
all paragraphs containing X
no diagnostics in module M

The dependency must change when membership relevant to the assertion can change, even if the positive result members do not.

docs.title: 7.4 Configuration dependencies
docs.text:
Examples include:

  • style revision;
  • compiler/toolchain configuration;
  • feature configuration;
  • schema version;
  • adapter version;
  • model/prompt policy identity.

Use exact identifiers or deterministic value identities. Do not hide semantically relevant configuration in process globals.

docs.title: 7.5 Derived-result dependencies
docs.text:
A derived result may depend on other immutable derived results.

This enables hierarchical reuse such as function summaries feeding module summaries.

Dependency types must remain extensible without hard-coding every domain.

docs.title: 8. Derived Result Record
docs.text:
result.rs defines runtime/cache metadata around the universal graph's derived artifact model.

A stored result must identify conceptually:

derivation key
immutable artifact/result reference
status
provenance
creation/observation metadata when relevant
freshness metadata when relevant
validation metadata when relevant

The result record does not make the artifact canonical.

A failure may also be represented as a result when caching the failure is useful and policy permits it.

Failure records must distinguish retryable/transient failures from failures that are deterministic for immutable inputs.

The result representation must permit multiple results for compatible subjects/profiles rather than one mutable cache row that is overwritten forever.

docs.title: 9. Repository Abstraction
docs.text:
repository.rs defines a backend-independent persistence/query contract for derived knowledge.

The contract must support at least:

put immutable derived result
lookup results by exact derivation key
lookup derived results related to an entity/revision
record dependency metadata
lookup reverse dependencies
remove disposable result metadata/artifacts
inspect result provenance

The repository abstraction must not expose SQL.

A backend may store canonical and derived data in the same physical database, but the API must preserve lifecycle separation.

This design does not require a durable backend implementation yet. The conformance tests may use a small in-memory implementation local to tests or an existing backend-neutral memory facility if one already exists.

A later persistence integration may map this contract onto the canonical database without changing derivation semantics.

docs.title: 10. Result Selection
docs.text:
selection.rs separates exact identity from convenience selection.

Exact lookup asks:

Do we have a result for this exact DerivationKey?

Selection may ask:

What is the preferred current summary for F@R7?
What is the newest fresh external observation for source X?
What is the cheapest compatible summary?
What is the latest successful validation for snapshot S?

Selection policy must not mutate historical results.

Preferred-result pointers or indexes are derived selection metadata. Changing them does not advance canonical snapshots.

Selection results should explain which candidate was chosen and why when requested by diagnostics/debugging tools.

docs.title: 11. Freshness
docs.text:
freshness.rs models derivations whose validity includes time-varying external state.

Local immutable revision derivations normally do not expire merely because time passed.

External observations may require:

  • source identity;
  • observation time;
  • optional source revision/validator;
  • freshness deadline or policy;
  • revalidation metadata;
  • retry-after or failure freshness rules.

Freshness is separate from immutable historical truth.

An observation can remain historically exact after it becomes too old to satisfy a request for current information.

The freshness model must permit source-specific policy without embedding web-specific concepts into the universal crate.

docs.title: 12. Retention
docs.text:
retention.rs defines the lifecycle strength of derived artifacts.

At minimum distinguish concepts equivalent to:

disposable cache
expensive reusable artifact
historical evidence
pinned derived artifact

Dependency references from disposable cache entries must not automatically act as strong roots that keep all historical canonical revisions alive forever.

Retention policy must be separate from validity.

A result can still be valid but eligible for eviction because it is cheap to recompute.

A result can be retained for audit/history even if it is no longer the preferred current result.

docs.title: 13. Reverse Dependencies and Invalidation
docs.text:
invalidation.rs defines how semantic changes identify affected derivations.

Given a set of changed exact revisions, structures, scopes, configuration revisions, or snapshots, the system must be able to find derivation records whose declared dependencies may no longer match.

Invalidation means:

this result must not satisfy a request whose required dependency state differs.

It does not necessarily mean immediate deletion or recomputation.

The result may remain stored as a correct historical artifact for its original inputs.

The API should support a conceptual outcome such as:

Unaffected -> reuse
Affected   -> miss for new state; recompute if/when policy requests

Do not invalidate semantic results because a file timestamp changed when reconciliation preserved the same semantic revisions.

docs.title: 14. Explainability
docs.text:
explain.rs defines structured diagnostic reasons for cache decisions.

The system should be able to represent explanations such as:

ReuseReason:
  exact derivation key matched

MissReason:
  no compatible result exists

RecomputeReason:
  dependency Type T changed R5 -> R6

FreshnessReason:
  external observation expired

SelectionReason:
  preferred profile resolved to profile P7

Use machine-readable reason codes plus human-readable context.

Do not reduce explanations to log strings only.

The same explanation objects may later be rendered by CLI, server, web, TUI, and agent surfaces.

docs.title: 15. Derived Events
docs.text:
event.rs defines domain-level events that higher runtime/protocol layers can translate.

At minimum support equivalents of:

DerivationStarted
DerivedResultAvailable
DerivationFailed
DerivedResultSelected
DerivedResultEvicted
DerivedResultInvalidatedForState
IndexUpdated

These events must be distinct from canonical events such as:

CanonicalSnapshotChanged

The derivation crate owns event semantics, not transport encoding.

Do not add HTTP/WebSocket types here.

docs.title: 16. Derivation Registry
docs.text:
registry.rs lets domain adapters declare derivations without each adapter inventing its own cache mechanics.

A registration should conceptually describe:

  • derivation profile/kind;
  • accepted input/scope kinds;
  • dependency discovery strategy;
  • eager versus lazy policy hint;
  • freshness behavior if any;
  • retention default;
  • producer/implementation version identity;
  • optional cost information.

The registry must not require an agent runtime.

A Markdown, Rust, PDF, session, or future domain adapter should be able to use the same contracts.

Execution of domain-specific derivation code may be synchronous or asynchronous in later designs. This Level 2 design defines registration and identity, not a mandatory task scheduler or async runtime.

docs.title: 17. Eager Versus Lazy Policy
docs.text:
Eager and lazy are scheduling policy, not validity semantics.

The same exact derivation key and result type must remain valid regardless of whether the result was precomputed or requested on demand.

The first implementation should support policy metadata sufficient to distinguish:

Lazy
Eager

without introducing a background scheduler unless another design already provides one.

The cache model must be useful in embedded/library-only applications that have no server and no agent runtime.

docs.title: 18. Concurrency
docs.text:
Concurrent requests for the same exact derivation key should not corrupt state or produce ambiguous identity.

The architecture permits more than one immutable result for nondeterministic derivations, but duplicate deterministic work should be avoidable by higher execution layers when practical.

The repository contract must remain correct if two workers finish compatible derivations concurrently.

Selection policy, not mutation of old results, decides which artifact is preferred.

Do not make process-local locks part of persistent semantic identity.

docs.title: 19. Domain Boundaries
docs.text:
The universal derivation crate must not hard-code derivation types such as:

RustTypeCheck
MarkdownSummary
PdfExtraction
SessionBranchSummary

Profiles and adapter registration carry domain meaning.

Domain adapters may use the universal engine for:

  • compiler/static analysis;
  • render intermediates;
  • descriptions/summaries;
  • extracted document structure;
  • semantic diffs;
  • agent context fragments;
  • validation results;
  • search/index materialization.

The universal crate provides mechanics, identity, dependency, lifecycle, and observability.

docs.title: 20. Canonical Promotion Is Outside Cache Mutation
docs.text:
The derivation subsystem may expose enough provenance to support promotion, but it must not silently promote derived results.

Promotion is a canonical migration handled by the normal change system.

Conceptually:

DerivedResult D
    |
    | explicit acceptance
    v
canonical entity/revision
    |
    v
new canonical snapshot

The derivation repository remains unchanged in authority even if the promoted canonical object points back to D for provenance.

docs.title: 21. Persistence Shape
docs.text:
A durable backend should be able to represent the derivation layer conceptually as four independent concerns:

immutable derived results
exact derivation-key -> result lookup
result -> dependency metadata
reverse dependency -> affected result lookup

Additional mutable derived metadata may include:

preferred-result selection
retention/pinning state
freshness/revalidation state

These structures are outside canonical snapshot identity.

The physical backend may use tables, key/value namespaces, indexes, or another representation. It must preserve the same logical contracts.

Do not require one database transaction to advance a canonical snapshot merely because a derived result was inserted.

docs.title: 22. Public API Shape
docs.text:
Exact names may evolve, but the crate should expose concepts equivalent to:

DerivationProfile
DerivationKey
Dependency
DependencySet
DerivedResultRecord
DerivedRepository
SelectionPolicy
FreshnessPolicy
RetentionPolicy
InvalidationSet
ReuseExplanation
DerivationEvent
DerivationRegistry

Prefer small explicit types over large maps of untyped strings.

Public APIs should make exact identity and lifecycle distinctions obvious.

docs.title: 23. Conformance Tests
docs.text:
tests/derived_knowledge.rs must cover at least these scenarios:

  1. identical exact inputs and profile produce equal derivation keys;
  2. changing one exact revision changes the derivation key;
  3. changing unrelated global state does not change a local derivation key;
  4. a global/snapshot derivation changes key when its snapshot changes;
  5. a completeness query can depend on scope independently of positive result members;
  6. multiple immutable results can coexist for nondeterministic derivations;
  7. preferred-result selection can change without a canonical snapshot operation;
  8. an external observation can be historically retained but no longer satisfy freshness policy;
  9. reverse dependency lookup identifies an affected result;
  10. an unaffected result remains reusable after an unrelated semantic change;
  11. formatting/style dependency invalidates rendering without invalidating semantic summary dependency;
  12. disposable cache dependencies do not imply strong canonical retention;
  13. derived failure policy distinguishes deterministic failure from retryable transient failure;
  14. derived events are distinct from canonical snapshot events;
  15. a domain-like test registration can declare a custom derivation without adding a production enum variant.

Tests should use test schemas/profile names only. Do not introduce production domain vocabulary.

docs.title: 24. Documentation Requirements
docs.text:
Public module documentation must explain:

  • canonical versus derived lifecycle;
  • exact revision-based reuse;
  • why global snapshots are not the default local cache key;
  • scope/absence dependencies;
  • freshness versus historical immutability;
  • retention versus validity;
  • selection versus identity;
  • why cache operations do not advance canonical snapshots.

The crate-level documentation should state clearly that the derivation subsystem is useful without agents, servers, or a UI.

docs.title: 25. Completion Criteria
docs.text:
Implementation status: complete. The canonical implementation is scriberig-derive; its repository, selection, freshness, retention, invalidation, explanation, event, and registration modules are covered by unit and conformance tests. Application-level authorization wraps this backend-neutral contract without adding product dependencies to the crate.

This Level 2 design is implemented when:

  • [x] one canonical derivation/cache crate exists and is registered in the workspace;
  • [x] derivation profiles and deterministic keys are represented explicitly;
  • [x] exact, scope, snapshot, configuration, and derived-result dependencies are supported;
  • [x] derived result records retain provenance and immutable identity;
  • [x] a backend-independent derived repository contract exists;
  • [x] multiple compatible results can coexist;
  • [x] selection policy is separate from exact identity;
  • [x] freshness is explicit for external observations;
  • [x] retention is independent of validity;
  • [x] reverse-dependency invalidation works without deleting historical artifacts;
  • [x] reuse/miss/recompute decisions can be explained structurally;
  • [x] derived events are separate from canonical snapshot events;
  • [x] domain derivations can be registered without hard-coded domain variants;
  • [x] conformance tests demonstrate local reuse plus global certainty;
  • [x] no agent runtime, concrete database driver, HTTP server, CLI, TUI, or UI dependency was introduced.

docs.title: 26. Level 3 Work Decomposition
docs.text:
Create focused implementation instructions in this order:

  1. scaffold the canonical derivation crate and implement profiles, dependency types, and deterministic derivation keys;
  2. implement immutable result records and the backend-independent derived repository contract;
  3. implement result selection, freshness, failure, and retention policy types;
  4. implement reverse-dependency invalidation and structured reuse/recompute explanations;
  5. implement derivation events and the domain registration contract;
  6. add the conformance test suite, crate documentation, and workspace validation.

Each implementation task must inspect the actual workspace first and extend canonical crates rather than duplicating a provisional sr-* versus scriberig-* naming variant.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document specifies the lower-level decisions required by the Level 1 persistence model for deterministic revision identity.

The Level 1 requirement is that a revision identifier never silently refer to different canonical content. This design chooses one concrete initial mechanism.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Revision identity is content-addressed.

The initial implementation uses:

  • BLAKE3 as the digest algorithm;
  • a versioned deterministic binary canonical encoding;
  • explicit object type and encoding version in the encoded value.

The exact Rust serialization library used internally may change, but the canonical byte format must be owned by Scriberig and tested independently of ordinary Rust serialization behavior.

docs.title: Canonical revision envelope
docs.text:
Every stored canonical revision is encoded conceptually as:

RevisionEnvelope
├── encoding_version
├── object_type
└── canonical_payload

RevisionId is computed from the complete canonical envelope bytes.

Two logically identical canonical revisions encoded under the same encoding version must produce identical bytes and therefore identical RevisionId values.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Map/object fields must have deterministic ordering.
  • Ordered semantic collections preserve order.
  • Unordered semantic collections must be canonicalized before encoding.
  • Incidental Rust memory layout must never affect bytes.
  • Timestamps, insertion order, database row IDs, cache metadata, and backend-specific information must not appear in canonical revision bytes unless a domain explicitly declares them canonical.
  • Parent location and reverse-index information must not be inserted merely for navigation convenience.
  • Unknown encoding versions must fail explicitly rather than being interpreted as the newest version.

docs.title: Identity types
docs.text:
RevisionId should be represented internally as the BLAKE3 digest bytes plus type safety provided by sr-core.

External textual formatting should be deterministic and round-trippable. The human representation may use a prefix such as rev: plus a stable textual digest encoding.

The exact display format is not part of semantic identity.

docs.title: Encoding evolution
docs.text:
A newer physical encoding must use a new EncodingVersion.

Storage migration and semantic migration must remain separate concepts.

If the system rewrites an old revision into a newer physical representation without semantic change, the storage migration layer must preserve the ability to understand that the semantic state is equivalent even if the physical revision representation receives a different content identity under the new encoding.

The first implementation does not need automatic cross-version deduplication, but it must not pretend that an encoding rewrite is a user semantic edit.

docs.title: Files prescribed by this design
docs.text:
Within sr-core:

crates/sr-core/src/
├── lib.rs
├── ids.rs
└── encoding.rs

Within sr-store:

crates/sr-store/src/
├── lib.rs
└── revision.rs

Tests must cover stable canonical byte output and stable IDs for fixed fixtures.

docs.title: Required tests
docs.text:
• Same value encoded twice gives byte-for-byte identical output.
  • Same value encoded through independently constructed Rust values gives the same ID.
  • Changing a canonical scalar changes the ID.
  • Changing ordered collection order changes the ID.
  • Reordering an unordered canonical collection does not change the ID after canonicalization.
  • Changing ObjectType changes the ID even if payload bytes are otherwise equal.
  • Changing EncodingVersion changes the encoded envelope.
  • Display/parse round-trip for RevisionId succeeds.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: This design does not define domain schemas or decide which domain fields are canonical. Domain adapters make that decision before handing a canonical revision value to the store.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This document specifies how the Level 1 snapshot model is represented without tying semantic containment to storage identity.

docs.title: Snapshot model
docs.text:
A snapshot is an immutable mapping:

EntityId -> RevisionId

The mapping is independent from domain containment.

Changing a paragraph revision must not automatically change the revision of its containing section unless the section's own canonical structure changed.

docs.title: Persistent snapshot map
docs.text:
The initial implementation must use a persistent structurally shared map abstraction.

The logical API must support:

lookup(snapshot, entity)
apply_changes(base_snapshot, changes) -> new_snapshot
iterate(snapshot)
diff(snapshot_a, snapshot_b)

A new snapshot may share all unchanged internal map nodes with its base snapshot.

The public API must not expose the concrete persistent-map implementation.

The first implementation may use a simple copy-on-write persistent tree suitable for correctness before later optimizing to a HAMT, radix trie, Merkle B-tree, or another structure.

The design requirement is behavioral:

  • creating a snapshot from a small change must not require copying every entity mapping;
  • snapshot identity must be deterministic for exact map content;
  • equal complete maps must converge to the same snapshot identity when encoded under the same format version.

docs.title: Snapshot changes
docs.text:
A snapshot builder accepts changes such as:

Set(EntityId, RevisionId)
Remove(EntityId)

The builder is not itself a semantic migration system. It only creates the resulting exact mapping.

Higher layers explain why those changes happened.

docs.title: Named roots
docs.text:
Named roots provide mutable names for immutable snapshots.

Examples:

main
workspace/123
session/current

The storage API must support:

read_root(name) -> SnapshotId?
compare_and_set_root(name, expected, new) -> result

Promotion must be atomic.

A compare-and-set failure means another writer advanced the root; it must never silently overwrite the newer value.

docs.title: Persistent semantic collections
docs.text:
Entity revisions may contain canonical ordered collections such as section children or function parameters.

Large collections should not require copying every element when one item is inserted, removed, or moved.

The storage-facing collection representation should therefore support structural sharing.

The first implementation may use a simple immutable chunked sequence. It must hide the physical representation behind a collection API so a later implementation can replace it.

Child revisions do not include their index merely because they appear in an ordered collection.

docs.title: Files prescribed by this design
docs.text:
Within sr-store:

crates/sr-store/src/
├── snapshot.rs
├── roots.rs
└── collection.rs

Within sr-store-memory:

crates/sr-store-memory/src/
├── lib.rs
├── snapshot.rs
└── roots.rs

The SQLite backend will implement the same behavior in its own backend modules.

docs.title: Required tests
docs.text:
• Build S2 from S1 with one changed entity and confirm all other mappings resolve identically.
  • Reconstruct the same complete mapping through a different update order and confirm identical SnapshotId.
  • Remove an entity and confirm the prior snapshot still resolves it.
  • Branch two snapshots from one base without altering the base.
  • Compare-and-set root succeeds with the expected value.
  • Compare-and-set root fails when the expected value is stale.
  • Reordering a semantic collection changes the container revision while leaving child revision IDs unchanged.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: This design does not define merge semantics, migration provenance, or domain-specific collection meaning.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the first durable backend implementation for the persistence model.

The Level 1 design allows any backend that preserves the required semantics. This Level 2 design selects SQLite for the first durable implementation because it provides an embedded transactional store while keeping the public storage API backend-independent.

docs.title: Backend boundary
docs.text:
sr-store-sqlite implements sr-store traits. No higher crate should issue SQL against its internal tables.

SQLite-specific schema and migration code stays inside this crate.

docs.title: Required persisted categories
docs.text:
The backend must persist enough information to reconstruct:

  • immutable revision records;
  • persistent snapshot-map nodes;
  • snapshot roots;
  • named roots;
  • storage format/schema version;
  • required backend indexes;
  • integrity/recovery metadata.

Derived caches may later use the same database, but they must remain distinguishable and removable.

docs.title: Transaction model
docs.text:
Canonical promotion is atomic.

A write flow is conceptually:

begin transaction
  insert missing immutable revisions
  insert missing persistent map/collection nodes
  insert new snapshot record
  update required indexes
  compare expected named root
  move named root to new snapshot
commit

If the expected root is stale, the transaction must fail without promoting the root.

Already-created immutable content may be safely reused if a retry later produces the same content.

docs.title: Crash safety
docs.text:
After process or machine interruption, one of two states is visible:

  • the previous committed root;
  • the complete newly committed root.

A partially published canonical snapshot is never visible.

Unreachable immutable records left by aborted or interrupted preparation are acceptable and can be reclaimed later.

docs.title: SQLite schema evolution
docs.text:
The backend owns a storage schema version separate from semantic schema versions and canonical encoding versions.

Backend schema upgrades must be transactional where SQLite permits it and must not invent semantic migrations.

An upgrade that reorganizes tables or indexes but preserves semantic state is a storage migration only.

docs.title: Connection behavior
docs.text:
The first implementation may use a single writer model. Reads may use additional connections if the chosen SQLite wrapper supports safe concurrency.

The public storage API must not promise SQLite-specific locking behavior.

Use explicit transactions for root promotion and integrity-sensitive multi-step writes.

docs.title: Files prescribed by this design
docs.text:
crates/sr-store-sqlite/src/
├── lib.rs
├── connection.rs
├── schema.rs
├── revision.rs
├── snapshot.rs
├── roots.rs
└── recovery.rs

Schema SQL may be embedded in Rust or stored under a crate-local migrations directory. If migration files are used, create:

crates/sr-store-sqlite/migrations/

with monotonically ordered migration files.

docs.title: Required tests
docs.text:
• Open a fresh database and initialize schema.
  • Reopen it and read previously stored revisions and roots.
  • Inserting the same revision twice does not create divergent logical copies.
  • Failed compare-and-set root does not publish the attempted snapshot as the named root.
  • Transaction rollback preserves the previous root.
  • Reopening after a committed write returns the new root.
  • Simulated failure before root promotion leaves the previous root visible.
  • Backend schema version is detectable and unsupported newer versions fail explicitly.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: This design does not implement semantic merging, projection reconciliation, or distributed multi-writer consensus.

docs.title: Indexes, Reachability, Garbage Collection, and Integrity
Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the lower-level maintenance model required by the Level 1 persistence design.

Canonical data must remain authoritative. Indexes and caches accelerate access but must be rebuildable. Immutable history requires explicit reachability and integrity rules.

docs.title: Derived indexes
docs.text:
The initial persistence layer should support backend-maintained indexes for operations that are expensive to derive repeatedly.

At minimum, design for indexes such as:

RevisionId -> stored revision location
SnapshotId -> snapshot map root
RootName -> SnapshotId
RevisionId -> references to other stored immutable nodes, when needed for traversal

Graph/domain indexes such as reverse semantic relations, symbol references, full-text search, or projection paths belong to higher layers unless a backend-neutral storage primitive is required.

Every derived index must have a rebuild path from authoritative data.

docs.title: Reachability
docs.text:
Reachability starts from protected roots.

The storage API must support enumerating or supplying protected snapshot roots and traversing all canonical immutable storage required to read them completely.

A protected snapshot must retain:

  • its snapshot-map structure;
  • every referenced canonical revision;
  • every persistent canonical collection node needed by those revisions;
  • required ancestry/history objects when retention policy marks them protected.

Derived caches do not automatically gain canonical retention merely because they reference a protected object.

docs.title: Garbage collection phases
docs.text:
The initial GC design should use a conservative mark-and-sweep model:

1. capture protected roots
2. mark reachable canonical storage
3. optionally mark policy-retained historical objects
4. identify unreachable candidates
5. sweep candidates in a transactionally safe way

The first implementation should support dry-run reporting before destructive sweep.

GC must never run against a moving root set without either a stable captured view or backend coordination that guarantees safety.

docs.title: Integrity verification
docs.text:
Integrity checking should be callable independently of the agent runtime and UI.

Checks include:

  • recompute revision identity from stored canonical bytes;
  • verify all referenced persistent nodes exist;
  • verify snapshot-map root integrity;
  • verify named roots resolve to valid snapshots;
  • verify protected snapshots are completely readable;
  • verify collection structure invariants;
  • verify backend index entries reference existing authoritative records;
  • report orphan/unreachable immutable records separately from corruption.

An unreachable object is not automatically corrupt.

docs.title: Repair policy
docs.text:
Canonical content must not be silently rewritten by an integrity checker.

Safe automatic repairs may include rebuilding derived indexes.

Missing or mismatched canonical content must be reported as corruption and require explicit recovery policy.

docs.title: Files prescribed by this design
docs.text:
Within sr-store:

crates/sr-store/src/
├── reachability.rs
└── integrity.rs

Within sr-store-sqlite:

crates/sr-store-sqlite/src/
├── indexes.rs
├── reachability.rs
├── gc.rs
└── integrity.rs

The memory backend should implement enough reachability and integrity behavior to participate in shared conformance tests.

docs.title: Required tests
docs.text:
• Rebuild a deleted derived index from authoritative data.
  • Mark all records reachable from one protected snapshot.
  • Confirm an abandoned branch is collectible only when no protected root reaches it.
  • Dry-run GC reports candidates without deleting them.
  • Sweep never deletes records required by a protected snapshot.
  • Corrupt canonical revision bytes are detected by identity verification.
  • Missing persistent snapshot-map node is reported as corruption.
  • Unreachable but valid immutable content is reported as unreachable, not corrupt.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: The first implementation does not need online incremental GC, compaction across distributed stores, or sophisticated retention-policy configuration.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The Level 1 persistence model requires the store to be inspectable, verifiable, and replaceable across backends. This document defines the shared conformance and observability surface needed to enforce those guarantees.

docs.title: Shared conformance suite
docs.text:
sr-store must expose a backend conformance test harness or reusable test functions.

Every backend implementation must pass the same behavior tests for:

  • immutable revision insertion and retrieval;
  • deterministic duplicate handling;
  • snapshot creation and lookup;
  • snapshot branching;
  • named-root compare-and-set;
  • stale-root conflict behavior;
  • historical snapshot readability;
  • reachability;
  • integrity verification;
  • transaction semantics that are visible through the public API.

The in-memory backend is not a weaker mock. It is an implementation of the same contract.

docs.title: Observability model
docs.text:
Storage observability must expose semantic operational facts without requiring consumers to know backend internals.

Initial concepts:

StoreStats
RootStatus
IntegrityReport
GcReport
IndexStatus

StoreStats should be able to report counts and sizes where the backend can provide them, such as:

  • revisions;
  • snapshots;
  • named roots;
  • reachable canonical objects;
  • unreachable candidate objects;
  • backend storage bytes where meaningful.

Metrics that are unavailable for a backend should be optional rather than fabricated.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
Errors returned by storage APIs must distinguish at least:

  • not found;
  • invalid identifier;
  • unsupported encoding/storage version;
  • stale root / compare-and-set conflict;
  • integrity failure;
  • backend I/O or transaction failure;
  • invalid operation.

Error types should preserve machine-readable categories while still producing useful human messages.

docs.title: Conformance fixtures
docs.text:
The repository should contain deterministic fixtures that describe small histories such as:

S1: A->R1, B->R1
S2 from S1: A->R2
S3 from S1: B->R2

The same fixture should be loadable against memory and SQLite implementations and yield the same logical IDs and results.

docs.title: Files prescribed by this design
docs.text:
Within sr-store:

crates/sr-store/src/
├── error.rs
├── stats.rs
└── conformance.rs

Shared integration tests:

crates/sr-store/tests/
└── conformance.rs

Backend tests may live in each backend crate, but they should call the shared conformance suite rather than duplicate expected behavior.

docs.title: Required tests
docs.text:
• Memory backend passes all conformance cases.
  • SQLite backend passes the same conformance cases.
  • Equivalent fixture histories produce equivalent logical IDs across backends.
  • Stale-root conflicts have the same error category across backends.
  • Integrity reports use the same backend-neutral model.
  • Optional statistics do not change semantic behavior.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: This document does not define a CLI command, HTTP endpoint, metrics exporter, or web diagnostics panel. Those surfaces can later consume the backend-neutral observability objects.

docs.title: Projection Crate Boundaries and Core Model
Purpose
docs.text:
This document turns the file-facing requirements of design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md into concrete Rust library boundaries.

It covers only projection capabilities that are required to create, track, render, and reconcile external files. Other projection kinds such as browser views and agent context remain governed by Level 1 and should get their own lower-level designs later.

This design depends on the identity, persistence, and migration layers defined by Levels 1–5. It does not change those models.

docs.title: Required crates
docs.text:
Create three backend-independent/domain-oriented crates:

crates/
├── sr-projection/
├── sr-projection-fs/
└── sr-markdown/

Dependency direction:

sr-core
   ↑
sr-store
   ↑
sr-change
   ↑
sr-projection
   ↑          ↑
sr-projection-fs   sr-markdown

sr-markdown may also depend on the universal graph/schema crates once those exist.

No crate in this slice may depend on agents, sessions, CLI, HTTP, TUI, React, or a concrete storage backend.

docs.title: sr-projection
docs.text:
sr-projection owns domain-independent projection concepts.

It must define public types or traits for:

  • projection identity/reference;
  • projection class;
  • projection capabilities;
  • projection kind;
  • style reference;
  • renderer version;
  • rendering context;
  • rendered output metadata;
  • persistent projection specification;
  • runtime synchronization state boundary;
  • adapter capabilities;
  • rendering;
  • parsing of editable representations;
  • reconciliation of parsed candidates;
  • projection validation hooks;
  • structured projection/import errors.

The crate must not know about filesystem watcher APIs, Markdown syntax, Rust ASTs, or agents.

docs.title: Projection classes
docs.text:
The core model must represent at least:

ReadOnly
Editable
Ephemeral
Interactive

For the file-focused implementation slice, ReadOnly and Editable must be fully usable. The other variants may initially be model-only.

docs.title: Projection capabilities
docs.text:
Adapters must declare capabilities instead of callers inferring them.

At minimum:

renderable
parseable
editable
round_trip_capable
structure_preserving
style_preserving

Capabilities must be explicit and deterministic for a given adapter/version.

docs.title: Projection specification
docs.text:
A persistent projection specification represents user-meaningful configuration. It should be able to identify:

  • semantic scope;
  • projection kind;
  • projection class;
  • style entity/revision or style selector;
  • adapter identity/version;
  • external location when applicable;
  • ownership policy;
  • domain configuration needed for deterministic rendering.

The specification is distinct from runtime synchronization state.

User-meaningful projection configuration may live as normal knowledge entities. Operational sync metadata may live in derived/runtime storage.

docs.title: Render contract
docs.text:
The rendering contract must make all output-affecting inputs explicit enough for reproducibility and cache keys.

Conceptually:

render(
    semantic scope,
    exact snapshot/revisions,
    projection kind,
    style revision,
    renderer version,
    rendering context
) -> RenderedProjection

A renderer must not read undeclared mutable global settings that affect output.

RenderedProjection must expose enough metadata to identify the exact bytes/text produced and the exact semantic/style inputs used.

docs.title: Editable adapter contract
docs.text:
An editable adapter must separate parsing from reconciliation.

Conceptually:

external representation
    -> parse
    -> candidate semantic representation
    -> reconcile(existing canonical state)
    -> semantic operations/migration proposal

Parsing must not assign stable canonical entity identity merely because candidate nodes happen to occupy similar positions.

Reconciliation is responsible for justified continuity.

docs.title: Reconciliation result
docs.text:
The generic projection layer must support results equivalent to:

NoSemanticChange
MigrationProposal
Ambiguous
Conflict
InvalidExternalState

The exact Rust enum names may differ, but the states must remain distinguishable.

A formatting-only external edit must be representable as NoSemanticChange rather than a fake migration.

docs.title: Structured diagnostics
docs.text:
Projection errors and conflicts must preserve structured information suitable for CLI, API, UI, and agent rendering.

Do not reduce all failures to strings.

At minimum, diagnostics must be able to identify:

  • projection/specification;
  • semantic scope;
  • synchronization base;
  • affected entity when known;
  • stage: render, observe, parse, reconcile, validate, commit, or rerender;
  • domain-specific details;
  • retryability where meaningful.

docs.title: Style model
docs.text:
sr-projection owns only the universal reference to style configuration and generic cache identity requirements.

Domain crates own actual style properties.

A style affecting output must resolve to an immutable revision or an equivalent exact immutable value before rendering.

Changing style must not create semantic content revisions merely because rendered bytes change.

docs.title: Incremental rendering boundary
docs.text:
The core renderer API must permit adapters to return or use reusable intermediate fragments keyed by exact local immutable inputs.

Do not require all adapters to implement incremental rendering immediately.

Do not key all rendering caches only by global SnapshotId.

docs.title: Prescribed files
docs.text:
Implementation of this design must create at least:

crates/sr-projection/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-projection/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/model.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/capabilities.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/style.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/render.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/adapter.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/reconcile.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/diagnostic.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/state.rs
crates/sr-projection/tests/projection_conformance.rs

crates/sr-projection-fs/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/lib.rs

crates/sr-markdown/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-markdown/src/lib.rs

The workspace Cargo.toml must include the three crates once implemented.

docs.title: Architectural rules
docs.text:
• Canonical state is never replaced directly from parsed projection bytes.
  • Projection code consumes public storage/change interfaces; it must not issue SQL directly.
  • sr-projection is domain-independent.
  • sr-projection-fs owns filesystem-specific behavior and depends on sr-projection, not the reverse.
  • sr-markdown implements projection contracts; sr-projection never depends on Markdown.
  • Agent functionality must remain optional and above these crates.
  • UI code must not gain a separate privileged mutation path.

docs.title: Completion criteria
docs.text: This design is satisfied when all three crates can exist in the workspace with the dependency direction above, sr-projection expresses the complete domain-independent render/parse/reconcile lifecycle, and no file/domain/agent-specific assumption leaks into its public core model.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document specifies the concrete file-synchronization layer required by design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md.

It applies only to projections whose external representation is a filesystem artifact. It does not define Markdown semantics or source-language AST semantics.

The implementation belongs primarily in crates/sr-projection-fs and uses the generic contracts from sr-projection.

docs.title: Core responsibilities
docs.text:
sr-projection-fs must own:

  • explicit file-projection ownership;
  • path/location mapping;
  • deterministic file rendering/write-out;
  • file-content hashing;
  • persistent/runtime synchronization metadata;
  • observation of external file changes;
  • dirty-state detection;
  • feedback-loop suppression;
  • import scheduling boundary;
  • failed-import retention/retry state;
  • rename/move observation;
  • delete/create observation;
  • establishing a new synchronization base after successful reconciliation.

It must not own domain parsing or semantic matching.

docs.title: Ownership classes
docs.text:
Every observed path must be classified explicitly enough to prevent accidental capture.

Support at least:

ManagedEditable
ManagedReadOnly
Unmanaged
ImportedExternal

Meaning:

  • ManagedEditable: Scriberig renders the file and supported external edits may be reconciled.
  • ManagedReadOnly: Scriberig renders the file; external changes are not imported as canonical edits.
  • Unmanaged: Scriberig does not own or rewrite the file.
  • ImportedExternal: the file is an external artifact used as input/knowledge but is not a Scriberig-owned projection.

A directory scan must never implicitly convert Unmanaged files into managed projections.

docs.title: External location
docs.text:
The filesystem layer owns a normalized external-location type for file paths.

Semantic entity identity must not derive from a path.

A projection specification may map one semantic scope to one path, and changing that mapping may represent a projection/configuration change rather than a semantic-content change.

Domain rules may declare path placement semantically meaningful, but that fact must come from the domain adapter rather than from the filesystem layer.

docs.title: Synchronization state
docs.text:
For each managed filesystem projection, runtime synchronization state must retain enough information for three-way reconciliation.

At minimum it must identify:

projection/spec reference
external path
last synchronization base snapshot
last synchronized semantic scope/revisions
last rendered content hash
last observed content hash when useful
adapter/renderer version used for the base
style revision used for the base
state/status

The exact storage representation is deferred, but the API must not require this state to be canonical semantic knowledge.

Suggested synchronization states include:

Synchronized
ExternallyModified
Rendering
ImportPending
ImportFailed
Conflict
Missing

docs.title: Hashing and dirty detection
docs.text:
The filesystem layer must compute a deterministic hash of exact file bytes or normalized bytes according to an explicit policy.

For the initial implementation, prefer hashing exact bytes written/read.

If the observed hash equals the last rendered synchronized hash, the file is not an independent external semantic edit.

If it differs, the path becomes externally modified and must enter the adapter import/reconciliation lifecycle.

A hash difference alone must not be interpreted as semantic difference.

docs.title: Rendering and atomic replacement
docs.text:
Writing a managed projection must avoid exposing partially written output where practical.

The file-writing boundary should support a write-temporary-then-replace strategy or an equivalent atomic mechanism appropriate to the platform.

After a successful write:

  1. compute/confirm the exact written hash;
  2. update synchronization metadata;
  3. mark the projection synchronized;
  4. make subsequent watcher notifications attributable to the render rather than to an independent user edit.

Do not update synchronization state before a failed write is known to have succeeded.

docs.title: Feedback-loop suppression
docs.text:
Filesystem watchers may report Scriberig's own writes.

The implementation must not re-import those writes.

The initial suppression strategy should use exact rendered hashes as the authoritative check. An operation token or short-lived write registry may be added as an optimization, but correctness must not depend only on timing/debounce.

The system must converge even if watcher events are duplicated, reordered, or coalesced.

docs.title: Observation abstraction
docs.text:
Filesystem event delivery must sit behind a small interface so tests can supply deterministic synthetic events.

Model at least:

Created(path)
Modified(path)
Removed(path)
Renamed { from, to }
RescanRequired(scope)

Do not expose a specific watcher library's event enum through the public crate API.

Watcher events are hints that cause state inspection. The current filesystem contents and synchronization records determine the actual state.

docs.title: External modification lifecycle
docs.text:
For ManagedEditable:

observe change
    -> read exact external content
    -> compare to synchronized hash
    -> if different, mark externally modified
    -> call domain adapter parse
    -> call reconcile against synchronization base/current canonical state
    -> validate proposed migration
    -> commit/promote when allowed
    -> render canonical result
    -> write file
    -> establish new synchronization base

For ManagedReadOnly, an external modification must not silently become canonical state. Policy may restore the generated file or surface drift; exact UX belongs elsewhere.

docs.title: Failed imports
docs.text:
If parsing, reconciliation, validation, or commit fails, retain:

  • previous valid synchronization base;
  • current external path;
  • exact observed content hash;
  • diagnostics;
  • enough access to the external content to retry while it remains available.

Do not advance the synchronization base on failure.

A later file event must be able to retry from the same known base or detect that the external file changed again.

docs.title: Three-way state
docs.text:
The synchronization layer must make the three required states available to reconciliation:

B = last synchronized semantic base / projection
D = current canonical state
F = current external file

The filesystem layer does not perform domain semantic merge itself. It supplies exact bases and current external bytes to the adapter/reconciliation layer.

docs.title: Renames and moves
docs.text:
A rename/move should first be interpreted as an external-location change for the projection.

It must not manufacture new semantic entities merely because the path changed.

If reliable rename information is unavailable from the platform, the system may conservatively observe remove/create and use projection/content matching to recover the move when possible.

docs.title: Deletes
docs.text:
Deleting a managed file is not automatically equivalent to deleting its semantic scope.

The projection specification/adapter policy must decide whether external deletion means:

  • projection drift requiring regeneration;
  • a candidate semantic deletion;
  • projection removal/configuration change;
  • unresolved user action.

The filesystem layer must surface the deletion without inventing semantic meaning.

docs.title: Prescribed files
docs.text:
Implementation must create at least:

crates/sr-projection-fs/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/location.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/ownership.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/state.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/hash.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/io.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/observe.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/sync.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/recovery.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/tests/sync_conformance.rs

docs.title: Testing requirements
docs.text:
Tests must cover at least:

  • rendered file becomes synchronized;
  • watcher notification for the exact rendered bytes is ignored as self-generated;
  • external byte change becomes ExternallyModified;
  • formatting-only semantic no-op can return to synchronized state without a canonical migration;
  • failed parse preserves previous base;
  • repeated watcher events are idempotent;
  • unmanaged files are never rewritten;
  • read-only projections do not import external edits;
  • rename preserves projection/semantic identity where domain semantics allow it;
  • canonical state changing while an external edit exists exposes the correct three-way base/current/external inputs.

Use temporary directories and a fake observation source for deterministic tests. Real watcher-library integration can have a smaller platform integration test set.

docs.title: Completion criteria
docs.text: This design is satisfied when managed files can be rendered, observed, classified as synchronized or externally modified, routed into a domain adapter without direct semantic mutation, recovered after failed imports, and resynchronized without feedback loops.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the first concrete editable file projection required by design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md.

Markdown is chosen because it exercises the full projection cycle—render, external edit, parse, identity reconciliation, migration, and rerender—without requiring compiler semantics.

The implementation belongs in crates/sr-markdown and plugs into sr-projection and sr-projection-fs.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The first adapter must support semantic objects corresponding to at least:

MarkdownDocument
Section
Heading
Paragraph
List
ListItem
Table
TableRow
TableCell
CodeBlock
QuoteBlock
Link

Inline formatting may be represented through a smaller inline model initially, but it must preserve authored text structure sufficiently for deterministic round-trip rendering.

The adapter must not require hidden Scriberig IDs in ordinary Markdown files.

docs.title: Domain boundary
docs.text:
The adapter owns the boundary between canonical document meaning and Markdown presentation.

Canonical domain structure includes:

  • document/section hierarchy;
  • block identity and order;
  • paragraph textual content;
  • list/list-item structure;
  • table/row/cell structure;
  • code block language/fence semantic data where represented;
  • links and quotations;
  • author-significant inline structure selected by the domain model.

Projection style may control:

  • blank-line policy;
  • list marker preference where semantically equivalent;
  • table spacing/alignment formatting;
  • wrapping where supported safely;
  • code-fence choice where equivalent;
  • final newline policy.

Style must not silently restructure sections, merge/split semantic paragraphs, or change link targets/code contents.

docs.title: Parser output
docs.text:
The Markdown parser must produce a candidate document representation distinct from stable canonical identity.

Candidate nodes should have local candidate IDs/paths sufficient for reconciliation diagnostics, but they must not invent EntityId values for existing canonical entities.

Parser output must preserve:

  • semantic node kind;
  • ordered child structure;
  • text/content needed for canonical construction;
  • source spans only as diagnostic/projection coordinates;
  • parse diagnostics.

Source offsets and line numbers must not become canonical identity.

docs.title: Renderer
docs.text:
Rendering must be deterministic for the same:

canonical document state
Markdown style revision
renderer version
relevant rendering context

The renderer should construct output from semantic blocks, not from a stored original Markdown blob.

Round-trip tests compare semantic structure, not byte equality across arbitrary input styles.

docs.title: Style
docs.text:
Define a MarkdownStyle domain value. The initial style should include only options the adapter can implement deterministically and safely.

Suggested initial properties:

list_marker
ordered_list_delimiter
blank_lines_between_blocks
final_newline
code_fence_preference
table_spacing

Do not add style options that imply semantic transformations.

docs.title: Reconciliation strategy
docs.text:
Reconciliation compares:

B = semantic state corresponding to the last synchronized Markdown projection
D = current canonical semantic state
C = parsed candidate semantic structure from the edited file

For the simple case where D == B, match candidate nodes against B and produce a migration proposal.

Matching evidence should be deterministic and ordered from strongest to weakest. Initial evidence should include:

  1. exact unchanged subtree/content;
  2. node type and exact content;
  3. parent/section correspondence;
  4. sibling sequence alignment;
  5. nearby unchanged anchors;
  6. heading/title or other domain-significant names;
  7. conservative text similarity for same-kind nodes.

Do not use text similarity to force continuity when multiple matches are equally plausible.

docs.title: Content versus structure
docs.text:
