  • old/new source content or a unified equivalent;
  • validation status;
  • stale/conflict status;
  • explicit apply/accept action;
  • reject/close action that does not mutate current state.

docs.title: 11. Validation Contract
docs.text:
The first Rust golden-path candidate must pass two levels of deterministic validation before acceptance is enabled:

  1. Scriberig semantic/projection validation: reconciliation parses successfully, semantic mappings remain valid enough to produce a candidate, and migration base is current;
  2. fixture project validation: execute cargo check against the candidate materialization or an isolated candidate workspace without network dependencies.

If the existing validation architecture already supports validator registration, add the fixture/project Rust validator there rather than special-casing the web UI.

Validation output must be represented as operation/result data consumable by web and TUI.

A failed validation prevents normal acceptance in the golden path and shows diagnostics.

Tests must also include one intentionally invalid candidate, such as malformed Rust, and assert that current snapshot and working tree remain unchanged.

docs.title: 12. Apply and Canonical Snapshot Contract
docs.text:
Applying a valid candidate must use shared compare-and-swap migration semantics.

The application operation must reject a stale base if current project state no longer matches the candidate base.

On successful application:

  • a successor immutable snapshot exists;
  • the project current root advances to that snapshot;
  • migration provenance/history links base and successor;
  • the selected semantic object is resolved against the successor when identity survives;
  • clients learn the authoritative new snapshot through operation result/event/refresh.

No product UI directly edits project snapshot tables.

docs.title: 13.1 Required successful behavior
docs.text:
After a candidate is accepted, the resulting Rust projection must be materialized to the fixture working tree using shared filesystem projection infrastructure.

The E2E test must observe:

src/lib.rs contains left.saturating_add(right)

and must confirm the file did not contain that text before acceptance.

docs.title: 13.2 Safety
docs.text:
Materialization must enforce:

  • target path belongs to active project;
  • target is the registered source projection/path;
  • stale source digest/external changes are detected;
  • atomic replacement semantics are used where supported;
  • symlink/path escape is rejected;
  • unrelated files are untouched.

docs.title: 13.3 External effect failure
docs.text:
Canonical database promotion and filesystem I/O cannot be assumed to be one transaction.

Use the repository's external-effect receipt/reconciliation design to represent success/failure.

If filesystem materialization fails after semantic promotion, expose a repairable out-of-sync/effect-failed state and retain the accepted canonical snapshot. Do not lie that write-back succeeded.

If the existing architecture stages materialization before final promotion, preserve its documented correctness rules. The key requirement is explicit recoverable state, not a particular impossible cross-resource transaction.

docs.title: 13.4 Conflict scenario
docs.text:
A required E2E/conformance scenario modifies src/lib.rs externally after the candidate is created but before write-back.

Acceptance/write-back must not silently overwrite the external content.

The operation must produce a stale/conflict result that is visible through the product surface, and the externally modified file must remain intact.

docs.title: 14. History and Post-Apply Refresh
docs.text:
After successful application and materialization:

  • active workspace snapshot changes from base to successor;
  • source projection reload shows left.saturating_add(right) from authoritative state;
  • history includes the change/migration/snapshot transition;
  • reloading the web page and reopening the project still shows successor state;
  • restarting the TUI against the same database/project still shows successor state;
  • project status reports the successor snapshot.

The E2E test records the base snapshot ID and asserts it differs from the successor snapshot ID.

docs.title: 15.1 Deterministic provider
docs.text:
Add/reuse a deterministic model provider for E2E tests.

It must not make network requests.

For a known prompt such as:

Change add so overflow saturates instead of wrapping.

it must exercise the real agent runtime/tool boundary sufficiently to produce a candidate equivalent to replacing left + right with left.saturating_add(right).

The provider may use scripted responses/tool calls; it must not bypass the agent application operation by inserting a migration directly from the test.

docs.title: 15.2 Scope assertion
docs.text:
The test must prove the agent operation received semantic scope containing the selected add entity and the active snapshot.

This may be asserted through captured deterministic-provider request metadata, operation/session records, or a test-visible agent-tool invocation record.

Do not reduce this to an assertion that the prompt string happened to contain add.

docs.title: 15.3 Same review path
docs.text:
The agent-generated candidate enters the same migration review/validation/apply surface as a human edit.

The agent must not auto-write the working tree in the golden scenario.

Before user acceptance, filesystem source remains unchanged.

docs.title: 16. Web Runtime Changes
docs.text:
The reference web application runtime must gain explicit active-project/workspace coordination.

Conceptually it owns:

connection
capabilities
project catalog access
active workspace
knowledge/semantic tree rooted at active workspace
shared semantic selection
operations/session state
workspace refresh

ProjectManager must not be an isolated island with only local projects state after import.

It must call a public runtime/controller action such as activateProject(projectId) or invoke an injected callback that does so.

Do not rebuild a second ScriberigClient or WorkspaceModel inside the project view.

On activation the raw/semantic navigation root is replaced by the active project's root rather than the server's unrelated generic bootstrap root.

docs.title: 17. TUI Runtime Changes
docs.text:
The native TUI must represent active project workspace explicitly in application state.

Starting with srig tui --project PATH --import must land in the imported project's browsable semantic workspace.

When multiple projects share a database, the TUI must use the selected ProjectId/workspace root and never infer the active project from whichever root was most recently imported globally.

Required user-visible context includes project name/path and current snapshot (full or shortened display is acceptable).

TUI explorer rows for supported named code entities use semantic labels, not opaque ordinal labels.

docs.title: 18. Public Protocol and Client Rules
docs.text:
If new data is required remotely, extend the canonical protocol/client/server path once.

Likely required data includes:

  • project workspace/root reference;
  • project snapshot refresh information;
  • source projection including mapping/editability/staleness;
  • create/reconcile candidate request/result;
  • validation operation/result;
  • materialization/effect status if not already public.

Before adding a new operation, inspect current public operations and reuse existing migration/render/reconcile/apply/operation mechanisms when their semantics already match.

Do not add one-off /web/... endpoints.

Do not serialize SQLite row IDs.

docs.title: 19. Capability Matrix Updates
docs.text:
As implementation lands, add or update entries in capabilities.toml for the user-level capabilities needed by this slice, for example conceptually:

project_workspace
semantic_code_navigation
source_projection
projection_edit_candidate
candidate_validation
migration_review_apply
filesystem_materialize
project_history_refresh
agent_semantic_edit_candidate

Use existing matrix vocabulary.

A surface reaches verified only when the required dedicated test exists.

Do not mark all surfaces verified merely because one shared lower-level unit test passes.

docs.title: 20. Required Browser E2E Scenarios
docs.text:
Extend the existing Playwright harness under web/e2e.

Tests launch the real server and real built/dev browser app as the harness already does.

Required scenarios:

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-01: onboard and open active project
docs.text:
1. copy golden fixture to temp workspace;
  2. initialize Git and add fixture files when needed;
  3. open Projects;
  4. scan temp path with Git-tracked mode;
  5. import reviewed scan;
  6. activate/open imported project;
  7. navigate to semantic project browser;
  8. assert active project name/path context;
  9. assert explorer visibly contains Calculator and add;
  10. assert browser health diagnostics are clean.

The test fails if it only sees status=imported.

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-02: selection opens exact source
docs.text:
1. continue from/import fixture;
  2. select add;
  3. navigate/open source projection;
  4. assert projection path contains src/lib.rs;
  5. assert source contains left + right;
  6. assert selection summary identifies add and current snapshot;
  7. assert projection is editable and not stale.

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-03: human edit creates reviewable candidate without write-through
docs.text:
1. edit the mapped source expression to left.saturating_add(right);
  2. submit/propose change;
  3. assert migration review opens;
  4. assert base snapshot equals recorded pre-edit snapshot;
  5. assert diff contains old and new expressions;
  6. assert changed path is src/lib.rs;
  7. assert validation becomes successful;
  8. read temp src/lib.rs from the test harness and assert it still contains left + right before acceptance.

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-04: accept writes file and refreshes snapshot/history
docs.text:
1. accept validated candidate;
  2. wait for operation completion and authoritative workspace refresh;
  3. assert successor snapshot differs from base;
  4. read temp file and assert left.saturating_add(right);
  5. reopen projection and assert accepted text;
  6. open history and assert the change/migration is present;
  7. reload browser;
  8. reopen active project if activation is intentionally session-local;
  9. assert accepted source and successor snapshot remain observable.

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-05: invalid edit cannot apply
docs.text:
1. start from fresh fixture;
  2. edit source to invalid Rust;
  3. propose candidate;
  4. assert validation failure/diagnostic is visible;
  5. assert normal apply action is disabled or application operation rejects it;
  6. assert project current snapshot remains base;
  7. assert filesystem source remains original.

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-06: stale external edit is not overwritten
docs.text:
1. create valid candidate from base;
  2. modify temp src/lib.rs externally through test harness before acceptance/write-back;
  3. attempt apply/materialize;
  4. assert conflict/stale/effect failure is visible;
  5. assert external content remains on disk;
  6. assert no silent overwrite occurs;
  7. assert product offers/reports a recoverable state.

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-07: agent uses selection and enters same review path
docs.text:
1. start fresh fixture and select add;
  2. switch to Session/Agent;
  3. submit the deterministic golden prompt;
  4. assert agent operation completes using fake provider;
  5. assert recorded semantic scope is the selected add entity at active snapshot;
  6. assert resulting candidate/migration can be opened in the normal migration review;
  7. assert diff contains the saturating-add change;
  8. assert filesystem is unchanged before user acceptance.

docs.title: 21. Required Native TUI E2E Scenarios
docs.text:
Extend the existing native PTY TUI suite rather than replacing it with reducer-only tests.

Tests run a real srig tui binary in a pseudo-terminal against a temporary database and golden fixture.

Required scenarios:

docs.title: TUI-GOLDEN-01: onboarded project is active and named symbols are navigable
docs.text:
Run the equivalent of:

srig tui --db <temp-db> --project <temp-project> --git-tracked --import

Then drive keys/actions to verify:

  • project context shows golden fixture;
  • current snapshot is visible;
  • explorer contains Calculator and add;
  • selection can reach add without typing an entity ID.

docs.title: TUI-GOLDEN-02: selected method opens source projection
docs.text:
Select add, open projection/source action, and assert terminal output contains:

src/lib.rs
left + right

docs.title: TUI-GOLDEN-03: create/review/apply candidate
docs.text:
Using the defined deterministic TUI edit interaction:

  • create the saturating-add candidate;
  • open review;
  • assert old/new expressions and validation success;
  • assert disk is unchanged before apply;
  • apply;
  • assert successor snapshot/current state is visible;
  • assert disk contains accepted expression;
  • assert history/projection reflects successor state.

docs.title: TUI-GOLDEN-04: stale external edit is protected
docs.text: Create candidate, mutate source externally, attempt apply/materialize, and assert terminal reports conflict/stale state while external file survives unchanged.

docs.title: TUI-GOLDEN-05: agent candidate uses selected semantic scope
docs.text:
With deterministic provider enabled, select add, issue the golden agent prompt, and assert the resulting migration is reviewable through the same TUI change-review path.

The PTY test may inspect deterministic provider/session records after the terminal run to prove exact semantic scope, but it must drive the user operation through the real TUI.

docs.title: 22. Cross-Surface Conformance Scenarios
docs.text:
In addition to UI E2E, add programmatic conformance tests over public interfaces:

  1. resolving the same ProjectId through embedded application and HTTP client returns equivalent workspace root/snapshot;
  2. semantic navigation to add yields the same entity identity through embedded, client, web-model, and TUI application adapter paths;
  3. rendering source for that entity at the same snapshot yields equivalent path/text/mapping;
  4. the same source edit produces equivalent migration semantics independent of initiating surface;
  5. stale-base application is rejected consistently;
  6. successful apply advances exactly one project root and does not affect another project in the same database;
  7. write-back modifies only the intended fixture source;
  8. agent candidate uses the same migration/change types and does not bypass application operations.

docs.title: 23. Test Harness Requirements
docs.text:
Product tests must be deterministic and diagnosable.

The harness must record or preserve on failure:

  • server stderr/stdout log;
  • web console/page errors;
  • operation failure diagnostics;
  • temporary database path or a copied artifact when practical;
  • fixture working-tree diff;
  • PTY screen/output transcript for failed TUI scenarios.

Tests must use bounded waits with explicit operation/state conditions. Avoid arbitrary multi-second sleeps when polling an operation/event/DOM condition is available.

Do not weaken assertions to make timing flakes disappear.

docs.title: 24. Required Quality Gate
docs.text:
The final implementation must pass the repository's normal quality gate plus the product E2E suites.

At minimum:

python3 tools/lint_repo.py
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
pnpm --dir web format:check
pnpm --dir web typecheck
pnpm --dir web test
pnpm --dir web build

Run the repository-defined browser E2E command from web/e2e/README.md/package scripts and the native TUI PTY suite.

If tools/check.sh already composes these checks, it must be updated so the golden product gate cannot be omitted from the normal full verification command, unless E2E environment setup is explicitly separated into a documented CI target. In that case CI must run both.

docs.title: 25. Implementation Order
docs.text:
Implement in this order and do not skip ahead by adding placeholders:

  1. active project workspace resolution/activation;
  2. semantic names and navigable Rust hierarchy;
  3. real source projection for selected Rust semantic objects;
  4. candidate creation from projection edit;
  5. review and deterministic validation;
  6. apply + controlled filesystem write-back + workspace refresh;
  7. web golden path;
  8. TUI golden path;
  9. deterministic agent-scoped candidate path;
  10. stale/conflict scenarios;
  11. cross-surface conformance and normal quality-gate integration.

Each step has a Level-3 task with a detailed checklist. Later tasks must not mark themselves complete while a prerequisite task has unchecked acceptance items.

docs.title: 26. Completion Criteria
docs.text:
This Level-2 design is satisfied only when:

  • every required Level-3 task created for this vertical slice is checked and verified;
  • all WEB-GOLDEN scenarios pass against real processes and temp fixture;
  • all TUI-GOLDEN scenarios pass against the real native binary;
  • cross-surface public-interface conformance passes;
  • the fixture working tree changes only after accepted change;
  • stale/conflicting source is never silently overwritten;
  • current snapshot/history refresh is observable after apply;
  • deterministic agent scope/candidate behavior is proven without external network;
  • capabilities.toml statuses are truthful;
  • full repository quality checks pass.

Subsystem tests from earlier design tasks are necessary regression coverage but cannot substitute for these criteria.

docs.title: Provider Continuation and Observable Model Execution
1. Purpose
docs.text:
This document translates design/level-1/020. provider continuation state and observable model execution.md into concrete subsystem boundaries for the current Rust implementation.

It also refines the implementation contracts in:

  • design/level-2/023. agent runtime model provider and branch orchestration.md;
  • design/level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md;
  • task 133 shared agent-console trace controls;
  • task 134 recursive TUI projection;
  • task 135 recursive semantic agent execution.

The central implementation rule is:

Scriberig persists canonical branch/session execution history and a complete safe provider-neutral effective model request. Provider-native continuation handles are opaque branch-local runtime metadata used only when they still match the canonical context lineage.

docs.title: 2. Existing Owners to Extend
docs.text:
Do not create parallel crates for this work.

Use the existing owners:

crates/scriberig-session/
  durable provider-neutral execution/session records

crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/
  context compilation
  provider adapters
  continuation reuse/reseed decisions
  stream/event normalization

crates/scriberig-app/src/agent_console/
  shared presentation preferences
  full-detail retrieval boundaries
  model library and execution configuration

crates/scriberig-protocol/
  transport DTOs

crates/scriberig-server/
  HTTP/event exposure

crates/scriberig-client/
  Rust remote client

web/packages/protocol
web/packages/client
web/packages/model
web/packages/agent-ui
  TypeScript/web equivalents

crates/scriberig-tui/
  terminal rendering and local presentation state

Relevant current runtime/session files include:

crates/scriberig-session/src/execution.rs
crates/scriberig-session/src/branch.rs
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/context.rs
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/context/
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/events.rs
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/model_provider.rs
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/openai_compatible.rs
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/openai_request.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/agent_console/detail.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/agent_console/preferences.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/agent_console/model.rs

If implementation has moved, extend the current equivalent owner and update the implementation task before coding.

docs.title: 3. Provider-Neutral Continuation Contract
docs.text:
Introduce or extend one provider-neutral runtime concept equivalent to:

struct ProviderContinuationState {
    provider_profile: ProviderProfileId,
    provider_kind: ProviderKind,
    branch: EntityId,
    strategy: ProviderContinuationStrategy,
    opaque_handle: SecretSafeOpaqueId,
    context_fingerprint: ContextFingerprint,
    created_for_invocation: EntityId,
    last_used_invocation: EntityId,
    status: ProviderContinuationStatus,
    metadata: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}

enum ProviderContinuationStrategy {
    Conversation,
    PreviousResponse,
    LocalSession,
    ProviderSpecific(String),
}

enum ProviderContinuationStatus {
    Reusable,
    Stale,
    Unavailable,
    Expired,
    Unknown,
}

Exact Rust names may differ.

Requirements:

  • opaque handle never becomes SessionId or BranchId;
  • no credential values in the structure;
  • no raw provider request/response bodies in the structure;
  • one branch may accumulate historical continuation records across provider/profile switches;
  • only the continuation matching the resolved provider/profile and context lineage is considered reusable;
  • durability policy may retain enough metadata to attempt restart reuse, but correctness must never depend on successful provider-state recovery.

docs.title: 4. Continuation Repository Boundary
docs.text:
Continuation state may be persisted with session/runtime records or through another existing durable runtime repository, but ownership must remain explicit.

The owning API needs operations equivalent to:

get continuation for branch + provider/profile
put continuation after successful initialization/use
mark continuation stale
mark continuation unavailable
record successor/fork relationship when useful

Do not expose a generic mutable map directly to TUI/web/server layers.

The application/protocol may expose safe read-only provenance such as provider kind/strategy/status, but mutation of continuation handles belongs to the runtime/provider boundary.

docs.title: 5. Canonical Effective Request Record
docs.text:
The existing bounded ModelRequestProjection is useful for normal activity rendering but is insufficient for the explicit Full prompt requirement.

Add a durable or durably retrievable complete safe request record concept equivalent to:

struct CanonicalModelRequest {
    invocation: EntityId,
    session: EntityId,
    branch: EntityId,
    continuation_anchor: Option<ContinuationAnchorRef>,
    context_fingerprint: ContextFingerprint,
    instructions: Vec<RequestSection>,
    messages: Vec<RequestMessage>,
    semantic_context: Vec<RequestContextItem>,
    dependency_results: Vec<SemanticRef>,
    ancestor_results: Vec<SemanticRef>,
    tools: Vec<ModelRequestTool>,
    structured_output: Option<SafeSchema>,
    model: ResolvedModelConfig,
    provider_continuation: Option<SafeContinuationRef>,
    estimated_tokens: Option<u64>,
    redactions: Vec<RedactionRecord>,
}

The exact representation should reuse existing provider-neutral context/message types instead of duplicating them.

The request must be constructed after Scriberig context compilation and before provider-specific serialization.

This record is the canonical source for prompt inspection.

docs.title: 6. Bounded Activity Projection Versus Full Detail
docs.text: Keep two layers:

docs.title: Bounded ordinary projection
docs.text:
Suitable for activity lists/event streams:

model identity
thinking level
section/message counts
bounded snippets
truncated flag
durable full-detail ref

docs.title: Full safe detail
docs.text:
Fetched on demand using stable invocation/request identity:

all safe instruction sections
all safe effective messages/context sections
all safe tool definitions
all safe dependency/ancestor result projections
resolved execution config
continuation strategy/status/ref
redaction markers

Do not force the full request through every live event.

Do not make Full mean "increase a truncation limit until it is probably enough".

docs.title: 7. Effective Context with Provider Continuation
docs.text:
When the provider wire request contains only new input plus a continuation identifier, CanonicalModelRequest must still describe the complete effective Scriberig context.

The runtime already owns enough information to compile/fingerprint context. Preserve a request representation before handing work to the provider adapter.

Conceptual flow:

ContextCompiler
   -> CompiledContext
   -> CanonicalModelRequest
   -> request fingerprint
   -> continuation reuse/reseed decision
   -> provider serialization

If continuation reuse allows the provider adapter to omit repeated items on the wire, that is an adapter optimization after canonical request construction.

docs.title: 8. Continuation Reuse Algorithm
docs.text:
Implement a deterministic decision equivalent to:

1. resolve branch execution assignment
2. compile exact Scriberig effective context
3. compute context fingerprint / continuation lineage fingerprint
4. load continuation for branch + provider/profile
5. if none -> initialize new provider state or run stateless
6. if provider/profile mismatch -> do not reuse
7. if lineage matches expected predecessor -> reuse
8. if lineage can be safely forked by provider capability -> fork explicitly
9. otherwise mark stale and reseed from canonical request
10. invoke provider
11. record returned successor provider state/request IDs
12. bind successor state to resulting Scriberig invocation/context lineage

Tests must not use wall-clock coincidence to decide compatibility.

docs.title: 9. Context Lineage and Fingerprints
docs.text:
Do not assume one static request hash is enough for a multi-turn provider conversation.

Represent or derive a lineage concept that can answer:

Does continuation P contain exactly the provider-visible state expected before invocation I?

A reasonable first implementation may use:

compiled-context fingerprint
+ previous invocation identity/fingerprint
+ provider/profile/model identity
+ continuation strategy

The exact hash schema must remain deterministic and secret-free.

If a local-model or other-provider turn changes canonical branch history, the old OpenAI continuation must no longer be considered the automatic successor unless the current context compiler deliberately excludes that turn and the fingerprints prove equivalence.

docs.title: 10. OpenAI Adapter Strategy
docs.text:
The OpenAI adapter should support provider capabilities equivalent to:

conversation continuation
previous-response continuation
provider-visible reasoning items/summaries
response/request IDs

Do not expose OpenAI types above the adapter boundary.

docs.title: Conversation strategy
docs.text:
When enabled for an isolated branch:

branch -> OpenAI conversation

Initialize/seeding behavior must use the branch's compiled canonical context.

docs.title: Previous-response strategy
docs.text:
Reuse/fork previous_response_id only where the runtime can prove exact lineage.

Resend effective top-level instructions as required by provider semantics.

docs.title: Mutual exclusion
docs.text:
The adapter must never send both a Conversation reference and previous_response_id in one request when the provider forbids that combination.

Represent the strategy choice explicitly rather than relying on Option field accidents.

docs.title: 11. Provider Switching
docs.text:
When branch execution assignment changes provider/profile:

  1. keep old continuation record as provenance/history;
  2. do not pass opaque continuation state to the new provider;
  3. compile current canonical Scriberig context;
  4. establish new provider state if supported;
  5. record the new state under the new provider/profile;
  6. if later switching back, validate the old continuation against current context lineage before reuse.

Never treat "same model name" as proof that provider state is compatible.

docs.title: 12. Observable Reasoning Segment Model
docs.text:
Extend provider-neutral model output/activity types to represent ordered provider-visible reasoning segments.

Conceptually:

struct ObservableReasoningSegment {
    id: EntityId,
    invocation: EntityId,
    branch: EntityId,
    ordinal: u64,
    kind: ObservableReasoningKind,
    text: String,
    completeness: ReasoningCompleteness,
    provider_ref: Option<String>,
}

enum ObservableReasoningKind {
    RuntimeStatus,
    ProviderSummary,
    ProviderVisibleReasoning,
}

enum ReasoningCompleteness {
    SummaryOnly,
    FullAvailable,
}

Do not add a HiddenChainOfThought or equivalent type.

Reasoning text enters these records only when it is explicitly safe/user-visible according to provider semantics.

docs.title: 13. Activity Ordering
docs.text:
Reasoning segments must share the same deterministic invocation-local ordering system as tool/semantic calls, results, model outputs, and validation/status events.

A fake-provider sequence such as:

reasoning 1
semantic operation A
result A
reasoning 2
tool B
result B
reasoning 3
assistant output

must be recoverable exactly from shared activity state.

Hiding reasoning in a client removes only reasoning rows. It must not reorder the remaining operations/results.

If current activity kinds are typed but content records are split across collections, introduce the minimum shared ordering/correlation representation necessary to project one causal stream.

docs.title: 14. Presentation Preference Types
docs.text:
Refine current prompt/reasoning preferences to support independent modes equivalent to:

enum PromptPresentation {
    Hidden,
    Summary,
    Full,
}

enum ReasoningPresentation {
    Hidden,
    Summary,
    FullAvailable,
}

Keep independently configurable existing controls for:

tool/semantic invocation presentation
tool/operation result presentation
branch expansion
plan/dependency detail

Presets may assign all fields but may not replace them with a single trace-level value.

docs.title: 15. Application Detail APIs
docs.text:
Extend the existing scriberig-app::agent_console::detail ownership rather than creating TUI/web-specific detail fetch paths.

Provide application operations equivalent to:

get_model_request_summary(invocation)
get_model_request_full(invocation)
get_reasoning_segments(invocation, detail)
get_tool_result_detail(...)

Full model-request retrieval must:

  • require stable invocation/request identity;
  • return safe/redacted provider-neutral structures;
  • never expose credential values;
  • return a structured unavailable/retention result when complete detail was not retained;
  • never re-execute a model to reconstruct detail.

docs.title: 16. Protocol Contract
docs.text:
Protocol DTOs should preserve the distinction between:

activity summary
full request detail
reasoning segment summary/full-available detail
provider continuation provenance

Do not serialize provider-native wire types directly.

A request-detail response should be versionable and structured, not one giant prompt string.

Clients may render it as text, but the protocol keeps sections/messages/tools/config separate.

docs.title: 17. Server and Client
docs.text:
Server routes/actions should map directly to application detail operations.

Remote clients must be able to perform the same presentation changes as embedded clients without changing execution.

Required semantics:

fetch full prompt detail -> read-only
fetch reasoning detail -> read-only
change local/shared presentation preference -> presentation only
continuation reuse/reseed -> runtime only

Do not add a server endpoint allowing clients to set arbitrary provider continuation IDs.

docs.title: 18. TUI and Web Rendering
docs.text:
TUI/web consume the same ordered activity + detail contract.

When prompt mode is Full, the invocation row can expand/fetch the complete safe effective request.

When reasoning is FullAvailable, render every provider-visible reasoning segment in its correct position around tool/semantic activity.

The two controls are independent.

Rendering must distinguish:

provider-visible reasoning
runtime status
semantic operation
generic external tool/process
assistant output

Do not imply that provider-visible reasoning is hidden chain-of-thought.

docs.title: 19. Retention and Availability
docs.text:
Define explicit retention policy for complete safe request records and observable reasoning segments.

At minimum, settled invocation history that claims to support later Full inspection must retain or durably reference the full safe request.

If configurable retention is introduced later, APIs must report:

available
expired/not-retained
redacted
provider-only/unavailable

Never silently substitute a truncated summary while labeling it Full.

docs.title: 20. Security Requirements
docs.text:
Before persistence/public exposure, redact or omit:

credentials
authorization headers
secret environment values
provider-secret connection fields
sensitive tool parameters according to capability policy
provider-private hidden reasoning/encrypted private reasoning

Redaction happens before public DTO construction.

Tests should seed obvious secret sentinel values and prove they do not appear in:

session records
full prompt detail
activity events
protocol JSON
TUI/web rendering snapshots
logs

docs.title: Runtime continuation
docs.text:
• new branch creates independent continuation state;
  • same branch reuses compatible continuation;
  • sibling branch never reuses sibling continuation;
  • provider switch invalidates automatic reuse;
  • switching back reseeds when fingerprint diverged;
  • unavailable provider state falls back to canonical context;
  • OpenAI adapter never sends both continuation strategies together;
  • previous_response_id path resends required instructions.

docs.title: Request observability
docs.text:
• full request contains all safe compiled context sections;
  • bounded projection points to full detail;
  • continuation wire optimization does not make full prompt incomplete;
  • full detail retrieval performs no model execution;
  • redacted values remain structurally marked.

docs.title: Reasoning observability
docs.text:
• provider-visible reasoning before/between/after tools preserves order;
  • hidden reasoning projection leaves tool/result order unchanged;
  • summary-only provider declares that limitation;
  • provider exposing no reasoning produces no invented reasoning content;
  • private/encrypted reasoning never enters visible activity.

docs.title: Cross-surface
docs.text:
• embedded and remote clients retrieve equivalent request detail;
  • TUI/web independent prompt/reasoning toggles do not cause runtime calls;
  • restart restores settled observable history without provider stream replay.

docs.title: 22. Completion Standard
docs.text: This Level-2 design is satisfied when Scriberig can run one isolated branch through a stateful provider continuation, create an independent continuation for a child/sibling branch, safely reseed after context/provider divergence, continue correctly when provider state disappears, preserve a complete safe canonical effective request for every inspectable invocation, preserve provider-visible reasoning segments in their exact order around semantic/tool activity, and expose independent prompt/reasoning presentation controls through the same application/protocol semantics to TUI and web without rerunning model work.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
This document turns design/level-1/014. agent native semantic self hosting.md into the concrete product workflow that Scriberig must support.

The reference scenario has exactly two user instructions issued in the native TUI:

Onboard the current project.

followed by:

Add support for ingesting PHP source files.

The first instruction begins with a fresh SQLite database containing no project. The second instruction begins from the exact semantic project snapshot created by the first and must end in a normal reviewed, validated, accepted project-wide candidate.

This workflow extends, rather than replaces, the first useful project workflow described in design/level-2/025. first useful project workflow vertical slice.md.

docs.title: 2. Required Existing Foundations
docs.text:
The self-hosting slice depends on the existing public architecture for:

  • project scan/import and ownership;
  • active project workspaces;
  • universal semantic read operations;
  • durable sessions, branches, operations, and branch results;
  • provider-neutral agent execution;
  • progressive capability discovery;
  • source projections and migration/candidate review;
  • validation evidence;
  • exact-base apply;
  • filesystem ownership, conflict detection, and external-effect receipts;
  • native TUI interaction and real PTY testing.

Relevant existing Level 3 work includes the project onboarding task and tasks 107 through 122. New work must extend those owners rather than creating a second self-hosting-only stack.

docs.title: 3. Starting Product State
docs.text:
The user is in the Scriberig repository root and starts:

srig tui --db <fresh-db>

The database has no project catalog rows and no project semantic snapshot.

The TUI opens agent mode successfully and visibly indicates that no project is active.

The local runtime provides bounded trusted bootstrap context:

working_directory
selected database/runtime
principal/capability context
agent profile/provider configuration

The working directory is environmental context only. It is not silently promoted to an active semantic project.

docs.title: 4.1 Start the operation
docs.text:
Submitting:

Onboard the current project.

starts the normal durable agent operation and immediately creates/reuses normal session/branch/operation identities.

No active project selection is required to start this operation.

docs.title: 4.2 Bootstrap capability catalog
docs.text:
The initial agent context contains a small trusted catalog sufficient to discover project onboarding.

The conceptual capabilities needed are:

capabilities
project.scan
project.import
project.workspace
inspect
list
operation.observe

The exact provider tool names may follow existing contracts.

The model must not receive a direct database tool or an unbounded filesystem crawl tool as a substitute for project onboarding.

docs.title: 4.3 Scan the current checkout
docs.text:
The agent resolves "current project" from trusted local runtime context and invokes project scan for the working directory.

For the golden repository-oriented scenario, the preferred selection policy is Git-tracked files.

The scan operation remains owned by scriberig-project and produces a durable manifest containing deterministic project-relative paths, exact source evidence/digests, classification, selected adapter, and diagnostics.

The model does not make one tool call per source file.

docs.title: 4.4 Review the persisted manifest
docs.text:
The agent receives a bounded scan summary and can inspect/list the persisted manifest.

Before import it verifies at least:

  • the canonical root is the intended Scriberig checkout;
  • the manifest is non-empty;
  • expected repository-defining files are present;
  • there are no blocking scan diagnostics.

The import request identifies the exact persisted manifest. Import must not perform a hidden fresh rescan.

docs.title: 4.5 Import and promote S0
docs.text:
The agent invokes the normal project import operation.

Import preserves exact source artifacts, invokes registered domain adapters, records project/source ownership, constructs immutable semantic state, and atomically promotes the project-specific current root according to the existing project transaction rules.

The first successful project snapshot in the scenario is called S0.

docs.title: 4.6 Resolve the active workspace
docs.text:
The agent resolves:

ProjectId P
SnapshotId S0
Root EntityId R

through the normal workspace operation.

The TUI activates that authoritative workspace using the same client/product state contract as human onboarding.

docs.title: 4.7 Semantic smoke check
docs.text:
The agent performs bounded semantic verification using normal operations such as:

inspect(R@S0)
find(P@S0, Cargo.toml or another named project object)
find(P@S0, known Scriberig package/name)
render(...) where useful

The purpose is to prove the imported workspace is semantically useful, not merely that an import status flag changed.

docs.title: 4.8 Durable onboarding result
docs.text:
The branch completes with a compact result equivalent to:

project = P
snapshot = S0
root = R
manifest = M0
outcome = success
important semantic references = [...]

Detailed model/tool traffic remains in durable session history but is not automatically replayed into every future model turn.

docs.title: 5. Phase Boundary — Semantic Scope Becomes Primary
docs.text:
After onboarding, subsequent project work starts from P@S0.

Paths remain useful source/projection metadata, but the agent should discover architecture through semantic find, inspect, follow, query, and render operations where those capabilities represent the requested knowledge.

The second instruction must not silently drop back to an unrelated raw-filesystem workspace with no exact snapshot binding.

docs.title: 6. Phase B — Request PHP Ingestion Support
docs.text:
The user submits:

Add support for ingesting PHP source files.

The continuation records exact context:

project = P
base snapshot = S0

No source change has happened yet.

The semantic definition of done is not simply "recognize .php". A valid implementation must make a PHP file:

  • classify as a first-class PHP/code source;
  • retain exact source evidence;
  • parse through the PHP adapter described by design/level-2/028. php code domain source adapter target.md;
  • produce deterministic semantic code/syntax entities;
  • participate in project ownership/re-import;
  • expose named PHP declarations through common semantic navigation;
  • render its source through normal projection/read operations;
  • fail with structured diagnostics without partially promoting a broken import.

docs.title: 7. Semantic Architecture Discovery Branch
docs.text:
The parent agent starts a read-only child branch whose purpose is to identify the minimal extension points for a new PHP code adapter.

The child branch receives explicitly:

base project P
base snapshot S0
read-only semantic capabilities
expected result = architecture map

It does not receive change/apply capabilities.

The child discovers project guidance and implementation precedent semantically, including as appropriate:

  • repository AGENTS.md guidance;
  • code-domain design and domain adapter conventions;
  • a representative Tree-sitter language adapter such as Python;
  • project scan classification;
  • project adapter dispatch/import mapping;
  • domain conformance helpers;
  • workspace/dependency metadata;
  • relevant tests and capability metadata.

The child returns a compact BranchResult with stable semantic references and required integration points.

The parent does not automatically ingest the child's full transcript.

docs.title: 8. Implementation Branch
docs.text:
The parent starts a second child branch for implementation.

It receives:

project P
exact base S0
architecture references from the discovery result
read + propose + validate capabilities
no normal change.apply capability

Before proposing edits it re-resolves important targets at S0.

The implementation is one coherent project-wide candidate and may contain:

  • a new scriberig-domain-php crate;
  • workspace/package dependency changes;
  • exact parser dependency and lockfile changes;
  • project scan classification change from generic text to PHP;
  • project import dispatch changes;
  • domain/schema/capability metadata;
  • PHP domain tests;
  • project import tests and fixtures;
  • authoritative format documentation when applicable.

The candidate is anchored to S0 and receives stable candidate identity C1.

The live project remains P@S0 and the live checkout remains unchanged.

docs.title: 9. Project-Wide Candidate Contract
docs.text:
The self-hosting scenario requires one candidate to create and update multiple files.

The candidate must retain exact base information and expected source state per affected path.

Required effect kinds are conceptually:

create(path, new content)
update(path, expected base digest/content identity, new content)
delete(path, expected base digest/content identity)

The candidate review model exposes aggregate and per-file semantic/source diffs.

A newly created file is still a projection/source effect owned by the candidate; it is not written early merely because it has no base file.

Detailed mechanics are defined in design/level-2/027. project wide candidate workspaces validation and materialization.md.

docs.title: 10. Validation Sequence
docs.text:
The implementation branch validates C1 against isolated candidate state.

The expected profiles are conceptually:

  1. php-domain-focused
  2. parser/domain tests;
  3. deterministic syntax/source-range tests;
  4. malformed PHP diagnostics;
  5. inline HTML coverage.
  6. project-import-focused
  7. .php scan classification;
  8. exact source preservation;
  9. ownership;
  10. semantic discovery/render;
  11. invalid import atomicity;
  12. unchanged re-import/regression classification.
  13. rust-workspace
  14. repository formatting/check/lint/tests according to current policy.
  15. project-ingestion-e2e
  16. fresh database;
  17. a small PHP project;
  18. scan/import/workspace/find/inspect/render through public operations.

Validation evidence is durable and exact-input-bound.

If a parser dependency must be acquired, dependency resolution is an explicit bounded external capability and the resolved version/lock state becomes candidate content/evidence.

Validation must not modify the live Scriberig checkout.

docs.title: 11. Repair During Validation
docs.text:
A validation failure does not authorize live edits.

The implementation branch inspects structured diagnostics, renders the exact affected candidate/base source context, and creates a revised/superseding candidate through the normal change path.

A complex failure may be delegated to another nested child branch with an explicit bounded capability set.

The final successful implementation result links to the validated candidate and its validation records.

docs.title: 12. Agent Result and Normal Review
docs.text:
The root agent returns a concise terminal result containing a stable candidate reference.

The TUI offers a normal Review candidate action.

The review is the same migration/change review used for non-agent changes and shows at least:

base snapshot S0
candidate C1
created/updated/deleted paths
important semantic contexts
source before/after or unified diffs
validation state
stale/conflict state

Before acceptance:

P.current == S0
live working tree == base
C1 is durable
validation evidence is durable

docs.title: 13. Acceptance and Materialization
docs.text:
The user explicitly chooses the normal Apply action.

The shared application operation verifies:

  • project current snapshot still equals S0;
  • all affected paths remain within the project root;
  • update/delete source digests still match expected base state;
  • create targets do not conflict with unexpected external files;
  • symlink/path-escape rules pass;
  • validation/applicability policy passes.

Application then follows the repository's existing canonical-promotion/external-effect ordering and records effect status truthfully.

On the successful path, the project advances to S1, the accepted project-wide source effects reach disk safely, and the TUI refreshes the authoritative workspace.

No direct TUI or agent file-writing path is involved.

docs.title: 14. Post-Apply Proof
docs.text:
After apply, the scenario must be able to establish:

  • S1 != S0 and P.current == S1;
  • history links S0 -> C1 -> S1 according to normal migration lineage;
  • changed PHP-support source is present in the checkout;
  • historical S0 remains addressable;
  • provenance links the user's request, discovery/implementation branches, candidate, validations, acceptance, and materialization result.

The agent may perform bounded semantic verification against P@S1.

docs.title: 15. Restart Requirement
docs.text:
Exit and restart the TUI against the same database and checkout.

The product must recover enough durable state to inspect:

P@S1
session and branch hierarchy
onboarding result
implementation result
C1
validation records
history/effect status

Replaying original provider streams is not required.

docs.title: 16. Critical Baseline Rule
docs.text:
The repository/build used at the beginning of the golden scenario must not already contain registered first-class PHP ingestion.

Test fixtures may contain the expected PHP extension source or declarative expected edits, but production scan/import dispatch in the baseline must still treat PHP as unsupported/generic according to current policy.

The agent candidate is what adds PHP support to the temporary tested checkout.

Do not satisfy the golden scenario by implementing PHP permanently first and then scripting an agent response that claims to add it.

docs.title: 17. Failure Scenarios
docs.text:
The product-level design must cover at least:

  • onboarding scan failure: no fake active project;
  • import failure: no project snapshot promotion to partial state;
  • exact manifest mismatch/stale request: explicit failure;
  • child branch lacks requested capability: tool is absent/denied, not bypassed;
  • candidate validation failure: current project/tree unchanged;
  • candidate becomes stale: normal stale rules apply;
  • one affected file changes externally before multi-file apply: no silent overwrite of that file or unrelated partial success presented as complete success;
  • materialization failure after canonical state transition: explicit effect/recovery status;
  • provider/tool cancellation: durable failed/cancelled operation, no hidden source mutation;
  • restart after completion: durable references recover.

docs.title: 18. Product Evidence
docs.text:
The final acceptance gate uses:

  • the real built srig executable;
  • an actual PTY;
  • a fresh temporary SQLite database;
  • a copied Scriberig checkout whose baseline lacks PHP ingestion;
  • normal TUI key/input sequences;
  • a deterministic scripted provider configured through normal provider contracts;
  • public application/project/change/validation operations;
  • filesystem assertions before and after Apply;
  • restart assertions.

The provider must not be special-cased in production code on the literal golden prompt.

The product gate must also prove the candidate's PHP implementation by running the required PHP ingestion E2E against the candidate workspace/build, not merely by checking that files named php were added.

docs.title: 19. Implementation Sequence
docs.text:
The corresponding Level 3 tasks intentionally build generic capability before the test-only PHP self-extension:

123 empty-database agent onboarding
124 semantic-first project context and nested discovery
125 project-wide source candidates
126 project-wide candidate validation/apply safety
127 PHP golden extension contract and fixture
128 deterministic self-hosting provider scenario
129 TUI two-command self-hosting workflow
130 real-process self-hosting product gate

Tasks 123 through 126 improve production capability without pre-installing PHP. Tasks 127 and 128 create test/reference material that describes and generates the PHP candidate while preserving the baseline invariant. Tasks 129 and 130 compose the complete scenario.

docs.title: 20. Completion Criteria
docs.text: This Level 2 design is satisfied only when the final real-process gate proves the entire two-command scenario from a fresh project database and a PHP-unaware starting checkout, with no direct database mutation, no agent-only file patch path, no live-tree mutation before acceptance, no hidden partial apply, and durable restartable project/session/history evidence.

docs.title: Project-Wide Candidate Workspaces, Validation, and Materialization
1. Purpose
docs.text:
The first useful project workflow proves a safe candidate change to an existing Rust projection. Self-hosting requires a broader but compatible unit of change: one candidate may create, update, and delete several project files that together implement one capability.

This document extends the existing migration/projection/apply model without introducing a parallel repository patch system.

The target case is an agent-produced candidate that adds a new source-domain crate, updates workspace metadata and project import dispatch, adds tests/fixtures, and may change a lockfile, while leaving the live project and working tree unchanged until explicit acceptance.

docs.title: 2. Core Invariant
docs.text:
A project-wide source change is still one normal candidate/migration based on one exact project snapshot.

Conceptually:

Project P @ S0
    + ordered source effects
    + semantic/reconciliation result
    + provenance
    = Candidate C

Creating C must not:

  • advance P.current;
  • write new files into the live checkout;
  • modify existing live files;
  • delete live files;
  • invent a second canonical patch/history type.

Human and agent callers consume the same candidate APIs.

docs.title: 3. Project Source Effect Model
docs.text: A candidate must be able to express at least three source effect kinds.

docs.title: 3.1 Create
docs.text:
Create {
    relative_path
    new_content or projection content reference
    expected_absence policy
    ownership/projection metadata
}

Create fails normal application if a conflicting external target exists and is not explicitly accounted for by reviewed reconciliation policy.

docs.title: 3.2 Update
docs.text:
Update {
    relative_path
    expected_base_source identity/digest
    new_content or projection result
    ownership/projection metadata
}

The expected base is exact. Apply must not silently update whatever content happens to be on disk later.

docs.title: 3.3 Delete
docs.text:
Delete {
    relative_path
    expected_base_source identity/digest
    ownership/projection metadata
}

Delete must not remove an externally modified or unrelated file merely because its path matches a stale candidate.

The implementation may use existing migration operation types internally. These conceptual effect kinds do not require a second storage model if equivalent semantics already exist.

docs.title: 4. Path and Ownership Rules
docs.text:
Every file effect is project-relative.

Clients and agents do not supply authoritative absolute target paths.

Before candidate creation/application as appropriate, shared projection/filesystem infrastructure enforces:

  • target resolves under the canonical project root;
  • path traversal is rejected;
  • symlink escape is rejected according to existing policy;
  • the effect is associated with the intended project;
  • update/delete targets correspond to expected source/projection ownership where ownership exists;
  • create targets cannot silently replace unrelated pre-existing data.

A candidate that contains one invalid escaping path is rejected rather than partially accepted.

docs.title: 5. Exact Base Binding
docs.text:
The aggregate candidate has one exact project base snapshot.

Each update/delete effect additionally retains enough exact source evidence to detect external divergence at materialization time.

At minimum this is equivalent to:

project_id
base_snapshot_id
relative_path
base source artifact/revision or digest

Create effects retain an expected-absence/precondition state.

Do not use "latest" or "whatever is current" as the base for an already-created candidate.

docs.title: 6. Candidate Semantic State
docs.text:
Where Scriberig can reconcile candidate source into semantic state before acceptance, the candidate/result snapshot contains the semantic result of all effects together.

This is important for changes where one file depends on another, for example:

new domain crate source
+ Cargo.toml workspace/dependency registration
+ project importer reference to the new crate

The candidate must be inspectable as a coherent whole, not as independent file patches whose combined meaning is unknown until after live write-back.

If some source format has only text-level candidate semantics, the candidate may retain source effects without pretending unsupported semantic reconciliation exists. Capability metadata must remain truthful.

docs.title: 7. New File Projection Semantics
docs.text:
A source projection may have no base live file.

Candidate infrastructure therefore needs a representation for proposed new owned output without first creating it in the project checkout.

The projection/render API should be able to answer conceptually:

render candidate C / path crates/.../lib.rs

and return candidate content and provenance even though the path does not yet exist in the live tree.

This proposed projection participates in diff, validation, review, and eventual materialization.

docs.title: 8. Aggregate Diff and Review
docs.text:
The candidate review model exposes both aggregate and per-path information.

Required aggregate data includes:

candidate id
project id
base snapshot
candidate/result snapshot when available
provenance
validation state
stale/conflict state
counts of create/update/delete effects

Per-path review includes:

relative path
effect kind
old content identity/content when applicable
new content identity/content when applicable
semantic context when known
source diff

The TUI/web/client layers may paginate or lazily render large diffs, but the canonical review model is shared.

docs.title: 9. Candidate Workspace
docs.text:
Validation requiring a filesystem view uses an isolated candidate workspace.

Conceptually it is derived from:

base project source state
+ all candidate source effects

Requirements:

  • exact candidate content is what validators see;
  • live project files are not modified;
  • created files appear in the candidate workspace;
  • deleted files are absent there;
  • unaffected project files match the intended base/current validation policy;
  • temporary build outputs stay outside canonical project state;
  • cancellation/failure does not leak a half-materialized live change.

Reuse existing candidate/projection staging infrastructure where possible rather than introducing an unrelated checkout manager.

docs.title: 10. Validation Profiles
docs.text:
Validation remains an application operation associated with an exact candidate.

A profile may compose deterministic checks such as:

semantic reconciliation/invariants
focused unit/integration tests
cargo fmt --check
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy ...
selected cargo test targets
fresh-database project ingestion E2E

The profile name is policy/configuration. Product UI does not hard-code shell execution.

Results are structured and durable, including bounded diagnostics and exact candidate reference.

docs.title: 11. External Process and Dependency Capabilities
docs.text:
Validation may need to execute repository tools.

Process execution must remain bounded by the existing operation/capability model. React/TUI/model-provider code must not directly spawn arbitrary commands merely because the candidate spans multiple files.

A new declared dependency may also require acquisition.

Dependency resolution, when not already satisfied by the build environment, is an explicit capability with bounded intent. It should record sufficient evidence to reproduce what entered the candidate, including exact lockfile/version changes.

This is distinct from granting the model arbitrary network access.

docs.title: 12. Validation Gating
docs.text:
Normal Apply is enabled only when required validation policy is satisfied and the candidate is not stale/conflicted.

For a project-wide candidate, validation success applies to the exact aggregate source state.

Any edit that changes candidate content after validation invalidates or supersedes the prior evidence according to existing exact-input binding rules.

Do not reuse a validation result from a previous set of source effects.

docs.title: 13. Preflight Before Multi-File Materialization
docs.text:
Application must not begin unsafe write-back before evaluating all required preconditions it can check in advance.

For each effect, preflight includes conceptually:

  • project/root containment;
  • path/symlink safety;
  • expected base digest for update/delete;
  • expected absence/conflict state for create;
  • projection ownership expectations;
  • candidate applicability/validation state.

If one effect is already known to conflict, do not apply the other source effects and report overall success.

The chosen external-effect protocol may still have unavoidable failure after canonical promotion or during I/O. Such cases must be represented honestly through receipts/recovery state.

docs.title: 14. Canonical Apply
docs.text:
Candidate acceptance uses the same exact-base compare-and-swap project semantics as existing single-projection changes.

Required aggregate semantics:

candidate.base_snapshot == project.current_snapshot

unless an explicit reviewed rebase/merge created a new candidate.

Application must not silently retarget all file effects to a newer snapshot.

On canonical success, the resulting successor snapshot/history records the one coherent change.

docs.title: 15. Filesystem Materialization
docs.text:
Accepted project-wide source effects are materialized through shared filesystem projection infrastructure.

For updates/creates, use the existing safe atomic-replacement strategy where applicable.

For deletes, preserve the repository's effect/recovery semantics and never remove an externally changed target under stale assumptions.

The operation result exposes aggregate and per-effect state sufficient to distinguish:

not attempted due to precondition conflict
materialized successfully
failed and recoverable/retryable
canonical state advanced but external effect incomplete

Do not reduce a multi-file result to one generic completed boolean that can hide a missing file.

docs.title: 16. Failure Ordering and Recovery
docs.text:
Database canonical promotion and multiple filesystem effects cannot be made literally atomic as one transaction.

Continue using the repository's external-effect receipt/reconciliation architecture.

The multi-file extension must make the chosen ordering and partial-effect recovery explicit.

Recovery must be able to identify exactly which intended paths/effects have been satisfied and which remain divergent.

Retry must remain idempotent/safe with respect to already completed effects.

docs.title: 17. External Conflict Example
docs.text:
Given candidate effects:

Create crates/domains/scriberig-domain-php/src/lib.rs
Update Cargo.toml from digest A
Update crates/scriberig-project/src/adapters.rs from digest B

if an external process edits Cargo.toml after candidate creation, Apply must not silently overwrite that edit and then report the whole project-wide candidate as successfully materialized.

The user must see a stale/conflict/reconciliation-required state and retain the external content.

docs.title: 18. Provenance
docs.text:
The aggregate candidate records normal provenance such as:

initiating principal
surface
session/branch/operation for agent changes
base project/snapshot

Per-path effects need not each create an independent history lineage unless the existing model requires it, but review/history must make their membership in the accepted migration clear.

Agent-generated and human-generated project-wide candidates remain structurally equivalent after initiation.

docs.title: 19. Protocol and Client Contract
docs.text:
Public application/protocol/client APIs must be able to:

create/propose a project-wide candidate
inspect its aggregate metadata
page/list changed paths
render per-path candidate source/diff
start/observe validation
apply through shared operation
inspect per-path external-effect result

Do not require clients to upload an opaque git patch as the canonical API if the server cannot validate project/path/source preconditions from it.

A textual patch may be a transient representation converted into shared candidate effects.

docs.title: 20. TUI Contract
docs.text:
The native TUI review view must scale from one file to a project-wide candidate.

It should let the user:

  • see candidate/base/validation state;
  • browse changed paths and effect kinds;
  • open old/new or unified diffs;
  • see important semantic labels where available;
  • invoke normal Apply only when allowed;
  • inspect conflict/effect-recovery state after Apply.

No full IDE multi-file editor is required for this milestone; the agent may be the producer of the candidate.

docs.title: 21. Cross-Surface Equivalence
docs.text:
Embedded application, remote protocol/client, TUI, web, and agent adapters must identify the same candidate and effects.

Do not create a TUI-only repository patch structure for the self-hosting test.

The reference web application may gain project-wide review affordances later or concurrently, but the canonical model/API must already be reusable by it.

docs.title: 22. Required Conformance Cases
docs.text: The implementation should provide reusable tests equivalent to:

docs.title: PROJECT-CANDIDATE-01 — create + update
docs.text: Create a candidate that adds a new source file and updates an existing manifest/config file. Assert current snapshot/tree unchanged and candidate render contains both changes.

docs.title: PROJECT-CANDIDATE-02 — delete
docs.text: Create a candidate deleting an owned source file. Assert live file remains until Apply.

docs.title: PROJECT-CANDIDATE-03 — aggregate diff
docs.text: Inspect candidate through public API and verify effect kinds/paths/source diffs.

docs.title: PROJECT-VALIDATE-01 — exact candidate workspace
docs.text: Run a validator that requires the newly created file and updated metadata together. It must succeed only if the isolated workspace contains the aggregate candidate.

docs.title: PROJECT-VALIDATE-02 — validation does not touch live tree
docs.text: Compare live bytes before/after validation.

docs.title: PROJECT-APPLY-01 — all effects materialize after acceptance
docs.text: Apply a valid candidate and verify successor snapshot plus intended create/update/delete results.

docs.title: PROJECT-CONFLICT-01 — external update conflict
docs.text: Externally modify one update target after candidate creation. Assert no silent overwrite/full-success claim.

docs.title: PROJECT-CONFLICT-02 — create target unexpectedly exists
docs.text: Create the proposed new path externally before Apply. Assert explicit conflict.

docs.title: PROJECT-STALE-01 — project snapshot advances
docs.text: Advance canonical project state after candidate creation and assert exact-base rejection.

docs.title: PROJECT-EFFECT-FAIL-01 — deterministic mid-effect failure
docs.text: Use shared fault injection to prove effect receipts/recovery identify incomplete paths without hiding canonical/external divergence.

docs.title: 23. Non-Goals
docs.text:
This design does not require:

  • replacing Git;
  • generic arbitrary binary patching;
  • transactions that falsely claim SQLite + filesystem atomicity;
  • automatically merging arbitrary external edits;
  • giving agents unrestricted filesystem access;
  • making every source adapter editable;
  • executing user-supplied project commands without validation policy/capability checks.

docs.title: 24. Completion Criteria
docs.text: This subsystem is complete for the self-hosting milestone when one exact-base candidate can safely create a new Rust domain crate, update workspace and importer source, add tests/fixtures, validate the complete candidate in isolation, remain non-current/non-materialized before acceptance, and after explicit acceptance produce one authoritative successor plus truthful safe multi-file materialization/effect state through the existing shared change architecture.

docs.title: PHP Code Domain Source Adapter Target
1. Purpose
docs.text:
This document defines the exact source-domain capability that the golden self-hosting agent is expected to add when the user asks:

Add support for ingesting PHP source files.

It is a target contract, not permission to pre-install PHP support before the self-hosting product gate.

The golden baseline must still lack registered first-class PHP ingestion. Test/reference fixtures may contain the expected candidate implementation described here, but the agent-produced candidate is what introduces PHP support into the temporary tested checkout.

docs.title: 2. Architectural Placement
docs.text:
PHP is a language-specific specialization of Scriberig's shared source/code domain.

The expected dependency direction is:

PHP source bytes
    -> PHP parser/adapter
    -> PHP document + deterministic syntax/code facts
    -> shared code-domain concepts
    -> universal graph/project ownership

The PHP adapter must not introduce a private database, private query engine, or PHP-specific project catalog.

The expected production crate shape produced by the golden candidate is equivalent to:

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-php/

and should follow the conventions used by existing language domain crates, especially a Tree-sitter-based source adapter such as Python where appropriate.

docs.title: 3. File Classification
docs.text:
The minimum required project extension is:

.php

A scanned .php file must be classified as a first-class PHP/code source and assigned the PHP adapter in the persisted project manifest.

Classification is decided during scan and retained in the manifest. Import must consume that decision rather than independently re-guessing the format from a fresh filesystem read.

The golden candidate must include regression coverage proving that unrelated source extensions keep their existing adapter choices.

Do not silently broaden the milestone to every PHP-adjacent extension unless repository policy explicitly adds them.

docs.title: 4. Exact Source Evidence
docs.text:
Before or alongside semantic parsing, project import retains the exact source artifact according to existing project ingestion conventions.

For every PHP source this includes at least:

project ownership
project-relative path
exact bytes
content digest
classification/media metadata
PHP adapter identity/version

Semantic PHP structure is additional knowledge. It does not replace exact source evidence.

All imported semantic PHP entities retain provenance to the exact source artifact/import that produced them.

docs.title: 5. Parser Strategy
docs.text:
The golden target should use a mature inert PHP parser compatible with the repository's deterministic syntax-domain architecture.

A Tree-sitter PHP grammar is the preferred target because it aligns with existing complete-syntax-tree adapters and supports PHP mixed with inline HTML.

The exact dependency version must be pinned/resolved through normal Cargo metadata and lockfile policy.

The parser is an implementation dependency, not a semantic identity exposed to clients beyond normal adapter/version provenance.

docs.title: 6. Inert Parsing
docs.text:
Importing PHP is parsing, not executing PHP.

The adapter must never, as part of ingestion:

  • execute the PHP program;
  • evaluate expressions for side effects;
  • follow include/require by executing them;
  • load Composer autoloaders;
  • run project scripts;
  • make network requests because source code asks it to;
  • contact application endpoints embedded in code;
  • resolve remote resources as an execution side effect.

Any later derived analyzer that intentionally resolves dependencies is a separate capability with separate trust/provenance rules.

docs.title: 7. PHP Document Model
docs.text:
The language adapter exposes a versioned root document concept equivalent to:

PhpDocument {
    adapter/schema metadata
    serialized complete syntax tree
    deterministic ordered syntax-node records
    source metadata
}

Use repository domain schema/version conventions instead of inventing ad-hoc unversioned property names.

The document should participate in the shared code-domain/source-document concepts where applicable.

docs.title: 8. Complete Syntax Preservation
docs.text:
The adapter must preserve complete deterministic syntax structure, not merely extract top-level symbol names.

For every syntax node where the existing source-domain pattern represents node entities, retain information equivalent to:

deterministic structural/node path
node kind
named flag
missing/error state
byte start/end
line/column start/end
parent/child ordering
field relationship when available
leaf/source text when appropriate
comment information

Unnamed nodes may be required to preserve faithful syntax and must not be discarded merely because they are not useful navigation labels.

Repeated parsing of identical source bytes must produce semantically equivalent serialized tree structure and deterministic traversal ordering.

docs.title: 9. Stable Node and Entity Identity
docs.text:
Imported PHP children use the repository's deterministic domain/project identity conventions.

Identity must not depend on:

  • random UUID generation for each parse;
  • nondeterministic filesystem enumeration order;
  • hash-map iteration order;
  • absolute machine-specific paths where project-relative ownership suffices.

Unchanged re-import should preserve semantic equivalence and stable identities wherever the domain identity policy promises continuity.

docs.title: 10. Source Ranges
docs.text:
Syntax/code records expose exact ranges needed for inspection and source projection:

byte start/end
start row/column
end row/column

Range conventions must be consistent with existing code-domain adapters.

These mappings must be sufficient for a common source renderer/client to identify where a named PHP declaration came from without parsing PHP privately in the frontend.

docs.title: 11. Comments
docs.text:
PHP comments are source knowledge and should remain represented through syntax and/or shared code-domain comment metadata according to existing adapter conventions.

Coverage should include the comment forms supported by the chosen grammar, including representative line and block comments.

Do not strip comments before constructing the canonical PHP syntax representation.

docs.title: 12. Named Declaration Metadata
docs.text:
In addition to complete syntax, the adapter should expose human-meaningful metadata for important named PHP declarations through the shared code navigation model where practical.

The golden target includes at least:

namespace
class
interface
trait
enum when supported by the grammar/version
function
method

For these concepts, clients should be able to obtain a display name/kind/source path/range/containment context through public semantic data rather than reparsing the serialized PHP tree.

Lower-level syntax remains available for raw knowledge inspection.

docs.title: 13. Inline HTML
docs.text:
A normal PHP source file may contain text/HTML around PHP code blocks.

Representative valid input:

<html>
<body>
<?php
function title(): string {
    return "Scriberig";
}
?>
</body>
</html>

The chosen grammar/adapter must treat this as legitimate PHP source according to parser semantics and retain the complete parse structure, including surrounding inline content represented by the grammar.

Do not assume every .php file begins with <?php and contains only PHP syntax until EOF.

docs.title: 14. UTF-8 and Decode Failures
docs.text:
Follow existing code adapter policy for source decoding.

If the PHP adapter requires UTF-8 input and exact bytes cannot be decoded as required, return the normal structured adapter diagnostic at the decode stage rather than lossy silent substitution.

Exact source bytes remain captured according to project import/error evidence policy.

docs.title: 15. Parse Error Semantics
docs.text:
Malformed PHP must not be presented as a successfully trusted PhpDocument merely because the parser could construct a partial error tree.

The adapter returns a structured diagnostic equivalent to:

path
adapter = php
stage = parse
code/category
message
source range/position when available
retryability

The project importer associates that diagnostic with the exact source artifact.

When PHP semantic parsing is required for the manifest-selected adapter, the project import does not silently promote a partial successor that omits/buries the PHP failure.

The previous valid project snapshot remains authoritative.

docs.title: 16. Project Import Mapping
docs.text:
For a valid PHP source artifact, project import creates ordinary universal/domain records equivalent to:

project source artifact
    -> PHP document entity/revision
        -> deterministic PHP syntax/code entities

Every imported entity that belongs to the file participates in normal source-relative project ownership so later re-import/deletion reconciliation can identify what the source contributed.

Do not create a PHP-only ownership table that project cleanup cannot understand.

docs.title: 17. Common Semantic Discovery
docs.text:
After importing a PHP fixture containing Greeter::greet, public semantic operations must be able to discover and inspect those named declarations through the same shared navigation/query model used for other code domains.

Conceptually:

find(project@S, name="Greeter", kind=class)
find(project@S, name="greet", kind=method)
inspect(Greeter@S)
inspect(greet@S)
render(source for relevant document/selection)
follow(source provenance)

The test must not pass solely because raw text search can find the token Greeter.

PHP must not require a private PHP-specific query universe for basic named navigation.

docs.title: 18. Source Projection
docs.text:
At minimum, imported PHP source supports a truthful read/source projection that returns:

project/snapshot identity
source-relative path
exact or faithful source text
semantic/source mapping for supported selected entities
read/write capability metadata

Bidirectional PHP editing is not required by this self-hosting milestone.

If the projection is read-only, advertise it as read-only rather than pretending reconciliation/apply support exists.

docs.title: 19. Domain Capability Metadata
docs.text:
Inspecting PHP domain objects should reveal relevant shared capabilities through the domain/capability registry.

Examples include:

inspect
list/follow syntax or containment
find named declarations
render source
follow provenance

The PHP adapter/schema version must participate in the repository's normal domain version metadata so imported results can explain which adapter version produced them.

docs.title: 20. Workspace and Dependency Integration
docs.text:
The golden candidate is expected to update normal Rust workspace metadata so the new domain crate compiles and scriberig-project can call it.

Likely candidate areas include:

Cargo.toml
Cargo.lock
crates/domains/scriberig-domain-php/**
crates/scriberig-project/**
capabilities.toml or domain/format registry metadata where authoritative
relevant test fixtures/documentation
