Follow actual repository ownership rather than duplicating extension lists across every product surface.

TUI/web/CLI should consume the project service result; they do not each implement .php classification independently.

docs.title: 21. Required Domain Tests
docs.text: The candidate must include focused tests equivalent to:

docs.title: PHP-DOMAIN-01 — declarations
docs.text: Parse a fixture containing namespace, class, method, and free function. Assert root/document, named declaration metadata, ranges, and deterministic node order.

docs.title: PHP-DOMAIN-02 — comments
docs.text: Assert representative PHP comments survive syntax/semantic import.

docs.title: PHP-DOMAIN-03 — nested syntax
docs.text: Use nested control flow/expressions and prove the adapter retains complete structure rather than only top-level declarations.

docs.title: PHP-DOMAIN-04 — inline HTML
docs.text: Parse mixed HTML/PHP input and verify complete successful structure plus discoverable PHP function/declaration.

docs.title: PHP-DOMAIN-05 — malformed input
docs.text: Use deterministic invalid PHP and assert structured parse failure/position with no trusted successful document result.

docs.title: PHP-DOMAIN-06 — deterministic output
docs.text: Parse identical bytes repeatedly and compare normalized serialized tree/node ordering and deterministic identity inputs.

docs.title: PHP-IMPORT-01 — classification
docs.text: Scan a project containing src/example.php. Persisted manifest selects the PHP adapter.

docs.title: PHP-IMPORT-02 — exact source preservation
docs.text: Import valid PHP. Exact bytes/digest on the source artifact match input.

docs.title: PHP-IMPORT-03 — ownership
docs.text: PHP document and syntax/code entities are owned by the correct project and relative source path.

docs.title: PHP-IMPORT-04 — semantic discovery
docs.text: Use public semantic operations to find a known class and method. Do not use private database queries or raw grep as the proof.

docs.title: PHP-IMPORT-05 — source projection
docs.text: Render the imported PHP source at the exact project snapshot and verify correct path/text/mapping.

docs.title: PHP-IMPORT-06 — malformed file blocks clean promotion
docs.text: Starting from a valid imported project snapshot, scan/import malformed PHP and assert structured diagnostic plus unchanged authoritative prior snapshot.

docs.title: PHP-IMPORT-07 — unchanged re-import
docs.text: Rescan/reimport unchanged valid PHP and verify idempotent semantic equivalence/stable ownership according to project invariants.

docs.title: PHP-IMPORT-08 — deletion reconciliation
docs.text: Remove the PHP source, rescan/import, and assert only entities owned by that source/project are reconciled away.

docs.title: 23. Classification Regression Matrix
docs.text:
Adding PHP must not steal unrelated files from existing adapters.

At minimum retain coverage equivalent to:

.rs -> Rust
.py/.pyi/.pyw -> Python
.ts/.tsx -> TypeScript
.js/... -> JavaScript
.c/.h/... -> current C/C++ policy
.md -> Markdown
.toml/json/yaml -> structured-data policy
unknown UTF-8 -> generic text policy
binary/non-UTF-8 -> binary policy as applicable
.php -> PHP after candidate

The baseline before the agent candidate intentionally does not make the final .php -> PHP assertion true.

docs.title: 24. Fresh-Database PHP E2E
docs.text:
The most important candidate validation creates a fresh database and a small standalone project such as:

php-golden/
  README.md
  src/Greeter.php

Then, using public project/semantic operations:

scan
review persisted manifest
import
workspace resolve
find Greeter
find greet
inspect/render

Expected result:

  • .php classified by the candidate's PHP adapter;
  • exact source retained;
  • semantic PHP structure created;
  • class/method discoverable;
  • source projection renders;
  • no blocking diagnostics.

This test must execute against the candidate workspace/build so it proves the proposed PHP feature actually composes before user acceptance.

docs.title: 25. Golden Baseline Fixture Rule
docs.text:
Repository test data may include:

  • expected PHP source fixtures;
  • declarative expected candidate file list;
  • scripted-provider instructions;
  • expected source snippets or complete test-only files needed to construct the candidate;
  • validation assertions.

It must not register the PHP adapter in the normal baseline runtime before the scenario begins.

If a future unrelated change adds first-class PHP support permanently, this golden scenario must deliberately choose another absent format or preserve an explicit historical/baseline fixture. For the present milestone, PHP is the required absent format.

docs.title: 26. Non-Goals
docs.text:
The PHP target does not require:

  • executing PHP;
  • Composer dependency resolution during import;
  • PHP type inference;
  • cross-file symbol resolution;
  • a PHP compiler/interpreter integration;
  • bidirectional PHP source reconciliation/editing;
  • LSP functionality;
  • formatting PHP;
  • interpreting templates beyond syntax represented by the chosen grammar.

Those may be later derived/domain capabilities.

docs.title: 27. Completion Criteria
docs.text: The PHP extension target is satisfied when the agent-produced project-wide candidate can add a versioned inert PHP code adapter that preserves complete deterministic syntax and source evidence, integrates .php into normal scan/import/ownership/navigation/rendering, rejects malformed PHP with structured non-promoting diagnostics, passes focused and fresh-database integration tests, and remains an ordinary Scriberig domain extension rather than a PHP-specific product path.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
Follow the trust boundary in Level 1 document 013 and the provider/session boundaries in Level 2 documents 023 and 024. scriberig-secrets is an Apache-2.0 reusable crate without semantic storage or runtime dependencies.

Configuration contains an atomic nullable credential reference with a tagged source: keyring plus name, environment plus name, or file plus an absolute path. Normalize api_key_env aliases within each source layer. Conflicting aliases fail before merging. No inline values or interpolation.

Credential use requires an exact normalized base URL, canonical project root, provider purpose, and execution mode binding in a protected user registry. System policy, when present, is a second mandatory allowlist. A project cannot write either policy. Explicit CLI environment-reference and base-URL pairs may grant a process-local binding, subject to system restrictions. Bindings are checked before reading a credential or making a network request.

docs.title: Storage and lifecycle
docs.text:
Use Windows Credential Manager, Apple Keychain, or Linux Secret Service with explicit platform features. Headless deployments may use environment or protected mounted-file references. Backend failure never selects plaintext. Protected buffers zeroize on drop; HTTP-library copies are outside that promise.

Registry metadata lives at the conventional user config directory under secrets/registry.json. System restrictions live under the corresponding system directory at secrets/policy.json. Atomic registry replacement is serialized by an OS file lock in the protected directory. No values or value hashes enter the registry. Lifecycle failures must leave authorization disabled or report an actionable partial operation. Management is local CLI only.

HTTPS is mandatory except explicitly bound numeric loopback HTTP. URLs cannot contain user information, queries, or fragments. Redirects are disabled for streaming and buffered calls. Resolve again before each request for rotation.

docs.title: Disclosure boundaries
docs.text: No value enters sessions, protocol DTOs, events, model context, fingerprints, configuration output, or audit metadata. Only safe categories leave adapters. Known sensitive files and registered secret paths are excluded at scan, import, candidate, and project-copy boundaries. Child processes receive an allowlisted environment. Arbitrary code under the credential owner's OS identity remains outside this protection: untrusted builds require a separate isolated identity.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text: Legacy environment flags remain supported. Implicit credentials combined with project-selected destinations require a binding. Existing stored secrets need issuer-side rotation and an explicit database/backup purge or rebuild procedure; immutable history must never be silently rewritten.

docs.title: Agent Profile, Context Component, and Prompt Experiment Runtime
1. Purpose
docs.text:
This document turns design/level-1/021. agent profiles context composition and evidence driven optimization.md into concrete subsystem boundaries and data-flow requirements.

It also refines the model/context portions of:

  • design/level-2/023. agent runtime model provider and branch orchestration.md;
  • design/level-2/025. provider continuation and observable model execution.md;
  • design/level-1/017. recursive agent decomposition and context isolation.md;
  • design/level-1/018. durable plans dependency scheduling and multi-model execution.md.

The controlling rule is:

Scriberig resolves a versioned agent profile into typed context components, activates only the components relevant to the exact branch invocation, compiles them with semantic/session state into the provider-neutral effective request, and records enough provenance to reproduce and evaluate that behavior.

The first implementation must improve ordinary branch behavior before attempting autonomous prompt optimization.

docs.title: 2. Current Implementation Baseline
docs.text: As of this design revision, the current implementation already provides important pieces that must be reused rather than replaced.

docs.title: scriberig-session
docs.text:
Branch owns durable branch activity and has parent, purpose, turns, model/tool evidence, status, and optional BranchResult.

BranchResult already contains:

status
summary
result_kind
references
result_handles
touched
produced_changes
validations
unresolved_questions

docs.title: scriberig-app
docs.text:
The local child completion path stores the child executor's final output as:

AgentOutput.text
BranchResult.summary
AgentResult.final_output

It then marks the child branch completed.

There is no separate branch-summarization model call in this path.

docs.title: native child runtime
docs.text:
The integrated delegate capability creates a durable child branch, runs the model/tool loop, completes the branch, and returns a compact ChildResult containing the completed output plus stable handles.

The current code calls this subsystem a child-agent runtime in some identifiers. New code should avoid deriving semantic agent identity from those historical names.

docs.title: scriberig-agent-runtime
docs.text:
The current context compiler already produces a deterministic provider-neutral CompiledContext from BranchExecutionContext and records canonical context text plus exact dependencies/omitted handles.

The existing system instruction is intentionally small but currently too weak to carry the Scriberig behavior invariants and non-root handoff contract defined by Level 1.

These existing owners remain authoritative. Do not add a second branch store, prompt compiler, child completion mechanism, or model loop.

docs.title: 3. Ownership Boundaries
docs.text: Keep the current dependency direction.

docs.title: scriberig-agent-core
docs.text:
Own provider-neutral reusable descriptors/value types for concepts such as:

AgentProfileDescriptor
AgentProfileRevisionRef
ContextComponentDescriptor
ContextComponentRevisionRef
ContextComponentKind
ContextActivationRule
ResolvedContextComponent

Only place types here when they are reusable independently of concrete HTTP/provider execution.

This crate must not own network execution or product UI policy.

docs.title: scriberig-agent-runtime
docs.text:
Own:

profile resolution for one invocation
context-component activation
ordering/composition into effective context
branch-role behavior selection
request/profile/component fingerprint contribution
provider-neutral execution-time prompt provenance
experiment probe execution support where runtime-specific

It must not become the canonical semantic store for profiles/lessons/experiments.

docs.title: scriberig-session
docs.text:
Continue to own durable session/branch/model/tool/result execution history.

Add session references to exact effective profile/component identities when that provenance belongs to a model invocation, but do not make reusable global profiles children of a session merely for convenience.

docs.title: shared semantic/application layer
docs.text:
Canonical reusable profile/component/lesson/experiment state is structured semantic knowledge exposed through shared application operations.

The exact storage adapter may evolve, but the API must preserve stable identities and immutable revisions rather than treating TOML/Markdown prompt files as canonical.

docs.title: product surfaces
docs.text: TUI/web/CLI/server may select, inspect, compare, or request authorized changes to profiles. They do not assemble prompt strings or independently decide component activation.

docs.title: 4. Terminology and Runtime Identity
docs.text:
Introduce or document these concepts without inventing duplicate global identity systems:

BranchRef
  canonical session-tree context scope

ExecutorAssignment
  resolved owner/model/profile configuration for a branch or invocation

AgentProfileRef
  stable profile identity + exact revision

ContextComponentRef
  stable component identity + exact revision

ModelInvocation
  one request/response step

A child branch with the same resolved executor/profile remains the same logical executor operating under another context frame.

A branch with a different explicit assignment is still the same kind of branch; only its ExecutorAssignment differs.

Do not add AgentId merely to rename BranchId.

docs.title: 5. Branch Role Must Be Explicit in Context Compilation
docs.text:
The context compiler needs enough information to distinguish root user-facing execution from non-root parent-handoff execution.

Prefer an explicit provider-neutral value rather than heuristics based on prompt text.

A minimal shape is conceptually:

BranchRole
  Root
  NonRoot { parent_branch }

or an equivalent parent-aware representation already available in session context.

BranchExecutionContext or its replacement must expose the branch role to component activation.

Do not infer non-root status from:

  • title strings such as delegated agent branch;
  • operation names;
  • provider continuation presence;
  • model/profile differences;
  • TUI indentation.

docs.title: 6. Agent Profile Shape
docs.text:
Define a provider-neutral profile descriptor conceptually equivalent to:

AgentProfileDescriptor
  identity
  revision
  name
  description
  components: ordered component refs
  context_policy
  optional execution-policy refs
  status

The first implementation may ship a built-in default profile whose identity/revision is deterministic.

That built-in profile is a bootstrap source, not an excuse to make literal source-code strings the permanent canonical architecture.

When durable semantic profile CRUD arrives, the built-in profile may be imported/materialized as normal semantic state while preserving behavior and revision identity.

docs.title: 7. Context Component Shape
docs.text:
Define components conceptually equivalent to:

ContextComponentDescriptor
  identity
  revision
  kind
  content
  activation
  scope
  priority
  provenance
  status

Initial kind values should cover:

CoreInvariant
BehaviorPolicy
DomainGuidance
ToolGuidance
SkillTrigger
ExecutionLesson

Do not require every kind to be fully persisted/authorable in the first code change. The enum/data model should leave room for the complete architecture without forcing speculative UI.

content is provider-neutral instructional content. It is not assumed to be one provider's system wire field.

docs.title: 8. Activation Rules
docs.text:
Activation must be deterministic and testable.

Initial rules may include concepts equivalent to:

Always
RootOnly
NonRootOnly
Domain(domain_id/kind)
Capability(capability_id)
Tool(tool_id)
BranchPolicy(policy_id)
Explicit

Do not introduce a general scripting language for activation in the first implementation.

A component activates only from explicit, inspectable invocation state.

Activation evaluation must not read arbitrary wall-clock mutable globals after the effective invocation configuration is snapshotted.

docs.title: 9. Default Profile Components
docs.text: The bootstrap/default profile should be composed from at least two separate components.

docs.title: Core Scriberig invariant component
docs.text:
Meaning equivalent to:

Operate inside the current Scriberig branch/context frame.
Prefer semantic/domain operations over raw file mutation for understood domains.
Treat files as projections where the domain is understood.
Use the shared candidate/migration/validation/promotion path for canonical change.
Use stable semantic handles and exact revisions/snapshots when exact state matters.
Use child branches for focused isolation when useful; branch creation alone does not imply a new agent.
Parents/dependencies consume compact durable results rather than child transcripts.
Use capabilities progressively.

Activation: Always.

docs.title: Non-root branch handoff component
docs.text:
Meaning equivalent to:

When you are about to finish this non-root branch, make the final response a compact one-paragraph summary for the parent. Include the important outcome, decisions/discoveries, remaining issues, and durable semantic/result handles the parent may need. Do not reproduce the branch transcript or hidden reasoning.

Activation: NonRootOnly.

Do not put the non-root instruction into root requests.

docs.title: 10. Context Compilation Order
docs.text:
The compiler should expose stable typed sections even if a provider later flattens them.

Use an ordering equivalent to:

1. activated core invariants
2. activated behavior policies
3. branch role/purpose and branch-specific contract
4. accepted ancestor/dependency BranchResults and decisions
5. exact semantic/project scope
6. current user/delegation instruction
7. bounded branch-local activity/history
8. activated domain/tool/skill guidance where appropriate
9. capability/tool definitions

The exact provider message roles may differ. The provider-neutral order and identities must be deterministic.

Avoid duplicated prose when a tool descriptor or deterministic runtime rule already communicates the behavior.

docs.title: 11. Parent/Child Context Frame Semantics
docs.text:
The runtime should make this invariant testable:

parent effective context = X
enter child B
child effective context = compile(X-compatible selected inheritance + B-local frame)
finish child -> BranchResult BR
resume parent = compile(parent state + selected BR)

This does not require byte-identical replay of X in the child.

The child compiler selects from canonical state. Unrelated parent turns and sibling histories remain omitted unless explicitly selected by policy.

The parent must not gain child model/tool history simply because the child completed.

If the parent needs more detail, it uses the stable child/result reference to inspect it.

docs.title: 12. Branch Completion Contract
docs.text:
Keep the current completion flow: final executor output becomes the source of the child BranchResult.summary.

Do not add an automatic second summarization invocation.

The runtime/application boundary should validate only mechanical requirements that can be checked without pretending to understand prose, for example:

non-empty final output for successful child branch
result handles remain separately preserved
branch result status matches terminal branch status

Do not reject a useful result solely because it is two paragraphs instead of one. The paragraph rule is model behavior guidance, while structured result integrity is runtime policy.

Future optional quality policy may flag poor summaries without corrupting branch completion.

docs.title: 13. Exact Profile/Component Provenance in Model Invocation
docs.text:
Each model invocation must be attributable to the effective profile revision and activated component revisions.

Extend existing invocation/request provenance rather than adding a separate trace store.

Conceptually retain:

agent_profile: AgentProfileRevisionRef
activated_context_components: [ContextComponentRevisionRef]
context_fingerprint
canonical effective request reference/projection

If the complete-request work from task 136 introduces a canonical request record first, attach these fields there and reference them from ModelInvocation rather than duplicating payloads.

The request fingerprint must change when output-relevant profile/component revisions or activation differ.

docs.title: 14. Compatibility with Provider Continuation
docs.text:
Task 136 / Level-2 provider-continuation design remains authoritative for provider state.

Profile/component activation contributes to context lineage.

Consequences:

  • changing an active behavior component may stale a provider continuation;
  • child continuation remains branch-local even when the same executor/profile enters the child;
  • returning from a child uses compatible parent continuation if it still represents parent lineage, otherwise reseeds from canonical parent context;
  • no provider conversation rewind is assumed;
  • full prompt inspection reports the effective profile/component revisions independently from provider wire optimization.

docs.title: 15. Learned Execution Lessons
docs.text:
Represent learned guidance as derived semantic knowledge, not as an append-only text memory.

A durable lesson contract should contain or reference:

identity + immutable revision
cue
lesson/guidance
applicability scope
source experiment
supporting evidence refs
confidence
producer provenance
status: candidate/accepted/superseded/rejected or equivalent

Lesson activation uses the same deterministic component pipeline after a lesson is accepted for use.

Candidate lessons are not automatically injected merely because one model proposed them.

Exact task/project facts remain bound to their original semantic revisions/snapshots and are not generalized into lessons without explicit evidence/derivation.

docs.title: 16. Prompt Experiment Model
docs.text:
Add a durable structured representation conceptually equivalent to:

PromptExperiment
  identity
  base_profile_revision
  evaluation_case/task/branch refs
  candidate_profile_revisions
  probe branch refs
  probe BranchResult refs
  validation refs
  behavioral contrast records
  composition decision
  attribution records
  status

and:

PromptAttribution
  component/candidate ref
  assessment: Helped | Hurt | NoObservedEffect | Confounded
  evidence refs
  note/summary

Do not encode the experiment only as a coordinator transcript.

These entities may initially be internal/application types if the universal semantic schema integration needs a separate migration, but the public contract must be stable enough to move into canonical semantic storage without reparsing prose.

docs.title: 17. Propose-Probe-Compose Execution
docs.text:
Implement optimization through normal plan/branch machinery when automatic experiments are enabled.

A minimal experiment plan is:

Experiment coordinator
  |
  +-- baseline probe
  |     profile = base revision
  |
  +-- candidate proposal A
  |     -> candidate profile revision A
  |     -> probe A
  |
  +-- candidate proposal B (optional)
  |     -> candidate profile revision B
  |     -> probe B
  |
  +-- compose/evaluate
        depends_on baseline + candidate probes
        consumes compact BranchResults + validations
        emits keep-base or selected candidate + attribution

Candidate probes should use equivalent task/base semantic state wherever meaningful.

Do not let the candidate proposer modify the live profile before probing.

The composer receives identities/results/evidence, not full hidden candidate transcripts by default.

docs.title: 18. Evidence Rules
docs.text:
Automated candidate creation should point to an observed execution moment or explicit evaluation case.

Prefer evidence in roughly this order when applicable:

repeated deterministic validation failure/success
repeated base behavioral failure with candidate correction
clear behavioral divergence tied to the changed component
single-run behavioral improvement
visible plausible risk without observed failure

A candidate may choose KEEP_BASE/no change.

Do not treat model agreement as independent proof when the models share the same evidence or prompt lineage.

When causality is not isolated, attribution is Confounded rather than forced positive/negative credit.

docs.title: 19. Profile Mutation and Promotion
docs.text:
Profile/context-component changes must use shared semantic change semantics.

The lower-level operation shape should be equivalent to:

inspect current profile revision
create candidate component/profile revision
validate structural invariants
run configured probes/validators
review evidence/policy
promote selected candidate
retain rejected alternatives/history

Raw edits to a prompt Markdown/TOML/source file may exist only as bootstrap/interoperability mechanisms until the semantic profile domain is available.

Do not make filesystem text the source of truth for automated optimization.

docs.title: 20. Public Application Operations
docs.text:
As the semantic profile domain becomes durable, expose shared operations rather than UI-specific mutation.

Likely operations include concepts equivalent to:

agent_profile.inspect
agent_profile.list
agent_profile.resolve
agent_profile.propose_change
agent_profile.validate_candidate
agent_profile.promote
prompt_experiment.inspect
prompt_experiment.start
prompt_experiment.status
execution_lesson.inspect/list

Names may follow existing application naming conventions discovered during implementation.

Do not add all operations speculatively if the first Level-3 slice only needs resolution and inspection.

docs.title: 21. Cross-Surface Behavior
docs.text:
All product surfaces consume the same resolved effective profile/context semantics.

The TUI or web may display something like:

Profile: default@R7
Activated guidance:
  core-invariants@R3
  non-root-handoff@R2
  rust-domain-guidance@R9

but that is a presentation over shared provenance.

Changing prompt visibility or expanding component detail must not rerun the model or change activation.

Profile selection changes future execution configuration according to existing branch/session/plan assignment rules; it does not retroactively mutate historical invocations.

docs.title: 22. Caching and Fingerprints
docs.text:
Existing request/context fingerprint machinery should include behaviorally relevant profile/component inputs.

At minimum, cache identity must distinguish:

same text + different profile revision
same profile + different activated component revision
root vs non-root when activation differs
same branch task + changed accepted ExecutionLesson
changed tool/domain guidance that is provider-visible

Do not hash credential values.

Do not use a profile display name alone as cache identity.

docs.title: 23. Tests
docs.text: The implementation needs focused tests at the owning layers.

docs.title: Context compiler tests
docs.text:
Prove:

  • default core invariant component is present;
  • non-root handoff component is present for child context;
  • non-root handoff component is absent for root context;
  • component ordering is deterministic;
  • unrelated inactive components are absent;
  • component revision change changes context/request identity;
  • same exact inputs compile identically;
  • child context does not contain unrelated parent/sibling transcript material.

docs.title: Child execution tests
docs.text:
Prove:

  • child final output becomes BranchResult.summary;
  • returned ChildResult.summary matches durable child result;
  • result handles remain preserved independently of prose summary;
  • ordinary child completion does not cause an extra summarization provider invocation;
  • parent activity contains the child result/handle without copying child model/tool history into parent-local activity.

docs.title: Root execution tests
docs.text:
Prove:

  • root request does not receive the non-root handoff instruction;
  • root output remains unrestricted by child-summary mechanics.

docs.title: Experiment tests
docs.text:
When the experiment layer is implemented, prove:

  • candidates do not mutate the base profile;
  • probes bind exact candidate revisions;
  • compose node waits for required durable results;
  • validation evidence is retained;
  • KeepBase is representable;
  • attribution supports Confounded;
  • promotion creates a new revision and preserves old/rejected revisions.

docs.title: 24. Migration Strategy
docs.text: Implement in layers.

docs.title: Stage 1 — behavior correctness
docs.text: Add branch-role-aware bootstrap profile components and final-handoff guidance using existing runtime/context structures.

docs.title: Stage 2 — explicit versioned resolution
docs.text: Make AgentProfile and ContextComponent descriptors/revisions first-class provider-neutral types and record exact resolution in invocation/effective-request provenance.

docs.title: Stage 3 — semantic persistence
docs.text: Move reusable profiles/components into canonical semantic/application storage if they are still bootstrap literals. Provide projection/import/export as needed.

docs.title: Stage 4 — evidence model
docs.text: Add ExecutionLesson, PromptExperiment, attribution, evidence references, and application inspection operations.

docs.title: Stage 5 — automated optimization
docs.text:
Use durable plans/branches to run propose-probe-compose experiments, validators, candidate promotion, and lesson extraction.

Each stage must leave the system architecturally valid if later stages are not yet implemented.

docs.title: 25. Architectural Prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not:

  • equate child branch identity with new agent identity;
  • add a second model call solely to summarize every child branch;
  • force root user output into a one-paragraph branch-handoff format;
  • copy full parent transcripts to children;
  • copy full child transcripts to parents;
  • implement prompt concatenation independently in TUI/web/server;
  • make mutable Markdown/TOML prompt files canonical learned state;
  • inject every lesson permanently into always-on prose;
  • let an experiment mutate the live base profile before validation/promotion;
  • satisfy experiment dependencies through transcript sharing;
  • use provider conversation identity as profile/branch identity;
  • exclude profile/component revisions from effective prompt observability;
  • expose hidden chain-of-thought as optimization evidence;
  • bypass semantic candidate/validation/promotion because the mutated object is "only a prompt".

docs.title: 26. Definition of Done for the Subsystem
docs.text:
The subsystem is conformant when:

  1. every invocation resolves an exact profile revision;
  2. context components activate deterministically from exact branch/invocation state;
  3. root and non-root behavior contracts are distinct where required;
  4. non-root final output is instructed to be a compact durable handoff and existing completion stores it as BranchResult.summary;
  5. no default second summarizer call exists;
  6. profile/component provenance is visible in the complete safe effective request and affects request identity;
  7. branch creation alone does not imply another executor;
  8. parent context after child completion uses selected durable results, not child transcripts;
  9. profiles/components can evolve into canonical semantic revisions rather than remaining opaque prompt blobs;
  10. prompt experiments and lessons, when enabled, are durable evidence-backed structures using normal branch/plan/change semantics.

docs.title: RPI TUI Adoption and Shared Presentation Migration Plan
docs.text: Superseded ownership target: Level-2 plan 032 is the current authority for final runtime and terminal ownership. This document and tasks 138–143 preserve historical research and implementation evidence only. In particular, the scriberig-tui-kit boundary and Ratatui-based acceptance language below do not authorize retaining a ScribeRig-owned commodity widget layer. The corrective migration must delegate reusable terminal machinery directly to upstream rpi-tui, remove local duplicates, and keep only ScribeRig semantic projections and adapters. Final acceptance is tracked by tasks 144–149.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
This document converts the research and recommendations in design/level-1/022. Adopt TUI.md into an implementation-oriented Level-2 plan for the current Scriberig repository.

It is constrained by the existing Scriberig architecture and by work that landed after the research snapshot. In particular, the repository now already has:

  • crates/scriberig-tui;
  • a Ratatui/Crossterm terminal stack;
  • an event -> action -> reducer -> effect architecture;
  • shared application/protocol/client boundaries;
  • recursive session/plan conversation behavior from tasks 134 and 135;
  • shared agent-console presentation/configuration models;
  • remote-client and web packages.

Therefore this is not a greenfield TUI design and it is not permission to replace Scriberig with the architecture of another coding agent.

The controlling rule is:

Adopt rpi-tui as reusable terminal presentation infrastructure while preserving Scriberig-owned semantic state, recursive sessions, plans, application operations, protocol, change model, and cross-surface behavior.

The plan must reduce locally maintained commodity terminal/editor/rendering code without changing which layer owns meaning.

docs.title: 2. Upward Design Constraints
docs.text:
This plan must preserve the invariants in at least:

  1. design/level-1/001. vision and principles.md;
  2. design/level-1/009. agent interaction and sessions.md;
  3. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md;
  4. design/level-1/014. extensibility ecosystem and licensing.md;
  5. design/level-1/015. terminal user interface principles.md;
  6. design/level-1/017. recursive agent decomposition and context isolation.md;
  7. design/level-1/018. durable plans dependency scheduling and multi-model execution.md;
  8. design/level-1/019. semantic agent operations and projection-first editing.md;
  9. design/level-1/022. Adopt TUI.md.

It also refines, rather than silently replacing:

  • design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md;
  • design/level-2/012. capability matrix and cross surface conformance.md;
  • design/level-2/014. licensing artifacts package metadata and notices.md;
  • design/level-2/017. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md;
  • design/level-2/021. terminal ui runtime and state architecture.md;
  • design/level-2/022. terminal ui views interaction and conformance.md;
  • design/level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md;
  • design/level-2/025. first useful project workflow vertical slice.md.

docs.title: 2.1 What this document changes
docs.text:
021 selected Ratatui/Crossterm because Scriberig needed a working terminal framework. The Level-1 reuse study now provides enough evidence to replace much of that locally owned presentation machinery with rpi-tui components.

This document therefore changes the terminal implementation strategy, not the semantic ownership rules in 021 or the product behavior in 022.

docs.title: 2.2 What this document does not change
docs.text:
This plan does not replace:

  • Scriberig session/branch identity with an upstream transcript/session type;
  • BranchResult with an upstream message summary type;
  • durable plans with an upstream task list;
  • Scriberig model/provider execution with rpi-agent or rpi-harness;
  • semantic operations with upstream file/shell tools;
  • candidate/migration/validation/promotion with upstream write-file behavior;
  • current application/client/protocol contracts with a new UI-only backend;
  • current web packages with a second browser application.

docs.title: 3. Current Baseline and Research Drift
docs.text:
The Level-1 study was written against an earlier repository snapshot and explicitly reported no current scriberig-tui crate. That statement is no longer true and must not guide implementation.

Current main has crates/scriberig-tui with direct dependencies on Ratatui and Crossterm plus shared Scriberig crates. It already contains action/effect/event/state/keymap/layout/rendering and conversation-oriented code.

Tasks 134 and 135 additionally establish that the default TUI is a recursive conversation/tree projection, not the earlier three-pane semantic browser as the ordinary home surface.

The migration must therefore preserve current behavior first and replace implementation pieces underneath it.

A migration agent must begin each task by verifying current repository owners rather than assuming the filenames in this plan remain exact.

docs.title: 4. Adoption Decision
docs.text:
The preferred terminal foundation is rpi-tui from bigfish1913/pi-rust.

Adopt the following categories from it where the current pinned revision proves suitable:

  • terminal lifecycle and normalized terminal input;
  • generic component/text primitives;
  • editor/composer behavior;
  • Markdown rendering;
  • selection/search/fuzzy interaction;
  • theme/style primitives;
  • width/wrapping/Unicode helpers;
  • clipboard support behind Scriberig policy;
  • streaming-friendly rendering patterns.

Use tape_tui only as a design/reference fallback when a specific rpi-tui behavior is insufficient. Do not combine two terminal runtimes casually.

The following remain Scriberig implementations:

  • recursive session/tree projection;
  • reply anchors and continuation semantics;
  • durable plans and dependency DAG rendering;
  • model invocation and reasoning visibility;
  • semantic selection;
  • semantic diff/change review;
  • candidate validation/promotion;
  • capability discovery;
  • application commands and operation lifecycle;
  • local/remote synchronization;
  • provider execution;
  • project/domain semantics.

No production dependency on rpi-agent, rpi-harness, rpi-tools, rpi-extensions, or another upstream coding-agent runtime is introduced by this plan.

docs.title: 5. Upstream Intake and Provenance
docs.text:
Scriberig must pin an exact upstream revision before copying or adapting code.

The default intake layout is:

third_party/
  rpi-tui/
    UPSTREAM.md
    LICENSE
    PATCHES.md
    ... pinned upstream crate source ...

crates/
  scriberig-tui-kit/
    Cargo.toml
    src/
      ... Scriberig-owned adapter/facade ...

If repository/Cargo constraints discovered during task 138 require a materially different vendor location, record that decision in the task before implementation and preserve the same provenance boundary.

UPSTREAM.md must record at least:

upstream repository
exact commit SHA
intake date
upstream crate/path
upstream license at that revision
source acquisition method
local files intentionally omitted, if any

PATCHES.md must describe intentional divergence from the pinned source. It is not a substitute for version control history.

Do not strip upstream copyright/license notices. Follow design/level-2/014. licensing artifacts package metadata and notices.md for repository notices and package metadata.

The vendored source is an implementation dependency, not architectural authority.

docs.title: 6. scriberig-tui-kit Boundary
docs.text:
Introduce a narrow terminal-presentation adapter crate named scriberig-tui-kit unless the implementation audit finds an already existing crate with exactly this responsibility.

Its purpose is to isolate upstream API churn and present Scriberig-owned generic terminal primitives.

It may own concepts equivalent to:

TerminalSession / TerminalGuard
normalized input events
text lines and styled segments
editor state and editor events
selection/list helpers
Markdown-to-safe-terminal-text rendering
theme/style mapping
clipboard facade and policy
terminal capability flags

It must not depend on:

scriberig-session
scriberig-app
scriberig-protocol
scriberig-agent-runtime
scriberig-project
semantic query/change/domain crates

The expected dependency direction is:

pinned rpi-tui source
        |
        v
scriberig-tui-kit
        |
        v
scriberig-tui
        |
        v
apps/scriberig

Shared Scriberig application/domain contracts remain a separate input to scriberig-tui:

scriberig-session / scriberig-app / scriberig-client / scriberig-protocol
                               |
                               v
                        scriberig-tui

Neither scriberig-tui-kit nor the upstream crate may become an owner of Scriberig semantic state.

docs.title: 7. Do Not Create a Parallel scriberig-ui Architecture by Default
docs.text:
The Level-1 study sketched a new scriberig-ui crate, ScriberigUiPort, new presentation snapshots, and HTTP/SSE command/event envelopes. Those sketches express useful separation principles, but the current repository already has shared application, protocol, client, agent-console, and web layers.

The implementation rule is therefore:

Reuse and extend the current shared owner before introducing a second presentation/application contract.

When both TUI and web need a new terminal-independent model, event, preference, or command:

  1. inspect scriberig-app, scriberig-protocol, scriberig-client, scriberig-session, and existing reusable web models;
  2. extend the existing public contract when responsibility fits there;
  3. add protocol serialization only for information that must cross the transport boundary;
  4. create a new shared presentation crate only if the audit demonstrates that existing ownership would otherwise create a dependency cycle or inappropriate product coupling.

A Level-3 task must not create a UiSnapshot, UiCommand, or event stream merely because those names appeared in the research report.

docs.title: 8. Preserve the Existing TUI State Machine
docs.text:
The current event -> action -> reducer -> effect model remains the controlling TUI architecture unless a separately approved design replaces it.

Adopting rpi-tui does not mean moving semantic effects into widgets.

The logical flow remains:

terminal/upstream input
      -> normalized Scriberig TUI event/action
      -> deterministic reducer
      -> TUI-local next state + typed effects
      -> shared application/client operation
      -> result/event action
      -> reducer
      -> render

Commodity upstream components may own their local editor cursor, selection, wrapping, theme, or terminal lifecycle state.

They may not directly:

  • start semantic operations;
  • mutate sessions/plans;
  • call model providers;
  • update project snapshots;
  • apply migrations;
  • bypass capability checks.

Widgets/components emit local actions or Scriberig intents; the existing effect/application boundary performs work.

docs.title: 9. Crossterm and Runtime Coherence
docs.text:
Terminal state is process-global enough that duplicate incompatible Crossterm lines are a correctness risk.

At intake time, audit the pinned rpi-tui dependency graph and Scriberig's current terminal dependencies.

The migration must converge on one compatible Crossterm version for the active TUI path. If the vendored upstream manifest uses an older compatible Crossterm line, adapt the vendored manifest/API calls as an explicit recorded patch rather than shipping two independently active terminal stacks.

Do not run the Ratatui terminal runtime and the rpi-tui terminal runtime simultaneously in one process/terminal session.

During migration, a feature-gated or separately selected legacy renderer is acceptable for rollback, but each actual terminal session has exactly one lifecycle owner.

docs.title: 10. Default Recursive Conversation Surface
docs.text:
Task 134's product behavior remains authoritative.

The adopted terminal foundation must support the existing default home surface:

  • composer focused on launch;
  • recursive structural placement of activity;
  • stable reply anchors;
  • nested branch rails;
  • compact completed child results with optional expansion;
  • plan/dependency state;
  • per-node model/thinking/profile information;
  • streaming model-visible output;
  • independent prompt/reasoning/tool visibility preferences;
  • slash-command access to auxiliary views.

Upstream transcript/message widgets may be reused only as rendering primitives. They must not define the session shape.

The renderer consumes Scriberig's existing recursive projection rows or their current replacement, keyed by stable semantic/session identities.

docs.title: 11. Auxiliary Semantic Views
docs.text:
The TUI must retain auxiliary inspection and control surfaces after the terminal foundation migration.

At minimum preserve access to behaviors equivalent to:

/session
/explorer
/inspect
/history
/diff
/projection
/changes or review
/operations
/models
/help

Exact slash-command names follow current task-134/current-main behavior, not this illustrative list.

These views may use adopted generic selection, Markdown, wrapping, editor, list, and theme primitives, but their data comes from shared Scriberig application/protocol contracts.

Semantic diff generation, validation interpretation, project navigation, branch structure, and capability availability are never delegated to the upstream TUI library.

docs.title: 12. Terminal Safety Policy
docs.text:
All model, tool, compiler, source, document, and external strings are untrusted terminal input.

The adopted rendering path must:

  • prevent untrusted content from becoming executable ANSI/OSC control sequences;
  • distinguish trusted style metadata from external text;
  • normalize or visibly escape unsafe control characters;
  • bound pathological width/wrapping cases;
  • restore terminal modes on normal exit, error, cancellation, and panic paths as far as the platform permits.

Clipboard access is explicit user action and must be disableable by policy/configuration.

Image-terminal protocol support is out of scope for the initial adoption and remains disabled unless a later task explicitly enables and threat-models it.

Do not add native upstream plugin loading as part of this migration.

docs.title: 13. Local and Remote Behavior
docs.text:
The same scriberig-tui state machine must continue to support embedded/local application access and the remote client path where currently implemented.

Do not let the upstream terminal library know whether data came from:

  • in-process application services;
  • scriberig-client;
  • server events;
  • deterministic fixtures.

Reconnect/resume correctness is Scriberig behavior.

Where current protocol already has sequence/cursor/idempotency semantics, reuse them. Where it lacks a behavior required to prevent duplicate side effects or reconstruct presentation state, extend the shared protocol/application design rather than building a TUI-only workaround.

No state-changing command is replayed merely because the terminal reconnected.

docs.title: 14. Web and Cross-Surface Conformance
docs.text:
The Level-1 report correctly requires TUI and browser to consume the same application semantics.

Current web packages remain the browser implementation. This plan does not create another React app.

The migration must strengthen shared conformance by using common deterministic fixtures for concepts such as:

recursive session/branch ordering
plan node status and dependencies
model invocation lifecycle
reasoning/tool visibility preferences
candidate/change status
validation result status
operation lifecycle
stable semantic labels/handles

A terminal-specific renderer may choose different layout and glyphs. It may not invent different semantic state transitions.

When a shared model is missing, add it to the appropriate existing shared owner before teaching each surface to reconstruct it independently.

docs.title: 15. Testing Strategy
docs.text: The adoption is accepted through layers.

docs.title: 15.1 Vendor/adapter tests
docs.text:
Prove:

  • pinned upstream provenance is recorded;
  • the wrapper compiles independently of semantic Scriberig crates;
  • editor, text, Markdown, selection, and theme primitives behave deterministically for fixtures;
  • unsafe control text is escaped/sanitized;
  • no duplicate active Crossterm line exists.

docs.title: 15.2 TUI reducer tests
docs.text:
Existing reducer/action/effect tests remain valuable and should require minimal semantic change.

Prove that changing the terminal foundation does not change:

  • semantic selection identity;
  • navigation anchors;
  • reply anchors;
  • plan coordinator cursor;
  • capability-driven operation dispatch;
  • candidate/review actions.

docs.title: 15.3 Rendering/golden tests
docs.text:
Use deterministic fixtures for:

  • recursive rails;
  • narrow widths;
  • Unicode and combining characters;
  • multiline editor behavior;
  • long Markdown;
  • malformed Markdown;
  • control characters;
  • resize sequences;
  • streaming updates;
  • completed/collapsed branches;
  • plan/dependency state.

docs.title: 15.4 Cross-surface fixtures
docs.text: Replay the same durable/shared event or state fixture through TUI and web/client reducers/models where corresponding reducers exist, and compare semantic outcomes rather than pixel/glyph output.

docs.title: 15.5 Terminal lifecycle E2E
docs.text: Exercise normal exit, Ctrl-C/cancellation, panic/error recovery harnesses, resize, and remote disconnect/reconnect without leaving the terminal unusable or replaying canonical mutations.

docs.title: 16. Ordered Level-3 Execution Plan
docs.text:
Implement this plan through the following Level-3 sheets in order unless the user explicitly authorizes a different sequence:

138  Pin, vendor, and wrap rpi-tui with provenance and dependency isolation
  |
139  Migrate generic terminal primitives and composer/editor infrastructure
  |
140  Migrate the recursive conversation home and streaming presentation
  |
141  Migrate auxiliary semantic views, palette, help, review, and safety policy
  |
142  Align local/remote/web presentation contracts and cross-surface conformance
  |
143  Harden terminal recovery, upstream maintenance, cleanup, and release gates

Each sheet is intentionally independently reviewable and contains its own focused verification commands.

An implementation agent must complete and verify the current sheet, update its checkboxes as work progresses, and only then continue to the next sheet.

docs.title: 17. Rollback Strategy
docs.text:
The migration must remain reversible until final acceptance.

Keep these boundaries intact:

shared Scriberig application/session/protocol semantics
                  |
                  v
          scriberig-tui state machine
                  |
                  v
        terminal presentation adapter
                  |
                  v
            rpi-tui foundation

If the pinned upstream foundation proves unsuitable:

  • remove/replace scriberig-tui-kit and the vendor tree;
  • keep shared session/application/protocol work;
  • keep Scriberig TUI actions/reducer/effects;
  • retain CLI/server/web behavior;
  • use tape_tui or another foundation only through the same adapter boundary.

Do not make a semantic schema or protocol depend on an rpi-tui type.

docs.title: 18. Final Acceptance
docs.text:
The migration is complete only when all of the following are true:

  1. rpi-tui is pinned to an exact reviewed upstream revision with preserved licensing/provenance.
  2. Upstream-specific types are contained behind the terminal-kit boundary except for narrowly documented unavoidable cases.
  3. The active TUI has one terminal lifecycle owner and one compatible Crossterm dependency line.
  4. Current recursive session/plan/reply-anchor behavior remains Scriberig-owned and passes focused tests.
  5. Semantic actions still flow through shared application/client capability and change semantics.
  6. Untrusted content cannot inject arbitrary terminal control sequences through normal rendering APIs.
  7. Clipboard/image/plugin behavior does not silently expand authority.
  8. Local and remote TUI modes preserve the same semantic command meaning.
  9. Web and TUI derive shared states from common application/protocol semantics rather than duplicated backend logic.
  10. Terminal recovery, resize, streaming, Unicode, and reconnect fixtures pass.
  11. Temporary migration compatibility code is removed or explicitly documented with an owner and follow-up.
  12. The repository-wide final quality gate passes after all Level-3 sheets are complete.

docs.title: Upstream-First Agent Runtime and Terminal Product Ownership Correction
1. Purpose
docs.text:
This document corrects the ownership boundary established by 031. rpi tui adoption and shared presentation migration plan.md.

The first migration successfully proved that Scriberig can consume rpi code without importing foreign session semantics, but it stopped at an adapter layer. It left Scriberig owning most of the visible TUI shell, terminal lifecycle, model catalog abstraction, thinking-level abstraction, model controls, and a substantial amount of commodity agent/runtime plumbing.

That is not the desired final architecture.

The new controlling rule is:

Scriberig owns the semantics that make Scriberig unique. Commodity provider, model, agent-loop, plugin, package, and terminal-product machinery should be owned by upstream rpi whenever upstream provides it or can reasonably be extended to provide it.

A second controlling rule is:

When a generally useful capability is missing upstream, prefer contributing or extracting that capability upstream and then consuming it from Scriberig. Do not create a Scriberig-only substitute merely because it is faster locally.

This plan supersedes the final ownership and completion criteria in Level-2 plan 031. Work from tasks 138 through 143 remains useful migration evidence and may be reused, but it is not the final target.

docs.title: 2. Why the Previous Migration Is Not the End State
docs.text:
The current branch demonstrates the problem clearly:

  • rpi-tui is vendored, but Scriberig still owns the Ratatui application shell;
  • upstream editor and Markdown output are adapted back into Scriberig-owned rendering instead of letting upstream own the terminal presentation stack;
  • Scriberig still defines its own model descriptors, thinking-level descriptors, model profiles, and model library;
  • Scriberig still owns provider/model selection presentation;
  • the active terminal lifecycle remains Scriberig Crossterm code;
  • the upstream plugin/extension/package ecosystem is not the integrated product extension mechanism;
  • the local agent runtime still owns provider and tool-loop machinery that upstream already exposes as reusable libraries.

The implementation can therefore change many files and pass many tests while the product still looks and feels like the same locally maintained TUI.

The corrective migration must optimize for delegation and deletion, not merely for wrapping upstream primitives.

docs.title: 3. Upstream Baseline
docs.text:
At the reviewed upstream revision aab74de0737f4b7c454cd8c8c16ca66e4dfbf898 (rpi 0.6.2), upstream already provides or documents reusable machinery for:

rpi-ai
  provider-neutral model descriptors
  provider protocol implementations
  model compatibility metadata
  model costs/context/max-output metadata
  model-specific sampling parameters
  model-specific compatibility/custom properties
  thinking-level maps and supported-level clamping

rpi-agent
  provider-neutral agent loop
  tool schemas and validation
  tool execution sequencing
  streaming events
  cancellation
  hooks/queues

rpi-tui
  terminal runtime
  regular/fullscreen modes
  component abstraction
  focus
  overlays
  editor/composer
  text and Markdown rendering
  fuzzy/select UI
  themes/styles
  transcript/message components
  scroll/resize/input behavior

rpi-plugin-sdk + rpi-extensions
  stable plugin ABI
  tool registration
  provider registration
  slash commands
  event handlers
  Markdown renderers
  discovered resources

rpi-cli / provider-package infrastructure
  dynamic model registry/catalog
  provider authentication status
  provider/model selection
  thinking selection
  provider packages
  package install/update/link/reload
  model catalog refresh

Some of these capabilities currently live in rpi-cli rather than a narrow reusable crate. That is an upstream API-boundary problem, not permission to copy the implementation into Scriberig.

When Scriberig needs one of those capabilities as a library and upstream has it only inside the CLI, the implementation sequence is:

identify reusable upstream capability
  -> contribute/extract reusable upstream library API
  -> pin/release upstream revision
  -> consume that API from Scriberig
  -> delete local duplicate

A temporary pinned Git dependency is acceptable while an upstream release is pending. A hand-maintained copied implementation is not the preferred final state.

docs.title: 4.1 Scriberig owns distinctive semantic architecture
docs.text:
Scriberig remains authoritative for:

universal semantic knowledge
stable semantic identity
immutable revisions
exact snapshots
schemas and domain adapters
semantic query/follow/inspect operations
projections and bidirectional semantic editing
candidate -> migration -> validation -> conflict -> promotion
session and branch semantic topology
ContinuationAnchor semantics
BranchResult semantics
context-isolation policy
agent profiles as semantic/context configuration
context-component activation
canonical effective model request construction
plan nodes
plan dependency DAG
one auto-advancing plan coordinator
branch/plan execution assignment
provider-continuation validity relative to Scriberig context fingerprints
semantic capability/trust policy
application operations
public Scriberig protocol/server/client/web semantics
execution provenance bound to semantic/session identities

These concepts must not be replaced by upstream transcript, filesystem, task-list, or session semantics.

docs.title: 4.2 Upstream owns commodity model/provider machinery
docs.text:
Scriberig must not maintain a parallel model catalog implementation.

Upstream owns:

provider implementations
provider packages
provider discovery
provider authentication and credential resolution
model catalog loading/refresh
model metadata schema
provider/model compatibility metadata
model cost/context/output metadata
model-specific custom properties
sampling parameters
model-specific request-shaping properties
thinking-level names/order/support
thinking-level mapping to provider effort
thinking-level clamping
provider/model selector behavior
provider reload/package lifecycle

Scriberig may store a reference or safe historical snapshot of the resolved upstream execution selection for provenance. It must not become the authority that decides which thinking levels or custom properties a model supports.

The existing Scriberig-owned ModelDescriptor, ThinkingLevelDescriptor, ModelCapabilities, and model-library catalog are migration targets for removal or reduction to compatibility/protocol projections.

docs.title: 4.3 Upstream owns the ordinary in-branch agent loop
docs.text:
Use rpi-agent for commodity loop behavior such as:

model invocation loop
tool-call schema handling
tool argument validation
streaming event normalization
tool result sequencing
cancellation
ordinary retry/settlement mechanics exposed by upstream

Scriberig still decides:

which branch is executing
what context that branch receives
which semantic capabilities become tools
whether a tool is atomic or branch-producing
when a child branch is created
what BranchResult returns to the parent
what durable session objects are recorded
what semantic mutations are allowed

Do not adopt rpi-harness as canonical Scriberig session storage or branch identity. It solves a different session problem.

docs.title: 4.4 Upstream owns the plugin/package host
docs.text:
The integrated Scriberig agent product should use the upstream plugin ABI, extension loader, and package lifecycle rather than creating another model/tool/slash-command plugin system.

Scriberig-specific integration supplies adapters and capability policy.

For example:

upstream plugin registers AgentTool
  -> Scriberig host checks configured trust/capability policy
  -> tool executes through allowed Scriberig/application capability or approved fallback environment
  -> any canonical semantic mutation still converges on Scriberig candidate/change semantics

Scriberig domain adapters remain Scriberig semantic extensions because they define semantic meaning, parsing, reconciliation, validation, and projections. They are not replaced by the upstream agent plugin ABI.

Where one extension needs both roles, keep the roles explicit:

Scriberig domain extension
  -> semantic/domain capability

upstream rpi plugin/package
  -> agent/provider/UI/runtime extension

Do not invent a second agent plugin loader to bridge them.

docs.title: 4.5 Upstream owns the terminal product framework
docs.text:
The active Scriberig TUI must run on upstream rpi-tui as the terminal runtime and component system.

Upstream should own:

terminal lifecycle
terminal input normalization
render scheduling/differential rendering
regular/fullscreen mode
scrolling
resize handling
focus
hardware cursor
editor/composer
selection/fuzzy lists
overlays
status/footer mechanics
Markdown rendering
theme/style system
copy/paste integration
model/provider/thinking selectors where upstream exposes them

Scriberig must not retain a parallel Ratatui application shell as the normal product path.

docs.title: 4.6 Scriberig custom terminal panels are upstream components
docs.text:
Scriberig will still need custom semantic views because upstream cannot know Scriberig concepts.

Those views are implemented on top of upstream UI contracts, not beside them.

Examples:

RecursiveConversationComponent
SessionTreeComponent
PlanComponent
SemanticExplorerComponent
SemanticInspectorComponent
ProjectionComponent
CandidateReviewComponent
OperationComponent
EffectivePromptComponent
ReasoningActivityComponent

They should implement/use rpi-tui Component, TUI child composition, overlays, upstream text/layout/theme/scroll primitives, and upstream focus/input conventions.

They may adapt Scriberig semantic state to UI rows. They may not recreate terminal lifecycle, a second widget framework, a second theme system, or a second event/render runtime.

If a generally useful panel/layout/tree/table primitive is missing from upstream, contribute it upstream first and use it from there.

docs.title: 5. The Upstream-First Rule
docs.text: For every implementation decision in the agent/TUI product layer, classify the desired behavior before coding.

docs.title: Class U — upstream commodity
docs.text:
A feature belongs upstream when it is useful independent of Scriberig semantic knowledge.

Examples:

model catalog
provider packages
provider auth
thinking levels
model custom properties
model selector
provider selector
package manager
plugin ABI
agent loop
editor
Markdown
scrolling
terminal lifecycle
overlay placement
tree/list/table widget primitives
status/footer widget
copy/paste
terminal images, if later enabled

Action:

use upstream; if the API is not reusable enough, contribute/refactor upstream before adding a Scriberig implementation.

docs.title: Class S — Scriberig semantic
docs.text:
A feature belongs in Scriberig when its meaning depends on Scriberig architecture.

Examples:

BranchResult
ContinuationAnchor
semantic entity/revision/snapshot navigation
candidate review
semantic diff
plan dependency semantics
context-component activation
semantic tool applicability
projection reconciliation
provider-continuation staleness after Scriberig context divergence

Action:

implement in Scriberig, but expose/present it through upstream runtime/UI extension seams.

docs.title: Class A — adapter
docs.text:
An adapter translates between Class S semantics and Class U infrastructure.

Examples:

Scriberig semantic operation -> rpi AgentTool
Scriberig branch execution selection -> upstream resolved model selection
rpi AgentEvent -> Scriberig ModelInvocation/Activity
Scriberig ConversationModel -> rpi-tui Component rows
Scriberig capability denial -> upstream tool disabled/error result
upstream safe model snapshot -> Scriberig invocation provenance

Adapters should be narrow and contain no duplicated catalog/UI/runtime policy.

docs.title: 6. Model Catalog, Thinking, and Custom Model Properties
docs.text: This boundary is explicit because Scriberig currently duplicates it.

docs.title: 6.1 Remove Scriberig as catalog authority
docs.text:
Do not maintain Scriberig-owned truth equivalent to:

ModelDescriptor
ModelCapabilities
ThinkingLevelDescriptor
supported thinking list
default thinking map
provider-specific model property schema
custom provider catalog parser
provider auth state

The upstream catalog is authoritative for these values.

docs.title: 6.2 Preserve Scriberig assignment semantics
docs.text:
Scriberig still needs to say:

this branch uses execution selection E
this plan node is assigned execution selection E
this invocation actually resolved to model M with thinking T

That does not require a Scriberig model catalog.

Use an upstream-owned execution-selection/configuration type where available. If upstream lacks a reusable safe selection/snapshot type, contribute one upstream.

Scriberig durable records should contain only what Scriberig needs for reproducibility/provenance, conceptually:

provider/model stable public identifiers
upstream catalog/version or selection fingerprint
selected thinking level as resolved by upstream
safe output-affecting model configuration snapshot/hash
safe provider/model metadata needed for historical explanation

Do not persist resolved credentials or secret headers.

docs.title: 6.3 Thinking levels are upstream semantics
docs.text:
The TUI and runtime must ask upstream which levels a selected model supports.

Do not hard-code or independently validate lists such as:

off
minimal
low
medium
high
xhigh
max

Scriberig may record the selected resolved value. Upstream decides support, mapping, fallback/clamping, and provider serialization.

docs.title: 6.4 Custom model properties are upstream semantics
docs.text:
Model-specific properties such as:

sampling parameters
reasoning effort maps
compatibility flags
strict-tool support
custom headers/endpoint metadata
provider-specific request-shaping fields
input modality
context/output limits
cost metadata

must come from upstream model/provider machinery.

If the product needs a UI for editing arbitrary/custom model properties, that editor should be implemented as or extracted into upstream UI/config machinery. Scriberig should consume it rather than build a Scriberig-specific property editor.

Scriberig may apply policy to whether a property/override is allowed in one project/session, but it must not redefine the property schema.

docs.title: 7. Agent Profiles Remain Scriberig-Owned but Stop Owning Models
docs.text:
AgentProfile remains a Scriberig semantic configuration because it controls Scriberig context composition, branching policy, semantic tool disclosure, and execution behavior.

Refine its execution portion from a local model profile/catalog to an upstream execution reference.

Conceptually:

AgentProfile
  Scriberig profile identity/revision
  context components
  context policy
  branch policy
  semantic capability policy
  runtime budget policy
  preferred upstream execution selector/reference

The upstream reference may express preferred provider/model/thinking/custom configuration through an upstream-owned type or stable serialized reference.

Scriberig does not duplicate model metadata merely because an AgentProfile references a model.

docs.title: 8. Per-Branch and Per-Plan-Node Model Assignment
docs.text:
Scriberig's multi-model semantics remain unchanged:

branch B -> execution assignment X
branch C -> execution assignment Y
plan node P -> execution assignment Z

The ownership split is:

Scriberig owns:
  which branch/node has an assignment
  inheritance/override rules
  assignment provenance
  when assignments change

upstream owns:
  what provider/model selections exist
  how a selection resolves
  thinking support
  custom model properties
  provider auth/readiness
  provider request serialization

A plan/session branch may keep an assignment that later becomes unavailable in the live upstream catalog. Historical identity remains inspectable; new execution must resolve/fail through upstream with a structured availability error.

docs.title: 9. Provider Continuation
docs.text:
Scriberig continues to own the semantic validity decision for provider continuation because only Scriberig knows whether canonical branch context diverged.

Upstream should own provider-wire continuation support whenever possible.

Therefore:

Scriberig:
  branch-local continuation association
  context fingerprint
  stale/reseed decision
  provider-neutral provenance

upstream:
  provider-specific conversation/response handles
  request serialization
  continuation request mechanics
  provider error interpretation

If an upstream provider lacks continuation support required by Scriberig, contribute it upstream rather than extending a separate Scriberig HTTP provider implementation.

docs.title: 10. Semantic Tools on Top of rpi-agent
docs.text:
Scriberig semantic operations become rpi-agent tools through a thin adapter.

The adapter owns:

stable exposed tool name
JSON schema generated from Scriberig operation input
capability check hook
conversion to shared application operation
bounded semantic result projection
correlation back to Scriberig activity identity

It does not own:

provider tool-call parsing
ordinary tool-call ordering
stream settlement
agent loop cancellation
model transcript mechanics

Those remain upstream.

docs.title: Branch-producing work
docs.text:
When a tool request requires focused recursive work, the Scriberig adapter may suspend/complete the current upstream tool call by creating a Scriberig child branch, executing that branch through another upstream agent-loop instance, then returning the child's compact BranchResult projection as the tool result.

The session tree is still Scriberig's.

docs.title: 11. Upstream Plugins and Scriberig Trust
docs.text:
Use the upstream plugin loader and package system for integrated agent-product extensions.

Do not automatically grant all loaded upstream plugins every Scriberig capability.

Scriberig contributes a host policy adapter that decides which registered tools/resources/commands are enabled in the current product/project/branch.

A plugin tool that wants to alter understood semantic content must call public Scriberig semantic operations or operate through a Scriberig-provided tool adapter. Direct filesystem writes remain fallback/interoperability behavior, not the canonical semantic editing path.

Where upstream plugin registration exposes a generic capability that Scriberig does not want for a given branch, Scriberig filters it from the model/tool surface rather than forking the plugin loader.

docs.title: 12. TUI Target Architecture
docs.text:
The terminal product should converge on:

Scriberig application/session semantic models
        |
        v
thin Scriberig TUI adapters/components
        |
        v
rpi-tui Component / TUI APIs
        |
        v
upstream terminal runtime/render/input/theme/editor

Not:

rpi-tui primitive
        |
        v
scriberig-tui-kit converts to plain text
        |
        v
Ratatui widgets
        |
        v
Scriberig terminal runtime

docs.title: 12.1 Remove the double-rendering bridge
docs.text:
The final path must not render upstream widgets to ANSI/plain lines merely to reconstruct them as Ratatui Paragraphs.

Use upstream components directly.

docs.title: 12.2 Use upstream model controls
docs.text:
Provider/model/thinking selectors and status presentation should come from upstream product/UI machinery.

If those components are currently private to rpi-cli, extract or expose them upstream before Scriberig implements an alternative.

docs.title: 12.3 Custom Scriberig panels use upstream composition
docs.text:
The recursive session tree, plan status, semantic browser, projection/review, and model-observability surfaces are custom because their data is Scriberig-specific.

They must nevertheless use upstream:

component contract
layout primitives
overlays
focus
scrolling
text/style/theme
input handling
status/footer conventions

A custom panel is not permission to retain the current Scriberig shell.

docs.title: 13. Upstream UI Gaps Must Be Fixed Upstream
docs.text:
If implementation discovers that rpi-tui lacks a reusable generic primitive required by Scriberig, classify it.

Examples likely useful upstream:

TreeView / hierarchical list
split/panel composition
virtualized large list/tree
structured status/footer slot
model custom-property editor
reusable provider/model/thinking selector
component registry/panel extension point
safe structured table

If the primitive is generally useful, implement it upstream and consume it after pinning a compatible revision.

A Scriberig-local implementation is acceptable only when the behavior is inherently Scriberig-semantic, such as how BranchResult rows relate to a ContinuationAnchor.

docs.title: 14. Plugin-Supplied UI
docs.text:
The reviewed upstream plugin ABI registers tools, providers, slash commands, event handlers, Markdown renderers, and resources. It does not currently establish that arbitrary native TUI panels are a stable plugin ABI.

Therefore:

  1. built-in Scriberig semantic panels may directly implement upstream rpi-tui components;
  2. do not create a separate Scriberig plugin ABI just for terminal panels;
  3. if third-party agent plugins need custom panels, design/contribute a generic upstream panel/component extension point;
  4. keep Scriberig semantic-domain UI extension needs separate from the agent runtime plugin ABI where their lifecycle/security requirements differ.

The important invariant is that all terminal panels render through the same upstream TUI framework.

docs.title: 15. Dependency and Source Policy
docs.text:
Prefer this dependency order:

released upstream crate
  > pinned upstream git revision
  > temporary local patch with explicit upstream PR/issue
  > copied/vendor fork only as a last resort

The current hand-copied third_party/rpi-tui tree is not the preferred final arrangement.

Once required upstream APIs are available through a release or pinned Git revision:

  • remove the hand-maintained vendor fork;
  • remove scriberig-tui-kit if it only wraps upstream commodity behavior;
  • keep a small integration/adaptation crate only for Scriberig-semantic adapters;
  • preserve licensing notices through normal dependency/license reporting.

Offline/reproducible builds may use generated Cargo vendoring in release tooling without making the vendored copy the architectural source of truth.

docs.title: 16. Server, Protocol, and Web Remain Scriberig Surfaces
docs.text:
Do not replace the Scriberig public server or web semantic API with upstream remote-agent session semantics.

Scriberig's server must expose Scriberig concepts such as entities, snapshots, migrations, branches, plans, candidates, and operations.

However, server-side model/provider information should be projected from upstream runtime state rather than reconstructed by Scriberig.

For example:

upstream model catalog
  -> safe protocol projection
  -> web model selector

The web client may have its own React rendering, but it consumes the same upstream-resolved model/provider/thinking/custom-property semantics through Scriberig's server projection.

Scriberig protocol types should avoid inventing a second model schema. Prefer safe passthrough/projection types generated from or versioned against upstream public model descriptors.

docs.title: 17. Migration Strategy
docs.text: The correction is executed in ordered slices. Do not perform another giant compatibility refactor that leaves all old owners in place.

docs.title: Phase 1 — freeze and classify
docs.text:
Inventory every local commodity owner and map it to an upstream owner or an explicit upstream-gap issue.

No new local catalog/TUI/plugin/runtime abstractions may be added during this phase.

docs.title: Phase 2 — model/provider ownership
docs.text:
Move catalog, provider, auth, thinking, custom properties, selection, and model readiness to upstream APIs.

Delete local model-catalog authority as soon as consumers migrate.

docs.title: Phase 3 — agent loop and extension host
docs.text:
Adopt rpi-agent and the upstream plugin/extension/package host for integrated agent execution.

Keep Scriberig branch/context/tool semantics as adapters around that loop.

docs.title: Phase 4 — upstream terminal runtime
docs.text:
Make rpi-tui the actual terminal lifecycle/render/input owner.

Move model/provider/thinking UI to upstream components.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Scriberig semantic components
docs.text: Port recursive session, plan, semantic explorer, projection/change review, prompt/reasoning, and operation views into upstream components.

docs.title: Phase 6 — delete duplicate infrastructure
docs.text: Remove Ratatui shell ownership, local terminal lifecycle, local generic TUI kit, local catalog/thinking machinery, local plugin duplication, and superseded provider/tool-loop code.

docs.title: 18. Acceptance Criteria That Prevent a Repeat of the Previous Outcome
docs.text: The correction is not complete until all of these are true.

docs.title: 18.1 Model/provider delegation
docs.text:
• No Scriberig-owned model catalog determines available providers/models.
  • No Scriberig-owned thinking-level catalog determines supported thinking values.
  • Model custom properties are defined/interpreted by upstream.
  • Provider authentication/readiness comes from upstream.
  • TUI model/provider/thinking controls consume upstream data/components.
  • Branch/plan assignment stores references/provenance without becoming a catalog.

docs.title: 18.2 Agent/runtime delegation
docs.text:
• Ordinary in-branch model/tool loop runs through rpi-agent or its current upstream replacement.
  • Provider wire implementations come from upstream.
  • Upstream plugin/extension/package machinery is used for integrated agent extensions.
  • Scriberig does not adopt upstream session/harness identity as canonical state.

docs.title: 18.3 TUI delegation
docs.text:
• The active TUI terminal lifecycle is upstream-owned.
  • scriberig-tui has no direct Ratatui dependency in the final path.
  • The active shell is composed from upstream TUI/Component APIs.
  • The composer is an upstream component, not rendered through a Scriberig text bridge.
  • Markdown is rendered by upstream directly, not rendered then stripped and reconstructed.
  • Focus, overlays, scrolling, resize, theme and status mechanics are upstream-owned.
  • Provider/model/thinking selection is upstream UI.
