  • Scriberig custom panels are upstream components.

docs.title: 18.4 Deletion evidence
docs.text:
The final implementation report must include a deletion ledger showing the local owners removed.

At minimum review/remove current equivalents of:

third_party/rpi-tui hand-maintained fork
scriberig-tui-kit generic wrappers
Ratatui application shell
direct Scriberig Crossterm lifecycle
local generic composer/editor
local Markdown/fuzzy/theme wrappers
local model descriptor/library/catalog authority
local thinking-level support/mapping authority
local provider/model selector logic
local plugin/extension host if any
local provider wire code superseded by upstream
local ordinary tool-loop code superseded by rpi-agent

Keeping one of these requires an explicit architectural exception in this Level-2 document, not merely a code comment.

docs.title: 18.5 Visible product acceptance
docs.text:
The migration must include a before/after deterministic terminal scenario proving that the normal TUI is actually running on the upstream interaction model.

A successful migration cannot be accepted solely because internal unit tests prove an upstream editor was called.

The golden/snapshot acceptance should exercise:

startup composer
streaming answer
Markdown/code rendering
model/provider selector
thinking selector
one custom model property flow when supported
slash command/palette
recursive child branch
historical reply anchor
plan state
semantic explorer
candidate review
resize/scroll
terminal exit

The output need not clone upstream's CLI product exactly, but the upstream component/runtime behavior must be the actual active implementation.

docs.title: 19. Ordered Level-3 Repair Sheets
docs.text:
Implement this correction in order:

144  Stop local commodity ownership and establish upstream contribution gates
  |
145  Replace local model catalog, provider auth, thinking and custom-model-property machinery with upstream
  |
146  Replace local provider/tool loop and agent extension host with upstream agent and plugin runtime
  |
147  Replace the Ratatui shell and TUI-kit bridge with the upstream TUI runtime and native model controls
  |
148  Rebuild Scriberig recursive semantic panels as upstream TUI components
  |
149  Remove superseded local infrastructure, prove cross-surface conformance, and finish the correction

Each task must keep its checklist current and must not begin the next task until its completion gate is satisfied.

If a required generic capability is missing upstream, the current task remains incomplete until one of these is true:

  1. the upstream capability exists in a released version;
  2. the upstream capability exists at a pinned reviewed commit that Scriberig can consume;
  3. the user explicitly authorizes a temporary local exception with an upstream issue/PR and a removal condition.

docs.title: 20. Relationship to Existing Tasks 138–143
docs.text:
Tasks 138–142 are historical foundation work. Their focused tests and useful safety/conformance improvements should be retained where compatible.

Task 143 must not be completed as the final adoption gate under the old ownership model.

Its remaining repository test gate can still be useful, but final architectural acceptance moves to task 149 and this Level-2 plan.

Do not interpret checked boxes in 138–142 as permission to preserve duplicated commodity ownership that this plan explicitly removes.

docs.title: 21. Final Principle
docs.text:
The simplest test for every contested owner is:

If this code would be useful in a generic terminal coding-agent runtime that knew nothing about Scriberig's semantic graph, revisions, branches, plans, migrations, or validation, why is Scriberig maintaining it?

If the answer is only convenience or historical accident, move it upstream.

Scriberig should spend its engineering budget on the semantic knowledge system, recursive context architecture, durable plans, semantic operations, validation/promotion, and cross-surface product semantics that upstream does not provide.

docs.title: Semantic Plan Graph Persistence, Rollups, Evidence, and Gates
1. Purpose
docs.text:
This document turns the plan refinements in:

  • design/level-1/018. durable plans dependency scheduling and multi-model execution.md;
  • design/level-1/023. semantic plan entities evidence gates and recoverable execution.md;

into concrete subsystem, storage, mutation, query, and migration design for the current Rust repository.

It also depends on:

  • design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md;
  • design/level-1/003. identity revisions and snapshots.md;
  • design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md;
  • design/level-1/008. derived knowledge caching and incrementality.md;
  • design/level-1/009. agent interaction and sessions.md;
  • design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md;
  • design/level-2/010. universal query and operation implementation.md;
  • design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md;
  • design/level-2/013. identity revision snapshot implementation.md;
  • design/level-2/016. universal knowledge model rust libraries.md;
  • design/level-2/023. agent runtime model provider and branch orchestration.md;
  • design/level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md;
  • design/level-2/032. upstream first agent runtime and terminal product ownership correction.md.

The controlling rule is:

Planning remains owned by Scriberig session/application semantics, but canonical plan state is persisted as independently revisioned semantic objects and relations in the universal knowledge store. Product DTOs and aggregate Rust views are projections over that state.

docs.title: 2. Current Implementation and Target
docs.text:
The current implementation contains a useful domain model in scriberig-session with concepts equivalent to:

Plan
PlanNode
PlanDependency
PlanNodeStatus
PlanStatus
WorkerClaim
CoordinatorClaim

It also has useful operations equivalent to:

add_node
add_dependency
replan
set_assignment
claim/start node
settle workers
complete node
fail node
refresh readiness

Those semantic operations should be preserved/refactored rather than discarded.

The persistence shape is the part that changes.

Current transitional shape is conceptually:

Session
  plans: Vec<Plan>

Plan
  nodes: Vec<PlanNode>
  dependencies: Vec<PlanDependency>
  history: Vec<PlanRevision>

with session SQLite persistence serializing the complete graph payload.

Target shape is:

universal semantic store
  EntityId -> RevisionId in Snapshot

Plan entity
PlanNode entities
PlanDependency relation/entities
PlanGate entities
summary relations
attempt/result relations
branch/session references

and separately:

rebuildable plan indexes / rollup cache

docs.title: 3.1 scriberig-session
docs.text:
scriberig-session remains the semantic owner of session/branch/plan vocabulary and lifecycle rules.

It should own or expose concepts equivalent to:

PlanRecord / PlanRevisionPayload
PlanNodeRecord / PlanNodeRevisionPayload
PlanNodeStatus
PlanStatus
PlanDependencyRecord
PlanGateRecord
PlanGateRequirement
PlanGatePhase
PlanGateWaiver
PlanAttemptReference or equivalent relation shape
plan mutation validation
status transition rules
rollup semantics
readiness/completion semantics
plan view assembly contracts

It must not own SQLite SQL.

docs.title: 3.2 scriberig-app
docs.text:
scriberig-app remains the mutation/query operation boundary used by agents, CLI, server, TUI, and web.

It owns application operations equivalent to:

plan_create
plan_add_node
plan_decompose
plan_add_next_step
plan_add_dependency
plan_add_gate
plan_attach_evidence
plan_update_summary
plan_set_assignment
plan_retry_node
plan_replan
plan_start/pause/resume/stop
plan_inspect
plan_node_inspect

Exact public operation names may preserve existing APIs for compatibility.

docs.title: 3.3 Universal graph/store crates
docs.text:
Use existing universal entity/revision/snapshot/relation/change infrastructure for canonical persistence.

Do not add a planning-specific canonical database beside scriberig-store.

Foundation store crates must not depend on scriberig-session.

docs.title: 3.4 scriberig-session-sqlite
docs.text:
The existing session-specific SQLite crate may own session/plan-specific compatibility persistence, derived indexes, or trigger-backed acceleration because it is allowed to know session semantics.

It must not become a second canonical revision store.

Its target role is one or more of:

legacy aggregate migration
session-specific derived indexes
backend-specific plan rollup acceleration
compatibility fixtures/tests

The exact role should shrink as universal semantic persistence becomes authoritative.

docs.title: 3.5 Product surfaces
docs.text:
scriberig-protocol, scriberig-client, web model packages, and terminal components consume shared application views/DTOs.

They do not inspect database tables.

docs.title: 4. Semantic Object Types
docs.text:
Register/use stable semantic object types equivalent to:

scriberig.session.plan
scriberig.session.plan-node
scriberig.session.plan-dependency
scriberig.session.plan-gate
scriberig.session.plan-attempt     # only if existing branch/execution records are insufficient

Prefer relation types for pure references when the universal graph already supports revisioned relation state adequately.

Do not introduce a plan-attempt entity solely because it is convenient in one serializer. Reuse branch/claim/result execution records when they provide stable independent identity and exact history.

docs.title: 5. Plan Revision Payload
docs.text:
A canonical Plan revision should remain small.

Conceptually:

PlanRevisionPayload {
    session: EntityId
    anchor: ContinuationAnchor or semantic reference
    goal: String
    status: PlanStatus
    mutation_revision: u64
    coordinator: optional semantic/branch reference
    coordinator_cursor: optional PlanNode EntityId
    coordinator_generation: u64
    coordinator_claim: optional safe claim reference/state
    default policy/assignment references when applicable
}

Do not embed all plan nodes, dependencies, gates, or complete historical plan copies.

mutation_revision preserves the existing optimistic concurrency/coordinator mechanism.

Every accepted plan mutation increments it exactly once unless an existing operation explicitly batches multiple logical mutations as one accepted revision.

docs.title: 6. PlanNode Revision Payload
docs.text:
A node revision contains node-local canonical state only.

Conceptually:

PlanNodeRevisionPayload {
    plan: EntityId
    title: String
    purpose: String
    status: PlanNodeStatus
    expected_result: optional ExpectedResult
    semantic_scope: semantic references
    assignment: optional execution assignment reference
    branch: optional EntityId
    result: optional EntityId
    superseded_by: optional EntityId
    claim_generation: u64
    active_claim: optional WorkerClaim
    abandon_reason: optional PlanAbandonReason
    last_failure: optional exact attempt/result/evidence reference
}

The exact payload should avoid copying data already represented as independent relations/entities.

In particular, do not embed:

children arrays solely for reverse navigation
dependency arrays
all evidence objects
all gates
full attempt history
subtree rollup counters
contains_ignored
contains_abandoned

Those are relations or derived views.

docs.title: 7. Structural Plan Relations
docs.text:
Plan membership and decomposition must support exact traversal.

Prefer canonical relations equivalent to:

Plan --contains_plan_node--> PlanNode
PlanNode --decomposes_to--> PlanNode

The relation representation must preserve enough history to answer:

which nodes belonged to plan P at snapshot S?
what was N's structural parent at snapshot S?
what are the current direct children of N?

Do not require a child content revision merely because it is moved between parents unless the domain deliberately stores parent identity inside the child payload.

If existing graph collection/relation primitives support this better than a parent field, prefer them.

docs.title: 8. Dependency Representation
docs.text:
Represent dependency semantics independently from structural relations.

Target conceptual record:

PlanDependencyRecord {
    id
    plan
    prerequisite
    dependent
    expected_result override/policy when needed
    fulfilled_by: optional exact BranchResult/result reference
    provenance
}

Initial policy remains strict successful dependency fulfillment.

Dependency mutations include:

add
remove/supersede
fulfill
clear/rebind only through explicit retry/replan rules

A node retry does not erase a prior failed attempt and does not fabricate fulfillment.

The dependency becomes fulfilled only after an accepted result satisfies its contract.

docs.title: 9. PlanNodeStatus and Direct Transition Rules
docs.text:
Keep one enum equivalent to:

Planned
Ready
Running
Completed
Failed
Abandoned

Do not add PlanNodeWorkState.

Initial direct transition rules should support at least:

Planned -> Ready
Planned -> Abandoned

Ready -> Running
Ready -> Planned          # dependency/gate became unavailable before claim
Ready -> Abandoned

Running -> Completed
Running -> Failed
Running -> Abandoned      # only through explicit cancellation/settlement policy

Failed -> Ready           # explicit retry/repair operation
Failed -> Abandoned

Completed -> Completed    # idempotent inspection/no-op only; do not silently reopen
Abandoned -> Abandoned

If a completed node later reveals required follow-up work, prefer adding a required repair/decomposition child or explicit superseding node rather than silently erasing the completed result.

docs.title: 10. PlanStatus Recovery Rules
docs.text:
Plan lifecycle may retain the existing vocabulary equivalent to:

Draft
Planned
Running
Paused
Completed
Failed
Cancelled

Refine mutation guards so Failed is recoverable.

Required explicit recovery path:

Failed -> Paused
Paused -> Running

or one equivalent atomic recovery operation that performs the same semantic transition.

Completed and Cancelled remain terminal for ordinary mutation.

A failed plan must retain all completed nodes/results and failure provenance.

docs.title: 11. Summary Representation
docs.text:
Use the common session/semantic Summary model when available.

Represent current node summary through an explicit relation/reference equivalent to:

PlanNode --summarized_by--> Summary

The summary record should retain or be derivable from exact source dependencies.

Application operations:

plan_update_summary(node, summary content/source)
plan_clear_or_supersede_summary(node, ...)

must create ordinary semantic revisions/relations.

A node's final result remains independent from its current summary.

docs.title: 12. Evidence Representation
docs.text:
Evidence is primarily a relation from a node or gate to an existing exact semantic object.

Use an association shape equivalent to:

PlanEvidenceAssociation {
    owner: PlanNode | PlanGate
    role: Supports | Contradicts | Informational
    evidence: SemanticRef
    note/summary: optional
    provenance: operation/user/agent reference
}

If the graph layer supports relation properties/revisions, use that mechanism.

If it does not, model the association as a small semantic entity rather than embedding copied evidence payloads.

Evidence references must preserve exact revision/snapshot identity where applicable.

Examples:

node -> BranchResult
node -> ValidationResult
gate -> Decision
gate -> HumanApproval
node -> Candidate
node -> exact entity revision

docs.title: 13. Gate Representation
docs.text:
A gate is a semantic object with stable identity.

Conceptually:

PlanGateRevisionPayload {
    owner: PlanNode
    phase: Entry | Completion
    requirement: PlanGateRequirement
    waiver: optional PlanGateWaiver
    provenance
}

Initial typed requirements:

ValidationPassed(reference/profile)
EvidencePresent(kind/reference policy)
DecisionResolved(decision)
HumanApproval(policy/role)
SemanticCondition(reference + safe typed predicate)
RequiredChildCompleted(child)

Avoid arbitrary user-supplied executable expressions.

Gate definition and waiver are canonical.

Gate evaluation is derived.

docs.title: 14. Gate Evaluation
docs.text:
Define a deterministic evaluator:

evaluate_gate(snapshot, gate) ->
    Pending | Satisfied | Failed | Waived

Evaluation returns supporting exact evidence references and a bounded reason.

A gate evaluation may be cached/materialized, but cache identity must include the smallest exact inputs that determine it.

The scheduler must never accept a gate cache from a different source snapshot without validation.

Entry gates participate in readiness.

Completion gates participate in completion.

A waived gate is considered satisfied for scheduling/completion but remains visibly waived with provenance.

docs.title: 15. Required Decomposition
docs.text:
Expose explicit semantic operations for decomposition rather than overloading generic node insertion.

Conceptually:

plan_decompose(parent, children, required=true|false)
plan_add_next_step(anchor/plan, node)

plan_decompose(... required=true):

  1. creates child node entities;
  2. creates structural child relations;
  3. creates RequiredChildCompleted(child) completion gates or an equivalent grouped gate on the parent;
  4. does not create sibling dependency edges unless explicitly requested.

Optional decomposition omits the completion obligation.

The lower-level implementation may group multiple required children into one gate if the semantics remain exact and individually inspectable.

docs.title: 16. Execution Attempt Provenance
docs.text:
Audit existing branch, claim, model invocation, operation, and BranchResult records before introducing a new attempt object.

The system must be able to answer:

how many times was node N attempted?
which branch did each attempt execute?
which claim/generation owned it?
what was each outcome?
what result/failure evidence did it produce?
which attempt produced the accepted node result?

Preferred mapping when existing records are sufficient:

PlanNode --attempted_on--> Branch
PlanNode --attempt_result--> BranchResult / failure result
claim generation recorded in execution provenance

Introduce PlanAttempt only if those relations cannot represent independent retry history safely.

docs.title: 17. Retry Operation
docs.text:
Add an explicit retry operation rather than making ordinary start_node accept failed nodes implicitly.

Conceptually:

plan_retry_node(node, policy)

Validation:

  • node is currently Failed;
  • no active claim owns it;
  • plan is not completed/cancelled;
  • failed result has not satisfied dependencies;
  • retry branch policy is valid;
  • required dependencies and entry gates can be re-evaluated.

Mutation:

  • preserve prior attempt/failure references;
  • clear only active claim/current failed-execution binding that must not carry into the next attempt;
  • create/bind the next attempt branch according to policy;
  • transition direct status to Ready when readiness inputs are satisfied, otherwise Planned;
  • increment plan mutation revision once;
  • preserve exact failure evidence.

The next worker claim then uses the normal ready-node claim/start path.

docs.title: 18. Normal Plan Growth While Running
docs.text:
Refactor mutation guards so a Running plan may accept safe ordinary evolution operations.

Allowed while running, subject to coordinator/user authorization and optimistic concurrency:

add node
add next step
decompose existing node
add dependency that does not invalidate already accepted completed work
add gate
attach evidence
update summary
retry failed node
change assignment of unstarted node

Operations that invalidate or replace already accepted structure/results use explicit replan/supersession semantics.

Do not require Paused | Failed merely to discover and add new work.

docs.title: 19. Atomic Plan Mutation Batch
docs.text:
Preserve the current plan mutation/CAS concept, but make the durable write a semantic change batch.

An accepted mutation is conceptually:

PlanMutation {
    plan
    expected_plan_mutation_revision
    base_snapshot
    operation/provenance
    entity revision writes
    relation writes/removals/supersessions
    derived-index invalidation/update intents
}

Commit flow:

load exact plan/node/relation state at base snapshot
validate operation and expected plan mutation revision
construct immutable successor revisions
construct semantic changes/migration
validate graph/lifecycle/gate/dependency invariants
apply/promote successor snapshot with ordinary conflict handling
refresh or mark derived plan indexes for the resulting snapshot
publish shared application event/result

No UI/agent/backend caller receives a direct SQL mutation path.

docs.title: 20. Plan Mutation Revision and Snapshot CAS
docs.text:
The existing plan-local revision remains useful for focused stale-write detection even though the universal root/snapshot also changes.

Use both identities deliberately:

base snapshot
  proves the exact semantic world observed

plan mutation revision
  provides compact plan-local optimistic concurrency/coordinator generation

An application operation should normally reject or reconcile when either required expectation is stale.

Do not use plan mutation revision as a replacement for exact semantic revisions/snapshots.

docs.title: 21. Derived PlanNode Aggregate
docs.text:
Define a backend-neutral derived view equivalent to:

PlanNodeAggregate {
    node
    source_snapshot
    effective_status: PlanNodeStatus
    direct_child_counts_by_status
    descendant_failed_count or sufficient equivalent
    descendant_abandoned_count or sufficient equivalent
    ignored_descendant_count
    pending_entry_gate_count
    failed_entry_gate_count
    pending_completion_gate_count
    failed_completion_gate_count
}

The exact stored counters may differ if a smaller set is sufficient to update incrementally.

The semantic rollup precedence comes from Level 1 document 023.

This aggregate is not part of PlanNode revision identity.

docs.title: 22. Incremental Ancestor Propagation
docs.text:
When one node direct status, structural relation, abandon reason, or gate-derived completion condition changes:

  1. recompute/update the affected node aggregate;
  2. update the direct parent aggregate;
  3. continue upward only while the parent's aggregate changes;
  4. stop at the root or first unchanged ancestor.

The normal complexity is O(depth) plus local child-counter maintenance, not O(subtree size) per read.

Structural reparenting may require updating both old and new ancestor chains.

Bulk import/rebuild may use a bottom-up batch algorithm instead of repeated single-node propagation.

docs.title: 23. SQLite Strategy and Triggers
docs.text:
SQLite triggers are permitted but not required.

The generic scriberig-store-sqlite revision table stores opaque typed revision payloads and must not gain a dependency on session plan semantics merely to implement triggers.

Therefore trigger-backed rollups are appropriate only if a session-specific SQLite layer maintains normalized derived/index rows such as:

plan_node_index
  plan_id
  node_id
  parent_node_id
  current_revision_id
  direct_status
  abandon_reason
  source_snapshot

plan_node_rollup
  node_id
  effective_status
  status counters
  ignored/abandoned counts
  gate counters
  source_snapshot

A trigger may update parent counters when plan_node_index changes.

Alternative initial implementation:

session semantic layer computes changed ancestor aggregates
-> session-specific SQLite index transaction writes them

Both approaches are valid if they preserve the same backend-neutral semantics.

Do not parse opaque canonical revision blobs inside fragile SQL triggers.

docs.title: 24. Derived Index Consistency
docs.text:
Every derived plan index/cache record must identify the canonical state it represents, normally by exact source snapshot and relevant schema/evaluator version.

Scheduler correctness rule:

Never dispatch work from a derived readiness/rollup record that is known to be stale relative to the authoritative plan snapshot.

If the materialized index is missing/stale:

  • recompute the smallest affected plan/ancestor path synchronously when needed for correctness; or
  • return a structured temporary-not-ready/index-rebuild condition;
  • then refresh the cache.

Do not silently use stale rollups for scheduling decisions.

docs.title: 25. Plan Query/View Assembly
docs.text:
Expose shared application/session views rather than leaking relation storage.

Conceptually:

PlanView {
    id
    exact_revision
    mutation_revision
    goal
    status
    coordinator
    root_nodes
    summary/status counts
}

PlanNodeView {
    id
    exact_revision
    plan
    parent
    title
    purpose
    direct_status
    effective_status
    contains_ignored
    contains_abandoned
    summary
    branch/current attempt
    assignment
    expected_result
    blockers
    dependencies
    gate_summary
    evidence_summary
    result
}

Provide bounded/lazy detail operations for large evidence, gate, attempt, dependency, and history sets.

Do not force every list operation to materialize full child histories.

docs.title: 26. Readiness
docs.text:
Refactor readiness to query exact canonical dependency/gate state rather than only fields embedded in one aggregate plan.

Conceptually:

ready(node, snapshot) =
    direct status in {Planned, Ready}
    AND branch/claim policy permits start
    AND every required dependency has exact accepted successful fulfillment
    AND every entry gate evaluates Satisfied or Waived

The operation may use validated derived indexes to accelerate the answer.

When readiness changes:

Planned <-> Ready

write the direct status transition as ordinary canonical node state when the scheduler currently persists Ready explicitly.

Do not introduce a second hidden readiness state machine.

docs.title: 27. Completion
docs.text:
Node completion requires:

successful accepted BranchResult/result contract
AND all completion gates Satisfied or Waived

Completing one node:

  1. writes the accepted result reference;
  2. writes node status Completed;
  3. fulfills compatible outgoing dependencies;
  4. creates/updates evidence associations as appropriate;
  5. invalidates/evaluates dependent readiness;
  6. updates affected parent rollups;
  7. may complete the whole plan if plan completion policy is satisfied.

A completed node must not retain an active worker claim.

docs.title: 28. Failure Settlement
docs.text:
Settling a failed attempt:

  1. clears the active claim;
  2. records exact failure attempt/result/evidence provenance;
  3. writes node direct status Failed;
  4. leaves successful outgoing dependencies unfulfilled;
  5. updates ancestor rollups;
  6. surfaces failure to the coordinator;
  7. does not automatically mark the whole plan irrecoverably terminal.

Coordinator policy may then choose retry, repair child, alternative sibling, replan, pause, or explicit stop.

docs.title: 29. Abandoned / Ignored Semantics
docs.text:
Use Abandoned as the lifecycle status and add a typed reason when needed.

Initial reasons may include:

Ignored
Superseded
Cancelled
NoLongerNeeded
Duplicate
Other

Do not require all reasons in the first implementation if only Ignored, Superseded, and Cancelled are needed.

An abandoned descendant does not automatically propagate Abandoned to the parent.

Derived plan views expose:

contains_abandoned
contains_ignored

Completion policy decides whether an abandoned required child requires a gate waiver/replan before the parent can complete.

docs.title: 30. Events and Operation Results
docs.text:
Extend shared durable/application event categories as needed with concepts equivalent to:

PlanNodeAdded
PlanNodeDecomposed
PlanDependencyAdded/Removed/Fulfilled
PlanGateAdded/Changed/Waived
PlanEvidenceAttached
PlanSummaryChanged
PlanNodeRetryRequested
PlanNodeReady
PlanNodeStarted
PlanNodeCompleted
PlanNodeFailed
PlanNodeAbandoned
PlanRollupChanged       # optional shared derived event; not required if views refresh
PlanRecovered

Do not create TUI-only event semantics.

Transient progress remains distinct from durable semantic changes.

docs.title: 31. Protocol Compatibility
docs.text:
Existing aggregate plan DTOs may remain temporarily for clients, but they become assembled projections from semantic state.

Protocol evolution should add fields only where shared product behavior needs them, for example:

effective_status
contains_ignored
summary preview/ref
gate counts/blockers
evidence counts
retry capability

Prefer separate detail endpoints/operations for full gates/evidence/attempt history.

Old clients must not force canonical storage to remain aggregate JSON.

docs.title: 32. TUI Integration After the RPI Migration
docs.text:
This design does not add a new terminal architecture.

Task 148 already requires a Scriberig PlanComponent implemented on upstream rpi-tui component/layout/focus/overlay/scroll/theme contracts.

After semantic plan migration, that component should consume PlanView/PlanNodeView and may present compact rows equivalent to:

✗ Implement parser            failed
  1 failed gate · 3 evidence

▶ Integration                 running
  contains ignored

○ Documentation               planned
  waits: Integration

Expanded/detail interaction may expose:

summary
exact result
dependency blockers
gates and their evidence/waivers
attempt history
abandon/ignore reason
assignment

All actions route through shared scriberig-app operations.

Do not implement direct DB queries, Ratatui widgets, a second plan tree renderer, or a plan-local input/runtime loop.

If task 148 or the RPI ownership correction changes exact component names before this plan lands, adapt to the merged upstream-first design rather than reviving superseded local TUI architecture.

docs.title: 33. Web and Other Surface Integration
docs.text:
The web model/client should consume the same shared plan projections and operations.

Reusable web plan UI may expose equivalent detail, but this implementation task does not require visual parity pixel-for-pixel.

Conformance compares semantic behavior:

same node identity/status
same effective rollup
same gates/evidence
same retry outcome
same dependency readiness
same plan mutation revision/result

not terminal/browser strings.

docs.title: 34. Legacy Aggregate Migration
docs.text:
Provide deterministic migration from stored aggregate plans.

For each stored legacy plan:

  1. preserve Plan.id;
  2. preserve every PlanNode.id;
  3. create independent Plan/PlanNode revisions;
  4. convert parent structure to semantic relations;
  5. convert dependencies to independent relation/entities;
  6. preserve branch/result/assignment/supersession/claim-generation data that remains valid;
  7. preserve plan mutation revision/coordinator generation;
  8. record migration provenance;
  9. rebuild derived rollup/index state from canonical entities;
  10. verify assembled PlanView is semantically equivalent to the legacy plan before promotion.

Historical history: Vec<PlanRevision> snapshots must not simply be discarded.

Migration should retain them as historical import/provenance records or convert them to snapshot/change history when feasible. The implementation task must inspect current retained data and choose the least lossy representation.

docs.title: 35. No Uncontrolled Dual Write
docs.text:
During migration, do not let aggregate session-plan storage and universal semantic plan storage both independently accept writes.

Use one of these bounded strategies:

A. one-time migration then semantic store authoritative
B. semantic store authoritative + legacy aggregate regenerated as read-only compatibility projection
C. short explicit compatibility phase with one canonical write path and deterministic projection into the other representation

Never accept conflicting writes to both representations.

docs.title: 36. Concurrency and Coordinator Safety
docs.text:
The single auto-advancing coordinator invariant remains unchanged.

Every coordinator mutation must validate:

plan identity
expected plan mutation revision
coordinator claim/generation
exact base snapshot when required
node/claim generation for worker settlement

Independent node entities do not authorize independent global plan coordinators.

Multiple worker branches may still settle independent nodes concurrently through conflict-aware semantic changes. The application layer must retry/rebase disjoint mutations safely rather than serializing all workers through one giant session blob when the underlying semantic changes are non-conflicting.

docs.title: 37. Implementation Order
docs.text:
Implement in this order:

  1. define semantic plan codecs/schemas and relation vocabulary;
  2. build plan graph read/view assembly over universal snapshots;
  3. implement semantic mutation batch/CAS for Plan + PlanNode;
  4. migrate add-node/dependency/assignment operations;
  5. add summary/evidence/gate semantic objects and evaluation;
  6. add required-decomposition completion gates;
  7. make Failed recoverable and add explicit retry/attempt provenance;
  8. add backend-neutral rollup semantics and in-memory/reference implementation;
  9. add session-specific SQLite derived index/optional triggers;
  10. migrate worker settlement/readiness/coordinator flows;
  11. add aggregate-plan legacy migration/compatibility projection;
  12. update protocol/client/web/TUI shared views on top of the merged upstream-first TUI design;
  13. remove canonical aggregate plan persistence after conformance proves the semantic path.

docs.title: 38. Completion Criteria
docs.text:
This Level 2 design is satisfied when:

  • Plan and each PlanNode are independently addressable semantic entities with immutable revisions;
  • current snapshots resolve exact plan/node revisions;
  • plan membership, decomposition, and dependencies are traversable without deserializing one full plan blob;
  • plan mutation revision and coordinator claim semantics remain intact;
  • one accepted application mutation atomically promotes the corresponding semantic changes;
  • running plans can add safe new work without mandatory replan mode;
  • summaries are first-class semantic references distinct from purpose/result;
  • evidence references exact existing semantic objects;
  • gates are first-class typed requirements with exact evidence and explicit waivers;
  • readiness checks dependencies plus entry gates;
  • completion checks result contracts plus completion gates;
  • Failed nodes can be explicitly retried without erasing failed-attempt provenance;
  • plan-level Failed can recover through an explicit repair/replan path;
  • parent effective status and ignored/abandoned flags are derived, rebuildable, and excluded from canonical node revision identity;
  • repeated parent-status reads do not require full-subtree traversal;
  • SQLite-specific acceleration does not leak into public semantic contracts;
  • legacy aggregate plan data can be migrated deterministically without changing stable plan/node identities;
  • no uncontrolled dual-write canonical plan representations remain;
  • protocol/web/TUI consume the same shared Plan/PlanNode views and operations;
  • TUI changes, if implemented, sit on top of the upstream-first RPI component design from Level 2 document 032 and task 148.

docs.title: Projection Style Resolution, Loss-Aware Reconciliation, and Cross-Surface Contracts
1. Purpose
docs.text:
This document turns the durable rules in level-1/024. projection styles personalized representations and materialization policy.md into concrete subsystem boundaries and implementation contracts.

It refines:

  • level-2/007. projection crate boundaries and core model.md;
  • level-2/008. filesystem projection synchronization.md;
  • level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md;
  • level-2/012. capability matrix and cross surface conformance.md;
  • level-2/017. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md;
  • level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md.

For terminal integration, level-2/032. upstream first agent runtime and terminal product ownership correction.md remains authoritative. This document does not reintroduce a Scriberig-owned commodity terminal framework or theme system.

The implementation target is:

style sources
  -> shared style resolution
  -> exact resolved projection style
  -> domain renderer
  -> rendered projection

editable external/view representation
  + exact reconciliation baseline
  -> parse
  -> loss-aware reconcile
  -> candidate/migration/conflict

docs.title: 2. Current Implementation Baseline
docs.text:
The current repository already contains important generic plumbing in sr-projection:

StyleRef
  Revision { entity, revision }
  Value(StyleValue)

ProjectionSpec.style
RenderRequest.style
RenderCacheKey.style
RenderedProjection.style

The generic projection tests already establish that style participates in deterministic render/cache identity.

However, current domain implementation is incomplete relative to those contracts:

  • the Rust syntax renderer accepts only a RustFile and hard-codes four-space indentation;
  • the ECMAScript domain currently focuses on parsing/ESTree-compatible structure and has no equivalent style-aware source renderer;
  • generic style values are exact but opaque and there is no shared style-schema/discovery contract;
  • there is no shared purpose-aware style resolution service separating personal view selection from shared materialization selection;
  • ReconciliationContext identifies base/current semantic state, scope, specification, and opaque metadata, but does not model the exact rendered baseline/style/output relationship as a first-class typed contract;
  • projection capabilities are primarily projection-kind-level, while lossiness/editability may depend on the exact resolved style.

This design keeps the useful generic primitives and fills those gaps.

docs.title: 3.1 sr-projection
docs.text:
sr-projection remains domain-neutral and owns only universal contracts needed for exact rendering and reconciliation.

It may own concepts equivalent to:

StyleRef
StyleValue
ResolvedStyle
StyleSchemaRef
ProjectionPurpose
ProjectionFidelity
ReconciliationBaseline
ProjectionMappingRef / adapter-owned mapping bytes

It must not define properties such as:

indent_width
quote_style
semicolons
brace_style
comment category names for a specific language

docs.title: 3.2 Domain projection crates
docs.text:
Domain crates such as Rust, ECMAScript, and Markdown own:

style schemas
style codecs/normalization
style defaults
style merge semantics
repository-convention interpretation
rendering semantics
comment/directive classification
resolved-style fidelity/editability decisions
loss-aware reconciliation rules

docs.title: 3.3 Shared application layer
docs.text:
The existing shared application owner resolves product/user/workspace selection into exact projection inputs.

It owns behavior equivalent to:

list applicable style schemas/profiles
read current effective style
select user preference
set/clear view override
select workspace materialization profile
resolve purpose-aware style
request render with resolved style
report provenance/diagnostics

Do not create a TUI-only or web-only style resolver.

docs.title: 3.4 Product surfaces
docs.text:
TUI/web/CLI/server/client code presents and transports style intent. It does not implement language formatting rules.

Under the RPI migration, upstream rpi-tui owns generic controls, overlays, lists, settings widgets, terminal style/theme, and terminal runtime. A Scriberig component may use those widgets to select a Scriberig projection style through shared application commands.

docs.title: 4. Keep StyleRef, but Add an Explicit Resolved Style Input
docs.text:
The current StyleRef is useful because it can identify either an exact semantic style revision or exact inline adapter-owned bytes.

However, a renderer receiving only:

StyleRef::Revision { entity, revision }

still needs the actual domain style value to apply unless the renderer is allowed to reach into storage. Renderers should not acquire hidden storage/global-setting dependencies.

Introduce a generic exact resolved input conceptually equivalent to:

struct ResolvedStyle {
    reference: StyleRef,
    value: StyleValue,
    schema: Option<StyleSchemaRef>,
}

Exact field names may differ.

Rules:

  1. reference preserves semantic/provenance identity.
  2. value is the exact canonical adapter-defined bytes the renderer consumes.
  3. schema identifies the adapter/schema contract when useful for validation and discovery.
  4. resolution of StyleRef::Revision occurs before the domain renderer is called;
  5. the renderer must not fetch mutable user/project settings on its own;
  6. canonical style bytes must be deterministic for semantically identical normalized style input.

For an inline StyleRef::Value, resolution may be trivial, but validation/normalization still belongs to the domain style adapter.

docs.title: 5. Render Contract Refinement
docs.text:
Refine the conceptual render request to contain an exact resolved style rather than an unresolved reference alone:

RenderRequest
  specification
  semantic scope
  exact base state
  projection kind
  resolved style
  renderer version
  deterministic rendering context

Compatibility migration may temporarily retain the existing style: StyleRef field while adding exact resolved style bytes through a typed field. The final contract must not require the renderer to consult undeclared mutable state.

The render cache identity must include every output-affecting component of the resolved style. A safe conceptual key is:

projection spec
semantic scope/revisions
projection kind
style reference
hash(canonical resolved style value)
renderer version
rendering context

If an immutable style revision cryptographically or otherwise guarantees its value identity, the implementation may avoid redundant data in a storage key, but the runtime contract must still detect mismatched reference/value pairs as an error.

docs.title: 6. Style Schema Discovery
docs.text:
Define an adapter-owned discovery contract separate from the universal meaning of style properties.

Conceptually:

StyleSchema
  schema id/version
  projection kinds
  property descriptors
  defaults
  constraints
  documentation/labels safe for clients

A property descriptor may support generic presentation metadata equivalent to:

stable property key
value kind
allowed enum values or numeric/string constraints
default value
human label/description
whether it may affect fidelity/editability
whether it is materialization-only/view-only/available for both

The schema is descriptive metadata. It must not become a second formatter implementation.

Domain code remains responsible for validating and interpreting actual style values.

A generic client should be able to render a basic settings editor from descriptors. Opinionated clients may provide richer controls keyed by stable schema/property identifiers.

docs.title: 7. Domain Style Adapter Contract
docs.text:
Use a separate domain-owned style capability rather than teaching sr-projection language-specific properties.

Conceptually the adapter must support behavior equivalent to:

schema(projection_kind)
normalize(style_input) -> canonical StyleValue
merge(base, overlay) -> canonical StyleValue or diagnostic
resolve_defaults(context) -> canonical StyleValue
classify(resolved_style, projection_kind, purpose) -> ProjectionFidelity

The exact Rust trait structure is an implementation choice. It may be a separate ProjectionStyleAdapter, capabilities on an existing domain adapter, or another narrow domain service if that better fits current crate ownership.

Requirements:

  • normalization is deterministic;
  • unknown unsupported properties produce structured diagnostics unless the schema explicitly supports extension keys;
  • merging is domain-defined rather than generic JSON object overlay;
  • required materialization properties cannot be silently overridden;
  • resolution returns canonical exact bytes for render/cache identity.

docs.title: 8. Style Sources and Provenance
docs.text:
Model style resolution as a composition of identified sources rather than one mutable global preference map.

Useful source classes include:

DomainDefault
RepositoryConvention
ProjectPolicy
WorkspaceMaterializationPolicy
UserPreference
ViewOverride
ExplicitExportOverride

The resolver should retain provenance sufficient to explain the effective result.

Conceptually:

ResolvedStyleProvenance
  sources in application order
  source identities/revisions
  optional per-property winning source information

Per-property provenance is useful but need not be stored in every render record if it can be deterministically recomputed from retained exact sources. The exact resolved value itself is mandatory for deterministic render identity.

Do not put credentials, unrelated user settings, or unstable environment data into style provenance.

docs.title: 9. Purpose-Aware Resolution
docs.text:
Define an explicit purpose enum/type at the shared application/projection boundary.

At minimum:

InteractiveView
SharedMaterialization
ExplicitExport

docs.title: 9.1 Interactive view
docs.text:
Preferred source order:

DomainDefault
RepositoryConvention / ProjectPolicy
UserPreference
ViewOverride

docs.title: 9.2 Shared materialization
docs.text:
Preferred source order:

DomainDefault
RepositoryConvention / ProjectPolicy
WorkspaceMaterializationPolicy

Do not include UserPreference by default.

docs.title: 9.3 Explicit export
docs.text:
An export may explicitly opt into user/view overrides. The operation must record that choice and its target rather than borrowing ambient UI state implicitly.

The resolver must make source application deterministic and return structured conflicts/diagnostics when domain constraints make a combination invalid.

docs.title: 10. Repository Convention Importers
docs.text:
Repository convention readers belong with the applicable domain/configuration integration, not inside renderers.

Examples include adapters/readers for:

.editorconfig
rustfmt.toml
Prettier configuration
Biome configuration

Their output is a typed/canonical domain style input or a structured unsupported/partial diagnostic.

Rules:

  1. do not spawn a formatter and let it read arbitrary ambient configuration as the hidden source of render truth;
  2. if an external formatter must be used, invoke it with an exact resolved configuration or in an environment whose relevant inputs are captured and declared;
  3. unsupported external options must be surfaced rather than silently approximated when approximation could change output materially;
  4. importing repository convention files does not automatically make them canonical project knowledge unless a configured projection/import relationship says so.

docs.title: 11. Projection Fidelity Must Be Evaluated After Style Resolution
docs.text:
Extend capability/fidelity modeling so callers can determine editability for an exact resolved projection.

Conceptually:

ProjectionFidelity
  LosslessEditable
  LossAwareEditable
  ReadOnlyLossy

Additional detail may include adapter-owned reasons or omitted semantic categories.

Do not encode this as a single permanent flag on ProjectionKind because one style may be lossless and another lossy.

The adapter must calculate fidelity from at least:

projection kind
resolved style
adapter version
relevant policy/purpose

A product surface that wants to enter edit mode queries this result. It must not infer editability from UI control values.

docs.title: 12. Typed Comment and Directive Policy
docs.text:
Code-domain style schemas should not expose only strip_comments: bool.

Define a domain model that can distinguish at least the categories the adapter semantically understands.

For ECMAScript/TypeScript this may include categories equivalent to:

ordinary comment
documentation/JSDoc
license/header
TypeScript/compiler suppression or expectation directive
lint directive
formatter directive
source-map/tooling directive

Rust has related but different categories such as ordinary comments, doc comments, attributes, and tool directives. Do not force all languages into one fixed universal comment enum.

The style schema may expose generic policies only after the adapter maps domain categories safely.

Materialization policy may mark some categories PreserveRequiredForm even when an interactive view may hide them.

docs.title: 13. First-Class Reconciliation Baseline
docs.text:
Refine ReconciliationContext so exact baseline representation information is typed rather than hidden in an opaque metadata map.

Conceptually:

struct ReconciliationBaseline {
    base_state: SemanticStateRef,
    scope: SemanticScopeRef,
    specification: ProjectionSpecRef,
    resolved_style: ResolvedStyle,
    renderer: RendererVersion,
    adapter_version: String,
    rendered_output: ProjectionOutputRef,
    mapping: Option<ProjectionMapping>,
    fidelity: ProjectionFidelity,
}

struct ReconciliationContext {
    baseline: ReconciliationBaseline,
    current: SemanticStateRef,
    metadata: ...,
}

Exact names/storage differ, but the information boundary is required.

ProjectionOutputRef should identify the exact baseline representation strongly enough to retrieve or validate the bytes used for reconciliation. A content-addressed blob/reference is preferable to retaining only a hash when later algorithms need baseline content.

docs.title: 14. Baseline Content Retention
docs.text:
Editable projection synchronization must be able to reconstruct the exact baseline representation even after:

canonical state advances
user preferences change
repository style policy changes
renderer version advances
current materialization changes

Therefore retain either:

  1. exact baseline bytes in content-addressed projection storage; or
  2. enough immutable inputs plus a guaranteed available exact renderer implementation to reproduce them.

The first option is generally safer for external synchronization because old renderer executables may no longer be available.

A hash by itself proves equality but cannot supply missing baseline structure/content for three-way reconciliation.

The filesystem synchronization record from Level-2 008 should therefore reference the exact baseline output artifact in addition to its hash when editable reconciliation needs it.

docs.title: 15. Projection Mapping Metadata
docs.text:
Some domains can reconcile safely using parsed structure plus base semantic state. Others benefit from adapter-produced mapping metadata created during render.

Allow optional adapter-owned mapping information equivalent to:

rendered ranges/tokens/nodes -> semantic entity/revision handles
hidden canonical entities/categories
structural anchors
adapter-specific layout/reconciliation evidence

This metadata is derived projection evidence, not canonical semantic content.

It must be bound to:

exact base state
exact resolved style
exact renderer/adapter version
exact rendered output

Do not expose unstable screen row numbers or raw parser memory identities as durable semantic identity.

docs.title: 16. Loss-Aware Reconciliation Algorithm Contract
docs.text:
For an exact LossAwareEditable baseline, reconciliation conceptually receives:

B_semantic = semantic state at synchronization base
B_rendered = exact representation shown/materialized
B_style = exact resolved style
D = current canonical semantic state
F = current edited external/view representation
M = optional render mapping/loss metadata

The domain adapter must distinguish:

entity absent from F because B_style never rendered it
entity represented in B_rendered and absent from F because user removed it
entity changed in D since B_semantic
new/modified visible structure in F

Hidden canonical entities are preserved unless the edit contains explicit evidence/operation that semantically changes or deletes them.

Do not synthesize deletions from mere non-observation of style-hidden content.

If the adapter cannot disambiguate safely, return Ambiguous or Conflict; do not guess.

docs.title: 17. Style Change While Editing
docs.text:
An edit session or managed file remains bound to the style in its synchronization baseline.

If the user changes their preferred style while an editable view contains uncommitted edits, the system must not silently reinterpret the edited bytes under the new style.

Allowed behaviors include:

finish/reconcile current edit against old baseline, then rerender with new style
explicitly rebase/reproject edit with adapter support
ask user to resolve a conflict when safe automatic rebase is unavailable

The baseline style remains immutable evidence.

For filesystem projections, changing materialization style is itself a projection configuration change and should establish a new baseline only after successful rerender/write synchronization.

docs.title: 18. Shared Application Operations
docs.text:
Extend the existing application capability/operation layer rather than creating product-specific APIs.

The shared application surface should eventually support operations/views equivalent to:

projection.style_schema(scope/kind)
projection.style_profiles(scope/kind/purpose)
projection.style_effective(scope/kind/purpose/view-context)
projection.style_set_user_preference(...)
projection.style_set_view_override(...)
projection.style_set_materialization_policy(...)
projection.render(... purpose/style selection ...)
projection.fidelity(... exact resolved style ...)

Exact operation names must follow current application command conventions.

Changing a user preference or view override is not a semantic code migration. Changing a project/workspace policy may be a configuration change in the appropriate configuration domain, but it still must not masquerade as source-code modification.

docs.title: 19. Persistence Scopes
docs.text:
Do not force all style-related state into the canonical project snapshot.

Use the appropriate ownership scope:

domain defaults
  -> code/domain implementation/version

project style policy
  -> project semantic/configuration knowledge when user-meaningful and shared

workspace materialization policy
  -> workspace/project runtime/configuration scope as designed by the application

user preferences
  -> user/profile configuration scope

view override
  -> presentation/view state, optionally persisted as user UI state

resolved exact style
  -> immutable render input/provenance record

A view override should not create canonical project history merely because the UI remembers it.

docs.title: 20. Protocol and Client Contracts
docs.text:
Only style information required across a transport boundary belongs in scriberig-protocol.

Local and remote clients should expose the same application semantics.

Protocol models may need representations for:

style schema descriptor
style profile/reference
purpose
resolved style summary/provenance
fidelity/editability
style diagnostics
style selection/update request

Do not serialize opaque internal Rust trait objects or domain parser structures.

Exact canonical style bytes need not be sent to every UI if the server can render and provide a safe descriptive projection, but clients that perform local deterministic rendering must receive the exact validated input contract required for that rendering mode.

docs.title: 21. TUI Integration on the RPI Redesign
docs.text:
The active TUI target is defined by Level-2 032: upstream owns terminal runtime/component/theme/settings infrastructure; Scriberig owns distinctive semantic projection behavior.

Therefore implement terminal style controls as:

rpi-tui settings/select/editor components
        |
        v
Scriberig ProjectionStyleComponent / intent adapter
        |
        v
shared Scriberig application style operations
        |
        v
style resolver + projection adapter

Do not add:

TUI-local TypeScript formatter settings logic
TUI-local precedence rules
TUI-owned source style persistence
parallel Scriberig terminal theme system
source projection rules inside upstream terminal theme types

If a generic settings control needed by this feature is missing in rpi-tui, follow Level-2 032's upstream-first rule and contribute/extract it upstream rather than creating a Scriberig-only commodity widget framework.

A temporary view override is TUI presentation state but its semantic interpretation is still performed by the shared style resolver.

docs.title: 22. Web Integration
docs.text:
The reusable web packages should consume the same protocol/client/application contracts.

The integrated editor may render semantic source locally or request rendered source depending on the existing editor architecture, but it must display the same effective style/provenance/fidelity for equivalent inputs.

MUI or another opinionated UI library may provide controls. It does not own domain style semantics.

Reusable packages should make it possible for third-party browser clients to:

query schemas
query effective style
select profiles/overrides
request projections
understand read-only versus editable fidelity

without importing the complete integrated application.

docs.title: 23. CLI and Server Integration
docs.text:
CLI commands may expose style/profile selection and explicit materialization/export options, but they must call shared application semantics.

Examples of user intent, not prescribed command syntax:

show effective TypeScript style and provenance
render this module using my view style
materialize project using workspace policy
export this scope using profile X

The server must not apply the server process owner's personal style as an ambient global default for remote users.

docs.title: 24. Agent Integration
docs.text:
Agents normally operate on semantic entities/operations rather than editing styled text.

When a styled source projection is supplied to an agent for inspection or interoperability:

  • its exact snapshot/scope/style/renderer identity should be part of the effective context/provenance;
  • the agent must not infer deletion of omitted semantic content solely from a lossy projection;
  • semantic mutation still uses candidate/migration/change semantics;
  • later user presentation changes do not mutate already compiled model context.

Style selection must not become a hidden source of provider-continuation divergence. If an invocation's compiled context genuinely changes because a differently styled projection is included, that change participates in the normal effective-context fingerprint.

docs.title: 25. Rust Domain Implementation Direction
docs.text:
The current Rust renderer is a small deterministic semantic renderer and hard-codes four-space indentation.

Its first style-aware slice should:

  1. define a Rust source-style schema/value in the Rust domain crate;
  2. normalize an indentation property at minimum;
  3. pass exact resolved style into rendering;
  4. replace hard-coded indentation with style-derived indentation;
  5. retain deterministic output;
  6. add two-style conformance tests proving different bytes from the same semantic RustFile;
  7. keep semantic Rust structures unchanged when only style changes.

Do not generalize Rust-specific properties into sr-projection.

Where mature formatter behavior is eventually delegated to rustfmt or another engine, the adapter must still preserve exact declared configuration and deterministic projection identity.

docs.title: 26. ECMAScript/TypeScript Domain Implementation Direction
docs.text:
The current ECMAScript crate already parses JavaScript/TypeScript/JSX/TSX through Oxc into serializable structural records.

Add source projection support behind the domain adapter boundary rather than teaching generic projection code JavaScript formatting.

Before choosing an implementation engine, evaluate the current Oxc code-generation/formatting capabilities and other viable formatter engines against:

Rust/library integration
exact configuration control
determinism
comment/directive preservation
source-map/mapping support
round-trip behavior
JS/TS/JSX/TSX coverage
ability to avoid hidden ambient config

The selected renderer must accept canonical/resolved Scriberig style input.

If it delegates to an external formatter, all output-affecting configuration must be explicit and captured in renderer/style identity.

docs.title: 27.1 Core projection tests
docs.text:
Prove:

  • resolved style reference/value mismatch is rejected;
  • resolved style participates in cache identity;
  • style-only changes do not create semantic content revisions;
  • fidelity is calculated from the exact style.

docs.title: 27.2 Domain tests
docs.text:
For Rust and ECMAScript as implemented:

  • same semantic source + style A/style B -> expected different bytes;
  • deterministic repeated render;
  • invalid style property -> structured diagnostic;
  • comment/directive policies preserve mandatory categories;
  • lossy styles classify correctly.

docs.title: 27.3 Reconciliation tests
docs.text:
Prove at least:

baseline contains canonical comment C
style hides C
user edits visible statement S
reconcile changes S and preserves C

Also prove:

  • a comment visible in baseline and explicitly removed may produce a deletion candidate according to domain rules;
  • concurrent canonical changes still produce correct conflict/merge behavior;
  • style changes after baseline creation do not alter interpretation of old edits;
  • unsupported loss-aware reconciliation produces read-only fidelity.

docs.title: 27.4 Materialization tests
docs.text:
Prove:

  • User A and User B have different personal styles;
  • shared materialization produces the same bytes for both under one workspace policy;
  • changing User A's preference does not mark managed shared files dirty;
  • changing workspace materialization policy deliberately rerenders and establishes a new synchronization baseline.

docs.title: 27.5 Cross-surface tests
docs.text:
Use deterministic fixtures to prove equivalent effective style/fidelity through:

embedded application
remote client/protocol
TUI semantic component
web client/model

Compare semantic/effective style results rather than terminal glyphs or browser pixels.

docs.title: 28. Migration and Compatibility
docs.text:
Do not break all existing projections in one step.

A suitable migration order is:

1. add resolved-style and fidelity contracts
2. retain compatibility constructors for current StyleRef-only render requests
3. implement shared resolver/application discovery
4. migrate one domain renderer (Rust) to prove the contract
5. add ECMA renderer/style support
6. introduce typed reconciliation baselines and baseline artifact retention
7. enable loss-aware editable styles only after tests prove preservation
8. expose shared controls through protocol/web/TUI
9. remove compatibility paths once all active adapters provide exact resolved style

During migration, an adapter that does not support style schema/discovery may expose one fixed exact default style and classify its capabilities conservatively.

docs.title: 29. Ordered Level-3 Work
docs.text:
Implement this design through focused tasks:

151  Implement resolved projection style and style resolution contracts
  |
152  Implement style-aware Rust and ECMAScript source projection rendering
  |
153  Implement loss-aware reconciliation and shared TUI/web style selection

Task 153 must be implemented on the current RPI TUI architecture from Level-2 032/current branch state, not on the superseded local terminal ownership target from Level-2 031.

Where TUI migration work changes files/contracts while these tasks are underway, preserve semantic ownership and adapt to the current upstream component boundary instead of restoring old TUI architecture.

docs.title: 30. Completion Criteria
docs.text:
This Level-2 design is satisfied when:

  • exact style references are resolved to exact renderer-consumable canonical values before rendering;
  • domain adapters advertise/validate meaningful style schemas without leaking language properties into sr-projection;
  • personal view and shared materialization resolution are separate and deterministic;
  • Rust and ECMAScript can render at least meaningful style differences from one canonical semantic source;
  • exact resolved style affects render/cache identity but not semantic source identity;
  • exact editable projection baselines include style/renderer/output evidence;
  • lossy editable styles preserve hidden canonical content through loss-aware reconciliation or are read-only;
  • shared application/protocol/client contracts expose effective style and fidelity;
  • TUI and web consume those shared contracts;
  • rpi-tui remains the terminal framework/theme owner while Scriberig remains the semantic projection/style owner.

docs.title: Rich Project Artifacts: Office, CAD, and Geospatial Implementation Plan
1. Purpose
docs.text:
This document turns level-1/025. compound artifacts scalable collections and rich domain editing.md into an implementation plan for the current Scriberig repository.

It also refines and depends on:

  • level-2/007. projection crate boundaries and core model.md;
  • level-2/008. filesystem projection synchronization.md;
  • level-2/010. universal query and operation implementation.md;
  • level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md;
  • level-2/012. capability matrix and cross surface conformance.md;
  • level-2/016. universal knowledge model rust libraries.md;
  • level-2/017. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md;
  • level-2/019. change history and merge crate design.md;
  • level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md;
  • level-2/025. first useful project workflow vertical slice.md;
  • level-2/027. project wide candidate workspaces validation and materialization.md;
  • level-2/032. upstream first agent runtime and terminal product ownership correction.md;
  • level-2/034. projection style resolution loss-aware reconciliation and cross-surface contracts.md.

The goal is to make a mixed project containing XLSX, DOCX, CAD, QGIS projects, and GIS layers behave like one Scriberig project: semantically navigable, editable through domain operations, candidate-based, reviewable, validated, and materialized through shared infrastructure.

docs.title: 2. Current Repository Baseline
docs.text:
The branch already contains these relevant owners:

crates/scriberig-project
crates/scriberig-core
crates/scriberig-store
crates/scriberig-graph
crates/scriberig-query
crates/sr-change
crates/scriberig-migration
crates/scriberig-projection
crates/sr-projection
crates/sr-projection-fs
crates/scriberig-app
crates/scriberig-protocol
crates/scriberig-client
crates/scriberig-conformance

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-markdown
crates/domains/scriberig-domain-code
crates/domains/scriberig-domain-rust
crates/domains/scriberig-domain-pdf
crates/domains/scriberig-domain-data
crates/domains/scriberig-domain-binary
crates/domains/test-support

web/packages/*
web/apps/scriberig
crates/scriberig-tui
apps/scriberig

The implementation must extend these boundaries first. Do not create a second project catalog, a second change engine, a second projection engine, a second protocol stack, or product-local domain stores.

The current binary domain only describes opaque binary files. It remains a fallback for unsupported artifacts; it must not become the implementation for supported XLSX/DOCX/CAD/GIS semantics.

The current PDF domain is the closest precedent for preserving exact source evidence while deriving richer semantic structure.

docs.title: 3. Implementation Strategy
docs.text:
Implement in this order:

Phase A  shared artifact + scalable collection infrastructure
Phase B  XLSX spreadsheet vertical slice
Phase C  DOCX rich-document vertical slice
Phase D  CAD schema + DXF vertical slice
Phase E  optional DWG provider boundary
Phase F  geospatial datasets + QGIS project vertical slice
Phase G  shared rich projections and cross-surface UI
Phase H  mixed-project conformance and product gates

Do not begin with four unrelated parser integrations. Shared correctness infrastructure must exist before format-specific write support.

docs.title: 4.1 Ownership
docs.text:
Use the existing project/domain/projection boundaries.

Recommended ownership:

scriberig-project
  scan classification
  grouping physical paths into logical imported artifacts
  project-relative source membership

universal graph/schema/domain crates
  artifact entities/revisions/relations as semantic knowledge

sr-projection
  artifact projection identity
  fidelity/editability descriptors
  exact baseline association
  logical output member descriptions

sr-projection-fs
  staged filesystem members
  multi-member write/recovery receipts
  external baseline verification

domain crates
  package/container parsing
  artifact grouping rules specific to the format
  semantic mapping
  rendering/reconciliation

Do not add a new generic scriberig-artifact-store unless implementation audit proves the existing immutable store/blob/projection infrastructure cannot represent exact artifact evidence without architectural distortion. If a new crate is truly required, document the gap in the implementing Level-3 task before adding it.

docs.title: 4.2 Shared types
docs.text:
Introduce or reuse contracts equivalent to:

ArtifactKind
ArtifactMemberId / logical member key
ArtifactMember
ArtifactSourceEvidence
ArtifactExternalReference
ArtifactPreservationMode
ArtifactFidelity
ArtifactMaterializationSet
ArtifactMaterializationReceipt

These names are illustrative. Reuse current repository naming conventions where equivalent types already exist.

docs.title: 4.3 Physical member identity
docs.text:
A member needs:

logical member key
physical target kind
project-relative path or container part name when applicable
exact source/output digest
media/format metadata
required/optional role

Do not use absolute local path as stable semantic identity.

docs.title: 5. Scan and Import Changes
docs.text:
Extend project classification/import so one scan manifest can describe both raw files and logical grouping candidates.

Required behavior:

  1. scanning still records every selected regular file as exact evidence;
  2. classification may nominate a grouping rule;
  3. import groups related files only through deterministic domain rules;
  4. one file may be imported as a compound container without extracting members as project files;
  5. grouped members retain their project-relative paths and digests;
  6. grouping ambiguity becomes a diagnostic instead of silently selecting a dataset;
  7. unsupported artifacts continue through the binary fallback.

Examples:

roads.shp + roads.dbf + roads.shx + roads.prj
  -> one Shapefile artifact

book.xlsx
  -> one OpenXML spreadsheet artifact with logical package parts

project.qgz
  -> one QGIS project artifact with logical package parts

No implicit filesystem rescan is allowed during semantic import; use the persisted scan manifest as already required by project onboarding design.

docs.title: 6.1 Exact source evidence
docs.text:
Every supported rich artifact must retain an exact source digest and retrievable evidence according to existing retention/storage policy.

For packages/multi-file sets, evidence is per member plus an exact artifact manifest identity.

docs.title: 6.2 Opaque preservation record
docs.text:
Domain adapters need an adapter-owned representation for unsupported-but-preserved content.

Do not force unknown bytes into generic semantic property maps.

The preserved content must be bound to:

artifact/member
base source identity
adapter version
location/ownership context
preservation behavior

docs.title: 6.3 Edit safety
docs.text:
Before advertising write support, an adapter must prove one of:

all source-significant content is modeled
or
unmodeled source-significant content is preserved through round trip
or
write support is restricted/read-only

This decision participates in capability discovery.

docs.title: 7.1 Do not change the universal model contract
docs.text: A worksheet cell or GIS feature remains a semantic object from the consumer perspective.

docs.title: 7.2 Add paged/ranged collection access
docs.text:
Extend the current query/list abstractions only where needed to support domain-specific selectors such as:

SpreadsheetRangeSelector
FeatureQuerySelector
SpatialWindow

Prefer domain query AST extensions over adding one universal Any blob selector.

docs.title: 7.3 Stable member handles
docs.text:
Stable semantic handles must be reconstructible/resolvable without enumerating the full collection.

For example, a cell handle may derive from workbook/worksheet identity plus semantic address and reconciliation state, but must still obey the Entity/Revision/Snapshot separation.

A GIS feature may use a stable native feature ID as reconciliation evidence, but Scriberig identity remains separate.

docs.title: 7.4 Indexes
docs.text:
Indexes are derived/rebuildable unless a domain explicitly makes some external index part of canonical source semantics.

Use existing derivation/provenance infrastructure for:

  • used-range indexes;
  • formula dependency indexes;
  • attribute indexes;
  • spatial R-tree-like indexes;
  • CAD layer/block/entity lookup indexes.

docs.title: 8. Projection and Fidelity Extensions
docs.text:
Build on Level-1 024 and Level-2 034.

Projection capabilities must expose at least:

projection kind
resolved style/policy when applicable
fidelity/editability
opaque-preservation status
baseline requirements
supported semantic operations
supported anchors/selections

Add typed non-text anchors in domain crates or shared projection contracts where they are genuinely generic enough.

Avoid one giant universal anchor enum if domain-owned opaque anchor payloads with schema identity fit the existing design better.

Required cross-surface semantics:

selection in UI projection
  -> semantic handle + exact snapshot/revision
  -> application semantic operation
  -> candidate

Never make grid row number, canvas pixel coordinate, map screen coordinate, or terminal row a canonical semantic identity.

docs.title: 9. Compound Materialization
docs.text:
Extend sr-projection-fs or the existing materialization owner with staged multi-member output.

Required state machine:

render complete artifact member set
validate staged set
verify expected external baseline(s)
stage every output
commit/replace members
record per-member + artifact receipt
establish new synchronization baseline

If a platform cannot atomically replace all members, implement explicit recovery journal/receipt semantics. Never report success after updating only some mandatory members.

Container formats such as XLSX/DOCX/QGZ may materialize to one outer file but should still produce logical member diagnostics internally when useful.

docs.title: 10.1 New crate
docs.text:
Add:

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-spreadsheet

This crate owns the format-independent spreadsheet schema/operations.

Add a separate XLSX adapter either as focused modules in that crate initially or as:

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-xlsx

Prefer a separate crate once external OpenXML dependencies or package-specific logic are nontrivial. Do not make generic spreadsheet semantics depend on XLSX implementation types.

docs.title: 10.2 Minimum schema
docs.text:
Implement at least:

Workbook
Worksheet
Cell
Range
Formula
DefinedName
Table
CellStyleRef

Rows/columns may be structural/index concepts rather than one entity per empty row/column. Avoid eager empty-grid expansion.

docs.title: 10.3 Minimum XLSX fidelity
docs.text:
The first vertical slice must support:

  • workbook and sheet names;
  • scalar cell values;
  • formulas as authored expressions;
  • shared strings as an adapter representation detail;
  • basic number/text/date distinction where safely available;
  • used-range discovery;
  • preserving package parts not modified by the operation when possible;
  • deterministic materialization;
  • reopen validation.

Charts, macros, pivot tables, external connections, signatures, and advanced formatting may remain preserved opaque/read-only initially, but their presence must influence fidelity/write capability if the chosen library cannot preserve them.

docs.title: 10.4 Semantic operations
docs.text:
First operations:

spreadsheet.set_cell_value
spreadsheet.set_formula
spreadsheet.rename_sheet
spreadsheet.insert_rows

If insert-row formula rewriting cannot be made correct in the first implementation, do not expose that operation until it is correct. Start with set-cell/set-formula vertical slice.

docs.title: 10.5 Library policy
docs.text:
Evaluate current Rust XLSX libraries during implementation. External library choice is adapter implementation detail and must be documented in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md when required.

Do not let an external library's in-memory object graph become the Scriberig canonical schema.

docs.title: 11. Rich Document Domain and DOCX Adapter
11.1 Shared document concepts
docs.text:
Prefer reuse/alignment with existing Markdown document semantic concepts instead of duplicating Paragraph, TableRow, and TableCell semantics without reason.

Where current Markdown types are format-specific, introduce a small shared rich-document schema crate only if reuse cannot be achieved cleanly through schema specialization.

Recommended new domain crate:

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-document

with DOCX-specific adapter crate/modules:

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-docx

docs.title: 11.2 Minimum schema
docs.text:
Support:

Document
Section
Paragraph
Inline/Run
Table
TableRow
TableCell
ImageReference
Hyperlink

DOCX-specific extension types include:

DocumentStyle
HeaderFooter
Footnote
Endnote
Bookmark
Field
Comment
TrackedChange
ContentControl

Not every extension must be editable in the first slice, but unsupported source-significant structures must be preserved or cause capability degradation.

docs.title: 11.3 First semantic operations
docs.text:
document.replace_paragraph
document.insert_paragraph
document.update_table_cell

docs.title: 11.4 Layout
docs.text: Do not model Word pagination as canonical paragraph identity. Page layout/rendering is derived unless a future adapter/provider proves an exact layout contract.

docs.title: 12. CAD Domain, DXF, and DWG Boundary
12.1 New CAD domain crate
docs.text:
Add:

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-cad

Minimum schema:

Drawing
DrawingSpace
Layout
Layer
BlockDefinition
BlockReference
Line
Polyline
Arc
Circle
Text
Dimension
EntityStyleRef
ExternalReference

docs.title: 12.2 DXF adapter
docs.text:
Implement DXF first because it provides a practical editable interchange target.

The adapter must:

  • parse supported entity types;
  • preserve native handles as external identifiers/provenance;
  • preserve unsupported sections/entities where safe;
  • render deterministic supported DXF;
  • reconcile by native handle plus semantic/structural evidence;
  • validate by reopening output.

First operations:

cad.move_entity
cad.change_layer
cad.update_text
cad.insert_polyline

Start with one or two operations if needed for vertical completion.

docs.title: 12.3 DWG
docs.text:
Do not make a native DWG library a mandatory dependency of the reusable CAD schema.

Implement an adapter-provider interface able to describe:
