docs.title: 10. External effect uncertainty is preserved
docs.text: Use a fake connector that accepts a request but simulates loss of the response. Verify the operation becomes Unknown, is not blindly retried, and can later be reconciled through an external observation.

docs.title: 11. Derived cache cannot bypass confidentiality
docs.text: Populate a cached summary while using a broad principal, then request it as a restricted principal. Verify cache hit is denied without deleting the reusable cache object.

docs.title: 12. Structured denial parity
docs.text: Trigger the same denied semantic operation through at least the direct application path and protocol/client path. Verify action, scope, reason, and approval-possible semantics agree.

docs.title: Audit Reconstruction Test
docs.text:
For one successful candidate, assert that a consumer can reconstruct this chain using semantic references rather than log scraping:

base snapshot
request/proposal
branch/workspace
migration
candidate snapshot
validation evidence
policy evaluation
approval if required
promotion
new canonical snapshot

Do not require private model reasoning traces.

docs.title: Failure-Mode Assertions
docs.text:
Add explicit regression names matching the Level 1 failure modes where practical:

model output is not automatically authoritative
web/imported text cannot grant capability
validation of A cannot promote B
external file edit cannot overwrite concurrent state silently
restricted cache/search cannot leak content
ambiguous reconciliation cannot create false lineage silently
local write cannot invoke unrelated external service
unknown external outcome is not retried as definite failure
stale validation is not presented as current
product surfaces cannot bypass application policy

docs.title: Test Quality Rules
docs.text:
• prefer semantic assertions over exact human-formatted strings;
  • verify IDs/references point to the exact expected revisions/snapshots;
  • never depend on network access;
  • use fake validators/connectors with deterministic behavior;
  • keep each scenario independently diagnosable;
  • do not mark blocked scenarios ignored without an issue/comment explaining the missing prerequisite according to repository conventions.

docs.title: Current Boundary
docs.text: The conformance suite now exercises the implemented production boundaries. Application integration tests cover guarded traversal, search filtering, derived-cache dependency checks, nested restrictions, and reusable immutable cache entries. crates/scriberig-conformance/tests/trust.rs covers exact validation, promotion/CAS, stale candidates, ambiguous projection outcomes, external-effect uncertainty, untrusted content, and application/protocol denial parity. The suite runs as a normal workspace test target and uses only deterministic in-memory fixtures.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run the full Rust workspace tests, protocol conformance tests, and web tests/build required by the repository. The task is complete only when trust conformance tests are part of normal CI or the existing aggregate test command.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not introduce production bypass hooks solely for testing. Do not test authorization only at UI level. Do not rely on textual logs as proof of provenance. Do not use real secrets or real external side effects.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] one deterministic end-to-end trust fixture exists;
  • [x] all ten Level 1 failure classes are covered by regression tests;
  • [x] application and protocol paths agree;
  • [x] provenance/audit chain is reconstructable;
  • [x] ambiguous and failed states stay explicit;
  • [x] cache/search confidentiality is tested;
  • [x] external-effect uncertainty is tested;
  • [x] conformance suite runs in normal project validation/CI.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the first shared application-layer primitives in scriberig-app.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md
  2. design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md
  3. the Level 1 identity/snapshot and change/migration documents that define the canonical ID and migration concepts already implemented by lower crates.

This task creates the reusable operation boundary. It does not implement HTTP, CLI parsing, agent model execution, or domain-specific editing.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
The runtime crate scaffold must exist.

The foundational crates must already expose the real identifier and snapshot types required by this task.

Reuse those types. Do not create duplicate EntityId, RevisionId, SnapshotId, MigrationId, or branch identifiers inside scriberig-app.

If an upstream type is not yet implemented, implement only the portions that can compile without inventing a competing identity model.

docs.title: Files to Create or Replace
docs.text:
Inside crates/scriberig-app/src/ create:

lib.rs
error.rs
context.rs
query.rs
command.rs
operation.rs
event.rs
capability.rs

Keep modules small and documented.

docs.title: context.rs
docs.text:
Define an application request context carrying the semantic base under which an operation runs.

It must be able to express:

  • exact snapshot when one is required;
  • caller/actor provenance in a generic form if the lower-level provenance model already exists;
  • capability/authorization context without embedding UI concepts;
  • a correlation/request identifier where useful.

Do not put HTTP headers, CLI arguments, or model prompts in this type.

Prefer explicit immutable values.

docs.title: error.rs
docs.text:
Define one structured application error enum with variants corresponding to these semantic classes:

NotFound
SchemaViolation
StaleBaseSnapshot
SemanticConflict
ValidationFailure
PermissionDenied
UnsupportedOperation
ProjectionOutOfSync
OperationCancelled
Internal

Use structured fields where existing lower-layer types make that useful.

Each error must implement normal Rust error/display behavior without requiring callers to parse its display string to discover the category.

Do not include HTTP status codes here.

docs.title: operation.rs
docs.text:
Define the application-level long-running operation model.

Required concepts:

OperationId
OperationKind
OperationStatus
OperationProgress
OperationResult reference/summary

Reuse a shared OperationId from scriberig-core if it already exists. If Level 2/3 identity work has not provided it, add it only in the canonical low-level crate, not locally in scriberig-app.

OperationStatus must represent at least:

Queued
Running
Completed
Failed
Cancelled

Ensure terminal states are distinguishable with a helper such as is_terminal().

Do not implement scheduling or threads in this task.

docs.title: event.rs
docs.text:
Define a transport-independent application event enum or equivalent typed model.

Include categories equivalent to:

SnapshotChanged
EntityChanged
ProjectionChanged
BranchChanged
MigrationCreated
OperationStarted
OperationProgressed
OperationCompleted
ValidationCompleted
AgentOutputProduced

Payloads should contain stable handles and concise metadata.

Do not copy full mutable entity state into events.

Do not use server/WebSocket types here.

docs.title: capability.rs
docs.text:
Define a small runtime capability vocabulary suitable for discovery.

The first implementation only needs to express:

  • a stable capability identifier/name;
  • short description;
  • whether it is available in the current application configuration;
  • optional domain/scope metadata if already supported cleanly.

Do not turn this into authorization policy or the repository capability matrix.

Those are separate concerns.

docs.title: query.rs
docs.text:
Define application-level read request/result forms for the first vertical capability: entity inspection.

Required semantic input:

entity
snapshot resolution mode
requested detail level if the existing graph API supports it

The result must identify:

  • the requested entity;
  • exact resolved revision;
  • exact snapshot used;
  • semantic type/summary information exposed by the graph layer.

Do not render terminal text here.

Do not serialize protocol DTOs here.

Use graph/query APIs already defined below the application layer.

If the lower graph API is not yet capable of inspection, keep request/result types and orchestration interfaces minimal rather than bypassing it.

docs.title: command.rs
docs.text:
Define command request boundaries, but do not implement broad mutations yet.

At minimum provide typed placeholders/interfaces for commands whose semantics already exist below the app layer, such as applying a migration against an explicit base snapshot.

Do not create an alternative mutation representation.

A command must delegate canonical change to scriberig-migration/snapshot infrastructure.

If those APIs are not ready, keep the module documented with only types that are justified by implemented lower layers.

docs.title: lib.rs
docs.text:
Re-export only stable application-facing types that callers actually need.

Do not glob-export internal implementation helpers.

Crate documentation should state clearly:

scriberig-app is the shared semantic operation boundary for CLI, server, TUI, clients, and agent adapters.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add unit tests for:

  • every application error category being inspectable without string parsing;
  • OperationStatus::is_terminal() or equivalent;
  • event payloads retaining stable IDs and not owning canonical state;
  • inspect request/result preserving snapshot identity;
  • application types not depending on transport-specific data.

Use compile-time dependencies and normal Rust tests; do not require a network.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not add server routes.
  • Do not define protocol serialization here.
  • Do not add a CLI command.
  • Do not add a model provider.
  • Do not access SQLite directly.
  • Do not duplicate core identifiers.
  • Do not mutate canonical state outside shared migration APIs.
  • Do not implement a general job scheduler.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-app
cargo check --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] All prescribed source modules exist.
  • [x] Semantic errors are structured and transport-neutral.
  • [x] Operation lifecycle types exist with explicit terminal states.
  • [x] Application events carry handles rather than copied canonical state.
  • [x] Runtime capability discovery has a minimal typed model.
  • [x] Entity inspection is represented through snapshot-aware request/result forms.
  • [x] No transport, UI, agent-provider, or database-specific types leaked into the crate.
  • [x] No canonical ID type was duplicated.
  • [x] Tests and workspace checks pass.

docs.title: Implement Protocol Contract and Schema Export
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the first authoritative remote protocol contract in scriberig-protocol and provide a reproducible machine-readable schema export path.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md
  2. design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md
  3. design/level-3/012. implement application operation primitives.md

The protocol must preserve semantic meaning while remaining independent of server routing and persistence internals.

docs.title: Files to Create or Replace
docs.text:
Create:

crates/scriberig-protocol/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/version.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/refs.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/request.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/response.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/error.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/operation.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/event.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/capability.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/bin/export-schema.rs

Update crates/scriberig-protocol/Cargo.toml with only dependencies required for serialization/schema export and shared low-level ID types.

Use the repository's normal serialization stack if one has already been established. Do not introduce a second serialization framework.

docs.title: Authoritative Contract Rule
docs.text:
The Rust types in scriberig-protocol are the authoritative first-version wire contract.

The schema exporter must derive its output from those types.

Do not hand-write a separate JSON schema that can drift from the Rust contract.

Do not create TypeScript protocol types manually in this task.

docs.title: version.rs
docs.text:
Define a protocol major version independent of crate version.

The initial value is:

1

Provide typed structures for version exchange/capability negotiation rather than using an unstructured string.

The design must allow future minor/additive metadata without redefining the major version concept.

docs.title: refs.rs
docs.text:
Define transport-safe wrappers or DTOs for stable references required by the initial protocol:

EntityReference
RevisionReference
SnapshotReference
OperationReference

Use canonical low-level identifiers from scriberig-core when they are already serializable and suitable for public use.

If the internal representation should not be exposed directly, wrap it while preserving round-trip identity.

Never expose database row IDs or backend-specific coordinates.

docs.title: request.rs
docs.text:
Implement the first requests needed for vertical runtime validation:

InspectEntityRequest
RuntimeCapabilitiesRequest
OperationStatusRequest
CancelOperationRequest
SubscribeRequest or equivalent subscription specification

InspectEntityRequest must support explicit snapshot-aware resolution.

Requests must contain semantic inputs, not endpoint paths or HTTP concepts.

docs.title: response.rs
docs.text:
Implement typed responses for the requests above.

InspectEntityResponse must identify:

  • entity;
  • exact resolved revision;
  • exact snapshot;
  • semantic type/summary data needed by generic clients.

Keep response values presentation-neutral.

No ANSI formatting, UI labels, or prompt text belongs here.

docs.title: error.rs
docs.text:
Define a serializable protocol error form that preserves the structured application error category.

It may contain:

code/category
human-readable message
structured details when safe
correlation/request ID where useful

Do not require clients to parse the message string.

Do not encode HTTP status as the primary semantic category.

docs.title: operation.rs
docs.text:
Mirror the public semantic operation lifecycle without importing private scriberig-app implementation structures directly.

Represent at least:

operation reference
kind
Queued
Running
Completed
Failed
Cancelled
progress
final result reference/summary

Add explicit conversion code between app and protocol forms in the appropriate adapter layer rather than making the protocol crate depend on scriberig-app.

docs.title: event.rs
docs.text:
Define serializable event forms for the application event categories supported by the current runtime.

Events must carry stable references and concise metadata.

Do not serialize a full canonical entity as the event payload merely for convenience.

docs.title: capability.rs
docs.text:
Define runtime capability discovery response types.

They must be suitable for generic clients and simpler agents to answer:

  • what operation families are available;
  • what protocol version is active;
  • what optional runtime features are present.

Do not merge authorization rules or capabilities.toml planning state into this protocol model.

docs.title: Schema Export
docs.text:
src/bin/export-schema.rs must generate a deterministic machine-readable schema bundle from the public protocol types.

Preferred output location when invoked by tooling:

target/scriberig-protocol-schema/

Do not commit generated files in this task unless another repository policy explicitly requires committed generated artifacts.

The exporter must fail clearly if schema generation fails.

The same source revision should produce semantically identical schema output.

docs.title: Serialization Tests
docs.text:
Add tests covering:

  • every request and response round trip;
  • every structured error category round trip;
  • operation states round trip;
  • representative events round trip;
  • protocol version data round trip;
  • stable ID/reference round trips;
  • schema exporter executes successfully.

Tests must not depend on a running server.

docs.title: Compatibility Discipline
docs.text:
For protocol-facing enums expected to evolve additively, choose serialization behavior deliberately.

Do not silently use Rust enum representation details as an accidental wire format.

Document the chosen tagged representation in crate-level docs or tests.

Avoid renaming serialized fields casually after this task lands.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not add server routes.
  • Do not add an HTTP framework.
  • Do not add TypeScript convenience clients.
  • Do not expose internal database rows.
  • Do not make scriberig-protocol depend on scriberig-app or scriberig-server.
  • Do not encode product presentation strings as semantic contract fields.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol
cargo run -p scriberig-protocol --bin export-schema
cargo check --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] All prescribed protocol modules exist.
  • [x] Protocol major version is explicitly represented and starts at 1.
  • [x] Stable references contain no backend implementation details.
  • [x] Initial inspect/capability/operation requests and responses exist.
  • [x] Errors preserve machine-readable semantic categories.
  • [x] Operations and events have serializable public forms.
  • [x] Schema export is generated from authoritative Rust types.
  • [x] No separate hand-maintained wire model was introduced.
  • [x] Protocol crate has no dependency on app/server internals.
  • [x] Round-trip and schema checks pass.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Complete the first executable vertical slice of Scriberig projections by wiring the generic projection layer, filesystem synchronization, Markdown adapter, migration/change layer, and storage backend into one end-to-end conformance scenario.

This task should not add new architecture unless a missing lower-layer contract is proven by the integration work. Prefer fixing the responsible lower layer and adding its local tests.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read all projection Level 2 designs:

  1. design/level-2/007. projection crate boundaries and core model.md
  2. design/level-2/008. filesystem projection synchronization.md
  3. design/level-2/009. markdown editable projection adapter.md

Read Level 3 tasks 007 through 013 and the Level 1 documents they reference.

docs.title: Files to create/modify
docs.text:
Create an integration test file at a location consistent with the workspace's existing testing convention. Prefer:

crates/sr-markdown/tests/file_sync.rs

If cross-crate integration tests already have a dedicated workspace crate/directory, use that established location instead and document the choice in the test module.

Modify lower-level files only to fix defects revealed by the acceptance scenarios.

Do not create CLI/API/UI/agent code merely to drive this test.

docs.title: Test harness
docs.text:
Use:

  • temporary filesystem directory;
  • in-memory storage backend where possible;
  • real sr-change migration/diff behavior;
  • real generic projection contracts;
  • real filesystem projection synchronization service;
  • real Markdown parser/renderer/reconciler;
  • fake/deterministic observation source instead of relying on OS watcher timing for most tests.

The test must exercise public crate APIs rather than reaching into private internals.

docs.title: Acceptance scenario 1: initial projection
docs.text:
Construct canonical Markdown semantic state equivalent to:

# Architecture

## Storage

Objects are immutable.

## Rendering

Files are projections.

Then:

  1. persist/construct the canonical state using existing graph/store APIs;
  2. create a managed editable Markdown projection specification;
  3. render it to architecture.md;
  4. verify exact file exists;
  5. verify synchronization state records the canonical base and exact rendered digest;
  6. verify a synthetic watcher event for the just-written file does not trigger import.

docs.title: Acceptance scenario 2: external semantic edit
docs.text:
Externally replace the file contents with:

# Architecture

## Storage

Objects are immutable and content addressed.

## Sessions

Sessions use the same object store.

## Rendering

Files are projections.

Feed a modification observation.

Verify:

  • file is detected as externally changed;
  • parser creates a candidate, not canonical identities;
  • Storage paragraph keeps its conceptual entity and gets a new revision;
  • Sessions section/entities are newly created;
  • unchanged Rendering section/entities retain their IDs/revisions where their own state did not change;
  • parent collection revisions change only where structure changed;
  • a migration records external-projection provenance;
  • a new snapshot/result is produced and promoted through normal change rules;
  • canonical state is rerendered;
  • new exact file digest becomes synchronization base;
  • a watcher event for rerendered output does not cause another semantic migration.

docs.title: Acceptance scenario 3: formatting-only edit
docs.text:
Modify the synchronized file only in ways the Markdown adapter defines as presentation-equivalent, such as supported list marker/spacing or blank-line differences in a fixture containing those constructs.

Verify:

  • byte digest changes;
  • parser/reconciler runs;
  • result is NoSemanticChange;
  • no new semantic migration/snapshot is created solely for formatting;
  • configured canonical style may rerender the file;
  • synchronization returns to a stable base.

docs.title: Acceptance scenario 4: invalid transient edit
docs.text:
Write external content that the supported Markdown adapter treats as invalid/unimportable.

Verify:

  • canonical snapshot remains unchanged;
  • synchronization base remains the previous valid base;
  • projection enters ImportFailed or equivalent;
  • structured diagnostic contains parse/import stage information;
  • fixing the file and sending another event retries successfully.

docs.title: Acceptance scenario 5: concurrent disjoint changes
docs.text:
From synchronization base B:

  1. change canonical Storage paragraph through a normal semantic migration to produce D;
  2. independently edit external file to insert a new paragraph/section elsewhere;
  3. process the external modification.

Verify:

  • reconciliation receives B, D, and F;
  • semantic changes are disjoint and merge automatically;
  • resulting snapshot contains both changes;
  • resulting file is rerendered from merged canonical state;
  • new synchronization base points to merged snapshot.

docs.title: Acceptance scenario 6: concurrent conflicting change
docs.text:
From a fresh synchronized base:

  1. change one paragraph canonically;
  2. change the same paragraph externally to incompatible text;
  3. process the event.

Verify:

  • no canonical overwrite occurs;
  • conflict is structured and identifies base/current/external semantic states;
  • projection state becomes conflict/attention-required;
  • external file is not silently normalized over the user's conflict;
  • synchronization base remains the original base until resolved.

docs.title: Acceptance scenario 7: unmanaged/read-only safety
docs.text:
Create one unmanaged file and one managed read-only generated file.

Verify:

  • unmanaged file is never rewritten or imported;
  • read-only file may be generated;
  • external modification of read-only file does not create semantic migration;
  • behavior is surfaced as drift/regeneration policy rather than semantic import.

docs.title: Acceptance scenario 8: rename/path independence
docs.text:
Rename/move the editable Markdown projection to another configured path using the supported mapping operation/event path.

Verify:

  • projection/path metadata changes;
  • semantic document/paragraph identities do not change solely due to path;
  • subsequent rendering/import works from the new location.

docs.title: Invariants to assert directly
docs.text:
Where APIs make it possible, assert:

  • exact unchanged entity revisions are reused;
  • global snapshot changes only for canonical semantic/config changes, not mere external formatting;
  • formatting-only edit changes projection bytes but not semantic revisions;
  • synchronization state advances only after successful commit and file write;
  • failed import leaves recoverable external state/base;
  • all canonical writes are represented by normal migration/change APIs.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
At minimum:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-projection
cargo test -p sr-projection-fs
cargo test -p sr-markdown
cargo test --workspace

If the repository has linting configured, run the workspace lint command as well.

docs.title: Failure handling while implementing
docs.text:
If an acceptance scenario fails because a lower-layer public API is missing:

  1. identify which existing Level 2/3 responsibility owns it;
  2. extend that layer minimally;
  3. add a focused unit/conformance test there;
  4. keep the integration test using the public API;
  5. do not add an integration-only bypass.

If a requested feature depends on an unimplemented prerequisite from earlier design work, implement only the minimum prerequisite contract needed and clearly keep it within the earlier design's invariants.

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not add agent behavior.
  • Do not create HTTP/CLI/UI shortcuts.
  • Do not manipulate storage backend tables directly from tests.
  • Do not make test-only hidden IDs part of Markdown.
  • Do not replace semantic reconciliation with textual diff.
  • Do not weaken conflict handling merely to make the acceptance test pass.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Initial Markdown projection renders and synchronizes.
  • [x] External semantic edit becomes a normal semantic migration.
  • [x] Unchanged entities are reused.
  • [x] Formatting-only edit creates no semantic history.
  • [x] Invalid edits are recoverable.
  • [x] Disjoint concurrent changes merge.
  • [x] Conflicting concurrent changes remain structured conflicts.
  • [x] Unmanaged/read-only safety rules hold.
  • [x] Path move does not redefine semantic identity.
  • [x] Full workspace tests pass.

Stop when all acceptance scenarios and checks pass.

docs.title: Expose Inspect Through CLI and Agent Adapters
Objective
docs.text:
Expose the existing inspect entity application capability through two additional consumers:

  • the command-line surface;
  • the reusable agent-tool adapter.

Also wire the scriberig executable far enough to run the CLI inspect path locally.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md
  2. design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md
  3. design/level-3/012. implement application operation primitives.md
  4. design/level-3/014. implement server client inspect transport.md

This task proves that CLI and agent consumers reuse application semantics instead of reaching into storage.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
crates/scriberig-cli/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-cli/src/command.rs
crates/scriberig-cli/src/inspect.rs
crates/scriberig-cli/src/output.rs

docs.title: Agent Core
docs.text:
crates/scriberig-agent-core/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-agent-core/src/tool.rs
crates/scriberig-agent-core/src/inspect.rs
crates/scriberig-agent-core/src/capability.rs

docs.title: Executable
docs.text:
apps/scriberig/src/main.rs

Update relevant manifests only for dependencies needed by this slice.

Do not implement TUI behavior in this task.

Do not implement a model provider or agent tool loop.

docs.title: CLI Command
docs.text:
Add an inspect command with input concepts equivalent to:

scriberig inspect <entity-id> [--snapshot <snapshot-id>]

Use the CLI parsing framework already chosen by the repository. If none has been prescribed, choose one established Rust CLI parser and keep all parser-specific types inside scriberig-cli.

The command must:

  1. parse the entity identifier using canonical ID parsing;
  2. optionally parse an explicit snapshot;
  3. invoke the shared application inspect operation;
  4. render a concise human-readable result;
  5. return a non-zero exit status on structured failure.

The CLI must not query graph/store crates directly.

docs.title: CLI Output
docs.text:
output.rs owns terminal presentation.

For a successful inspect include at least:

entity
resolved revision
snapshot
semantic type/name or short description when available

Do not make the text format the public machine API.

Do not duplicate protocol DTOs solely to format terminal output.

For errors, map application categories to clear human-readable messages while retaining category information internally.

docs.title: Application Construction
docs.text:
The final executable must construct the local application stack through a composition function/builder already present or a minimal composition path added for this purpose.

main.rs should only:

parse/receive CLI entry
construct dependencies
invoke scriberig-cli dispatcher
map final result to process exit

Do not place inspect semantics in main.rs.

If the actual storage backend is not yet ready, tests may use an injected fake application service. Do not commit a fake production database implementation merely to make the command run.

docs.title: Agent Tool Model
docs.text:
In scriberig-agent-core, define a generic tool contract that can describe and invoke application-backed tools without knowing a specific model provider.

The first concrete adapter is an inspect tool.

Its input must contain semantic fields equivalent to:

entity
optional snapshot
detail level if supported

Its result must contain a compact structured summary with stable handles.

Do not return raw source files or unrestricted database data.

Do not add prompt templates tied to one model vendor.

docs.title: Agent Capability Filtering
docs.text:
capability.rs should expose whether the inspect tool is available under the current application capability context.

Do not rely on merely hiding the tool description for security.

The application operation must still enforce capability/authorization checks.

The agent layer only reflects the allowed surface.

docs.title: Progressive Disclosure
docs.text:
The inspect tool should default to a compact result.

It should expose enough information for a model to choose a next semantic action:

  • object type;
  • short description if available;
  • counts or relation summaries when already provided by the application layer;
  • stable handles for follow-up inspection.

Do not serialize the entire underlying object graph by default.

Do not invent summaries in the agent adapter if the shared semantic/derived layer already provides them.

docs.title: CLI tests
docs.text:
Test command dispatch against an injected deterministic application fixture:

  • known entity succeeds;
  • explicit snapshot is preserved;
  • missing entity returns failure without panic;
  • output includes stable entity/revision/snapshot handles;
  • CLI code never requires direct store access.

Avoid snapshot-testing incidental whitespace as the primary semantic assertion.

docs.title: Agent adapter tests
docs.text:
Verify:

  • tool input maps to the same application inspect request;
  • snapshot identity is preserved;
  • result exposes stable handles;
  • denied capability produces a structured failure;
  • the tool does not access storage directly.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not implement an LLM/provider client.
  • Do not implement the full agent runtime loop.
  • Do not add TUI widgets.
  • Do not add server-specific code to the CLI.
  • Do not call SQLite, graph internals, or domain parsers from CLI/agent adapter code.
  • Do not create a second inspect implementation.
  • Do not make CLI output a wire protocol.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-cli
cargo test -p scriberig-agent-core
cargo check --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

If the executable can be constructed with a real local backend at this point, also run a simple local inspect smoke test. If not, do not fake production functionality; rely on injected tests.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] CLI inspect command exists and delegates to scriberig-app.
  • [x] CLI accepts optional explicit snapshot context.
  • [x] Terminal presentation is isolated from semantics.
  • [x] apps/scriberig remains a thin composition root.
  • [x] Agent core has a provider-neutral tool contract.
  • [x] Agent inspect adapter delegates to the same application operation.
  • [x] Agent result supports progressive disclosure and stable handles.
  • [x] Capability denial remains enforced below the tool-description layer.
  • [x] Neither CLI nor agent adapter accesses persistence directly.
  • [x] Tests and workspace checks pass.

docs.title: Create Capability Matrix and Conformance Harness
Objective
docs.text:
Create the concrete planning and test artifacts prescribed by:

  1. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md
  2. design/level-2/012. capability matrix and cross surface conformance.md

This task creates the repository-visible capability matrix and a dedicated non-published conformance crate.

The harness must verify semantic equivalence across public boundaries without depending on external services.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
The following should already exist or be in progress:

  • scriberig-app operation primitives;
  • scriberig-protocol contract;
  • scriberig-server and scriberig-client in-process transport path;
  • CLI and agent inspect adapters.

If some surfaces are not implemented yet, record them truthfully as planned. Do not create fake implementations just to make the matrix green.

docs.title: Files to Create
docs.text:
Create:

capabilities.toml

crates/scriberig-conformance/Cargo.toml
crates/scriberig-conformance/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-conformance/tests/inspect.rs
crates/scriberig-conformance/tests/protocol.rs
crates/scriberig-conformance/tests/operations.rs
crates/scriberig-conformance/tests/events.rs

Add crates/scriberig-conformance to the root Cargo workspace.

Set:

publish = false

Production crates must not depend on this crate.

docs.title: capabilities.toml
docs.text:
Create entries for exactly these initial capabilities:

inspect_entity
runtime_capabilities
operation_status
operation_cancel
event_subscription

Each entry has:

id
description
semantic_owner
surface status table

Use these surface keys exactly:

library
app
protocol
server
client
cli
tui
web
agent

Use only these status values:

not_applicable
planned
implemented
verified

Do not mark a surface implemented unless the corresponding code exists.

Do not mark a surface verified unless an appropriate test proves the semantic behavior.

At the end of this task inspect_entity should normally be the most complete entry. TUI and web may remain planned.

docs.title: Conformance Crate Dependencies
docs.text:
The conformance crate may use public APIs from runtime packages under test, including:

scriberig-app
scriberig-protocol
scriberig-client
scriberig-server
scriberig-agent-core

It may also use foundational test fixtures needed to build a deterministic semantic world.

Do not depend on private module paths.

Do not make any production crate depend on scriberig-conformance.

docs.title: Deterministic Fixture
docs.text:
Implement fixture helpers in src/lib.rs or a small internal module.

The fixture must create:

  • deterministic temporary/in-memory semantic storage using the supported test backend;
  • one explicit snapshot;
  • at least one inspectable entity with a known revision;
  • an application instance bound to that state;
  • a server dispatcher;
  • an in-process client transport;
  • an agent inspect adapter when available.

The fixture must not use:

  • external HTTP;
  • a model provider;
  • user home-directory configuration;
  • real project files outside the test temp area;
  • current time as semantic identity unless explicitly controlled.

docs.title: tests/inspect.rs
docs.text:
Use the same fixture to invoke inspect through each implemented surface that exposes a callable public API.

At minimum compare:

application inspect
server/client inspect
agent inspect adapter

If the CLI library exposes a structured dispatch path that can be called without scraping process output, include it as well.

Verify semantic equality of:

  • entity ID;
  • resolved revision ID;
  • snapshot ID;
  • semantic type/name/description fields supported by the current API;
  • structured error category for a missing entity.

Do not require byte-identical presentation strings.

docs.title: tests/protocol.rs
docs.text:
Verify public contract stability basics:

  • inspect request/response round trip;
  • capability response round trip;
  • structured error round trip;
  • operation status round trip;
  • representative event round trip;
  • protocol major version metadata;
  • schema exporter runs successfully if exposed as callable tooling or subprocess in tests.

Do not snapshot Rust Debug output as the wire contract.

docs.title: tests/operations.rs
docs.text:
Create a deterministic fake/test operation using the public application operation mechanism.

Verify:

  • one stable operation ID is used throughout its lifecycle;
  • legal status progression reaches a terminal state;
  • terminal states do not regress;
  • operation status survives server/client transport;
  • cancellation produces a structured status/result when cancellation support is implemented;
  • a disconnected observer is not required for the final result to exist.

If cancellation has not been implemented yet, keep the relevant capability planned and test only implemented lifecycle behavior.

docs.title: tests/events.rs
docs.text:
Using the public event path available at the time of implementation, verify:

  • event subject IDs survive adapter/transport conversion;
  • an event can be associated with the operation or entity that caused it;
  • a consumer can resolve authoritative state through normal application/client queries after the event;
  • the event payload is not treated as an independently mutable copy of canonical state.

If streaming transport has not yet been implemented, test the application/server event conversion boundary and leave event_subscription surfaces truthfully marked planned where necessary.

docs.title: Matrix Validation Test
docs.text:
Add a test/helper that parses the root capabilities.toml and rejects:

  • duplicate capability IDs;
  • unknown surface keys;
  • unknown status values;
  • missing semantic owner;
  • empty descriptions.

Use a normal TOML parser already present in the workspace when possible.

Do not make capabilities.toml control runtime permissions or Cargo features.

docs.title: Updating Statuses
docs.text:
After all tests pass, update matrix statuses truthfully.

A useful rule:

implemented = code path exists
verified = code path exists and the conformance harness exercises it

Do not use verified merely because a unit test exists in the implementation crate if the matrix is intended to claim cross-surface equivalence.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not build a web UI.
  • Do not build a TUI just for test coverage.
  • Do not add a network dependency to the fixture.
  • Do not weaken semantic assertions to make differing implementations pass.
  • Do not make presentation formatting part of semantic equality.
  • Do not use the capability matrix as authorization configuration.
  • Do not add runtime business logic to the conformance crate.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-conformance
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

Also inspect cargo tree -p scriberig-conformance and verify no production crate has acquired a reverse dependency on the conformance crate.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] capabilities.toml exists with exactly the prescribed first entries.
  • [x] Status and surface vocabularies are consistent.
  • [x] scriberig-conformance exists and is publish = false.
  • [x] Fixture is deterministic and uses no external services.
  • [x] Inspect semantics are compared across implemented public surfaces.
  • [x] Protocol round-trip checks exist.
  • [x] Operation lifecycle conformance checks exist.
  • [x] Event boundary conformance checks exist to the extent implemented.
  • [x] Matrix validation rejects malformed entries.
  • [x] Statuses are truthful; unimplemented TUI/web/event paths remain planned rather than faked.
  • [x] Production crates do not depend on the conformance crate.
  • [x] Workspace tests and Clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement Find and the Structured Query AST
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the universal discovery and structured query vocabulary in scriberig-query.

This task adds:

  • find request/result types for ranked or approximate discovery;
  • a storage-independent declarative query AST for exact structural selection;
  • a query execution boundary that operates against exact snapshots;
  • structured unsupported-query behavior;
  • composable semantic results.

This task does not implement application-layer diff/history/render/change composition, protocol transport, UI behavior, or domain-specific high-level edits.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md
  2. design/level-2/010. universal query and operation implementation.md
  3. design/level-3/015. implement universal query handles scope and pagination.md
  4. design/level-3/016. implement inspect list and follow read operations.md
  5. universal graph/schema implementation designs
  6. derived-knowledge/caching design, especially provenance and exact dependency rules

Inspect the current scriberig-query APIs and preserve established naming where reasonable.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Within crates/scriberig-query/:

src/lib.rs
src/find.rs
src/query.rs
src/result.rs
src/error.rs

tests/universal_read_model.rs

Do not modify concrete storage backends unless an already-defined generic provider trait requires a narrowly scoped test implementation elsewhere.

docs.title: 1. Implement Find Strategy
docs.text:
In src/find.rs, implement an extensible FindStrategy or equivalent capable of expressing at least:

ExactText
Token
StructuredName
Semantic
DomainSpecific(String or stable capability id)

Do not claim that every provider supports every strategy.

The request/executor must allow a provider to return UnsupportedCapability for a strategy it cannot perform.

docs.title: 2. Implement Find Request
docs.text:
Implement FindRequest with conceptual fields:

scope: QueryScope
query: search text/expression
strategy: FindStrategy
page: PageRequest
requested detail: DetailLevel

The scope already carries an exact SnapshotId.

Do not add a hidden current-snapshot lookup to the query crate.

docs.title: 3. Implement Find Hits
docs.text:
Implement FindHit with at least:

semantic handle
entity type
short label/description
optional preview
optional score/rank
optional projection anchor
optional provenance/derivation summary

If a source is only a raw resource and cannot yet be mapped to a semantic entity, model that explicitly rather than inventing a fake entity.

When semantic correspondence exists, the semantic handle is primary; byte/line/page offsets are anchors only.

Implement FindResult with:

scope/snapshot
strategy
Page<FindHit>

docs.title: 4. Define the Query Expression AST
docs.text:
In src/query.rs, create a small declarative AST.

It must represent at least logical equivalents of:

All
TypeIs
PropertyEq
PropertyExists
Related
MemberOf / ContainedIn
And
Or
Not

Use existing universal property values and type/relation/collection identifiers.

Do not embed raw SQL, backend table names, closures, function pointers, or non-serializable storage objects in the public AST.

Keep recursion explicit and bounded by normal memory limits; do not add arbitrary scripting/evaluation.

docs.title: 5. Query Specification
docs.text:
Implement a QuerySpec or equivalent with fields for:

scope
expression
ordering
page/limit
requested detail

Provide simple universal ordering concepts such as:

StableDefault
Property { key, direction }

Only add ordering variants that can have domain-independent semantics.

Do not promise relevance ranking for exact structural query; relevance belongs primarily to find unless a specific query predicate defines it.

docs.title: 6. Relation Traversal Predicates
docs.text:
Related must preserve relation identity.

A useful conceptual form is:

Related {
    relation,
    direction,
    target: Box<QueryExpr>,
}

This allows expressions like:

TypeIs(Function)
AND
Related(calls, TypeIs(PaymentProvider))

Use the schema/graph relation model already implemented.

If reverse traversal requires a derived index that is not available, query execution must return a structured unsupported/derived-data failure rather than silently changing semantics.

docs.title: 7. Collection Membership Predicates
docs.text:
Provide a collection-membership expression using the established collection identifiers.

The initial AST only needs to express useful membership/containment relationships.

Do not add positional slicing, arbitrary recursive path languages, or XPath-like syntax unless another design explicitly requires it.

Keep the first query model small and composable.

docs.title: 8. Query Result
docs.text:
Implement a semantic QueryRow or QueryHit and QueryResult.

At minimum return:

semantic handle
entity type
optional compact metadata

The result must report the exact snapshot/scope and page continuation.

Avoid returning loosely typed maps as the only result format.

A later query projection may render rows differently, but the core result should remain directly usable by another operation.

docs.title: 9. Execution Boundary
docs.text:
Expose a FindService/QueryService trait or integrate with the read-service trait already created.

The executor must operate against graph/index provider abstractions.

Do not put SQL planning inside the public query model.

It is acceptable for the first implementation to execute a limited subset in memory over a graph test provider.

When an AST node is understood by the model but not supported by the provider, return a structured error identifying the unsupported expression/capability.

Do not silently drop predicates.

docs.title: 10. Determinism and Provenance
docs.text:
query should be deterministic for its declared canonical inputs except where it explicitly consumes derived data whose provenance is reported.

find may be ranked or approximate.

When semantic or model-derived search is used, return enough provenance/strategy metadata for callers to distinguish it from canonical structural facts.

Do not represent a semantic-similarity rank as a canonical relation.

docs.title: 11. Tests
docs.text:
Extend tests/universal_read_model.rs to cover at least:

  1. exact text find returns semantic handles in scope;
  2. a find hit can be inspected directly without rediscovery;
  3. unsupported semantic find strategy returns UnsupportedCapability rather than falling back silently;
  4. query by TypeIs works against an in-memory graph provider;
  5. query by property equality works;
  6. And, Or, and Not compose correctly;
  7. relation traversal can constrain a query;
  8. collection membership can constrain a query;
  9. reverse relation query without required derived support returns a structured failure;
  10. query results report the exact snapshot used;
  11. page limits and continuation are preserved;
  12. the public AST contains no SQL/backend-specific concepts;
  13. malformed/unsupported query expressions produce structured InvalidQuery or UnsupportedCapability errors;
  14. a newer snapshot appearing during/after evaluation does not alter the result's snapshot identity.

Run:

cargo test -p scriberig-query
cargo check --workspace

docs.title: 12. Non-Goals
docs.text:
Do not implement:

  • a text query language parser;
  • GraphQL;
  • SQL generation as a public contract;
  • embeddings or model calls themselves;
  • diff/history/render;
  • branch/apply/commit;
  • protocol serialization;
  • CLI syntax;
  • agent tool schemas.

docs.title: Completion Criteria
docs.text:
This task is complete when:

  • find supports extensible discovery strategies and semantic results;
  • the structured query AST covers the initial Level 1 structural concepts;
  • the AST is independent of storage implementation;
  • exact snapshot scope is preserved in every request/result;
  • unsupported provider capabilities fail explicitly;
  • query/find results return handles reusable by inspect, list, and follow;
  • tests demonstrate composability and the find versus query distinction.

docs.title: Implement Universal Application Request, Result, and Capability Model
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the transport-independent universal application vocabulary in scriberig-app.

This task creates the request/result enums or equivalent typed command model for all eleven universal operations and the capability descriptors needed for discoverable clients.

It does not implement transport endpoints, CLI commands, React hooks, agent tools, or the actual diff/history/render/change engines. Later tasks wire those engines into the application service.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md
  2. design/level-2/010. universal query and operation implementation.md
  3. design/level-3/015. implement universal query handles scope and pagination.md
  4. design/level-3/016. implement inspect list and follow read operations.md
  5. design/level-3/017. implement find and structured query ast.md
  6. design/level-2/001. workspace and package layout.md
  7. existing change/history and projection Level 2 designs

Inspect the workspace and use the canonical scriberig-app crate. If it has not been scaffolded by prerequisite workspace work, create it only at the path prescribed by the workspace design and register it there. Do not create a second application crate.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Within crates/scriberig-app/:

Cargo.toml
src/lib.rs
src/request.rs
src/result.rs
src/capability.rs

You may add narrowly scoped private helper modules only if necessary.

Do not edit protocol, server, client, CLI, TUI, agent-runtime, or web packages.

docs.title: 1. Dependencies
docs.text:
Add dependencies only on established reusable crates required by the public application vocabulary, primarily:

scriberig-core
scriberig-query
scriberig-migration / change subsystem public types
scriberig-projection public types

If history/diff types live in a distinct canonical crate, depend on that crate rather than duplicating them.

The app crate must not depend on HTTP, terminal UI, model providers, or browser packages.

docs.title: 2. Universal Operation Kind
docs.text:
Define a stable domain-independent OperationKind or equivalent covering exactly the Level 1 universal grammar:

Inspect
List
Follow
Find
Query
Diff
History
Render
Branch
Apply
Commit

This type identifies semantic operation kind only.

Do not add surface-specific variants such as HttpInspect, CliQuery, or AgentRender.

Domain-specific high-level operations should use a separate extensible capability identifier rather than endlessly expanding this universal enum.

docs.title: 3. Application Request
docs.text:
In src/request.rs, define an AppRequest/ApplicationRequest enum or an equivalent typed command family with one variant for each universal operation.

Reuse request types already owned by scriberig-query for:

Inspect
List
Follow
Find
Query

For the remaining operations, carry canonical subsystem request/spec types where they already exist rather than cloning their entire model into the app crate.

The application request must be transport-neutral.

Do not include:

  • URL paths;
  • HTTP methods/headers;
  • CLI flags;
  • terminal rendering preferences;
  • React state;
  • model-provider settings.

docs.title: 4. Snapshot Resolution Input
docs.text:
Allow convenience requests to indicate that the application layer should resolve a named/current root only through an explicit application-level selector.

A useful abstraction is conceptually:

SnapshotSelector {
    Exact(SnapshotId),
    NamedRoot(RootName),
}

If another canonical type already represents named roots, reuse it.

Do not put Current into scriberig-query scopes.

Before dispatching any canonical read, the application service must later resolve this selector to one exact SnapshotId and return that exact ID in the result.

This task only defines the request vocabulary; service resolution is implemented later.

docs.title: 5. Universal Application Result
docs.text:
In src/result.rs, define an AppResult/ApplicationResult enum or equivalent typed result family.

Provide variants for:

Inspect
List
Follow
Find
Query
Diff
History
Render
Branch
Apply
Commit
OperationStarted

Reuse canonical result types from owning crates.

Do not flatten structured results into String.

Every result that describes canonical state must expose the exact snapshot/revision/branch context used or contain an underlying result type that does so.

docs.title: 6. Capability Identifiers
docs.text:
In src/capability.rs, define stable extensible identifiers for capabilities that go beyond the universal eleven operations.

Distinguish categories equivalent to:

RelationCapability
CollectionCapability
ViewCapability
DomainOperationCapability
FindStrategyCapability

A capability identifier should be serializable later without using Rust type names as its public identity.

Use a stable string/newtype or established typed identifier convention.

docs.title: 7. Capability Descriptor
docs.text:
Implement a common descriptor structure with fields equivalent to:

id
kind
short label
short description
applicable entity types (optional)
availability
canonical/derived classification where relevant
estimated information cost (optional)

Specialized descriptors may include:

  • relation target/cardinality/direction;
  • collection ordering;
  • view style/projection requirements;
  • domain-operation input hints.

Keep these hints declarative and transport-neutral.

Do not encode executable closures/function pointers in descriptors.

docs.title: 8. Domain Operation Request Envelope
docs.text:
Provide an extensible application-level envelope for a high-level domain operation without adding every future operation to OperationKind.

Conceptually:

DomainOperationRequest {
    capability: CapabilityId,
    subject: semantic handle/selection,
    branch/workspace: change context,
    arguments: typed or schema-described values,
}

Prefer existing universal KnowledgeValue or schema/value types for arguments if they are sufficient.

Do not use arbitrary JSON as the only in-process representation.

Document that domain operations must eventually produce ordinary semantic changes through the canonical branch/migration system.

docs.title: 9. Referential Results
docs.text:
Ensure application results expose semantic handles directly.

A caller must never need to parse a rendered message such as:

"Function process_payment"

to recover the target for a follow-up request.

Where a canonical subsystem result lacks a reusable handle, add an application wrapper field rather than relying on display text.

docs.title: 10. Public Exports
docs.text:
Update src/lib.rs so later surfaces can import:

OperationKind
ApplicationRequest
ApplicationResult
SnapshotSelector
CapabilityId
CapabilityDescriptor
DomainOperationRequest

or the established equivalent names.

Avoid exposing private service implementation details here.

docs.title: 11. Tests
docs.text:
Add focused unit tests verifying:

  1. every universal operation has a request representation;
  2. every universal operation has a structured result representation;
  3. query request/result types are reused rather than copied into new incompatible structs;
  4. application requests contain no transport/UI-specific fields;
  5. exact and named-root snapshot selectors are distinguishable;
  6. capability IDs survive clone/equality/hash use as appropriate;
  7. a capability descriptor can describe a relation, view, and domain operation;
  8. a domain operation request identifies its branch/change context;
  9. results retain semantic handles;
  10. no test needs an HTTP server or database backend.

Run:

cargo test -p scriberig-app
cargo check --workspace

docs.title: 12. Non-Goals
docs.text:
Do not implement:

  • dispatch/service execution;
  • named-root lookup itself;
  • diff/history/render algorithms;
  • branch/apply/commit algorithms;
  • validation policy;
  • operation scheduling;
  • HTTP/CLI/TUI/web/agent adapters.

docs.title: Completion Criteria
docs.text:
This task is complete when:

  • scriberig-app contains one transport-independent vocabulary for all eleven universal operations;
  • later surfaces can depend on one request/result model instead of inventing their own semantics;
  • exact-vs-named snapshot selection is explicit at the application boundary;
  • capability discovery has stable extensible descriptors;
  • high-level domain operations have an extensible envelope tied to branch/change context;
  • all public results remain structured and referential.

docs.title: Integrate Universal Read, Diff, History, Render, and Change Operations
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the scriberig-app service layer that dispatches the universal application grammar onto the canonical subsystems already owned by query, history/change, projection, and migration libraries.

This task is about composition, not duplication.

The application layer must provide one transport-independent execution boundary for:

inspect
list
follow
find
query
diff
history
render
branch
apply
commit

while preserving exact snapshot context, structured results, explicit change semantics, and subsystem ownership.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md
  2. design/level-2/010. universal query and operation implementation.md
  3. design/level-3/018. implement universal application request result and capability model.md
  4. Level 3 query read-operation tasks
  5. Level 2 and Level 3 change/history designs
  6. Level 2 and Level 3 projection designs
  7. named-root/snapshot implementation tasks

Inspect the actual public APIs that exist in the canonical subsystem crates and adapt to them. Do not create a second diff, history, projection, branch, migration, or commit engine because an exact method name differs from this document.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Within crates/scriberig-app/:

src/lib.rs
src/service.rs
src/request.rs        # only if integration requires small additions
src/result.rs         # only if integration requires small additions
src/error.rs

tests/universal_operation_model.rs

Modify Cargo.toml only to depend on already-established canonical subsystem crates.

Do not edit server/CLI/TUI/web/agent adapters.

docs.title: 1. Define the Application Service Boundary
docs.text:
In src/service.rs, define a public service trait or concrete facade following existing project conventions.

It must execute the universal request vocabulary and return the universal result vocabulary.

A simple conceptual boundary is:

execute(ApplicationRequest) -> ApplicationResult

Typed convenience methods such as inspect(...) or render(...) may also be provided.

Do not force every caller to construct one enum if typed methods improve Rust ergonomics, but all methods must share the same semantic implementation path.

docs.title: 2. Inject Canonical Subsystem Providers
docs.text:
The application service should depend on provider traits/objects for:

query/read service
history/diff service
projection/render service
change/migration service
snapshot/named-root resolution

Use generics, trait objects, or another existing project pattern.

Do not instantiate SQLite, an HTTP client, or a model provider directly in the app crate.

The service must be testable with in-memory doubles.

docs.title: 3. Resolve Snapshot Selectors Before Reads
docs.text:
When a request specifies an exact snapshot, use it directly.

When a request specifies a named root/current-root selector:

  1. resolve it to one exact SnapshotId before starting the semantic operation;
  2. rewrite/build the downstream query request with that exact snapshot;
  3. execute entirely against that snapshot;
  4. return the exact SnapshotId in the application result.

Never allow a long read to re-resolve the named root midway through execution.

If the named root disappears or cannot be resolved, return a structured application error.

docs.title: 4. Delegate Read Operations
docs.text:
Dispatch:

Inspect
List
Follow
Find
Query

to scriberig-query service contracts.

Do not reproduce graph traversal/search/query logic in scriberig-app.

Preserve result handles, continuation tokens, provenance, and exact snapshot context unchanged except for application-level wrapping.

docs.title: 5. Delegate Diff and History
docs.text:
Dispatch Diff and History to the canonical change/history subsystem.

Requirements:

  • accept only exact comparable states where the owning subsystem requires them;
  • preserve semantic diff/history structures;
  • do not render them to text in the app layer;
  • map subsystem failures into structured application errors without losing conflicting/subject handles;
  • preserve ancestry, migration, and provenance handles returned by the history layer.

If the canonical subsystem uses different names such as compare or lineage, adapt those operations rather than adding duplicate engines.

docs.title: 6. Delegate Render
docs.text:
Dispatch Render to scriberig-projection or the canonical projection service.

Preserve:

subject
exact semantic state
projection/view identifier
style identifier/options
semantic correspondence/anchors where returned

A render operation must not mutate canonical knowledge.

If render-cache population occurs below this layer, it must not advance the canonical snapshot.

docs.title: 7. Delegate Branch
docs.text:
Dispatch Branch to the canonical change/workspace subsystem.

The request must identify an exact base snapshot after selector resolution.

Return the canonical branch/workspace handle and base state.

Do not create a separate application-only branch graph.

If the underlying system uses WorkspaceId, wrap/adapt it through the application result without manufacturing duplicate branch state.

docs.title: 8. Delegate Apply
docs.text:
Dispatch Apply to the canonical change/migration subsystem.

Preserve:

branch/workspace
base/candidate state
migration proposal/change set
diagnostics
conflicts
validation requirements

Applying a change must not advance a canonical named root.

Add a test double that fails the suite if Apply invokes root promotion.

High-level domain operations, once registered later, must eventually route through this same apply/change mechanism.

docs.title: 9. Delegate Commit
docs.text:
Dispatch Commit to the canonical promotion/commit operation.

Preserve:

base snapshot
candidate snapshot
accepted migration
validation/provenance handles
ancestry
resulting promoted/retained snapshot

Commit is the explicit universal promotion boundary.

Do not embed authorization or validation policy rules in this task beyond invoking the owning subsystem/policy service where required.

docs.title: 10. Map Structured Errors
docs.text:
In src/error.rs, map subsystem failures into application-level categories without reducing them to strings.

Support at least:

NotFound
InvalidRequest
UnsupportedCapability
Conflict
ValidationFailed
Ambiguous
PermissionDenied
SnapshotUnavailable
OperationFailed
Internal

Where the source error includes handles such as:

subject entity
base revision
current revision
left/right migration
candidate matches

retain them in the mapped error payload.

Use an internal/source error chain for diagnostics where project conventions permit it.

docs.title: 11. Do Not Add Surface Formatting
docs.text:
Application results must remain structured.

Do not add:

ANSI text
Markdown-formatted status messages
JSON strings as a shortcut
HTML
terminal tables
agent prompt prose

Later adapters decide how to present the result.

docs.title: 12. Tests
docs.text:
In tests/universal_operation_model.rs, use deterministic test doubles for each subsystem.

Test at least:

  1. all eleven operation kinds dispatch to the expected provider;
  2. a named root is resolved exactly once before a read;
  3. the resolved snapshot is visible in the read result;
  4. inspect/list/follow/find/query do not invoke history/projection/change providers;
  5. diff/history delegate to the history provider;
  6. render delegates to projection and does not invoke canonical mutation;
  7. branch records the exact base snapshot;
  8. apply updates only branch/candidate state and never promotes a named root;
  9. commit invokes the canonical promotion boundary;
  10. structured conflict data survives error mapping;
  11. validation failure remains distinguishable from conflict and internal failure;
  12. result values contain no presentation-only strings as their sole semantics.

Run:

cargo test -p scriberig-app
cargo check --workspace

If a canonical subsystem prerequisite does not yet compile, use local test traits/doubles only where the Level 2 design explicitly permits it; do not commit duplicate domain logic to work around the missing prerequisite.

docs.title: 13. Non-Goals
docs.text:
Do not implement:

  • HTTP/server endpoints;
  • CLI commands;
  • TypeScript bindings;
  • React hooks/components;
  • agent tool schemas;
  • authorization policy;
  • background scheduling;
  • domain high-level operation algorithms;
  • storage/index algorithms.

docs.title: Completion Criteria
docs.text:
This task is complete when:

  • one application service executes all eleven universal operations;
  • read operations are snapshot-resolved before execution;
  • each operation delegates to its canonical owning subsystem;
  • no diff/history/render/change algorithm is duplicated in the app crate;
  • apply and commit preserve the explicit candidate-versus-promotion boundary;
  • structured errors and handles survive subsystem mapping;
  • the service is testable entirely with in-memory providers;
  • the resulting public API is transport-independent.

docs.title: Implement Operation Handles, Structured Errors, and the Extension Registry
Objective
docs.text:
Complete the cross-cutting parts of the universal application model that make it usable by future CLI, server, web, TUI, and agent surfaces.

This task implements:

  • application-level long-running operation handles and lifecycle records;
  • structured application failures with semantic context;
  • the extensible registry/provider mechanism through which domains advertise relations, collections, views, find strategies, and high-level operations.

It must not implement a background worker runtime, transport event stream, authorization policy, or any domain operation algorithm.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md
  2. design/level-2/010. universal query and operation implementation.md
  3. design/level-3/018. implement universal application request result and capability model.md
  4. design/level-3/019. integrate universal read diff history render and change operations.md
  5. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  6. design/level-1/008. derived knowledge caching and incrementality.md
  7. existing domain-capability discovery implementation tasks

Inspect existing capability/provider traits before adding new ones. If a domain registry already exists in another canonical crate, integrate with it rather than creating a second registry with overlapping responsibility.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Within crates/scriberig-app/:

src/lib.rs
src/capability.rs
src/operation.rs
src/error.rs
src/service.rs

tests/universal_operation_model.rs

Within crates/scriberig-query/, modify only narrowly required shared descriptor/error types if the app layer needs an upstream reusable contract.

Do not create protocol/server/web files.

docs.title: 1. Operation Reference
docs.text:
Use the universal OperationRef type established in the query/application vocabulary.

If it is only a placeholder newtype, define the canonical application-layer ownership now without changing its public semantic meaning.

An operation reference identifies one tracked execution attempt, not the semantic entity being operated on.

Do not derive operation identity from display text.

docs.title: 2. Operation Lifecycle
docs.text:
In src/operation.rs, implement a lifecycle enum equivalent to:

Queued
Running
Completed
Failed
Cancelled

Keep terminal states unambiguous.

Do not add retry/scheduler policy into the lifecycle enum.

Implement an OperationRecord/OperationStatus capable of carrying:

operation ref
operation kind or capability id
base snapshot/branch context
state
optional progress
optional produced result handles
optional diagnostics/error reference

Progress should be coarse and optional. A simple structure containing completed/total/message is sufficient if used.

Do not require every operation to report progress.

docs.title: 3. Immediate Versus Tracked Results
docs.text:
The application model must support both:

immediate typed result

and:

OperationStarted(OperationRef)

without changing the semantic meaning of the requested operation.

Do not make all operations artificially asynchronous.

The choice to execute inline or delegate to a runtime is an execution/runtime concern.

This task defines only the representation used when tracking is needed.

docs.title: 4. Structured Application Error
docs.text:
In src/error.rs, implement or complete the application error enum/record.

Required categories:

NotFound
InvalidRequest
UnsupportedCapability
Conflict
ValidationFailed
Ambiguous
PermissionDenied
SnapshotUnavailable
OperationFailed
Internal

Each error should include:

operation kind/capability when known
snapshot or branch context when known
subject handles when known
structured diagnostics/details

Use nested typed detail enums/records for important cases instead of a single free-form message.

A human-readable message is allowed as supplemental information.

docs.title: 5. Structured Conflict Details
docs.text:
Add conflict detail structures capable of preserving cases such as:

subject entity
base revision
expected revision
current revision
left/right revisions or migrations
conflicting collection/relation operation

Do not require every conflict to use every field.

If the canonical change subsystem already defines conflict types, wrap or reuse them. Do not create a second semantic conflict model merely for the app crate.

The key requirement is that downstream surfaces can inspect and resolve conflicts without parsing an error string.

docs.title: 6. Ambiguity Details
docs.text:
Add an ambiguity representation capable of returning candidate semantic handles.

Example conceptual result:

Ambiguous {
    scope,
    candidates: [EntityRef...],
    reason,
}

This is needed for reconciliation, selection, and query-like operations where multiple semantic targets are plausible.

Do not choose a candidate silently at the application boundary.

docs.title: 7. Capability Provider Trait
docs.text:
In src/capability.rs, define a provider/registry abstraction through which domains can advertise capabilities for a semantic subject.

It should support discovery of at least:

relations
collections
views
find strategies
high-level domain operations

The registry should operate on stable capability descriptors from the previous task.

Avoid a global mutable singleton when a normal injected registry/service can work.

The application service must be testable with a small in-memory registry.

docs.title: 8. Registration and Composition
docs.text:
Provide a mechanism to combine multiple domain capability providers.

Requirements:

  • adding a new domain should not require editing a central match statement over every domain type;
  • duplicate capability IDs for the same applicability scope must be rejected or resolved by an explicit deterministic rule;
  • providers may declare that a capability is unavailable because required derived data is missing;
  • generic capabilities and domain capabilities can coexist;
  • capability ordering shown to clients is not canonical semantic state.

Do not make registry population advance the project snapshot.

docs.title: 9. Capability Execution Boundary
docs.text:
High-level domain operation capabilities should expose an execution adapter that ultimately receives:

semantic subject/selection
exact snapshot or branch/workspace context
arguments

and produces a canonical change request/result through the existing migration/change subsystem.

Do not let a capability provider update storage rows directly.

For this task, it is sufficient to define the trait boundary and test it with a dummy operation. Do not implement real domain algorithms such as rename-symbol or split-paragraph.

docs.title: 10. Capability Discovery Integration
docs.text:
Update the application service so inspect can merge:

  • relation/collection capabilities from schema/graph inspection;
  • registered views;
  • registered find strategies;
  • registered high-level operations.

Inspection must remain useful when no domain provider is registered.

Unknown/unsupported entities should still expose generic operations that actually apply.

Do not advertise capabilities whose provider reports unavailable.

docs.title: 11. Tests
docs.text:
Extend tests/universal_operation_model.rs to cover at least:

  1. operation lifecycle moves through valid states;
  2. completed/failed/cancelled are distinguishable terminal states;
  3. immediate results do not require an operation record;
  4. tracked work returns an OperationRef that can retrieve status through the application abstraction or test registry;
  5. conflict errors preserve exact semantic handles/revisions;
  6. ambiguity errors preserve candidate handles;
  7. validation failure is distinct from conflict;
  8. two independent capability providers can be composed;
  9. duplicate capability IDs are handled deterministically;
  10. a new dummy domain capability can be registered without editing core dispatch code;
  11. inspect advertises registered capabilities;
  12. unavailable derived capability is not falsely advertised as ready;
  13. dummy high-level operation routes through the change-service test double rather than direct storage mutation;
  14. registry/cache population does not advance the canonical snapshot.

Run:

cargo test -p scriberig-app
cargo check --workspace

docs.title: 12. Non-Goals
docs.text:
Do not implement:

  • a thread pool or job scheduler;
  • process supervision;
  • WebSocket/SSE events;
  • HTTP status-code mapping;
  • CLI progress bars;
  • authorization decisions;
  • model-provider execution;
  • real Rust/Markdown/PDF high-level operations;
  • persistent operation-history storage unless another design already owns it.

docs.title: Completion Criteria
docs.text:
This task is complete when:

  • long-running work has a reusable application-level OperationRef and lifecycle model;
  • important failures are structured and preserve semantic context;
  • conflicts and ambiguity are machine-inspectable;
  • domains can register discoverable capabilities without central core branching;
  • capability execution cannot bypass the canonical change boundary;
  • inspect can advertise generic and domain-provided capabilities coherently;
  • no transport/runtime dependency is required.

docs.title: Verify Universal Query and Operation Conformance
Objective
docs.text:
Add the end-to-end conformance tests that prove the universal query and application-operation model behaves consistently across the reusable Rust layers.

This task does not add new product features. It verifies that the implementation created by the previous Level 3 tasks preserves the architectural invariants in design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md.

The test suite must remain usable without an HTTP server, CLI, TUI, web application, agent runtime, or SQLite backend.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md
  2. design/level-2/010. universal query and operation implementation.md
  3. design/level-3/015. implement universal query handles scope and pagination.md
  4. design/level-3/016. implement inspect list and follow read operations.md
  5. design/level-3/017. implement find and structured query ast.md
  6. design/level-3/018. implement universal application request result and capability model.md
  7. design/level-3/019. integrate universal read diff history render and change operations.md
  8. design/level-3/020. implement operation handles structured errors and extension registry.md
  9. relevant graph, history/change, and projection conformance designs

Inspect existing tests before adding new fixtures. Reuse canonical memory backends/test helpers where they already exist.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Primary test files:

crates/scriberig-query/tests/universal_read_model.rs
crates/scriberig-app/tests/universal_operation_model.rs

If shared test fixtures are needed, prefer an already-established test-support crate/module. Otherwise add a narrowly scoped local tests/support/ module inside the owning crate.

Do not create a new production crate only for these tests unless the workspace already has a designated conformance-test crate.

docs.title: 1. Build a Small Multi-Domain-Like Fixture
docs.text:
Create a generic graph fixture using universal entities rather than requiring real Rust/Markdown/PDF parsers.

The fixture should contain at least:

Project P
  collection modules/documents -> E1, E2

Entity E1
  type: Function-like test type
  relation calls -> E3
  collection groups -> E4, E5

Entity E2
  type: Section-like test type
  collection paragraphs -> E6, E7

Entity E3
  type: Function-like test type

Branch/workspace B
  based on Snapshot S1

Create at least two snapshots so one entity changes between S1 and S2 while another remains unchanged.

Use real canonical identity/snapshot types and the actual in-memory graph/store helpers.

Do not hard-code production domain adapters merely for this test.

docs.title: 2. Prove Snapshot-Bound Reads
docs.text:
Test:

  1. inspect E1 at S1;
  2. advance a named root to S2;
  3. verify the completed result still reports S1 and the S1 revision;
