If prerequisite traits do not yet exist, expose narrow functions in the Markdown crate and document the future integration point. Do not redesign the projection framework in this task.

docs.title: Semantic Mapping Rules
docs.text:
At minimum:

  • heading level determines section nesting;
  • paragraphs remain independently addressable;
  • list item order is canonical;
  • table row and cell order is canonical;
  • code block language/info string is preserved where available;
  • link target and visible content are preserved;
  • image target and descriptive text are preserved;
  • formatting-only whitespace is not promoted to canonical semantic state.

Unsupported syntax must return an explicit adapter error or preserve a safe fallback representation if the shared schema already defines one. Do not silently drop content.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Create fixtures covering:

nested headings
multiple paragraphs
ordered and unordered lists
tables
code blocks
quotes
links
images
mixed document structure

Test:

  1. parsing produces the expected semantic hierarchy;
  2. semantic order is preserved;
  3. paragraphs/rows/cells are separate objects;
  4. parse -> render -> parse preserves equivalent semantic structure;
  5. deterministic rendering returns identical bytes on repeated calls;
  6. formatting-only differences do not require different semantic meaning where the schema classifies them as projection-only;
  7. source coordinates, if present, are metadata rather than IDs.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-domain-markdown
cargo clippy -p scriberig-domain-markdown --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not implement filesystem watching.
  • Do not implement the generic projection record store.
  • Do not implement three-way merge orchestration.
  • Do not call an LLM for parsing or mapping.
  • Do not create Markdown-specific database tables.
  • Do not expose parser-library AST types through public universal APIs.
  • Do not silently discard unsupported source content.
  • Do not implement agent tools or UI components.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Markdown source parses into the canonical domain schema.
  • [x] Section hierarchy is semantic, not only flat heading tokens.
  • [x] Paragraphs, rows, cells, and list items remain separately addressable.
  • [x] Rendering is deterministic.
  • [x] Supported parse/render round trips preserve semantic structure.
  • [x] Parser-specific details stay inside the adapter.
  • [x] Source coordinates do not become semantic identity.
  • [x] No alternate persistence model exists.
  • [x] Tests, formatting, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement: Snapshots, Roots, Collections, and Memory Backend
Objective
docs.text: Implement the backend-independent snapshot/root/collection APIs and a complete in-memory backend that acts as the executable reference implementation.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/004. persistence and storage model.md
  2. design/level-2/003. snapshots roots and persistent collections.md
  3. design/level-2/006. persistence observability and conformance.md
  4. Level 3 tasks 001 and 002.

docs.title: Files to create or update
docs.text:
In sr-store:

crates/sr-store/src/
├── lib.rs
├── snapshot.rs
├── roots.rs
└── collection.rs

In sr-store-memory:

crates/sr-store-memory/src/
├── lib.rs
├── revision.rs
├── snapshot.rs
└── roots.rs

Add tests under the relevant crate test directories.

docs.title: Snapshot API
docs.text:
Define backend-independent operations equivalent to:

resolve(snapshot, entity) -> RevisionId?
apply_changes(base_snapshot, changes) -> SnapshotId
iterate(snapshot) -> entity/revision pairs
diff_snapshots(a, b) -> changed entity mappings

Snapshot changes are storage-level operations only:

Set(EntityId, RevisionId)
Remove(EntityId)

Do not encode semantic migration meaning here.

docs.title: Snapshot identity
docs.text:
Snapshot identity must be deterministic for the complete entity-to-revision mapping.

Two snapshots produced through different update orders but containing the exact same mapping must obtain the same SnapshotId.

Do not use insertion order, timestamps, allocation IDs, or backend row numbers in snapshot identity.

docs.title: Persistent representation
docs.text:
The in-memory implementation must provide structural sharing rather than cloning the entire map for every update.

A simple correctness-first persistent tree or layered immutable map is acceptable. Keep the physical representation private so it can be replaced later.

Add a test or internal instrumentation proving a one-entry update shares unchanged structure with its base. The test should not expose the private representation through the public API.

docs.title: Named roots
docs.text:
Implement:

read_root(name)
compare_and_set_root(name, expected_snapshot_or_none, new_snapshot)

Rules:

  • promotion is atomic within the in-memory backend's synchronization model;
  • stale expected values return a typed conflict;
  • a failed promotion leaves the root unchanged;
  • moving a root never mutates either snapshot.

docs.title: Persistent collections
docs.text:
Define a backend-neutral immutable ordered collection abstraction for canonical semantic lists.

Required operations:

create
len
get
iterate
insert
remove
move/replace sequence as justified by implementation

The implementation must keep position in the collection rather than in child IDs.

Use a simple immutable chunked sequence or similarly replaceable structure. Do not optimize prematurely.

docs.title: Memory revision storage
docs.text:
Complete the memory backend implementation of the revision API from task 002.

Exact duplicate revisions are reused/idempotent.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
At minimum:

  • old snapshot remains readable after creating a descendant snapshot;
  • one entity changes while unrelated entity mappings remain identical;
  • removing an entity from a new snapshot does not remove it from the base;
  • two branches can be created from one base;
  • equivalent mappings converge to the same SnapshotId;
  • root CAS succeeds when expected value matches;
  • root CAS fails cleanly when stale;
  • failed root CAS leaves root unchanged;
  • reordering a collection changes collection state without changing child IDs;
  • memory backend revision insertion is idempotent.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not add SQL.
  • Do not implement migrations or merges.
  • Do not make a section/document/function type.
  • Do not use the global snapshot ID as the identity of individual revisions.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Snapshot API is backend-neutral.
  • [x] Snapshot identity is deterministic.
  • [x] In-memory snapshot updates structurally share unchanged state.
  • [x] Named-root CAS works and reports conflicts.
  • [x] Persistent ordered collection abstraction exists.
  • [x] Memory backend implements revision and snapshot/root behavior.
  • [x] All workspace tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the storage-independent universal graph records and snapshot-bound read contracts required by the universal knowledge model.

This task owns runtime semantic revision payloads, typed relations, ordered/unordered collections, descriptions, derived artifacts, and a read-only graph view contract.

It must reuse the existing shared core, schema, and identity/storage abstractions. It must not create a second persistence system.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md
  2. design/level-2/001. universal knowledge model rust libraries.md
  3. design/level-3/001. extend shared core with knowledge values and provenance.md
  4. design/level-3/002. implement universal schema contracts.md
  5. the repository-wide workspace/package-layout design;
  6. the identity/revision/snapshot implementation design.

Inspect the actual workspace before editing.

Use the canonical universal graph crate already established by the workspace. If it does not exist, create it at the path prescribed by the repository-wide layout. Do not invent a competing crate prefix.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Inside the canonical universal graph crate:

Cargo.toml
src/lib.rs
src/revision.rs
src/relation.rs
src/collection.rs
src/description.rs
src/derived.rs
src/view.rs

If the graph crate already contains storage-backed graph functionality from another task, integrate these semantic records with its existing public contracts rather than creating parallel record types.

docs.title: 1. Runtime Relation Values
docs.text:
In relation.rs, implement the runtime representation for an owned semantic relation.

The representation must keep separate:

relation type identity
target semantic entity identity/identities

Targets must use the established EntityId or equivalent semantic entity handle.

Do not use:

  • filenames;
  • line numbers;
  • database row IDs;
  • display names;

as relation identity.

docs.title: Semantics
docs.text:
• Ordinary canonical relations point to conceptual entities.
  • The exact target revision is resolved in a snapshot when needed.
  • Derived relations may be represented as derived artifacts rather than silently inserted into canonical revision data.
  • Reverse relation copies are not required inside target revisions.

Use the schema relation cardinality to validate how many targets are legal; do not bake every cardinality rule into the raw relation-value type itself unless the existing schema API makes that natural.

docs.title: 2. Ordered and Unordered Collection Values
docs.text:
In collection.rs, implement a public collection-value model with semantically distinct ordered and unordered cases.

Conceptually:

Ordered(Vec<EntityId>)
Unordered(Set<EntityId>)

The concrete containers may differ, but required behavior is:

  • ordered collections preserve member sequence exactly;
  • reordering produces a different ordered collection value;
  • unordered collections compare/behave by membership rather than insertion order;
  • collection members are semantic entity handles;
  • parent position is not stored in the child entity;
  • moving a member changes the owning collection state, not the member entity identity.

Document duplicate-member policy explicitly.

If duplicates are prohibited, enforce that deterministically. If ordered duplicate membership is allowed for a specific future domain, the universal representation must not accidentally prohibit it without schema support. Prefer the least surprising generic representation and let schemas constrain it.

docs.title: 3. Universal Semantic Revision Record
docs.text:
In revision.rs, implement a storage-independent RevisionRecord or equivalent representing one exact semantic entity state.

It must include conceptually:

entity type
properties
owned relation values
owned collection values

Use deterministic maps where practical.

docs.title: Interaction with existing revision storage
docs.text:
The identity/storage layer may already define a lower-level canonical revision blob/value used to compute RevisionId.

Do not replace it.

Instead, this semantic revision record should be encodable/serializable through the existing canonical revision mechanism or otherwise be a higher-level model that the store can persist without redefining revision identity rules.

If a canonical-encoding trait already exists, implement it here as appropriate.

Do not invent a second RevisionId algorithm.

docs.title: Prohibited state
docs.text:
A semantic revision record must not require:

  • mutable parent pointer;
  • database connection;
  • database row ID;
  • mutable current snapshot;
  • reverse-index cache;
  • file path as semantic identity;
  • agent runtime state.

docs.title: 4. Schema Validation Integration
docs.text:
Implement the universal schema crate's ValidationSubject or equivalent trait for RevisionRecord.

Expose:

entity type
property keys/values
relation types/targets
collection types/members

When target/member entity type validation requires a context, adapt the graph/read-view layer to provide the schema validator with the required type resolution.

Do not add a graph dependency to the schema crate.

docs.title: 5. Description Object
docs.text:
In description.rs, implement a derived description record.

Required semantic content:

exact source entity + revision
description profile
text
provenance
optional information-cost metadata

Information-cost metadata may include optional estimates such as:

bytes
characters
estimated tokens

Do not require a tokenizer dependency.

Generated descriptions are derived knowledge by default and must not be inserted into the canonical semantic revision record merely because they describe it.

docs.title: 6. Derived Artifact
docs.text:
In derived.rs, implement a generic derived-artifact representation.

It must expose at least:

artifact/profile kind
exact immutable dependencies
producer/configuration identity
provenance
result payload or result reference
status if useful

Use the shared KnowledgeValue for generic small payloads where appropriate, or an explicit typed result reference if the existing architecture provides one.

The important invariant is that exact dependency revisions remain inspectable.

Do not implement caching or invalidation here. Later caching logic will decide reuse by comparing declared dependencies.

docs.title: 7. Snapshot-Bound Read View
docs.text:
In view.rs, define or extend a storage-independent trait such as KnowledgeView.

Required conceptual operations:

resolve(snapshot, entity) -> exact revision
read semantic revision
obtain schema/entity-type information
obtain reverse relations through a view/index abstraction

Owned forward properties, relations, and collections may be read directly from the semantic revision record.

docs.title: Explicit snapshot requirement
docs.text:
Any operation whose result depends on which revision of an entity is active must accept an explicit SnapshotId or operate on an already snapshot-bound view object.

Do not make an unqualified get_current(entity) the universal semantic API.

docs.title: Backend neutrality
docs.text:
Use an associated error type or equivalent abstraction so the trait can be implemented by:

  • in-memory test stores;
  • SQLite-backed stores;
  • future remote stores;
  • test doubles.

The graph crate must not expose SQLite error types in its universal API.

docs.title: 8. Reverse Navigation
docs.text:
Define a small result type for reverse navigation, conceptually:

source entity
relation type
optional resolved source revision

Reverse navigation is provided by an index/view implementation.

It must not require adding canonical parent or reverse-edge fields to every target revision.

docs.title: 9. Public API
docs.text:
lib.rs should expose the main universal graph concepts through stable imports:

RevisionRecord
RelationValue
CollectionValue
Description
DerivedArtifact
KnowledgeView
ReverseRelation

Use existing project names if equivalent types already exist.

Avoid two public types that represent the same semantic concept just because separate design tasks created provisional names.

docs.title: 10. Focused Unit Tests
docs.text:
Add module-level tests for:

  1. ordered collection order preservation;
  2. reordered ordered collection is different;
  3. unordered collection membership is independent of insertion order;
  4. relation targets are semantic entity IDs;
  5. revision record requires no parent pointer;
  6. revision record implements schema validation subject;
  7. description binds to exact entity/revision and provenance;
  8. derived artifact retains exact dependencies;
  9. a mock/read view resolves one entity to different revisions in different snapshots;
  10. reverse lookup can be represented without canonical reverse-edge duplication.

Do not add database integration tests in this task unless the existing graph crate already has a backend-neutral test harness that makes this free.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Public docs must explain:

  • revision records are exact semantic state, but revision-ID generation belongs to identity/storage code;
  • relations target semantic identities;
  • collections own order/membership semantics;
  • child entities do not carry parent position;
  • descriptions and derived artifacts are separate derived knowledge;
  • graph interpretation is snapshot-bound;
  • reverse navigation is an index/view capability.

docs.title: Validation Commands
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt
cargo check --workspace
cargo test --workspace

If available:

cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
Do not:

  • create another core/store implementation;
  • redefine revision hashing;
  • redefine snapshot-map semantics;
  • add SQLite-specific public APIs;
  • implement migrations;
  • implement history/diff;
  • implement universal search;
  • implement domain schemas;
  • implement Markdown/Rust/PDF/session adapters;
  • add agent/server/UI code;
  • duplicate reverse relations canonically;
  • make generated descriptions canonical by default.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] canonical graph crate is reused/created at the workspace-prescribed path;
  • [x] typed runtime relations exist;
  • [x] ordered/unordered collections are distinct;
  • [x] semantic revision record integrates with existing identity/storage rules;
  • [x] child records require no parent pointer;
  • [x] schema validation subject is implemented;
  • [x] descriptions bind to exact revisions and provenance;
  • [x] derived artifacts expose exact dependencies;
  • [x] graph view is explicitly snapshot-bound;
  • [x] reverse navigation is modeled as derived/index-backed;
  • [x] no duplicate persistence or identity subsystem was introduced;
  • [x] workspace checks and tests pass.

docs.title: Implement Validation Evidence and Exact Input Binding
Objective
docs.text: Represent validation as structured, provenance-bearing knowledge bound to exact immutable inputs. A validator produces evidence; it does not grant permission or promote a candidate.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
1. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md, especially sections 16–18, 32–35 and 64.
  2. design/level-1/008. derived knowledge caching and incrementality.md.
  3. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md.
  4. design/level-3/001. extend shared core with knowledge values and provenance.md.
  5. Existing schema/graph/application designs and implementations.

If exact revision/snapshot references or graph/schema persistence are not implemented yet, stop and report the missing prerequisite.

docs.title: Expected Area
docs.text:
Use the existing schema/graph mechanisms to persist validation results as knowledge objects, and the application layer to orchestrate validators.

Likely modules:

crates/scriberig-app/src/validation.rs
crates/scriberig-schema/... validation schema registration if required
crates/scriberig-app/src/lib.rs

Do not invent a separate database table that bypasses the universal graph unless an existing lower-level design explicitly requires one.

docs.title: Validation Result Model
docs.text:
Represent at least:

validator identity
validator version/profile/configuration
subject entity/revision or candidate snapshot
explicit dependency set
status
structured diagnostics
produced artifact references
provenance

Status must distinguish at least:

Passed
Failed
Error
Skipped
Unknown

Do not reduce all results to a boolean.

docs.title: Exact Input Binding
docs.text:
A validation result must identify the exact candidate snapshot or exact immutable dependency revisions it checked.

Provide one reusable function that decides whether prior evidence is applicable to a later candidate. It may reuse evidence only when its declared dependencies are still identical. If dependency information is incomplete, return not-applicable conservatively.

Never infer that validation for snapshot A applies to snapshot B merely because their rendered files look similar.

docs.title: Validator Interface
docs.text:
Define an application-facing validator trait/interface using the conventions already present in the repository. It should receive an explicit candidate/context and return structured validation evidence.

Validators must not directly promote candidates.

A validator may be deterministic or interpretive, but its provenance/configuration must make the distinction inspectable where known.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
Keep diagnostics structured enough for CLI, protocol, web, and agents to consume the same evidence. At minimum support severity/category, message, optional subject reference, and optional source coordinates.

Do not require every validator to produce source coordinates.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests proving:

  1. a passing result is bound to the exact candidate;
  2. a candidate revision change invalidates evidence when that revision is a dependency;
  3. unrelated snapshot changes do not invalidate evidence when all declared dependencies are unchanged;
  4. unknown dependency coverage causes conservative non-reuse;
  5. failed validation remains stored/inspectable;
  6. validator error is distinct from validation failure;
  7. two validator configurations produce distinguishable evidence;
  8. structured diagnostics survive persistence/round-trip;
  9. validation does not mutate canonical roots;
  10. validation does not imply a capability to promote.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run workspace format/check/tests/lint. Include at least one application-level test using an in-memory or test store if the repository provides one.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not implement project promotion policy here. Do not hard-code Rust compiler commands or Markdown validators into the universal interface. Do not attach a mutable validated=true field to snapshots. Do not erase failed evidence.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] validation is structured knowledge;
  • [x] exact inputs/configuration are recorded;
  • [x] reuse is dependency-based and conservative;
  • [x] failed/error results remain inspectable;
  • [x] validators cannot promote candidates;
  • [x] protocol/UI-specific rendering is deferred.

docs.title: Initialize Web Workspace and Headless Packages
Objective
docs.text:
Create the TypeScript/web workspace and the reusable non-visual/headless packages prescribed by design/level-2/001. workspace and package layout.md.

This task creates package boundaries only. Do not implement server calls, state management behavior, React hooks, semantic tree controllers, protocol generation, or application screens.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/001. vision and principles.md
  2. design/level-2/001. workspace and package layout.md

The important architectural rules are:

  • the official editor must be buildable from public reusable packages;
  • the TypeScript client must not depend on React or MUI;
  • client-side model and editor behavior must remain usable independently of the integrated editor;
  • transport types must reflect one wire contract shared with Rust rather than becoming a separate conceptual protocol;
  • MUI must not appear in the packages created by this task.

docs.title: Files to Create
docs.text:
Create:

web/package.json
web/pnpm-workspace.yaml
web/tsconfig.base.json

web/packages/protocol/package.json
web/packages/protocol/src/index.ts
web/packages/client/package.json
web/packages/client/src/index.ts
web/packages/model/package.json
web/packages/model/src/index.ts
web/packages/editor-core/package.json
web/packages/editor-core/src/index.ts
web/packages/react/package.json
web/packages/react/src/index.ts

Also extend the repository root .gitignore with web/Node generated artifacts as described below.

Do not create components, components-mui, agent-ui, or the integrated editor app in this task. They are created by Level 3 task 004.

docs.title: web/package.json
docs.text:
Create a private workspace-root package.

Requirements:

  • mark it private;
  • do not publish it;
  • do not add an application framework;
  • do not add MUI;
  • do not add a bundler unless required by a later design;
  • do not add repository-wide scripts that assume tools not yet selected.

The purpose of this file at this stage is to establish the package-manager root.

docs.title: web/pnpm-workspace.yaml
docs.text:
Configure pnpm to discover:

packages/*
apps/*

The apps/* pattern is included now so the later editor app joins the same workspace without restructuring it.

docs.title: web/tsconfig.base.json
docs.text:
Create a strict reusable TypeScript base configuration suitable for library packages.

Requirements:

  • enable strict type checking;
  • use modern ECMAScript syntax;
  • do not assume browser-only globals at the base level;
  • do not configure React JSX globally for all packages;
  • do not include package-specific source files from the root config.

Keep the configuration small. Package-specific build details may be added later when the build tooling is designed.

docs.title: Package Names and Roles
docs.text:
Use these names exactly:

web/packages/protocol     -> @scriberig/protocol
web/packages/client       -> @scriberig/client
web/packages/model        -> @scriberig/model
web/packages/editor-core  -> @scriberig/editor-core
web/packages/react        -> @scriberig/react

All packages start at version 0.1.0.

At this scaffold stage, package manifests may be private to prevent accidental publishing before packaging/release design exists. The architectural intention is still that these are reusable public packages later.

docs.title: Internal Dependency Direction
docs.text:
Represent these workspace dependencies in package manifests:

@scriberig/protocol

@scriberig/client
└── @scriberig/protocol

@scriberig/model
├── @scriberig/protocol
└── @scriberig/client

@scriberig/editor-core
└── @scriberig/model

@scriberig/react
└── @scriberig/model

Use pnpm workspace references for internal packages.

Do not make @scriberig/model depend on React.

Do not make @scriberig/editor-core depend on MUI.

Do not make any package depend on the future integrated editor application.

docs.title: src/index.ts Content
docs.text:
Each src/index.ts should contain only package-level documentation comments and an empty module export such as:

export {};

Do not create speculative classes, hooks, DTOs, stores, controllers, query clients, event streams, or selection models yet.

The documentation should accurately state each intended role:

  • @scriberig/protocol: TypeScript representation of the shared wire contract;
  • @scriberig/client: reusable browser/Node server client boundary;
  • @scriberig/model: UI-framework-independent client state/model boundary;
  • @scriberig/editor-core: headless semantic editor/browser behavior boundary;
  • @scriberig/react: React bindings over public model/client behavior, without styling assumptions.

Do not claim generated protocol support is implemented until the generation mechanism exists.

docs.title: .gitignore
docs.text:
Preserve every existing Rust ignore rule.

Append rules covering at least:

node_modules/
**/node_modules/
**/dist/
**/.vite/
*.tsbuildinfo
web/.pnpm-store/

Do not add ignores for tools that have not been selected.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
If pnpm is available, run from web/:

pnpm install
pnpm list -r --depth -1

Verify that all five packages are discovered and their workspace dependency links resolve.

Do not introduce a compile/build command solely to satisfy this task if no TypeScript build toolchain has yet been selected. Validate JSON/YAML syntax and package discovery instead.

Also run the existing Rust workspace checks after changing .gitignore only to ensure no unrelated repository damage occurred:

cargo check --workspace

if the Rust workspace already exists.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not create the integrated editor app.
  • Do not create visual components.
  • Do not add MUI.
  • Do not add a React rendering implementation.
  • Do not implement hooks.
  • Do not choose Redux, Zustand, MobX, RxJS, or another state library.
  • Do not choose Vite, Next.js, Remix, or another application framework.
  • Do not manually duplicate future Rust protocol DTOs as if they were already designed.
  • Do not add server-specific business logic.
  • Do not edit Level 1 or Level 2 design documents.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] web/ is a valid pnpm workspace root.
  • [x] packages/* and apps/* are workspace patterns.
  • [x] Strict shared TypeScript configuration exists.
  • [x] All five prescribed headless/public package directories exist.
  • [x] Package names match this document exactly.
  • [x] Internal workspace dependency direction is correct.
  • [x] No MUI dependency exists.
  • [x] @scriberig/model and @scriberig/editor-core are React-independent.
  • [x] Source files contain documentation only and no speculative API.
  • [x] Existing Rust .gitignore rules remain intact.
  • [x] Node/pnpm/build artifacts are ignored.
  • [x] pnpm discovers the expected packages when pnpm is available.

docs.title: Agent Task: Implement Branches, Workspaces, and Promotion
Goal
docs.text:
Implement the branch/workspace model and optimistic named-root promotion for sr-change.

This task must preserve the Level 1 rule that branches are lines of work over snapshots, not copies of the database.

docs.title: Read before editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md, especially sections 14 through 20, 36 through 39, and 45 through 49.
  2. design/level-2/001. persistence crate boundaries.md for named-root semantics.
  3. design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md.
  4. Existing sr-store named-root compare-and-promote API.

docs.title: Files to modify
docs.text:
crates/sr-change/src/branch.rs
crates/sr-change/src/workspace.rs
crates/sr-change/src/promotion.rs
crates/sr-change/src/provenance.rs
crates/sr-change/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs

Modify sr-store only if a backend-independent atomic compare-and-promote capability is missing. If you extend that trait, update both memory and SQLite conformance expectations rather than calling a concrete backend directly.

docs.title: Branch model
docs.text:
Represent branch identity separately from branch head state.

The model must support at least:

stable branch/entity reference
base snapshot
current snapshot
status
optional title
optional purpose
optional short description
optional outcome
optional resulting migration

Do not make the descriptive fields part of snapshot identity unless the universal graph model explicitly treats them as canonical branch data.

Use existing universal entity/reference types where available.

docs.title: Workspace model
docs.text:
A workspace is an isolated working line with:

base SnapshotId
current SnapshotId
optional target named root
status
provenance

Required status transitions should cover the equivalent of:

Active
Ready
Promoted
Abandoned
FailedValidation

Keep the status vocabulary small and deterministic. Do not turn validation details into workspace status strings; validation result objects belong elsewhere.

A workspace must be able to advance from one descendant snapshot to another without altering its base.

docs.title: Promotion API
docs.text:
Implement a promotion operation equivalent in semantics to:

promote(
    root,
    expected_snapshot,
    result_snapshot,
)

The underlying store must perform an atomic compare-and-promote.

Return a typed result that distinguishes:

Promoted
StaleRoot { expected, actual }
InvalidTarget
StoreError

If the root points to a newer snapshot than expected, do not retry automatically and do not overwrite it.

The caller decides whether to merge, rebase, create a branch, or abandon.

docs.title: Promotion provenance
docs.text:
On successful promotion, preserve enough information to connect the promoted snapshot and migration/workspace to the named-root advance when the surrounding history model supports it.

Do not make named-root movement the only record of history. The migration remains the semantic transition record.

docs.title: Branch creation
docs.text:
Creating a branch from snapshot S must be O(1) or equivalent in logical state: it records a reference to S; it does not enumerate or duplicate all entities in S.

Do not implement branch creation as snapshot copying in sr-change.

docs.title: Failed attempts
docs.text:
Tests must prove that a failed or abandoned workspace does not alter:

  • its base snapshot;
  • the target named root;
  • sibling workspace state.

Failed descendants may remain addressable according to retention policy.

docs.title: Concurrent work
docs.text:
Create tests with two workspaces from one base:

S1
├── S2
└── S3

Promote one successfully, then attempt to promote the other with expected = S1.

The second promotion must fail with the actual current root and preserve both descendant snapshots.

docs.title: Branch descriptions
docs.text:
Expose branch title/purpose/description/outcome through compact inspection data without requiring traversal of all workspace history.

Do not generate model-written descriptions in this task. Store or expose the fields only.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Branches reference snapshots; they never own full snapshot copies.
  • Named roots are mutable references; snapshots are immutable.
  • No silent last-writer-wins behavior.
  • No automatic merge/rebase on promotion failure.
  • No agent-specific branch type.
  • Do not depend on a concrete store backend.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  • branch creation from an existing snapshot;
  • workspace base remains fixed while current snapshot advances;
  • branch creation does not materialize a copied snapshot mapping;
  • successful compare-and-promote;
  • stale-root promotion failure reports actual snapshot;
  • concurrent workspaces preserve both results;
  • abandoned workspace leaves named root untouched;
  • failed-validation workspace leaves named root untouched;
  • compact branch metadata can be read without opening full history.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-change
cargo test -p sr-store-memory
cargo check --workspace

If sr-store was extended, also run its full backend conformance suite.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Branch identity and branch head are separate.
  • [x] Workspace has exact base/current snapshots.
  • [x] Promotion uses atomic optimistic concurrency.
  • [x] Stale promotion never overwrites concurrent work.
  • [x] Failed/abandoned work leaves base and roots unchanged.
  • [x] Branch descriptions are available for navigation.
  • [x] Tests cover sibling workspaces and stale promotion.

docs.title: Final response from implementing agent
docs.text: Report the branch/workspace public API, promotion result type, any sr-store trait extension, and the concurrency tests added.

docs.title: Implement Candidate Promotion and Approval Pipeline
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the application-level path that turns an isolated candidate snapshot into canonical state only after capability checks, required validation evidence, policy evaluation, and any required approval.

This task must make promotion an explicit state transition rather than a storage write shortcut.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
1. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md, especially sections 14–19, 34–36 and 61.
  2. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md.
  3. design/level-3/001. implement principal and capability model.md.
  4. design/level-3/003. implement validation evidence and exact input binding.md.
  5. Existing migration/snapshot/application designs.

If branches/candidate snapshots or atomic canonical-root update are not implemented, stop and report the prerequisite.

docs.title: Expected Area
docs.text:
Work in the application layer and reuse migration/store primitives. Typical modules:

crates/scriberig-app/src/promotion.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/policy.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/approval.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/lib.rs

Do not put project promotion policy in the generic store.

docs.title: Promotion Request
docs.text:
Define a promotion request that includes at least:

principal
base canonical snapshot
candidate snapshot
migration/change reference
available validation evidence references
requested policy/profile
optional approvals

The request must be explicit about the expected current canonical snapshot.

docs.title: Promotion Evaluation
docs.text:
Implement the pipeline in this order:

verify Promote capability
verify expected base/current canonical state
collect required evidence
verify evidence applies to exact candidate/dependencies
evaluate promotion policy
verify required approval evidence
atomically advance canonical root
record promotion provenance/result

If the canonical root changed after proposal creation, do not apply approximately. Return a structured result such as rebase/merge/conflict required.

docs.title: Policy Interface
docs.text:
Define a project/domain-extensible policy interface that consumes candidate metadata plus validation/approval evidence and returns a structured decision:

Allow
Reject
RequireApproval
RequireAdditionalValidation
ConflictOrStale

Record which exact policy revision/profile produced the decision.

Do not hard-code tests passed => allow as the universal policy.

docs.title: Approval
docs.text:
Represent approval as an attributable operation/evidence object, not a mutable boolean. It must record principal, candidate, policy context, and time/operation metadata according to existing history conventions.

Approval for candidate A must not silently apply to candidate B.

docs.title: Promotion Result
docs.text:
Return and persist enough information to reconstruct:

old canonical snapshot
candidate/new canonical snapshot
migration/change
principal/proposer if known
validation evidence used
policy evaluation
approval evidence used
promotion operation

Rejected candidates remain non-canonical and inspectable if retained by normal branch/history policy.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Test at least:

  1. promotion without Promote capability is denied;
  2. validation capability alone cannot promote;
  3. stale base snapshot prevents direct promotion;
  4. evidence for another candidate is rejected;
  5. policy can require additional validation;
  6. policy can require approval;
  7. approval for the wrong candidate is rejected;
  8. successful promotion atomically advances the canonical root;
  9. failed policy evaluation leaves canonical state unchanged;
  10. promotion provenance can explain why the candidate was accepted.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run workspace formatting, check, tests, and lint. Include a concurrency/stale-root test if the store supports compare-and-swap or equivalent root guards.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not let validators call root-update APIs directly. Do not bypass migration/history recording. Do not rewrite candidate snapshots in place. Do not grant approval based solely on actor identity or model quality.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] promotion is one application operation;
  • [x] exact base/current state is checked;
  • [x] exact validation evidence is checked;
  • [x] policy decision is structured and attributable;
  • [x] approval is attributable evidence;
  • [x] canonical root update is atomic;
  • [x] rejected/stale candidates cannot silently become canonical.

docs.title: Implement Client Semantic Model and Incremental Events
Objective
docs.text:
Implement @scriberig/model as the framework-independent browser/client semantic state layer.

This package coordinates loaded protocol data, immutable revision caches, current snapshot resolution, operation state, and event application. It must not become a second canonical database and must not depend on React or MUI.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/003. identity revisions and snapshots.md
  2. design/level-1/008. derived knowledge caching and incrementality.md
  3. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
  4. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md
  5. design/level-3/002. implement protocol package boundary.md
  6. design/level-3/003. implement framework independent transport client.md

Prerequisite: @scriberig/protocol and @scriberig/client compile.

docs.title: Files to Create or Replace
docs.text:
Create:

web/packages/model/src/workspace-model.ts
web/packages/model/src/revision-cache.ts
web/packages/model/src/snapshot-state.ts
web/packages/model/src/relation-cache.ts
web/packages/model/src/operation-store.ts
web/packages/model/src/event-reducer.ts
web/packages/model/src/stale-state.ts
web/packages/model/src/subscription.ts
web/packages/model/test/revision-cache.test.ts
web/packages/model/test/event-reducer.test.ts
web/packages/model/test/workspace-model.test.ts

Update:

web/packages/model/src/index.ts
web/packages/model/package.json

docs.title: Model Boundary
docs.text:
The model owns client-side knowledge of already loaded server state.

It may cache and coordinate:

  • immutable revisions;
  • entity resolution for one or more known snapshots;
  • loaded relation pages;
  • operation records;
  • connection/event status;
  • stale-view markers;
  • pending migration previews represented by public protocol objects.

It must not claim that locally cached state is authoritative beyond the snapshot/revision references received from the server.

docs.title: Revision Cache
docs.text:
Implement a cache keyed by immutable RevisionId.

Required behavior:

  • inserting the same revision twice is idempotent;
  • immutable revision content is never mutated in place;
  • a later global snapshot does not evict unchanged revisions automatically;
  • consumers may query whether a revision is loaded;
  • cache values preserve the protocol type/summary required to render or inspect them.

Do not key immutable content solely by mutable/current entity identity.

docs.title: Snapshot State
docs.text:
Represent at least:

current server snapshot
viewed/selected snapshot
historical snapshot state
branch/candidate snapshot state when supplied by protocol

The model must make it possible to distinguish:

  • viewing the current snapshot;
  • viewing an older exact snapshot;
  • a view that became stale because current state advanced;
  • candidate state that has not become canonical.

Do not silently advance historical views when the current snapshot changes.

docs.title: Entity Resolution
docs.text:
Maintain loaded entity-to-revision resolutions scoped by snapshot when required by the protocol.

A snapshot-advanced event may mark current resolutions stale or replace them when the event contains enough information.

Do not rewrite immutable cached revision data when an entity resolves to a new revision.

docs.title: Relation Cache
docs.text:
Cache loaded relation/collection pages by enough identity to prevent mixing incompatible states.

At minimum include semantic scope such as:

snapshot or exact revision context
entity
relation
page/cursor parameters

If the server returns immutable relation-result identities, prefer those.

Do not merge pages from different snapshots without explicit compatibility evidence.

docs.title: Operation Store
docs.text:
Track long-running operations independently from the component/panel that started them.

Support lifecycle states from the protocol:

queued
running
completed
failed
cancelled

Store progress and result references without copying canonical objects into ad-hoc UI-only forms.

Operation updates from events must be idempotent where possible.

docs.title: Event Reducer
docs.text:
Implement a pure or testable event-application layer.

It must handle the event categories provided by @scriberig/protocol, including where available:

  • snapshot advanced;
  • entity revision changed;
  • projection changed;
  • branch/session changed;
  • migration/validation completed;
  • operation progress/completion/failure/cancellation;
  • agent output references or chunks;
  • connection/resume state.

Important rule:

A global snapshot change invalidates only current-resolution assumptions, not every immutable cached revision.

docs.title: Subscription API
docs.text:
Expose a small framework-independent subscription mechanism so React and other consumers can observe changes.

Requirements:

  • subscribe/unsubscribe;
  • notify only after consistent model transitions;
  • no React dependency;
  • no direct component references;
  • allow selectors or narrowly scoped subscriptions if simple to implement without a state framework.

Do not add Redux, Zustand, MobX, RxJS, or another state library in this task.

docs.title: Stale-State Helpers
docs.text:
Provide reusable helpers for determining conditions such as:

view snapshot != current snapshot
entity changed since edit base
candidate migration base is stale
connection lost while viewing live state

Helpers should return structured state, not user-facing prose.

docs.title: Workspace Model
docs.text:
workspace-model.ts composes the client, caches, event reducer, and subscriptions.

It should provide high-level methods needed by later packages for:

  • inspecting/loading semantic objects through the client;
  • resolving loaded entities;
  • loading relation pages;
  • observing current snapshot;
  • inspecting operations;
  • applying incoming events;
  • starting/stopping event subscriptions.

Do not add visual selection or command palette logic here; those belong to @scriberig/editor-core.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Required tests include:

  1. a snapshot advances while an unchanged revision remains cached and reusable;
  2. an entity resolves to a new revision without mutating the old revision object;
  3. historical viewed snapshot remains historical after live snapshot advances;
  4. relation pages from different snapshots do not mix;
  5. operation progress events update one durable operation record;
  6. duplicate/replayed events do not corrupt state;
  7. disconnect state becomes observable.

Use fake client/transport objects. Do not require a running server.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

pnpm --filter @scriberig/model typecheck
pnpm --filter @scriberig/model test
pnpm --filter @scriberig/model build
pnpm typecheck

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not add React.
  • Do not add MUI.
  • Do not store panel layout.
  • Do not implement universal selection yet.
  • Do not implement command discovery yet.
  • Do not hide snapshot identity from consumers.
  • Do not mutate immutable cached revisions.
  • Do not refetch all known data after every snapshot event.
  • Do not persist browser-local state into canonical knowledge.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Immutable revisions are cached by revision identity.
  • [x] Snapshot state distinguishes current, historical, and stale views.
  • [x] Entity resolution is snapshot-aware.
  • [x] Relation pages are snapshot/revision scoped.
  • [x] Long-running operations have durable client-side records.
  • [x] Events update state incrementally.
  • [x] A framework-independent subscription API exists.
  • [x] No third-party global state framework is introduced.
  • [x] Required model tests pass.
  • [x] Workspace typecheck remains green.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the Markdown-specific reconciliation logic required to interpret an externally edited Markdown projection as semantic changes against an existing canonical Markdown state.

This task does not own file watching, snapshot storage, or generic three-way merge orchestration. It implements the domain-specific comparison and identity-matching step that scriberig-projection can invoke.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
  2. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  3. design/level-3/002. implement markdown domain schema.md
  4. design/level-3/003. implement markdown adapter mapping.md
  5. current public APIs in scriberig-migration and scriberig-projection

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Inside crates/domains/markdown/, create or update:

src/lib.rs
src/reconcile.rs
src/match_nodes.rs
src/change.rs
src/error.rs

Add tests under:

tests/reconcile.rs

Reuse parsing from Task 003. Do not build a second parser.

docs.title: Inputs and Output
docs.text:
The reconciliation layer must be able to accept conceptually:

base semantic Markdown state
newly parsed candidate Markdown state

and produce:

semantic change proposal / migration operations
plus ambiguity/conflict information

Use existing shared migration types where available. Do not invent a Markdown-only history format.

The adapter must not write directly to persistence.

docs.title: Identity Matching Strategy
docs.text:
Implement deterministic matching before any model-assisted behavior exists.

Use domain evidence in this order where practical:

  1. exact semantic subtree equality;
  2. exact canonical content equality;
  3. same structural role under an already matched parent;
  4. sibling sequence alignment;
  5. heading/title identity for sections when sufficiently distinctive;
  6. text/content similarity for paragraphs and simple blocks;
  7. structural similarity for lists and tables.

The implementation may use a simpler subset initially, but exact equality, parent context, sibling order, and heading/paragraph similarity must be covered.

Never use source byte offsets as the primary identity signal.

docs.title: Required Change Classes
docs.text:
Support at least:

unchanged entity reuse
content revision of an existing paragraph
heading/section title revision
block insertion
block deletion
block reordering
section insertion
section deletion
list-item insertion/deletion/reordering
table-row insertion/deletion/change
cell content change

Where the shared migration model has generic operations, map Markdown changes onto those operations rather than creating a parallel history mechanism.

docs.title: Ambiguity Rules
docs.text:
False continuity is worse than creating a new entity.

When two or more old entities are equally plausible predecessors for one candidate entity, return explicit ambiguity instead of silently choosing one.

Examples include:

  • duplicate paragraphs reordered around each other;
  • repeated identical headings under similar parents;
  • repeated table rows with no stable distinguishing content.

The result must allow the caller to decide whether to create new entities, request manual resolution, or use a later assisted reconciliation layer.

Do not call an LLM in this task.

docs.title: Semantic vs Formatting-Only Changes
docs.text:
Formatting-only edits classified as projection-only by the Markdown schema must not produce semantic revisions.

Examples include changes only to:

line wrapping
blank-line count
non-semantic indentation
table padding/alignment spacing

Add explicit tests proving these do not generate semantic changes for supported syntax.

docs.title: Migration Construction
docs.text:
The reconciliation result must preserve the universal change model.

For example, changing:

A

B

to:

A changed

C

B

must be representable as:

revise existing A entity
create/insert C entity
reuse B entity

not as "replace entire document blob."

Unchanged entities must be reusable by identity.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Cover at least:

  1. unchanged document -> no semantic operations;
  2. paragraph edit -> existing entity receives a new semantic revision/change;
  3. inserted paragraph -> one new entity plus collection change;
  4. moved unchanged paragraph -> reuse entity plus order change;
  5. renamed heading -> section continuity when unambiguous;
  6. inserted nested section;
  7. table row edit with unchanged surrounding rows reused;
  8. formatting-only edit -> no semantic change;
  9. duplicate/ambiguous content -> explicit ambiguity;
  10. large unchanged sibling region -> unchanged identities reused.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-domain-markdown
cargo clippy -p scriberig-domain-markdown --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not watch files.
  • Do not commit snapshots directly.
  • Do not create Markdown-specific migration tables.
  • Do not treat every edited file as a replacement document.
  • Do not use line numbers or byte offsets as semantic identity.
  • Do not silently resolve ambiguous identity matches.
  • Do not call an agent/model.
  • Do not implement generic merge logic owned by scriberig-migration or scriberig-projection.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Reconciliation compares base semantic state to a parsed candidate.
  • [x] Unchanged entities are reused.
  • [x] Content edits become semantic revisions/operations.
  • [x] Insertions, deletions, and moves are represented structurally.
  • [x] Formatting-only edits do not cause semantic churn.
  • [x] Ambiguity is explicit.
  • [x] Output uses shared migration/change abstractions.
  • [x] No direct persistence writes occur.
  • [x] Tests, formatting, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement Persistent Snapshots and Snapshot Diffs
Mission
docs.text:
Implement immutable snapshots as a persistent Merkle radix map from EntityId to RevisionId.

This task is the core answer to the change-propagation problem: one entity revision change must produce a new global SnapshotId without forcing unrelated semantic entities to receive new revisions.

Do not implement named roots in this task.

docs.title: Read Before Editing
docs.text:
Read completely:

design/level-1/003. identity revisions and snapshots.md
design/level-2/001. identity revision snapshot implementation.md
design/level-3/001. bootstrap workspace and identity types.md
design/level-3/002. implement canonical encoding and revision hashing.md
design/level-3/003. implement immutable revision store.md

Assume tasks 001 through 003 are complete.

docs.title: Files You Own
docs.text:
Create or modify:

crates/sr-store/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-store/src/snapshot.rs
crates/sr-store/src/snapshot_trie.rs
crates/sr-store/tests/snapshots.rs

Do not modify revision semantics from task 003.

docs.title: Required Snapshot Model
docs.text:
A snapshot is exactly a mapping:

EntityId -> RevisionId

The mapping must be immutable.

Operations that appear to modify a snapshot must return a new Snapshot and leave the input snapshot fully usable.

The semantic containment graph must not be used as the storage Merkle tree.

docs.title: Persistent Trie
docs.text:
Implement a private immutable 16-way radix trie over all 128 bits of EntityId.

Each tree level consumes one 4-bit nibble.

There are therefore at most 32 branch levels before a leaf.

Logical node kinds:

Empty
Branch(children[16])
Leaf(EntityId, RevisionId)

You may represent empty children compactly internally, but the logical hash must behave as though all nibble positions are ordered and explicit.

Use Arc or another immutable shared pointer so unchanged branches are physically shared between related snapshots.

docs.title: Node Hashing
docs.text:
Use BLAKE3.

Define different fixed domain tags for:

empty trie node
branch trie node
leaf trie node
snapshot root

Every node hash must include EncodingVersion.

docs.title: Leaf hash
docs.text:
Hash the canonical encoding of:

leaf domain tag
encoding version
EntityId bytes
RevisionId bytes

docs.title: Branch hash
docs.text:
Hash the canonical encoding of:

branch domain tag
encoding version
16 child node digests in nibble order

docs.title: Empty hash
docs.text: Define one deterministic empty-node hash per encoding version.

docs.title: Snapshot ID
docs.text:
The SnapshotId must be derived from:

snapshot-root domain tag
encoding version
root trie digest

Do not use the internal root node digest directly as SnapshotId without the extra snapshot-root domain separation.

docs.title: Required Snapshot Operations
docs.text:
Expose behavior equivalent to:

Snapshot::empty(version)
snapshot.id()
snapshot.len()
snapshot.resolve(entity)
snapshot.with_revision(entity, revision)
snapshot.without_entity(entity)
snapshot.iter()
snapshot.diff(other)

Exact Rust signatures may differ, but the semantics must match.

docs.title: with_revision
docs.text:
• [x] Returns a new snapshot.
  • [x] Old snapshot remains unchanged.
  • [x] If the entity already resolves to the exact requested revision, return an equivalent snapshot with the same SnapshotId.
  • [x] Only nodes on the entity's radix path may be newly allocated, except for harmless implementation metadata.

docs.title: without_entity
docs.text:
• [x] Returns a new snapshot when the entity exists.
  • [x] Returns an equivalent snapshot with the same ID when the entity is absent.
  • [x] Must not mutate the previous snapshot.
  • [x] May collapse now-empty internal branches if canonical hashing stays deterministic.

docs.title: resolve
docs.text: Resolve only against the supplied snapshot. Do not consult a global current root.

docs.title: Deterministic Iteration
docs.text:
Iteration order must be ascending by EntityId bytes.

Do not expose hash-table ordering.

This deterministic order is also the required order for diff results.

docs.title: Snapshot Diff
docs.text:
Define public diff result cases equivalent to:

Added(entity, revision)
Removed(entity, revision)
Changed(entity, from_revision, to_revision)

snapshot.diff(other) must return only entity resolutions that actually differ.

The first implementation may compare the deterministic iterators if that is simpler and clearly correct.

Do not block this task on an optimized Merkle-aware diff.

Keep trie internals private so a later optimized implementation can skip equal subtrees by digest without changing the public API.

docs.title: Structural-Sharing Verification
docs.text:
Add a test-only mechanism to determine whether unchanged trie subtrees are pointer-shared.

This mechanism must not become part of the normal public production API.

Construct two snapshots that differ in one entity whose first nibble differs from at least one unchanged entity.

Verify that an unaffected top-level child subtree is shared between old and new snapshots.

docs.title: Required Tests
docs.text:
In crates/sr-store/tests/snapshots.rs, test at least:

  • [x] empty snapshot ID is deterministic;
  • [x] two independently built empty snapshots have identical IDs;
  • [x] inserting one mapping changes the snapshot ID;
  • [x] old snapshot does not resolve the newly inserted mapping;
  • [x] new snapshot resolves it;
  • [x] setting the same revision again preserves SnapshotId;
  • [x] removing an absent entity preserves SnapshotId;
  • [x] removing an existing entity changes SnapshotId;
  • [x] insertion order does not affect final SnapshotId;
  • [x] two snapshots with the same complete mapping have the same ID;
  • [x] iteration is deterministic by EntityId;
  • [x] diff reports added entities;
  • [x] diff reports removed entities;
  • [x] diff reports changed revisions;
  • [x] diff omits unchanged entities;
  • [x] an unaffected trie branch is structurally shared;
  • [x] many entities sharing long nibble prefixes resolve correctly.

Also add a regression test demonstrating the architectural rule:

changing P2 from PR8 to PR9

changes only the P2 mapping while F, P1, and B continue resolving to their previous revision IDs.

docs.title: Performance Guardrail
docs.text:
Do not add a benchmark requirement yet, but ensure one mapping update does not rebuild an iterator-sized copy of the whole mapping.

The implementation path for one update must be bounded by trie depth, not by total entity count.

docs.title: Commands to Run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
• Do not recursively hash the semantic object graph.
  • Do not include parent entity revisions automatically in a child update.
  • Do not use a mutable HashMap as the authoritative snapshot state.
  • Do not make SnapshotId an incrementing integer.
  • Do not create a global current snapshot.
  • Do not implement named roots or CAS in this task.
  • Do not expose Arc or trie nodes as public semantic API.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Persistent 16-way radix trie exists.
  • [x] Snapshot IDs are content-derived and domain-separated.
  • [x] Updates structurally share unaffected branches.
  • [x] Equivalent mappings have equivalent IDs regardless of construction order.
  • [x] Snapshot resolution is explicit and local to the snapshot.
  • [x] Snapshot diff is deterministic and exact.
  • [x] Old snapshots remain usable after successor creation.
  • [x] Tests, formatting, and clippy all pass.

docs.title: Implement Reverse Dependency Invalidation and Explanations
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the reusable mechanics that determine which derived results are affected by semantic change and explain why a cached result can or cannot be reused.

This task must use declared dependencies. It must not invalidate everything merely because the global snapshot changed.

It also must not eagerly delete historical artifacts simply because they are not valid for a newer state.

Do not implement domain-specific analyzers, background scheduling, protocol transport, agents, or a durable backend in this task.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/008. derived knowledge caching and incrementality.md
  2. design/level-2/001. derived knowledge runtime and cache design.md
  3. derived Level 3 tasks 001, 002, and 003.

Inspect the repository contract implemented by task 002.

If reverse dependency lookup is already part of that contract, reuse it. Do not create a second index abstraction with overlapping meaning.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Inside the canonical derivation crate:

src/invalidation.rs
src/explain.rs
src/repository.rs   # only if a minimal lookup extension is required
src/lib.rs

Tests may be module-local now and consolidated by the final conformance task later.

docs.title: 1. Change Input Model
docs.text:
Define InvalidationSet, ChangeSet, or an equivalent domain-neutral input type describing semantic changes relevant to derived dependencies.

It must support at least conceptual changes for:

entity revision changed
snapshot changed
scope/collection revision changed
configuration identity changed
derived-result dependency changed

Do not encode file timestamps or line ranges as universal invalidation inputs.

Domain adapters may later translate a semantic migration into this universal change set.

The input model should make old and new exact identities available where useful for explanation.

Example:

ExactRevisionChanged {
    entity: Type T,
    from: R5,
    to: R6,
}

docs.title: 2. Affected Result Lookup
docs.text:
Implement a service/function that uses reverse dependency lookup to find derived result records potentially affected by the change set.

The outcome should separate:

Affected
Unaffected / not returned

A result is affected when one of its declared dependencies no longer matches the requested semantic state.

Do not automatically classify all results created under an older global snapshot as affected.

Snapshot-dependent results are affected only when they explicitly declared the relevant snapshot dependency.

docs.title: 3. Scope and Absence Dependencies
docs.text:
Add tests proving that scope dependencies work even when positive result members are unchanged.

Example:

query: all callers of F
old result: [G, H]

A new function J is added and now calls F.

Neither G nor H changed.

The cached result must still be considered affected because its completeness dependency on caller scope changed.

Do not implement source-code caller analysis in this task. Model the scenario with generic test dependency identities.

docs.title: 4. Historical Artifacts Remain Valid for Old Inputs
docs.text:
Invalidation for new state must not mutate the old result record into an invalid object.

The historical statement remains:

result D was produced for DerivationKey K

The new request simply has a different key/dependency state.

Therefore invalidation should conceptually produce:

result D does not satisfy new state

not:

rewrite D as invalid

A backend may maintain disposable invalidation/index metadata, but immutable result content must remain unchanged.

docs.title: 5. Reuse Explanation Model
docs.text:
In explain.rs, define structured explanation types with stable machine-readable reason codes.

Support at least equivalents of:

ExactKeyMatch
NoStoredResult
ProfileMismatch
RevisionChanged
SnapshotChanged
ScopeChanged
ConfigurationChanged
DerivedDependencyChanged
FreshnessExpired
StatusNotReusable
SelectionRejected

Reuse freshness/selection outcomes from task 003 rather than redefining them.

Every explanation should be capable of carrying relevant exact IDs in structured fields when available.

Do not make callers parse prose to discover which dependency changed.

docs.title: 6. Reuse Decision
docs.text:
Implement a pure or mostly pure evaluation path that can answer conceptually:

Can this stored result satisfy this requested DerivationKey/policy?

Possible outcomes should include:

Reuse(result, explanation)
Miss(explanation)
Recompute(explanation)

If Miss and Recompute are semantically the same at this layer, use one type plus a reason that higher scheduling layers can interpret. Do not invent fake distinctions just to match names in the design.

The important behavior is structured explainability.

docs.title: 7. Invalidation Propagation Through Derived Dependencies
docs.text:
Support derived-result dependencies transitively.

Example:

Function F@R1 -> Summary SF
Summary SF + Summary SG -> ModuleSummary M1

If F@R1 changes to F@R2:

  1. SF is affected for the new function state;
  2. results depending on SF, such as M1, are also affected for any derivation request expecting a summary built from the changed function state.

Implement cycle protection even if derivation graphs are expected to be acyclic in normal operation.

Use visited-result tracking during traversal.

Do not crash or loop forever if malformed metadata contains a dependency cycle.

docs.title: 8. Conservative Dependencies Are Correct
docs.text:
Add tests demonstrating that a derivation may depend on an entire snapshot.

When that snapshot changes, the result is affected even if the particular leaf objects it inspected did not.

This is conservative invalidation and is valid.

The invalidation engine must not attempt to second-guess declared dependencies by inspecting result payloads.

Dependency precision belongs to the producer/adapter.

docs.title: 9. Formatting vs Semantic Change
docs.text:
Add a generic test proving this intended pattern:

semantic summary depends on FunctionRevision F@R7
rendering depends on F@R7 + Style ST1

When only style changes:

ST1 -> ST2

then:

  • rendering for the old style does not satisfy the new render request;
  • semantic summary remains reusable.

Do not require a Rust renderer for this test.

Use generic dependency identities.

docs.title: 10. Public API
docs.text:
Expose equivalents of:

InvalidationSet
SemanticChange
AffectedResult
ReuseDecision
ReuseExplanation
ReuseReasonCode

Keep APIs small and domain-neutral.

Documentation must state that invalidation is based on declared semantic dependencies rather than file timestamps.

docs.title: Required Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  1. exact revision change affects a dependent result;
  2. unrelated revision change does not affect a local result;
  3. explicit snapshot dependency is affected by snapshot change;
  4. local result without snapshot dependency survives unrelated snapshot change;
  5. scope dependency invalidates a completeness result when membership changes;
  6. configuration/style change affects only results that declared it;
  7. derived-result dependency propagates invalidation transitively;
  8. cycle protection terminates safely;
  9. old result record remains immutable after invalidation analysis;
  10. explanation includes exact changed dependency IDs;
  11. no stored result returns a structured miss reason;
  12. stale freshness result integrates with explanation without duplicating freshness logic;
  13. failed status integrates with explanation without parsing error strings.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt
cargo check --workspace
cargo test --workspace

Use clippy if already part of repository practice.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
Do not:

  • invalidate all results on every snapshot change;
  • inspect source files to infer dependencies;
  • mutate old result records;
  • delete results automatically during invalidation;
  • recompute derivations;
  • add a task scheduler;
  • add domain-specific dependency variants;
  • add agent/server/UI code.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] semantic change-set type exists;
  • [x] reverse dependency lookup finds affected results;
  • [x] unrelated local results remain reusable;
  • [x] scope/absence dependency behavior is tested;
  • [x] snapshot-conservative dependency behavior is tested;
  • [x] derived-result invalidation propagates transitively;
  • [x] cycles are safe;
  • [x] structured reason codes exist;
  • [x] exact changed identities appear in explanations;
  • [x] historical result records remain immutable;
  • [x] no eager recomputation is introduced.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement sr-store-sqlite as the first durable backend for the storage interfaces already implemented by sr-store and exercised by sr-store-memory.

The SQLite backend must preserve exactly the same logical behavior as the memory backend while adding durable transactions and recovery.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/004. persistence and storage model.md
  2. design/level-2/001. persistence crate boundaries.md
  3. design/level-2/004. sqlite backend transactions and recovery.md
  4. Level 3 tasks 001 through 003.

Do not redesign the public storage traits unless a concrete incompatibility is found. If a trait must change, update the memory backend and tests in the same change.

docs.title: Files to create or update
docs.text:
crates/sr-store-sqlite/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-store-sqlite/src/
├── lib.rs
├── connection.rs
├── schema.rs
├── revision.rs
├── snapshot.rs
├── roots.rs
└── recovery.rs

If using external SQL migration files, also create:

crates/sr-store-sqlite/migrations/

Use one established Rust SQLite crate. Keep it private to sr-store-sqlite.

docs.title: Database initialization
docs.text:
Implement opening a database by path and an in-memory SQLite database for tests.

On first open:

  • create the backend schema;
  • record a backend schema version;
  • initialize any required metadata.

On later opens:

  • detect the schema version;
  • reject unsupported newer versions explicitly;
  • run supported storage-schema upgrades if any exist.

Do not treat storage-schema upgrades as semantic migrations.

docs.title: Revision persistence
docs.text:
Persist immutable revision records keyed by RevisionId.

Requirements:

  • exact duplicate insertion is idempotent;
  • retrieval reconstructs the same logical revision record;
  • stored bytes are sufficient to recompute and verify revision identity;
  • backend row IDs are never exposed as semantic IDs.

docs.title: Snapshot persistence
docs.text:
Persist the internal structurally shared snapshot-map representation selected by the existing storage API.

A snapshot record must identify its persistent map root and deterministic SnapshotId.

Do not serialize a complete entity-to-revision map into a new monolithic blob for every snapshot if that defeats the Level 1 structural-sharing requirement.

docs.title: Named roots and transactions
docs.text:
Implement root promotion with compare-and-set semantics inside a SQLite transaction.

Conceptual sequence:

BEGIN
insert missing immutable revisions/map nodes/snapshot
read root current value
compare with expected
if mismatch: ROLLBACK and return stale-root conflict
update root
COMMIT

The exact SQL may differ, but externally visible behavior must match this model.

docs.title: Recovery behavior
docs.text:
A reopened database must expose only committed named-root state.

Prepared immutable objects that were inserted but never made reachable by a promoted root are allowed.

No recovery path may mutate an old revision or snapshot to repair an incomplete write.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add durable backend tests for:

  • initialize fresh database;
  • close and reopen database;
  • revision survives reopen;
  • snapshot survives reopen;
  • named root survives reopen;
  • duplicate revision insert is idempotent;
  • stale root CAS fails and root remains unchanged;
  • explicit transaction rollback leaves old root visible;
  • unsupported newer backend schema version fails with a typed error;
  • failure before root promotion does not expose attempted new root.

Where possible, run tests against temporary database files rather than only SQLite :memory:.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not expose a raw SQLite connection through the public sr-store interface.
  • Do not add agent/session/domain tables.
  • Do not rely on SQLite row order for canonical identity.
  • Do not mutate existing canonical revision rows.
  • Do not implement semantic merges.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] SQLite backend implements the existing revision/snapshot/root interfaces.
  • [x] Fresh initialization and reopen work.
  • [x] Named-root promotion is transactional and compare-and-set based.
  • [x] Previous snapshots remain readable.
  • [x] Backend schema versioning is explicit.
  • [x] Crash/reopen semantics expose only committed roots.
  • [x] Workspace tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Scaffold Web UI Packages and Editor Shell
Objective
docs.text:
Extend the web workspace created by 003. initialize web workspace and headless packages.md with reusable UI packages and the integrated Scriberig editor shell prescribed by design/level-2/001. workspace and package layout.md.

This task creates package boundaries and a minimal application shell only. Do not implement semantic browsers, editors, agent panels, MUI widgets, routing, server communication, or application state behavior.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/001. vision and principles.md
  2. design/level-2/001. workspace and package layout.md
  3. design/level-3/003. initialize web workspace and headless packages.md

The important architectural rules are:

  • the integrated editor is a consumer of public packages;
  • low-level database/revision views and high-level semantic/agent views must eventually resolve through the same public model;
  • reusable components must not depend on the private integrated editor app;
  • MUI-specific code belongs only in the MUI package or integrated app;
  • product behavior must not bypass @scriberig/client, @scriberig/model, and the public editor abstractions.

docs.title: Files to Create
docs.text:
Create:

web/packages/components/package.json
web/packages/components/src/index.ts
web/packages/components-mui/package.json
web/packages/components-mui/src/index.ts
web/packages/agent-ui/package.json
web/packages/agent-ui/src/index.ts

web/apps/editor/package.json
web/apps/editor/src/main.tsx

Do not create additional application framework files unless a later design explicitly chooses the framework/build system.

docs.title: Package Names and Roles
docs.text:
Use these names exactly:

web/packages/components      -> @scriberig/components
web/packages/components-mui  -> @scriberig/components-mui
web/packages/agent-ui        -> @scriberig/agent-ui
web/apps/editor              -> @scriberig/editor-app

Use version 0.1.0 for the reusable packages.

Mark the integrated editor app private.

At this stage the reusable packages may also remain private to avoid accidental publication before release design exists.

docs.title: Internal Dependency Direction
docs.text:
Represent these workspace dependencies:

@scriberig/components
├── @scriberig/react
└── @scriberig/editor-core

@scriberig/components-mui
├── @scriberig/react
├── @scriberig/editor-core
└── @scriberig/components

@scriberig/agent-ui
├── @scriberig/react
├── @scriberig/editor-core
└── @scriberig/model

@scriberig/editor-app
├── @scriberig/client
├── @scriberig/model
├── @scriberig/editor-core
├── @scriberig/react
├── @scriberig/components
├── @scriberig/components-mui
└── @scriberig/agent-ui

Use pnpm workspace references for all internal packages.

No public package may depend on @scriberig/editor-app.

docs.title: MUI Boundary
docs.text:
This task reserves the MUI-specific package boundary but does not need to install or implement MUI yet.

If MUI dependencies are added while performing this task, they are allowed only in:

web/packages/components-mui
web/apps/editor

They must not appear in:

@scriberig/protocol
@scriberig/client
@scriberig/model
@scriberig/editor-core
@scriberig/react
@scriberig/components
@scriberig/agent-ui

Do not add MUI merely to make the package name appear justified. An empty documented scaffold is acceptable and preferred until component design exists.

docs.title: Reusable Package Source Files
docs.text:
Each reusable package src/index.ts should contain only documentation comments and an empty module export.

Document the intended roles accurately:

  • @scriberig/components: reusable style-neutral or styleable Scriberig component boundary;
  • @scriberig/components-mui: opinionated MUI implementation over public editor/React primitives;
  • @scriberig/agent-ui: reusable UI primitives for sessions, branches, agent operations, and agent-scoped semantic selections.

Do not invent components such as ObjectTree, AgentPanel, or SemanticDiff until their API has a lower-level design.

docs.title: Integrated Editor main.tsx
docs.text:
Create a compileable placeholder module only.

It may contain a comment explaining that the integrated editor will compose public Scriberig packages and an empty export:

export {};

Do not create a private semantic model in the app.

Do not create a raw database API client in the app.

Do not add direct server fetches.

Do not add placeholder UI that would establish accidental product architecture before the editor design exists.

docs.title: Editor App Manifest
docs.text:
The editor app manifest must express dependencies on the public packages listed above using pnpm workspace references.

Do not add a production framework, router, state library, or build system unless a later design explicitly selects it.

This means the app may not yet have a runnable browser bundle. That is acceptable: this task establishes the dependency boundary, not the final web runtime.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
From web/, if pnpm is available, run:

pnpm install
pnpm list -r --depth -1

Verify that the three new packages and editor app are discovered.

Inspect package manifests and verify:

  • no package imports the editor app;
  • only the MUI package/editor may contain MUI dependencies;
