  • the editor depends on reusable packages rather than private source paths;
  • workspace dependencies resolve without cycles.

Do not introduce a framework just to create a build command for this scaffold.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not implement actual UI components.
  • Do not choose a router.
  • Do not choose an application state library.
  • Do not implement HTTP/WebSocket calls.
  • Do not implement agent commands.
  • Do not implement raw entity browsing.
  • Do not implement semantic editing.
  • Do not add private product-only model types.
  • Do not bypass the public package boundaries.
  • Do not edit Level 1 or Level 2 design documents.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] @scriberig/components exists with the correct dependencies.
  • [x] @scriberig/components-mui exists with the correct dependencies.
  • [x] @scriberig/agent-ui exists with the correct dependencies.
  • [x] @scriberig/editor-app exists and is private.
  • [x] Editor app dependencies use public workspace packages.
  • [x] No public package depends on the editor app.
  • [x] No MUI dependency leaks into headless packages.
  • [x] No speculative component API was created.
  • [x] No application framework was selected prematurely.
  • [x] pnpm discovers all web packages and the editor app when pnpm is available.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Complete the first universal knowledge model implementation with cross-crate conformance tests and public API documentation.

The tests must prove that the shared core, schema, and graph layers satisfy the semantic rules in design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md without relying on an agent runtime, UI, parser, or specific database backend.

This task should primarily add tests and documentation. Only make small implementation fixes needed to satisfy explicit invariants.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md
  2. design/level-2/001. universal knowledge model rust libraries.md
  3. design/level-3/001. extend shared core with knowledge values and provenance.md
  4. design/level-3/002. implement universal schema contracts.md
  5. design/level-3/003. implement universal graph semantic records.md
  6. the identity/revision/snapshot design used by the implemented workspace.

Inspect the actual crate names and APIs before writing tests. Reuse the canonical shared crates; do not create alternate versions of them.

docs.title: Primary Test File
docs.text:
Create or fill the universal graph crate's integration test:

tests/universal_model.rs

Use the path inside the canonical graph crate already registered in the workspace.

You may also improve public documentation in the shared core/schema/graph modules when the tests reveal unclear contracts.

docs.title: 1. Define a Test-Only Domain Schema
docs.text:
Inside the integration test, define a small schema using names such as:

Document
Section
Paragraph

These are test fixtures only.

Suggested test structure:

Document --sections--> Section       ordered collection
Section  --blocks----> Paragraph     ordered collection
Section  --related---> Section       typed relation
Paragraph.text                       required string property
Section.title                        optional string property

Use schema/type IDs created through the normal public API.

Do not add Document, Section, or Paragraph as variants or production structs in the universal crates.

docs.title: 2. Entity Continuity vs Exact Revision
docs.text:
Create one paragraph entity and represent two exact revisions for it.

The test must demonstrate:

same EntityId
+ different RevisionId
= same conceptual entity at different exact states

Use the identity/storage APIs already defined by prerequisite work.

Do not invent a second ID implementation in the test.

Assert that EntityId and RevisionId are distinct public types.

docs.title: 3. Snapshot-Bound Interpretation
docs.text:
Use the existing in-memory snapshot/store implementation if one exists; otherwise implement a tiny test double for the graph-view trait.

Create two snapshots:

S1: Paragraph P -> Revision R1
S2: Paragraph P -> Revision R2

Assert that resolving P in S1 and S2 returns the different expected revisions.

This test must fail if the graph API silently uses an implicit global current revision instead of the requested snapshot.

docs.title: 4. Ordered Collection Semantics
docs.text:
Construct an ordered collection containing:

[P1, P2, P3]

Assert order is preserved.

Construct another ordered collection:

[P2, P1, P3]

Assert the values differ.

The entities P1, P2, and P3 must keep the same identities in both collections.

This proves that position belongs to the parent collection rather than the child entity.

docs.title: 5. Unordered Collection Semantics
docs.text:
Construct two unordered collections containing the same members supplied in different input orders.

Assert they have identical semantic membership/equality according to the public API.

The test must show that callers cannot infer semantic order from insertion or storage order.

docs.title: 6. No Canonical Parent Requirement
docs.text:
Construct a paragraph revision containing only its own type/property state.

Construct a section revision whose collection contains the paragraph entity.

Assert that the paragraph revision does not require a parent ID or position.

If reverse navigation exists in the graph view, use a test/mock reverse index to find the parent and demonstrate that reverse lookup is a derived/view concern.

docs.title: 7. Typed Relation Validation
docs.text:
Using the test schema, validate:

Section A --related--> Section B

as valid.

Then validate an invalid target type such as:

Section A --related--> Paragraph P

Assert the invalid case produces a structured validation issue with a stable machine-readable code.

Do not determine validity by matching the human-readable message string.

docs.title: 8. Property Validation
docs.text:
Validate at least:

  1. a paragraph with required string text;
  2. a paragraph missing text;
  3. a paragraph with text set to the wrong value shape.

Assert:

  • the valid subject has no error-severity issues;
  • invalid subjects have error-severity issues;
  • issues contain semantic locations where practical;
  • validation does not panic for ordinary invalid input.

docs.title: 9. Provenance
docs.text:
Create provenance examples for:

user-authored knowledge
parser-produced knowledge
model-generated description

Assert source kinds remain distinguishable.

Create provenance with exact entity/revision dependencies and assert those dependencies can be inspected directly.

Do not add trust ranking assertions. Provenance records origin only.

docs.title: 10. Derived Description
docs.text:
Create a description for one exact paragraph revision.

It must contain:

exact entity/revision reference
description profile
text
provenance

Use model-generated provenance for this test.

Assert that the description remains a separate derived object and is not automatically inserted into the canonical revision record.

docs.title: 11. Derived Artifact Dependencies
docs.text:
Create a generic derived artifact with at least two exact immutable input dependencies.

Example concept:

Section S@R1 summary depends on:
  Section S@R1
  Paragraph P@R3

Assert that exact dependency revision IDs remain inspectable.

This proves the future incremental-cache contract: an unrelated global snapshot change need not invalidate a derived result whose declared inputs are unchanged.

Do not implement a cache in this task.

docs.title: 12. Cross-Domain Neutrality
docs.text:
Search the production universal crates before completing the task.

They must not hard-code production variants/types such as:

MarkdownSection
RustFunction
PdfPage
SessionBranch

Documentation may mention these as examples.

Runtime schemas/domain crates must supply those names later.

Add a test or compile-time usage pattern showing that test domain entity types are represented through schema IDs/definitions rather than universal enum variants.

docs.title: 13. Reverse Navigation Contract
docs.text:
If the graph-view API exposes reverse relation lookup, verify that:

  • forward canonical relation exists only in the owning source revision;
  • target revision does not need a duplicate reverse edge;
  • reverse lookup can still return the source through the view/index abstraction.

If reverse lookup is not yet implemented because it belongs to a later index design, test the type-level contract as far as currently possible and document the deferred behavior clearly.

Do not add backend-specific indexing solely for this test.

docs.title: 14. Public Documentation Review
docs.text:
Review public API docs across the three layers.

Ensure they clearly communicate:

EntityId   = conceptual continuity
RevisionId = exact immutable state
SnapshotId = exact consistent graph view

Also document:

  • property values are not a substitute for semantic relations;
  • relations are typed;
  • ordered/unordered collections differ semantically;
  • child entities do not own parent position;
  • canonical and derived knowledge differ;
  • descriptions/derived artifacts carry provenance and dependencies;
  • graph reads that depend on state are snapshot-bound;
  • universal libraries do not depend on the agent runtime.

Keep API docs concise; do not copy whole design documents into Rust comments.

docs.title: 15. Validation Commands
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt
cargo check --workspace
cargo test --workspace

If available:

cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

If clippy reports pre-existing unrelated warnings, do not broadly rewrite unrelated code; report them separately.

docs.title: 16. Final Scope Audit
docs.text:
Before completing, verify this universal-model work did not accidentally add:

  • a second core/store crate;
  • a new identity/hash algorithm;
  • a second snapshot implementation;
  • SQLite-specific semantic APIs;
  • parser libraries;
  • renderers;
  • migrations;
  • agent runtime;
  • HTTP server/client behavior;
  • CLI/TUI behavior;
  • UI components;
  • hard-coded production domain schemas.

The result must remain a reusable semantic model layer.

  • [x] snapshot-bound resolution is demonstrated;

  • [x] production universal crates remain domain-neutral;
  • [x] public docs state the key semantic contracts;
  • [x] workspace checks and tests pass;
  • [x] no deferred subsystem was introduced.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement @scriberig/editor-core as the framework-independent interaction layer for semantic selection, knowledge-tree navigation, commands, history, diffs, branches, migration review, and projection coordination.

This package contains behavior and state transitions only. It must not render JSX and must not depend on React or MUI.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md
  2. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
  3. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md
  4. design/level-3/004. implement client semantic model and incremental events.md

Prerequisite: @scriberig/model compiles and exposes framework-independent subscriptions/state access.

docs.title: Universal Selection
docs.text:
Implement one semantic selection type/model capable of representing:

entity
optional exact revision
snapshot
optional relation/path context
optional projection location

Requirements:

  • support current-resolution selection and exact historical selection;
  • preserve snapshot identity;
  • allow projection views to attach location metadata without changing semantic identity;
  • support equality/comparison helpers based on semantic meaning;
  • avoid file-path/line-number assumptions in the core representation.

Selection is local interaction state, not canonical knowledge.

docs.title: Selection Controller
docs.text:
Implement a small controller/state object for active selection.

It must support:

  • get current selection;
  • set/clear selection;
  • subscribe/unsubscribe;
  • update projection/path context while retaining semantic entity where appropriate;
  • preserve historical exact revisions when current snapshot advances.

Do not couple selection to browser URL routing in this package.

docs.title: Command Model
docs.text:
Implement a command descriptor model with at least:

id
title
read-only or mutating classification
applicability predicate/capability requirements
execute descriptor or operation factory
optional keyboard/menu metadata
optional domain metadata

Commands must resolve to public application/client operations, not frontend-only database mutations.

Implement command discovery given:

  • current semantic selection;
  • server/client capability set;
  • registered domain extensions.

The same command descriptor must be usable later from palettes, menus, buttons, and agent-oriented action surfaces.

Do not embed JSX or MUI icons in the core descriptor. Use semantic icon keys/metadata if necessary.

docs.title: Knowledge Tree
docs.text:
Implement a headless expandable semantic tree controller.

It must support:

  • a root semantic reference;
  • lazy child loading by relation/collection;
  • expand/collapse;
  • loading/error state per node;
  • child counts or summary metadata where supplied;
  • stable semantic node handles;
  • selection integration;
  • pagination/cursor continuation for large child sets;
  • refreshing a loaded branch when current resolution changes.

It must not recursively load all descendants.

The controller should work for raw knowledge, domain trees, sessions, PDFs, and other relation-driven structures.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
Implement reusable navigation state for semantic history such as:

back
forward
open selection
reveal related entity

Navigation entries must preserve enough snapshot/revision context to revisit exact historical state.

Do not assume URL routing or one fixed panel layout.

docs.title: History and Diff Controllers
docs.text:
Provide headless coordination models for:

  • loading entity/snapshot history;
  • selecting two comparable revisions/snapshots;
  • requesting semantic diff;
  • tracking raw/projection diff availability when provided;
  • navigating changed semantic entities.

Do not implement visual diff rendering here.

docs.title: Branch Navigation
docs.text:
Provide a controller/model for session/project branches that can:

  • list child branches lazily;
  • expose branch description/purpose/outcome;
  • select/open a branch;
  • resolve result references such as migrations or snapshots;
  • preserve branch semantic identity independently of chat transcript rendering.

docs.title: Migration Review
docs.text:
Implement local review state around a protocol migration proposal/detail.

It should support:

  • current proposal/base snapshot;
  • list of affected semantic objects;
  • selected change;
  • validation status reference;
  • stale/conflict state;
  • accept/apply command creation through the public client operation;
  • reject/close local review without mutating canonical state.

Do not directly apply database updates.

docs.title: Projection Session
docs.text:
Implement reusable state for coordinating a semantic object with a projection editor/view.

It should carry:

  • semantic selection;
  • projection identity;
  • snapshot/base state;
  • candidate/draft state when present;
  • semantic location mapping when available;
  • stale/conflict markers.

Do not implement Monaco, CodeMirror, PDF rendering, or Markdown editing in this task.

docs.title: Domain Extension Registry
docs.text:
Implement a minimal public extension registry supporting descriptors for:

  • inspectors;
  • projection handlers;
  • diff handlers;
  • relation views;
  • command providers;
  • labels/icons metadata;
  • validation presentation metadata.

The registry stores descriptors/handlers, not React components in the core package. React/component packages may interpret view keys or adapters later.

Keep the API small and typed.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Required tests:

  1. one selection can retain entity identity while projection location changes;
  2. historical exact selection does not silently resolve to a newer revision;
  3. command discovery filters by capabilities and applicability;
  4. knowledge tree loads only expanded children;
  5. pagination adds children without losing stable node state;
  6. navigation back/forward preserves snapshot context;
  7. migration review exposes stale/conflict state without mutating canonical model;
  8. extension registration cannot overwrite an existing extension silently unless explicitly allowed.

Use fake model/client objects.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the language-independent source-code vocabulary described by design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md in scriberig-domain-code.

This crate defines broad concepts that are genuinely shared across programming languages. It must not pretend that all languages have the same AST and must not absorb Rust-specific syntax.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md
  2. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  3. design/level-3/001. scaffold domain adapter crates.md
  4. current public APIs of scriberig-core, scriberig-schema, scriberig-graph, and scriberig-migration

If required shared schema APIs are not yet available, stop and report the prerequisite rather than implementing a private substitute.

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Inside crates/domains/code/, create or update:

src/lib.rs
src/schema.rs
src/types.rs
src/comment.rs
src/code_group.rs
src/classification.rs

Add tests under:

tests/schema.rs
tests/code_groups.rs

Do not add a parser in this crate. Language-specific adapters own parsing.

docs.title: Shared Code Vocabulary
docs.text:
Define broad entity concepts for:

CodeProject
Module
Type
Function
Parameter
CodeGroup
Statement
Expression
Comment
Symbol
Reference

These types exist only to support operations and navigation that genuinely overlap across languages.

Do not define Rust-specific constructs such as:

match arm
Rust pattern kinds
attribute syntax
macro invocation details
token trees
trait-specific syntax

Those belong to the Rust specialization.

docs.title: Core Structural Relations
docs.text:
Make the schema capable of representing at least:

CodeProject --contains--> Module
Module --contains--> Type/Function/other declarations
Function --parameters--> Parameter
Function --code_groups--> CodeGroup
CodeGroup --contains--> Statement
Statement/Expression --contains--> language-specific syntax children where specialized schemas allow it
Comment --attached_to--> semantic code entity
Reference --targets--> Symbol or semantic entity

Where order is meaningful, collections must preserve order.

Do not store reverse parents as canonical child properties solely for navigation.

docs.title: Canonical and Derived Boundaries
docs.text:
The shared code domain must distinguish broad canonical source structure from derived compiler analysis.

Canonical-capable concepts include:

author-chosen declarations
parameters
statement/expression structure
comments intentionally preserved
meaningful ordering
code groups when they reflect intentionally preserved source grouping

Derived concepts include by default:

resolved symbol targets
inferred types
call graph
control-flow graph
data-flow graph
compiler diagnostics
lint diagnostics
model-generated code-group descriptions

Do not mark compiler or model output canonical merely because it is stored in the same graph.

docs.title: Comment Model
docs.text:
Comments must be first-class where the language adapter preserves them.

Support a shared classification vocabulary at least broad enough for:

ordinary
documentation
explanation
invariant
safety
todo
directive
generated

Language adapters may extend or refine this classification.

A source-authored comment and a generated description must remain distinguishable.

docs.title: Code Groups
docs.text:
Define CodeGroup as an explicit semantic navigation layer between a function and its statements.

A code group must be able to carry or reference:

ordered statement membership
optional source-authored leading comment or grouping evidence
optional derived description/purpose
provenance/classification indicating which parts are canonical vs inferred

The shared domain must not require every function to have generated descriptions.

A function should remain inspectable even when code-group descriptions have not been produced.

docs.title: Progressive Disclosure
docs.text:
The schema must support this navigation shape:

Project
  -> Module
     -> Function/Type
        -> CodeGroup
           -> Statement
              -> Expression

The model must allow consumers to inspect counts, identifiers, names/signatures where available, and descriptions before loading fine-grained syntax.

Do not flatten a function body into one opaque text property.

docs.title: Semantic Handles
docs.text:
Every important code entity should be referenceable through normal universal entity handles.

The code domain must not use these as primary identity:

file path + line number
byte range
parser node pointer
compiler-internal transient ID

External coordinates may be attached as projection/adapter metadata.

docs.title: Public API
docs.text:
Expose the minimum stable domain API needed for:

register/obtain the code schema
refer to shared code type/relation identifiers
classify shared comment kinds
construct or inspect CodeGroup metadata through universal graph primitives

Do not invent a second graph API.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests proving:

  • every required shared code type is registered;
  • ordered parameters, groups, and statements are representable;
  • comments are separate semantic entities;
  • generated descriptions remain derived;
  • language-specific extension points can add specialized entity/relation types without modifying the shared store;
  • obvious invalid relation endpoints are rejected if supported by the shared schema layer;
  • no file coordinate is required for code identity.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-domain-code
cargo clippy -p scriberig-domain-code --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not create a universal AST for every language.
  • Do not add Rust syntax here.
  • Do not choose a parser.
  • Do not implement compiler analysis.
  • Do not create source-file persistence tables.
  • Do not make generated descriptions canonical.
  • Do not depend on agent crates.
  • Do not store code only as raw source text.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Shared code vocabulary is implemented through the universal schema system.
  • [x] Language-specific extension remains possible.
  • [x] Code groups and comments are first-class semantic concepts.
  • [x] Canonical vs derived boundaries are explicit.
  • [x] Progressive disclosure is structurally supported.
  • [x] No parser or language-specific syntax leaked into this crate.
  • [x] No alternate persistence architecture exists.
  • [x] Tests, formatting, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Mission
docs.text:
Implement mutable named roots that point to immutable SnapshotId values.

Named roots provide familiar moving names such as main while preserving the rule that snapshots themselves never change.

This task adds the only mutable coordination primitive required by the initial identity subsystem.

docs.title: Read Before Editing
docs.text:
Read completely:

design/level-1/003. identity revisions and snapshots.md
design/level-2/001. identity revision snapshot implementation.md
design/level-3/004. implement persistent snapshots and diffs.md

Assume Level 3 tasks 001 through 004 are complete.

docs.title: Files You Own
docs.text:
Create or modify:

crates/sr-store/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-store/src/roots.rs
crates/sr-store/tests/roots.rs

Do not change the snapshot hashing or revision hashing rules in this task.

docs.title: Root Name
docs.text:
Define a small validated root-name type or an equivalent checked string wrapper.

Requirements:

  • [x] non-empty;
  • [x] deterministic textual representation;
  • [x] no hidden normalization;
  • [x] suitable for names such as main, active-workspace, and current-project;
  • [x] validation failure uses a typed error.

Keep validation conservative and simple. Do not invent a complex path hierarchy in this task.

docs.title: Root Store Contract
docs.text:
Define a backend-independent public trait with behavior equivalent to:

get(name) -> Option<SnapshotId>
set(name, snapshot) -> Result<...>
compare_and_swap(name, expected, new) -> Result<CasOutcome, ...>

The exact signatures may return owned values or references as appropriate, but callers must not receive mutable access to internal storage.

docs.title: get
docs.text: Returns the exact snapshot currently referenced by the name, or None if the root does not exist.

docs.title: set
docs.text:
Unconditionally points the name at the supplied immutable snapshot ID.

This changes only the mutable root pointer. It does not change either snapshot.

docs.title: compare_and_swap
docs.text:
This is the concurrency-sensitive operation.

It succeeds only when the currently stored value equals expected.

Support both cases if practical:

expected = Some(snapshot)   # update an existing root only if still at this snapshot
expected = None             # create only if the root is currently absent

Return an explicit outcome containing enough information for a caller to distinguish success from stale expectation.

Do not silently retry inside the store.

docs.title: In-Memory Implementation
docs.text:
Create MemoryRootStore backed by an RwLock-protected map or an equivalent standard synchronization primitive.

The compare-and-swap check and update must happen while holding one exclusive critical section so another writer cannot change the root between them.

Do not expose the lock through the trait.

docs.title: Required Tests
docs.text:
In crates/sr-store/tests/roots.rs, test at least:

  • [x] missing root returns None;
  • [x] set creates a root;
  • [x] set can move a root from S1 to S2;
  • [x] moving a root does not change S1 or S2;
  • [x] CAS succeeds when expected value matches;
  • [x] CAS fails when expected value is stale;
  • [x] failed CAS leaves the current root unchanged;
  • [x] CAS with expected = None can create a missing root;
  • [x] CAS with expected = None fails when root already exists;
  • [x] two independent root names may point to the same snapshot;
  • [x] one root moving does not affect another root.

Add one concurrency test using two threads if it can be written deterministically enough to avoid flaky timing assumptions. Prefer barriers/channels over sleeps.

The test should demonstrate that only one writer can successfully advance a root when both use the same old expected snapshot.

docs.title: Error and Outcome Types
docs.text:
Keep storage failures distinct from compare-and-swap conflicts.

A stale expectation is not an exceptional storage failure; it is a normal concurrency outcome.

A caller must be able to inspect the actual current snapshot after a failed CAS, either in the outcome or with a subsequent get.

docs.title: Public API Rule
docs.text:
Named roots are mutable aliases.

They must never be accepted where an exact SnapshotId is required without first resolving the name.

Do not create an API such as:

SnapshotId::from_root_name(...)

A name and a snapshot ID are fundamentally different concepts.

cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
• Do not mutate a Snapshot when moving a root.
  • Do not put root names into snapshot hashes.
  • Do not turn root names into snapshot identities.
  • Do not silently overwrite after a failed compare-and-swap.
  • Do not add SQLite or network coordination yet.
  • Do not add retry loops that hide conflicts from higher layers.
