docs.text:
• [x] Root-name validation exists.
  • [x] Backend-independent root-store trait exists.
  • [x] In-memory implementation exists.
  • [x] Compare-and-swap is atomic within the in-memory store.
  • [x] Stale CAS is an explicit normal outcome.
  • [x] Roots point to snapshots without mutating them.
  • [x] Tests, formatting, and clippy all pass.

docs.title: Implement: Reachability, Garbage Collection, and Integrity
Objective
docs.text:
Implement storage maintenance features required by the Level 1 persistence model without changing canonical semantics.

This task adds backend-neutral reachability and integrity reporting plus SQLite garbage-collection support.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/004. persistence and storage model.md
  2. design/level-2/005. indexes reachability gc and integrity.md
  3. Level 3 tasks 001 through 004.

docs.title: Files to create or update
docs.text:
In sr-store:

crates/sr-store/src/
├── reachability.rs
└── integrity.rs

In sr-store-sqlite:

crates/sr-store-sqlite/src/
├── indexes.rs
├── reachability.rs
├── gc.rs
└── integrity.rs

Update lib.rs exports only as needed.

Add corresponding support to sr-store-memory if required by shared public traits/tests.

docs.title: Reachability API
docs.text:
Define backend-neutral types for:

  • protected roots;
  • reachable canonical object enumeration;
  • unreachable candidate reporting.

Reachability must begin from an explicit stable set of protected roots/snapshots.

Traversal must retain every immutable storage object required to read a protected snapshot completely, including snapshot-map structure, revisions, and persistent collection/storage nodes.

Do not automatically retain rebuildable caches merely because they mention a protected object.

docs.title: Integrity report
docs.text:
Define a structured IntegrityReport or equivalent with machine-readable issues.

At minimum detect/report:

  • revision ID does not match stored canonical content;
  • referenced persistent node missing;
  • invalid snapshot-map structure;
  • named root points to missing/invalid snapshot;
  • protected snapshot cannot be read completely;
  • persistent collection invariant violation;
  • derived/backend index points to missing authoritative data;
  • unreachable but otherwise valid immutable object.

Keep unreachable separate from corrupt.

docs.title: Index rebuild
docs.text:
Implement rebuilding of any backend-derived indexes introduced so far.

A rebuild must derive results from authoritative persisted data and must not modify canonical revision bytes or snapshot meaning.

docs.title: Garbage collection
docs.text:
Implement conservative mark-and-sweep for SQLite.

Required API behavior:

gc_dry_run(protected_roots) -> report
gc_sweep(protected_roots) -> report

Rules:

  • capture a stable protected-root set before marking;
  • dry run deletes nothing;
  • sweep deletes only objects proven unreachable under the captured root set and retention policy supported so far;
  • sweep must not make any protected snapshot unreadable;
  • when uncertain, retain rather than delete.

The first implementation does not need concurrent online GC. It may require exclusive/serialized maintenance access if documented internally.

docs.title: Integrity repair policy
docs.text:
Safe automatic repair is limited to rebuildable derived indexes.

Do not silently rewrite or synthesize canonical revisions to repair corruption.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Create tests for:

  • reachability from one root marks all required canonical storage;
  • two protected roots preserve the union of their reachable state;
  • abandoned branch becomes a GC candidate only after no protected root reaches it;
  • dry run reports candidates and deletes nothing;
  • sweep removes an unreachable candidate;
  • sweep preserves all data required by protected snapshots;
  • altered stored canonical revision bytes are reported as corruption;
  • missing snapshot-map node is corruption;
  • unreachable valid record is not categorized as corrupt;
  • derived index can be deleted and rebuilt without changing canonical IDs.

After destructive GC tests, run integrity verification against every protected snapshot.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not add retention policy UI or CLI.
  • Do not implement distributed GC.
  • Do not compact or rewrite canonical identities.
  • Do not automatically repair canonical corruption.
  • Do not make GC dependent on an agent runtime.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Reachability API exists.
  • [x] Structured integrity report exists.
  • [x] SQLite dry-run GC works.
  • [x] SQLite sweep preserves protected snapshots.
  • [x] Derived index rebuild works (the current schema has no derived indexes; the backend maintenance boundary is explicit and a no-op).
  • [x] Corruption and unreachability are distinguished.
  • [x] Memory and SQLite behavior remain consistent where public APIs overlap.
  • [x] Workspace tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Agent Task: Implement Universal Semantic Diff
Goal
docs.text:
Implement backend-independent comparison of two exact snapshots.

A diff answers what differs between states. It must work whether the snapshots are directly related, distant ancestors, siblings, or historically unrelated but available in the same store.

Do not implement merge resolution in this task.

docs.title: Read before editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md, especially sections 10 through 13, 21, 23, 24, 29, 30, 42, 43, 44, and 48.
  2. design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md.
  3. Existing sr-store snapshot enumeration/diff capabilities.

docs.title: Files to modify
docs.text:
crates/sr-change/src/diff.rs
crates/sr-change/src/summary.rs
crates/sr-change/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs

Extend sr-store only if a generic efficient snapshot-mapping comparison capability is missing and cannot be implemented correctly through the existing public API.

docs.title: Universal diff result
docs.text:
Implement a result containing, at minimum:

left SnapshotId
right SnapshotId
entity deltas

Reuse the universal EntityDelta model rather than defining another incompatible changed-entity type.

The diff must classify:

introduced entities
removed entities
modified entities

Do not include unchanged entities in the main result.

docs.title: No ancestry requirement
docs.text:
The API must accept arbitrary snapshots.

Do not require one snapshot to be an ancestor of the other.

Add tests for:

S1 -> S2 -> S3: diff(S1, S3)

       S1
      /  \
    S2    S3: diff(S2, S3)

docs.title: Snapshot-level optimization
docs.text:
If left == right, return an empty diff immediately.

If storage provides a persistent-map structural diff, use it through the backend-independent interface.

Correctness must not depend on a specific Merkle/trie implementation.

docs.title: Relation and collection details
docs.text:
If generic relation/collection state is available through universal graph/storage APIs, define optional detail structures for:

relation added/removed
collection member inserted/removed
collection order changed

These details must be subordinate to the authoritative revision/entity delta.

Do not parse domain-specific payloads in the generic diff engine.

docs.title: Domain enrichment interface
docs.text:
Expose a narrow extension point that allows a domain crate to turn a universal diff into richer meaning.

The generic crate must remain useful without any domain adapter installed.

The extension point should receive exact entity/revision references and return additional interpretation without mutating the universal diff.

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text:
Diff output must have deterministic ordering independent of backend iteration order.

Choose and document a stable ordering for entity deltas using canonical identifier ordering.

Do not use timestamps or insertion sequence for ordering.

docs.title: Summary support
docs.text:
Implement a compact deterministic summary containing at least:

introduced count
removed count
modified count
total changed entities

This summary should be obtainable without rendering textual source or opening domain-specific details.

docs.title: Large diffs
docs.text:
Design the API so it can later support pagination/streaming without changing semantic meaning.

Do not prematurely implement a complex streaming framework unless the storage API already supports one. Avoid forcing all higher layers to rely on a giant formatted string.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  • identical snapshots produce empty diff;
  • one modified entity;
  • one introduced entity;
  • one removed entity;
  • multiple changes sorted deterministically;
  • ancestor-to-descendant comparison;
  • sibling comparison;
  • same final revision reached through different histories still compares as state, not history;
  • unrelated unchanged entities are absent from result;
  • summary counts exactly match deltas;
  • generic diff requires no domain adapter.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Diff is not migration.
  • Diff is not textual file diff.
  • Do not infer historical intent.
  • Do not declare conflicts; merge owns that.
  • Do not mark all entities changed because SnapshotId differs.
  • No concrete backend dependency.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-change
cargo check --workspace

Run shared store conformance tests if the storage API changed.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Arbitrary snapshots can be compared.
  • [x] Entity changes use EntityDelta.
  • [x] No unchanged entities are emitted.
  • [x] Result ordering is deterministic.
  • [x] Compact summary exists.
  • [x] Sibling snapshot tests pass.
  • [x] Domain enrichment is optional and dependency-safe.

docs.title: Final response from implementing agent
docs.text: Report the diff API, any storage capability added, deterministic ordering rule, performance shortcut used for equal snapshots, and tests added.

docs.title: Persist Projection Conflicts and Captured Evidence
Objective
docs.text: Preserve ambiguous or failed projection reconciliation as structured knowledge so an external edit is never reduced to a transient watcher event or silently guessed into canonical history.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
1. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md, especially sections 20–23, 44–45, 51 and 60.
  2. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md.
  3. Existing projection/reconciliation Level 2 and Level 3 designs.
  4. Existing provenance/core task.

If projection state, captured projection bytes/text, or candidate reconciliation does not exist yet, stop and report the prerequisite.

docs.title: Expected Area
docs.text:
Work primarily in the projection layer and its schema/graph integration. Typical modules:

crates/scriberig-projection/src/conflict.rs
crates/scriberig-projection/src/reconcile.rs
crates/scriberig-projection/src/lib.rs

Use existing graph/schema facilities for persistence. Do not create an unrelated logging database.

docs.title: Captured Observation
docs.text:
When a managed projection changes externally, capture an immutable observation before attempting destructive normalization. It must retain enough data to identify:

projection identity
previous rendered projection/revision
observed external content or blob reference
observation metadata/time if supported
current semantic snapshot
parser/adapter identity and version

The original observation must remain distinguishable from any parsed candidate.

docs.title: Conflict Object
docs.text:
Define a structured conflict capable of representing at least:

base projection/reference
current canonical snapshot
observed external evidence
candidate parse/revision if one exists
ambiguous mappings
conflicting entities/relations
conflict kind
status

Support unresolved and resolved states through immutable history/operations rather than by erasing the original conflict.

docs.title: Reconciliation Behavior
docs.text:
When matching is confident, normal reconciliation may continue.

When matching is ambiguous, the reconciler must return/persist an explicit conflict or candidate alternatives. It must not choose an uncertain lineage silently.

The canonical root remains unchanged until a later resolution produces a normal migration that passes the standard validation/promotion path.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
Provide an application-facing resolution input that references the exact conflict and selected interpretation. The result should produce a normal migration/candidate plus provenance linking back to the conflict and captured observation.

Do not make conflict resolution a privileged direct storage mutation.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Create fixtures for:

  1. clean external edit -> no conflict;
  2. ambiguous paragraph merge/split -> conflict persisted;
  3. conflicting concurrent canonical change -> conflict references both states;
  4. original observed content remains accessible after parse failure;
  5. parser output is distinguishable from original evidence;
  6. unresolved conflict does not change canonical root;
  7. resolution creates migration provenance back to conflict;
  8. resolving stale conflict against changed canonical state requires re-evaluation;
  9. conflict history preserves the original competing states.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run workspace formatting, check, tests, and lint. Use deterministic small projection fixtures.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not insert textual conflict markers into canonical semantic objects as the primary conflict representation. Do not discard the external observation after parsing. Do not auto-promote a parser's best guess when the matcher reports ambiguity.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] external observations are immutable evidence;
  • [x] ambiguity becomes a first-class conflict;
  • [x] canonical state is unchanged by unresolved conflicts;
  • [x] conflict resolution creates a normal migration/candidate;
  • [x] provenance reaches back to original observation;
  • [x] tests cover ambiguity and concurrent changes.

docs.title: Implement External Effect Receipts and Reconciliation
Objective
docs.text:
Create the application-level record and state machine for side-effecting external operations so retries, failures, and local/external disagreement remain explicit.

This task provides reusable external-effect semantics. It does not implement any specific GitHub, email, cloud, or messaging connector.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
1. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md, especially sections 27–30 and 61.
  2. design/level-3/001. implement principal and capability model.md.
  3. Existing application operation/event designs.
  4. Existing session/tool invocation designs if they are already implemented.

If application operations and capability checks are not implemented, stop and report the prerequisite.

docs.title: Expected Area
docs.text:
Typical modules:

crates/scriberig-app/src/external_effect.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/lib.rs

Protocol exposure is handled by a later task. Connector-specific code must remain outside this module.

docs.title: External Effect Intent
docs.text:
Represent an immutable intent containing at least:

principal
operation kind
external destination identifier
request fingerprint or idempotency key when available
input semantic snapshot/revisions
capability reference/context
created operation id

Do not store reusable credentials in the semantic object.

docs.title: State Model
docs.text:
Represent explicit states equivalent to:

Requested
Attempted
ConfirmedExternally
ReflectedLocally
Failed
Unknown

A local exception after sending a remote request must not be reported as definitely failed when the external outcome is unknown.

State transitions must preserve history/provenance. Do not overwrite a single mutable status without retaining the operation chain.

docs.title: Receipt
docs.text:
Provide a durable receipt/result representation capable of storing non-secret evidence such as:

external operation id
remote resource reference
response/status metadata
confirmation observation
time if supported by existing history model
request fingerprint/idempotency key

Keep raw secrets and credential material out of receipts.

docs.title: Execution Boundary
docs.text:
The application operation must verify InvokeExternal authority for the exact destination before calling connector code.

A local ModifyBranch or Promote capability must not imply external invocation authority.

Run all applicable local validation and approval checks before irreversible invocation where the operation permits it.

docs.title: Retry Semantics
docs.text:
Expose enough state for connector adapters to make safe retry decisions:

  • confirmed success: do not resend blindly;
  • definite failure before remote acceptance: retry may be safe according to connector policy;
  • unknown outcome: require reconciliation/lookup when supported;
  • idempotency key available: reuse it for the same semantic intent.

Do not pretend all external systems are transactional or idempotent.

docs.title: Reconciliation
docs.text: Provide an operation to record a later external observation and reconcile it with the pending intent. The result must state whether the effect is confirmed externally and whether local semantic state reflects that confirmation.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Use a fake connector and test:

  1. external invocation without destination capability is denied;
  2. local write capability alone cannot invoke remote effect;
  3. confirmed success records a receipt;
  4. timeout after send becomes Unknown, not definite failure;
  5. unknown outcome can be reconciled by later observation;
  6. repeated confirmed operation is not blindly resent;
  7. idempotency key is stable for retry of the same intent where configured;
  8. credentials are absent from persisted intent/receipt fixtures;
  9. external success plus local persistence failure remains recoverable/inspectable;
  10. all transitions retain operation provenance.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run workspace formatting, check, tests, and lint. No live external service is required.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not implement a generic secret vault. Do not add a universal network client. Do not claim local database transactions make remote services atomic. Do not log credential values for debugging.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] external authority is destination-specific;
  • [x] intent and receipt are durable structured objects;
  • [x] unknown outcome is representable;
  • [x] retry behavior can use idempotency/reconciliation;
  • [x] local and external state remain distinguishable;
  • [x] no connector-specific policy leaks into the universal model.

docs.title: Implement: Observability and Shared Store Conformance
Objective
docs.text:
Create one backend-neutral conformance suite and one backend-neutral observability/error model, then run the same behavior tests against the in-memory and SQLite backends.

This task proves that higher layers can depend on sr-store rather than on a particular backend.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/004. persistence and storage model.md
  2. design/level-2/006. persistence observability and conformance.md
  3. All earlier Level 3 persistence tasks.

docs.title: Files to create or update
docs.text:
In sr-store:

crates/sr-store/src/
├── error.rs
├── stats.rs
└── conformance.rs

Add or update:

crates/sr-store/tests/conformance.rs

Backend crates may add small test adapters, but expected behavior must live in shared conformance logic rather than duplicated test bodies.

docs.title: Error model
docs.text:
Ensure storage errors have machine-readable categories for at least:

  • not found;
  • invalid identifier or encoding;
  • unsupported encoding/storage version;
  • stale named-root compare-and-set;
  • integrity failure;
  • invalid operation;
  • backend transaction/I/O failure.

Backend-specific errors may be retained as sources, but callers must not need to parse backend-specific strings to determine category.

docs.title: Observability types
docs.text:
Implement backend-neutral data types equivalent to:

StoreStats
RootStatus
IntegrityReport
GcReport
IndexStatus

Do not require every backend to provide every numeric statistic. Use optional values when a metric cannot be determined cheaply or meaningfully.

At minimum, expose where possible:

  • revision count;
  • snapshot count;
  • named-root count;
  • reachable/unreachable counts after reachability analysis;
  • backend storage byte count if meaningful;
  • integrity issue counts;
  • GC candidate/deleted counts.

Observability values must not participate in canonical revision or snapshot identity.

docs.title: Shared conformance harness
docs.text:
Build reusable test functions that accept a backend factory or test-store instance implementing the public storage traits.

The suite must verify at least:

  1. put/get immutable revision;
  2. duplicate revision insertion is idempotent;
  3. create/read snapshot;
  4. historical base snapshot remains readable after descendant creation;
  5. branch two snapshots from one base;
  6. deterministic snapshot identity for equivalent maps;
  7. named-root compare-and-set success;
  8. stale compare-and-set conflict and unchanged root;
  9. reopen/durability test when backend declares durable capability;
  10. reachability from protected roots;
  11. integrity verification of healthy data.

Use backend capabilities to skip only behavior that is genuinely inapplicable, such as reopening an in-memory-only store. Core semantic behavior must not be skipped.

docs.title: Cross-backend fixtures
docs.text:
Create deterministic fixture histories such as:

S1: A -> R1, B -> R1
S2: A -> R2, B -> R1
S3: A -> R1, B -> R2

Run the same fixture against memory and SQLite.

Assert that logical RevisionId and SnapshotId values are identical across backends for the same canonical content and complete mapping.

This test is critical: a backend must not influence semantic identity.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• memory backend passes shared suite;
  • SQLite in-memory database passes shared suite;
  • SQLite temporary file database passes durable parts of suite;
  • fixture IDs match across memory and SQLite;
  • error categories match for equivalent failures;
  • observability calls do not change snapshots or roots.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace

Run any stricter lint command already established by the repository. Do not introduce a new CI system in this task.

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not add HTTP/CLI observability surfaces.
  • Do not add Prometheus or telemetry dependencies yet.
  • Do not let conformance tests import SQLite internals.
  • Do not loosen semantics merely to make both backends pass.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Shared conformance suite exists.
  • [x] Memory backend passes it.
  • [x] SQLite backend passes it.
  • [x] Cross-backend logical IDs match.
  • [x] Error categories are backend-neutral.
  • [x] Observability models are backend-neutral.
  • [x] Statistics do not affect canonical identity.
  • [x] Entire workspace tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement @scriberig/react as a thin React integration over @scriberig/client, @scriberig/model, and @scriberig/editor-core.

The package must expose providers and hooks that subscribe React components to reusable model/controller state without moving semantic logic into hooks.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
  2. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md
  3. design/level-3/004. implement client semantic model and incremental events.md
  4. design/level-3/005. implement headless editor core primitives.md

Prerequisite: model and editor-core packages compile and provide framework-independent subscription interfaces.

docs.title: Files to Create or Replace
docs.text:
Create:

web/packages/react/src/provider.tsx
web/packages/react/src/use-object.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-children.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-snapshot.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-operation.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-session.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-selection.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-commands.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-knowledge-tree.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-migration-review.ts
web/packages/react/test/provider.test.tsx
web/packages/react/test/hooks.test.tsx

Update:

web/packages/react/src/index.ts
web/packages/react/package.json

docs.title: Provider
docs.text:
Create a public React provider that supplies the reusable runtime objects needed by hooks.

The provider should accept already-created objects rather than constructing hidden global singletons.

Expected dependencies include equivalents of:

ScriberigClient
WorkspaceModel
SelectionController
CommandRegistry/ExtensionRegistry as required

The provider must support tests with fake objects.

Do not couple provider creation to one server URL or authentication mechanism.

docs.title: Subscription Strategy
docs.text:
Hooks must subscribe to reusable model/controller state using React-compatible external-store subscription patterns.

Prefer useSyncExternalStore or an equivalent correct React mechanism for framework-external stores.

Do not duplicate model state into per-component React state merely to trigger renders.

Do not introduce Redux or another React state framework.

docs.title: Object Hook
docs.text:
use-object.ts should expose the state needed to inspect a semantic object/reference.

It should distinguish where possible:

not requested/loading
loaded
not found/error
stale relative to current snapshot
historical exact state

Loading must go through WorkspaceModel/client APIs.

Do not silently replace an exact historical revision with a current revision.

docs.title: Children Hook
docs.text:
use-children.ts should bind relation/collection loading to React.

Support:

  • initial page load;
  • loading state;
  • error state;
  • loaded children;
  • child counts when known;
  • load-more/cursor behavior;
  • snapshot-aware cache reuse.

Do not recursively load descendants.

docs.title: Snapshot Hook
docs.text:
use-snapshot.ts should expose at least:

  • current canonical snapshot known by the model;
  • viewed snapshot when supplied by context/controller;
  • whether the view is current, historical, candidate, or stale.

Do not reduce snapshot awareness to a boolean if the model exposes richer state.

docs.title: Operation Hook
docs.text:
use-operation.ts observes one long-running operation by OperationId.

Expose lifecycle, progress, result references, error information, and cancellation capability when available.

Do not tie an operation to the lifecycle of the initiating component.

Unmounting a view must not implicitly cancel a server operation.

docs.title: Session Hook
docs.text:
use-session.ts exposes loaded session/branch semantic summaries and loading operations.

It must not reinterpret sessions as only chat message arrays.

Preserve branch IDs, descriptions, outcomes, decisions, tasks, and migration/result references exposed by protocol/model.

docs.title: Selection Hook
docs.text:
use-selection.ts binds the shared SelectionController to React.

Expose:

selection
setSelection
clearSelection

plus any small helper required to update relation/projection context.

All editor views must be able to share the same controller instance.

docs.title: Commands Hook
docs.text:
use-commands.ts returns command descriptors applicable to the current or supplied selection/capability context.

It must use editor-core command discovery.

Do not hard-code command lists in the hook.

Execution should invoke the operation descriptor/client path defined by editor-core.

docs.title: Knowledge Tree Hook
docs.text:
Wrap the headless knowledge tree controller for React consumption.

Expose rows/nodes and actions such as:

expand
collapse
select
loadMore
refresh

Do not implement tree markup in this package.

docs.title: Migration Review Hook
docs.text:
Bind the headless migration review controller to React.

Expose selected change, affected objects, validation/stale/conflict state, and public apply/reject actions.

Do not perform direct state mutation outside controller/client APIs.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Use React Testing Library or hook test utilities compatible with the workspace.

Required cases:

  1. provider can use fake client/model/controller objects;
  2. one model subscription updates multiple consumers consistently;
  3. selection changed by one consumer is observed by another;
  4. historical snapshot state remains exact after current snapshot advances;
  5. operation hook survives initiating component removal when observed elsewhere;
  6. commands update when capabilities or selection change;
  7. no hook requires MUI context.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

pnpm --filter @scriberig/react typecheck
pnpm --filter @scriberig/react test
pnpm --filter @scriberig/react build
pnpm typecheck

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not add MUI.
  • Do not create visual components.
  • Do not hard-code app routes.
  • Do not create a global singleton client/model.
  • Do not duplicate cache logic from @scriberig/model.
  • Do not duplicate selection/tree/command state machines from @scriberig/editor-core.
  • Do not treat sessions as only message arrays.
  • Do not cancel server operations automatically on component unmount.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] A configurable public provider exists.
  • [x] Hooks subscribe to external model/controller state correctly.
  • [x] Object/children/snapshot/operation/session hooks exist.
  • [x] Selection and commands use shared editor-core controllers.
  • [x] Knowledge tree and migration review have headless React bindings.
  • [x] No MUI dependency exists.
  • [x] Tests demonstrate shared selection and snapshot correctness.
  • [x] Package and workspace checks pass.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the Rust-specific source syntax specialization and adapter in scriberig-domain-rust on top of scriberig-domain-code.

This task represents Rust source syntax faithfully enough for semantic inspection, editing, and later projection reconciliation. It does not implement compiler-derived analysis; that is a separate task.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  2. design/level-3/005. implement language independent code domain.md
  3. current public APIs of scriberig-schema, scriberig-graph, scriberig-migration, and scriberig-projection

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Inside crates/domains/rust/, create or update:

src/lib.rs
src/schema.rs
src/syntax.rs
src/parse.rs
src/render.rs
src/mapping.rs
src/comments.rs
src/code_groups.rs
src/error.rs

Add tests under:

tests/parse_render.rs
tests/schema.rs
tests/comments_and_groups.rs

Do not create compiler-analysis modules in this task.

docs.title: Parser Dependency
docs.text:
Choose one mature Rust parser that preserves source-level syntax needed for round-trip semantics, including attributes, patterns, macros/token trees, comments or source ranges sufficient to recover comments, and nested expressions/statements.

Prefer an already-selected workspace dependency if one exists. Do not introduce multiple competing Rust syntax parsers.

Parser-specific types must remain private to the adapter.

docs.title: Rust Schema Specialization
docs.text:
Extend the language-independent code domain with Rust-specific constructs needed for the supported syntax slice.

At minimum represent:

functions
parameters
patterns
type syntax
let statements
expression statements
path expressions
call/method-call expressions
binary/unary expressions
blocks
if expressions
match expressions and arms
return/break/continue where relevant
structs/enums where needed for module inspection
impl blocks
attributes
macro invocations
token trees or equivalent concrete syntax for macros
comments

Use language-independent Module, Function, Parameter, CodeGroup, Statement, Expression, and Comment concepts where appropriate, and Rust-specific types where semantics differ.

Do not normalize Rust into a generic compiler IR.

docs.title: Canonical Syntax Rules
docs.text:
Canonical state must preserve author-chosen syntax that matters to source-level meaning or faithful reconstruction.

Preserve at least:

  • declaration structure and order;
  • parameter patterns and type syntax;
  • statement/expression structure;
  • attributes;
  • macro invocation syntax and token trees where normalization would lose information;
  • source-authored comments that can be reliably attached;
  • meaningful grouping and ordering.

Do not make ordinary indentation, line wrapping, or spacing semantic identity.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
Recover comments from source and represent them through the shared code-domain comment model.

Attach comments to the nearest domain object only when the attachment is deterministic enough to preserve author intent.

When attachment is ambiguous, preserve source-location metadata and avoid inventing a false semantic attachment.

Distinguish source-authored comments from future generated descriptions.

docs.title: Code Groups
docs.text:
Create initial deterministic code groups from source evidence only.

Use signals such as:

blank-line boundaries
leading explanatory comments
explicit block boundaries
statement sequence

Do not call a model to name groups.

A group may have no human-readable purpose description yet. Preserve the group boundary/provenance separately from any later derived summary.

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
Implement deterministic source rendering for the supported canonical syntax.

The renderer may use an existing pretty-print/formatting library if compatible with the projection architecture, but must render from Scriberig semantic state rather than retaining the original source file as the authoritative representation.

Macros/token structures that cannot be safely normalized must round-trip without semantic loss.

Do not silently replace unsupported constructs with placeholders.

docs.title: Source Coordinates
docs.text:
Parser source spans, filenames, line numbers, and byte positions are adapter/projection metadata.

They may support diagnostics, external editing, and UI highlighting, but they must not be the primary semantic identities of functions, statements, expressions, or comments.

docs.title: Adapter API
docs.text:
Expose syntax-domain operations through existing domain/projection abstractions where available:

parse/import Rust source -> candidate semantic objects
render Rust semantic scope -> source text

Do not expose parser AST types publicly.

Do not write directly to persistence from parse/render operations.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Include fixtures covering at least:

simple functions
patterns and typed parameters
nested expressions
if/match
attributes
impl blocks
macros
comments
blank-line/comment code grouping

Test:

  • parse produces expected semantic structure;
  • shared code-domain concepts are reused;
  • Rust-specific syntax remains specialized;
  • comments are preserved without becoming parser trivia;
  • macro/token syntax survives round trip;
  • parse -> render -> parse preserves equivalent canonical syntax for supported fixtures;
  • formatting-only differences do not change canonical semantics;
  • no semantic identity depends on line numbers.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-domain-rust
cargo clippy -p scriberig-domain-rust --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not implement symbol resolution or type inference.
  • Do not implement call/CFG/data-flow graphs.
  • Do not use rustc IR as canonical storage.
  • Do not flatten macros into expanded compiler syntax as the only representation.
  • Do not add agent dependencies.
  • Do not create Rust-specific persistence tables.
  • Do not make formatting whitespace canonical.
  • Do not silently discard unsupported syntax.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Rust-specific schema extends the shared code domain.
  • [x] Source syntax is represented semantically rather than as one text blob.
  • [x] Comments are preserved as first-class knowledge where deterministic.
  • [x] Initial code groups come from source evidence only.
  • [x] Macros/token trees preserve author syntax.
  • [x] Rendering is deterministic for supported syntax.
  • [x] Parser implementation details remain private.
  • [x] No compiler-derived analysis is mixed into canonical syntax.
  • [x] Tests, formatting, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Agent Task: Implement Three-Way Merge and Structured Conflicts
Goal
docs.text:
Implement the universal three-way merge engine and structured conflict model for sr-change.

This task consumes exact snapshots and universal diffs. It must merge independent changes automatically and preserve ambiguity as semantic conflicts.

docs.title: Read before editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md, especially sections 21 through 30 and 49.
  2. design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md.
  3. Level 3 task 005 implementation of universal semantic diff.
  4. Existing history/common-ancestor APIs.

docs.title: Files to modify
docs.text:
crates/sr-change/src/conflict.rs
crates/sr-change/src/merge.rs
crates/sr-change/src/diff.rs
crates/sr-change/src/history.rs
crates/sr-change/src/summary.rs
crates/sr-change/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs

docs.title: Merge input
docs.text:
Expose a public merge request equivalent in meaning to:

MergeInput {
    base: SnapshotId,
    left: SnapshotId,
    right: SnapshotId,
}

The caller may supply the base explicitly. If a convenience API derives it, use explicit history topology and common-ancestor logic rather than timestamps.

docs.title: Base validation
docs.text:
When the merge API is given an explicit base, verify that it is a valid ancestry base when the operation requires ancestry.

Return a typed error for an invalid base rather than silently substituting another snapshot.

docs.title: Universal merge rules
docs.text:
Apply these rules in order:

  1. Compute base -> left and base -> right diffs.
  2. If an entity changed on only one side, adopt that side.
  3. If both sides resolve an entity to the same exact revision, converge without conflict.
  4. If neither side changes an entity, omit it from the merge change set.
  5. If both sides make different changes to the same entity, attempt deeper generic merge only when the available structure proves it is safe.
  6. If safe resolution is not possible, create a structured conflict.

Do not choose left or right by default.

docs.title: Structured conflict model
docs.text:
Implement a universal conflict type with at least:

entity: EntityId
base: Option<RevisionId>
left: Option<RevisionId>
right: Option<RevisionId>
kind: ConflictKind

Initial ConflictKind values must cover:

BothModified
DeleteModify
CompetingCreate
RelationConflict
CollectionConflict
DomainConflict

Allow optional structured detail for an affected generic field/relation/collection path and optional domain detail.

Do not store textual conflict markers as the canonical conflict.

docs.title: Minimal conflict scope
docs.text:
If only one entity conflicts, preserve all other automatically resolved entity changes in the merge result.

The result should separate:

resolved entity deltas
unresolved conflicts

A conflict must not erase unrelated successful merge work.

docs.title: Merge result
docs.text:
Return a structure equivalent in meaning to:

MergeResult {
    base,
    left,
    right,
    resolved_deltas,
    conflicts,
}

Do not automatically promote the result to a named root.

If creating a provisional result snapshot is supported, it must be a new immutable snapshot and must clearly remain provisional when unresolved conflicts exist.

docs.title: Domain merge strategy
docs.text:
Implement the extension point prescribed by Level 2.

A domain strategy receives exact base/left/right state for one conflicted semantic area and may return either:

Resolved(delta or revision)
Conflict(domain detail)
NotApplicable

Domain strategies must not mutate input snapshots.

The generic merge engine must work with zero registered domain strategies.

docs.title: Generic collection merge
docs.text:
Only implement generic collection resolution where the intent is mechanically unambiguous.

Examples that may be safe:

  • independent insertion at distinct stable positions;
  • identical insertion by both sides;
  • independent changes to different members when identity and order are unambiguous.

If ordering intent is ambiguous, emit CollectionConflict.

Do not implement a large domain-specific list algorithm in this task.

docs.title: Merge provenance
docs.text:
Provide enough output for a later migration record to retain:

merge base
left input
right input
automatically resolved entities
explicit/domain resolutions
unresolved conflicts

Do not require history persistence to be performed inside the pure merge algorithm.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  • left-only change merges;
  • right-only change merges;
  • disjoint changes to two entities merge;
  • both sides produce same revision and converge;
  • different edits to same entity produce BothModified;
  • left delete/right modify produces DeleteModify;
  • competing creation of same semantic entity produces CompetingCreate when revisions differ;
  • one conflict does not discard unrelated resolved changes;
  • domain strategy can resolve one same-entity change;
  • no domain strategy still returns structured conflict;
  • ambiguous collection order produces CollectionConflict;
  • merge does not mutate base/left/right snapshots.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• No textual merge as the canonical algorithm.
  • No left-wins/right-wins fallback.
  • No timestamp-based base selection.
  • No automatic named-root promotion.
  • Domain-specific code must stay outside sr-change.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-change
cargo check --workspace

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Merge is explicitly three-way.
  • [x] Disjoint changes merge automatically.
  • [x] Equal revisions converge.
  • [x] Ambiguity becomes structured conflict.
  • [x] Conflict scope is minimal.
  • [x] Domain strategy extension is optional.
  • [x] Inputs remain immutable.
  • [x] Tests cover delete/modify and competing edits.

docs.title: Final response from implementing agent
docs.text: Report the merge stages, conflict kinds, domain strategy interface, automatic-resolution cases, and tests proving unresolved conflicts preserve unrelated merged work.

docs.title: Mission
docs.text:
Review the completed sr-core and sr-store identity subsystem as one integrated unit, add any missing conformance coverage, and fix only defects that violate the Level 1 or Level 2 identity contracts.

This task is not an opportunity to add new product features. Its purpose is to prove that the implementation created by Level 3 tasks 001 through 005 actually satisfies the architecture before higher layers depend on it.

docs.title: Read Before Editing
docs.text:
Read completely:

design/level-1/003. identity revisions and snapshots.md
design/level-2/001. identity revision snapshot implementation.md
design/level-3/001. bootstrap workspace and identity types.md
design/level-3/002. implement canonical encoding and revision hashing.md
design/level-3/003. implement immutable revision store.md
design/level-3/004. implement persistent snapshots and diffs.md
design/level-3/005. implement named roots and compare and swap.md

Then inspect all source and tests under:

crates/sr-core/
crates/sr-store/

docs.title: Files You May Modify
docs.text:
Prefer adding integration coverage in:

crates/sr-store/tests/identity_conformance.rs

You may fix defects in existing sr-core or sr-store files when a test demonstrates that they violate the design.

Do not redesign APIs merely for style preference.

docs.title: Required End-to-End Scenario
docs.text: Add an integration test that performs this exact logical sequence.

docs.title: Step 1: Create entities
docs.text:
Create stable entities:

F
P1
P2
B

Create canonical revisions:

FR7
PR3
PR8
BR2

Store all revisions.

docs.title: Step 2: Build snapshot S1
docs.text:
Build a snapshot containing:

F  -> FR7
P1 -> PR3
P2 -> PR8
B  -> BR2

Record S1 and its SnapshotId.

docs.title: Step 3: Change only P2
docs.text:
Create a new revision for the same entity P2:

PR9

The EntityId of P2 must stay unchanged.

Create successor snapshot S2 with only:

P2 -> PR9

changed.

docs.title: Step 4: Assert local stability
docs.text:
Verify:

  • [x] F still resolves to FR7 in S2;
  • [x] P1 still resolves to PR3 in S2;
  • [x] B still resolves to BR2 in S2;
  • [x] P2 resolves to PR8 in S1;
  • [x] P2 resolves to PR9 in S2;
  • [x] no semantic parent revision was manufactured merely because P2 changed.

docs.title: Step 5: Assert global certainty
docs.text:
Verify:

  • [x] S1.id() != S2.id();
  • [x] rebuilding S1 in another insertion order produces the same SnapshotId;
  • [x] rebuilding S2 in another insertion order produces the same SnapshotId.

docs.title: Step 6: Assert exact history
docs.text:
Verify that S1 remains readable after S2 exists and still resolves every entity to the original revisions.

No operation may retarget S1.

docs.title: Step 7: Assert semantic snapshot diff
docs.text:
Verify S1.diff(S2) contains exactly one change:

Changed {
  entity: P2,
  from: PR8,
  to: PR9
}

No unchanged entity may appear.

docs.title: Step 8: Assert named-root concurrency semantics
docs.text:
Set:

main -> S1

Advance it with compare-and-swap:

expected S1
new S2

Verify success.

Then try another update still expecting S1.

Verify:

  • [x] it fails as stale;
  • [x] main remains at S2;
  • [x] neither S1 nor S2 changed.

docs.title: Additional Invariant Audit
docs.text: Check the implementation manually and with tests for every item below.

docs.title: Identity separation
docs.text:
• [x] EntityId, RevisionId, and SnapshotId are distinct Rust types.
  • [x] An EntityId is not computed from current content.
  • [x] A RevisionId is content-derived.
  • [x] A SnapshotId is content-derived from global mapping state.

docs.title: Historical exactness
docs.text:
• [x] Revisions have no mutable update method.
  • [x] Snapshots have no mutable update method that changes an existing value in place.
  • [x] Named roots are pointers, not snapshot identities.

docs.title: Canonical hashing
docs.text:
• [x] Encoding version is included in revision hashes.
  • [x] Type ID is included in revision hashes.
  • [x] Entity ID is not included in revision hashes.
  • [x] Snapshot internal node hashes use domain separation.
  • [x] Snapshot root hash uses separate root domain separation.
  • [x] No unordered map iteration participates in canonical identity.

docs.title: Change propagation
docs.text:
• [x] One entity update does not copy the full entity-to-revision mapping.
  • [x] An update copies only the bounded trie path plus the new leaf/state required.
  • [x] Unaffected branches are structurally shared.

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text:
• [x] Equivalent revision values have equivalent IDs.
  • [x] Equivalent snapshot mappings have equivalent IDs regardless of insertion order.
  • [x] Diff order is deterministic.
  • [x] ID textual forms round-trip exactly.

docs.title: Dependency direction
docs.text:
• [x] sr-core does not depend on sr-store.
  • [x] Neither crate depends on agent, server, UI, domain, filesystem watcher, or database-driver crates.

docs.title: Test Organization
docs.text:
If existing tests already prove an invariant clearly, do not duplicate them unnecessarily.

The new conformance test should focus on cross-module behavior that individual unit tests cannot prove alone.

Use fixed EntityId::from_bytes(...) values for most deterministic tests. Use EntityId::new() only when testing fresh identity generation.

docs.title: Documentation Check
docs.text:
Ensure the public APIs make these distinctions understandable without reading implementation internals:

EntityId = conceptual continuity
RevisionId = exact immutable local state
SnapshotId = exact immutable global state
named root = mutable pointer to SnapshotId

Add short rustdoc where the distinction is unclear.

Do not add long architectural essays to source files; the design documents remain authoritative.

docs.title: Commands to Run
docs.text:
Run all of the following successfully:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo doc --workspace --no-deps

If rustdoc warnings are enabled by the workspace, fix warnings introduced by these crates.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
• Do not add SQLite.
  • Do not add migrations.
  • Do not add domain schemas.
  • Do not add projection rendering.
  • Do not add agent APIs.
  • Do not optimize snapshot diff unless correctness requires a fix.
  • Do not change identity semantics to make tests easier.
  • Do not replace the persistent trie with a full copied HashMap.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Cross-module conformance scenario exists and passes.
  • [x] Local entity stability is demonstrated.
  • [x] Immutable historical revisions are demonstrated.
  • [x] Global snapshot change is demonstrated.
  • [x] Snapshot diff identifies only the changed entity resolution.
  • [x] Named-root CAS behavior is demonstrated.
  • [x] Structural sharing is still covered.
  • [x] All workspace tests pass.
  • [x] cargo fmt --check passes.
  • [x] clippy with warnings denied passes.
  • [x] docs build successfully.

When this task is complete, the identity subsystem is ready for later Level 2 designs covering durable persistence, migrations, domains, projections, sessions, and agents.

docs.title: Expose Trust State Through Protocol and Events
Objective
docs.text:
Expose trust-relevant application results through the shared Rust/wire protocol so server, remote clients, web libraries, TUI, CLI adapters, and agent tooling can observe the same semantics.

This task is transport representation only. It must not reimplement authorization, validation, promotion, or external-effect logic inside the protocol/server.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
1. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md, especially sections 30, 32, 37–39, 49, 52–54.
  2. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md.
  3. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md.
  4. design/level-3/001. implement principal and capability model.md.
  5. design/level-3/003. implement validation evidence and exact input binding.md.
  6. design/level-3/004. implement candidate promotion and approval pipeline.md.
  7. design/level-3/006. implement external effect receipts and reconciliation.md.

If the shared protocol crate or application operations do not exist, stop and report the prerequisite.

docs.title: Expected Area
docs.text:
Typical files/modules:

crates/scriberig-protocol/src/trust.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/event.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-server/... application-to-protocol adapters
web/packages/protocol/... generated/shared representations if that path already exists

Follow the repository's established schema generation approach. Do not maintain unrelated Rust and TypeScript wire models manually if generation already exists.

docs.title: Protocol Types
docs.text:
Expose serializable representations for at least:

CapabilityDenied
TrustSummary / provenance summary
ValidationSummary
ValidationDiagnostic
PolicyEvaluationSummary
ApprovalSummary
PromotionResult
ConflictSummary
ExternalEffectSummary / ReceiptSummary

Use stable IDs/references to inspect full underlying knowledge objects rather than embedding entire graphs into every response.

A compact trust summary should be able to say things equivalent to:

source kind
current validation state
last accepted migration/promotion
whether generated vs authored/observed
links/handles for deeper provenance

Do not invent one global trust score.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Add event variants for at least:

CandidateCreated
ValidationStarted
ValidationCompleted
ApprovalRecorded
ConflictDetected
CapabilityDenied
ExternalEffectUpdated
SnapshotPromoted

Events must carry operation/candidate/snapshot handles sufficient for a client to fetch current details.

Do not duplicate full validation output into every event when a result object can be referenced.

docs.title: Server Adapter
docs.text:
Map application results/errors to protocol types. The server must not reinterpret policy or retry denied operations with broader authority.

A capability denial must remain a denial, not become a generic 500/error string.

A stale/conflict promotion result must remain distinguishable from validation failure.

docs.title: TypeScript Parity
docs.text: If the TypeScript protocol package exists, update the generated/shared type surface and add compile-time tests/examples proving the trust/event variants are available to web clients.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Test:

  1. structured capability denial round-trip;
  2. validation result with diagnostics round-trip;
  3. promotion allowed/rejected/stale states remain distinct;
  4. conflict summary contains resolvable handles;
  5. external-effect unknown state survives serialization;
  6. events reference exact candidate/snapshot/operation IDs;
  7. no secret/credential field exists in trust protocol objects;
  8. Rust and TypeScript protocol representations stay in sync using the repository's normal conformance test.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run Rust workspace checks and web/type generation checks already defined by the repository.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not add server-only business rules. Do not flatten all trust state into strings. Do not leak restricted payloads inside denials/events. Do not expose reusable credentials.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] trust outcomes have stable protocol representations;
  • [x] denial/validation/conflict/promotion states remain distinct;
  • [x] trust events use the common event model;
  • [x] server is an adapter, not policy owner;
  • [x] TypeScript consumers receive the same contract;
  • [x] no sensitive material is serialized.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement @scriberig/components as a reusable React component library over @scriberig/react and @scriberig/editor-core with minimal visual assumptions and no MUI dependency.

The components provide ready-made semantic views while preserving replaceability and styling freedom for third-party applications.

Read before editing:

  2. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md
  3. design/level-3/005. implement headless editor core primitives.md
  4. design/level-3/006. implement react bindings.md

Prerequisite: React bindings and headless controllers compile.

docs.title: Styling Rules
docs.text:
The package must not depend on MUI or another application design system.

Allowed styling mechanisms:

  • semantic class names;
  • data attributes;
  • minimal package CSS if needed for structural layout/accessibility;
  • render props/slots for caller-owned rendering;
  • standard HTML attributes and ARIA roles.

Do not hard-code Scriberig product colors, typography, spacing system, or panel layout.

Components should accept className and relevant standard DOM props where practical.

docs.title: ObjectTree
docs.text:
Render the headless knowledge tree state.

Requirements:

  • lazy expanded children only;
  • expandable/collapsible rows;
  • loading and error state per node;
  • semantic labels/descriptions where present;
  • selection integration;
  • load-more behavior;
  • keyboard navigation provided through shared interaction behavior;
  • accessible tree/treeitem semantics where appropriate.

Do not fetch descendants independently from editor-core/model logic.

docs.title: ObjectInspector
docs.text:
Render semantic object information in a domain-neutral form.

Support at least:

  • semantic identity/reference;
  • type/schema label;
  • description/provenance where supplied;
  • current/exact revision information;
  • properties/summary values;
  • available relations;
  • stale/historical indicators.

Allow domain extensions or caller slots to replace sections.

docs.title: RelationBrowser
docs.text:
Render one selected relation/collection with pagination and semantic child selection.

Do not treat relation contents as a flat static array if the model exposes paging/count metadata.

docs.title: HistoryView and SemanticDiffView
docs.text:
HistoryView renders semantic history/lineage summaries and allows selection of revisions/snapshots for comparison.

SemanticDiffView renders structured semantic diff data rather than computing diffs itself.

Support caller/domain rendering overrides for specialized diff entries.

Do not implement source-text diffing algorithms in this package.

docs.title: MigrationPreview
docs.text:
Render a migration proposal/detail including:

  • base snapshot;
  • affected objects;
  • selected semantic changes;
  • validation status;
  • stale/conflict state;
  • apply/accept action when capability permits;
  • reject/close local review action.

Use the migration review controller/hook.

Do not directly mutate server/database state.

docs.title: SessionTree and BranchView
docs.text:
Represent sessions as structured semantic objects.

SessionTree must expose branches and nested branch structure progressively.

BranchView should show, where available:

  • title/description;
  • purpose;
  • status;
  • outcome;
  • touched objects;
  • decisions/tasks;
  • resulting migrations/snapshots;
  • links to detailed turn/chat projection when requested.

Do not reduce the session model to one chronological chat list.

docs.title: ValidationResults and OperationView
docs.text:
ValidationResults renders structured validation results and preserves distinctions among checks, diagnostics, pass/fail states, and references.

OperationView renders one durable operation lifecycle and progress/result references.

Closing/unmounting the component must not cancel the operation automatically.

docs.title: ProjectionHost
docs.text:
ProjectionHost is a domain-neutral host for registered projection view/editor implementations.

Responsibilities:

  • receive projection identity and semantic selection context;
  • locate the applicable registered projection handler;
  • display unsupported/readonly states explicitly;
  • pass semantic location selection callbacks between projection handler and shared selection model;
  • surface stale/candidate/conflict state.

Do not hard-code Monaco, CodeMirror, PDF.js, or Markdown editors in this task.

docs.title: AgentOperationView
docs.text:
Render agent operation state and semantic result links.

It may show streamed text/output when protocol exposes it, but semantic links to branch, migration, validation, and affected objects are first-class.

Do not make plain chat output the only result representation.

docs.title: Slots and Domain Extension
docs.text:
Where domain-specific rendering is expected, accept typed render callbacks/registered view descriptors rather than importing every domain package directly.

The neutral package should be able to render a useful fallback when no specialized extension exists.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
Required shared behavior:

  • keyboard-operable tree and command controls;
  • semantic button labels;
  • focusable interactive rows where appropriate;
  • ARIA roles for trees, lists, status, progress, dialogs/panels when applicable;
  • no interaction that is pointer-only.

Do not duplicate complex focus logic if editor-core already provides it.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Required tests:

  1. ObjectTree renders only loaded/expanded children;
  2. selection changes through a tree row update shared selection;
  3. keyboard navigation works for the primary tree interaction;
  4. historical/stale state is visible in ObjectInspector;
  5. MigrationPreview shows conflict/stale state distinctly from validation failure;
  6. SessionTree renders branch summaries without loading every branch transcript;
  7. unmounting OperationView does not cancel the underlying operation;
  8. package tests run without MUI context/theme.

Run:

pnpm --filter @scriberig/components typecheck
pnpm --filter @scriberig/components test
pnpm --filter @scriberig/components build

• Do not add MUI.

  • Do not implement app routing or panel layout.
  • Do not duplicate transport/model/editor-core state machines.
  • Do not implement source-specific projection editors.
  • Do not query the server directly from visual components when a hook/controller exists.
  • Do not create frontend-only mutation semantics.

  • [x] No MUI dependency exists.

docs.title: Agent Task: Implement Rebase and Semantic Replay
Goal
docs.text:
Implement rebase as creation of new history by replaying existing semantic work onto a different base snapshot.

The implementation must preserve original history and prefer recorded semantic intent over textual or positional patching.

docs.title: Read before editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md, especially sections 31 through 35 and 49.
  2. design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md.
  3. The completed migration, history, diff, and conflict models.

docs.title: Files to modify
docs.text:
crates/sr-change/src/rebase.rs
crates/sr-change/src/operation.rs
crates/sr-change/src/conflict.rs
crates/sr-change/src/history.rs
crates/sr-change/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs

docs.title: Rebase model
docs.text:
A rebase takes:

original base snapshot
original result snapshot or migration sequence
new base snapshot

and attempts to produce a new descendant of the new base.

Conceptually:

S1 -> S2
 \
  -> S3

rebase S1->S2 onto S3

S3 -> S4

S2 and its migration history remain unchanged.

docs.title: Replay order
docs.text:
For each original migration, replay in historical order.

For each change, use this preference order:

  1. recorded domain semantic operation through a registered domain replay strategy;
  2. recorded universal generic semantic operation;
  3. exact entity delta only when it can be applied safely against the new base;
  4. structured conflict when intent cannot be preserved safely.

Never fall back to byte offsets, line numbers, or rendered text patches in the universal engine.

docs.title: Domain replay strategy
docs.text:
Implement the Level 2 extension point for domain replay.

A domain strategy should receive:

  • the semantic operation;
  • old base/result references needed to understand it;
  • current target snapshot/context.

It should return an equivalent of:

Applied(changes)
Conflict(detail)
NotApplicable

The strategy must not mutate historical input state.

docs.title: Generic replay
docs.text:
Support replay for universal operations whose semantics remain unambiguous, such as:

  • replace entity revision when the target still resolves to the expected old revision;
  • insert/remove relation when the precondition still holds;
  • collection insertion/removal/move when stable entity identities and anchors still resolve unambiguously.

If a precondition does not hold, return a structured replay conflict instead of guessing.

docs.title: Replay preconditions
docs.text:
Each generic operation should define the semantic condition under which it can be safely replayed.

Examples:

ReplaceRevision(E, old, new)
requires target snapshot resolves E -> old

RemoveRelation(A, R, B)
requires relation exists

InsertCollectionMember(after X, Y)
requires X still identifies an unambiguous anchor

Do not silently adapt a failed precondition unless a domain strategy explicitly understands the change.

docs.title: Rebase result
docs.text:
Return a structure containing at least:

original base
original work/result
new base
new result snapshot if fully applied
new migration records or proposals
conflicts

Do not promote the rebased result automatically.

docs.title: History preservation
docs.text:
Tests must prove:

  • original snapshots and migrations remain readable;
  • rebased work receives new result snapshots;
  • rebased migration base references the new line of history;
  • original and rebased histories are distinguishable even if they converge to the same final state.

docs.title: Multi-migration replay
docs.text:
Support replaying a sequence, not only one migration.

Stop or continue after a conflict according to a documented deterministic policy. Prefer stopping at the first unresolved migration unless the implementation can safely isolate independent later work.

Do not partially claim a complete rebase when conflicts remain.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  • clean replay of one ReplaceRevision onto an unchanged entity;
  • replay conflict when the new base already changed that entity differently;
  • generic relation operation replay;
  • replay of two sequential migrations preserves order;
  • domain replay strategy resolves an operation unknown to the generic engine;
  • missing domain strategy yields conflict rather than discarded intent;
  • original history remains unchanged;
  • rebased state is a descendant of the new base;
  • same final state through rebase still has distinct history provenance.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Rebase never rewrites old history.
  • Do not use textual patch application.
  • Do not silently ignore failed operations.
  • Do not automatically promote rebased work.
  • Do not introduce domain-specific code into sr-change.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-change
cargo check --workspace

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Rebase creates new history.
  • [x] Semantic operations are preferred for replay.
  • [x] Generic operation preconditions are explicit.
  • [x] Failed preconditions become conflicts.
  • [x] Domain replay is optional and dependency-safe.
  • [x] Original history remains exact.
  • [x] Multi-migration replay is tested.

docs.title: Final response from implementing agent
docs.text: Report the replay order, precondition rules, conflict behavior, domain extension interface, and tests proving original history is unchanged.

docs.text:
Add Rust compiler/static-analysis integration as derived knowledge over canonical Rust syntax.

This task must keep compiler facts separate from canonical source syntax. The same canonical Rust entities remain authoritative even when compiler/toolchain-derived analysis is absent, stale, or rebuilt.

  2. design/level-3/005. implement language independent code domain.md
  3. design/level-3/006. implement rust syntax domain adapter.md
