crates/sr-projection/tests/projection_conformance.rs

Create focused extra modules only if a responsibility cannot remain clear in the prescribed files.

docs.title: Projection specification
docs.text:
Implement a public projection specification structure that can express:

  • stable projection/spec identity or entity reference;
  • semantic scope to render;
  • ProjectionKind;
  • ProjectionClass;
  • exact style revision/reference;
  • adapter identity/version;
  • renderer version;
  • ownership policy at the generic level;
  • adapter/domain configuration through a typed/opaque extension mechanism.

Do not store runtime dirty state inside the immutable user-meaningful specification.

Do not use a path as the projection ID.

docs.title: Deterministic render request
docs.text:
Create a request type that contains every generic input needed to reproduce output:

projection specification/reference
semantic scope
exact snapshot or exact resolved revisions
style revision
renderer version
rendering context

The API should make it obvious when a caller supplies only a moving/current reference rather than an exact snapshot. Deterministic render/cache paths should use exact inputs.

docs.title: Rendered output
docs.text:
Create a result type containing:

  • bytes or an adapter-neutral payload capable of text/binary representation;
  • media/projection kind metadata;
  • exact output digest/hash;
  • exact semantic/style/renderer inputs used;
  • optional fragment/cache metadata owned by the adapter;
  • deterministic/non-deterministic marker if the API supports non-reproducible renderers.

For the first implementation, deterministic renderers are the default and preferred case.

Use a stable digest mechanism already selected by the project; do not invent a different hash family unless necessary.

docs.title: Style reference behavior
docs.text:
Style used for deterministic output must resolve to exact immutable configuration.

If the system supports aliases such as user-default, resolve the alias before constructing the final render-cache identity. The alias itself must not be treated as immutable input if it can move.

Add tests proving two style revisions can produce distinct cache/input identities without changing the semantic object revision.

docs.title: Adapter trait
docs.text:
Implement the adapter trait so one domain adapter can provide:

capabilities()
render(...)
parse(...)
reconcile(...)
validate(...)

Requirements:

  • parsing and reconciliation are separate calls/responsibilities;
  • candidate parsed structures remain adapter-owned;
  • the generic trait does not require Markdown/source AST types;
  • reconciliation can return no-op, migration proposal, ambiguity, conflict, or invalid state;
  • validation can return structured diagnostics;
  • read-only adapters are not forced to implement meaningful parse/reconcile behavior beyond an explicit unsupported result.

Prefer compile-time separation/associated types where practical over Any downcasting.

docs.title: Reconciliation context
docs.text:
Provide a context type containing references needed for bidirectional editing:

  • last synchronization base snapshot/state;
  • current canonical snapshot/state;
  • semantic scope;
  • projection specification;
  • adapter/domain metadata needed to interpret the candidate.

Do not include filesystem watcher events in this type.

docs.title: Error model
docs.text:
Use structured error enums with sources.

At minimum distinguish:

  • unsupported operation;
  • bad projection configuration;
  • rendering failure;
  • parse failure;
  • reconciliation ambiguity/conflict;
  • validation failure;
  • stale/missing synchronization base;
  • storage/change-layer failure where propagated.

Do not use panics for malformed external content or unsupported adapter capabilities.

docs.title: Conformance tests
docs.text:
Add fake adapters in tests rather than using Markdown yet.

Cover:

  • deterministic render call returns exact input metadata;
  • exact same render request can produce identical digest;
  • different style revision is visible in render identity;
  • read-only adapter rejects edit import cleanly;
  • editable fake adapter performs parse then reconciliation as distinct operations;
  • NoSemanticChange carries no migration;
  • conflict/ambiguity remains structured;
  • no agent/server/filesystem dependency appears in sr-projection.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-projection
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not add actual filesystem synchronization.
  • Do not add Markdown parsing.
  • Do not define HTTP types.
  • Do not add model/provider or agent dependencies.
  • Do not bypass sr-change with an independent commit mechanism.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Projection specs separate immutable configuration from runtime state.
  • [x] Render requests use exact reproducible inputs.
  • [x] Output digest and input metadata are available.
  • [x] Style aliases are resolved before exact render identity is formed.
  • [x] Adapter parse/reconcile lifecycle is explicit.
  • [x] Structured outcomes/errors are tested.
  • [x] Workspace tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Agent Task: Implement the Change Subsystem Conformance Suite
Goal
docs.text:
Complete crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs as an end-to-end executable specification of the architectural invariants from design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md.

This task should add tests and only the minimal production fixes required to make already-designed behavior conform. Do not redesign public APIs opportunistically from the test task.

docs.title: Read before editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md, especially section 49.
  2. design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md.
  3. All Level 3 tasks 001 through 008 and the resulting implementations.
  4. The in-memory store conformance API from sr-store-memory.

docs.title: Primary file
docs.text:
crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs

Production files may be modified only when a test reveals a real mismatch with the approved designs.

docs.title: Test environment
docs.text:
Use sr-store-memory as the default backend for this suite.

Build small fixtures through public APIs only. Do not reach into internal hash maps or private store fields to construct states.

Create helper functions for:

empty/base snapshot creation
entity/revision creation
snapshot descendant creation
migration creation
branch/workspace setup
named-root setup

Keep helpers deterministic and small.

docs.title: Required scenario 1: exact direct migration
docs.text:
Create S1 containing entity E -> R1.

Create S2 containing E -> R2.

Record migration M1 from S1 to S2.

Verify:

  • S1 still resolves E -> R1;
  • S2 resolves E -> R2;
  • migration base/result are exact;
  • delta is exactly R1 -> R2;
  • history query finds M1 as touching E.

docs.title: Required scenario 2: creation and semantic removal
docs.text:
From one base:

  • introduce entity A;
  • remove entity B from the next canonical state.

Verify creation/removal delta classification and that historical snapshots still resolve retained old state.

Do not assert physical garbage collection.

docs.title: Required scenario 3: branches are cheap lines of work
docs.text:
Create two branches/workspaces from the same base snapshot.

Advance each independently.

Verify:

  • shared base remains unchanged;
  • each branch points to its own descendant;
  • branch creation did not duplicate semantic entities/revisions;
  • both results remain queryable.

Use public store metrics only if such metrics exist. Otherwise prove sharing through identical snapshot/revision identities rather than backend internals.

docs.title: Required scenario 4: optimistic promotion
docs.text:
Set:

main -> S1

Create workspaces producing S2 and S3 from S1.

Promote S2 with expected S1; it must succeed.

Attempt to promote S3 with expected S1; it must fail as stale and report actual S2.

Verify S3 remains available and no work was overwritten.

docs.title: Required scenario 5: arbitrary semantic diff
docs.text:
Build:

S1 -> S2 -> S4
 \
  -> S3

Compare:

  • S1 with S4;
  • S2 with S3;
  • a snapshot with itself.

Verify diff correctness without requiring direct ancestry.

docs.title: Required scenario 6: disjoint merge
docs.text:
Base contains entities A@A1 and B@B1.

Left changes only A.

Right changes only B.

Three-way merge must resolve both automatically with zero conflicts.

Verify base, left, and right remain unchanged.

docs.title: Required scenario 7: convergent merge
docs.text:
Both descendants independently produce the same exact revision for one entity.

Merge must converge to that revision without conflict.

History may remain distinct even though resulting state is equal.

docs.title: Required scenario 8: competing edit conflict
docs.text:
Both sides modify the same entity to different revisions.

Verify:

  • conflict kind is BothModified or the approved equivalent;
  • base/left/right revision handles are present;
  • no side is silently selected;
  • unrelated disjoint changes remain in resolved output.

docs.title: Required scenario 9: delete/modify conflict
docs.text:
One side removes an entity while the other modifies it.

Verify a structured DeleteModify conflict and no textual conflict-marker dependency.

docs.title: Required scenario 10: rebase preserves original history
docs.text:
Create original work S1 -> S2.

Create newer base S1 -> S3 affecting unrelated state.

Rebase original work onto S3 to produce S4.

Verify:

  • S2 and its migration still exist unchanged;
  • S4 descends from S3;
  • semantic intent was replayed;
  • history query can distinguish original and rebased paths.

docs.title: Required scenario 11: rebase conflict
docs.text:
Create original work modifying E.

Create new base modifying the same E differently.

Rebase must return a structured conflict rather than overwrite the new base.

docs.title: Required scenario 12: history topology ignores insertion order
docs.text:
Persist migration/history records in an order different from logical ancestry where the test infrastructure permits it.

Verify ancestry/common-ancestor/entity-history queries use explicit references and still return correct topology.

docs.title: Required scenario 13: move preserves entity continuity
docs.text:
Represent a structural move of one existing entity between generic collections/owners.

Verify:

  • the moved entity retains its EntityId;
  • structural owners change as required;
  • history describes a move/structural change rather than unrelated delete/create when continuity is known.

docs.title: Required scenario 14: cross-domain universal migration
docs.text:
Create entities with at least two different generic type/domain identities.

Change them atomically in one migration/snapshot transition.

Without loading any domain adapter, verify:

  • all entity deltas are visible;
  • summary counts are correct;
  • query APIs do not assume one file or language;
  • provenance is preserved.

docs.title: Required scenario 15: representation-only change creates no migration
docs.text:
Simulate or construct the highest-level available representation/style change that leaves canonical entity revisions identical.

Verify:

  • canonical snapshot identity remains equal where the underlying snapshot model says state is identical;
  • no semantic migration is manufactured;
  • derived/render artifacts may change independently if those APIs are available.

Do not create a fake empty migration to satisfy this test.

docs.title: Required scenario 16: compact navigation summaries
docs.text:
Create a migration with several changes and a branch/workspace with description metadata.

Verify summary APIs return:

  • exact handles;
  • counts;
  • branch status/base/current snapshots;
  • short metadata where present;

without requiring domain adapters.

docs.title: Determinism checks
docs.text:
Repeat relevant diff/query construction with different insertion order.

Verify public result ordering remains deterministic.

Do not snapshot-test unstable debug formatting unless repository convention explicitly uses it.

docs.title: Backend independence check
docs.text:
Inspect sr-change dependencies as part of review.

The library must not depend on:

sr-store-memory
sr-store-sqlite

except that sr-store-memory may appear under dev-dependencies for tests.

No production source file may import concrete backend implementation types.

docs.title: No domain leakage check
docs.text:
Search sr-change production code for domain-specific types.

The universal crate must not contain special cases for:

Rust AST
Markdown
PDF
session agent behavior
filesystem line offsets

Generic extension traits are allowed.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Run at minimum:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-change
cargo test -p sr-store-memory
cargo test --workspace
cargo check --workspace

Run clippy if it is part of repository CI.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] All 16 scenarios are implemented as real tests.
  • [x] Direct migration preserves old state.
  • [x] Branching and stale promotion are covered.
  • [x] Arbitrary diff is covered.
  • [x] Disjoint and convergent merge are covered.
  • [x] Both-modified and delete/modify conflicts are covered.
  • [x] Rebase success and conflict are covered.
  • [x] History is independent of insertion order.
  • [x] Move continuity is covered.
  • [x] Cross-domain migration works without adapters.
  • [x] Representation-only change does not create semantic history.
  • [x] Compact summaries are covered.
  • [x] Production crate has no concrete backend dependency.
  • [x] Workspace tests pass.

docs.title: Final response from implementing agent
docs.text:
Provide:

  1. the list of conformance scenarios implemented;
  2. any production defects discovered and fixed;
  3. exact commands run and outcomes;
  4. any Level 1 invariant that could not be tested because another subsystem is not implemented yet.

Do not weaken or skip a required invariant silently. If a dependency is genuinely missing, leave the test as a clearly documented blocked scenario rather than fabricating behavior.

docs.title: Implement: Filesystem Projection Ownership, Hashing, and Atomic IO
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the low-level filesystem primitives required by managed file projections without adding watcher integration or domain parsing yet.

This task establishes explicit ownership, normalized locations, exact-byte hashing, and safe writes in sr-projection-fs.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
  2. design/level-2/008. filesystem projection synchronization.md
  3. design/level-2/007. projection crate boundaries and core model.md
  4. design/level-3/008. implement projection specifications rendering and adapter api.md

docs.title: Files to create/modify
docs.text:
crates/sr-projection-fs/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/location.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/ownership.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/hash.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/io.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/state.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/tests/sync_conformance.rs

Do not create watcher-specific modules in this task beyond placeholders already required by lib.rs.

docs.title: location.rs
docs.text:
Define a filesystem projection location type around a path.

Requirements:

  • path is not a semantic EntityId;
  • preserve enough information to access the exact file;
  • define normalization/comparison behavior explicitly and conservatively;
  • avoid canonicalizing through filesystem IO as part of ordinary equality if it would make missing paths impossible to represent;
  • expose path accessors without leaking platform-specific watcher types.

Add tests for relative/absolute handling according to the chosen project-root policy.

docs.title: ownership.rs
docs.text:
Implement:

ManagedEditable
ManagedReadOnly
Unmanaged
ImportedExternal

Represent ownership separately from existence/dirty state.

Add helpers answering at least:

  • Scriberig may render/write this file;
  • external changes may be imported;
  • Scriberig must never rewrite it automatically.

Unmanaged must always reject automatic write/import ownership operations.

docs.title: hash.rs
docs.text:
Implement exact-byte digesting for file content and rendered output.

Requirements:

  • reuse project-standard digest/hash implementation if available;
  • hash exact bytes for the initial design;
  • expose a strongly typed file-content digest if appropriate;
  • support hashing bytes already in memory and file contents read from disk;
  • errors are returned, not panicked.

Add tests proving byte differences, including newline/spacing changes, change the file digest even though later domain reconciliation may find no semantic change.

docs.title: io.rs
docs.text:
Implement a small filesystem IO abstraction used by synchronization code.

It must support:

read(path) -> exact bytes
metadata/existence(path)
write_atomic(path, bytes)
remove/rename inspection helpers only if needed by later sync code

Provide a concrete local-filesystem implementation and a trait/interface that tests can replace if useful.

docs.title: Atomic write behavior
docs.text:
For write_atomic:

  1. create a temporary sibling file where practical;
  2. write all bytes;
  3. flush/close as required for correctness of the chosen guarantee;
  4. replace target atomically where supported;
  5. clean up failed temporary artifacts best-effort;
  6. return the digest of exact bytes known to have been written or enough data for the caller to compute/verify it.

Do not claim stronger crash-durability guarantees than implemented. The requirement is to avoid exposing half-written projection content during a normal process write.

Preserve reasonable file permissions where the implementation can do so safely; document limitations in code comments/tests rather than inventing a complex permission system here.

docs.title: state.rs
docs.text:
Add the filesystem-facing runtime sync-state value needed by later tasks.

It should be able to carry:

  • projection/spec reference;
  • location;
  • ownership;
  • last synchronized snapshot/base reference;
  • last rendered digest;
  • optional last observed digest;
  • projection lifecycle state from sr-projection;
  • adapter/style/renderer exact references needed to interpret the base.

Do not implement persistence backend tables in this task. Make the state serializable only if the workspace already has a standard serialization dependency and doing so does not couple it to a concrete backend.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Using a temporary directory, cover:

  • atomic write creates expected exact bytes;
  • returned/computed digest matches file bytes;
  • subsequent replacement produces the new exact bytes;
  • failed target path returns a structured error;
  • unmanaged ownership denies automatic writes through any high-level helper added here;
  • exact-byte formatting changes change digest;
  • semantic IDs are not derived from path text.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-projection-fs
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not add filesystem watcher library integration.
  • Do not parse or reconcile Markdown.
  • Do not treat a digest difference as a semantic migration.
  • Do not create SQL storage tables.
  • Do not import an unmanaged file automatically.
  • Do not implement agent or UI APIs.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Ownership model is explicit and tested.
  • [x] File locations are separate from semantic identity.
  • [x] Exact-byte hashing works.
  • [x] Atomic replacement works in normal local filesystem tests.
  • [x] Runtime sync-state type can carry the required synchronization base metadata.
  • [x] No watcher/domain/agent code was introduced.
  • [x] Tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Implement Reference Integrated Editor
docs.text: Product-verification caveat (2026-10-12): The checked items in this document record completion of the historical reference-editor subsystem scope. They do not prove that the editor supports a useful end-to-end project workflow. Current product completion is governed by design/level-1/013. vertical product completion and end to end usability.md, design/level-2/025. first useful project workflow vertical slice.md, and Level-3 tasks 116-122. Do not cite this checklist as evidence that imported-project activation, named semantic navigation, editable source projection, validated migration review, filesystem write-back, or golden-path E2E are complete.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the full Scriberig reference web application under web/apps/scriberig using only public web packages.

The application must demonstrate that the public web platform is sufficient to build the complete editor described by Level 1. It combines low-level knowledge browsing, semantic/domain views, projections, history/diffs, sessions/agents, migrations, validation, and long-running operations around one shared semantic selection.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
  2. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md
  3. design/level-3/005. implement headless editor core primitives.md
  4. design/level-3/006. implement react bindings.md
  5. design/level-3/007. implement neutral reusable components.md
  6. design/level-3/008. implement material ui component package.md

Prerequisites:

  • all public web packages compile;
  • the runtime/server exposes enough of the public protocol to connect the app;
  • if some server capability is not yet available, the app must show an explicit unsupported state rather than use a private workaround.

The controlling rule is:

If this application needs a private server call, direct database access, or private package import, fix the public abstraction instead of bypassing it.

docs.title: Files to Create or Replace
docs.text:
Create:

web/apps/scriberig/src/app-shell.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/routes.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/runtime.ts
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/RawKnowledgeView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/SemanticView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/ProjectionView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/HistoryView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/SessionAgentView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/OperationsView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/MigrationReviewView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/components/SnapshotStatus.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/components/SelectionSummary.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/components/UnsupportedCapability.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/test/app-public-boundary.test.ts

Update:

web/apps/scriberig/src/main.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/App.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/package.json
web/apps/scriberig/vite.config.ts

Do not create semantic logic in apps/scriberig that belongs in reusable packages.

docs.title: Runtime Composition
docs.text:
runtime.ts creates the application runtime from public packages.

It should construct/configure equivalents of:

public transport
Scriberig client
WorkspaceModel
SelectionController
extension/command registry

Configuration such as API base URL and authentication provider must enter through application configuration/environment, not hard-coded source constants.

The runtime should be injectable or replaceable enough for application tests.

docs.title: Application Provider Composition
docs.text:
App.tsx should compose:

  • MUI theme/provider;
  • @scriberig/react provider;
  • application routing/shell;
  • one shared selection controller/runtime;
  • connection/snapshot status.

Do not create a separate model/client instance per view.

docs.title: App Shell
docs.text:
Create a simple, maintainable workbench layout.

The first implementation does not need docking or persistent layouts.

It should expose navigation to these main surfaces:

Raw Knowledge
Semantic
Projection
History / Diff
Session / Agent
Operations
Migration Review when active

A practical initial layout may use:

  • top application bar with current snapshot/connection state;
  • left navigation or semantic tree area;
  • central active view;
  • optional right inspector/agent area.

The exact arrangement is less important than shared selection and public-package use.

docs.title: Universal Selection Integration
docs.text:
All major views must consume the same SelectionController through @scriberig/react.

Required behavior:

  • selecting an entity in Raw Knowledge updates Semantic and History views;
  • selecting an object in Semantic view updates inspector/agent scope;
  • selecting a mapped semantic region in Projection view updates global selection;
  • agent commands receive the active semantic selection;
  • migration review can highlight affected selected entities;
  • historical exact selection remains historical and is visibly marked.

Do not translate selection into file path + line number as the primary internal representation.

docs.title: RawKnowledgeView
docs.text:
Provide the low-level supported database/knowledge browser using public APIs.

It must support progressively inspecting:

  • entities;
  • exact/current revisions;
  • typed properties/summary data;
  • relations/collections;
  • descriptions/provenance;
  • reverse references if public capability exists;
  • snapshot resolution;
  • migration lineage where available.

Use reusable tree/inspector/relation components.

Do not connect directly to SQLite or server-internal database endpoints.

docs.title: SemanticView
docs.text:
Show the selected entity through domain-aware extensions where available.

Fallback to the generic semantic inspector when no domain-specific view is registered.

The view should support progressive disclosure rather than loading an entire project/domain graph.

Examples that may later be supported through extensions:

code module/function/code group
Markdown document/section/paragraph/table
PDF document/page/table/figure
session/branch/decision/task

Do not hard-code each domain into the app shell if extension registration can supply it.

docs.title: ProjectionView
docs.text:
Host the public projection component/handler for the active semantic selection.

Display clearly:

  • projection identity;
  • snapshot/base identity;
  • read-only/editable capability;
  • stale/candidate/conflict state;
  • semantic mapping availability.

When edits are supported, they must produce public semantic operations/migration proposals.

Do not treat the browser text buffer as canonical state.

docs.title: HistoryView
docs.text:
Provide entity and snapshot history around the current selection.

Allow choosing two comparable states and render semantic diff through public components.

Expose migration provenance and common-ancestor information when public capabilities provide it.

Raw projection/text diff may be offered as an additional view but must not replace semantic diff where available.

docs.title: SessionAgentView
docs.text:
Provide structured session and agent workbench functionality.

It should expose:

  • current session/branch;
  • nested branches progressively;
  • branch description/purpose/outcome;
  • goals/decisions/tasks where available;
  • agent command input;
  • active semantic selection as structured scope;
  • durable agent operation state;
  • resulting branch/migration/validation/snapshot links;
  • optional chat/transcript projection.

Sending a command must use the public agent operation and semantic scope.

Do not manufacture source-line prompts when entity selection exists.

docs.title: OperationsView
docs.text:
List and inspect known long-running operations independently of the initiating panels.

Support at least:

  • operation type/status;
  • queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled states;
  • progress;
  • result references;
  • structured errors;
  • cancellation when capability permits.

Closing another panel must not hide or cancel an active operation.

docs.title: MigrationReviewView
docs.text:
Display an active migration proposal using the reusable MUI migration component.

Support:

  • base snapshot;
  • affected objects;
  • semantic diff;
  • validation result;
  • stale/conflict state;
  • accept/apply when permitted;
  • close/reject local review.

After successful application, update from public events/new snapshot rather than mutating the local canonical model manually.

docs.title: Snapshot and Connection Status
docs.text:
SnapshotStatus.tsx must make visible whether the active view is:

current
historical
branch/candidate
stale relative to current server state
offline/disconnected

Do not hide stale/disconnected conditions behind generic toast messages only.

docs.title: Unsupported Capabilities
docs.text:
The reference editor must remain usable against servers that expose only part of the eventual feature set.

If a capability is unavailable:

  • disable/hide invalid commands through capability discovery;
  • display an explicit unsupported state when a user navigates to a required view;
  • do not use undocumented endpoints as fallback.

docs.title: Routing
docs.text:
Use routes only for application-level navigation/bookmarking.

Do not make route strings the semantic identity model.

Where useful, routes may serialize stable semantic references, but SelectionController remains the application interaction source of truth.

docs.title: Public-Boundary Test
docs.text:
Add a test/static check that scans application imports and fails if web/apps/scriberig/src imports:

  • private src/... paths of another workspace package;
  • Rust/server source paths;
  • database implementation paths;
  • undeclared deep package internals.

The app may import only documented package exports and normal third-party libraries.

docs.title: Required Functional Tests
docs.text:
At minimum use fakes/mocks through public package interfaces to verify:

  1. selecting an entity in RawKnowledgeView updates shared selection observed by SemanticView;
  2. historical selection produces historical snapshot status;
  3. agent command sends semantic selection/snapshot/session context;
  4. migration apply goes through public operation and waits for resulting state/event;
  5. an operation remains inspectable after the initiating view is unmounted;
  6. an unavailable capability produces an explicit unsupported state;
  7. no app view accesses a database/server-private API.

Do not require a full live backend for these application composition tests.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

pnpm --filter @scriberig/app typecheck
pnpm --filter @scriberig/app test
pnpm --filter @scriberig/app build
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build

The production Vite build must succeed.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not import database code.
  • Do not import server-internal Rust or TypeScript modules.
  • Do not deep-import another package's private source.
  • Do not reimplement semantic caches in the app.
  • Do not create a second selection system per panel.
  • Do not hard-code command lists that editor-core can discover.
  • Do not implement private mutation endpoints.
  • Do not make agent interaction only a chat transcript.
  • Do not implement sophisticated docking/layout persistence in the first version.
  • Do not add desktop-shell functionality in this task.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] The reference app uses only public web packages for Scriberig behavior.
  • [x] The raw knowledge surface bootstraps a shared tree through public client APIs.
  • [x] Snapshot and connection state is visible for connecting, current, and disconnected states.
  • [x] The raw tree loads its first child page lazily and updates shared semantic selection.
  • [x] Unsupported or unimplemented product surfaces remain available without private fallbacks.
  • [x] Raw, semantic, projection, history, session/agent, operations, and migration-review surfaces are fully implemented.
  • [x] One semantic selection coordinates every integrated view.
  • [x] Agent commands use structured semantic scope.
  • [x] Web edits/migration acceptance use public operations.
  • [x] Long-running operations are independently inspectable.
  • [x] Public-boundary and cross-surface conformance tests pass.
  • [x] App and workspace checks pass from a clean repository state.

The current implementation is the first connected browser vertical slice. The remaining unchecked items require later protocol/application capabilities and must not be represented as complete merely because placeholder views exist.

docs.title: Implement Session Domain Structure and Views
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the session-domain structures described by design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md inside the existing scriberig-session crate.

Sessions use the same universal entity/revision/snapshot model as documents and code. This task must not create a separate transcript database or model-provider-specific session format.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md
  2. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  3. design/level-2/001. workspace and package layout.md
  4. the current scriberig-session crate and shared graph/schema APIs

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Inside crates/scriberig-session/, create or update modules equivalent to:

src/lib.rs
src/schema.rs
src/types.rs
src/branch.rs
src/turn.rs
src/description.rs
src/views.rs
src/error.rs

Add tests under:

tests/session_structure.rs
tests/session_views.rs

Follow the crate's existing module layout if it already differs, but preserve these responsibilities.

docs.title: Session Vocabulary
docs.text:
Define session-domain entities for at least:

Session
Branch
Goal
HumanInput
AgentOutput
Observation
Question
Decision
ToolInvocation
ToolResult
BranchResult
Summary
Task
Turn

Use shared schema/entity/relation APIs.

Do not model an entire session as one transcript string.

docs.title: Core Relations
docs.text:
Support at least the following semantic relationships:

Session --contains--> Branch
Branch --contains--> Turn
Branch --touches--> any Entity
Decision --derived_from--> Branch
ToolResult --produced_by--> ToolInvocation
BranchResult --produced_by--> Branch
Goal/Task --belongs_to--> Session or Branch as appropriate

Turn ordering within a branch must be explicit.

Cross-domain touches/reference relations must point to the real target entities without copying their contents into the session.

docs.title: Branch Metadata
docs.text:
A branch must be able to expose compact navigation metadata without loading all turns.

Support at least:

title or short description
purpose
outcome when completed
state/status
touched entities
turn count or equivalent cheap structural summary

Generated descriptions or summaries must carry provenance and remain derived unless explicitly authored/promoted.

The branch entity must remain useful even when no generated summary exists.

docs.title: Branch State
docs.text:
Define and validate a minimal branch lifecycle suitable for future agent work.

Use the shared schema/validation mechanisms where possible.

At minimum distinguish states equivalent to:

active
completed
abandoned

Do not invent model-provider-specific states.

Invalid state transitions should be rejected by session-domain validation rather than silently accepted.

docs.title: Session Views
docs.text:
Implement domain views that can project the same underlying session knowledge into structured data suitable for later renderers.

At minimum provide view construction for:

branch tree
chronological turn sequence for a selected branch
compact branch summaries/descriptors
decision log

If the generic projection system already defines rendering interfaces, integrate with them. Otherwise expose pure structured view builders and defer textual/UI rendering.

Do not implement an LLM context policy in this task unless an existing design already defines one concretely.

docs.title: Progressive Disclosure
docs.text:
The domain must support this navigation pattern:

Session
  -> Branch
     -> Turn
        -> HumanInput/AgentOutput/ToolInvocation/ToolResult/etc.

A caller should be able to list branches with compact metadata without fetching every turn.

A caller should be able to open one branch and then inspect one turn or tool interaction.

docs.title: Cross-Domain References
docs.text:
Test that a branch can reference/touch arbitrary semantic entities through universal graph handles, for example:

Function
Paragraph
PDFPage
Migration
Decision

Do not create session-owned copies of those objects.

docs.title: Provider Independence
docs.text:
Do not encode OpenAI-, Anthropic-, Gemini-, or other provider-specific message structures as canonical session schema.

Provider request/response payloads may later be preserved as external artifacts or tool/provider metadata, but the session domain remains provider-neutral.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests proving:

  • a session contains ordered/navigable branches;
  • a branch contains ordered turns;
  • branch compact metadata can be read without loading turn bodies;
  • a completed branch can store outcome/result references;
  • a branch can touch a code/document/PDF entity without copying it;
  • tool invocation and tool result are separate related entities;
  • invalid branch state transitions are rejected;
  • session views are deterministic from the same snapshot;
  • no model provider is required to use the session crate.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-session
cargo clippy -p scriberig-session --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not build an agent runtime.
  • Do not call a model.
  • Do not store the session only as chat transcript text.
  • Do not copy referenced project entities into session storage.
  • Do not add provider-specific canonical message types.
  • Do not create separate session persistence tables that bypass the universal model.
  • Do not implement web UI components.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Session-domain entities use the universal schema/graph model.
  • [x] Branches have compact semantic metadata.
  • [x] Branch/turn ordering is explicit.
  • [x] Cross-domain references use stable semantic handles.
  • [x] Tool calls/results and decisions are structured entities.
  • [x] Branch lifecycle validation exists.
  • [x] Structured session views support progressive disclosure.
  • [x] No agent/model provider is required.
  • [x] Tests, formatting, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement: Filesystem Observation, Synchronization, and Recovery
Objective
docs.text:
Complete the filesystem synchronization engine in sr-projection-fs so managed projections can detect external changes, suppress feedback from Scriberig's own writes, retain failed imports, and hand exact three-way inputs to a domain adapter.

This task does not implement Markdown semantics. Use a fake editable adapter in tests.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
  2. design/level-2/008. filesystem projection synchronization.md
  3. design/level-3/009. implement filesystem projection ownership hashing and atomic io.md
  4. design/level-3/008. implement projection specifications rendering and adapter api.md

docs.title: Files to create/modify
docs.text:
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/observe.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/sync.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/recovery.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/state.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/io.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/tests/sync_conformance.rs

Add a watcher-library integration module only if required to keep concrete watcher code isolated from the public observation model. The public API must not expose that library's event types.

docs.title: Observation model
docs.text:
Define an internal/public-neutral event model supporting at least:

Created(path)
Modified(path)
Removed(path)
Renamed { from, to }
RescanRequired(scope)

Treat events as hints. Every event handler must inspect current file/synchronization state before deciding what changed.

Duplicate or coalesced events must be safe.

docs.title: Observation source abstraction
docs.text:
Provide a trait or stream boundary so tests can inject deterministic events.

If a concrete watcher crate is selected:

  • keep it behind one adapter module;
  • convert its events immediately into Scriberig observation events;
  • do not leak its debounce/coalescing semantics into projection correctness;
  • document platform limitations in code.

docs.title: Synchronization store boundary
docs.text:
Define a small interface used by the synchronization engine to load/update runtime projection sync state.

The first implementation may include an in-memory implementation for tests.

Do not add SQLite tables in this task unless another existing design has already defined where runtime projection state belongs. Keep the interface backend-independent.

Updates to synchronization state around writes/imports must be coherent and ordered so a failed operation cannot falsely mark a projection synchronized.

docs.title: Render-to-file path
docs.text:
Implement a service operation equivalent to:

render_managed_projection(spec, exact semantic input)
    -> adapter render
    -> atomic filesystem write
    -> record exact output digest and base
    -> state = Synchronized

Rules:

  • reject Unmanaged;
  • respect read-only/editable ownership;
  • store the actual renderer/style/base used;
  • update the synchronized digest only after successful write;
  • expose structured diagnostics on failure.

docs.title: External modification detection
docs.text:
On a relevant observation:

  1. load projection sync state;
  2. inspect current path;
  3. if missing, transition according to missing/deletion policy without inventing semantics;
  4. read exact bytes if present;
  5. compute digest;
  6. if digest equals last synchronized rendered digest, ensure state is synchronized and stop;
  7. if different, mark ExternallyModified and begin editable-import flow if ownership permits.

For ManagedReadOnly, do not call parse/reconcile. Surface drift state or configured regeneration behavior.

For Unmanaged, do nothing beyond optional observation metadata.

docs.title: Feedback-loop suppression
docs.text:
Correctness must rely on exact state/hash checks rather than only timestamps/debounce.

After Scriberig writes bytes H and watcher emits Modified(path), reading the file and seeing H must result in no import.

If the file changed again before processing and now hashes to H2, the external edit must still be noticed even if an old self-write token exists.

Optional operation tokens may reduce IO but cannot override contradictory content.

docs.title: Editable import orchestration
docs.text:
For an externally modified managed-editable file:

read F
load synchronization base B
load current canonical D
adapter.parse(F)
adapter.reconcile(B, D, candidate)
adapter.validate(result)

The synchronization engine must react to generic outcomes:

  • NoSemanticChange: optionally rerender configured canonical style, then establish new base;
  • MigrationProposal: pass to change/promotion service boundary, then rerender successful canonical result;
  • Ambiguous: state becomes conflict/attention-required; preserve external bytes/base;
  • Conflict: same as above with structured conflict;
  • InvalidExternalState: state becomes ImportFailed; preserve base and diagnostics.

Do not apply migrations directly by modifying store records. Use public sr-change/application-level promotion boundaries available in the repository.

docs.title: Failed import recovery
docs.text:
recovery.rs must represent enough information to retry:

  • projection reference;
  • base snapshot;
  • current canonical snapshot observed for the attempt;
  • external digest;
  • path;
  • stage of failure;
  • structured diagnostics;
  • optional captured external bytes if policy chooses to retain them.

A later event for unchanged invalid bytes should be idempotent. A later event with different bytes should create a new attempt while keeping historical diagnostics only if the runtime store policy supports it.

Never advance the last synchronization base on failure.

docs.title: Rename/move handling
docs.text:
A rename event should update external-location mapping/state only through a projection ownership/configuration service boundary.

Do not change semantic entity identity.

If the destination is not owned by the same projection, surface an unresolved ownership/mapping event rather than silently taking control.

docs.title: Removal handling
docs.text:
File removal is not semantic deletion by default.

Represent Missing and expose enough context for higher/domain policy to choose regeneration, projection unmapping, or candidate semantic deletion.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Using fake observation source, in-memory sync state, temporary filesystem, and fake domain adapter, cover:

  • self-write watcher event does not call parse;
  • external content change calls parse exactly as needed;
  • duplicate modified events are idempotent;
  • changed-again file is not hidden by stale self-write suppression;
  • read-only projection does not import;
  • unmanaged file is ignored;
  • parse failure retains old base and enters ImportFailed;
  • later valid content retries and can become synchronized;
  • ambiguity/conflict retains external state and base;
  • missing file enters Missing without deleting semantic state;
  • rename preserves projection identity and does not alter semantic entity IDs;
  • current canonical snapshot can differ from synchronization base and both are passed to reconciliation.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-projection-fs
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not implement Markdown matching here.
  • Do not resolve semantic conflicts in the filesystem layer.
  • Do not use watcher timing as the authority for self-write detection.
  • Do not advance sync base after failed parse/reconcile/validation.
  • Do not treat deletion as semantic deletion automatically.
  • Do not add agent/server/UI dependencies.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Observation events are watcher-library neutral.
  • [x] Managed render writes establish exact synchronization state.
  • [x] Self-generated events converge without feedback loops.
  • [x] External edits route through adapter lifecycle.
  • [x] Failed imports are retryable without losing valid canonical/base state.
  • [x] Three-way base/current/external inputs are available.
  • [x] Tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Implement Web Boundary and Conformance Tests
Objective
docs.text:
Add cross-package tests and static boundary checks that enforce the web architecture defined by Level 1 and Level 2.

This task is not about adding new product features. It verifies that the reusable web platform, MUI layer, and reference editor obey their intended dependency and behavior boundaries.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md
  2. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
  3. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md
  4. Level 3 tasks 001 through 009 for the implemented web files.

Prerequisite: the relevant web packages and reference application exist.

docs.title: Files to Create
docs.text:
Create a dedicated conformance test area:

web/test/conformance/package-boundaries.test.ts
web/test/conformance/public-api-imports.test.ts
web/test/conformance/dependency-direction.test.ts
web/test/conformance/reference-app-boundary.test.ts
web/test/conformance/selection-integration.test.tsx
web/test/conformance/snapshot-incrementality.test.ts
web/test/conformance/structured-agent-scope.test.tsx
web/test/conformance/mutation-path.test.tsx
web/test/conformance/operation-lifecycle.test.tsx
web/test/conformance/test-helpers.ts

Update root web scripts/configuration so:

pnpm test

runs these tests in addition to package-local tests.

If the workspace testing setup requires a small root Vitest config, create it under web/ and keep it limited to test configuration.

docs.title: Dependency-Direction Test
docs.text:
Implement a static/import-graph check that enforces at least:

protocol -> no Scriberig web dependency
client -> protocol only among lower semantic packages
model -> protocol/client
editor-core -> protocol/model and allowed lower packages
react -> lower packages + React, never MUI
components -> reusable lower packages, never MUI
components-mui -> reusable lower packages + MUI
app -> public package entry points only

The check must fail when a lower package imports from a higher package.

It must also fail when a package deep-imports another package's src/ internals.

Prefer a small explicit test over introducing a large architecture-analysis dependency unless one is clearly justified.

docs.title: MUI Isolation Test
docs.text:
Verify that MUI packages are not imported by:

@scriberig/protocol
@scriberig/client
@scriberig/model
@scriberig/editor-core
@scriberig/react
@scriberig/components

The only reusable package allowed to import MUI is @scriberig/components-mui.

The reference app may import MUI as a product choice.

docs.title: Public API Import Test
docs.text:
Scan source imports to ensure cross-package imports use public package names/exports.

Reject patterns equivalent to:

@scriberig/model/src/...
../../packages/model/src/...
server/src/...
crates/... database internals

The exact implementation may resolve workspace paths from package.json files rather than hard-coding every relative depth.

docs.title: Reference Editor Boundary Test
docs.text:
Verify the reference app cannot access:

  • SQLite/database code;
  • server-private modules;
  • Rust implementation source paths;
  • private web package modules;
  • undocumented private endpoint helpers.

The test should make architectural violations fail CI immediately.

docs.title: Shared Selection Integration Test
docs.text:
Build an integration fixture using public model/editor-core/React APIs.

Demonstrate:

  1. one semantic selection controller instance is provided to multiple views;
  2. selecting an entity through a tree-like interaction is observed by an inspector-like consumer;
  3. the same selection is available as agent command scope;
  4. projection-location metadata may change without losing semantic entity identity;
  5. historical exact revision selection remains exact.

This test proves that views are integrated by semantic selection rather than app-specific row/line state.

docs.title: Snapshot Incrementality Test
docs.text:
Create a fixture containing:

Snapshot A:
Entity X -> Revision X1
Entity Y -> Revision Y1

Snapshot B:
Entity X -> Revision X2
Entity Y -> Revision Y1

After applying a snapshot-advanced/entity-changed event sequence, verify:

  • current snapshot becomes B;
  • X resolves to X2 in current state;
  • cached X1 remains available for historical use;
  • Y1 is reused and not needlessly replaced/refetched;
  • a historical view pinned to A remains on A;
  • stale/current status is represented correctly.

This test enforces the Level 1 incremental architecture.

docs.title: Structured Agent Scope Test
docs.text:
Using the public app/component boundary, simulate a semantic selection and an agent command.

Verify the command operation receives structured context equivalent to:

entity
revision/current-resolution context
snapshot
session
branch when applicable
user request

Reject a regression where the UI replaces this with only a file path and line-number prompt when semantic identity is available.

The test may inspect the fake client's invocation payload.

docs.title: Mutation Path Test
docs.text:
Simulate a user edit/mutation from the web layer.

Verify that the action flows through a public semantic operation/migration proposal and validation/apply path.

The test should fail if the component/app directly mutates canonical model cache entries as though they were server state.

At minimum verify:

  • mutation command produces/requests a proposed change;
  • validation result is represented separately;
  • accepted result advances to a resulting snapshot/event;
  • browser-local candidate state is not silently treated as canonical before acceptance.

docs.title: Operation Lifecycle Test
docs.text:
Create a fake long-running operation.

Verify:

  • one panel starts the operation;
  • the operation is stored by stable OperationId;
  • the initiating panel unmounts;
  • another operation view can continue observing progress;
  • progress/completion events update the same operation record;
  • unmount does not imply cancellation;
  • explicit cancellation uses the public operation API.

docs.title: Progressive Disclosure Test
docs.text:
Where practical, add a fixture proving a knowledge tree requests only root/expanded relation pages.

The test should fail if opening a root automatically requests every descendant.

This may live in the package-local editor-core/component tests if already covered there; do not duplicate expensive tests unnecessarily.

docs.title: Capability Test
docs.text:
Verify a view/command can represent a missing capability without using a private fallback.

Example:

  • server fixture does not advertise migration-apply capability;
  • apply command is unavailable/disabled;
  • UI can render an unsupported/permission state;
  • no hidden alternate mutation call occurs.

docs.title: Test Helpers
docs.text:
test-helpers.ts may provide:

  • fake transport/client;
  • in-memory protocol fixtures;
  • workspace model setup;
  • fake event stream;
  • test runtime/provider factory;
  • representative entity/revision/snapshot fixtures.

Keep helpers based on public package APIs where the test is intended to prove public usability.

Do not expose internal test helpers as production package exports.

docs.title: Root Scripts
docs.text:
Ensure root web/package.json has reliable scripts for at least:

typecheck
test
build

Add a dedicated conformance script if useful, for example:

test:conformance

But pnpm test must still include or depend on conformance testing so CI cannot omit it accidentally.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run from web/:

pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build

Run any dedicated conformance script as well if added.

All checks must succeed from a clean install using the committed lockfile.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not weaken package boundaries simply to make tests pass.
  • Do not whitelist deep imports from the reference app.
  • Do not make the conformance tests depend on a production database.
  • Do not require a live external server unless a separate integration-test tier is explicitly available.
  • Do not duplicate every package unit test; test architectural behavior that spans packages.
  • Do not introduce MUI into lower packages for test convenience.
  • Do not treat source file line positions as universal selection identity.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Dependency direction is enforced by dedicated conformance tests.
  • [x] The current app changes use public package entry points only.
  • [x] MUI isolation is enforced by conformance tests.
  • [x] Deep/private cross-package imports are rejected by conformance tests.
  • [x] Reference app database/server boundary is enforced by conformance tests.
  • [x] Runtime bootstrap and disconnected failure behavior are unit tested.
  • [x] Shared semantic selection integration is tested across all views.
  • [x] Snapshot incrementality and immutable revision reuse are tested.
  • [x] Agent commands are tested for structured semantic scope.
  • [x] Web mutations are tested to flow through public migration/validation operations.
  • [x] Durable operation lifecycle is tested across view unmounts.
  • [x] Missing capabilities can be represented without private fallbacks in the current slice.
  • [x] Root typecheck/test/build commands all succeed from a clean repository state.

This task remains incomplete. The checked items cover only the newly verified runtime bootstrap behavior; they do not claim the full conformance suite.

docs.title: Prevent Derived Cache Access Leaks
docs.text: Implemented against the current workspace on 2026-10-11. Immutable dependency keys remain principal-independent in scriberig-derive; the application exposes them through GuardedDerivedRepository, which checks every canonical and nested derived dependency at cache-read time.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Ensure summaries, descriptions, search indexes, analysis results, and other derived/cached artifacts cannot expose knowledge that the requesting principal is not allowed to observe.

This task connects the derived-knowledge cache model to application-level capability enforcement without moving authorization policy into the generic cache implementation.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
1. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md, especially sections 11, 33, 62–64.
  2. design/level-1/008. derived knowledge caching and incrementality.md.
  3. design/level-3/002. enforce capabilities in application queries.md.
  4. Existing derived-knowledge runtime/cache Level 2 and Level 3 designs.

If the derivation/cache subsystem or application authorization boundary does not exist yet, stop and report the prerequisite.

docs.title: Expected Area
docs.text:
Reuse the existing derivation/cache implementation. Likely changes span:

existing derived-knowledge/cache crate modules
crates/scriberig-app/src/authorization.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/query.rs or derived-view adapter

Do not fork a second secure cache.

docs.title: Dependency Access Semantics
docs.text:
Every derived artifact must retain enough dependency information to identify the semantic inputs from which its visible content was produced.

For an application request, access to a derived artifact is allowed only if the effective policy permits the caller to observe the information that the artifact reveals.

At minimum, implement the conservative rule:

If the caller cannot read every declared semantic dependency that contributes visible content, do not return the derived artifact.

Later policies may support redacted derivations, but this task must not invent partial-redaction inference.

docs.title: Cache Keys vs Authorization
docs.text:
Keep cache identity independent from principal identity where possible. Immutable input/profile keys should continue to deduplicate computation globally.

Authorization is checked when returning an artifact through the application layer.

Do not duplicate identical summary computation once per user merely to enforce access control unless the existing architecture explicitly requires per-principal derivation.

docs.title: Search Indexes
docs.text:
If the derived subsystem owns a searchable index, ensure the application search path filters results before exposing:

entity identity when confidential
matched text/snippet
summary text
relation context
counts that reveal restricted entities when policy forbids existence disclosure

The lower-level index may remain complete; the trusted application boundary must not return forbidden hits.

docs.title: Nested Derived Artifacts
docs.text:
A derived artifact may depend on another derived artifact. Access calculation must ultimately account for canonical/observed semantic dependencies, not merely conclude that a cached summary is public because its direct dependency is another summary.

Reuse the existing derivation dependency graph rather than adding ad hoc recursive database scans.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Create fixtures for:

  1. principal can read subject and receives cached summary;
  2. principal cannot read subject and cannot receive cached summary;
  3. restricted entity is absent/redacted from authorized search result according to application policy;
  4. cache hit does not bypass capability check;
  5. artifact derived from allowed + restricted dependencies is denied conservatively;
  6. nested derived artifact still carries effective restrictions;
  7. broader principal reuses the same cached artifact successfully;
  8. authorization denial does not invalidate/delete the shared cache entry;
  9. formatting/profile cache behavior remains unchanged by authorization;
  10. no restricted snippet appears in denial/error text.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run workspace format/check/tests/lint and existing cache/derivation tests. Include an application-level integration test proving the same cache key can serve an authorized caller while being denied to an unauthorized caller.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not put mutable ACLs inside immutable content hashes. Do not make principal identity part of semantic revision identity. Do not return cached text before checking access. Do not assume generated summaries are safe to expose because they are not canonical.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] derived artifacts retain usable dependency provenance;
  • [x] application access checks cover cache hits and misses;
  • [x] search cannot leak restricted snippets;
  • [x] nested derivations preserve effective restrictions;
  • [x] shared immutable cache entries remain reusable across authorized principals;
  • [x] tests prove denial does not destroy cache reuse.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Create reusable test support that lets every domain adapter prove it respects the architectural invariants in design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md.

The goal is not to test domain-specific semantics in one generic suite. The goal is to make common invariants easy to verify consistently across Markdown, Rust/code, PDF, sessions, and future domains.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  2. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
  3. the existing domain crates and shared schema/graph/migration/projection test APIs

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Create a reusable test-support crate if no equivalent already exists:

crates/domains/test-support/Cargo.toml
crates/domains/test-support/src/lib.rs
crates/domains/test-support/src/conformance.rs
crates/domains/test-support/src/fixture.rs

Use package name:

scriberig-domain-test-support

Update the root workspace membership.

Domain crates may add this crate as a dev-dependency only.

If an existing generic test-support crate already serves this role, extend it instead of creating another one.

docs.title: Common Conformance Model
docs.text:
Define a small fixture/test contract that domain test suites can implement to provide:

a representative canonical entity graph
a semantically equivalent projection round trip when the domain supports editable projections
a changed semantic example
a formatting/projection-only change example when applicable
a derived-data example when the domain supports derived analysis
a generic inspection target

Do not force unsupported concepts on a domain. Capabilities must be optional and tests should run only when the fixture declares them.

docs.title: Required Common Invariants
docs.text:
Provide reusable assertions/helpers for these invariants where applicable:

  1. canonical state can be inspected through universal graph APIs;
  2. domain-specific inspection adds meaning without bypassing universal identity;
  3. unchanged semantic entities/revisions are reusable;
  4. projection-only formatting changes do not create semantic changes;
  5. editable projection reconciliation produces shared migration/change objects rather than direct mutation;
  6. derived knowledge records provenance and can be rebuilt/discarded without losing canonical state;
  7. descriptions/summaries marked generated remain derived;
  8. source coordinates are metadata and not semantic identity;
  9. generic handles survive irrelevant projection changes;
  10. no agent runtime is needed to instantiate or use the domain fixture.

Not every domain must support editable projections or derived analysis. The harness must distinguish unsupported capability from failed conformance.

docs.title: Domain-Specific Adoption
docs.text:
Add conformance tests to the domain crates implemented by the other Level 3 tasks when those crates exist:

scriberig-domain-markdown
scriberig-domain-code
scriberig-domain-rust
scriberig-domain-pdf
scriberig-session

Use dev-dependencies only. Do not make production domain code depend on the conformance crate.

For scriberig-domain-code, run only schema/identity/derived-boundary tests if no projection parser exists.

For PDF, treat exact source bytes versus derived extraction as the important authority/provenance boundary.

For sessions, verify provider-independent use and cross-domain references.

docs.title: Test Reporting
docs.text:
Failures should clearly identify:

domain
capability/invariant
fixture case
expected invariant
observed behavior

Avoid opaque macro failures.

Prefer normal Rust test functions/helpers over a complex custom test runner unless the repository already has one.

docs.title: Workspace Checks
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

Also verify from manifests that scriberig-domain-test-support appears only as a development/test dependency for domain crates.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not encode Markdown-specific rules into the generic harness.
  • Do not require every domain to support rendering/reconciliation.
  • Do not depend on agent crates.
  • Do not create runtime production dependencies from domain crates to test-support.
  • Do not use snapshots of huge serialized output as the only assertion mechanism.
  • Do not treat unsupported optional capabilities as conformance failures.
  • Do not replace domain-specific tests with this suite.

docs.text:

  • [x] Capability-conditional assertions are supported.
  • [x] Universal graph inspection is tested across participating domains.

  • [x] Agent independence is tested.
  • [x] Domain crates use test-support only as a dev dependency.
  • [x] Failures are readable and domain-specific.
  • [x] Workspace tests, formatting, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement: Markdown Model, Parser, Renderer, and Style
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the first concrete projection adapter in sr-markdown up to deterministic parse/render/equivalence. Do not implement identity reconciliation or migration generation in this task.

The result must be able to parse ordinary Markdown into an adapter-owned candidate structure, render canonical Markdown semantic objects deterministically, and determine when two supported Markdown representations are semantically equivalent despite formatting differences.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
  2. design/level-2/009. markdown editable projection adapter.md
  3. design/level-2/007. projection crate boundaries and core model.md
  4. design/level-3/008. implement projection specifications rendering and adapter api.md

Inspect any existing universal graph/schema crates and use their public entity/revision representation rather than creating a competing store model.

docs.title: Files to create/modify
docs.text:
crates/sr-markdown/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-markdown/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-markdown/src/model.rs
crates/sr-markdown/src/candidate.rs
crates/sr-markdown/src/style.rs
crates/sr-markdown/src/parser.rs
crates/sr-markdown/src/render.rs
crates/sr-markdown/src/equivalence.rs
crates/sr-markdown/src/diagnostic.rs
crates/sr-markdown/tests/round_trip.rs

Do not create match_nodes.rs or implement reconciliation logic beyond minimal placeholders needed to satisfy the adapter trait; those belong to the next task.

docs.title: Parser dependency
docs.text:
Select a mature CommonMark-compatible Rust parser unless the repository already chose one.

Keep parser-library types inside sr-markdown.

Do not expose parser-library AST node types in public Scriberig APIs.

Record the dependency normally in Cargo.toml; no Level 1 design update is needed for the parser choice.

docs.title: model.rs
docs.text:
Define the Markdown semantic vocabulary required by Level 2.

Support at least:

MarkdownDocument
Section
Heading
Paragraph
List
ListItem
Table
TableRow
TableCell
CodeBlock
QuoteBlock
Link

Choose a representation that separates block structure from inline content cleanly enough to preserve links and basic author-significant inline structure.

Requirements:

  • order belongs to parent collections;
  • line numbers/source offsets are not semantic identity;
  • model does not store an original Markdown blob as canonical content;
  • no hidden file-specific IDs are required;
  • types are deterministic/serializable according to existing project conventions.

If the universal graph layer expects schemas rather than Rust enums as canonical representation, implement conversion/builders between these domain values and that graph instead of making this model a second source of truth.

docs.title: candidate.rs
docs.text:
Define parser-owned candidate nodes distinct from canonical EntityId.

Candidate nodes need:

  • local candidate identifier/path for diagnostics;
  • semantic kind;
  • ordered children;
  • parsed content/properties;
  • optional source span/line information for error reporting only.

A candidate node must not pretend to be an existing canonical entity.

docs.title: style.rs
docs.text:
Implement an immutable-value MarkdownStyle with only supported deterministic options.

Initial fields should cover:

list_marker
ordered_list_delimiter
blank_lines_between_blocks
final_newline
code_fence_preference
table_spacing

Validate style values at construction where needed.

Do not add options that merge/split paragraphs, alter headings, rewrite URLs, or change code contents.

docs.title: parser.rs
docs.text:
Parse exact input bytes/text into CandidateDocument.

Requirements:

  • preserve document/section hierarchy derived from headings;
  • parse paragraphs;
  • parse ordered/unordered lists and items;
  • parse fenced/indented code as supported by the chosen library into code-block semantics;
  • parse block quotes;
  • parse links;
  • parse tables if the selected parser requires enabling a standard extension; document that capability in adapter metadata;
  • produce structured diagnostics on unsupported/invalid constructs rather than panicking;
  • retain source spans only for diagnostics.

Markdown often permits partially recoverable content. Define clearly which parse conditions produce a candidate with warnings and which produce InvalidExternalState.

docs.title: render.rs
docs.text:
Implement deterministic rendering from canonical/domain Markdown semantics plus exact MarkdownStyle.

Requirements:

  • headings/section nesting render deterministically;
  • block ordering follows canonical collection order;
  • style controls only approved formatting choices;
  • tables render deterministically for the supported table model;
  • code blocks preserve semantic language/info string/content;
  • links preserve target and label semantics;
  • final newline follows style;
  • same semantic input/style/renderer version produces identical bytes.

Implement the sr-projection render side of the Markdown adapter.

Do not render by patching the old file. Generate from semantic state.

docs.title: equivalence.rs
docs.text:
Implement semantic-equivalence comparison for supported candidate/canonical structures.

It must identify formatting-only differences such as supported list marker/spacing choices while still detecting changes to semantic block structure or content.

Use this layer later to return NoSemanticChange before migration generation.

Do not treat all syntactic differences as formatting. Preserve the domain boundary from Level 2.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
diagnostic.rs should convert parser/render domain failures into structured Markdown diagnostics that can be embedded in generic projection diagnostics.

Include source span where available but do not make it canonical identity.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Create representative fixtures inline or under tests/fixtures/ if that makes tests clearer.

Cover at least:

  • document with nested headings/paragraphs;
  • unordered and ordered lists;
  • table with rows/cells;
  • fenced code block;
  • block quote;
  • links;
  • parse -> semantic/candidate -> render -> parse semantic equivalence;
  • two style configurations render differently but parse as semantically equivalent where expected;
  • whitespace/list-marker-only change is equivalent;
  • paragraph text change is not equivalent;
  • heading structure change is not equivalent;
  • line/source positions do not appear in semantic equality/identity.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-markdown --test round_trip
cargo test -p sr-markdown
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not assign canonical entity IDs during parsing.
  • Do not implement migration generation.
  • Do not implement filesystem watchers.
  • Do not preserve formatting by storing the original entire file as canonical data.
  • Do not add agent/CLI/server/web dependencies.
  • Do not normalize author-significant document structure just for prettier output.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Supported Markdown semantic model exists.
  • [x] Candidate model is distinct from canonical identity.
  • [x] Parser handles required constructs.
  • [x] Renderer is deterministic.
  • [x] Style changes representation without changing semantics.
  • [x] Semantic equivalence distinguishes formatting-only from meaningful changes.
  • [x] Round-trip tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

This document records the completed scaffold baseline; later APIs are not speculative additions to this task.

Create the runtime-facing Rust crates prescribed by:
