docs.title: Implement Domain Schema and Adapter Version Metadata
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the version/provenance metadata needed to distinguish domain schema evolution from adapter implementation evolution, as required by design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md.

A schema version defines what stored domain knowledge means. An adapter version/profile defines how an external representation or tool maps to that schema. These must not be conflated.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md
  2. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  3. current schema, provenance, and derived-knowledge APIs
  4. design/level-3/010. implement domain capability discovery.md

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Prefer shared metadata types in scriberig-schema and shared provenance types in the crate that already owns provenance/derived metadata.

Expected files are equivalent to:

crates/scriberig-schema/src/version.rs
crates/scriberig-schema/src/domain.rs
crates/scriberig-schema/src/lib.rs

and, only if needed by the established architecture:

<shared provenance crate>/src/producer.rs
<shared provenance crate>/src/profile.rs

Do not create a new cross-cutting crate solely for two version structs if an existing owner is clear.

docs.title: Schema Version
docs.text:
Provide an explicit, serializable domain schema version identifier.

It must be suitable for answering:

which schema defines the meaning of this canonical domain revision?

Requirements:

  • stable across process runs;
  • transport-safe;
  • comparable for equality;
  • independent of Rust crate version unless the project explicitly aliases them;
  • included in domain descriptors/registration.

Do not assume semantic-version ordering alone is sufficient to migrate data. Migration support remains explicit.

docs.title: Adapter/Producer Identity
docs.text:
Provide metadata capable of identifying a producer/adapter independently from the schema.

At minimum represent:

adapter/producer identifier
adapter version
optional profile/configuration identifier

Examples include:

Markdown parser adapter
Rust syntax parser adapter
Rust compiler analyzer
PDF extractor

The same schema version may be served by multiple adapter versions or entirely different adapters.

docs.title: Provenance Integration
docs.text:
Derived results created by adapters/analyzers must be able to record:

producer identity
producer version
producer profile/configuration identifier where interpretation depends on it
exact semantic input revisions/dependencies

Do not force credentials, machine-local absolute paths, secrets, or volatile timestamps into reusable producer-profile identity.

Configuration identity should include only values that affect interpretation/result semantics.

docs.title: Canonical Import Metadata
docs.text:
Where imported canonical knowledge depends on the adapter's interpretation, preserve enough import provenance to know which adapter mapped the external source into the schema.

Do not make adapter metadata itself part of an entity's semantic content unless the domain explicitly requires that producer identity to distinguish canonical meaning.

The common case should keep semantic state and provenance related but distinct.

docs.title: Schema Migration Boundary
docs.text:
Provide types/metadata sufficient to distinguish:

ordinary user-content migration

from:

domain schema migration

Do not implement a full schema migration engine in this task unless one already exists and only needs these metadata hooks.

A future schema migration must be able to state:

from schema version
to schema version
migration implementation/profile
input snapshot/scope
result snapshot/scope

docs.title: Capability Discovery Integration
docs.text:
Update domain capability descriptors so clients can observe:

current installed schema version
provider/adapter versions for advertised capabilities where relevant

Do not expose implementation details that are not needed by clients.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests proving:

  • schema version and adapter version are distinct types/fields;
  • two adapters can target the same schema version;
  • one adapter can evolve versions while the schema remains unchanged;
  • derived output provenance records adapter version/profile;
  • domain descriptor exposes schema version;
  • capability provider metadata can expose adapter version;
  • schema migration metadata distinguishes schema transitions from ordinary content migrations;
  • serialization is deterministic/stable according to project conventions.

Run formatting/tests/clippy for affected crates.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not equate schema version with Cargo package version automatically.
  • Do not make every adapter update force a schema migration.
  • Do not put secrets into producer/profile metadata.
  • Do not implement automatic schema migration heuristics.
  • Do not make provenance disappear when derived data is cached.
  • Do not depend on agent crates.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Schema version is explicit and transport-safe.
  • [x] Adapter/producer identity and version are separate from schema version.
  • [x] Derived provenance can record producer/profile metadata.
  • [x] Capability discovery exposes appropriate version metadata.
  • [x] Schema migration metadata is distinguishable from content migration metadata.
  • [x] No secrets or volatile local details contaminate reusable identity.
  • [x] Tests, formatting, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement: Markdown Node Matching and Semantic Reconciliation
Objective
docs.text:
Implement deterministic Markdown node matching and reconciliation in sr-markdown so an edited Markdown candidate can be mapped back onto existing canonical entities without hidden IDs and converted into a semantic migration proposal.

This task handles the common single-base case where the current canonical state still equals the synchronization base. Three-way concurrent reconciliation is the next task.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
  2. design/level-2/009. markdown editable projection adapter.md
  3. design/level-3/011. implement markdown model parser renderer and style.md
  4. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md
  5. the public sr-change APIs implemented in the repository.

docs.title: Files to create/modify
docs.text:
crates/sr-markdown/src/match_nodes.rs
crates/sr-markdown/src/reconcile.rs
crates/sr-markdown/src/diagnostic.rs
crates/sr-markdown/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-markdown/tests/reconcile.rs

Modify model/candidate helpers only where required by reconciliation.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
The reconciler receives:

  • exact synchronization-base snapshot/semantic scope;
  • current canonical state, which for this task must equal the base for the target scope;
  • parsed CandidateDocument;
  • projection specification and Markdown adapter configuration.

If current canonical state differs from base, return/route to an explicit three-way-required result rather than pretending this task resolved concurrency.

docs.title: Matching phases
docs.text:
Implement deterministic matching in passes. Keep evidence/results inspectable for diagnostics.

Recommended order:

  1. exact subtree/content equality within corresponding structural context;
  2. exact same-kind content match;
  3. heading/section name plus parent-context match;
  4. ordered sibling sequence alignment using already matched anchors;
  5. neighboring unchanged anchors;
  6. conservative same-kind text similarity only where one best candidate is clearly distinguishable.

Do not use one global fuzzy match across the whole document.

Prefer local structural context.

docs.title: Match result model
docs.text:
For each candidate semantic node, represent at least:

Matched(existing EntityId, evidence)
New
Ambiguous(possible matches, evidence)

Also track canonical entities in the projected semantic surface that were not matched, so removals/structural changes can be proposed deliberately.

Do not mark a canonical entity deleted merely because the Markdown projection does not represent unrelated relations/metadata.

docs.title: Duplicate-content safety
docs.text:
Explicitly test duplicate paragraphs/list items.

If two canonical candidates remain equally plausible after structural context and anchors, produce Ambiguous.

Do not choose the first by hash-map iteration or source position alone.

Stable identity correctness is more important than reducing the number of new entities.

docs.title: Content update semantics
docs.text:
When a candidate matches an existing entity but projected canonical properties changed:

  • keep the same EntityId;
  • create/propose a new immutable revision containing only the semantic dimensions owned by Markdown;
  • preserve canonical fields/relations outside the projection surface;
  • record an entity delta/operation through sr-change.

A line/column change alone must never create a new revision.

docs.title: Insert semantics
docs.text:
For an unmatched candidate that clearly belongs in a projected collection:

  • create a new semantic entity through the normal graph/change construction APIs;
  • create its initial revision;
  • update the parent collection structure;
  • do not recreate unchanged siblings.

docs.title: Remove semantics
docs.text:
If an existing projected child is absent from the candidate and the Markdown projection owns that child collection, propose removal from that collection.

Do not automatically delete the entity globally if it may still be referenced elsewhere; follow the universal graph/change semantics for entity removal versus relation/collection removal.

docs.title: Reorder/move semantics
docs.text:
If the same child entities are present but order changes, propose a collection-order/structure change rather than delete-and-recreate.

If a block moves between sections and identity continuity is justified, preserve the block entity and update collection membership/structure.

Do not let projected line numbers define a move.

docs.title: Formatting-only no-op
docs.text:
Call semantic equivalence before producing revisions/migrations where possible.

If candidate semantics equal canonical projected semantics:

ReconciliationOutcome::NoSemanticChange

No migration/entity revision should be created.

docs.title: Migration proposal
docs.text:
Use sr-change rather than implementing a separate migration type.

The proposal should identify:

  • base snapshot;
  • affected entity deltas;
  • generic collection/relation operations where available;
  • provenance source as external projection;
  • projection reference/path as structured provenance metadata;
  • domain-specific Markdown operation details only through supported extension mechanisms.

Do not promote/commit the migration inside the pure reconciler.

docs.title: Preserving unrepresented knowledge
docs.text:
When replacing a paragraph revision due to changed text, retain all canonical fields/relations that Markdown does not own.

Add a test where a paragraph has an extra provenance/citation/custom relation not represented in Markdown; editing text must not remove that relation.

docs.title: Ambiguity diagnostics
docs.text:
Return structured Markdown reconciliation diagnostics containing:

  • candidate local node/path;
  • node kind;
  • possible existing EntityId matches;
  • evidence/scores/categories used;
  • containing section/collection;
  • suggested safe action if known.

Do not expose only a string.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Cover at least:

  • edit one paragraph: same entity, new revision;
  • insert paragraph between two unchanged paragraphs: neighbors reused, one new entity, parent structure changes;
  • remove paragraph from projected section without deleting unrelated knowledge;
  • reorder paragraphs: identities retained, collection order changes;
  • move a paragraph between sections when anchors make identity clear;
  • formatting-only input returns no semantic migration;
  • exact duplicate paragraphs with insufficient context return ambiguity;
  • changed heading keeps section identity when evidence is sufficient;
  • inserting a heading creates new section entity;
  • unrelated canonical relations survive projected text edit;
  • parser source spans never enter migration identity.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-markdown --test reconcile
cargo test -p sr-markdown
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not perform three-way merge when current differs from base.
  • Do not commit/promote migrations.
  • Do not resolve ambiguity with an LLM.
  • Do not use hidden IDs inserted into Markdown.
  • Do not rebuild the whole canonical document from the candidate.
  • Do not discard relations not represented in Markdown.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Deterministic staged matching exists.
  • [x] Exact identity is preserved where justified.
  • [x] Ambiguity remains structured.
  • [x] Content and structural changes become different operations/deltas.
  • [x] Formatting-only changes produce no migration.
  • [x] Unrepresented knowledge survives.
  • [x] Tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement Rust-specific reconciliation that compares an existing canonical Rust syntax graph with newly parsed externally edited Rust source and produces shared semantic migration/change operations.

This task is the reverse-editing half of the Rust syntax adapter. It must preserve stable conceptual identity when the evidence is strong and report ambiguity when it is not.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
  2. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  3. design/level-3/005. implement language independent code domain.md
  4. design/level-3/006. implement rust syntax domain adapter.md
  5. current public APIs in scriberig-migration and scriberig-projection

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Inside crates/domains/rust/, create or update:

src/lib.rs
src/reconcile.rs
src/match_syntax.rs
src/change.rs
src/error.rs

Add tests under:

tests/reconcile.rs

Reuse the Rust parser and canonical syntax mapping from Task 006. Do not parse through a second syntax implementation.

docs.title: Inputs and Output
docs.text:
The reconciliation layer must accept conceptually:

base canonical Rust semantic state
newly parsed candidate Rust semantic state

and return:

shared semantic migration/change proposal
identity matches/reuse information
ambiguities/conflicts

It must not commit persistence directly.

docs.title: Matching Strategy
docs.text:
Use deterministic structural evidence first.

For declarations/functions/types, use signals such as:

exact semantic subtree equality
kind/declaration type
name
signature/parameter structure
containing module/impl context
sibling/declaration order
body similarity
attributes

For statements/expressions, use:

exact subtree equality
matched parent context
sibling sequence alignment
syntax kind
semantic content similarity

For comments/code groups, use source grouping and matched surrounding syntax.

Line numbers and byte offsets may be tie-breaking metadata but must not be primary identity.

docs.title: Required First-Slice Changes
docs.text:
Support at least:

function body expression change
statement insertion
statement deletion
statement reorder within one block
parameter rename/change when continuity is unambiguous
function signature change
function insertion/deletion
function move within the same module when detectable
comment edit/insertion/deletion
code-group boundary changes caused by source grouping

Preserve unchanged child entities wherever possible.

Changing one expression must not force unrelated sibling functions to become new conceptual entities.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Changing:

let result = a + b;

to:

let result = a * b;

must produce a semantic change at the relevant expression path while reusing unchanged surrounding function/module entities as conceptual identities according to the shared revision model.

Do not represent this as replacing the entire source file.

docs.title: Rename vs Delete/Create
docs.text:
When a local binding, parameter, or declaration changes name, preserve conceptual continuity only when structural/context evidence makes the match strong.

Do not infer a rename merely because one old name disappeared and one new name appeared.

If matching is ambiguous, return explicit ambiguity and let a higher layer decide whether to treat the candidate as new entities or request resolution.

docs.title: Moves
docs.text:
A source entity may move without semantically changing.

For a confidently detected move:

  • preserve the conceptual entity;
  • update collection/containment structure through shared migration operations;
  • do not rewrite the entity merely because its line/file coordinates changed.

Cross-file/module moves may be deferred unless the projection orchestration already provides both affected modules as one reconciliation scope.

docs.title: Formatting-Only Changes
docs.text:
Changes only to formatting/style must not create semantic source revisions when parsing maps both versions to the same canonical syntax.

Add tests for:

indentation changes
line wrapping
spacing around operators
brace/formatting changes that do not change chosen syntax semantics

Use canonical parse structure, not textual diff, to decide this.

docs.title: Macro Safety
docs.text:
Macros and token trees may be difficult to reconcile structurally.

For unsupported or ambiguous macro-internal changes:

  • preserve the macro invocation as the smallest safe replacement unit;
  • do not pretend individual expanded compiler nodes are stable source entities;
  • return ambiguity rather than inventing continuity inside opaque token structures.

A future task may add more precise macro reconciliation.

docs.title: Migration Output
docs.text:
Map Rust changes onto shared migration operations.

Do not create a Rust-only history representation.

The output must be usable by generic validation/branch/snapshot code.

The adapter may attach domain-specific explanation metadata to operations where the shared migration model supports it.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Cover at least:

  1. unchanged source -> no semantic migration;
  2. expression operator change -> local semantic change;
  3. statement insert/delete/move -> structural operations with unchanged siblings reused;
  4. function signature edit -> function continuity where unambiguous;
  5. formatting-only edit -> no semantic change;
  6. function reorder -> move/reorder rather than delete/create where unambiguous;
  7. comment edit -> comment revision/change without unrelated AST churn;
  8. ambiguous similar functions/declarations -> explicit ambiguity;
  9. macro token change -> safe macro-level replacement or explicit ambiguity;
  10. unrelated functions retain identity across one-function edit.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-domain-rust
cargo clippy -p scriberig-domain-rust --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not reconcile by textual line diff alone.
  • Do not use line numbers as semantic identity.
  • Do not replace the whole module/file for every local edit.
  • Do not inspect compiler-expanded macro AST as if it were canonical source identity.
  • Do not silently guess ambiguous renames/moves.
  • Do not call an LLM.
  • Do not commit snapshots directly.
  • Do not create Rust-specific migration storage.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Rust reconciliation compares canonical syntax to parsed candidate syntax.
  • [x] Unchanged entities are reused.
  • [x] Local syntax changes stay local where possible.
  • [x] Moves/reorders are structural changes rather than text replacements.
  • [x] Formatting-only changes do not produce semantic churn.
  • [x] Ambiguous matches are explicit.
  • [x] Macro handling is conservative and safe.
  • [x] Output uses shared migration abstractions.
  • [x] Tests, formatting, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement: Three-Way Markdown Synchronization and Conflicts
Objective
docs.text:
Extend Markdown/file synchronization to the normal concurrent case where canonical state changed after the last synchronized file was rendered.

Implement semantic three-way reconciliation using:

B = synchronization base
D = current canonical state
F = externally edited Markdown

The result must merge disjoint semantic changes automatically and return structured conflicts for incompatible overlapping changes.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
  2. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md
  3. design/level-2/008. filesystem projection synchronization.md
  4. design/level-2/009. markdown editable projection adapter.md
  5. design/level-3/010. implement filesystem observation synchronization and recovery.md
  6. design/level-3/012. implement markdown node matching and semantic reconciliation.md

Inspect and reuse the existing sr-change three-way merge/conflict APIs. Extend generic interfaces only if necessary; do not create a Markdown-only history system.

docs.title: Files to modify
docs.text:
Primarily:

crates/sr-markdown/src/reconcile.rs
crates/sr-markdown/src/match_nodes.rs
crates/sr-markdown/src/diagnostic.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/sync.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/recovery.rs
crates/sr-markdown/tests/reconcile.rs
crates/sr-markdown/tests/file_sync.rs

Create a dedicated Markdown merge helper module only if the domain-specific logic would otherwise obscure reconcile.rs.

docs.title: Three-way preparation
docs.text:
For an externally changed file:

  1. parse F into a candidate;
  2. reconstruct/read the exact semantic scope from synchronization base B;
  3. reconcile candidate against B to derive the external semantic intent B -> F_semantic;
  4. obtain canonical change B -> D using sr-change/snapshot diff;
  5. combine both changes through generic merge first;
  6. invoke Markdown-specific resolution only for conflicts that require document semantics.

Do not match F directly against only D because that loses the edit base and can misinterpret concurrent movement/changes.

docs.title: Automatic merge rules
docs.text:
At minimum automatically merge:

  • canonical change to entity A plus external change to unrelated entity B;
  • canonical text change to paragraph P1 plus external insertion P3 in a different collection/location when structurally independent;
  • both sides producing the same resulting revision;
  • independent insertions at non-competing collection positions;
  • style/formatting-only external change plus semantic canonical change;
  • path/projection-location-only change when domain semantics say location is non-semantic.

docs.title: Conflict cases
docs.text:
Return structured conflicts for at least:

  • both sides changing the same paragraph text differently;
  • one side removing a projected entity while the other modifies it;
  • competing incompatible reorder/collection edits;
  • ambiguous identity matching that prevents safe external intent construction;
  • incompatible heading/section restructuring;
  • external edit based on a synchronization base that is no longer retrievable.

Use the universal sr-change conflict object as the authoritative base/result conflict model. Add Markdown domain detail through its extension/domain-detail mechanism.

docs.title: Conflict detail
docs.text:
Markdown conflict detail should be able to expose:

  • affected semantic entity/collection;
  • base revision;
  • canonical/current revision;
  • external candidate/proposed revision;
  • candidate source span for presentation only;
  • operation kind: text update, insertion, removal, move, restructure, ambiguity;
  • possible resolutions when deterministic alternatives are known.

Do not write conflict marker text into the canonical Markdown document as the conflict representation.

docs.title: Formatting-only external edit during canonical change
docs.text:
If the external file differs from B only by presentation but D contains semantic changes:

  • do not generate an external semantic migration;
  • render D using configured style;
  • write result;
  • advance synchronization base to D after successful write.

Add an explicit test for this path.

docs.title: Successful merge path
docs.text:
If merge succeeds:

B + D + F
    -> merged migration/result snapshot M
    -> validate Markdown result
    -> promote through normal change/root rules
    -> deterministic Markdown render
    -> atomic file write
    -> synchronization base = promoted snapshot

Do not advance synchronization base until promotion and rerender/write succeed.

If promotion fails because the target root changed again, restart reconciliation from the preserved external input/new current state rather than silently overwriting.

docs.title: Failed/conflicted path
docs.text:
On conflict:

  • preserve last valid canonical root;
  • preserve original synchronization base;
  • preserve external digest/content access;
  • set projection state to conflict/attention-required;
  • store structured conflict diagnostics;
  • do not normalize/rewrite the external file unless policy explicitly requests a preview/alternate output;
  • allow retry after canonical or external state changes.

docs.title: Stale base handling
docs.text:
If B was garbage-collected or cannot be resolved, do not guess a two-way merge.

Return a structured MissingSynchronizationBase/equivalent error requiring user/system policy to re-establish a baseline or perform a consciously lossy import.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Before promotion of merged state:

  • validate universal schema invariants;
  • validate Markdown domain structure;
  • render resulting Markdown;
  • parse rendered Markdown;
  • verify semantic equivalence for the supported projection surface.

Validation failure leaves current canonical state unchanged.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Cover at least:

  • canonical modifies P1, external inserts P3 elsewhere -> merge succeeds;
  • canonical inserts one paragraph, external inserts another at independent location -> merge succeeds;
  • both change P1 to same semantic text -> converges;
  • both change P1 differently -> structured conflict;
  • canonical removes P1, external modifies P1 -> delete/modify conflict;
  • canonical semantic change plus external formatting-only change -> no external semantic delta and canonical change renders successfully;
  • competing section reorder -> structured collection conflict;
  • ambiguous external duplicate matching -> conflict/ambiguity preserved;
  • promotion race after reconciliation -> no overwrite; retry required;
  • missing synchronization base -> explicit error;
  • successful merge rerenders and establishes new base.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-markdown --test reconcile
cargo test -p sr-markdown --test file_sync
cargo test -p sr-projection-fs
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not replace current canonical state with parsed file content.
  • Do not use textual Git-style conflict markers as canonical conflict state.
  • Do not advance the base before successful promotion/rerender.
  • Do not silently two-way merge when B is missing.
  • Do not let filesystem layer invent Markdown conflict semantics.
  • Do not add agent-assisted conflict resolution in this task.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] B/D/F flow is explicit in code.
  • [x] Disjoint changes merge automatically.
  • [x] Same-entity incompatible changes return structured conflicts.
  • [x] Formatting-only external change does not create semantic history.
  • [x] Failed/stale cases preserve recoverable state.
  • [x] Successful merges rerender and establish a new synchronization base.
  • [x] Tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the first remote-capable vertical slice: inspect one entity through the shared application operation, server adapter, protocol contract, and reusable Rust client.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md
  2. design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md
  3. design/level-3/012. implement application operation primitives.md
  4. design/level-3/013. implement protocol contract and schema export.md

This task must prove that remote use preserves the same semantics as embedded use.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Implement only enough transport/runtime behavior for:

inspect entity
runtime capabilities
operation status

Do not implement the whole API surface.

Start with an in-process transport abstraction and server dispatcher so behavior is testable without binding a TCP port. If the repository already has an approved HTTP framework design, add the HTTP adapter behind the same transport-neutral dispatch boundary; otherwise do not choose a framework here.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
crates/scriberig-server/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-server/src/server.rs
crates/scriberig-server/src/transport.rs
crates/scriberig-server/src/dispatch.rs
crates/scriberig-server/src/operation.rs
crates/scriberig-server/src/subscription.rs

docs.title: Client
docs.text:
crates/scriberig-client/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-client/src/client.rs
crates/scriberig-client/src/transport.rs
crates/scriberig-client/src/operation.rs
crates/scriberig-client/src/subscription.rs

Update the two crate manifests only with dependencies required by the chosen in-process transport and asynchronous/synchronous boundary already established by the repository.

docs.title: Server Application Interface
docs.text:
scriberig-server must receive an application service/trait/object through construction.

Do not instantiate the persistence backend inside request dispatch.

The server dispatcher should conceptually perform:

decode protocol request
-> validate protocol compatibility
-> construct application request context
-> invoke application operation
-> map application result/error to protocol form
-> return response

Mapping code belongs in the server adapter or a small explicit conversion module if needed.

Do not make scriberig-protocol depend on app types to avoid mapping work.

docs.title: dispatch.rs
docs.text:
Implement dispatch for the initial requests:

InspectEntityRequest
RuntimeCapabilitiesRequest
OperationStatusRequest

Each request must return a typed protocol response or typed protocol error.

No database query should appear directly in this module.

No semantic diff, migration, or graph traversal algorithm should be implemented here.

docs.title: transport.rs on the Server
docs.text:
Define a small transport-facing boundary that can accept a protocol request and produce a protocol response.

For the first task provide an in-process implementation suitable for tests.

It should preserve:

  • request/correlation identity;
  • protocol version checks;
  • structured errors.

Do not expose private server structs through the public client API.

docs.title: client.rs
docs.text:
Expose semantic client methods for the initial capabilities.

Required methods/concepts:

inspect(...)
capabilities(...)
operation_status(...)

The client constructs protocol requests, sends them through its Transport, decodes the typed response, and returns structured errors.

Do not require callers to know endpoint names or serialization details.

docs.title: Client transport.rs
docs.text:
Define a client transport trait/interface that is independent of the semantic methods.

Provide an in-process transport implementation that points at the server dispatcher for tests.

The purpose is to establish the boundary that a later HTTP/WebSocket implementation can satisfy without changing client semantics.

Avoid generic abstractions beyond what the initial requests need.

docs.title: Operation and Subscription Modules
docs.text:
For this task:

  • operation.rs should wrap polling/querying operation status through the client;
  • subscription.rs may define the minimal interface needed by later event streaming but must not invent a network streaming protocol if none is designed yet;
  • server operation.rs may adapt the application operation registry/status provider;
  • server subscription.rs may remain a documented minimal abstraction until event streaming is implemented.

Do not create fake streaming just to populate these modules.

docs.title: Protocol Compatibility
docs.text:
The transport path must check protocol major version before executing semantic operations.

Unsupported major versions return a structured protocol error.

The check belongs above semantic application logic.

docs.title: Snapshot Preservation
docs.text:
The inspect request must support an explicit snapshot.

The remote result must report the same resolved revision and snapshot as direct application-layer inspection against the same test world.

Do not replace exact snapshot identity with "latest" during transport mapping.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add server/client integration tests that use the in-process transport.

Required cases:

  1. inspect a known entity at a known snapshot;
  2. inspect a missing entity and verify structured NotFound category;
  3. request an unsupported protocol major version;
  4. retrieve runtime capabilities;
  5. compare direct application inspect result with client/server inspect result for semantic equivalence.

Do not compare terminal formatting strings.

No external network access is allowed in tests.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not access SQLite directly from server code.
  • Do not duplicate inspect semantics in dispatch.rs.
  • Do not make client depend on server internals.
  • Do not add CLI/TUI code.
  • Do not implement agent execution.
  • Do not choose an HTTP framework unless already prescribed by another accepted design.
  • Do not broaden the task to every command/query.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-server
cargo test -p scriberig-client
cargo check --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Server and client source modules exist.
  • [x] Server receives application semantics through a public boundary.
  • [x] Initial requests dispatch without direct persistence access.
  • [x] Client exposes semantic methods rather than raw transport construction.
  • [x] In-process transport proves the remote boundary without network dependency.
  • [x] Protocol major-version mismatch returns a structured error.
  • [x] Snapshot/revision identity survives the round trip exactly.
  • [x] Direct and remote inspect results are semantically equivalent.
  • [x] No server business-logic fork was introduced.
  • [x] Tests and workspace checks pass.

docs.title: Implement Universal Query Handles, Scope, and Pagination
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the foundational data types in scriberig-query required by the universal query and operation model.

This task creates semantic handles, selection/anchor types, explicit query scope, opaque pagination, and progressive-detail vocabulary. It does not implement graph traversal, search execution, the structured query AST, application operations, protocol serialization, or UI behavior.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md
  2. design/level-2/010. universal query and operation implementation.md
  3. design/level-2/001. workspace and package layout.md
  4. the identity/revision/snapshot implementation design
  5. the universal knowledge-model Rust library design

Inspect the workspace before editing.

Use the canonical scriberig-core, scriberig-graph, and scriberig-query crates already present. If scriberig-query has not yet been scaffolded by prerequisite workspace work, create that crate at the path prescribed by the workspace design and register it in the workspace. Do not create a differently named duplicate query crate.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Within crates/scriberig-query/:

Cargo.toml
src/lib.rs
src/handle.rs
src/scope.rs
src/pagination.rs
src/detail.rs

If these files already exist, extend them instead of creating parallel modules.

Do not edit protocol, server, CLI, TUI, agent-runtime, or web packages.

docs.title: 1. Reuse Existing Identity Types
docs.text:
Import the existing canonical identifiers rather than redefining them.

Use the established equivalents of:

EntityId
RevisionId
SnapshotId
RelationTypeId
CollectionTypeId
ProjectionId

If one optional identifier such as ProjectionId is owned by another crate not yet available, isolate that dependency behind a small generic/opaque reference instead of inventing a competing global ID type.

The query crate must not own hashing or identifier generation.

docs.title: 2. Implement Semantic Handle Types
docs.text:
In src/handle.rs, implement lightweight public types for the semantic targets needed by queries.

Required concepts:

EntityRef
RevisionRef
SnapshotRef
RelationRef
CollectionRef
ProjectionRef
OperationRef

Prefer newtypes or small structs/enums that preserve type distinction.

Do not collapse all identifiers to String.

Provide an exact entity/revision target equivalent to:

EntityAtRevision {
    entity: EntityId,
    revision: RevisionId,
}

Provide a snapshot-relative entity target equivalent to:

EntityInSnapshot {
    entity: EntityId,
    snapshot: SnapshotId,
}

A unified TargetRef enum is allowed if it makes APIs simpler, but exact revision and snapshot-relative meanings must remain distinguishable.

Add sensible traits such as Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, and Hash where the wrapped canonical identifiers support them honestly.

docs.title: 3. Implement Relation Paths and Selection
docs.text:
Add a semantic relation-path representation suitable for recording context inside a graph without turning physical storage paths into identity.

A relation-path step should be able to identify a typed relation or collection traversal.

Implement Selection with conceptual fields equivalent to:

snapshot: SnapshotId
entity: EntityId
revision: Option<RevisionId>
relation_path: Vec<RelationStep>
projection_anchor: Option<ProjectionAnchor>

Keep ProjectionAnchor transport/UI neutral.

A safe first implementation is an enum or tagged structure that can represent opaque anchor data such as:

TextRange
PageRegion
Opaque { kind, value }

Do not import DOM, terminal, editor, or browser types.

Document clearly that projection anchors are convenience mappings, not canonical identity.

docs.title: 4. Implement Query Scope
docs.text:
In src/scope.rs, implement an explicit QueryScope or equivalent.

It must support at least:

Snapshot(SnapshotId)
Entity {
    snapshot: SnapshotId,
    entity: EntityId,
}
ExplicitEntities {
    snapshot: SnapshotId,
    entities: Vec<EntityId>,
}

If the graph layer already defines a subtree/container abstraction, reuse it rather than duplicate it.

Every scope variant must identify one exact snapshot.

Do not add a Current variant inside the query crate. Resolving “current” to an exact snapshot is an application-layer responsibility.

Add helper methods for retrieving the bound SnapshotId.

docs.title: 5. Implement Opaque Pagination
docs.text:
In src/pagination.rs, implement:

PageRequest
ContinuationToken
Page<T>

Requirements:

  • PageRequest includes a bounded limit and optional continuation.
  • Choose a conservative default and maximum limit, but keep constants easy to change.
  • Reject zero or obviously unreasonable limits through a constructor/validation method instead of relying on every caller.
  • ContinuationToken is opaque to callers.
  • Do not expose SQL offsets, row IDs, or backend cursor fields in the public type.
  • Page<T> carries items and optional next continuation.

A token may internally wrap bytes or a string in the first version.

Do not promise that tokens remain valid across different snapshots. Document that continuation belongs to the operation/snapshot context that produced it.

docs.title: 6. Implement Progressive Detail
docs.text:
In src/detail.rs, implement a small universal detail enum equivalent to:

Identity
Compact
Structure
Full

Keep this universal.

Do not add variants such as CodeGroups, PdfLayout, or SessionTurns; those are domain views/capabilities.

Add an optional InformationCost structure capable of expressing coarse estimates such as:

items
bytes
approx_tokens

All fields may be optional.

Information cost is advisory only; do not use it for authorization or correctness.

docs.title: 7. Public Exports
docs.text:
Update src/lib.rs to expose stable public paths for the implemented types.

The crate should allow downstream code to import the common types without reaching into private implementation details.

Avoid a giant prelude if the project does not already use that pattern.

docs.title: 8. Tests
docs.text:
Add focused unit tests in the module files or an appropriate crate test file covering:

  1. exact revision and snapshot-relative targets remain distinguishable;
  2. a Selection can represent semantic-only selection with no projection anchor;
  3. a Selection can carry a projection anchor without changing entity/revision identity;
  4. every QueryScope exposes one exact SnapshotId;
  5. explicit entity-set scope preserves entity order only if the API promises order; otherwise document/order-normalize appropriately;
  6. pagination rejects invalid limits;
  7. Page<T> carries a continuation independently of item content;
  8. continuation token internals are not exposed through public fields;
  9. progressive detail values remain domain-independent;
  10. information-cost fields are optional.

Run:

cargo test -p scriberig-query
cargo check --workspace

If workspace prerequisites are incomplete, run the narrowest available checks and report the exact unmet prerequisite.

docs.title: 9. Non-Goals
docs.text:
Do not implement:

  • inspect, list, follow, find, or query execution;
  • SQL/index lookups;
  • diff/history/render;
  • branch/apply/commit;
  • HTTP/JSON schemas;
  • CLI parsing;
  • React selection state;
  • agent tools.

docs.title: Completion Criteria
docs.text:
This task is complete when:

  • scriberig-query has reusable semantic handle types;
  • exact revision versus snapshot-relative entity targeting is explicit;
  • semantic selections can carry optional projection anchors;
  • every query scope is bound to one exact snapshot;
  • pagination is bounded and storage-independent;
  • progressive detail and optional information-cost hints exist;
  • public docs explain the identity and snapshot semantics;
  • unit tests pass without requiring a database backend.

docs.title: Implement Inspect, List, and Follow Read Operations
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the universal orientation and traversal contracts in scriberig-query.

This task adds inspect, list, and follow request/result types and the read-service boundary that resolves them against exact snapshots. It must preserve progressive disclosure, semantic handles, typed relation/collection meaning, and bounded traversal.

This task does not implement search, the structured query AST, application-layer composition, transport schemas, or write operations.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md
  2. design/level-2/010. universal query and operation implementation.md
  3. design/level-3/015. implement universal query handles scope and pagination.md
  4. the universal knowledge-model Rust library design and graph implementation tasks
  5. domain capability/schema designs already present

Inspect the existing scriberig-query, scriberig-graph, and scriberig-schema public APIs before choosing exact method names.

Reuse existing graph-view abstractions. Do not query SQLite directly from this crate.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Within crates/scriberig-query/:

src/lib.rs
src/inspect.rs
src/traverse.rs
src/result.rs
src/error.rs

tests/universal_read_model.rs

Modify Cargo.toml only if a dependency on an already-established workspace crate is required.

Do not create storage-backend code.

docs.title: 1. Inspection Request
docs.text:
In src/inspect.rs, implement an InspectRequest or equivalent containing:

target
resolved snapshot or exact revision context
detail level
optional requested view

Do not support an unresolved Current snapshot in this crate.

If the target is only an EntityId, require a snapshot-bound target type from the previous task.

docs.title: 2. Inspection Result
docs.text:
Implement an Inspection result capable of representing the Level 1 orientation data without forcing every field to exist.

Required conceptual fields:

subject handle
snapshot
revision
entity type
short label/title
short description
important properties
counts
relation capabilities
collection capabilities
view capabilities
operation capabilities
provenance summary
information cost

Use reusable domain-neutral property/value types already owned by core/graph libraries.

Do not encode rich domain objects as arbitrary JSON strings.

Keep the default result compact. A full semantic revision body should be returned only for an explicit full-detail request or domain view.

docs.title: 3. Capability Descriptors Used by Inspection
docs.text:
If scriberig-app capability descriptors do not exist yet, define only the read-side capability metadata needed here in a way that can later be reused/re-exported by the application layer.

At minimum distinguish:

relation
collection
view
operation

Each descriptor should include a stable identifier and short description.

Where schema data exists, include target type/cardinality/ordering/canonical-vs-derived metadata without hard-coding domain names.

Do not implement execution of high-level operations in this task.

docs.title: 4. List Request and Result
docs.text:
In src/traverse.rs, implement ListRequest or equivalent.

It must specify:

snapshot-bound subject
collection identifier
PageRequest
detail level for entries

Implement a compact NavigationEntry containing at least:

semantic handle
entity type
short label/description
optional compact metadata/count

Implement ListResult containing:

subject
snapshot
collection identity
Page<NavigationEntry>

Collection order must be preserved when the schema says the collection is ordered.

Do not sort semantic collections merely for display convenience.

docs.title: 5. Follow Request and Result
docs.text:
Implement FollowRequest or equivalent with:

snapshot-bound subject
relation identifier
direction if supported
PageRequest
detail level for entries

Implement FollowResult containing:

subject
snapshot
relation identity
relation metadata
Page<NavigationEntry>

Preserve typed relation meaning.

Do not return generic unlabeled graph edges when a relation type is known.

If reverse traversal is unavailable because no index/derived provider exists, return UnsupportedCapability or DerivedDataUnavailable as appropriate rather than scanning hidden storage structures or fabricating reverse edges.

docs.title: 6. Read Service Trait
docs.text:
Expose a transport-independent service trait or small set of traits covering:

inspect
list
follow

Choose async versus sync consistently with existing project conventions. Do not introduce an async runtime dependency merely for hypothetical future networking.

The service implementation should depend on graph/schema/store-facing traits rather than one concrete backend.

The service must resolve each operation entirely within the request's exact snapshot.

docs.title: 7. Snapshot Resolution Rules
docs.text:
For snapshot-relative targets:

EntityInSnapshot(E, S)

resolve E -> Revision once for S and use that exact result throughout the operation.

For exact revision targets:

EntityAtRevision(E, R)

use R directly for local revision content.

If surrounding traversal requires collection/relation membership, require or retain a snapshot context rather than guessing current state.

A query must not start in one snapshot and finish against a newer named root.

docs.title: 8. Structured Errors
docs.text:
In src/error.rs, add or extend semantic errors required by these operations:

NotFound
InvalidTarget
WrongType
UnsupportedCapability
SnapshotUnavailable
DerivedDataUnavailable
InvalidContinuation
Internal

Errors should carry the operation kind and relevant subject/snapshot/relation/collection handles when useful.

Do not expose raw database-driver error strings as the public API.

docs.title: 9. Unknown and Partially Adapted Entities
docs.text:
inspect must succeed for entities that have only generic graph/schema metadata whenever possible.

For an unsupported blob-like entity, an inspection may expose:

type
size/metadata if known
available generic relations
available raw projection/view if registered

It must not claim domain capabilities that are unavailable.

This behavior is important for forward-compatible domain adapters.

docs.title: 10. Tests
docs.text:
Extend tests/universal_read_model.rs using memory/test-double graph data.

Cover at least:

  1. inspect resolves an entity against the exact requested snapshot;
  2. newer snapshots do not alter a completed inspection result;
  3. default inspection is compact and advertises deeper capabilities;
  4. ordered collections preserve order;
  5. unordered collections are not accidentally given semantic order guarantees;
  6. list respects page limits and continuation;
  7. follow returns typed relation identity and semantic handles;
  8. reverse traversal unavailable from the provider returns a structured capability/derived-data error;
  9. handles from list can be passed directly to inspect;
  10. unknown entity types remain generically inspectable;
  11. full content is not required merely to list children;
  12. invalid collection/relation identifiers produce structured errors.

Run:

cargo test -p scriberig-query
cargo check --workspace

docs.title: 11. Non-Goals
docs.text:
Do not implement:

  • text/semantic find;
  • the query AST/executor;
  • semantic diff or history engines;
  • render/projection execution;
  • branch/apply/commit;
  • HTTP or CLI adapters;
  • agent tools;
  • domain-specific operations such as rename_symbol.

docs.title: Completion Criteria
docs.text:
This task is complete when:

  • inspect, list, and follow have reusable Rust contracts;
  • every operation is bound to one exact snapshot/revision context;
  • inspection advertises useful next relations/collections/views/operations;
  • list/follow results are compact, semantic, and pageable;
  • typed relation/collection meaning is preserved;
  • unsupported capabilities and derived-data absence are structured failures;
  • no concrete database backend or product surface is required.

docs.title: Required Repository Guidance

docs.title: Required Source Conventions
docs.text:
The root guidance must require:

  • source files no longer than 400 lines after excluding the leading preamble;
  • Markdown and prose/text files exempt from that size limit;
  • same-stem directory/module splitting as a preferred oversized-file strategy;
  • a file-level description in every source file;
  • documentation for every public or private function and method;
  • parameter, return, and error documentation where applicable;
  • class/class-like documentation including member documentation;
  • a one- or two-line plain intent comment for each logical code block, placed after declaration documentation; in Rust, keep it directly adjacent to /// comments with no blank line.

The conventions must apply to tooling code as well as product/library code.

docs.text:

Rust:                    4 spaces

Prettier must be the formatter for supported web source files.

Rustfmt must be the formatter for Rust source files.

docs.title: Required Automation
docs.text:

tools/lint_repo.py
tools/repo_lint/
tools/fix.sh
tools/check.sh
tools/install-hooks.sh
.pre-commit-config.yaml
.github/workflows/quality.yml

The custom linter should automatically fix safe deterministic violations where practical and produce precise diagnostics for violations that require manual judgment.

The linter implementation must obey the same 400-line source rule rather than exempting itself.

docs.title: Pre-Commit Formatting

The web formatting hook must format staged JavaScript/TypeScript source with Prettier --write and re-stage only those exact files.

The hook must not format or stage unrelated workspace files.

CI remains verification-only and uses a non-mutating formatting check.

docs.title: Bootstrap Ratatui Terminal Runtime and Shell
docs.text: Status: [x] Implemented

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Replace the documentation-only scriberig-tui crate with the smallest real terminal runtime that can safely enter/leave terminal mode and render a responsive Scriberig shell without performing semantic work inside rendering.

This task implements the terminal foundation from:

  1. design/level-1/015. terminal user interface principles.md;
  2. design/level-2/021. terminal ui runtime and state architecture.md;
  3. design/level-2/022. terminal ui views interaction and conformance.md.

Do not wire srig tui to a database in this task. Product composition is a later task.

docs.title: Required Dependencies
docs.text:
Add Ratatui and a compatible Crossterm dependency arrangement to crates/scriberig-tui/Cargo.toml.

Keep one compatible Crossterm line in the resolved dependency graph. Prefer workspace dependency declarations if the repository already centralizes versions by the time this task is implemented.

Do not add SQLite, server, HTTP, agent-provider, or domain-parser dependencies to the TUI crate.

docs.title: Target Modules
docs.text:
Create an initial structure equivalent to:

crates/scriberig-tui/src/
├── lib.rs
├── runtime.rs
├── terminal.rs
├── event.rs
├── state.rs
├── layout.rs
└── render.rs

Additional focused modules are allowed if needed to remain under the repository source-file size limit.

Every Rust file/function/type must follow the repository documentation/comment conventions from Level 2 document 020.

docs.title: Terminal Guard
docs.text:
Implement a terminal lifecycle wrapper that owns setup and restoration.

It must support the equivalents of:

raw mode on/off
alternate screen enter/leave
cursor hide/show where appropriate
bracketed paste enable/disable when supported
optional mouse capture kept disabled by default initially

Restoration must be attempted for normal exit and event-loop error paths.

Install a panic-restoration strategy that composes with the previous panic hook rather than swallowing it.

Keep the guard concerned only with terminal state. It must not own application/store cleanup.

docs.title: Event Types
docs.text:
Define TUI-level terminal events independent of view semantics, at minimum:

Key(...)
Paste(String)
Resize { width, height }
Tick
Shutdown

Translate Crossterm events at the terminal/event boundary. Do not expose raw Crossterm event types throughout view state.

Ignore unsupported terminal events safely.

docs.title: Initial State
docs.text:
Create a minimal TuiState containing only presentation/runtime state needed by this task, such as:

should_quit
terminal_size
focus
shell_message

Do not add fake entity/snapshot data to make the shell look populated.

The shell may state that no semantic service is attached in this task's test harness.

docs.title: Responsive Shell
docs.text:
Implement the layout classes defined by Level 2:

>= 120 columns -> explorer + primary + inspector
80..119       -> explorer + primary
< 80          -> primary only

Render a context bar, body region, status region, and key-hint row.

At very small sizes render a clear small-terminal message while keeping quit/help key handling possible.

Resize must not panic.

docs.title: Rendering Rules
docs.text:
render functions take state and a Ratatui frame/rectangle only.

They must not:

  • open files;
  • call application services;
  • wait on channels;
  • query the database;
  • mutate semantic state.

Keep frame rendering deterministic from state.

docs.title: Runtime Loop
docs.text:
Implement a minimal runtime loop that:

  1. initializes the terminal guard;
  2. draws the initial state;
  3. waits for terminal events without busy-spinning;
  4. updates local state;
  5. redraws only when state/size requires it;
  6. exits on the local quit action;
  7. restores terminal state.

This task may keep event/action handling simple. The full action/reducer/effect architecture is task 100.

docs.title: Test Support
docs.text:
Use Ratatui's TestBackend or equivalent in-memory backend to test the shell without touching the developer's real terminal.

Add focused tests for at least:

140x40 wide layout
100x30 medium layout
72x24 narrow layout
very small terminal guard rendering
resize state change
quit event

Terminal lifecycle tests should abstract terminal commands so tests do not leave CI runners in raw mode.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
Do not implement in this task:

  • application queries;
  • semantic selection;
  • command palette;
  • history/diff/projection views;
  • sessions or agents;
  • SQLite composition;
  • remote mode;
  • capability matrix changes claiming semantic TUI support.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run the repository Rust formatting/check/lint path and the TUI crate tests. At minimum the implementation must pass the equivalents of:

cargo fmt --check
cargo check -p scriberig-tui
cargo clippy -p scriberig-tui --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p scriberig-tui

Use the repository's current tools/check.sh when it covers these checks.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Ratatui/Crossterm dependencies are added without duplicate incompatible terminal backends.
  • [x] Terminal setup and restoration are owned by one focused wrapper.
  • [x] Panic/error paths attempt terminal restoration.
  • [x] Crossterm input is translated into TUI-level events.
  • [x] The shell renders all required responsive width classes.
  • [x] Rendering performs no semantic I/O.
  • [x] The runtime does not busy-spin when idle.
  • [x] TestBackend coverage exists for representative terminal sizes.
  • [x] The crate passes formatting, check, Clippy, and tests.

docs.title: Implement TUI Actions, Reducer, Navigation, and Keymap
docs.text: Status: [x] Implemented

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Replace ad-hoc event handling from the bootstrap slice with the stable TUI interaction core: typed actions, a pure reducer, navigation history, focus, overlays, and a data-driven keymap.

Read first:

  1. design/level-2/021. terminal ui runtime and state architecture.md;
  2. design/level-2/022. terminal ui views interaction and conformance.md;
  3. design/level-3/099. bootstrap ratatui terminal runtime and shell.md.

This task is presentation-only. It must not invent semantic application behavior.

docs.title: Target Modules
docs.text:
Add or complete modules equivalent to:

src/action.rs
src/effect.rs
src/selection.rs
src/navigation.rs
src/keymap.rs
src/state.rs
src/overlay/mod.rs
src/overlay/help.rs
src/overlay/palette.rs
src/overlay/input.rs

Keep rendering modules dependent on state/view models, not on service implementations.

docs.title: Action Model
docs.text:
Define typed actions for local interaction and future service results. The initial set must cover concepts equivalent to:

QuitRequested
OverlayClosed
FocusNext
FocusPrevious
CursorMoved
Activated
Back
Forward
RefreshRequested
HelpOpened
PaletteOpened
FindOpened
InputChanged
InputSubmitted
TerminalResized

Leave semantic result actions extensible for later tasks.

Do not use string command names as the reducer's primary internal dispatch mechanism.

docs.title: Reducer Contract
docs.text:
Implement one deterministic update boundary equivalent to:

reduce(state, action) -> Vec<Effect>

or a result that contains next_state + effects.

Reducer responsibilities include:

  • changing focus;
  • changing local cursor/scroll state;
  • opening/closing overlays;
  • updating navigation stacks;
  • recording local input;
  • requesting effects without executing them.

The reducer must not call scriberig-app, filesystem APIs, or terminal APIs.

docs.title: Navigation State
docs.text:
Implement back/forward navigation locations that can eventually carry:

semantic selection
primary view kind
snapshot/branch context
optional comparison target

For this task, define the stable structure even if only empty/no-selection locations are exercised.

Rules:

  • pushing a new location clears forward history;
  • back/forward does not mutate canonical state;
  • pane focus changes do not create semantic history entries;
  • resize does not change history;
  • cursor indexes are presentation state, not semantic identity.

docs.title: Keymap
docs.text:
Represent bindings as data mapping key chords + interaction context to action identifiers.

Implement the default Level 2 bindings for at least:

Ctrl-C
Esc
Tab
Shift-Tab
Enter
arrow keys
Backspace
:
/
?
r
q

Optional h/j/k/l aliases may be included for ordinary browse mode.

Text-input mode must consume printable keys as text rather than triggering browse commands.

Paste must arrive as one input-data event, not as a replay of command keystrokes.

docs.title: Help and Key Hints
docs.text:
Generate the help overlay and contextual key-hint labels from the same keymap/action metadata.

Do not duplicate a manually maintained help table that can drift away from actual bindings.

The help overlay must be reachable from every non-fatal state and closable without changing semantic navigation.

docs.title: Command Palette Foundation
docs.text:
Create the palette state/model with two future action sources:

local presentation actions
semantic contextual actions

Implement filtering and selection for local actions in this task.

Semantic actions may remain empty until task 101 attaches the service/capability model.

Palette filtering may be simple case-insensitive substring matching initially. Keep the filtering function isolated so ranking can evolve later.

docs.title: Effects
docs.text:
Define an Effect enum or equivalent boundary now even if most effects are local placeholders.

At minimum distinguish:

NoEffect / none
RequestRefresh
RequestFind { text }
RequestSemanticAction { id, inputs }
RequestQuit

The runtime executes effects outside the reducer. Later tasks expand effect variants with typed application operations.

docs.title: Rendering Updates
docs.text:
Update the shell so focused regions, overlays, and key hints are visibly represented by more than color alone.

A focus marker, border label, prefix, or equivalent textual cue is required.

Do not make mouse support a prerequisite.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add reducer/keymap tests for at least:

  • focus cycling;
  • overlay precedence/close behavior;
  • text input not triggering global printable-key actions;
  • paste treated as input data;
  • navigation push/back/forward invariants;
  • forward history cleared after a new activation;
  • resize preserving navigation;
  • help/key hints derived from actual bindings;
  • palette filtering local actions;
  • quit request from browse mode.

Use pure tests where possible; do not require a real terminal.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
Do not implement:

  • database/application adapters;
  • real entity rows;
  • capability discovery;
  • semantic action execution;
  • history/diff/projection data loading;
  • session/agent behavior;
  • remote connections.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Typed TUI actions exist.
  • [x] State transitions are centralized through a deterministic reducer/update boundary.
  • [x] Semantic/presentation effects are represented separately from state reduction.
  • [x] Navigation history and pane focus are independent.
  • [x] Default keyboard navigation is implemented.
  • [x] Text input and paste do not trigger browse commands.
  • [x] Help and key hints derive from the keymap metadata.
  • [x] Command palette filtering works for local actions.
  • [x] Reducer/keymap tests cover the required invariants.
  • [x] Formatting, check, Clippy, and TUI tests pass.

docs.title: Implement TUI Application Adapter, Explorer, and Inspector
docs.text: Status: [x] Implemented

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Make the TUI semantically useful for the first time by attaching it to public scriberig-app query/capability contracts and implementing semantic selection, progressive explorer navigation, and entity inspection.

This is the first TUI slice that may advance capability-matrix entries from planned to implemented.

Read first:

  1. design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md;
  2. design/level-2/012. capability matrix and cross surface conformance.md;
  3. design/level-2/021. terminal ui runtime and state architecture.md;
  4. design/level-2/022. terminal ui views interaction and conformance.md;
  5. tasks 099 and 100.

docs.title: Service Boundary
docs.text:
Create src/service.rs with a TUI-facing adapter/port over public application services.

The adapter must expose semantic operations needed by this task without leaking storage internals. At minimum support the currently available equivalents of:

inspect entity/reference
runtime/context capabilities

Add list/follow/find only when matching public application operations exist. If they do not yet exist, keep their UI affordances unavailable rather than querying lower crates directly.

Preserve structured application errors and explicit ApplicationContext.

Do not open SQLite or construct the concrete store inside scriberig-tui.

docs.title: Semantic Selection
docs.text:
Implement a stable selection model backed by public Scriberig references/identifiers.

For the first slice, entity selection must distinguish:

conceptual EntityId
exact RevisionId when returned
SnapshotId/context when returned or requested

Rows and navigation locations store semantic references, not display-row indexes.

A cursor index may identify which visible row is focused, but activation uses the row's stored reference.

docs.title: Request/Result State
docs.text:
Expand Effect and result actions for typed semantic requests.

Use request/generation identifiers so a late inspect result cannot replace a newer selection's inspector.

Represent view loading explicitly:

NotRequested
Loading
Ready
Failed

When a refresh fails after prior success, retaining prior data is allowed only when visibly marked stale.

docs.title: Inspector View Model
docs.text:
Create a TUI-specific inspector view model derived from public application results.

It should contain only presentation-ready data/references such as:

entity id
revision id
snapshot context
kind/schema summary
short description
important public properties
provenance/trust summary
available next operations/capabilities

Do not copy private application/domain structs wholesale into TUI state if a small public projection suffices.

Exact identifiers must be available through an inspect/details action even when compact display shortens them.

docs.title: Explorer
docs.text:
Implement an explorer with semantic root/row models.

If public list/follow operations are not yet implemented, the first explorer may start from explicitly entered/go-to entity identifiers and maintain navigation history of inspected entities. It must not fake relation/collection trees.

When list/follow becomes available during implementation, support expandable rows using those operations and bounded/paginated result models.

Expansion state is keyed by stable semantic references.

docs.title: Go-To / Inspect Input
docs.text:
Add a palette action equivalent to Go to entity or Inspect entity.

Collect a valid EntityId through an input overlay, then produce the typed inspect effect.

Invalid identifiers stay in input state with a clear parse message; they must not reach application code as fabricated IDs.

Activation of a successful result pushes a semantic navigation location.

docs.title: Capability-Driven Palette
docs.text:
Attach shared runtime/context capability information to the palette.

At minimum:

  • inspect appears only when the application context permits it;
  • unavailable semantic actions are absent or visibly disabled according to the metadata available;
  • denial returned by the application is still handled even if the palette thought the action was available.

Do not infer authorization from local process ownership.

docs.title: Error and Trust Presentation
docs.text:
Map structured application error categories into safe presentation states.

Permission denial, not-found, unsupported operation, and internal failure must be distinguishable.

Show trust/provenance summary from public inspect results when available. Use text/symbols in addition to color.

Do not emit untrusted control characters directly to the terminal.

docs.title: Test Fixture
docs.text:
Use a deterministic in-memory/application fixture where possible. Do not make TUI crate tests depend on a developer SQLite database.

Test at least:

  • inspect success renders expected stable identifiers/summary;
  • exact revision and snapshot context are not conflated;
  • not-found/permission-denied produce distinct states;
  • stale late result does not replace a newer inspector request;
  • invalid entity input never calls the service;
  • semantic activation pushes navigation history;
  • capability absence prevents advertising the action;
  • rendered external text is sanitized for terminal control characters.

docs.title: Capability Matrix
docs.text:
Update capabilities.toml only for functionality that actually exists after this task.

Expected first progress is for capabilities equivalent to:

inspect_entity
runtime_capabilities

Use implemented, not verified, unless the repository conformance suite actually proves the TUI adapter semantics in this task.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
Do not implement:

  • direct database access in the TUI crate;
  • canonical mutations;
  • history/diff/projection views;
  • agent/session views;
  • remote client mode;
  • fake relation trees when list/follow application APIs are absent.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] TUI semantic I/O goes through a public application adapter/port.
  • [x] Stable semantic selection is stored separately from row cursor position.
  • [x] Inspect requests/results use typed effects/actions and stale-response protection.
  • [x] Inspector renders entity/revision/snapshot identity correctly.
  • [x] Explorer contains only semantic structures supported by shared operations.
  • [x] Go-to/inspect input validates identifiers.
  • [x] Palette semantic actions use shared capability information.
  • [x] Structured application errors have distinct safe presentation.
  • [x] TUI tests use deterministic fixtures rather than a developer database.
  • [x] Capability matrix status is updated honestly.
  • [x] Formatting, check, Clippy, and tests pass.

docs.title: Implement TUI History, Diff, Projection, and Change Review Views
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Extend semantic browsing beyond a single current entity by adding primary views for history, semantic diff, rendered projections, validation, conflicts, and reviewable changes using only shared application operations.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md;
  2. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md;
  3. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md;
  4. design/level-2/021. terminal ui runtime and state architecture.md;
  5. design/level-2/022. terminal ui views interaction and conformance.md;
  6. tasks 099 through 101.

This task is dependency-gated: implement only views whose public scriberig-app operations exist. If an operation is still missing, add it to the correct application/domain layer in its owning task before exposing it here. Do not bypass that layer from the TUI.

docs.title: Target Views
docs.text:
Add focused modules equivalent to:

src/view/history.rs
src/view/diff.rs
src/view/projection.rs
src/view/changes.rs

Each view consumes a small TUI view model built from public application results.

docs.title: History View
docs.text:
Use the shared history operation for the current semantic selection.

The view must show stable revision/snapshot references and useful descriptions/timestamps/provenance summaries when provided by the application result.

Activating a history row creates an exact historical selection. It must not silently resolve back to the current entity revision.

History loading must be bounded/paginated if the application contract supports or requires it.

docs.title: Diff View
docs.text:
Use the shared semantic diff operation.

The view header must keep both sides explicit:

left/base reference
right/target reference

Render structured change groups when returned by the application/domain layer. Text-oriented hunks may be displayed when they are part of a public diff/projection result, but the TUI must not compute semantic diff by comparing rendered strings.

Provide navigation among changed semantic objects using their stable references.

docs.title: Projection View
docs.text:
Render a projection through the shared projection/application operation.

Display, when available:

projection identity
source semantic reference
style identity
rendered content
synchronization state
last known base/reference needed for reconciliation

The first projection view may be read-only.

Do not open or write projection files directly from the widget. External-edit/reconcile behavior remains an application/projection operation.

Sanitize terminal control characters in rendered projection text before drawing it.

docs.title: Change and Validation Review
docs.text:
Add a review view for migration/change/validation results.

The view must make visible:

base snapshot or branch
proposed target/change identity
affected semantic objects
conflicts
validation state/diagnostics
trust/provenance summary where relevant
state-changing action that will be invoked

Canonical application is never performed merely by opening the view.

A confirm action invokes the existing shared application command with the explicit reviewed base/context.

If the application reports a stale base or conflict after confirmation, retain the proposal/result and show the failure. Do not silently rebase and retry.

docs.title: Confirmation Overlay
docs.text:
Implement the modal confirmation/review behavior needed by state-changing operations.

The overlay must show at least:

action label
semantic target
base snapshot/branch when relevant
short risk/change summary
explicit confirm and cancel keys

Confirmation only expresses user intent. Capability checks and semantic validation remain authoritative in scriberig-app.

docs.title: View Switching
docs.text:
Add local palette actions for switching among supported primary views without losing semantic selection:

overview
history
diff
projection
changes/validation

When a view requires additional context, such as a diff comparison target, collect it explicitly through input/selection state.

Switching views must not push duplicate semantic history entries unless the semantic location itself changes.

docs.title: Loading, Refresh, and Freshness
docs.text:
Each view uses explicit request/generation state.

Application events or successful canonical changes may mark related cached views stale. Refresh through shared operations rather than mutating cached rows in ways that pretend to be authoritative.

After a successful canonical change, navigate or refresh according to the result's returned semantic references/snapshot rather than assuming the target ID remained current.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add deterministic tests for at least:

  • exact historical revision activation;
  • diff header preserves both explicit sides;
  • diff rows link to stable semantic references;
  • projection control characters are rendered harmlessly;
  • view switching preserves selection;
  • confirmation does not itself perform a mutation;
  • confirmed command carries reviewed base context;
  • stale-base/conflict result is surfaced without automatic retry;
  • validation failure remains inspectable;
  • late results cannot overwrite a newer comparison/projection request.

Use fake/public application adapters rather than storage internals.

docs.title: Capability Matrix
docs.text:
Advance only capabilities genuinely implemented by this slice. Where conformance coverage exists, move to verified; otherwise use implemented.

Do not mark generic mutation support verified because one confirmation overlay exists.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
Do not add:

  • a terminal source-code editor;
  • TUI-specific merge semantics;
  • direct projection file writes;
  • direct migration application outside scriberig-app;
  • session/agent UI;
  • remote mode.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] History uses shared history semantics and exact revision references.
  • [x] Diff uses shared semantic diff results and keeps both sides explicit.
  • [x] Projection view uses shared rendering/projection operations.
  • [x] Change/validation review shows base, affected objects, conflicts, and diagnostics.
  • [x] Canonical actions require explicit user confirmation.
  • [x] Confirmed commands preserve reviewed base context.
  • [x] Stale/conflict failures are visible and are not automatically retried.
  • [x] Terminal control content is sanitized before rendering.
  • [x] Tests cover stale results, exact history, review, and confirmation behavior.
  • [x] Capability status is updated honestly.
  • [x] Formatting, check, Clippy, and tests pass.

docs.title: Implement TUI Sessions, Agent Interaction, and Operation Observation
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the TUI as an interactive observer/controller of the shared branch-aware agent runtime: session-tree navigation, nested branch inspection, agent input and continuation, operation progress, transient streaming, cancellation, result navigation, and promotion/review.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/009. agent interaction and sessions.md;
  2. design/level-1/016. model driven agent execution and branch isolation.md;
  3. design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md;
  4. design/level-2/021. terminal ui runtime and state architecture.md;
  5. design/level-2/022. terminal ui views interaction and conformance.md;
  6. design/level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md;
  7. design/level-3/111. expose agent execution through application protocol server and clients.md;
  8. tasks 099 through 102 and 107 through 111 as applicable.

This task must use public session/application/client agent boundaries. It must not call model providers directly from scriberig-tui and must not recreate branch orchestration in presentation code.

docs.title: Dependency Gate
docs.text:
Before implementing each workflow, confirm that shared layers expose the required public operations/results.

Expected concepts include:

AgentStartRequest / AgentStartResponse
