AgentContinueRequest / AgentContinueResponse
OperationId and shared lifecycle
operation cancellation
session/root branch references
branch tree and compact descriptors
branch activity pagination
BranchResult
AgentResult
agent/session event observation
stable semantic result handles

If a required semantic concept is missing, implement it in its owner under the applicable Level 2/3 task before adding a TUI-only substitute.

Do not invent:

terminal-only session storage
terminal-only operation states
terminal-only branch identities
terminal-only tool execution

docs.title: TUI Service Port
docs.text:
Extend the existing TUI service/effect boundary with concepts equivalent to:

StartAgent(AgentStartRequest)
ContinueAgent(AgentContinueRequest)
LoadSession(SessionRef)
LoadBranch(BranchRef)
LoadBranchChildren(BranchRef, page)
LoadBranchActivity(BranchRef, page)
LoadBranchResult(BranchResultRef)
ObserveOperation(OperationId)
CancelOperation(OperationId)

Use existing universal inspect/list/follow operations where they already cover session objects cleanly.

The same TUI state machine must work with:

embedded local adapter -> scriberig-app
remote adapter -> scriberig-client

No view/reducer behavior may depend on whether the model provider is local, remote, OpenAI-compatible, or fake.

docs.title: Session/Branch View Model
docs.text:
Represent the session as a real branch tree rather than a flat chat list.

A branch row/view model should contain bounded public information equivalent to:

BranchRef
parent/child relationship
short title/purpose
status
compact outcome
child count
activity count
BranchResultRef when terminal
important result/touched handles
running-operation marker when active

Do not load every branch activity item just to draw the tree.

Branch expansion triggers an explicit branch-child/activity load.

docs.title: Completed Branch Collapse
docs.text:
Completed child branches must default to a compact representation in the parent flow.

A compact branch card/row shows at least:

purpose
terminal status
outcome summary
result handles
expand affordance

Expanding the branch reveals retained activity:

human inputs
model outputs
structured tool calls/results
nested child branches
validation/result references

Collapsing a branch changes only presentation state. It must not delete or summarize-overwrite canonical session history.

This UI behavior should make the architectural context-collapse rule visible to users: parent work consumes the result, while full child provenance remains inspectable.

docs.title: Active Branches
docs.text:
Active/running branches should be distinguishable from completed/abandoned branches using text/symbols as well as color.

The tree may show bounded phase metadata such as:

thinking/model request
tool operation
waiting for child branch
validation
completing

These phases come from shared operation/events and are not durable branch lifecycle states invented by the TUI.

docs.title: Agent Composer
docs.text:
Provide an explicit input composer for starting or continuing agent work.

Requirements:

  • ordinary typed text;
  • pasted text remains data rather than command-key replay;
  • multiline content where supported;
  • visible target session and branch;
  • visible semantic scope/selection when present;
  • start-vs-continue behavior is explicit;
  • no provider credentials/configuration fields;
  • submission invokes StartAgent or ContinueAgent through the TUI service port;
  • returned OperationId, SessionRef, and RootBranchRef become observable state immediately.

The TUI never assembles provider messages/tool schemas itself.

docs.title: Universal Selection Binding
docs.text:
When the user starts agent work from a selected semantic object, construct the public agent request from the existing TUI semantic selection.

Preserve stable data equivalent to:

entity reference
optional exact revision
snapshot/branch context
projection location when public selection supports it

Do not reduce the scope to an informal filename/line-range prompt before it reaches the shared agent operation.

The composer should show a concise human-readable scope summary and provide a way to inspect the exact selection.

docs.title: Start
docs.text:
user enters prompt
-> StartAgent effect
-> start response returns operation/session/root branch
-> navigate/select root branch as appropriate
-> observe operation/events

docs.title: Continue
docs.text:
When a branch/session is selected and continuation is supported:

user enters follow-up
-> ContinueAgent effect
-> application decides direct continuation vs continuation child branch
-> returned operation/branch handles drive UI

Do not locally reopen a completed branch if shared branch policy says continuation creates a child/sibling branch.

docs.title: Operations View
docs.text:
Use the shared operation lifecycle:

queued
running
completed
failed
cancelled

Display when available:

OperationId
operation kind
session/root branch
current phase summary
active branch count/handles
progress counters
final AgentResult/BranchResult reference
structured failure

Completed result references must be activatable through ordinary semantic navigation.

Do not create an agent-only lifecycle that disagrees with the standard operation view.

docs.title: Event Integration
docs.text:
Feed agent/session events through the existing event -> action -> reducer path.

Handle concepts equivalent to:

BranchCreated
BranchStateChanged
ModelInvocationStarted
ModelTextDelta
ToolInvocationStarted
ToolInvocationCompleted
ChildBranchStarted
ChildBranchCompleted
BranchResultProduced
AgentOutputCommitted
AgentOperationCompleted/Failed/Cancelled

Events carry operation-local sequence/cursor metadata where available.

Out-of-order or duplicate transport events must not regress already newer local presentation state.

For durable objects, prefer event reference -> authoritative load/refresh rather than treating the whole event payload as canonical object state.

docs.title: Streaming Presentation
docs.text:
Maintain transient streaming buffers separately from durable session objects.

A stream buffer is keyed by operation/branch/invocation correlation and may contain partial model text.

Required rules:

  • deltas may render immediately;
  • deltas are labeled/inferred as in-progress;
  • AgentOutputCommitted or an authoritative branch reload replaces the transient buffer with durable output;
  • leaving a view does not cancel execution;
  • returning to the view resolves durable state rather than trusting retained fragments;
  • reconnect without stream replay still recovers from operation/session queries.

Do not insert every text delta into the canonical session view model as if it were a committed message.

docs.title: Branch Activity View
docs.text:
Opening a branch loads bounded/paginated activity using public handles.

Render semantically distinct rows for concepts such as:

HumanInput
ModelOutput / AgentOutput
ToolInvocation
ToolResult
child branch reference/result
Decision/Observation/Summary
Migration/Validation result reference

Tool rows should default to compact summaries and expose exact result handles for deeper inspection.

Do not dump unbounded raw provider JSON or raw tool payloads into the terminal.

docs.title: Nested Branch Navigation
docs.text:
A branch activity row pointing to a child branch/result must be activatable.

Navigation should support:

parent -> child branch
child -> nested child
child result -> semantic artifact
back -> previous semantic location

Branch depth must not be hard-coded into rendering logic. Use indentation/breadcrumb/compact tree strategies that remain usable at depth.

At narrow widths, preserve semantic hierarchy even if metadata columns collapse.

docs.title: Cancellation
docs.text:
Expose cancellation only when shared operation/capability state permits it.

Closing an overlay, navigating away, or pressing Esc to leave the current view is not equivalent to operation cancellation.

Cancellation flow:

user requests cancel
-> optional confirmation if appropriate
-> CancelOperation effect
-> show cancellation requested/pending
-> wait for shared terminal operation state

Do not optimistically mark the operation cancelled.

Ctrl-C behavior must compose with the TUI's global quit/cancel interaction policy and terminal-restoration guarantees.

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
Structured agent failures should remain inspectable after transient notifications disappear.

Render concise categories such as:

provider configuration/auth/transport/rate limit
capability denied
tool failure
child branch failure
validation failure
budget exceeded
cancelled
internal failure

Link to operation/branch result handles when safe.

Never show provider secret values, Authorization headers, or complete sensitive compiled context in ordinary diagnostics.

docs.title: Trust, Candidate Changes, and Promotion
docs.text:
When an agent branch produces candidate changes or durable knowledge eligible for promotion:

  • show result handles in branch/operation views;
  • invoke existing shared review/validation/change surfaces;
  • require the normal confirmation/capability path;
  • handle stale-base/conflict results explicitly.

The session view cannot directly mutate canonical state because a model completed successfully.

docs.title: Concurrent Navigation
docs.text:
Users must be able to inspect unrelated project/session knowledge while an operation continues.

The runtime state should retain active operation handles globally enough that:

  • status/progress remains visible;
  • the user can return to active branches;
  • completion can notify without stealing focus;
  • completion does not automatically navigate away from the user's current work unless explicitly configured.

Rendering/navigation remains responsive while model/network/tool work is pending.

docs.title: Local and Remote Mode
docs.text:
The TUI presentation/reducer must be shared between:

srig tui --db <PATH>       # local embedded service
srig tui --connect <URL>   # remote public client, once transport task exists

Provider configuration exists where the agent runtime is hosted:

  • local composition for embedded mode;
  • server composition for remote mode.

The TUI never needs provider credentials in either mode.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Use deterministic fake TUI services/agent operations. No external model provider or public network is allowed.

Cover at least:

  • nested branch tree renders with stable references;
  • completed branches default to compact result rows/cards;
  • expanding a child loads activity on demand;
  • collapsing does not alter canonical/session service data;
  • composer start request includes current semantic selection;
  • continue request targets the selected session/branch;
  • paste remains input data;
  • start response immediately tracks stable operation/session/root branch handles;
  • model deltas update only transient stream state;
  • durable output replaces transient buffer;
  • leaving the view does not cancel work;
  • cancellation waits for shared operation terminal state;
  • out-of-order/duplicate events do not regress state;
  • child result handle activates semantic navigation;
  • reconnect/reload can rebuild branch tree without stream history;
  • promotion routes through shared change review;
  • no provider configuration/credential type appears in TUI state/service API.

Use Ratatui test backend for representative branch tree/activity frames at wide, medium, and narrow sizes.

docs.title: Capability Matrix
docs.text:
Advance TUI capability states only when implementation and tests are real.

Relevant rows include:

agent_start
agent_continue
session_branch_tree
session_branch_activity
agent_event_subscription
agent_streaming_output
operation_status
operation_cancel
agent_final_result

Use verified only after TUI semantic/conformance tests pass.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Run at least:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-tui
cargo clippy -p scriberig-tui --all-targets -- -D warnings

Also run changed application/client/conformance tests for service integration.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
Do not add:

  • model-provider credentials to TUI configuration;
  • provider-specific APIs or DTOs in scriberig-tui;
  • terminal-only branch/session persistence;
  • a TUI-owned model/tool loop;
  • automatic promotion of model output;
  • direct canonical mutation from stream fragments;
  • a requirement to load complete child histories to render the parent branch tree.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] TUI service port starts/continues shared agent operations.
  • [x] Agent requests preserve the current stable semantic selection.
  • [x] Session view renders real nested branch structure.
  • [x] Completed child branches collapse to compact descriptors/results by default.
  • [x] Child activity loads on demand and supports nested navigation.
  • [x] Stable operation/session/root branch handles are tracked immediately after start.
  • [x] Streaming output remains transient until durable session output is committed.
  • [x] Users can navigate elsewhere while agent work continues.
  • [x] Cancellation uses shared operation lifecycle/capabilities.
  • [x] Durable result handles activate ordinary semantic navigation/review.
  • [x] Reconnection/reload recovers from authoritative operation/session state.
  • [x] Local and remote adapters share the same TUI state machine.
  • [x] No provider credentials or provider-specific request construction exists in TUI code.
  • [x] Capability matrix status is updated honestly.
  • [x] Formatting, tests, and Clippy pass.

docs.title: Wire srig tui to Local Application Composition
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Replace the existing honest srig tui stub with the real local embedded TUI while preserving the repository's composition boundaries.

Read first:

  1. design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md;
  2. design/level-2/020. repository scaffold conventions and native command surface.md;
  3. design/level-2/021. terminal ui runtime and state architecture.md;
  4. design/level-2/022. terminal ui views interaction and conformance.md;
  5. design/level-3/097. expose srig native command stubs.md;
  6. tasks 099 through 103 as applicable.

The key boundary is:

scriberig-cli parses TUI startup arguments, apps/scriberig constructs concrete local dependencies, and scriberig-tui owns interactive terminal behavior.

docs.title: CLI Arguments
docs.text:
Change the Tui command from a unit variant to a typed argument structure equivalent to:

srig tui --db <PATH>

Use the repository's current local-development database default consistently with other local native commands when practical.

Do not add storage opening or application construction to scriberig-cli.

The top-level command name remains exactly srig tui.

docs.title: Composition Root
docs.text:
In apps/scriberig/src/main.rs or a focused composition module if the file would become too large:

  1. receive parsed TUI args;
  2. open the selected concrete local store;
  3. construct the required scriberig-app services/adapters;
  4. create an explicit ApplicationContext/principal for local TUI use;
  5. grant only the capabilities appropriate for the current implemented TUI feature set/product policy;
  6. adapt the application service to the TUI service port;
  7. invoke the public scriberig_tui::run(...) entry point;
  8. propagate a safe error to the process boundary if startup/runtime fails.

The TUI crate itself must not import scriberig-store-sqlite just to make this wiring convenient.

docs.title: Principal and Capabilities
docs.text:
Use an explicit principal equivalent to:

local-tui

Do not equate local process access with unrestricted semantic authority.

Construct capability grants through the existing application capability model. Start with the least set required by implemented views/actions, for example inspect/read capabilities first.

When later tasks add mutations or agents, expand product grants deliberately rather than using an unrestricted catch-all grant.

docs.title: Startup Validation
docs.text:
Before entering raw/alternate-screen terminal mode, fail cleanly for startup problems that can be detected first, including:

invalid database path/configuration
store open failure
application construction failure
non-interactive terminal when interactive mode is required

Errors detected after terminal entry must still restore the terminal before surfacing process failure.

Do not print ordinary startup diagnostics on top of an active alternate-screen UI unless they are routed through the TUI status/error model.

docs.title: Process Exit Behavior
docs.text:
Normal user quit returns success.

Startup or unrecoverable runtime failure returns a non-zero process result through the existing executable error path.

User cancellation of an individual semantic operation is not automatically a process failure.

Do not call std::process::exit from deep inside scriberig-tui; allow RAII terminal restoration and normal error propagation.

docs.title: Existing Inspect Composition
docs.text:
The repository already constructs a SQLite store, ApplicationService, guarded query service, and explicit capability context for the inspect command.

Reuse composition helpers where doing so removes duplication without moving product composition into lower layers. If both inspect and TUI need the same local application construction, extract a focused helper under apps/scriberig or another appropriate composition-only module.

Do not make the CLI crate own the concrete store simply to share code.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add parser/composition tests where feasible for:

  • srig tui parses;
  • srig tui --db <PATH> parses;
  • invalid arguments are rejected by Clap;
  • TUI command no longer prints the old "not implemented" stub;
  • composition gives the TUI an explicit principal/capability context;
  • a fake/headless TUI entry can be invoked in tests without taking over the test runner's real terminal;
  • startup failure before terminal entry reports cleanly.

Do not make automated tests launch an uncontrolled interactive terminal.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Update native help/output and any repository command documentation that still describes srig tui as unimplemented.

Do not change the stable command spelling established by Level 2 document 020.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
Do not implement in this task:

  • remote --connect mode;
  • a server inside the TUI process;
  • automatic unrestricted capability grants;
  • direct SQLite usage from scriberig-tui;
  • provider-specific agent construction unless a separate owning composition task already defines it.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] srig tui starts the real local TUI instead of the stub message.
  • [x] --db is parsed in scriberig-cli and consumed by product composition.
  • [x] Concrete SQLite/store construction remains outside scriberig-tui.
  • [x] Local TUI uses an explicit application principal and capability context.
  • [x] Capability grants are no broader than required by implemented features.
  • [x] Detectable startup failures occur before terminal takeover when practical.
  • [x] Runtime failures restore terminal state before propagation.
  • [x] Normal quit returns success.
  • [x] Automated tests do not require an uncontrolled real terminal.
  • [x] Help/documentation no longer describes TUI mode as a stub.
  • [x] Formatting, check, Clippy, and relevant workspace tests pass.

docs.title: Add Remote TUI Mode Through scriberig-client
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Allow the same TUI state machine and views—including branch-aware agent/session workflows—to operate against a remote Scriberig server through the public scriberig-client/protocol boundary.

This task proves that the TUI is a peer product surface rather than a privileged local database or model-provider console.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md;
  2. design/level-1/015. terminal user interface principles.md;
  3. design/level-1/016. model driven agent execution and branch isolation.md;
  4. design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md;
  5. design/level-2/021. terminal ui runtime and state architecture.md;
  6. design/level-2/022. terminal ui views interaction and conformance.md;
  7. design/level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md;
  8. design/level-3/103. implement tui sessions agent interaction and operation observation.md;
  9. design/level-3/104. wire srig tui to local application composition.md;
  10. design/level-3/114. implement http protocol and event transport for remote clients.md.

This task is dependency-gated on a usable public client/server transport for the operations exposed by the TUI.

docs.title: Command Surface
docs.text:
Extend TUI startup with a mutually exclusive remote form equivalent to:

srig tui --connect <ENDPOINT>

The local form remains:

srig tui --db <PATH>

Define clear parser behavior when both local and remote selectors are supplied. Prefer a Clap argument group or equivalent parser-level mutual exclusion.

If neither is supplied, retain the documented local default unless product policy changes in a higher-level design.

The CLI crate parses endpoint text. It does not implement the client transport and does not accept model-provider credentials for remote mode.

docs.title: Remote Adapter
docs.text:
Add a remote implementation of the TUI service port using scriberig-client.

The adapter must preserve the same TUI-facing semantics as the embedded adapter for:

stable references
explicit snapshot/branch context
structured errors
capability discovery
operation IDs/status
operation cancellation
event observation
pagination/cursors
agent start/continue
session and nested branch queries
BranchResult / AgentResult navigation

Do not make views branch on HTTP status codes or protocol serialization details. Translate transport/protocol results at the adapter boundary.

Do not depend on scriberig-server internals.

The local and remote adapters should implement the same service trait/port expected by the TUI reducer/effect runner.

docs.title: Agent Execution in Remote Mode
docs.text:
Remote TUI agent work follows exactly the same public flow as local TUI work:

composer
-> AgentStartRequest / AgentContinueRequest
-> remote scriberig-client
-> server scriberig-app AgentService
-> server-hosted agent runtime/model provider
-> OperationId + SessionRef + BranchRef
-> protocol events/session queries back to TUI

The TUI must not:

connect directly to OpenAI-compatible endpoint
hold provider API key
serialize provider tool definitions
run a second local model loop while connected remotely

Provider configuration and secrets live on the server host in remote mode.

docs.title: Connection State
docs.text:
Add explicit connection presentation states equivalent to:

connecting
connected
reconnecting
disconnected
failed

Connection state is product/runtime state, not canonical semantic state.

A disconnected remote client may retain previously loaded view models as visibly stale. It must not present them as current or allow state-changing actions that require a live authority unless the shared client/application model explicitly supports queued/offline operations.

No offline mutation or offline agent queue is required by this task.

docs.title: Capability Discovery
docs.text:
After connection, obtain runtime/server capabilities through the public protocol/client path.

The command palette and view actions must use the same capability-driven behavior as local mode.

Agent-related capabilities include concepts equivalent to:

agent_start
agent_continue
session_branch_tree
session_branch_activity
agent_event_subscription
agent_streaming_output
operation_cancel

Do not enable an action in remote mode merely because it exists locally.

If the server/protocol/provider configuration cannot support a required operation, render it unavailable with a safe compatibility reason where the client contract provides one.

docs.title: Authentication and Secrets
docs.text:
Use only authentication mechanisms defined by the public client/server design at implementation time.

Do not invent provider credentials or persist secrets inside TUI view state.

Sensitive server-authentication values must not appear in debug/status messages, command history, snapshots, or rendered error details.

Provider API credentials never cross this boundary at all.

If interactive server credential entry is required, use a dedicated protected input flow defined by the client/auth design; do not implement ad-hoc secret persistence in this task.

docs.title: Events and Resume
docs.text:
Use the public client event-subscription mechanism implemented by the remote transport task.

Track the latest event cursor/sequence where the client exposes it.

On reconnect:

attempt resume from last cursor
-> if replay succeeds, reduce retained events
-> if cursor is too old/unavailable, mark affected views stale
-> query authoritative operation/session/branch state
-> subscribe from current cursor

Never infer that an agent operation stopped merely because the event connection dropped.

Transient model text may be lost across a disconnect. Durable AgentOutput, BranchResult, and AgentResult must recover through normal queries.

docs.title: Remote Branch Tree
docs.text:
The branch-tree behavior from task 103 must be unchanged in remote mode.

In particular:

  • completed child branches remain compact/collapsed by default;
  • expanding a branch loads child descriptors/activity through client queries;
  • full child history is not eagerly downloaded merely to draw the parent tree;
  • nested result handles navigate through the same TUI semantic navigation;
  • active operation markers come from shared status/events.

Network transport must not force a flat transcript presentation.

docs.title: Remote Streaming
docs.text:
Agent streaming events arrive as Scriberig protocol events, not provider-native SSE/JSON.

The remote adapter converts those events to the same TUI actions used by embedded mode.

Rules remain:

ModelTextDelta -> transient TUI stream buffer
AgentOutputCommitted -> authoritative session refresh/output
BranchResultProduced -> result handle/branch refresh
terminal operation event -> operation/result refresh

Do not persist remote stream fragments as a TUI-owned transcript.

docs.title: Cancellation
docs.text:
Remote cancellation calls the same public operation cancellation endpoint used by other clients.

The TUI shows cancellation as pending until the remote server reports terminal state.

Closing the connection, closing a view, or exiting a branch screen is not equivalent to cancellation.

If the entire TUI process exits while remote work continues, server product policy determines whether the operation remains running; client disconnect alone must not implicitly cancel unless explicitly defined by the operation contract.

docs.title: Transport Errors
docs.text:
Separate transport failures from semantic application/agent failures in presentation.

Examples:

transport unavailable / timeout / TLS / incompatible protocol
vs.
not found / permission denied / stale base / validation failure
vs.
provider authentication / rate limit / runtime budget failure returned safely by server

The remote adapter performs this mapping. Views consume the same TUI error model used by local mode where semantic categories match.

Provider diagnostics received from the server are already sanitized; the TUI must not attempt to reconstruct provider details.

docs.title: Pagination and Lazy Loading
docs.text:
Remote branch/session/object lists must preserve pagination/bounded loading.

Do not fetch:

all branches
all activity in every branch
all tool result bodies
all session history

when the current view needs only descriptors or one selected page.

The same progressive-disclosure behavior required for model context should also keep remote UI bandwidth bounded.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Use localhost/in-process deterministic server/client test infrastructure. Do not require public network or model access.

Cover at least:

  • parser rejects simultaneous --db and --connect;
  • same inspect fixture produces equivalent semantic TUI model in local and remote adapters;
  • same deterministic agent_start returns equivalent operation/session/root branch state locally and remotely;
  • nested child branch tree/result appears equivalently through both adapters;
  • remote capability absence disables the same action path;
  • transport failure is distinct from semantic/provider-safe failure;
  • disconnect marks cached state stale but does not mark operation cancelled;
  • recent event cursor reconnect resumes when supported;
  • too-old cursor causes authoritative operation/session refresh;
  • lost text deltas do not prevent durable final result recovery;
  • remote cancellation uses shared operation lifecycle;
  • secrets/auth material are not included in formatted TUI errors;
  • provider credential fields do not exist in remote TUI service state;
  • remote adapter does not depend on server private modules.

docs.title: Conformance
docs.text:
Compare local-TUI and remote-TUI adapter semantics using the deterministic agent conformance fixtures from task 115 when available.

Compare semantic references/result fields, not terminal cell snapshots.

Advance TUI capability entries to verified only when both local and remote paths required by that capability are actually tested according to the capability matrix policy.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Run relevant checks including:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-client
cargo test -p scriberig-tui
cargo test -p scriberig-cli
cargo clippy -p scriberig-client -p scriberig-tui -p scriberig-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings

Run server/conformance tests needed by the remote fixture as well.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
Do not implement:

  • offline canonical mutations;
  • offline agent execution while disconnected;
  • a private TUI-only protocol;
  • direct server-internal calls;
  • direct model-provider calls/credentials;
  • automatic credential persistence;
  • a separate remote-only view hierarchy;
  • eager download of entire session/branch histories.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] srig tui --connect <ENDPOINT> is parsed as a remote mode.
  • [x] Local and remote selectors are mutually exclusive.
  • [x] Remote access uses scriberig-client, not server internals.
  • [x] The existing state machine/views work through the remote service adapter.
  • [x] Remote agent start/continue use the same public operation as local mode.
  • [x] Nested branch tree/result behavior is equivalent in local and remote mode.
  • [x] Connection and stale-state status are visible.
  • [x] Remote capabilities drive semantic/agent action availability.
  • [x] Transport, semantic, and sanitized runtime/provider failures remain distinguishable.
  • [x] Event resume or authoritative refresh handles reconnect safely.
  • [x] Lost streaming fragments do not prevent final durable result recovery.
  • [x] Remote cancellation uses shared operation semantics.
  • [x] Provider credentials are absent from TUI/client state.
  • [x] Tests run without external network/model dependencies.
  • [x] Conformance status is advanced only when verified.
  • [x] Formatting, tests, and Clippy pass.

docs.title: Verify TUI Conformance, Accessibility, and Terminal Recovery
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Complete the first TUI design suite by proving that terminal behavior is robust, semantic behavior conforms to shared operations, responsive layouts remain usable, and failure paths restore the user's terminal.

This is a verification/hardening task, not an excuse to introduce new semantic behavior.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/015. terminal user interface principles.md;
  2. design/level-2/012. capability matrix and cross surface conformance.md;
  3. design/level-2/021. terminal ui runtime and state architecture.md;
  4. design/level-2/022. terminal ui views interaction and conformance.md;
  5. tasks 099 through 105 that are applicable/complete when this task runs.

docs.title: Test Layers
docs.text:
Ensure the repository has coverage at four distinct layers:

pure reducer/keymap tests
Ratatui TestBackend rendering tests
TUI service-adapter semantic tests
cross-surface conformance tests

Do not replace semantic tests with screenshots, and do not replace rendering tests with semantic adapter assertions. Each layer catches a different class of defect.

docs.title: Cross-Surface Conformance
docs.text:
Extend scriberig-conformance or its current equivalent so TUI-invoked operations can be compared without launching an interactive terminal and without scraping ANSI/cell output.

For every TUI capability marked verified, compare the TUI adapter/result model against the authoritative application semantics using the same deterministic fixture.

At minimum verify currently implemented equivalents of:

inspect_entity
runtime_capabilities
operation_status         when implemented
operation_cancel         when implemented
event_subscription       when implemented

For history/diff/mutation/session capabilities, add conformance cases only when their shared operation contracts and TUI adapters exist.

Update capabilities.toml so verified means a real test proves the path.

docs.title: Rendering Matrix
docs.text:
Use deterministic rendering tests for at least:

140x40 wide
100x30 medium
72x24 narrow
minimum-size guard case

Cover representative states:

empty/loading
successful inspect
structured error
permission denied
stale data
history/diff or another secondary view when implemented
modal command palette
confirmation/review
running operation when implemented

Assert important labels/regions and focus state rather than relying only on brittle full-frame snapshots.

A small number of full-frame golden assertions are acceptable for shell regressions.

docs.title: Accessibility Checks
docs.text:
Tests/review must verify:

  • every core workflow is keyboard reachable;
  • focus is represented by text/symbol/border semantics, not color alone;
  • validation/conflict/error/permission states have textual or symbolic meaning;
  • no-color or limited-color rendering remains understandable;
  • help can be opened from normal interactive states;
  • command palette exposes contextual actions discoverably;
  • mouse support, if present, is optional;
  • Unicode decoration is not necessary to understand semantic status.

If the theme implementation supports a no-color mode, include it in rendering tests. Otherwise make style-free semantic markers directly testable.

docs.title: Terminal Recovery Tests
docs.text:
Abstract terminal command execution enough to test the lifecycle state machine without taking over the CI terminal.

Verify attempted restoration after:

normal user quit
runtime loop error
render error
input/event error
panic restoration hook path where safely testable
partial startup failure after raw mode but before full initialization

Restoration expectations include the supported equivalents of:

leave alternate screen
disable bracketed paste
disable mouse capture if enabled
show cursor
disable raw mode

Test idempotent/drop behavior so an explicit exit followed by Drop does not produce an invalid state transition.

Do not write a test that can leave the developer shell in raw mode when it fails.

docs.title: Input Safety Tests
docs.text:
Add cases for untrusted/pasted strings containing:

ESC
CSI/control sequences
newlines/tabs
very long lines
invalid/edge Unicode sequences representable in Rust strings

Verify that application/projection/session text cannot inject terminal control behavior through ordinary rendering.

Paste must remain input data and must not execute palette/global key commands.

Where the terminal backend provides bracketed-paste events, test the TUI translation rather than manually splitting the text into key events.

docs.title: Resize and State Preservation
docs.text:
Exercise transitions among width classes while state is populated:

wide -> medium -> narrow -> wide

Verify preservation of:

semantic selection
navigation back/forward stack
active primary view
open data/view models
operation observation state

Presentation-only cursor/scroll state may be adjusted when a pane disappears, but it must remain safe and deterministic.

No resize path may panic on zero-sized intermediate rectangles.

docs.title: Responsiveness and Bounded Work
docs.text:
Add deterministic tests or instrumentation proving that:

  • drawing does not call the semantic service;
  • a static UI does not busy-spin continuously;
  • large list rendering processes only the bounded/visible model supplied to it;
  • stale service responses do not overwrite newer requests;
  • event bursts do not create unbounded duplicate refresh work for the same visible target where coalescing is implemented.

Do not use fragile wall-clock microbenchmarks as the only evidence. Prefer counters/fakes that make forbidden work observable.

docs.title: Error Hygiene
docs.text:
Review and test that user-visible/internal error formatting does not expose:

raw SQL
private backend row identifiers
secrets/authentication values
Rust debug dumps as product output
untrusted ANSI/control sequences

Semantic error categories and safe diagnostics should remain visible.

docs.title: Repository Quality Gate
docs.text:
Run the full repository checks required by current guidance, including the TUI/conformance crates.

At minimum verify the equivalents of:

cargo fmt --check
cargo check --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace

and the repository's current non-mutating tools/check.sh when available.

Do not mark this task complete with ignored/failing TUI tests unless a higher-level design explicitly records the limitation.

docs.title: Documentation Review
docs.text:
Before completion:

  • remove text that still calls implemented TUI paths stubs;
  • keep unimplemented Level 3 tasks marked Pending;
  • ensure crates/scriberig-tui/AGENTS.md still matches actual ownership boundaries;
  • update capabilities.toml accurately;
  • repair stale design references encountered in files touched by this task.

Do not mark future remote/session/agent capabilities complete just because the shell has placeholders for them.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] TUI semantic capabilities marked verified have cross-surface conformance coverage.
  • [x] Wide, medium, narrow, and too-small terminal layouts are tested.
  • [x] Important states remain understandable without color alone.
  • [x] Core workflows are keyboard reachable.
  • [x] Terminal restoration is tested across normal and failure paths through abstractions safe for CI.
  • [x] Paste/untrusted text cannot inject terminal commands/control sequences through normal rendering.
  • [x] Resize preserves semantic navigation/selection.
  • [x] Rendering performs no semantic service calls.
  • [x] Static runtime behavior does not busy-spin.
  • [x] Stale responses and event bursts are bounded correctly.
  • [x] Product errors do not leak backend internals or secrets.
  • [x] Capability matrix reflects actual implemented/verified TUI coverage.
  • [x] Full repository formatting, check, Clippy, and tests pass.

docs.title: Extend Session Records for Model Execution and Branch Results
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Extend scriberig-session so the durable session graph can represent model-driven branch execution without introducing provider-specific canonical message types.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/009. agent interaction and sessions.md;
  2. design/level-1/016. model driven agent execution and branch isolation.md;
  3. design/level-2/023. agent runtime model provider and branch orchestration.md;
  4. design/level-3/082. implement session domain structure and views.md.

Task 082 already implemented the base session domain. This task extends that implementation; do not create a second session model.

docs.title: Files to Update
docs.text:
Inside crates/scriberig-session/src/, update or add focused modules equivalent to:

lib.rs
schema.rs
types.rs
branch.rs
turn.rs
execution.rs
model.rs
tool.rs
result.rs
views.rs
error.rs

Add tests equivalent to:

crates/scriberig-session/tests/execution_records.rs
crates/scriberig-session/tests/branch_results.rs
crates/scriberig-session/tests/execution_views.rs

Preserve repository source-file limits and existing public re-export conventions.

docs.title: Required Provider-Neutral Records
docs.text:
Represent at least these semantic records:

ModelInvocation
ModelOutput
ToolInvocation
ToolResult
BranchResult
AgentOutput

Reuse existing Branch, Turn, Summary, Observation, Decision, and relation primitives.

docs.title: ModelInvocation
docs.text:
Must be able to retain non-secret provenance equivalent to:

branch
turn/sequence position
agent profile reference/revision
context identity/fingerprint
provider profile display id
model id
request fingerprint
cache disposition
started/completed timestamps or ordering metadata
usage/result references when available

Do not store API keys, Authorization headers, or secret environment values.

docs.title: ModelOutput
docs.text:
Must represent externally meaningful complete output:

assistant text or structured output reference
complete requested tool calls
finish/termination category
usage metadata when available
provider request/fingerprint metadata when safe

Do not require hidden chain-of-thought.

docs.title: ToolInvocation / ToolResult
docs.text: Use stable Scriberig tool identity and structured arguments/results. Provider-native tool-call ids may be optional correlation metadata only.

docs.title: BranchResult
docs.text:
Must support:

branch reference
terminal outcome/status
compact summary
result kind
result handles
touched entities
produced migration/workspace handles
validation handles
unresolved question handles

The result must be usable by the parent without loading all child turns.

docs.title: Branch Relationships
docs.text:
Add/verify relations equivalent to:

Branch --parent--> Branch
Branch --contains--> ModelInvocation
ModelInvocation --produced--> ModelOutput
ModelInvocation --requested--> ToolInvocation
ToolInvocation --produced--> ToolResult
Branch --produced--> BranchResult
BranchResult --references--> semantic results
Branch --child--> Branch

Avoid duplicating existing generic containment/ordering relations when they already express the same semantics.

docs.title: Ordering
docs.text:
Execution activity within a branch must have deterministic explicit ordering independent of database row order.

The branch view must be able to interleave:

HumanInput
ModelInvocation
ModelOutput
ToolInvocation
ToolResult
child branch start/result reference
AgentOutput

Do not derive chronology from UUID lexical order or insertion accidents.

docs.title: Compact Branch Descriptor
docs.text:
Extend the existing branch descriptor/view so a caller can read without loading activity bodies:

purpose
status
outcome summary
child branch count
activity count
active operation/reference when modeled outside canonical branch state
result reference
important touched semantic handles

Runtime-transient scheduler phases do not belong in the durable branch lifecycle unless they have durable semantic value.

docs.title: Parent Collapse Support
docs.text:
Add a view/helper that returns a parent-consumable child result equivalent to:

ChildBranchSummary {
  branch
  title/purpose
  terminal status
  outcome
  result handles
}

It must be possible to obtain this without loading the child's model/tool history.

docs.title: Provider Independence
docs.text:
Do not add canonical types named after specific wire payloads such as:

ChatCompletionMessage
OpenAIResponse
AnthropicMessage
GeminiPart

Provider-specific raw JSON may later be linked as optional artifact/evidence but cannot be required to interpret the session graph.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Prove at least:

  • model invocation/output can be recorded in one branch;
  • tool invocation/result are separately addressable and ordered;
  • a child branch can produce a compact BranchResult;
  • parent code can retrieve child descriptor/result without child activity bodies;
  • nested child branches preserve parent identity;
  • provider/model provenance contains no secret field;
  • deterministic session views preserve execution ordering;
  • historical exact references remain exact after unrelated session/project changes;
  • the crate requires no HTTP client or model provider.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-session
cargo clippy -p scriberig-session --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not implement HTTP model calls.
  • Do not implement the model/tool loop.
  • Do not put provider credentials into session entities.
  • Do not store hidden chain-of-thought as required session state.
  • Do not create a transcript-only execution representation.
  • Do not add TUI/web presentation code.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Provider-neutral model/tool execution records exist.
  • [x] BranchResult carries compact outcome and semantic result handles.
  • [x] Parent/child branch relationships are explicit and nested.
  • [x] Execution ordering is deterministic and explicit.
  • [x] Compact branch/result views avoid loading full child history.
  • [x] Secret provider configuration cannot be represented in canonical records.
  • [x] No provider-specific wire types leak into session schema.
  • [x] Tests cover nesting, ordering, compact results, and provider independence.
  • [x] Formatting, tests, and Clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement OpenAI-Compatible Model Provider Transport
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the first production model-provider adapter in scriberig-agent-runtime behind a provider-neutral contract.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/016. model driven agent execution and branch isolation.md;
  2. design/level-2/023. agent runtime model provider and branch orchestration.md;
  3. design/level-3/107. extend session records for model execution and branch results.md.

This task implements transport and provider normalization only. It does not implement nested branch orchestration or public UI surfaces.

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Within crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/, create focused modules equivalent to:

src/lib.rs
src/config.rs
src/error.rs
src/provider/mod.rs
src/provider/types.rs
src/provider/openai_compatible.rs
src/provider/stream.rs
src/provider/error.rs

Add integration/unit tests equivalent to:

tests/provider_fake.rs
tests/openai_compatible_http.rs
tests/openai_compatible_stream.rs

Update Cargo.toml with the minimum HTTP/serialization/runtime dependencies required by the chosen implementation.

docs.title: Provider-Neutral Contract
docs.text:
Define a provider abstraction that allows both a real HTTP adapter and a deterministic fake provider.

It must accept a provider-neutral request containing at least:

model identifier
ordered context blocks/messages
tool definitions
structured tool-choice policy
optional structured-output schema
output-affecting generation options
safe request metadata

It must return or stream normalized concepts equivalent to:

assistant text
structured output
tool calls with structured arguments
finish reason
usage metadata
provider request id
provider model/fingerprint metadata when returned

No higher layer should need to know the OpenAI wire field names.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Support a provider configuration structure equivalent to:

profile id
base URL
model id
credential source
request timeout
connect timeout
stream default
compatibility profile
optional default model parameters

Credentials must be loaded at runtime and must not implement Debug/serialization in a way that leaks secret values.

Prefer a credential source abstraction that can initially read an environment variable while allowing future secret-store integration.

docs.title: OpenAI-Compatible Wire Support
docs.text:
Implement the compatibility subset required for the agent runtime:

  • user/system/assistant-like context content;
  • tool/function declarations;
  • tool calls with JSON arguments;
  • normal complete responses;
  • streaming response assembly;
  • usage metadata when present;
  • structured HTTP/provider errors.

The adapter may initially target one well-defined OpenAI-compatible endpoint family. Keep serialization isolated so another endpoint style can be added behind the same provider-neutral trait without touching orchestration code.

Do not expose provider DTOs from the crate's main public agent API unless they are explicitly under a provider-specific module.

docs.title: Capability Detection/Profile
docs.text:
Define ProviderCapabilities and a compatibility profile.

Represent at least:

streaming
tool_calls
parallel_tool_calls
structured_output
usage_reporting
provider_request_id
provider_model_fingerprint

The compatibility profile may configure known deviations rather than attempting unreliable runtime probing for every feature.

Unsupported required behavior must fail before dispatch where possible.

docs.title: HTTP Requirements
docs.text:
Use a production HTTP client with:

  • HTTPS support;
  • connect and request timeouts;
  • bounded response bodies;
  • cancellation support;
  • explicit status handling;
  • safe user-agent/product identification;
  • no logging of Authorization headers;
  • proxy behavior that is either standard library/client behavior or explicitly documented.

reqwest is preferred unless implementation constraints justify another client.

Keep async/runtime dependencies inside runtime/product layers.

docs.title: Streaming Assembly
docs.text:
Normalize provider stream fragments into internal events equivalent to:

ResponseStarted
TextDelta
ToolCallDelta
UsageUpdate
ResponseCompleted
ResponseFailed

The adapter must assemble complete tool calls before presenting the final ModelResponse to orchestration.

Handle fragmented JSON argument strings safely; do not parse incomplete fragments as final arguments.

An interrupted stream must return an incomplete/failure result and must not be treated as a successful cacheable response.

docs.title: Error Mapping
docs.text:
Map transport/provider failures into stable categories equivalent to:

Configuration
Authentication
Permission
RateLimited
Timeout
Transport
InvalidRequest
UnsupportedCapability
MalformedResponse
ServerFailure
Cancelled

Capture safe status/request identifiers where available.

Do not include full prompts or secret headers in ordinary error display text.

docs.title: Fake Provider
docs.text:
Implement a deterministic fake provider usable by later branch-orchestration tests.

It must support a scripted queue of normalized responses, including:

text response
tool call response
multiple tool calls
provider failure
stream fragments

The fake records received provider-neutral requests for assertions.

No network access is allowed in fake-provider tests.

docs.title: Local Mock HTTP Tests
docs.text:
Use a local in-process mock HTTP server or equivalent fixture to test the concrete adapter.

Cover at least:

  • configured base URL is honored;
  • authorization is sent but never surfaced in diagnostics;
  • assistant text is normalized correctly;
  • tool definitions are serialized;
  • tool calls are normalized;
  • stream fragments assemble into the same semantic response as non-stream mode;
  • rate-limit/auth/server failures map to structured errors;
  • timeout/cancellation terminate correctly;
  • malformed provider JSON is rejected;
  • incomplete stream is not reported as success.

Tests must not contact the public internet.

docs.title: Logging and Diagnostics
docs.text:
Safe diagnostics may include:

provider profile id
model id
HTTP status
provider request id
elapsed duration
usage counts

Do not log by default:

API key
Authorization header
complete prompt/context
complete tool results
raw provider body containing sensitive context

A future explicit audit mode may retain sanitized payloads separately.

docs.title: Validation Commands
docs.text:
Run at least:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime
cargo clippy -p scriberig-agent-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings

If an async runtime feature is optional, test the production feature set used by apps/scriberig.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not implement session branch orchestration.
  • Do not directly call scriberig-store.
  • Do not expose provider credentials through protocol types.
  • Do not add provider SDK dependencies to TUI, CLI parsing, web, or foundation crates.
  • Do not assume streamed deltas are durable session objects.
  • Do not require the provider for unit tests of provider-neutral logic.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] A provider-neutral model contract exists.
  • [x] A deterministic fake provider implements the same contract.
  • [x] OpenAI-compatible text responses work through a local mock server.
  • [x] Tool definitions/calls work through the adapter.
  • [x] Streaming assembles complete normalized responses.
  • [x] Provider capabilities are explicit.
  • [x] Errors are structured and secrets are redacted.
  • [x] Timeout and cancellation behavior are tested.
  • [x] No public-internet call is required by tests.
  • [x] Formatting, tests, and Clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement Branch Context Compiler and Model Request Cache
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement deterministic branch-scoped context compilation, exact dependency manifests, model request fingerprints, and policy-controlled model-result caching.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/008. derived knowledge caching and incrementality.md;
  2. design/level-1/009. agent interaction and sessions.md;
  3. design/level-1/016. model driven agent execution and branch isolation.md;
  4. design/level-2/023. agent runtime model provider and branch orchestration.md;
  5. tasks 107 and 108.

This task stops before implementing the full model/tool branch loop.

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Within crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/, create focused modules equivalent to:

context/mod.rs
context/compiler.rs
context/policy.rs
context/dependencies.rs
context/fingerprint.rs
cache/mod.rs
cache/key.rs
cache/record.rs
cache/repository.rs

If persistent cache storage belongs in an existing derived-knowledge repository abstraction, adapt to it rather than creating a duplicate persistence subsystem.

Add tests equivalent to:

tests/context_compiler.rs
tests/context_branch_isolation.rs
tests/request_fingerprint.rs
tests/model_cache.rs

docs.title: Context Input
docs.text:
Define a BranchExecutionContext or equivalent containing stable inputs such as:

session reference
branch reference
branch purpose/goal
current user instruction
parent descriptor/result inheritance
recent current-branch activity selector
semantic selection/scope
pinned semantic handles
accepted decision/open-task selectors
agent profile revision
context policy revision
provider capability descriptor
tool catalog descriptor
context budget

The compiler receives resolved semantic/session data through application/session query interfaces. It must not query SQLite directly.

docs.title: Compiled Context
docs.text:
Produce a provider-neutral ordered context with explicit blocks/messages and a dependency manifest.

Each block should preserve enough metadata to explain its origin without sending that metadata verbatim to the model unless useful.

Conceptual block categories:

system/profile instructions
branch purpose
delegation/parent summary
current user instruction
recent branch activity
accepted decisions/open tasks
semantic object descriptions/content
tool-result summaries
child branch results
tool catalog metadata handled separately

The provider adapter later serializes this form.

docs.title: Branch Isolation Rules
docs.text:
For a child branch, default context inheritance is:

child purpose/delegation instruction
parent compact descriptor
explicitly selected parent result handles
explicit semantic scope/base snapshot
selected accepted decisions
capability/tool subset

Do not automatically copy:

all parent turns
all sibling turns
all child history from completed siblings
all project/session objects

A policy may explicitly request a bounded excerpt, but that choice must be represented in the compiled context and dependency manifest.

Add a test where a secret/unrelated marker in the parent's old activity is absent from the child compiled context unless explicitly selected.

docs.title: Current-Branch Recency
docs.text:
Implement a deterministic recent-activity policy.

Use semantic activity items rather than a provider transcript blob.

The policy should be able to retain recent:

human inputs
committed model outputs
tool calls/results
child branch result references

Large tool results should prefer compact stored projections or semantic handles and remain reopenable.

Do not silently truncate structured identifiers out of summaries.

docs.title: Dependency Manifest
docs.text:
Record exact dependencies actually used in compilation.

A dependency entry should identify a stable kind and exact immutable identity where available, for example:

session entity + revision
project entity + revision
branch result + revision
derived summary result id/revision
agent profile revision
context policy revision
tool schema hash

Do not include an entire current global snapshot merely because compilation happened while it was current.

Where a current selector is resolved, record the exact resulting revision/snapshot used.

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text:
Given the same resolved inputs, profile/policy revisions, provider capability descriptor, and tool catalog, compilation must produce the same canonical provider-neutral representation and dependency manifest ordering.

Avoid nondeterministic map iteration.

Timestamps that do not affect model input must not perturb the canonical representation.

docs.title: Budgeting
docs.text:
Implement deterministic bounded selection using a size/token estimate abstraction.

The compiler should prioritize conceptually:

  1. required system/profile instructions;
  2. branch purpose/current user instruction;
  3. required result/selection handles;
  4. recent current-branch activity;
  5. relevant decisions/summaries;
  6. optional deeper context.

When content cannot fit, preserve stable handles and short descriptors so the model can request deeper information.

Provider-specific token counting may be approximate initially, but the budgeting algorithm must be deterministic for a fixed estimator.

docs.title: Tool Catalog Contribution
docs.text:
The selected tool definitions participate in context identity even when serialized outside the message list.

Canonicalize each exposed tool descriptor using:

tool id
description
argument schema
result description
execution mode

Sort or preserve an explicit deterministic catalog order.

Capability-denied tools must not appear in the compiled catalog.

docs.title: Request Fingerprint
docs.text:
Create a canonical model request fingerprint over at least:

fingerprint schema version
provider compatibility profile
provider/model id
provider capabilities affecting serialization
agent profile revision
context policy revision
compiled context canonical form
dependency manifest
tool definitions
structured-output schema
output-affecting generation parameters

Use the repository's preferred cryptographic content hash/canonical encoding primitives where available.

Explicitly exclude:

credentials
Authorization headers
non-semantic request UUIDs
wall-clock timestamp
UI focus/scroll state
unrelated snapshot changes

docs.title: Cache Policy
docs.text:
Implement at least:

Disabled
RecordOnly
ReuseExact

docs.title: Disabled
docs.text: Never reads/writes model response cache.

docs.title: RecordOnly
docs.text: Calls the provider and records a successful complete result under the fingerprint.

docs.title: ReuseExact
docs.text:
Checks for an exact successful cached response first. On hit, returns it without provider invocation and records a reuse provenance relation/event for the new invocation.

Do not treat cache lookup as permission to bypass current capability checks or branch creation. The execution still exists in the current session/branch.

docs.title: Cache Record
docs.text:
Store enough metadata to audit reuse:

request fingerprint
fingerprint schema version
provider profile/model identity
provider fingerprint/version metadata if available
complete normalized response
usage metadata
original model invocation reference
created/retention metadata

Do not store provider credentials.

Incomplete/cancelled/failed responses are not successful cache hits.

docs.title: Reuse Provenance
docs.text:
When a cached result is reused:

  • create the current model-invocation/session record;
  • mark it as cache-reused;
  • reference the original cache/model invocation;
  • preserve the current branch and dependency context;
  • do not fabricate a new provider request id.

Later audit must be able to distinguish provider execution from cache reuse.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Cover at least:

  • identical input produces identical compiled context/fingerprint;
  • unrelated global/session change outside dependencies does not change fingerprint;
  • changing one referenced revision changes fingerprint;
  • changing agent profile/context policy changes fingerprint;
  • changing exposed tool schema changes fingerprint;
  • secret credential value does not affect or appear in fingerprint material;
  • child branch excludes unselected parent history;
  • bounded compilation preserves handles for omitted detail;
  • RecordOnly calls provider/cache write path;
  • ReuseExact hit avoids provider invocation;
  • reused response preserves origin provenance;
  • incomplete/failed response cannot be reused as success.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime
cargo clippy -p scriberig-agent-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not implement the complete model/tool loop.
  • Do not flatten entire sessions into provider messages.
  • Do not key cache only by global snapshot id.
  • Do not include secrets in fingerprints or cache records.
  • Do not make cache reuse invisible in provenance.
  • Do not require provider-specific DTOs for context compilation tests.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Branch execution context has explicit provider-neutral inputs.
  • [x] Context compilation is deterministic and branch-scoped.
  • [x] Child branches inherit only selected parent context by default.
  • [x] Exact dependency manifests are produced.
  • [x] Tool definitions participate in request identity.
  • [x] Model request fingerprints exclude secrets/unrelated global changes.
  • [x] Disabled, RecordOnly, and ReuseExact cache policies exist.
  • [x] Cache reuse preserves current and original provenance.
  • [x] Tests prove isolation, invalidation precision, and cache behavior.
  • [x] Formatting, tests, and Clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement Nested Branch Orchestrator and Trusted Tool Loop
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the branch-scoped model/tool execution loop, trusted tool dispatch, and recursive child-branch orchestration described by the Level 1 and Level 2 agent designs.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/016. model driven agent execution and branch isolation.md;
  2. design/level-2/023. agent runtime model provider and branch orchestration.md;
  3. tasks 107 through 109;
  4. the public application operation/capability APIs used by current agent tools.

This task owns orchestration inside scriberig-agent-runtime. It does not implement product-specific UI.

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Within crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/, add modules equivalent to:

runtime.rs
budget.rs
cancel.rs
event.rs
branch/mod.rs
branch/state.rs
branch/orchestrator.rs
branch/policy.rs
branch/result.rs
tools/mod.rs
tools/catalog.rs
tools/dispatch.rs
tools/projection.rs

Update lib.rs with a small public runtime boundary.

Add tests equivalent to:

tests/agent_loop.rs
tests/tool_dispatch.rs
tests/nested_branches.rs
tests/branch_isolation.rs
tests/agent_cancellation.rs
tests/agent_budgets.rs

Use the fake provider from task 108.

docs.title: Runtime Entry Point
docs.text:
Expose a runtime service conceptually equivalent to:

start_branch_execution(request, execution_context) -> operation/handle

The exact application-facing wrapper is added in the next protocol task, but the runtime API must already accept:

session
branch
prompt/current user input
agent profile
semantic selection/base snapshot
capability scope
retention policy
limits/cancellation

The runtime assumes the branch exists before the first provider request.

docs.title: Branch State Machine
docs.text:
Implement explicit runtime states equivalent to:

Created
CompilingContext
AwaitingModel
InterpretingModel
ExecutingTools
AwaitingChildren
Completing
Completed
Failed
Cancelled
BudgetExceeded

Keep runtime phase separate from the simpler durable session branch lifecycle.

Every transition should be testable and emit a bounded runtime event suitable for later application/protocol forwarding.

docs.title: Core Loop
docs.text:
Implement the loop:

compile context
-> compute request fingerprint
-> apply cache policy
-> invoke provider or reuse cache
-> persist complete ModelInvocation/ModelOutput semantics
-> interpret normalized model result
-> if final output: complete branch
-> if tool calls: validate/dispatch tools
-> append tool/child results
-> repeat

No provider-specific DTO should appear in branch orchestration code.

docs.title: Trusted Tool Catalog
docs.text:
Build the model-visible catalog only from registered trusted Scriberig tool descriptors.

Each descriptor must expose:

stable id
description
argument schema
result shape summary
read-only/state-changing classification
execution mode: atomic or child branch
required capability/domain applicability

The runtime validates returned tool names and arguments against this catalog.

Unknown tool ids never become arbitrary function dispatch.

docs.title: Atomic Tool Execution
docs.text:
Atomic tools execute within the current branch when they do not require an independent reasoning loop.

Required behavior:

  1. create/record ToolInvocation;
  2. validate capability and arguments;
  3. invoke the public application/session operation;
  4. create/record ToolResult;
  5. project a bounded result back into the next model context;
  6. preserve semantic result handles.

Use public app APIs rather than storage internals.

For state-changing operations, the returned result must still follow shared migration/validation semantics.

docs.title: Child-Branch Tool Execution
docs.text:
For tools classified as child-branch operations:

  1. derive child purpose from trusted descriptor plus validated arguments;
  2. resolve explicit parent-to-child context inheritance;
  3. derive capability subset;
  4. resolve base snapshot/workspace/selection;
  5. create the child branch in scriberig-session before provider execution;
  6. recursively invoke the same branch orchestrator;
  7. wait/observe according to tool semantics;
  8. obtain durable BranchResult;
  9. return only a compact child-result projection to the parent loop by default.

The parent model context must not automatically absorb child model/tool history.

docs.title: Recursive Limits
docs.text:
Enforce at least:

max model steps per branch
max branch depth
max child branch count
max tool calls
max total active branches
max provider request duration
optional total operation duration

Budget exhaustion becomes a structured terminal result and session provenance.

No recursion path may panic or overflow the process stack because the model repeatedly delegates.

An iterative scheduler is acceptable/preferred when useful, but semantic nesting must remain explicit.

docs.title: Parallelism
docs.text:
Initial correctness is more important than broad parallelism.

The runtime may execute independent read-only atomic tools concurrently when:

  • provider requested them together;
  • their tool descriptors allow it;
  • application semantics say they are independent;
  • result ordering is reconstructed deterministically.

Serialize by default:

state-changing tools
child branches sharing mutable workspace state
tools with declared ordering dependencies

Parallel child branches are allowed only when their base/workspace isolation is explicit.

docs.title: Tool Result Projection
docs.text:
Do not return unbounded raw tool payloads to the model.

Every tool result projection should prefer:

short result summary
exact semantic result handles
resolved revision/snapshot identity when important
structured status/error category
advertised next operations when available

Large content remains queryable through semantic handles.

The durable ToolResult may reference larger stored artifacts without injecting them into context.

docs.title: Model Final Output
docs.text:
A model result counts as branch-final only when normalized response semantics indicate no required tool calls and runtime policy accepts the output as terminal.

On completion:

  • record the final externally meaningful AgentOutput;
  • construct a durable BranchResult;
  • include produced semantic change/validation handles;
  • transition durable branch state to completed;
  • emit terminal runtime event.

A branch may complete with a structured result and no user-facing text when a delegated task is purely semantic.

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text:
Map failures into stable runtime categories.

For recoverable tool errors, policy may return a structured tool error to the model for correction.

For non-recoverable errors, finish the branch as failed/abandoned with a compact failure result.

Child failure must be representable as a tool result to the parent when parent policy allows recovery.

Never silently discard failed child branch history.

docs.title: Cancellation Tree
docs.text:
Implement a cancellation token/tree rooted at the agent operation.

Root cancellation propagates to:

in-flight provider request
active atomic tool where cancellable
active child branches
scheduler waits

Child cancellation/failure does not necessarily cancel the parent unless branch policy declares it fatal.

Persist already completed durable records; do not roll back history merely because execution was cancelled.

docs.title: Runtime Events
docs.text:
Emit normalized events equivalent to:

BranchExecutionStarted
BranchPhaseChanged
ModelInvocationStarted
ModelTextDelta
ToolStarted
ToolCompleted
ChildBranchStarted
ChildBranchCompleted
BranchResultProduced
BranchExecutionCompleted
BranchExecutionFailed
BranchExecutionCancelled

Events carry operation/branch correlation and bounded metadata.

Do not emit secret configuration or entire context blobs by default.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Use scripted fake-provider sequences to prove at least:

docs.title: Simple final answer
docs.text: user prompt -> model final text -> completed root branch

docs.title: Atomic tool loop
docs.text: model requests inspect -> tool result -> model final text

docs.title: Nested branch
docs.text:
model requests edit/delegated tool
-> child branch created
-> child executes two model/tool steps
-> child BranchResult produced
-> parent receives compact result only
-> parent final answer

docs.title: Nested branch isolation
docs.text: Put a unique marker in child internal history and verify it is absent from the next parent context unless parent explicitly opens/references the child history.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text: Run the same fingerprint with ReuseExact and prove the provider invocation count does not increase.

docs.title: Capability denial
docs.text: Provider requests a registered tool outside branch capability scope; verify application operation is never executed.

docs.title: Unknown tool
docs.text: Provider invents a tool id; verify structured failure rather than dynamic dispatch.

docs.title: Cancellation
docs.text: Cancel while a child/provider request is active and verify the execution tree reaches stable cancellation state.

docs.title: Budget exhaustion
docs.text:
Script repeated tool calls and verify deterministic budget failure.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime
cargo clippy -p scriberig-agent-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not implement CLI/TUI/web presentation.
  • Do not dispatch arbitrary provider-returned function names.
  • Do not let model output write canonical state directly.
  • Do not copy complete child histories into parent context by default.
  • Do not make provider/network access mandatory for tests.
  • Do not bypass application capability checks because a tool was advertised earlier.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Explicit branch runtime state machine exists.
  • [x] Model/tool loop uses provider-neutral responses.
  • [x] Trusted catalog validates names and arguments.
  • [x] Atomic tools execute through public application boundaries.
  • [x] Child-branch tools create real nested session branches.
  • [x] Parent receives compact BranchResult rather than child history.
  • [x] Recursion/tool/model budgets are enforced.
  • [x] Cancellation propagates through the execution tree.
  • [x] Runtime events are emitted with safe bounded metadata.
  • [x] Tests cover simple, atomic, nested, isolated, cached, denied, cancelled, and budgeted flows.
  • [x] Formatting, tests, and Clippy pass.

docs.title: Expose Agent Execution through Application, Protocol, Server, and Clients
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Expose the completed branch-aware agent runtime as one shared long-running application operation available to embedded callers, server/client transports, one-shot CLI, TUI, web, and third-party clients.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/016. model driven agent execution and branch isolation.md;
  2. design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md;
  3. design/level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md;
  4. tasks 107 through 110.

This task owns semantic/transport exposure. Product presentation is implemented by later tasks.

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Update focused modules in:

crates/scriberig-app/src/
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/
crates/scriberig-server/src/
crates/scriberig-client/src/
capabilities.toml

Expected files include equivalents of:

scriberig-app/src/agent.rs
scriberig-app/src/operation.rs
scriberig-app/src/event.rs
scriberig-app/src/capability.rs

scriberig-protocol/src/request.rs
scriberig-protocol/src/response.rs
scriberig-protocol/src/agent.rs
scriberig-protocol/src/event.rs
scriberig-protocol/src/capability.rs

scriberig-server/src/dispatch.rs
scriberig-server/src/subscription.rs

scriberig-client/src/client.rs
scriberig-client/src/operation.rs
scriberig-client/src/subscription.rs

Split oversized modules according to repository rules instead of adding more logic to an already large file.

docs.title: Application Agent Service
docs.text:
Add an application-facing service boundary equivalent to:

AgentService
  start(context, request)
  continue_branch(context, request)

Cancellation should reuse the shared operation cancellation API unless a thin convenience wrapper materially improves callers.

The concrete product composition wires this service to scriberig-agent-runtime.

Tests must be able to inject a fake agent service.

docs.title: Start Request and Response
docs.text:
Represent the Level-2 contract with typed application structures.

Request must support at least:

prompt
create/select session
optional parent branch
optional semantic selection
optional exact base snapshot
optional agent profile/context policy
retention policy
optional runtime limits

Response must return immediately with:

OperationId
SessionRef
RootBranchRef
accepted/base snapshot when meaningful

Do not block application start until the model finishes.

docs.title: Continue Request
docs.text:
Support follow-up input against an existing session/branch.

Validate:

  • session and branch exist;
  • caller has access;
  • branch lifecycle permits direct continuation or the application creates the required continuation child;
  • semantic selection/base context is explicit when supplied.

Return a new operation handle for the continuation execution.

docs.title: Operation Integration
docs.text:
Use the existing shared operation lifecycle.

Agent operation records must be able to expose safe metadata:

kind = agent
session/root branch
current phase summary
active branch count or handles when appropriate
final AgentResult reference
structured failure

Do not create an independent AgentOperationStatus lifecycle that disagrees with normal application operations.

docs.title: Agent Result
docs.text:
Define a structured terminal result equivalent to:

AgentResult {
  session
  root_branch
  final_output
  branch_result
  produced_changes
  validation_results
  unresolved_questions
}

The exact representation may use universal semantic references.

A final plain text answer is only one projection of this result.

docs.title: Application Events
docs.text:
Map runtime events into shared application events.

Durable event kinds should carry references to committed session objects. Transient streaming/progress events may carry bounded payloads.

Include operation-local sequence/cursor metadata sufficient for deterministic ordering and reconnection logic.

At minimum expose concepts equivalent to:

branch created/state changed
model invocation started
model text delta
tool started/completed
child branch started/completed
branch result produced
agent output committed
agent operation terminal

Sanitize provider diagnostics before publishing them.

docs.title: Protocol Types
docs.text:
Add transport-safe types for:

SessionReference
BranchReference
BranchResultReference
AgentStartRequest/Response
AgentContinueRequest/Response
AgentLimits
RetentionPolicy
AgentResult
AgentFailure
AgentEvent metadata/payloads

Reuse existing operation, error, snapshot, capability, and request-envelope structures.

Provider credentials and raw provider DTOs are forbidden in scriberig-protocol.

docs.title: Server Dispatch
docs.text:
Add server dispatch for agent start/continue/status/cancel/event observation.

The server must:

  • authenticate/authorize as configured;
  • decode public requests;
  • invoke scriberig-app;
  • return stable handles immediately;
  • forward shared operation/event state;
  • never build provider prompts itself.
