If the repository still only has in-process transport, implement and test semantic dispatch first. HTTP/event transport remains the responsibility of the server transport work required by the remote/web surface, but protocol shapes must not need redesign when that transport arrives.

docs.title: Rust Client
docs.text:
Add semantic client methods equivalent to:

start_agent
continue_agent
operation_status
cancel_operation
subscribe/observe agent events

Reuse universal session queries for branch/session inspection where possible.

The client must hide protocol envelopes and must not expose provider connection details.

docs.title: Capability Matrix
docs.text:
Add rows equivalent to:

agent_start
agent_continue
agent_final_result
session_branch_tree
session_branch_activity
agent_event_subscription
agent_streaming_output
operation_cancel

Set statuses honestly based on implementation and tests. Do not mark TUI/web verified in this task unless those product paths actually exist.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
Starting/continuing an agent must enforce both:

  1. permission to create/modify the target session branch;
  2. the capability scope available to tools the runtime may expose.

The runtime still checks each individual tool invocation at execution time. Start-time capability discovery is not a permanent authorization grant.

docs.title: Event Recovery
docs.text:
Tests should prove a client can recover after missing transient events by querying:

operation status
session branch tree
branch activity/result

Do not make final result correctness depend on stream replay.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests at the lowest owning layers plus a vertical deterministic slice.

Cover at least:

  • start creates/returns session and root branch handles before completion;
  • fake runtime completion populates shared OperationStatus and AgentResult;
  • continuation targets an existing branch/session correctly;
  • provider secrets cannot serialize into protocol DTOs;
  • agent runtime errors map to stable application/protocol categories;
  • event sequence ordering is preserved through server/client dispatch;
  • cancellation request uses shared operation lifecycle;
  • missed stream events can be recovered from durable session/operation state;
  • embedded app and client/server dispatch return semantically equivalent deterministic results.

Run relevant commands, including:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-app
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol
cargo test -p scriberig-server
cargo test -p scriberig-client
cargo test -p scriberig-conformance
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

Narrow commands are acceptable during development; final verification must cover all changed crates.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not put OpenAI wire DTOs into scriberig-protocol.
  • Do not send provider credentials to clients.
  • Do not block start until the model finishes.
  • Do not invent a second operation lifecycle for agents.
  • Do not make transient stream delivery authoritative.
  • Do not implement product UI in server/client crates.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] scriberig-app owns typed start/continue agent operations.
  • [x] Start returns operation/session/root-branch handles immediately.
  • [x] Agent work uses shared operation status/cancellation.
  • [x] Structured AgentResult is available at terminal completion.
  • [x] Agent/session protocol DTOs are provider-neutral and secret-free.
  • [x] Server dispatch maps public requests to application semantics.
  • [x] Rust client exposes semantic agent methods.
  • [x] Events preserve operation ordering/correlation and safe payloads.
  • [x] Capability matrix has honest agent/session rows.
  • [x] Recovery from missed transient events is tested.
  • [x] Embedded and transport-backed deterministic results are conformant.
  • [x] Formatting, tests, and Clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement One-Shot Agent Command through Shared Runtime
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Replace the provisional one-shot provider behavior with a non-interactive product surface over the same branch-aware agent operation used by TUI, web, remote clients, and the integrated agent runtime.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/016. model driven agent execution and branch isolation.md;
  2. design/level-2/020. repository scaffold conventions and native command surface.md;
  3. design/level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md;
  4. design/level-3/111. expose agent execution through application protocol server and clients.md;
  5. CLI_REFERENCE.md.

The controlling rule is:

srig run waits for a shared agent operation; it does not implement a private prompt-to-provider shortcut.

docs.title: User-Facing Command
docs.text:
Keep the stable top-level spelling:

srig run <PROMPT>

The implementation may add options needed for real composition while preserving the positional prompt.

Recommended first option set:

srig run <PROMPT>
  [--db <PATH>]
  [--provider <PROFILE>]
  [--model <MODEL>]
  [--base-url <URL>]
  [--api-key-env <NAME>]
  [--format <human|json>]
  [--no-stream]
  [--keep-session]

Do not add a raw --api-key <SECRET> flag. Secrets supplied on command lines are exposed through shell history and process listings.

If repository-wide configuration infrastructure already provides equivalent settings, use it instead of duplicating command-only configuration.

docs.title: Relationship to srig agent
docs.text:
The existing srig agent <PROMPT> command must not retain an independent orchestration engine.

For the first complete implementation choose one of these compatible behaviors:

  1. make agent an alias/delegating command that starts the same shared operation; or
  2. retain agent as the advanced/profile-selecting spelling while run uses the default agent profile.

In both cases:

same AgentStartRequest semantics
same branch/session runtime
same provider boundary
same tool loop
same cancellation
same AgentResult

Document the selected behavior in CLI_REFERENCE.md in the same implementation change.

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Update focused files in:

crates/scriberig-cli/
apps/scriberig/
CLI_REFERENCE.md

Expected responsibilities include equivalents of:

crates/scriberig-cli/src/args.rs        # parsing only
crates/scriberig-cli/src/run.rs         # presentation/dispatch helper if this crate owns it
apps/scriberig/src/main.rs              # composition only
apps/scriberig/src/agent.rs             # local runtime composition if a split is needed

Follow the existing actual module layout and split files before they exceed the repository source limit.

The CLI crate must not construct OpenAI wire requests.

docs.title: Composition Flow
docs.text:
The one-shot path is:

parse CLI
-> resolve database/runtime configuration
-> resolve model-provider profile and secret source
-> compose local application/session/agent runtime
-> build AgentStartRequest
-> start agent operation
-> receive OperationId + SessionRef + RootBranchRef
-> observe shared operation until terminal
-> resolve AgentResult/final output
-> print result and exit

The provider configuration belongs in the composition root/runtime configuration, not in scriberig-app protocol DTOs.

docs.title: Session and Branch Semantics
docs.text:
Every invocation creates or selects a real session and root execution branch.

The default one-shot behavior should create a fresh session/root branch unless an existing public configuration/request option explicitly asks to continue an existing session.

The command does not need to display the branch tree interactively, but the completed session/branch/result remains inspectable according to retention policy.

--keep-session, if implemented, requests durable retention beyond project defaults. Omitting it does not permit bypassing session creation; it only affects post-completion retention.

docs.title: Prompt and Semantic Scope
docs.text:
The required positional prompt becomes the human input/current instruction in the root branch.

If future one-shot options add a semantic target, pass stable semantic selection/reference data into AgentStartRequest. Do not pre-convert a semantic target into only raw filename/line text.

No implicit TUI/web selection exists in ordinary one-shot mode.

docs.title: Provider Configuration
docs.text:
The one-shot command may override safe provider configuration such as:

provider profile
model id
base URL
streaming preference

Secrets are resolved indirectly, preferably by a named environment variable or shared secret source.

Precedence must be deterministic and documented, for example:

explicit CLI non-secret override
-> selected provider profile/config file
-> product defaults

Secret lookup is separate and never printed.

Do not record the API-key environment variable value in session provenance. Recording the variable name may also be omitted unless useful and safe.

docs.title: Human Output
docs.text:
For --format human:

  • final user-facing agent text goes to stdout;
  • bounded progress/diagnostics go to stderr;
  • no provider request JSON is dumped by default;
  • on success with no final text but a structured semantic result, render a concise result summary and stable handles.

When stdout is not a terminal, avoid dynamic carriage-return progress rendering.

Do not make progress output part of the final answer stream consumed by shell pipelines.

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
For --format json, emit one stable machine-readable terminal object after completion.

It should include concepts equivalent to:

status
operation id
session ref
root branch ref
final output text when available
branch result ref
produced change refs
validation refs
structured failure when unsuccessful

Do not emit provider credentials or raw request/response payloads.

Progress may be disabled in JSON mode or written separately to stderr in a documented non-JSON human diagnostic format. Prefer no decorative progress by default.

docs.title: Streaming Presentation
docs.text:
Streaming is optional presentation over the same operation.

If enabled and supported:

  • transient model text may be shown on stderr or in a clearly separated interactive terminal presentation;
  • the durable final output is still resolved from operation/session state;
  • a lost stream does not make the command unable to finish if operation polling/status remains available.

For the simplest first implementation, it is acceptable to show phase/progress on stderr and print only the final durable output on stdout.

--no-stream disables transient output without changing agent semantics.

docs.title: Cancellation and Signals
docs.text:
Handle Ctrl-C/SIGINT as a cancellation request for the shared OperationId when execution has started.

Required behavior:

  1. request shared operation cancellation;
  2. stop starting new work;
  3. allow a bounded runtime shutdown path;
  4. preserve already durable session/branch provenance;
  5. exit using the documented cancellation status.

Do not simply drop the process and report success.

A second interrupt may use the platform's conventional immediate termination behavior if required, but document/test that path separately.

docs.title: Exit Status
docs.text:
Define and document a stable exit mapping.

At minimum distinguish:

success
usage/configuration failure
permission denied
provider/runtime/application failure
validation/conflict terminal failure when the agent result is unsuccessful
user cancellation

Preserve the repository's existing permission-denied convention (77) where applicable.

Use conventional interrupt status (130) where the supported platform behavior permits.

Do not infer success only from whether the provider returned assistant text; use the shared terminal operation/result status.

docs.title: Failure Rendering
docs.text:
Map structured failures to concise terminal diagnostics.

Useful categories include:

provider configuration/authentication
provider timeout/rate limit/transport
capability denied
tool/application failure
validation failure
budget exceeded
cancelled
internal runtime failure

Human diagnostics should include the operation/session short handle when useful for later inspection.

Never print API keys, Authorization headers, or full sensitive compiled context in ordinary errors.

docs.title: Deterministic Tests
docs.text:
Use a fake provider and temporary/in-memory application composition where practical.

Cover at least:

  • srig run "hello" starts the shared agent operation rather than a direct provider call;
  • start returns and the CLI waits until deterministic completion;
  • final stdout contains only the final answer/result in human mode;
  • progress/diagnostics do not pollute stdout;
  • JSON output contains operation/session/branch/result handles;
  • --no-stream changes presentation only;
  • provider/model/base-url overrides affect runtime configuration but not public agent request semantics;
  • secret environment value is never printed or serialized into result/session DTO fixtures;
  • Ctrl-C requests shared cancellation and returns cancellation exit status;
  • deterministic nested-child execution still produces the same final one-shot result;
  • srig agent delegates to the same runtime path under the selected compatibility behavior.

No test may contact a public model endpoint.

docs.title: CLI Documentation
docs.text:
Update CLI_REFERENCE.md in the implementation change.

It must describe:

  • real srig run agent behavior;
  • supported provider/runtime options;
  • secret-source guidance;
  • output-format behavior;
  • srig agent relationship;
  • exit/cancellation behavior.

Remove provisional language that says run merely echoes through a provider boundary once that behavior is replaced.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Run at least the relevant repository checks:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-cli
cargo test -p scriberig
cargo clippy -p scriberig-cli -p scriberig --all-targets -- -D warnings

Also run agent-runtime/application tests affected by composition changes.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not call the model HTTP endpoint from CLI parsing code.
  • Do not create a second one-shot-only model loop.
  • Do not add raw API keys as command-line arguments.
  • Do not bypass session/root-branch creation.
  • Do not treat transient stream fragments as the durable final result.
  • Do not print provider secrets or complete sensitive context by default.
  • Do not make run and agent semantically divergent runtimes.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] srig run starts the shared branch-aware agent operation.
  • [x] A real session and root branch are created for one-shot execution.
  • [x] The command waits on shared operation status and resolves AgentResult.
  • [x] Provider configuration is composed below the public agent request boundary.
  • [x] No raw API-key CLI argument exists.
  • [x] Human stdout/stderr behavior is pipeline-safe.
  • [x] JSON terminal output contains stable semantic handles.
  • [x] Ctrl-C requests shared cancellation and produces documented exit status.
  • [x] srig agent uses the same runtime path.
  • [x] CLI_REFERENCE.md matches implemented behavior.
  • [x] Tests use no public model/network service.
  • [x] Formatting, tests, and Clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement Branch-Aware Web Agent Experience
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement reusable browser support for starting and observing the shared branch-aware agent runtime, then compose it into the integrated Scriberig web application.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md;
  2. design/level-1/016. model driven agent execution and branch isolation.md;
  3. design/level-2/017. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md;
  4. design/level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md;
  5. design/level-3/111. expose agent execution through application protocol server and clients.md.

The controlling rule is:

The browser talks only to the public Scriberig client/protocol. It never contacts the model provider and never stores provider credentials.

The existing @scriberig/agent-ui package is the reusable React agent/session presentation layer. Do not implement the complete behavior only inside web/apps/scriberig.

docs.title: Packages to Update
docs.text:
Update the existing web packages in dependency order:

@scriberig/protocol
@scriberig/client
@scriberig/model
@scriberig/editor-core   # only where generic branch/selection navigation belongs
@scriberig/react
@scriberig/agent-ui
web/apps/scriberig

Do not add server/provider dependencies to the web workspace.

The existing @scriberig/agent-ui package already depends on:

@scriberig/editor-core
@scriberig/model
@scriberig/react

Preserve that reusable boundary unless a focused dependency change is justified.

docs.title: Protocol Package
docs.text:
Expose generated/authoritative public types needed for agent execution and session navigation, including equivalents of:

SessionReference
BranchReference
BranchResultReference
AgentStartRequest / Response
AgentContinueRequest / Response
AgentResult
AgentLimits
AgentFailure
AgentEvent
operation status/cancellation
session/branch descriptors
branch activity page

Do not hand-invent incompatible browser-only protocol semantics.

If Rust protocol generation is available, consume/update generated output through the stable @scriberig/protocol export boundary.

docs.title: Client Package
docs.text:
Extend @scriberig/client with semantic methods equivalent to:

startAgent(request)
continueAgent(request)
getOperation(operation)
cancelOperation(operation)
subscribeAgentEvents(operation/session, cursor?)
getSession(session)
getBranch(branch)
listBranchChildren(branch, page?)
listBranchActivity(branch, page?)
getBranchResult(result)

Use the existing transport abstraction.

The client must not expose:

OpenAI base URL construction
provider Authorization headers
provider request DTOs
provider model-stream parsing

The Scriberig server/client transport is the only browser network boundary.

docs.title: HTTP and Event Stream
docs.text:
Use the existing http-transport.ts and event-stream.ts boundaries rather than adding a second agent-specific network stack.

Agent event subscription must support:

operation/session correlation
monotonic event cursor/sequence
clean close/reconnect
error state
resume cursor when server supports replay
fallback authoritative refresh when replay is unavailable

A dropped event stream must not lose the final result because operation/session queries remain authoritative.

docs.title: Model Package State
docs.text:
Extend @scriberig/model with reusable state equivalent to:

AgentWorkspaceState
  sessions
  branchDescriptors
  loadedBranchChildren
  loadedBranchActivityPages
  activeOperations
  transientStreams
  eventCursors
  loading/errors/stale markers

Keep these categories distinct:

docs.title: Canonical/durable loaded state
docs.text:
Derived from authoritative server session/operation queries:

session descriptor
branch descriptor/tree
branch activity objects
BranchResult
AgentResult
operation terminal state

docs.title: Transient presentation state
docs.text:
Derived from live events and safe to discard/rebuild:

partial model text
current phase label
optimistic loading marker
latest received event cursor

Never merge a ModelTextDelta directly into canonical session history.

docs.title: Event Reducer
docs.text:
Extend model event reduction with deterministic handling of agent events.

Rules:

  • ignore already-applied duplicate sequence numbers;
  • do not regress state when an older event arrives after a newer one;
  • BranchCreated may mark parent-child data stale or insert a bounded descriptor when the event carries authoritative-enough metadata;
  • durable-result events should trigger/reference authoritative objects;
  • ModelTextDelta updates only transient stream buffers;
  • AgentOutputCommitted clears/replaces the relevant transient stream after authoritative output is loaded;
  • terminal operation events cause an operation/result refresh;
  • connection loss marks live state disconnected/stale without pretending the operation stopped.

Add focused pure reducer tests.

docs.title: Universal Selection Integration
docs.text:
Starting agent work from the integrated editor must pass the existing universal semantic selection into AgentStartRequest.

Preserve concepts equivalent to:

entity
optional exact revision
snapshot/branch context
optional projection location

Do not turn the selection into only an interpolated prompt string.

The reusable agent UI should accept selection through existing editor/react bindings rather than importing application-global state directly.

docs.title: React Bindings
docs.text:
Add focused hooks/controllers under @scriberig/react only where they are generic reusable bindings, for example:

useAgentOperation(operationRef)
useSession(sessionRef)
useBranch(branchRef)
useBranchChildren(branchRef)
useBranchActivity(branchRef)
useAgentEvents(operation/session)

Avoid duplicating model reducer logic inside hooks.

Hooks expose loading/stale/error state explicitly.

Event subscriptions must clean up correctly when references change or components unmount.

docs.title: @scriberig/agent-ui Source Layout
docs.text:
Replace the current placeholder-only panels with focused reusable components/controllers equivalent to:

src/index.ts
src/agent-composer.tsx
src/session-panel.tsx
src/session-branch-tree.tsx
src/branch-row.tsx
src/branch-summary-card.tsx
src/branch-activity.tsx
src/tool-invocation-view.tsx
src/agent-output-view.tsx
src/operation-panel.tsx
src/agent-panel.tsx
src/use-agent-controller.ts
src/types.ts

Split further if needed to preserve source-size rules.

The package should remain visually reusable and must not take a hard dependency on Material UI unless repository architecture is intentionally revised at Level 2 first.

The integrated application may wrap/style reusable agent-ui components using its MUI shell.

docs.title: Agent Composer
docs.text:
The reusable composer must support:

new-session/root start
continue selected session/branch
multiline prompt
current semantic selection summary
submit disabled/loading state
structured start/continue failures

It must not expose provider credentials.

On submit:

  1. build the public start/continue request;
  2. invoke @scriberig/client through model/controller bindings;
  3. immediately store returned operation/session/root branch refs;
  4. begin operation/event observation;
  5. preserve prompt text appropriately on failure.

docs.title: Session Branch Tree
docs.text:
Render nested branch descriptors without loading all branch activity.

Each branch row/card should support:

purpose/title
active/completed/abandoned state
compact outcome
child count
activity count
result availability
active-operation marker
expand/collapse
select/navigate

Completed branches default to compact collapsed representation.

Expanding a node loads child descriptors on demand.

Do not hard-code a maximum visual nesting depth. Deep trees may use indentation caps plus breadcrumbs/ancestry markers rather than becoming unusable.

docs.title: Branch Summary Card
docs.text:
A completed child branch shown in its parent flow should render primarily from BranchResult/descriptor:

purpose
outcome
status
important result handles
produced change/validation badges
Open branch action

It must not require fetching all child turns.

This component is the browser expression of context collapse: result first, provenance expandable.

docs.title: Branch Activity
docs.text:
When a branch is opened, render paginated semantic activity:

HumanInput
AgentOutput / ModelOutput
ToolInvocation
ToolResult
child branch/result
Decision/Observation/Summary
Migration/Validation references

Tool invocation/result rows default to bounded summaries with explicit expansion or semantic-handle navigation.

Do not render raw provider JSON as the primary user experience.

docs.title: Streaming Output
docs.text:
Show partial model output from transientStreams while an operation is active.

Requirements:

  • visibly in-progress;
  • keyed to exact operation/branch/invocation;
  • discarded/replaced when durable output is committed/loaded;
  • never inserted into durable branch activity as a fake message;
  • survives component rerenders but need not survive page reload;
  • after reload, recover from durable branch/operation state without stream replay.

If the transport cannot resume from the previous event cursor, perform authoritative refresh and continue from the new subscription point.

docs.title: Operation Panel
docs.text:
Render shared operation lifecycle and safe phase metadata:

queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled
operation id
session/root branch
current phase
active child count where available
progress counters
final AgentResult
structured failure

Cancellation button availability comes from shared capability/operation metadata.

Do not optimistically mark cancellation complete.

docs.title: Result Navigation
docs.text:
All semantic result handles must integrate with the existing universal editor navigation.

Examples:

produced migration -> change review
validation result -> validation view
changed function -> semantic/projection view
decision -> knowledge inspector
child BranchResult -> child branch view

@scriberig/agent-ui emits semantic navigation intents/uses editor-core public APIs; it does not implement duplicate routing semantics.

docs.title: Candidate Change Review
docs.text:
When a branch produces candidate canonical changes:

  • show them as result handles/status in agent UI;
  • route to existing MigrationPreview/validation/review abstractions;
  • require normal confirmation/capability flow;
  • display stale/conflict/validation failures through shared error/result models.

Do not add an "Accept model output" shortcut that bypasses change semantics.

docs.title: Integrated App Composition
docs.text:
Update the reference application SessionAgentView (or current equivalent) to compose:

current universal selection
AgentComposer
active operation summary
SessionBranchTree
selected BranchActivity/BranchSummary
result navigation/actions

The app may provide MUI layout/styling, but semantic state and network calls come only through public web packages.

Do not import Rust server internals, generated private files, or provider libraries into web/apps/scriberig.

docs.title: Reconnect and Page Reload
docs.text:
Test and implement recovery behavior:

reload/open app
-> restore/select known session or operation ref where product state persists it
-> fetch operation status
-> fetch session/root branch descriptors
-> fetch selected branch activity on demand
-> subscribe from known cursor when supported

The exact browser-local persistence of last-open session may remain product-local UI state. It must not become canonical session identity.

The final result must remain visible after reload even if all transient stream fragments were lost.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Assert at compile/test boundaries that browser types do not contain provider secret fields.

Never add:

apiKey
Authorization provider header
provider secret token
raw provider credential config

to public web agent requests.

Safe provider/model display metadata may be shown if the public protocol intentionally exposes it.

Escape/render external/model/tool text as ordinary React text. Do not use raw HTML injection for model output.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
Reusable agent UI must support keyboard operation and non-color status communication.

At minimum:

  • tree rows/buttons are keyboard focusable;
  • expanded/collapsed state is exposed accessibly;
  • running/completed/failed states have text labels;
  • composer has associated accessible labeling;
  • cancellation is identifiable and disabled state explained when practical;
  • live progress regions avoid excessively noisy screen-reader announcements for every token delta.

Use throttled/bounded live-region updates for streaming rather than announcing every fragment.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Use fake transports and deterministic protocol fixtures. No public model endpoint is allowed.

Cover at least:

docs.title: Client/model
docs.text:
• start returns/stores operation/session/root branch refs;
  • nested branch descriptors reduce correctly;
  • duplicate/out-of-order events do not regress state;
  • model text deltas update only transient buffers;
  • durable output replaces transient state;
  • disconnect/reconnect marks state and refreshes correctly;
  • final result survives losing all stream deltas.

docs.title: React/agent-ui
docs.text:
• composer includes current universal selection;
  • completed branches default collapsed;
  • expanding loads children/activity lazily;
  • child result handles trigger semantic navigation;
  • cancel button obeys capability/lifecycle state;
  • nested branch tree keyboard navigation works;
  • no raw provider credential field is present;
  • model/tool text renders safely as text.

docs.title: Integrated app
docs.text:
• SessionAgentView communicates only through public packages;
  • a deterministic fake-backed start -> child branch -> final result flow renders end to end;
  • produced migration/result can navigate into existing review/semantic views.

Run at least:

pnpm --dir web format
pnpm --dir web typecheck
pnpm --dir web test
pnpm --dir web build

Run repository boundary/conformance checks that validate package import direction.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not contact the OpenAI-compatible provider from browser code.
  • Do not add provider API keys to browser configuration.
  • Do not make the web app own a second agent/session store.
  • Do not flatten branch trees into a chat-only canonical model.
  • Do not treat streamed text as durable branch activity.
  • Do not require full child history to render parent branch results.
  • Do not bypass universal selection/navigation or migration review.
  • Do not put reusable agent behavior only in web/apps/scriberig.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Web protocol/client expose shared agent/session operations.
  • [x] @scriberig/model separates durable branch state from transient stream state.
  • [x] Event reduction handles ordering, duplicates, reconnect, and terminal refresh.
  • [x] Universal selection scopes new agent work.
  • [x] @scriberig/agent-ui contains reusable composer, branch tree, branch summary/activity, operation, and output views.
  • [x] Completed branches collapse to result-first UI and expand on demand.
  • [x] Streaming remains transient and reload-safe.
  • [x] Cancellation uses shared lifecycle/capability state.
  • [x] Result handles navigate through editor-core/shared semantic navigation.
  • [x] Candidate changes route through existing review/validation UI.
  • [x] Integrated app imports only public packages for agent semantics.
  • [x] Browser code contains no provider credentials/provider SDK calls.
  • [x] Accessibility and deterministic tests cover branch-aware workflows.
  • [x] Formatting, typecheck, tests, build, and boundary checks pass.

docs.title: Implement HTTP Protocol and Event Transport for Remote Clients
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the concrete remote transport required by the web application and future remote TUI/third-party clients: JSON protocol requests over HTTP plus resumable semantic event streaming.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md;
  2. design/level-1/016. model driven agent execution and branch isolation.md;
  3. design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md;
  4. design/level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md;
  5. design/level-3/111. expose agent execution through application protocol server and clients.md;
  6. web/packages/client/src/http-transport.ts and event-stream.ts.

The existing web transport already assumes operation requests under /protocol/{operation} but event subscription is still transport-owned/unimplemented. This task makes that public transport real without moving semantics into HTTP routing.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Implement remote transport in:

crates/scriberig-server/
crates/scriberig-client/        # Rust remote transport where appropriate
crates/scriberig-cli/           # serve composition/options only as needed
apps/scriberig/                 # server composition root
web/packages/client/

Do not change semantic ownership of application operations.

docs.title: Server Framework
docs.text:
Use a small asynchronous Rust HTTP stack suitable for JSON request handling and streaming.

Preferred first implementation:

Tokio
Axum
Serde / serde_json

A different framework requires an explicit implementation justification but must preserve the wire contract described here.

Async/server framework dependencies remain in server/product layers. Do not propagate them into foundation/domain crates merely for transport convenience.

docs.title: Request Endpoint
docs.text:
Support the existing web-client shape:

POST /protocol/{operation}
Content-Type: application/json

The {operation} segment maps to a stable public protocol operation identifier.

Logical flow:

HTTP request
-> authentication/request context
-> decode typed public request
-> protocol/server dispatcher
-> scriberig-app operation
-> typed protocol response/error
-> JSON HTTP response

Routing must not implement semantic behavior that bypasses the existing dispatcher/application service.

docs.title: Operation Registry and Routing
docs.text:
Do not create a giant stringly typed switch disconnected from scriberig-protocol.

Use a centralized operation mapping where:

  • stable operation ids are defined/exported by the protocol layer;
  • route decoding maps operation id to a typed request variant;
  • dispatch maps the typed request to the existing server dispatcher;
  • response encoding preserves structured protocol errors.

Unknown operation ids return a structured unsupported-operation/not-found protocol failure.

docs.title: HTTP Response Semantics
docs.text:
Use predictable status mapping while keeping the body as the authoritative structured protocol result/error.

Recommended classes:

2xx successful protocol response
400 malformed JSON/request
401 unauthenticated when authentication configured
403 capability/permission denied
404 unknown public operation/resource where appropriate
409 stale/conflict semantic failure where mapping is stable
422 schema/validation request failure where appropriate
429 rate-limited transport/runtime failure when known
5xx internal/server/provider-host failure

Do not force every semantic failure into HTTP status alone. Clients must parse the structured error body.

docs.title: Request Correlation
docs.text:
Preserve/generate a correlation identifier for each HTTP request.

Expose it safely through:

protocol response metadata and/or
X-Request-Id style HTTP header

Internal/provider request ids remain separate.

Logs and safe error messages may use the correlation id without dumping request bodies.

docs.title: Event Stream Endpoint
docs.text:
Add a streaming endpoint conceptually equivalent to:

GET /protocol/events
Accept: text/event-stream

Support optional query/filter parameters such as:

after=<cursor>
operation=<OperationId>
session=<SessionRef>

The exact filter combination may be restricted initially, but the public event envelope must always identify its correlation scope.

Use Server-Sent Events for the first implementation because the traffic is server-to-client observation rather than bidirectional command transport. Commands continue to use ordinary POST requests.

The browser implementation should consume SSE using fetch() streaming rather than requiring the native EventSource API, so existing dynamic authorization headers can still be supplied.

docs.title: Event Envelope
docs.text:
Each emitted event must contain a serialized ProtocolEvent plus stable stream metadata equivalent to:

event id / cursor
operation-local or global sequence
kind
operation/session/branch references when relevant
payload

Use the SSE id: field for the resumable cursor where possible.

Do not encode canonical state only in event text. Durable referenced objects remain queryable through ordinary protocol requests.

docs.title: Event Buffer and Resume
docs.text:
Implement a bounded replay buffer or event-log adapter sufficient for reconnect.

Requirements:

  • assign monotonically ordered cursors in the stream scope;
  • retain a bounded recent replay window;
  • accept after=<cursor> and replay later retained events before switching to live delivery;
  • report a structured cursor_too_old/resume-unavailable condition when requested history is outside retention;
  • clients then refresh operation/session state and subscribe from the current cursor.

Do not retain unbounded token-delta streams solely for reconnection.

Replay retention is transport/observation policy, not canonical session retention.

docs.title: Backpressure
docs.text:
A slow/disconnected client must not block agent/model/application execution.

Use bounded per-connection queues/broadcast semantics.

When a subscriber falls behind beyond the safe buffer:

  • terminate/restart the stream with an explicit gap/resync condition, or
  • emit a gap marker supported by the protocol;
  • require authoritative refresh.

Do not grow an unbounded in-memory queue for a slow browser.

docs.title: Heartbeats and Idle Connections
docs.text:
Send bounded heartbeat comments/events during long silent operations when useful to keep intermediaries from closing the connection.

Heartbeats are transport frames, not semantic ProtocolEvent objects.

Clients ignore them for session/operation state.

docs.title: Authentication and CORS
docs.text:
Keep authentication pluggable through server request-context construction.

For the first local browser-host use case:

  • default bind remains loopback unless user explicitly chooses otherwise;
  • CORS should be restrictive by default;
  • configure exact allowed origin(s) for separately hosted development web app;
  • never use credentialed wildcard CORS.

If authentication is not yet implemented, keep the transport boundary ready for it and document the security implications of binding beyond loopback.

Provider credentials remain server-side and are unrelated to browser authentication.

docs.title: Request Limits
docs.text:
Configure bounded limits for:

HTTP request body size
JSON nesting/parse failures
header sizes through framework defaults/config
stream event payload size
concurrent connections where practical

Large semantic artifacts should be accessed through bounded query/projection operations rather than huge agent request bodies.

docs.title: Server Shutdown
docs.text:
srig serve must support graceful shutdown.

On Ctrl-C/shutdown:

  • stop accepting new connections;
  • close event streams cleanly where practical;
  • preserve application/agent operation consistency;
  • use shared runtime cancellation policy only when product shutdown policy requires operations to stop;
  • flush required durable state before process exit.

Transport shutdown and agent-operation cancellation are related but not identical.

docs.title: Web HttpTransport.request
docs.text:
Keep the existing request shape unless protocol generation requires a compatible refinement:

POST `${baseUrl}/protocol/${operation}`
JSON payload
AbortSignal support
structured protocol error decode

Add tests for:

  • base URL normalization;
  • structured errors/statuses;
  • abort behavior;
  • correlation metadata if surfaced;
  • no accidental provider endpoint usage.

docs.title: Web HttpTransport.subscribe
docs.text:
Replace the current no-op subscription with a fetch-backed SSE consumer.

It must:

open GET /protocol/events
send dynamic auth/application headers
parse SSE framing incrementally
parse ProtocolEvent JSON
track latest cursor/id
support AbortSignal/unsubscribe
reconnect according to caller/policy
resume with last cursor when supported
surface/handle cursor-too-old by triggering authoritative refresh

Do not use provider streaming protocols in this transport. This stream contains Scriberig protocol events only.

Split the SSE parser into a focused transport utility with deterministic byte/chunk tests rather than implementing parsing inside one oversized method.

docs.title: Rust Remote Client Transport
docs.text:
Where scriberig-client remote mode is part of the same milestone, add an HTTP transport implementing the public client boundary.

It should support:

request/response protocol operations
event subscription or event-stream handle
cancellation/shutdown
structured error mapping

If the existing Rust ProtocolTransport is synchronous and cannot correctly express streaming, introduce a separate asynchronous remote transport/subscription abstraction rather than forcing async behavior through a blocking fake API.

Preserve the in-process transport for tests/embedded use.

docs.title: TUI Remote Compatibility
docs.text:
Do not alter TUI semantic state/reducer for remote mode.

The future/current task 105 remote adapter should consume scriberig-client and implement the same TUI service port used by local mode.

This transport task must provide enough client support that agent/session event observation can work remotely without giving the TUI provider credentials.

docs.title: Static Web Hosting
docs.text:
Hosting the built reference web application from srig serve is optional for this task unless already required by repository product design.

If implemented, keep static-file hosting separate from /protocol/* routing and do not make the web application depend on co-hosting; a separately hosted frontend must still work under configured CORS/auth rules.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Use localhost/in-process server tests only. No public internet/model endpoint is allowed.

Cover at least:

docs.title: Request transport
docs.text:
• known operation round-trips typed request/response;
  • malformed JSON returns structured error;
  • unknown operation is rejected;
  • semantic application error preserves category/body;
  • cancellation/AbortSignal closes client request;
  • correlation id is stable per request.

docs.title: Event stream
docs.text:
• live ProtocolEvent arrives in browser/Rust client;
  • SSE framing survives arbitrary network chunk boundaries;
  • event ids/cursors are monotonic;
  • reconnect with recent cursor replays missing retained events;
  • too-old cursor produces explicit resync behavior;
  • slow subscriber cannot grow unbounded server memory;
  • heartbeat frames are ignored semantically;
  • cancelling subscription closes network task cleanly.

docs.title: Agent vertical slice
docs.text:
With deterministic fake agent runtime:

POST agent_start
-> receive operation/session/root branch
-> subscribe events
-> observe child branch/model/tool progress
-> query terminal operation/session result

Prove the terminal result remains correct after intentionally dropping the event connection mid-operation and reconnecting/refreshing.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Run relevant checks including:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-server
cargo test -p scriberig-client
cargo test -p scriberig
cargo clippy -p scriberig-server -p scriberig-client -p scriberig --all-targets -- -D warnings
pnpm --dir web typecheck
pnpm --dir web test

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not put semantic agent logic in Axum route handlers.
  • Do not expose provider credentials or provider HTTP endpoints to the browser.
  • Do not make WebSocket a requirement when server-to-client SSE is sufficient.
  • Do not use unbounded subscriber queues or replay buffers.
  • Do not make event delivery authoritative over queryable durable state.
  • Do not bind publicly by default without explicit user intent/security guidance.
  • Do not create a second browser event model unrelated to ProtocolEvent.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] /protocol/{operation} is a real typed HTTP transport over existing server dispatch.
  • [x] /protocol/events streams Scriberig protocol events with resumable cursors.
  • [x] Event replay is bounded and gap/resync behavior is explicit.
  • [x] Slow subscribers cannot block runtime work or grow memory unboundedly.
  • [x] Web HttpTransport.subscribe consumes Scriberig SSE using fetch and auth headers.
  • [x] Request/subscription cancellation works.
  • [x] Rust remote client support is added or cleanly separated behind an async transport abstraction.
  • [x] Local/remote TUI can share semantic service state rather than provider details.
  • [x] Security defaults favor loopback/restrictive CORS and keep provider secrets server-side.
  • [x] Deterministic agent operation survives event disconnect/reconnect.
  • [x] Tests require no public network/model service.
  • [x] Formatting, tests, typecheck, and Clippy pass.

docs.title: Verify Agent Branch Isolation and Cross-Surface Conformance
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Build deterministic conformance fixtures proving that one-shot CLI, embedded application, server/client, TUI adapters, and web client/model consume the same branch-aware agent semantics and preserve branch isolation.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/016. model driven agent execution and branch isolation.md;
  2. design/level-2/012. capability matrix and cross surface conformance.md;
  3. design/level-2/023. agent runtime model provider and branch orchestration.md;
  4. design/level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md;
  5. tasks 107 through 114;
  6. the updated TUI task 103.

The controlling rule is:

Conformance compares semantic operation/session results, not screenshots, terminal strings, React markup, or provider wire payloads.

docs.title: Test Locations
docs.text:
Use existing cross-package test infrastructure, adding focused fixtures/tests equivalent to:

tests/fixtures/agent/
tests/conformance/agent_runtime.rs
tests/conformance/agent_surfaces.rs
tests/end-to-end/agent_http.rs

Add web tests in the owning packages for browser-specific adapters/models, and expose fixture JSON/generated protocol data from a shared test artifact when useful.

Do not duplicate large fake scenarios separately in every crate/package.

docs.title: Deterministic Provider Fixture
docs.text:
Create a deterministic fake-provider script format capable of expressing steps equivalent to:

expect model request matching semantic assertions
return assistant text
return tool call(tool_id, args)
return multiple tool calls
return stream fragments
return provider error
wait until cancellation

The fixture should support referencing symbolic semantic handles created by the test setup rather than hard-coding unstable database ids.

The fake provider records received provider-neutral model requests for branch/context assertions.

No public model endpoint is used.

docs.title: Canonical Scenario A: Simple Root Answer
docs.text:
Set up:

user prompt: "Summarize X"
provider: final answer without tools

Assert across embedded app and product adapters:

one session created
one root branch created
one ModelInvocation/AgentOutput path
terminal OperationStatus = completed
AgentResult references session/root branch/BranchResult
same final output text

Presentation formatting may differ.

docs.title: Canonical Scenario B: Atomic Semantic Tool
docs.text:
Script:

root model requests inspect(entity X)
atomic tool returns exact X @ revision R
root model returns final answer

Assert:

  • tool id resolves through trusted catalog;
  • invocation/result are stored in the root branch;
  • exact entity/revision handle is preserved;
  • no unnecessary child branch is created;
  • final result is visible through all relevant surfaces;
  • provider request after the tool contains the bounded tool-result projection/handle rather than hidden database structures.

docs.title: Canonical Scenario C: Nested Child Branch
docs.text:
Script:

root model requests focused complex/delegated tool
-> child branch B1 created
B1 model requests atomic inspect
B1 model receives result
B1 model returns child outcome
-> BranchResult BR1
root model receives compact BR1 projection
root model returns final answer

Assert:

session
└── root branch
    └── child B1

and:

  • B1 has explicit parent root;
  • B1 has its own model/tool history;
  • BR1 is durable and referenced by parent activity;
  • root's next compiled context contains the compact child result;
  • root's next compiled context does not contain B1's full activity by default;
  • TUI/web branch tree can open B1 later through the stable reference;
  • one-shot final result succeeds without needing to print B1 history.

docs.title: Canonical Scenario D: Nested Branch Isolation Marker
docs.text:
This is a required architectural regression test.

Inside child B1 create a unique marker only in an internal child tool/model result, for example:

CHILD_PRIVATE_CONTEXT_MARKER_7F3A

Do not include it in BranchResult.

After B1 completes, capture the next root provider-neutral model request.

Assert the marker is absent.

Then explicitly use the supported semantic operation/tool to open deeper child history and assert the marker can become visible only after deliberate retrieval.

This proves:

retained history remains reachable, but completed branch internals are not automatically permanent parent context.

The test must operate on the provider-neutral compiled context, not vendor-specific serialized JSON.

docs.title: Canonical Scenario E: Nested Depth and Budget
docs.text:
Script recursive delegation until one configured limit is reached.

Assert:

  • branch hierarchy is preserved up to the limit;
  • no extra branch/model request occurs after limit exhaustion;
  • terminal failure category is budget exceeded or equivalent;
  • already-created branches/history remain inspectable;
  • no stack overflow/panic;
  • all product surfaces observe the same semantic failure category.

docs.title: Canonical Scenario F: Cache Reuse
docs.text:
Run an execution path with ReuseExact using exact unchanged inputs.

Assert:

  • first matching model invocation calls fake provider and records cache entry;
  • second exact matching invocation does not increment provider call count;
  • second session/branch still records its own ModelInvocation/reuse provenance;
  • original invocation/cache source is referenced;
  • final semantic result is equivalent;
  • unrelated global snapshot/session change outside request dependencies does not invalidate the hit.

Then mutate one referenced semantic revision and assert cache miss/fingerprint change.

docs.title: Canonical Scenario G: Capability Denial
docs.text:
Advertise or request a tool that the current branch/caller lacks capability to execute.

Assert:

  • runtime denies at trusted dispatch boundary;
  • application mutation/read operation is not executed;
  • structured denial is stored/returned safely;
  • model may receive bounded tool error only according to configured recovery policy;
  • no product surface can bypass the denial;
  • TUI/web action availability reflects capability state where applicable.

docs.title: Canonical Scenario H: Candidate Change and Validation
docs.text:
Use a child branch that produces a semantic migration/candidate and validation result.

Assert:

  • branch completion references candidate/validation handles;
  • model completion alone does not advance canonical main state;
  • one-shot result reports produced candidate handles;
  • TUI/web navigate those handles into shared review surfaces;
  • promotion/application through the normal change path advances state only after required validation/confirmation/capability conditions;
  • stale/conflict result remains shared across surfaces.

docs.title: Canonical Scenario I: Cancellation
docs.text:
Configure fake provider or child branch to wait.

Start operation, then request cancellation from each supported control path.

Assert:

  • same shared OperationId cancellation semantics;
  • provider wait is cancelled where supported;
  • active child branches stop starting new work;
  • terminal operation category is cancelled;
  • already durable history remains inspectable;
  • no surface reports cancellation merely because its view/subscription closed.

For one-shot, assert Ctrl-C adapter maps to shared cancellation and selected exit status.

docs.title: Canonical Scenario J: Event Disconnect and Recovery
docs.text:
Run through concrete HTTP/event transport with deterministic fake runtime.

Flow:

start agent
subscribe events
observe root/child progress
intentionally disconnect stream
allow operation to complete
reconnect with cursor or force cursor-too-old path
refresh operation/session

Assert:

  • final AgentResult is correct regardless of missing stream deltas;
  • branch tree/result can be reconstructed from durable queries;
  • replay works inside retention window;
  • too-old cursor triggers explicit resync rather than silent omission;
  • web/TUI transient stream buffers do not become fake durable history.

docs.title: Surface Adapters to Exercise
docs.text:
Where implementation exists, exercise these boundaries against the same deterministic scenario data:

1. scriberig-app embedded AgentService
2. scriberig-server dispatcher/in-process transport + Rust client
3. concrete HTTP protocol + event transport
4. one-shot command adapter/composition helper
5. TUI service adapter/reducer model
6. TypeScript @scriberig/client + @scriberig/model
7. integrated web agent controller/component smoke path

Do not require terminal screen scraping or browser screenshots for semantic equivalence.

TUI/web rendering tests remain in their own packages; conformance operates below presentation.

docs.title: Semantic Equivalence Assertions
docs.text:
Create reusable comparison helpers for normalized results.

Compare concepts such as:

operation terminal category
session/root branch topology
branch parent/child relations
BranchResult status/kind/result handles
AgentResult semantic handles
structured error category
exact referenced entity/revision/snapshot identities
candidate/validation references

Exclude from equality when nondeterministic/non-semantic:

local request correlation ids
wall-clock timestamps
transport connection ids
provider request id unless scenario asserts preservation
presentation labels/formatting
stream chunk boundaries

docs.title: One-Shot Assertions
docs.text:
In addition to semantic adapter testing, verify command presentation contract:

human final output on stdout
progress/diagnostics on stderr
JSON mode structured terminal result
nested branches do not dump full histories by default
cancellation exit code
permission/error exit mapping

The CLI is conformant only if it uses the shared semantic result used by embedded/server paths.

docs.title: TUI Assertions
docs.text:
Use TUI service/reducer tests to assert:

root/child branch refs map to branch-tree state
completed child defaults to compact result state
expand requests activity deliberately
stream delta stays transient
committed output replaces transient buffer
navigation away does not cancel operation
cancel action invokes shared cancellation
result handle becomes normal semantic navigation intent

Do not compare cell styling for cross-surface semantic conformance.

docs.title: Web Assertions
docs.text:
Use TypeScript client/model/controller fixtures to assert:

same AgentStartResponse handles
same nested branch topology
same BranchResult handles
same duplicate/out-of-order event behavior
same disconnect -> authoritative refresh recovery
same final AgentResult
no provider credential fields in public request/state

A minimal integrated React test may prove the public packages compose, but semantic equality belongs in model/client tests.

docs.title: Secret Leakage Tests
docs.text:
Use unmistakable fake secret values such as:

TEST_PROVIDER_SECRET_DO_NOT_LEAK_9A2D

Inject through the provider secret source.

Search/assert it is absent from:

session records
BranchResult / AgentResult
protocol request/response DTO snapshots
ProtocolEvent payloads
cache fingerprints/material
TUI formatted errors/state
web model state/serialized fixtures
CLI stdout/stderr on normal structured failures
server safe logs captured by tests where feasible

The provider HTTP mock may assert that the secret is correctly used only in the outbound authorization header.

docs.title: Capability Matrix Advancement
docs.text:
After all relevant implementation paths are real, update capabilities.toml.

Rows may advance toward verified for:

agent_start
agent_continue
agent_final_result
session_branch_tree
session_branch_activity
agent_event_subscription
agent_streaming_output
operation_cancel

Each surface column advances independently.

Do not mark web/TUI verified based only on runtime tests.

docs.title: Regression Fixture Stability
docs.text:
Keep deterministic fixture scripts small and semantic.

Prefer symbolic fixture helpers over copying provider JSON blobs.

When protocol schemas evolve add explicit compatibility fixtures rather than silently updating expected objects so older-version behavior disappears from tests.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Final verification should include the repository-wide relevant checks, at least:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
pnpm --dir web format
pnpm --dir web typecheck
pnpm --dir web test
pnpm --dir web build
python3 tools/lint_repo.py

Use narrower commands during development, but the task is not complete until the cross-surface suite and changed product packages pass together.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not call a public model endpoint in conformance tests.
  • Do not use hidden chain-of-thought as fixture data or assertion input.
  • Do not compare provider wire JSON as the definition of Scriberig semantics.
  • Do not compare screenshots/terminal cells for semantic conformance.
  • Do not make branch isolation tests depend only on UI collapse state; assert compiled parent context directly.
  • Do not mark capability rows verified without a real corresponding surface path.
  • Do not ignore secret leakage merely because tests use fake credentials.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Shared deterministic fake-provider scenarios exist.
  • [x] Simple root execution is semantically conformant across implemented surfaces.
  • [x] Atomic tool execution is conformant and does not create unnecessary branches.
  • [x] Nested child branch topology/result behavior is conformant.
  • [x] Child-internal marker is excluded from parent context until explicitly reopened.
  • [x] Branch-depth/tool/model budgets fail safely and consistently.
  • [x] Exact model cache reuse and invalidation are proven.
  • [x] Capability denial cannot be bypassed by any surface.
  • [x] Candidate changes remain non-canonical until shared review/promotion.
  • [x] Cancellation semantics are shared across product controls.
  • [x] Event disconnect/reconnect cannot lose durable final state.
  • [x] One-shot stdout/stderr/JSON/exit behavior derives from shared result.
  • [x] TUI branch collapse/expand/stream semantics use shared state.
  • [x] Web client/model branch/reconnect semantics use shared state.
  • [x] Provider secret values are absent from public/session/cache/UI artifacts.
  • [x] Capability matrix statuses are advanced only where verified.
  • [x] Repository-wide relevant formatting, tests, typecheck, build, lint, and Clippy pass.

docs.title: Deliver First Useful Project Workflow and Product Evidence
Objective
docs.text:
Deliver the first product-verified Scriberig workflow defined by:

  1. design/level-1/013. vertical product completion and end to end usability.md
  2. design/level-2/025. first useful project workflow vertical slice.md

This file is the master implementation task for Level-3 tasks 117 through 122.

Do not treat this as a request to add another independent subsystem. The job is to connect the existing subsystems into a real user workflow and prove the workflow with end-to-end tests.

The required final user sequence is:

import/open temporary Git/Rust project
-> activate that project workspace
-> browse named symbol Calculator/add
-> open real Rust source projection
-> produce candidate edit
-> review old/new source and validation
-> accept migration
-> write accepted source to working tree
-> observe successor snapshot/history
-> repeat candidate path from semantically-scoped agent

Both web and native TUI must reach the required interactive outcomes.

docs.title: Mandatory Reading Before Editing
docs.text:
Read these files completely before making implementation changes:

AGENTS.md
design/AGENTS.md

design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md
design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
design/level-1/013. vertical product completion and end to end usability.md

design/level-2/012. capability matrix and cross surface conformance.md
design/level-2/017. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md
design/level-2/021. terminal ui runtime and state architecture.md
design/level-2/022. terminal ui views interaction and conformance.md
design/level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md
design/level-2/025. first useful project workflow vertical slice.md

design/level-3/024. implement project onboarding across surfaces.md
design/level-3/059. implement language independent code domain.md
design/level-3/067. implement rust syntax domain adapter.md
design/level-3/078. implement projection specifications rendering and adapter api.md
design/level-3/080. implement filesystem projection ownership hashing and atomic io.md
design/level-3/081. implement reference integrated editor.md
design/level-3/083. implement filesystem observation synchronization and recovery.md
design/level-3/091. implement rust semantic reconciliation.md
design/level-3/101. implement tui application adapter explorer and inspector.md
design/level-3/102. implement tui history diff projection and change review views.md
design/level-3/103. implement tui sessions agent interaction and operation observation.md
design/level-3/104. wire srig tui to local application composition.md
design/level-3/106. verify tui conformance accessibility and terminal recovery.md
design/level-3/113. implement branch aware web agent experience.md
design/level-3/115. verify agent branch isolation and cross surface conformance.md

Also inspect the current implementation before choosing method/type names. Reuse existing public abstractions when they already express the required semantic operation.

docs.title: Controlling Rules
docs.text: These rules are mandatory for every subtask.

docs.title: Rule 1: no private shortcuts
docs.text:
Do not make the web app, TUI, CLI, or agent mutate database tables directly.

Do not add web-only server endpoints.

Do not deep-import private package source.

Do not let the agent patch files directly as a privileged alternative to the migration path.

docs.title: Rule 2: active project is not a global server variable
docs.text:
The server/database may store project catalog/current project snapshot data, but each client chooses its own active workspace.

Do not implement one mutable server-wide current_project setting.

docs.title: Rule 3: named semantic data comes from shared semantics
docs.text:
Do not solve explorer labels by parsing Rust source separately in React or the TUI.

The shared adapter/object summary/navigation result must expose meaningful names/kinds.

docs.title: Rule 4: a source projection is real source
docs.text:
Do not satisfy the projection step with the generic object inspector.

For the supported Rust golden fixture, source projection must expose src/lib.rs and the actual expression left + right.

docs.title: Rule 5: editing creates a candidate first
docs.text:
Before user acceptance:

  • current canonical project snapshot is unchanged;
  • fixture working-tree source is unchanged.

A source edit becomes a candidate migration based on an exact base snapshot.

docs.title: Rule 6: accepted change uses shared apply/write-back infrastructure
docs.text:
Do not write the file from a React click handler or TUI widget.

Use application/change/projection/filesystem infrastructure and expose effect status.

docs.title: Rule 7: tests must prove user outcomes
docs.text:
An HTTP 200, status=imported, rendered route, reducer action, or database row is not enough.

Use the exact WEB-GOLDEN and TUI-GOLDEN outcome assertions from Level 2.

docs.title: Rule 8: deterministic CI
docs.text:
No network model service.

No external Cargo dependencies in the golden fixture.

No edits to Scriberig's own tracked source during E2E.

docs.title: Rule 9: do not claim partial success as completion
docs.text:
If a required golden scenario does not pass, this master task remains incomplete.

Older [x] checklists prove only their historical subsystem scope.

docs.title: Required Subtask Order
docs.text:
Complete in this order:

117 active project workspace
118 semantic navigation and source projection
119 projection edit, candidate, review and validation
120 apply, filesystem materialization, refresh and conflicts
121 semantically scoped agent candidate
122 real-process golden E2E and product completion gate

You may make a foundational change needed by a later task while implementing an earlier one, but do not mark later task checklists complete until their own tests have run.

Do not skip task 122 because lower-level tests pass.

docs.title: Golden Fixture
docs.text:
Task 117 must establish/reuse one deterministic fixture with this semantic shape:

pub mod math {
    pub struct Calculator;

    impl Calculator {
        pub fn add(&self, left: i32, right: i32) -> i32 {
            left + right
        }
    }
}

The target accepted replacement is:

left.saturating_add(right)

If an existing fixture already has these exact stable anchors and is appropriate for both web and native E2E, reuse it instead of duplicating it.

All product E2E tests copy the fixture into a fresh temp directory.

docs.title: Implementation Discipline for a Simple Agent
docs.text:
For each Level-3 task 117-122:

  1. read the entire task;
  2. inspect existing owners/types/tests named in the task;
  3. write or adjust failing tests for the required behavior before or with implementation;
  4. implement the smallest shared public capability that satisfies those tests;
  5. run the focused tests;
  6. run affected Rust/web package checks;
  7. update capabilities.toml truthfully when the task says to;
  8. update that task's checklist only after the named tests pass;
  9. do not edit this master checklist yet unless the subtask is complete;
  10. proceed to the next task only when prerequisites are green.

If repository structure differs from a path suggested in a task, find the current owner by type/function/title and apply the semantic requirement there. Do not create duplicate subsystems just to match a stale filename.

docs.title: Evidence File
docs.text:
Create a concise machine/human-readable verification record when task 122 is implemented.

Recommended path:

tests/product-golden/README.md

It must document:

  • exact commands for browser golden E2E;
  • exact commands for native TUI golden E2E;
  • exact command for cross-surface conformance;
  • fixture location;
  • deterministic provider configuration used by tests;
  • which WEB-GOLDEN and TUI-GOLDEN IDs are implemented by which test files;
  • how failure artifacts/logs are located.

Do not paste transient test output into the design document as proof. The executable tests are the proof.

docs.title: Capability Matrix Constraint
docs.text:
By the end of this program, capabilities.toml must contain truthful coverage for the product capabilities required by the golden path.

Use the existing status vocabulary only:

not_applicable
planned
implemented
verified

Do not mark web or tui verified for a capability unless a dedicated test proves that surface.

Do not invent a new status such as done.

docs.title: Required Final Commands
docs.text:
At the end of task 122, run the repository's authoritative commands. At minimum the final evidence must include successful execution of equivalents of:

python3 tools/lint_repo.py
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
pnpm --dir web format:check
pnpm --dir web typecheck
pnpm --dir web test
pnpm --dir web build

Also run:

  • browser Playwright golden suite through the repository-defined command;
  • native PTY/TUI golden suite;
  • cross-surface conformance tests for the golden workflow.

Prefer ./tools/check.sh when it is the canonical umbrella command, but verify that it actually includes or is paired in CI with the product golden suites. Do not assume it does.

docs.title: Stop Conditions
docs.text:
Do not work around these conditions. Fix them.

  • If import succeeds but project root cannot be resolved: fix public project workspace contract.
  • If Calculator/add cannot be named without UI parsing: fix shared semantic summaries/adapter data.
  • If source cannot be rendered from semantic selection: fix projection/application operation.
  • If edit can only directly overwrite file: fix candidate/reconciliation path.
  • If migration cannot expose source diff/validation: fix shared change/review result.
  • If apply advances DB but filesystem effect is invisible: expose materialization/effect status and recovery.
  • If agent can only chat without producing a shared candidate: connect agent tools to the same change operation.
  • If product tests require a real network model: add/reuse deterministic provider.
  • If E2E is flaky because of sleeps: wait on explicit operation/DOM/PTY state instead of relaxing assertions.
