docs.title: Implement Active Project Workspace Across Application, Web, and TUI
Objective
docs.text:
Make an imported project immediately usable as the semantic workspace for the client that opened it.

This task fixes the gap where project scan/import succeeds but the browser/TUI remains rooted at an unrelated server bootstrap root or requires restart/manual IDs.

This is prerequisite 117 for the first useful project workflow. Do not start task 118 until the focused acceptance tests in this file pass.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

AGENTS.md
design/AGENTS.md
design/level-1/013. vertical product completion and end to end usability.md
design/level-2/025. first useful project workflow vertical slice.md
design/level-3/024. implement project onboarding across surfaces.md
design/level-3/081. implement reference integrated editor.md
design/level-3/104. wire srig tui to local application composition.md

Inspect the current project service/application/protocol/client/server types before changing them. Also inspect:

web/apps/scriberig/src/runtime.ts
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/ProjectManager.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/App.tsx

Find the current TUI state/application-adapter owner by searching for project context, root entity, explorer root, and srig tui --project handling.

docs.title: 1. Resolve project workspace by ProjectId
docs.text:
There must be one shared application-level operation capable of resolving an imported project into an exact semantic workspace.

The result must contain enough data to construct:

project_id
project_name
canonical project path or safe path metadata
project status
snapshot_id
root entity reference at that snapshot

Prefer an existing project status, project get, or equivalent operation if it can be extended without changing meaning. Add a new project workspace/open operation only if existing semantics are unsuitable.

The result must not expose a SQLite row ID as semantic identity.

The root must be the selected project's root, not a generic global root advertised by runtime capabilities.

docs.title: 2. Project activation is local client state
docs.text:
Web runtime and TUI state each maintain an active project/workspace.

Do not persist a single server-wide current project value.

Two clients connected to one server must be able to activate different projects without changing each other's active workspace.

docs.title: 3. Import-to-activation
docs.text:
After successful import:

  • resolve authoritative workspace for the imported ProjectId;
  • activate it in the initiating product runtime;
  • replace/reset explorer root to the project root and exact current snapshot;
  • clear selection if it belongs to another project/snapshot and cannot be resolved safely;
  • show project name/path and snapshot in product context;
  • make semantic/raw navigation immediately available.

The web implementation may navigate automatically from Projects to the semantic/raw browser, or expose an explicit Open project button after import. Whichever behavior is chosen must be deterministic and covered by Playwright.

docs.title: 4. Existing project activation
docs.text:
A user must also be able to open an already imported project from the project list without rescanning/importing it.

Web project list items need an explicit accessible action, e.g. Open <project-name>.

TUI startup with an existing ProjectId/path/database must resolve the same project-specific root.

docs.title: 5. Refresh after project snapshot change
docs.text:
Create a shared runtime/controller method equivalent to:

activateProject(projectId)
refreshActiveProject()

Names may differ to fit current code.

refreshActiveProject re-resolves authoritative project workspace and replaces snapshot/root state when the project current snapshot advances.

Do not mutate snapshot IDs locally based only on a UI assumption.

docs.title: 6. Selection behavior
docs.text:
On activation:

  • if there is no selection, leave it empty until user selects an entity;
  • if old selection points to another project, clear it;
  • if refresh advances the same project and the selected entity still resolves, preserve entity identity at the successor snapshot;
  • if it no longer resolves, clear selection and display a non-fatal selection-invalidated state.

Do not silently keep an exact old snapshot selection while labeling it current.

docs.title: Runtime
docs.text:
Refactor web/apps/scriberig/src/runtime.ts only as needed so the shared runtime owns active workspace state.

It should expose subscription or model state sufficient for React views to react to workspace activation.

Do not create a second transport/client in ProjectManager.

The initial generic server root may still be useful before any project is active, but once a project is active the knowledge tree/root used for project work must be the project's exact root.

docs.title: ProjectManager
docs.text:
ProjectManager must no longer treat import as only local list-state completion.

Inject or acquire the shared workspace controller/runtime action through public app composition.

After import, activate the returned/resolved project.

For existing imported projects, render an accessible open action.

Show active status in the project list or workspace shell.

docs.title: App shell/context
docs.text:
Show at least:

active project display name
current snapshot (short display allowed)

Path may appear in Projects/detail context.

Do not rely only on a hidden selection summary to tell the user which project is active.

docs.title: TUI Implementation Requirements
docs.text:
Find the TUI application state that currently stores project path/context.

Add explicit semantic workspace data rather than only a display path.

When launched with:

srig tui --db <db> --project <path> --git-tracked --import

the explorer root must be the imported project's current semantic root before the user begins navigation.

When a matching already imported project exists and import is not requested, resolve its current project workspace rather than falling back to a global root.

Display active project name/path and snapshot in the terminal shell/status area.

Do not make rendering code query SQLite.

docs.title: Public Protocol/Client Changes
docs.text:
If project workspace data is not available remotely:

  1. define/extend application result type in application/project owner;
  2. expose through canonical protocol schema;
  3. update Rust and TypeScript clients through the authoritative contract path;
  4. update server adapter to call application operation;
  5. add serialization/conformance tests.

Do not add a special endpoint consumed only by the reference app.

docs.title: Golden Fixture Setup
docs.text:
Create or reuse:

tests/fixtures/golden-rust-project/Cargo.toml
tests/fixtures/golden-rust-project/src/lib.rs

The fixture source must include:

math
Calculator
add
left + right

and no external dependencies.

Create a shared test helper that copies the fixture into a fresh temporary directory and initializes a Git repository/index for --git-tracked tests.

The helper may live in an existing cross-layer test-support crate/module if one exists. Do not duplicate fixture-copy/Git-init logic independently in browser and TUI tests if a practical shared helper can be used.

docs.title: APP-WORKSPACE-01: project-specific workspace resolution
docs.text:
Create two imported fixture projects in the same temporary database.

Resolve each by ProjectId.

Assert:

  • both return their own current snapshot;
  • both return their own root entity reference;
  • project A root/snapshot is not accidentally project B root/snapshot;
  • resolving A does not mutate B or any global active state.

docs.title: PROTOCOL-WORKSPACE-01: embedded vs remote equivalence
docs.text:
Resolve one project through embedded application operation and through server/client public path.

Assert equivalent project ID, snapshot ID, and root semantic reference.

docs.title: WEB-WORKSPACE-01: import activates workspace
docs.text:
Using the real browser E2E harness or, while task 122 is not yet complete, a focused Playwright spec:

  1. copy/init fixture;
  2. scan/import from Projects;
  3. activate/open it;
  4. assert active project name is visible;
  5. assert current snapshot is visible/non-empty;
  6. navigate to raw/semantic explorer;
  7. assert the root now belongs to the imported workspace rather than the pre-import bootstrap root.

This test may use a stable project/root label in task 117; symbol assertions Calculator/add belong to 118.

docs.title: WEB-WORKSPACE-02: open existing project without reimport
docs.text: Reload browser/server against same database, choose imported project from list, open it, and assert the same project current snapshot/root becomes active.

docs.title: TUI-WORKSPACE-01: launch imports and opens project
docs.text:
Drive the real PTY TUI with temp db/project and --import.

Assert visible project context and current snapshot.

Assert explorer root corresponds to the selected project.

docs.title: TUI-WORKSPACE-02: multi-project isolation
docs.text:
Prepare two projects in one database.

Launch TUI targeting project A and verify A context/root; launch another run targeting B and verify B. No "last imported project" global behavior is allowed.

docs.title: Failure Cases to Test
docs.text:
• project has no successful imported snapshot: workspace resolution returns structured not-ready error/state;
  • unknown ProjectId: structured not-found error;
  • project path no longer exists: catalog/workspace inspection remains possible, but filesystem-dependent actions report missing/unavailable path explicitly;
  • project snapshot changes while active: refresh returns new authoritative snapshot/root;
  • activation network failure in web: previous active workspace remains intact or transitions to explicit disconnected/error state; do not install a half-resolved root.

docs.title: Implement Named Semantic Code Navigation and Rust Source Projection
Objective
docs.text:
Make an active imported Rust project understandable and inspectable through real semantic names and real source projection.

After task 117, products know which project root/snapshot is active. This task makes that workspace useful enough that a person can navigate to Calculator::add without entity IDs and view the exact source containing left + right.

This is prerequisite 118. Do not begin candidate-edit work in task 119 until every required test here passes.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
design/level-1/013. vertical product completion and end to end usability.md
design/level-2/025. first useful project workflow vertical slice.md

Inspect current code-domain schemas, Rust adapter extraction, generic object summaries, list/inspect application operations, projection rendering operations, web tree components, and TUI explorer row generation before adding fields.

docs.title: Required User Outcome
docs.text:
With the golden fixture active, both web and TUI must let a user reach the method add by reading normal labels.

The user must be able to identify this semantic context:

src/lib.rs
math
Calculator
add

Selecting add and opening Projection/Source must show source that includes:

left + right

The user must not need to copy/paste an entity ID or understand ordinal syntax-node labels.

docs.title: 1. Named code entities
docs.text:
For Rust entities that represent named concepts, shared semantic data must expose at least:

name/display_label
semantic kind
source-relative path
source range or projection mapping
containment parent or a navigable semantic relation

Required named kinds for the fixture:

module: math
type/struct: Calculator
method/function: add

If existing code-domain schema uses different canonical kind names, keep those canonical names and map presentation consistently. Do not create duplicate kinds solely to match this wording.

docs.title: 2. Object summaries
docs.text:
Ensure public ObjectSummary/equivalent responses can carry a meaningful label without clients inspecting raw adapter payloads.

Prefer a generic semantic summary field or description mechanism already intended for this purpose.

The web and TUI must consume the same summary/name semantics.

docs.title: 3. Deterministic extraction
docs.text:
Rust import must extract these names deterministically from syntax/semantic data.

Reimporting unchanged source must preserve stable entity identity and labels according to existing adapter identity rules.

docs.title: 4. Raw syntax remains available
docs.text:
Do not delete complete syntax-tree entities or raw graph access merely to simplify the product tree.

Instead provide a semantic/domain navigation relation/view that can skip or collapse low-level syntax nodes for ordinary navigation.

docs.title: 1. Public operation
docs.text:
Use or extend the public list, relation traversal, query, or domain-navigation operation so clients can request meaningful semantic children from the active project/root.

Do not make React recursively fetch the entire graph and guess which nodes are important.

Do not make the TUI parse source files directly.

docs.title: 2. Required reachability
docs.text:
Starting from the golden project root, there must be a deterministic public navigation path to add.

The exact relation chain can follow existing schemas, but an integration test must traverse only public application operations and discover labels:

src/lib.rs
math
Calculator
add

If directories such as src are not semantic entities in the current model, the product may display source-relative file path context rather than invent a fake canonical directory entity. The required outcome is recognizable navigation, not a specific database hierarchy.

docs.title: 3. Pagination
docs.text:
If semantic children are paginated, the fixture path must remain discoverable through normal pagination and products must request additional pages correctly.

Do not assume required symbols are always in the first arbitrary page.

docs.title: 4. Duplicate names
docs.text: Display disambiguating path/kind context when two entities share a name. Stable entity identity remains the selection key.

docs.title: 1. Render from semantic selection
docs.text:
Use shared projection/application operations to render source for a selected semantic entity at an exact snapshot.

For add, response must contain or allow derivation of:

projection_id
entity reference
snapshot/base reference
source path: src/lib.rs
source text containing the selected method or file
selection/source mapping
editability capability
stale/current state

docs.title: 2. Mapping
docs.text:
The mapping must identify where selected add appears inside returned source text.

At minimum include a byte/character range using the repository's canonical range semantics.

Products may highlight the range, scroll to it, or show the selected region. Mapping must remain protocol/public-model data where remote clients need it.

docs.title: 3. Text source of truth
docs.text:
Projection text must be rendered/resolved from canonical semantic/source-artifact state for the requested snapshot.

Do not read the live filesystem directly in the web server merely to make the Projection panel look correct, because historical/candidate snapshots must remain renderable independently of current disk contents.

docs.title: 4. Read-only vs editable
docs.text:
For the golden Rust source projection, mark it editable only when the reconciliation/change path required by task 119 is actually available.

During implementation of this task it is acceptable for focused tests to observe source as read-only until task 119 lands, but do not falsely advertise editable capability.

docs.title: 5. Historical behavior
docs.text:
Rendering an exact historical snapshot must show the source belonging to that snapshot, even after current project state later changes.

Add a lower-level regression test for this behavior if projection infrastructure did not already prove it.

docs.title: Semantic view/tree
docs.text:
The web application must expose a semantic/domain navigation view distinct from opaque raw knowledge where practical.

Required browser behavior for fixture:

  • visible Calculator text;
  • visible add text after expanding/navigating appropriate ancestors;
  • clicking/selecting add updates shared SelectionController with its entity and exact active snapshot;
  • selection summary shows a human label/kind where supported, not only the ID.

You may reuse MuiObjectTree if it can consume semantic summaries, or extend reusable components/headless tree primitives. Do not hard-code golden fixture names into the app.

docs.title: Projection view
docs.text:
Replace the generic inspector fallback for supported Rust source selection with the real projection handler.

Required visible fields/state:

src/lib.rs
source text containing left + right
current snapshot/base context
current/read-only or editable status

The generic object inspector remains a fallback for selections with no registered projection.

docs.title: Shared selection
docs.text:
Navigating between Semantic and Projection routes must preserve the same entity selection.

Do not create a separate source-view selection object keyed only by path.

docs.title: Explorer labels
docs.text:
For named Rust entities, TUI rows display semantic names and kinds.

Examples acceptable:

Calculator  struct
add         method

or compact equivalents.

Do not display src/lib.rs :: function #42 when add is known.

Raw/debug mode may still expose IDs/ordinals.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
The PTY test must reach add through normal explorer expansion/selection keys or command palette navigation.

Do not add a test-only key that selects a hard-coded entity.

docs.title: Source projection
docs.text:
Provide a TUI action/view that renders the selected source projection and visibly contains:

src/lib.rs
left + right

It must use the same application projection operation as other clients.

docs.title: Protocol/TypeScript Contract
docs.text:
If existing inspect/list/render protocol results lack fields needed for name/path/mapping, extend canonical protocol types and regenerate/update checked language representations according to project rules.

Do not add browser-only JSON shapes.

Any new fields should be additive where protocol compatibility permits.

Add round-trip/schema/conformance tests for new public fields.

docs.title: CODE-NAME-01: Rust adapter extracts stable names
docs.text:
Import golden fixture and assert shared semantic data contains named entities for:

math
Calculator
add

Assert semantic kinds are correct according to code-domain schema.

Reimport unchanged fixture and assert identities/labels remain stable according to existing identity rules.

docs.title: CODE-NAV-01: public navigation reaches fixture method
docs.text:
Using embedded application public operations only:

  1. resolve golden project workspace;
  2. navigate/list semantic children/relations;
  3. find Calculator then add;
  4. assert selected entity belongs to src/lib.rs;
  5. assert no test reaches into adapter-private tables/payloads.

docs.title: CODE-NAV-02: client/server navigation equivalence
docs.text: Perform equivalent navigation through Rust/TS public client path and assert same add entity identity and snapshot.

docs.title: SOURCE-PROJ-01: exact source projection
docs.text:
Render source for add at imported base snapshot.

Assert:

path == src/lib.rs
text contains left + right
mapping contains selected add entity/range
base snapshot == active workspace snapshot

docs.title: SOURCE-PROJ-02: historical exactness
docs.text: After creating a successor snapshot in a focused fixture test, render base snapshot again and assert original text remains available.

docs.title: WEB-NAV-01
docs.text:
Real Playwright:

  1. activate golden project using task 117 flow;
  2. open semantic browser;
  3. expand/navigate until Calculator and add are visible;
  4. select add;
  5. assert selection summary/semantic view identifies add;
  6. open Projection;
  7. assert src/lib.rs and left + right visible;
  8. assert no browser console/page errors.

docs.title: TUI-NAV-01
docs.text:
Real PTY:

  1. launch golden project as active workspace;
  2. navigate explorer to visible Calculator/add;
  3. select add;
  4. open source projection action;
  5. assert terminal includes src/lib.rs and left + right.

docs.title: Negative Tests
docs.text:
• anonymous/unnamed syntax node: falls back to kind/compact diagnostic label without fabricated symbol name;
  • duplicate symbol names in different scopes: UI can distinguish through context while identity stays correct;
  • selection with no source projection: explicit unsupported/no-projection state, not crash;
  • stale/historical selection: projection shows exact historical state and visible historical status;
  • binary/non-source entity: no attempt to decode as Rust source.

docs.title: Performance Constraint
docs.text:
Do not make product startup load every syntax node/source file in the project.

Navigation must remain progressive/lazy using existing list/query pagination.

Golden fixture tests are small, but implementation must not bake in eager full-project traversal.

Add a focused test or instrumentation assertion if a proposed implementation accidentally fetches the whole graph to show the first tree level.

docs.title: Implement Projection Edit Candidate Review and Validation
Objective
docs.text:
Turn a real Rust source projection edit into a reviewable, validated candidate migration without changing current canonical state or the working tree before acceptance.

This task starts from the named add selection and source projection delivered by task 118.

Required human edit:

left + right

becomes:

left.saturating_add(right)

Before the user presses Apply/Accept:

  • the active project's current canonical snapshot must still be the base snapshot;
  • the temporary fixture's src/lib.rs on disk must still contain left + right;
  • a candidate/migration with exact base snapshot, source/semantic diff, and validation results must exist.

This is prerequisite 119. Do not implement direct filesystem write-back here; that belongs to task 120.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md
design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
design/level-1/013. vertical product completion and end to end usability.md
design/level-2/025. first useful project workflow vertical slice.md
design/level-3/078. implement projection specifications rendering and adapter api.md
design/level-3/081. implement reference integrated editor.md
design/level-3/091. implement rust semantic reconciliation.md
design/level-3/102. implement tui history diff projection and change review views.md
design/level-3/118. implement named semantic code navigation and rust source projection.md

Inspect existing migration/proposal, reconcile, validate, diff, operation, and candidate snapshot APIs before inventing new concepts.

docs.title: 1. Input
docs.text:
A projection edit request must identify at least:

project/workspace identity
projection identity
exact base snapshot
source-relative path
edited projection text or a structured semantic edit equivalent
provenance / initiating surface

When editing a selected region rather than an entire file, include enough mapping/base information to reject a stale or mismatched range.

Do not accept a request that means "edit whatever is current now" without an exact base snapshot.

docs.title: 2. Reconciliation
docs.text:
Use the shared Rust projection/reconciliation implementation to parse the edited representation and derive semantic changes.

Do not create a web-only text patch format that bypasses semantic reconciliation.

Do not create a TUI-only direct source patch path.

Reconciliation output must become the repository's normal migration/proposal representation.

docs.title: 3. Candidate state
docs.text:
Candidate creation must not advance the project's current root.

It may create immutable candidate snapshot/revisions according to existing change architecture, but the project current snapshot remains base until apply.

docs.title: 4. Candidate identity and provenance
docs.text:
Candidate/migration must have stable identity addressable by web/TUI/agent/operation results.

Record provenance sufficient to distinguish at least human web, human TUI, agent, or other caller according to existing provenance model.

Do not use provenance as a separate mutation path.

docs.title: Diff Contract
docs.text:
For the golden edit, the review model must expose both semantic and source-representation information where available.

Required user-observable information:

base snapshot
candidate/result snapshot or candidate identity
src/lib.rs
selected/affected add entity when identity survives
old expression: left + right
new expression: left.saturating_add(right)

The source diff may be a unified diff, structured before/after range, or equivalent reusable representation.

The semantic diff must not be fabricated by comparing UI strings. Use shared change/diff semantics.

If reconciliation replaces/reidentifies a lower-level syntax entity, review must still present the stable human context add/src/lib.rs when available.

docs.title: Layer 1: semantic/reconciliation validation
docs.text:
Candidate must prove:

  • edited Rust parses;
  • required semantic extraction/reconciliation succeeds;
  • candidate change has exact base;
  • projection mapping is internally consistent enough for candidate rendering/diff;
  • any migration schema/invariant validation passes.

docs.title: Layer 2: project validation
docs.text:
For the deterministic Rust golden fixture, run cargo check without network dependencies before normal acceptance is enabled.

Use existing validation/operation architecture. Do not spawn Cargo directly from React/TUI code.

The validator receives an isolated candidate materialization/workspace or another safe representation that validates candidate source without modifying the user's live working tree.

The command must be bounded/cancellable according to existing operation conventions where applicable.

Capture structured result:

status
exit/result category
diagnostics/stdout/stderr in bounded form
candidate/migration identity
base/candidate snapshot context

Do not treat the literal text "Finished" as the semantic validation API.

docs.title: Validation gating
docs.text:
Normal Apply/Accept action is enabled only when required validation is successful and candidate is not stale/conflicted.

If product architecture allows privileged force-apply in the future, it is outside this milestone and must not be exposed by the golden path.

docs.title: Invalid Candidate Scenario
docs.text:
Create a deterministic invalid edit, for example replacing the expression with malformed Rust such as:

left +

or another edit that reliably fails parsing/validation.

Required outcome:

  • candidate creation returns structured parse/reconcile/validation failure or a non-applicable invalid candidate according to existing architecture;
  • product displays diagnostic;
  • Apply remains unavailable or application apply rejects it;
  • active project current snapshot remains unchanged;
  • live fixture file remains unchanged.

Do not silently repair the invalid human edit through the agent in this test.

docs.title: Editable source projection
docs.text:
For supported current Rust projection, provide a clear editable control.

The first implementation may use a textarea/code editor component appropriate to current web dependencies. Do not add a heavyweight editor dependency unless necessary.

The control must preserve exact loaded base snapshot/projection identity.

Show dirty state when local buffer differs from loaded projection.

docs.title: Propose/Review action
docs.text:
Editing the buffer does not mutate canonical state.

Provide an explicit action such as:

Review change
Propose change

The action invokes the public candidate/reconcile operation.

On success, navigate/open the normal MigrationReviewView using returned migration identity.

Do not construct a private in-memory fake migration in the React component.

docs.title: MigrationReviewView
docs.text:
Extend/reuse this view so the live candidate displays:

  • base snapshot;
  • candidate/result identity;
  • changed path;
  • semantic/source diff old/new expressions;
  • validation progress/result;
  • stale/conflict state;
  • Apply disabled until validation success;
  • Reject/close local review without changing canonical state.

If validation is a long-running operation, show operation status and update from public operation/events.

docs.title: TUI Interaction Requirements
docs.text:
Implement one deterministic terminal-appropriate editing interaction.

Preferred order:

  1. existing projection edit/change command if already present;
  2. a small editable projection buffer/modal within TUI;
  3. a command palette action that replaces the currently mapped source region using entered text;
  4. external editor only if deterministic PTY test support exists and edited content returns through projection reconciliation.

The interaction must not write the live source file before acceptance.

Required TUI review screen/state displays:

src/lib.rs
left + right
left.saturating_add(right)
validation status
base snapshot/candidate context

Use same application candidate/validation operations as web.

docs.title: Application/Protocol Operations
docs.text:
Prefer existing operations equivalent to:

render projection
reconcile edited projection
create migration/candidate
validate candidate
inspect migration/diff

If current protocol exposes only some of these, extend canonical application/protocol/client once.

Candidate creation that may take time may return an OperationId; final operation result must contain stable candidate/migration reference.

Validation must be independently inspectable as operation/result, not hidden only in UI local state.

Add Rust and TypeScript client methods only through public exports.

docs.title: Candidate Render Isolation for cargo check
docs.text:
The golden fixture validator must not overwrite live workspace while validating.

Choose the smallest architecture-consistent method, e.g.:

  • materialize candidate project projection into a temporary validation directory derived from base project plus candidate changes;
  • use an existing projection staging area;
  • use a repository-defined candidate checkout/worktree abstraction if it already exists.

Requirements:

  • no network dependency;
  • no mutation of live fixture source;
  • candidate exact content is what Cargo checks;
  • temporary validation artifacts are cleaned normally;
  • failure diagnostics are retained in validation result.

Add a test that reads live src/lib.rs during/after validation and proves it remains base content.

docs.title: CANDIDATE-01: valid edit creates candidate, not current state
docs.text:
1. import golden fixture and record base project snapshot;
  2. select/render add projection;
  3. edit expression to saturating form;
  4. reconcile/create candidate through public application operation;
  5. assert candidate base equals recorded base;
  6. assert project current snapshot is still base;
  7. assert live file still contains left + right;
  8. assert candidate rendered source contains left.saturating_add(right).

docs.title: CANDIDATE-02: diff exposes expected change
docs.text:
Inspect candidate/migration through public diff/review API.

Assert changed path src/lib.rs, old expression, new expression, and affected named context add where available.

docs.title: VALIDATE-01: valid candidate passes semantic and cargo check
docs.text:
Run required validators.

Assert successful structured result associated with candidate.

Assert live file/current snapshot remain unchanged.

docs.title: VALIDATE-02: invalid Rust cannot become applicable candidate
docs.text:
Submit malformed Rust edit.

Assert structured failure/diagnostic, no current-snapshot change, no live-file change, and apply precondition remains false.

docs.title: VALIDATE-03: cargo validator actually checks candidate
docs.text:
Create a syntactically valid but type-invalid Rust candidate when practical, so parser passes but cargo check fails.

Assert semantic parse phase succeeds while project validation fails.

This prevents a fake validator that only parses.

docs.title: WEB-EDIT-01
docs.text:
Real Playwright:

  1. activate golden project;
  2. navigate/select add;
  3. open editable source projection;
  4. replace left + right with saturating form;
  5. click Review/Propose;
  6. assert migration review visible;
  7. assert base snapshot equals pre-edit displayed/recorded value;
  8. assert old/new expressions visible;
  9. wait for validation success;
  10. assert Apply becomes enabled;
  11. from harness read live fixture file and assert original left + right still present.

Do not click Apply in this task's focused test.

docs.title: WEB-EDIT-02
docs.text:
Real Playwright invalid edit:

  • submit malformed Rust;
  • assert visible diagnostic/validation failure;
  • assert Apply disabled/unavailable;
  • assert live file/current snapshot unchanged.

docs.title: TUI-EDIT-01
docs.text:
Real PTY:

  • select add;
  • use defined edit interaction to create saturating candidate;
  • open review;
  • assert old/new expressions and successful validation visible;
  • assert live file remains original before Apply.

docs.title: TUI-EDIT-02
docs.text:
Real PTY invalid edit:

  • create invalid candidate;
  • assert diagnostic/failure visible;
  • assert no apply-ready state;
  • assert live file/current snapshot unchanged.

docs.title: Negative and Concurrency Tests
docs.text:
• request uses base snapshot that is not active/current: candidate may still be inspectable but must be marked stale/not normally applicable;
  • edited projection identity does not match base/project: reject structured invalid request;
  • source path escapes project root: reject before any validation/materialization;
  • selected mapping/range no longer matches loaded projection: reject stale edit rather than patch a different location;
  • validation process fails to start: candidate remains unapplied and shows operation failure;
  • user closes review: candidate/current state behavior follows existing retention policy, but current project root and disk remain unchanged.

docs.text:

candidate_validation
migration_review

Web/TUI verified requires their real interactive tests above.

Do not mark filesystem_materialize verified yet.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Editable Rust projection preserves exact project/projection/base identity.
  • [x] Web edit buffer does not mutate canonical state or filesystem while dirty.
  • [x] TUI edit interaction does not mutate canonical state or filesystem before acceptance.
  • [x] Edited projection reconciles through shared Rust/change infrastructure.
  • [x] Valid edit creates stable candidate/migration identity with exact base snapshot.
  • [x] Candidate source can be rendered independently of live filesystem.
  • [x] Public review/diff exposes src/lib.rs, old expression, new expression, and semantic context.
  • [x] Semantic/reconciliation validation is structured and public.
  • [x] Candidate Rust is validated with deterministic no-network cargo check in isolation.
  • [x] Valid candidate enables normal Apply only after validation success.
  • [x] Invalid parse candidate cannot advance current state or disk.
  • [x] Type-invalid candidate proves cargo check validation is real.
  • [x] Validation never writes live fixture source.
  • [x] Candidate stale/base mismatch is represented explicitly.
  • [x] CANDIDATE-01 and CANDIDATE-02 pass.
  • [x] VALIDATE-01, VALIDATE-02, and VALIDATE-03 pass.
  • [x] WEB-EDIT-01 and WEB-EDIT-02 pass in a real browser.
  • [x] TUI-EDIT-01 and TUI-EDIT-02 pass in native PTY.
  • [x] Concurrency/negative tests above pass.
  • [x] capabilities.toml is truthful.

docs.title: Implement Migration Apply, Filesystem Materialization, Refresh, and Conflict Recovery
Objective
docs.text:
Complete the human change path by applying a validated candidate through shared migration semantics, materializing the accepted Rust projection to the project's working tree, refreshing the active workspace to the authoritative successor snapshot, and preventing silent overwrite of external edits.

This task starts with a validated candidate from task 119.

Required successful outcome:

base source on disk:       left + right
candidate source:          left.saturating_add(right)
user accepts
canonical project advances to successor snapshot
working tree src/lib.rs contains left.saturating_add(right)
web/TUI refresh to successor snapshot
history shows the transition

Required conflict outcome:

candidate created from base
external process changes src/lib.rs
user attempts accept/materialize
external content is NOT silently overwritten
product reports stale/conflict/effect state
recovery is explicit

This is prerequisite 120. Do not begin agent golden-path task 121 until the focused acceptance tests here pass.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md
design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
design/level-1/013. vertical product completion and end to end usability.md
design/level-2/025. first useful project workflow vertical slice.md
design/level-3/064. implement external effect receipts.md
design/level-3/080. implement filesystem projection ownership hashing and atomic io.md
design/level-3/083. implement filesystem observation synchronization and recovery.md
design/level-3/119. implement projection edit candidate review and validation.md

If numbering/titles changed, locate these designs by title/content. Inspect current migration apply, project-root compare-and-swap, projection materialization, source digest, filesystem ownership, event, and history code before editing.

docs.title: 1. Apply uses exact base compare-and-swap
docs.text:
The accepted candidate carries an exact base project snapshot.

Application must fail as stale/conflicted if the project's authoritative current snapshot no longer equals the candidate's required base, unless existing merge/rebase semantics explicitly create a new reviewed candidate.

Do not silently retarget the migration to a newer snapshot.

docs.title: 2. Apply is an application operation
docs.text:
Web/TUI call the shared public application apply operation.

Do not update project snapshot tables from product code.

Do not let product code manually create successor snapshot IDs.

docs.title: 3. Filesystem materialization is shared projection infrastructure
docs.text:
Do not use fs.writeFile in the web app, terminal renderer code, or agent runtime.

The application/projection/filesystem layer owns materialization and safety checks.

docs.title: 4. External filesystem effect is observable
docs.text:
The final operation/result must make it possible to distinguish at least:

canonical apply failed
canonical apply succeeded + materialization succeeded
canonical apply succeeded + materialization failed/requires recovery
candidate rejected as stale/conflicting before unsafe overwrite

Do not report a generic completed result that hides a failed required write-back.

docs.title: 5. No silent overwrite
docs.text: A source file whose expected base digest/content changed externally after candidate creation must not be silently replaced.

docs.title: Decide and Preserve Existing Effect Ordering
docs.text:
Database canonical-state promotion and filesystem write cannot be one atomic transaction.

Before implementing, inspect the repository's chosen external-effect receipt/materialization design.

Use that design rather than inventing a second transaction protocol.

The accepted implementation must document in code/tests which of these conceptual orders it uses:

A. validate expected filesystem state
   -> canonical compare-and-swap apply
   -> materialize projection
   -> record effect receipt/status

or

B. stage/materialize through existing safe protocol
   -> canonical apply/finalize
   -> record effect receipt/status

Either can be acceptable only if existing architecture supports it and failure recovery is explicit.

Do not claim database + filesystem are fully atomic.

docs.title: Filesystem Preconditions
docs.text:
Before writing src/lib.rs, verify through shared filesystem projection rules:

  • active/project identity matches candidate target;
  • target relative path is src/lib.rs or another registered owned path;
  • canonicalized target remains under project root;
  • path traversal is rejected;
  • symlink escape is rejected according to existing security design;
  • current filesystem digest/state matches expected projection/base state unless reconciliation has produced a new candidate;
  • target ownership/projection identity matches the accepted candidate;
  • write is limited to intended file(s).

Do not trust a client-supplied absolute path.

docs.title: Atomic Local Write
docs.text:
Use existing atomic I/O helper/contract from filesystem projection infrastructure.

Expected successful pattern is equivalent to:

write temporary sibling/staging file
flush as required by existing durability contract
atomic rename/replace
record resulting digest/effect receipt

Do not truncate the target in place if the existing design requires atomic replacement.

Preserve required permissions/metadata according to existing projection design.

docs.title: Successful Apply Result
docs.text:
The stable operation/result returned through application/protocol/client should allow products to learn:

migration/candidate id
base snapshot
successor snapshot
project id
changed semantic references
changed projection/source paths
validation reference/result
filesystem effect/materialization status
history/provenance reference when available

Products must refresh authoritative active workspace after success rather than installing a locally invented snapshot.

docs.title: Web Apply Behavior
docs.text:
In MigrationReviewView or the reusable review primitive:

  1. Apply is available only for validated, non-stale candidate;
  2. clicking Apply invokes public application/client operation;
  3. show operation progress/status;
  4. on canonical+materialization success, call shared runtime refreshActiveProject() equivalent;
  5. resolve/preserve selected add entity against successor snapshot when possible;
  6. show successor snapshot/current status;
  7. Projection reload shows accepted source;
  8. History route shows migration/snapshot transition;
  9. close/reject after successful apply must not roll state back.

If materialization fails after canonical apply, show a distinct error/out-of-sync state with recovery information. Do not simply display Migration applied while source file is unchanged.

docs.title: TUI Apply Behavior
docs.text:
The terminal review view must provide an explicit Apply action for validated candidate.

After operation finishes:

  • successful canonical/materialization state is visible;
  • active workspace snapshot refreshes;
  • selection/source projection can be reopened at successor state;
  • history/diff shows the transition;
  • effect failure/conflict appears as a persistent/inspectable status, not a transient toast that disappears.

Do not close the review view and pretend success before authoritative operation result is known.

docs.title: Post-Apply Selection Resolution
docs.text:
When add retains stable entity identity:

  • keep its EntityId selected;
  • replace exact snapshot context with successor current snapshot only after authoritative refresh;
  • refresh object/projection caches keyed by snapshot;
  • do not reuse base-snapshot source text as if current.

If identity no longer exists, clear selection and show selection no longer exists in current snapshot or equivalent explicit state.

docs.title: History Requirements
docs.text:
Successful apply must be discoverable through existing history APIs.

Focused tests must establish:

  • base snapshot remains addressable;
  • successor snapshot is current project snapshot;
  • history/diff links or includes the migration/change;
  • rendering base source still shows left + right;
  • rendering successor source shows left.saturating_add(right).

Do not delete the base source/revision during normal apply.

docs.title: Stale Canonical Snapshot Scenario
docs.text:
Test separately from filesystem conflict.

  1. create candidate against base snapshot A;
  2. advance the project canonical snapshot to B through another valid operation;
  3. attempt to apply candidate based on A;
  4. assert structured stale/conflict rejection;
  5. assert project remains B, not candidate result;
  6. assert candidate is not silently rebased;
  7. product shows stale state and requires new/reconciled candidate.

docs.title: External Filesystem Conflict Scenario
docs.text:
Required sequence:

  1. import fixture at base snapshot;
  2. create valid saturating-add candidate;
  3. before candidate apply/materialization, modify live temp src/lib.rs externally to a known marker, e.g. add a comment:
// external edit

while retaining or altering the expression as needed for deterministic digest mismatch; 4. attempt accepted change; 5. shared filesystem layer detects source mismatch before unsafe overwrite or records conflict according to projection sync design; 6. externally edited file remains present and is not replaced by stale candidate output; 7. operation/product reports conflict/stale/reconciliation-required state; 8. recovery path allows rescan/reconcile/new candidate rather than force-overwriting by default.

The test must read the file after the failed/conflicted operation and assert the external marker still exists.

docs.title: Materialization Failure Scenario
docs.text:
Create a deterministic failure without relying on platform-specific permission hacks when possible. Examples:

  • inject a filesystem implementation/test fault at the shared I/O boundary;
  • replace target parent with controlled invalid state in a test fixture;
  • use an existing fault-injection hook.

Assert:

  • operation distinguishes canonical and external-effect state;
  • receipt/recovery record exists when architecture requires it;
  • product can inspect/report failure;
  • retry/recovery follows existing design;
  • no unrelated file is changed.

Do not add production-only global environment flags merely for testing if dependency injection/fault abstraction already exists.

docs.title: Multi-Project Isolation
docs.text:
With projects A and B in one database:

  • candidate/apply for A advances only A root;
  • only A filesystem path is targeted;
  • B snapshot/root/files remain unchanged;
  • events identify A sufficiently for client A to refresh and client B not to adopt A state.

Add a conformance test for this.

docs.title: APPLY-01: valid candidate advances canonical project
docs.text:
1. create validated golden candidate;
  2. record base snapshot;
  3. apply through shared application operation;
  4. assert operation success;
  5. resolve project workspace;
  6. assert successor snapshot differs from base;
  7. assert migration/history connects them.

docs.title: MATERIALIZE-01: accepted projection reaches disk
docs.text:
Continue APPLY-01 or use fresh fixture.

Assert temp src/lib.rs contains left.saturating_add(right) only after acceptance.

Assert unrelated fixture files are byte-identical.

docs.title: MATERIALIZE-02: historical source retained
docs.text:
Render base and successor projections after apply.

Assert base contains left + right; successor contains saturating form.

docs.title: APPLY-STALE-01: stale base rejected
docs.text: Advance project after candidate creation and assert stale candidate cannot overwrite current state.

docs.title: MATERIALIZE-CONFLICT-01: external edit protected
docs.text: Perform external-marker scenario and assert no silent overwrite.

docs.title: MATERIALIZE-FAIL-01: effect failure is explicit
docs.text: Inject deterministic I/O failure and assert effect status/receipt/recovery state.

docs.title: MULTIPROJECT-APPLY-01
docs.text: Apply to A and assert B remains untouched semantically and physically.

docs.title: WEB-APPLY-01
docs.text:
Real Playwright:

  1. perform WEB-EDIT-01 candidate flow;
  2. capture base snapshot displayed;
  3. assert live file still base;
  4. click Apply;
  5. wait for terminal successful operation/materialization state;
  6. assert displayed current snapshot changed;
  7. test harness reads file and sees saturating form;
  8. reopen Projection and see saturating form;
  9. open History and see transition/change;
  10. reload app, reopen project if needed, and confirm successor state persists;
  11. assert browser diagnostics clean.

docs.title: WEB-CONFLICT-01
docs.text:
Real Playwright:

  1. create candidate;
  2. mutate temp source externally from test harness;
  3. click Apply;
  4. assert conflict/effect state visible;
  5. assert external marker remains on disk;
  6. assert UI does not claim write-back success.

docs.title: TUI-APPLY-01
docs.text:
Real PTY:

  1. create/review validated candidate;
  2. assert disk base before apply;
  3. invoke Apply;
  4. assert terminal shows successful new current snapshot/materialization state;
  5. assert disk saturating form;
  6. reopen source/history and assert successor state.

docs.title: TUI-CONFLICT-01
docs.text: Real PTY equivalent of external marker scenario; assert terminal reports conflict and external file survives.

docs.title: Event/Refresh Tests
docs.text:
Add test proving a connected client with active project receives enough event/operation information after apply to know it must refresh that project.

If event payload intentionally contains only references, client must resolve authoritative project workspace after event.

Do not stuff a second mutable canonical object copy into events merely to avoid refresh.

docs.text:

docs.title: Implement Semantically Scoped Agent Candidate Through Shared Change Path
Objective
docs.text:
Prove that the agent is a consumer of the same active project, semantic selection, projection, migration, validation, and review machinery as a human.

The required golden scenario is:

active golden project
-> select semantic entity add
-> start agent with exact selected entity + snapshot scope
-> deterministic provider requests/uses shared semantic tools
-> agent proposes saturating-add change
-> result is a normal candidate/migration
-> normal review shows old/new source and validation
-> working tree remains unchanged until user accepts

This task does not permit an agent-only file patch path.

This is prerequisite 121. Do not begin final product gate task 122 until every required test here passes.

design/level-3/120. implement migration apply filesystem materialization refresh and conflict recovery.md

If the deterministic fake provider already exists, extend/reuse it. Do not create a parallel test-only agent runtime.

docs.title: Semantic Scope Contract
docs.text:
When the user starts the golden agent operation with add selected, the agent request/session operation must carry structured semantic selection equivalent to:

project_id or resolvable project context
entity_id = selected add entity
snapshot_id = active exact/current project snapshot
optional revision_id when available
optional projection mapping/location

The selected entity and snapshot are authoritative scope.

Do not reduce scope to:

"src/lib.rs line 6"

or to prompt text such as:

"please look at add"

Path/range may be derived supplementary context, but semantic identity must survive in operation/session/tool context.

docs.title: Agent Tool Use Contract
docs.text:
The agent runtime may expose coarse agent-oriented tools, but they must delegate to shared application operations.

For the golden scenario, the agent must be able to do the conceptual equivalent of:

inspect selected semantic entity
render/read source projection for selection
propose/reconcile edited projection or structured semantic change
return stable migration/candidate reference

If the current agent catalog already exposes generic inspect/render/migrate/reconcile tools, reuse them.

Do not add a tool that directly opens SQLite.

Do not add a tool that directly writes src/lib.rs and then asks the project importer to notice later.

Do not allow the deterministic provider itself to insert a migration by calling test internals outside the agent tool/runtime contract.

docs.title: Required prompt
docs.text:
Use a stable user prompt such as:

Change add so overflow saturates instead of wrapping.

docs.title: Required deterministic behavior
docs.text:
Configure the existing fake/scripted provider so it behaves like a small tool-using model for this exact test world.

The provider should, through normal runtime messages/tool requests:

  1. observe that structured semantic selection exists;
  2. request inspection/source for the selected entity when the runtime protocol expects tools;
  3. receive source containing left + right;
  4. request the normal edit/candidate operation to change it to left.saturating_add(right);
  5. return a concise terminal response referencing the candidate/migration;
  6. allow the session/operation result to expose the candidate reference to product surfaces.

The exact provider message format follows existing provider-neutral contracts.

Do not special-case production agent runtime code on the literal prompt string. The scripted behavior belongs in deterministic test provider configuration/fixture.

docs.title: Capturable Scope Evidence
docs.text:
Tests must be able to prove exact semantic scope reached the agent/provider/tool layer.

Use an existing event/trace/session record where possible.

Acceptable evidence includes:

  • deterministic provider captured normalized model request containing structured selection context;
  • agent tool invocation record contains EntityId and SnapshotId matching the selected add;
  • durable agent operation input/session episode records preserve the selection.

Not acceptable by itself:

  • prompt contains word add;
  • UI selected row text happened to be add;
  • source path was included without semantic identity.

Keep captured test data bounded and free of secrets.

docs.title: Candidate Result Contract
docs.text:
A successful agent operation that proposes a change must expose a stable result reference that product surfaces can navigate to.

Prefer existing operation result/session activity concepts.

Required semantics:

operation_id
session_id
branch_id when applicable
selected semantic scope
candidate/migration id
base snapshot
result status

The migration itself is the same type used by human editing.

Do not create AgentPatch as a separate canonical mutation type unless it is only a transient provider-facing representation converted into the shared migration before product review.

docs.title: Review and Validation Integration
docs.text:
After the agent operation finishes, web and TUI must open/navigate to the normal migration review used by task 119.

Review must show:

src/lib.rs
add
left + right
left.saturating_add(right)
validation success

Before user Apply:

  • project current snapshot remains base;
  • live fixture file remains base;
  • agent result may be durable, but it has not silently committed canonical project change.

Applying later uses task 120 unchanged.

docs.title: Web Requirements
docs.text:
SessionAgentView already passes a semantic selection shape to agent start/continue operations. Verify and extend rather than replacing this path.

Required browser flow:

  1. user selects add in semantic explorer;
  2. Session/Agent view visibly indicates selected scope or otherwise preserves it;
  3. user submits golden prompt;
  4. deterministic agent operation runs through normal API/events;
  5. terminal operation result exposes migration candidate;
  6. Review candidate action opens normal MigrationReviewView;
  7. normal review/validation data is visible;
  8. source file is unchanged before Apply.

If the current UI changes selection while opening agent result, fix shared selection/navigation rather than creating a second agent selection store.

docs.title: TUI Requirements
docs.text:
The native TUI agent command must use current semantic selection in the same way.

Required flow:

  1. select add in explorer;
  2. open agent/session command/input;
  3. submit golden prompt using deterministic provider configuration;
  4. observe operation completion/result;
  5. navigate to resulting candidate through normal TUI review view;
  6. see old/new source and validation;
  7. verify disk remains unchanged before Apply.

No TUI-only direct agent patch --write command satisfies this task.

docs.title: CLI/One-Shot Diagnostic Coverage
docs.text:
Where existing one-shot/CLI agent surface accepts semantic selection/reference, add a focused non-interactive regression proving it can start the same semantically scoped operation.

CLI does not need to reproduce the entire interactive review UI in this task, but its operation result must expose the same candidate/migration identity rather than a private textual patch.

docs.title: Branch/Session Behavior
docs.text:
The golden agent operation should use existing durable session/branch semantics.

Required assertions:

  • operation belongs to expected session;
  • resulting candidate link remains inspectable after live streaming ends;
  • refreshing/reopening the product can recover operation/session result from durable state;
  • continuing a branch preserves explicit selected/current context rules rather than accidentally using an obsolete implicit project root.

Do not make ephemeral SSE/WebSocket stream data the only location of the candidate reference.

docs.title: Cancellation and Failure
docs.text:
Add focused tests for:

  • agent operation cancelled before candidate creation: no candidate/current snapshot/file change;
  • provider/tool failure: operation failed with structured error; no current snapshot/file change;
  • selected entity cannot be resolved at requested snapshot: agent operation/tool fails or requests explicit refresh; do not silently inspect a different current entity;
  • candidate becomes stale before review/apply: normal migration review shows stale state and task 120 protections apply.

docs.title: AGENT-SCOPE-01: exact semantic scope reaches runtime/tool/provider
docs.text:
1. import/activate golden fixture;
  2. resolve/select add;
  3. start agent with golden prompt through application operation;
  4. inspect deterministic provider/tool/session trace;
  5. assert EntityId equals selected add;
  6. assert SnapshotId equals active base snapshot;
  7. assert project context resolves to golden project.

docs.title: AGENT-CANDIDATE-01: agent uses shared candidate operation
docs.text:
Run deterministic scenario to completion.

Assert:

  • result contains normal migration/candidate ID;
  • candidate base equals selected snapshot;
  • candidate diff is same saturating-add change;
  • live project snapshot remains base;
  • live file remains left + right.

docs.title: AGENT-CANDIDATE-02: human and agent candidate semantics are equivalent
docs.text:
Create one human candidate and one agent candidate from fresh equivalent bases using same edit.

Compare semantic/source change meaning, not random IDs/timestamps.

Assert both are consumable by same migration detail/validation/apply operation types.

docs.title: AGENT-DURABLE-01: result survives stream/view lifetime
docs.text: After operation completes, disconnect/recreate client or reopen session and recover candidate reference from durable operation/session state.

docs.title: AGENT-FAIL-01
docs.text: Script provider/tool failure and assert no migration/current snapshot/filesystem mutation.

docs.title: AGENT-CANCEL-01
docs.text: Cancel operation before candidate creation and assert same no-mutation guarantees.

docs.title: WEB-AGENT-01
docs.text:
Real Playwright:

  1. activate golden fixture;
  2. navigate/select add;
  3. open Session/Agent;
  4. submit golden prompt;
  5. wait for deterministic operation completion;
  6. click/open candidate review through product UI;
  7. assert src/lib.rs, old expression, new expression, and validation result;
  8. assert harness-captured scope is exact selected entity/snapshot;
  9. assert live file remains base before Apply;
  10. assert browser diagnostics clean.

docs.title: TUI-AGENT-01
docs.text:
Real PTY:

  1. launch/select add;
  2. submit golden prompt;
  3. wait for operation result;
  4. open candidate review;
  5. assert old/new expressions and validation;
  6. inspect captured deterministic trace after run for exact entity/snapshot;
  7. assert live file remains base before Apply.

docs.title: No-Network Test Requirement
docs.text:
All tests above must pass with external network unavailable.

The deterministic provider must be selectable through normal provider/runtime configuration suitable for tests.

Do not require environment secrets.

Add a test/assertion or CI environment setting that would fail if the golden agent suite attempts outbound model-provider access.

docs.title: Capability Matrix
docs.text:
Add/update truthful capability equivalent to:

agent_semantic_edit_candidate

agent plus initiating web/TUI surfaces may become verified only after exact scope + real product interaction tests pass.

Do not infer verification merely from generic agent_start coverage.
