docs.text:
Run focused agent runtime/provider/session/tool/application/protocol tests, web tests/typecheck, real Playwright agent test, real native PTY agent test, and no-network deterministic suite.

Then at least:

cargo check --workspace --all-targets
pnpm --dir web typecheck

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Agent start/continue preserves structured active project semantic selection.
  • [x] Exact selected add EntityId and base SnapshotId reach agent runtime/tool/provider evidence.
  • [x] Agent tools delegate to shared inspect/projection/change application operations.
  • [x] No direct database or direct working-tree write tool was added for the golden edit.
  • [x] Existing deterministic fake/scripted provider is reused/extended through normal provider contracts.
  • [x] Golden provider scenario requires no external network or secrets.
  • [x] Agent result exposes durable normal migration/candidate reference.
  • [x] Agent candidate uses same migration/detail/validation/apply types as human candidate.
  • [x] Agent candidate is not auto-applied in golden workflow.
  • [x] Live working tree/current snapshot remain base before user acceptance.
  • [x] Web Session/Agent can open result in normal MigrationReviewView.
  • [x] TUI agent flow can open result in normal change-review view.
  • [x] Operation/session result survives stream/view lifetime.
  • [x] Cancellation/provider failure cannot mutate current project/file.
  • [x] Stale agent candidate is handled by normal migration stale rules.
  • [x] AGENT-SCOPE-01 passes.
  • [x] AGENT-CANDIDATE-01 and AGENT-CANDIDATE-02 pass.
  • [x] AGENT-DURABLE-01 passes.
  • [x] AGENT-FAIL-01 and AGENT-CANCEL-01 pass.
  • [x] WEB-AGENT-01 passes in a real browser.
  • [x] TUI-AGENT-01 passes in native PTY.
  • [x] No-network requirement is enforced.
  • [x] capabilities.toml is truthful.
  • [x] Affected Rust/web checks pass.

Do not begin task 122 with unchecked items.

docs.title: Enforce Real-Process Golden Path E2E Product Gate
Objective
docs.text:
Create the final executable product-verification gate for the first useful Scriberig workflow.

This task is intentionally test-heavy. Its job is to prove that tasks 117 through 121 compose through the actual user products, not merely that their individual unit/integration tests pass.

Do not implement missing product behavior by weakening this test task. If a golden scenario fails because product behavior is missing, go back to the owning implementation task and fix the product.

The first useful project workflow is not product-verified until every required scenario in this file passes from a clean checkout.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Every checklist item in these tasks must already be complete:

117. implement active project workspace across application web and tui.md
118. implement named semantic code navigation and rust source projection.md
119. implement projection edit candidate review and validation.md
120. implement migration apply filesystem materialization refresh and conflict recovery.md
121. implement semantically scoped agent candidate through shared change path.md

If any prerequisite is incomplete, stop and finish it before closing this task.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

AGENTS.md
design/AGENTS.md
design/level-1/013. vertical product completion and end to end usability.md
design/level-2/025. first useful project workflow vertical slice.md
design/level-3/116. deliver first useful project workflow and product evidence.md
web/e2e/README.md

Inspect the existing browser E2E fixture/global setup/page-object conventions and the native TUI PTY test harness. Extend them rather than building a second E2E framework.

docs.title: Browser scenarios
docs.text:
Browser golden tests must use:

  • a real Scriberig server process or the repository's normal E2E server composition;
  • the real reference web application served through its normal E2E/Vite/build path;
  • Playwright/browser interaction through accessible selectors;
  • a real temporary SQLite/database/runtime as normally configured;
  • a copied temporary golden project on disk;
  • public HTTP/protocol paths used by the real app.

Do not replace the server with request mocks for golden scenarios.

Do not call React component methods directly.

Do not mark a scenario passed because an API request succeeded if the required UI/file outcome was not observed.

docs.title: TUI scenarios
docs.text:
TUI golden tests must use:

  • the real built srig executable;
  • an actual pseudo-terminal harness;
  • normal CLI arguments;
  • actual terminal key/input sequences;
  • a copied temporary golden project and temp database;
  • screen/output assertions through the terminal harness.

Do not replace these with reducer snapshots or direct state mutation.

docs.title: Shared backend/conformance scenarios
docs.text: Programmatic conformance tests use public application/protocol/client interfaces. They may create in-process servers/transports when that is the repository's established conformance pattern, but must not access private database tables to fake semantic results.

docs.title: Test Fixture Lifecycle
docs.text:
Provide one reusable fixture factory for golden product tests.

For every scenario unless intentionally testing persistence across restarts:

  1. create fresh temporary directory;
  2. copy tests/fixtures/golden-rust-project into it;
  3. initialize Git repository if needed;
  4. git add the fixture files so --git-tracked includes them;
  5. create fresh SQLite/database path;
  6. start required Scriberig process(es) with project-root authorization containing only the temporary workspace where relevant;
  7. run scenario;
  8. on failure preserve/log useful diagnostics;
  9. terminate child processes cleanly;
  10. clean temporary data after success according to test-harness conventions.

Never point write-back tests at the Scriberig repository root.

docs.title: Stable Acceptance Anchors
docs.text:
The golden fixture/tests rely on these semantic/source anchors:

project source path: src/lib.rs
module: math
type: Calculator
method/function: add
base expression: left + right
accepted expression: left.saturating_add(right)
agent prompt: Change add so overflow saturates instead of wrapping.
external-conflict marker: // external edit

Tests may use accessible labels that include additional kind/context text, but they must verify these anchors remain user-visible/semantically discoverable.

docs.title: Browser Golden Suite
docs.text:
Create/organize specs so every scenario below has one obvious test mapping. You may use one file such as web/e2e/specs/golden-project-workflow.spec.ts or several focused files.

Do not delete existing bootstrap/offline/onboarding tests; keep them as regression tests.

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-01 — onboard and open active project
docs.text:
Required steps:

  1. launch clean server/app against fresh temp db and allowed project root;
  2. navigate to Projects;
  3. enter copied fixture path;
  4. enable Git-tracked-only scan;
  5. scan;
  6. assert scan review lists src/lib.rs;
  7. import reviewed scan;
  8. activate/open imported project through user-visible action/automatic documented flow;
  9. navigate to semantic browser;
  10. assert active project name/context visible;
  11. capture visible/non-empty base snapshot ID or stable shortened representation plus test-accessible full value if UI shortens it;
  12. expand/navigate semantic structure;
  13. assert Calculator visible;
  14. assert add visible;
  15. assert browser has no uncaught page/console errors.

Failure conditions:

  • test stops at status=imported;
  • explorer still uses generic pre-import root;
  • only opaque #N labels exist for named symbols;
  • test reaches add by hard-coded entity ID.

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-02 — selection opens exact source projection
docs.text:
Required steps:

  1. begin with active imported fixture;
  2. select visible add entry through UI;
  3. assert selection/semantic context identifies add;
  4. open Projection/Source route/action;
  5. assert src/lib.rs visible;
  6. assert source text contains left + right;
  7. assert projection is current at recorded base snapshot;
  8. assert editability is advertised for this supported Rust projection;
  9. assert selected semantic mapping/context is present enough that returning to Semantic still identifies same add.

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-03 — human edit creates reviewed validated candidate without write-through
docs.text:
Required steps:

  1. open editable source for add;
  2. replace only left + right with left.saturating_add(right) using real UI control;
  3. assert dirty/local-edit state if product exposes one;
  4. click Review/Propose change;
  5. wait for candidate/migration review;
  6. assert review base snapshot is the recorded base;
  7. assert changed path src/lib.rs;
  8. assert old expression visible;
  9. assert new expression visible;
  10. wait for semantic/project validation completion;
  11. assert validation successful and Apply enabled;
  12. from test harness read live temp src/lib.rs;
  13. assert disk STILL contains left + right and does NOT contain accepted expression;
  14. resolve project status through public API if needed and assert current snapshot is still base.

This test is specifically designed to fail a direct-write implementation.

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-04 — accept writes file and refreshes snapshot/history
docs.text:
Required steps:

  1. continue from or recreate valid reviewed candidate;
  2. record base snapshot;
  3. click Apply;
  4. wait for terminal operation state that explicitly includes successful required materialization/effect;
  5. assert active current snapshot changes to successor;
  6. assert successor != base;
  7. read live temp src/lib.rs and assert accepted expression present;
  8. assert base expression is no longer the active expression at target location;
  9. reopen Projection and assert accepted source;
  10. open History/Diff and assert transition/change is visible;
  11. if UI exposes migration ID, assert it remains inspectable;
  12. reload browser application;
  13. reopen/select existing imported project if active workspace is session-local;
  14. navigate back to add projection;
  15. assert accepted expression and successor current snapshot remain observable;
  16. assert browser diagnostics clean.

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-05 — invalid edit cannot apply
docs.text:
Fresh fixture.

Required steps:

  1. record base snapshot and base file bytes;
  2. select add and edit to deterministic invalid Rust;
  3. propose/review;
  4. assert structured parse/validation diagnostic visible;
  5. assert Apply disabled/unavailable or application rejects through normal UI with clear validation failure;
  6. assert current project snapshot still base;
  7. assert live file bytes equal original;
  8. assert no successor/materialization success is shown.

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-06 — stale external edit is not overwritten
docs.text:
Fresh fixture.

Required steps:

  1. create valid reviewed candidate and wait for validation;
  2. before Apply, modify live temp src/lib.rs from test harness to include // external edit;
  3. click Apply;
  4. wait for conflict/stale/effect outcome;
  5. assert UI explicitly shows conflict/stale/reconciliation-required or equivalent non-success state;
  6. read disk and assert // external edit still exists;
  7. assert stale candidate did not silently replace file with its old-base output;
  8. assert UI does not show full write-back success;
  9. if canonical apply already occurred per architecture, assert UI exposes out-of-sync/effect-recovery state rather than hiding it;
  10. if canonical apply was prevented, assert project remains at appropriate pre-apply snapshot.

docs.title: WEB-GOLDEN-07 — agent uses semantic selection and enters same review path
docs.text:
Fresh fixture with deterministic provider configured.

Required steps:

  1. import/activate fixture;
  2. navigate/select add semantically;
  3. record selected entity ID through public/test-observable semantic state and base snapshot;
  4. open Session/Agent;
  5. submit exact golden prompt through UI;
  6. wait for real agent operation completion/events;
  7. open candidate result through product Review candidate/equivalent action;
  8. assert normal Migration Review is used;
  9. assert src/lib.rs, old expression, new expression, and validation success;
  10. assert deterministic trace/session/tool evidence contains same selected EntityId and base SnapshotId;
  11. assert live source still base before Apply;
  12. assert no external provider/network access occurred;
  13. assert browser diagnostics clean.

docs.title: Native TUI Golden Suite
docs.text: Extend existing native PTY E2E suite with exact scenario IDs in test names/comments so failures are easy to map.

docs.title: TUI-GOLDEN-01 — onboarded project is active and named symbols are navigable
docs.text:
Launch equivalent of:

srig tui --db <temp-db> --project <temp-project> --git-tracked --import

Drive normal terminal interactions.

Assert:

  • active project context visible;
  • current snapshot visible;
  • explorer contains Calculator;
  • explorer contains add;
  • test reaches add through normal navigation rather than entity-ID injection.

docs.title: TUI-GOLDEN-02 — selected method opens source projection
docs.text:
Starting from active project:

  1. select add;
  2. invoke source/projection view action;
  3. assert terminal shows src/lib.rs;
  4. assert terminal shows left + right;
  5. assert current/base snapshot context is visible/inspectable;
  6. return to explorer and ensure selection remains coherent.

docs.title: TUI-GOLDEN-03 — create review apply and observe durable successor
docs.text:
Fresh fixture.

Required steps:

  1. select/open add source;
  2. use the task-119 terminal edit interaction to replace base expression with accepted expression;
  3. propose/review;
  4. assert old/new expressions visible;
  5. wait for validation success;
  6. read disk from harness and assert base source still present before apply;
  7. invoke Apply;
  8. wait for explicit successful operation/materialization state;
  9. assert terminal current snapshot changes;
  10. read disk and assert accepted expression;
  11. open projection/history and assert successor/change;
  12. exit TUI cleanly;
  13. restart TUI against same database/project;
  14. navigate/select add and assert accepted expression/current successor persists.

docs.title: TUI-GOLDEN-04 — stale external edit is protected
docs.text:
Fresh fixture.

  1. create valid reviewed candidate;
  2. externally add // external edit from harness;
  3. invoke Apply;
  4. assert terminal shows conflict/stale/effect recovery state;
  5. read disk and assert external marker remains;
  6. assert terminal never reports complete successful write-back for stale candidate.

docs.title: TUI-GOLDEN-05 — agent candidate uses selected semantic scope
docs.text:
Fresh fixture with deterministic provider.

  1. navigate/select add;
  2. record base snapshot/selected entity through public fixture/helper evidence;
  3. open TUI session/agent input;
  4. submit golden prompt;
  5. wait for operation completion;
  6. navigate to resulting normal candidate review;
  7. assert old/new source and validation;
  8. inspect deterministic trace/session/tool record and assert exact selected EntityId + SnapshotId;
  9. read disk and assert base source remains before user acceptance;
  10. assert no network provider was used.

docs.title: Cross-Surface Golden Conformance Suite
docs.text:
Add/extend scriberig-conformance or the repository's current cross-surface test owner.

Required tests:

docs.title: GOLDEN-CONFORMANCE-01 — workspace equivalence
docs.text: Embedded application and server/client resolution for same ProjectId return equivalent project snapshot/root.

docs.title: GOLDEN-CONFORMANCE-02 — semantic selection equivalence
docs.text: Public navigation reaches the same add EntityId/SnapshotId across embedded application and remote client. Web/TUI adapters/models must preserve that identity rather than translate it into private IDs.

docs.title: GOLDEN-CONFORMANCE-03 — source projection equivalence
docs.text: Rendering add at the same exact snapshot yields equivalent source-relative path/text/mapping through embedded and remote public paths.

docs.title: GOLDEN-CONFORMANCE-04 — human initiation does not change migration meaning
docs.text: Equivalent human edit initiated through available surface adapters produces the same semantic/source change meaning. Random migration IDs/timestamps may differ.

docs.title: GOLDEN-CONFORMANCE-05 — stale apply semantics
docs.text: Stale base is rejected consistently through embedded and server/client application operation.

docs.title: GOLDEN-CONFORMANCE-06 — multi-project isolation
docs.text: Applying project A candidate advances/materializes only A; B root/files unchanged.

docs.title: GOLDEN-CONFORMANCE-07 — agent uses shared change type
docs.text: Agent result candidate can be consumed by the same migration detail/validation/apply public APIs as a human candidate. No agent-specific canonical patch type bypasses them.

docs.title: Failure Artifact Requirements
docs.text:
When browser golden tests fail, preserve/report enough evidence to debug without rerunning blindly:

Playwright trace/screenshot when configured
browser console/page errors
server stdout/stderr log
operation error/result diagnostics
temp fixture path or captured git diff when safe
current project/snapshot identifiers

When TUI golden tests fail, preserve/report:

PTY transcript/final screen
process exit status
stderr/logs
fixture git diff/current file content
project/snapshot identifiers

Do not dump secrets. Deterministic provider uses no secrets.

docs.title: Timing and Flake Rules
docs.text:
Do not use long arbitrary sleeps as synchronization.

Browser tests wait for:

  • accessible UI state;
  • operation terminal state;
  • network response only when paired with user outcome;
  • authoritative refreshed snapshot text/state.

TUI tests wait for expected screen token/state with bounded timeout through existing harness helpers.

Agent tests wait for operation lifecycle/event result.

Filesystem assertions should retry only when architecture is explicitly asynchronous and there is a durable operation/effect state indicating completion is pending.

Do not weaken content assertions to substring-free generic states such as Ready merely to reduce flakes.

docs.title: Test Independence
docs.text:
Except where a scenario explicitly tests reload/restart persistence, each golden test gets fresh fixture/db state.

Do not make WEB-GOLDEN-04 depend on WEB-GOLDEN-03 having run earlier in the test process unless the framework fixture deliberately scopes them as one serial scenario with clear setup. Prefer independent tests/helpers for parallel reliability.

Do not depend on test execution order across files.

docs.title: Product Gate Commands
docs.text:
Add stable repository commands/scripts for the product gate if equivalents do not exist.

Prefer commands such as:

make test-product-golden

or repository-idiomatic script names that compose:

browser golden e2e
native TUI golden e2e
cross-surface golden conformance

Do not introduce a Make target that silently skips unavailable components and exits success.

Document exact commands in:

tests/product-golden/README.md

and reference them from the top-level README or contributor/testing documentation where appropriate.

docs.title: Normal Quality Gate Integration
docs.text:
Inspect tools/check.sh, CI workflows, Makefile, and package scripts.

Ensure the product golden gate runs in CI in addition to existing unit/integration/static checks.

If product E2E is too environment-specific for every local tools/check.sh invocation, use an explicit separate mandatory CI job/target and document that distinction. The full release/merge quality policy must not omit it.

Do not remove existing checks to make room for E2E.

docs.title: Update Completion/Status Documentation
docs.text:
Once and only once all tests pass:

  • update capabilities.toml statuses from implemented to verified for the exact surfaces proven;
  • update Level-3 tasks 117-122 checklists based on actual evidence;
  • update master task 116 checklist last;
  • update README product status with precise useful workflow and remaining limitations;
  • do not claim unsupported languages/edit workflows are complete.

Earlier Level-3 checked tasks remain historical subsystem records and should carry/retain the product-verification caveat introduced by this design program.

docs.title: Required Final Verification
docs.text:
From clean working tree/environment suitable for repository development, run the authoritative equivalents of:

python3 tools/lint_repo.py
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
pnpm --dir web format:check
pnpm --dir web typecheck
pnpm --dir web test
pnpm --dir web build

Then run the complete product golden command(s) that execute:

WEB-GOLDEN-01 through WEB-GOLDEN-07
TUI-GOLDEN-01 through TUI-GOLDEN-05
GOLDEN-CONFORMANCE-01 through GOLDEN-CONFORMANCE-07

If a test is skipped, quarantined, todo, ignored, or conditionally disabled in the normal supported test environment, the corresponding checklist item is not complete.

docs.title: Enable Agent Bootstrap and Project Onboarding From an Empty Database
Objective
docs.text:
Make the native TUI capable of starting a normal agent operation when no project exists, and let that agent onboard the TUI's current working directory through shared project scan/import/workspace operations.

Required user-level result:

fresh SQLite database
+ launch `srig tui --db <db>` from a project checkout
+ no active project
+ type "Onboard the current project."
-> agent discovers onboarding capability
-> scans the trusted current working directory
-> reviews the persisted manifest
-> imports that exact manifest
-> resolves/activates the new project workspace P@S0
-> returns a durable onboarding result

Do not require --project, --import, a preexisting ProjectId, or manual entity IDs for this flow.

This task is prerequisite 123 for the self-hosting sequence. Complete it before task 124 relies on semantic-first post-onboarding context.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

design/level-1/009. agent interaction and sessions.md
design/level-1/013. vertical product completion and end to end usability.md
design/level-1/014. agent native semantic self hosting.md
design/level-2/023. agent runtime model provider and branch orchestration.md
design/level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md
design/level-2/025. first useful project workflow vertical slice.md
design/level-2/026. agent native self hosting golden workflow.md
design/level-3/024. implement project onboarding across surfaces.md
design/level-3/103. implement tui sessions agent interaction and operation observation.md
design/level-3/104. wire srig tui to local application composition.md
design/level-3/107. extend session records for model execution and branch results.md
design/level-3/109. implement branch context compiler and model request cache.md
design/level-3/110. implement nested branch orchestrator and trusted tool loop.md
design/level-3/111. expose agent execution through application protocol server and clients.md
design/level-3/117. implement active project workspace across application web and tui.md

If filenames were renumbered, locate them by title.

Inspect existing TUI startup composition, agent start request shape, runtime environment/context construction, project scan/import service, agent tool catalog, and active workspace resolution before adding concepts.

docs.title: Required Starting State
docs.text:
The focused test starts from:

working directory = temporary copy of a Git-backed project
database path = new nonexistent/empty SQLite path
project catalog = empty
active project = none

Launch the real/native composition equivalent to:

srig tui --db <fresh-db>

The TUI must start successfully and allow entering agent mode/input even though no active project exists.

A blank project catalog is normal bootstrap state, not a fatal application error.

docs.title: Trusted Bootstrap Context
docs.text:
The local application composition must provide a bounded runtime context that an authorized onboarding tool can use.

It must contain or be able to resolve at least:

current working directory
selected database/runtime identity
principal/capability context
agent/provider profile

Do not encode the current working directory into prompt text as the only authoritative source.

Do not create a fake ProjectId/root for it before scan.

The path is trusted local environmental context supplied by the product composition and remains distinct from semantic project identity until onboarding completes.

Remote agent surfaces must not inherit an arbitrary server process working directory as an authorized project path unless existing server root authorization explicitly permits it.

docs.title: Agent Start Without Project Scope
docs.text:
Review existing agent start validation.

Allow a project-less start only when the selected agent profile/context permits bootstrap operations.

The durable operation/session/branch still exists normally:

OperationId
SessionId
BranchId
HumanInput

The operation input should record that no active semantic project existed at start plus the trusted bootstrap environment reference necessary for authorized tools.

Do not weaken the normal requirement for exact semantic scope on operations that actually target existing project entities. This exception is for bootstrap capability discovery/onboarding, not for arbitrary project mutation.

docs.title: Bootstrap Tool Catalog
docs.text:
The initial trusted catalog must expose a small bounded set sufficient for onboarding.

Conceptually include existing/shared tools equivalent to:

capabilities
project.scan
project.import
project.workspace
inspect/list manifest where needed
operation observation/result helpers

Reuse the normal capability-filtered agent catalog and application operations.

Do not add:

sqlite_query
project_table_insert
recursive_read_every_file
set_current_snapshot_directly

as onboarding shortcuts.

If project scan/import are not currently registered as agent tools, add adapters that delegate to the shared scriberig-project/application operations. They must not reimplement scan/import in scriberig-agent-runtime.

docs.title: project.scan Agent Contract
docs.text:
The agent-facing scan tool accepts a trusted/resolved path reference or a path allowed by the local capability context and existing security policy.

For the golden command, the model should be able to request conceptually:

project.scan {
  path: current_working_directory,
  name: "scriberig" or inferred/default,
  selection_policy: git_tracked
}

Use the existing deterministic scan service.

The result exposed to the model is bounded but includes stable references:

ProjectId
manifest/scan identity
canonical project metadata
file/classification summary
diagnostics

The complete persisted manifest remains inspectable through stable references rather than injected wholesale into model context.

docs.title: Manifest Review Contract
docs.text:
Before import, the scripted/deterministic golden agent must inspect enough persisted manifest state to prove it is importing the intended checkout.

Provide existing or minimal shared read operations for:

manifest summary
bounded/paginated file listing
classification/diagnostics

The agent must be able to establish at least:

  • manifest is non-empty;
  • repository-defining files such as Cargo.toml are present for the Scriberig fixture;
  • root/project identity is intended;
  • no blocking scan error exists.

Do not require loading every file body into the model to review a manifest.

docs.title: project.import Agent Contract
docs.text:
The import tool receives the exact persisted manifest/scan reference returned by scan.

It must delegate to the existing project import service and inherit all existing guarantees:

  • import only persisted manifest data;
  • preserve exact source artifacts;
  • invoke selected adapters;
  • record ownership;
  • create immutable successor state;
  • atomically promote the project root/status according to existing transaction rules;
  • preserve prior valid state on import failure.

For the first successful import, return stable references including:

ProjectId P
SnapshotId S0
project semantic root where available
structured diagnostics

docs.title: Resolve and Activate Workspace
docs.text:
After import, the agent or application flow must call the same project workspace resolution used by product activation.

Resolve authoritative:

project_id = P
snapshot_id = S0
root_entity_id = R

Then activate it in the TUI's client/product state using the existing ActiveProjectWorkspace path.

Do not create a TUI-only project activation mutation.

The agent's operation result and the TUI state may both reference the workspace, but server/application project state remains canonical.

docs.title: Minimal Semantic Smoke Check
docs.text:
The deterministic golden provider for this task should, after workspace resolution, request at least one normal semantic inspection/search proving the imported root is useful.

Use existing public operations such as:

inspect root R at S0
find a known project source/package/config entity

Do not complete the onboarding golden response immediately after receiving status=imported.

The agent's terminal response should only claim onboarding after semantic workspace resolution/check succeeds.

docs.title: Durable Branch Result
docs.text:
Persist a compact branch/operation result equivalent to:

purpose = onboard current project
project_id = P
snapshot_id = S0
root_entity_id = R
manifest_ref = M0
outcome = success
important refs = [...]

Reuse existing BranchResult/operation result types where possible.

Do not store the only copy of these references in TUI local state or transient streaming events.

After disconnect/reopen, session inspection must recover them.

docs.title: TUI Behavior
docs.text:
Required visible behavior:

  1. launch with fresh DB;
  2. agent input is available;
  3. UI indicates no active project initially;
  4. submit Onboard the current project.;
  5. operation/progress is observable;
  6. on success, active project name/context and non-empty current snapshot become visible;
  7. agent response confirms onboarding succinctly;
  8. semantic explorer/navigation can use the newly activated root without restart.

The TUI may summarize scan/import progress, but must not implement scan/import logic itself.

docs.title: Security and Authorization Tests
docs.text:
Add focused coverage for:

  • bootstrap scan uses only path permitted by local runtime context;
  • remote/server composition cannot use an unauthorized arbitrary cwd/path;
  • path escape/invalid path errors are structured;
  • agent lacking project-scan capability cannot call it even if prompt requests onboarding;
  • import tool cannot import a manifest belonging to a different unauthorized project/context;
  • no direct database tool is present in the golden catalog.

docs.title: BOOTSTRAP-AGENT-01 — project-less agent start
docs.text: Create a fresh DB with no project. Start agent operation through public application API with bootstrap context. Assert normal session/branch/operation identities exist and no fake active project is created merely by starting.

docs.title: BOOTSTRAP-CATALOG-01 — bounded onboarding catalog
docs.text: Assert authorized bootstrap agent can discover scan/import/workspace operations and cannot see direct storage mutation tools.

docs.title: BOOTSTRAP-SCAN-01 — trusted cwd scan
docs.text: Use a temporary Git project, set runtime cwd context, call agent scan tool, and assert returned persisted manifest points to the intended project and Git-tracked set.

docs.title: BOOTSTRAP-IMPORT-01 — exact manifest import
docs.text: Scan, record manifest identity, then import through agent tool. Assert import consumed that manifest and returned a project snapshot/root.

docs.title: BOOTSTRAP-WORKSPACE-01 — import becomes active semantic workspace
docs.text: Resolve/open workspace after import and assert TUI/client state uses exact returned ProjectId/SnapshotId/root.

docs.title: BOOTSTRAP-DURABLE-01 — result survives operation stream
docs.text: Complete onboarding, recreate client/session view, and recover project/snapshot/manifest refs from durable operation/session data.

docs.title: BOOTSTRAP-FAIL-01 — import failure does not fake success
docs.text: Use deterministic failing source/import case. Assert no successful active workspace transition, structured diagnostic, and terminal agent result is failure/bounded explanation.

docs.title: TUI-BOOTSTRAP-01 — real PTY
docs.text:
Using real built srig and a fresh DB:

  1. launch from temporary Git project without --project;
  2. assert no active project;
  3. enter agent prompt;
  4. deterministic provider uses normal onboarding tools;
  5. wait for operation completion;
  6. assert active project and snapshot visible;
  7. assert semantic view can be opened;
  8. exit cleanly.

Do not satisfy this with reducer/component-only tests.

docs.title: Deterministic Provider
docs.text:
Extend/reuse the existing deterministic/scripted provider through normal provider contracts.

For this focused task it should behave like a tool-using model:

  1. request capability discovery;
  2. call project scan for current runtime context;
  3. inspect manifest summary/files;
  4. call exact-manifest import;
  5. resolve workspace;
  6. inspect/find a semantic object;
  7. return terminal success with stable project/snapshot refs.

Do not special-case production agent runtime code on the literal prompt string.

No external model/network service is required for these tests.

docs.title: Likely Areas to Change
docs.text:
Inspect actual ownership first. Likely areas include:

crates/scriberig-agent-core/**
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/**
crates/scriberig-app/**
crates/scriberig-project/**
crates/scriberig-protocol/**
crates/scriberig-client/**
crates/scriberig-session/**
crates/scriberig-cli/** and/or apps/scriberig/**
TUI runtime/application composition and PTY tests
capabilities.toml

Do not add project scan/import business logic to terminal widgets.

docs.title: Required Verification
docs.text:
Run focused agent/session/catalog/project/app tests plus real PTY bootstrap onboarding.

Then run at least repository-standard equivalents of:

cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo test for affected crates

and the existing agent/TUI conformance suites affected by the change.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] TUI can start normally with a fresh DB and no project.
  • [x] Agent operation can start without semantic project scope in authorized bootstrap mode.
  • [x] Trusted cwd/runtime context is represented separately from semantic project identity.
  • [x] Bootstrap agent catalog is capability-filtered and bounded.
  • [x] Agent project.scan delegates to shared project scan service.
  • [x] Scan result exposes stable project/manifest refs and bounded summary.
  • [x] Agent can review persisted manifest without reading all file bodies.
  • [x] Agent project.import consumes the exact persisted manifest.
  • [x] Import retains existing atomicity/ownership/source-evidence guarantees.
  • [x] Agent resolves exact P@S0 workspace/root after import.
  • [x] TUI activates authoritative workspace without restart.
  • [x] Agent performs at least one semantic smoke check before claiming success.
  • [x] Durable result retains project/snapshot/root/manifest references.
  • [x] Failure/cancellation cannot create a fake active project or hidden source mutation.
  • [x] Unauthorized path/capability cases are rejected.
  • [x] BOOTSTRAP-AGENT-01 passes.
  • [x] BOOTSTRAP-CATALOG-01 passes.
  • [x] BOOTSTRAP-SCAN-01 and BOOTSTRAP-IMPORT-01 pass.
  • [x] BOOTSTRAP-WORKSPACE-01 passes.
  • [x] BOOTSTRAP-DURABLE-01 passes.
  • [x] BOOTSTRAP-FAIL-01 passes.
  • [x] TUI-BOOTSTRAP-01 passes in a real PTY.
  • [x] No external model provider is required by the suite.
  • [x] Affected repository quality gates pass.

Do not begin task 124 with unchecked golden-path prerequisites.

docs.title: Make Onboarded Project Semantic Context Primary for Agent Discovery
Objective
docs.text:
After task 123 onboards the current checkout, make the resulting exact project workspace the authoritative context for subsequent agent work, and prove that nested agent branches can discover repository architecture semantically while returning compact durable results to their parent.

Required transition:

bootstrap environment path
    -> onboard project P@S0
    -> continuation bound to P@S0
    -> semantic find/inspect/render/follow
    -> nested read-only discovery branch
    -> compact BranchResult

This task does not implement project-wide source changes yet. It prepares exact semantic discovery/context so task 125 can build changes from reliable targets.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

design/level-1/009. agent interaction and sessions.md
design/level-1/014. agent native semantic self hosting.md
design/level-2/023. agent runtime model provider and branch orchestration.md
design/level-2/026. agent native self hosting golden workflow.md
design/level-3/094. implement universal query handles scope and pagination.md
design/level-3/095. implement inspect list and follow read operations.md
design/level-3/107. extend session records for model execution and branch results.md
design/level-3/109. implement branch context compiler and model request cache.md
design/level-3/110. implement nested branch orchestrator and trusted tool loop.md
design/level-3/115. verify agent branch isolation and cross surface conformance.md
design/level-3/117. implement active project workspace across application web and tui.md
design/level-3/118. implement named semantic code navigation and rust source projection.md
design/level-3/123. enable agent bootstrap and project onboarding from empty database.md

Inspect existing branch context compiler, session result records, tool catalog filtering, semantic selection/project scope types, query/find/inspect/render adapters, and TUI continuation behavior before adding fields.

docs.title: Exact Continuation Scope
docs.text:
When onboarding completes, subsequent agent continuation in the same TUI session must carry exact semantic project context equivalent to:

project_id = P
snapshot_id = S0
root_entity_id = R
optional current semantic selection

This structured scope is authoritative.

Do not reduce it to prompt text such as:

"we are in /tmp/scriberig"

or to a mutable implicit global project.

The continuation may still retain trusted environment metadata as supplementary context, but project semantic operations resolve against the exact project/snapshot.

docs.title: Context Compiler Behavior
docs.text:
Extend/reuse the existing branch context compiler so it can compile a project-oriented model request containing a bounded orientation summary such as:

active project identity/display name
exact current/base snapshot
semantic root/selection handles
relevant recent parent branch result(s)
small capability catalog

Do not inject the entire imported repository, entire raw semantic graph, or entire onboarding transcript into the provider request.

The model should discover details through tools.

Context/cache keys must include exact semantic/project/branch/tool-catalog inputs according to existing cache design. A cached request built for a different snapshot must not be reused as if it described S0.

docs.title: Semantic Read Catalog
docs.text:
For an onboarded source project, the authorized agent should be able to discover/use shared operations equivalent to:

capabilities
inspect
list
follow
find
query
render
history where useful

Use existing public application/query/projection operations.

Do not add a second agent-only semantic search engine.

Tool results should return stable handles plus bounded summaries and pagination rather than unbounded source/graph dumps.

docs.title: Project Guidance Discovery
docs.text:
The golden repository task must be able to discover repository guidance through the imported semantic project.

The deterministic provider should locate objects corresponding to:

AGENTS.md
design/AGENTS.md
relevant Level 1/2 design documents

through semantic find/navigation and render their source projection as needed.

The proof must establish that the agent can retrieve the exact imported project source representation at S0.

A direct raw filesystem read may remain available as an explicitly authorized fallback for unsupported cases, but the golden discovery path must use semantic project operations after onboarding.

docs.title: Architecture Discovery Target
docs.text:
For the later PHP extension, the agent must be able to discover semantic/source references for at least:

shared code domain
representative Tree-sitter language adapter (Python is a useful precedent)
project scan/classification logic
project adapter/import dispatch
workspace Cargo metadata
domain conformance/test support
relevant capability/format registry metadata

The test should not hard-code entity IDs. It may use stable names/text/kinds and then inspect the returned semantic handles.

Path strings may appear in results as human/source context, but semantic identity/snapshot remain attached.

docs.title: Nested Read-Only Discovery Branch
docs.text:
The parent branch starts a child branch with an explicit request equivalent to:

purpose = determine minimal extension points for PHP source ingestion
base project = P
base snapshot = S0
selection = project/root or relevant semantic scope
capabilities = read-only semantic operations
expected result = architecture map

The child must not receive:

change.propose
change.apply
direct filesystem write
direct database mutation

unless some unrelated existing policy explicitly grants them; the golden child test must verify they are absent/denied.

docs.title: Child Branch Context Isolation
docs.text:
The child receives only deliberately inherited context plus its own task.

At minimum, tests must prove:

  • child project/snapshot equals P@S0;
  • child tool catalog is the requested bounded read-only subset;
  • child does not see unrelated parent-only secret/transient model data;
  • child operations are durably associated with child BranchId;
  • child can inspect project semantic references returned by its own tools;
  • cancellation/failure does not mutate parent/project state.

Reuse existing branch isolation mechanisms instead of adding self-hosting-specific branch storage.

docs.title: Architecture BranchResult
docs.text:
On successful completion, the child produces a durable compact result equivalent to:

purpose
base project P
base snapshot S0
conclusion = use shared code-domain language adapter pattern
required integration areas = [...]
important semantic/source refs = [...]
notable constraints = [...]
outcome = success

The important references should remain addressable by the parent without converting them into bare unscoped file paths.

The result may contain source-relative paths for human readability, but where semantic handles exist they should be included.

docs.title: Parent Continuation Must Use Result, Not Full Transcript
docs.text:
After child completion, compile the next parent model context from:

parent's prior context
child BranchResult
relevant stable refs
new user/task state

Do not automatically append every child model request, response, tool invocation, and tool result into the parent's active transcript.

Those details remain retrievable through session/branch inspection if the parent explicitly needs them.

Add an assertion/captured provider request proving bounded result inheritance.

docs.title: Staleness Rules
docs.text:
The discovery result is bound to S0.

If the project current snapshot advances before the parent uses the result to construct a change, the parent must not treat old source mappings/revisions as silently current.

Later code-edit operations must re-resolve important targets against the intended exact base.

The branch result may remain useful historical evidence, but its exact base remains visible.

Do not rewrite stored branch result references to a newer snapshot.

docs.title: TUI Session Behavior
docs.text:
After task 123 onboarding, the user can submit a second agent instruction in the same session without manually selecting a project again.

The TUI/session view should make it possible to inspect:

active project P
snapshot S0
parent branch
nested discovery branch
branch status/result

The TUI does not need to render every child token stream inline by default.

A compact nested activity/result presentation is preferred, with explicit navigation into child detail when requested.

docs.title: Semantic-First Regression Rule
docs.text:
The golden provider trace for this task must demonstrate that after onboarding it uses semantic operations to locate repository guidance/architecture.

An implementation fails the golden intent if the provider is handed a universal unrestricted grep/read/write filesystem tool and solves all discovery outside Scriberig semantic state while P@S0 is ignored.

This does not ban all filesystem capabilities in Scriberig. It makes the semantic project useful and primary for this scenario.

docs.title: SEMANTIC-CONTEXT-01 — continuation binds exact project/snapshot
docs.text: Onboard a fixture through task 123, continue the session, capture normalized provider request/tool context, and assert ProjectId, SnapshotId, and root match the active workspace.

docs.title: SEMANTIC-CONTEXT-02 — no implicit retarget
docs.text: Advance project state after capturing a context/result and assert an exact-S0 read/change request does not silently resolve as a different snapshot.

docs.title: SEMANTIC-DISCOVERY-01 — find repository guidance
docs.text: Using an onboarded fixture containing AGENTS.md, use public semantic find then render and assert exact guidance source is retrieved at S0.

docs.title: SEMANTIC-DISCOVERY-02 — architecture refs are semantic
docs.text: Locate representative language adapter and project scanner/import objects without hard-coded entity IDs. Assert returned refs include exact project/snapshot/semantic identity sufficient for later inspection.

docs.title: BRANCH-DISCOVERY-01 — read-only child catalog
docs.text: Start nested architecture discovery branch. Assert child has expected semantic read tools and lacks candidate/apply/direct-write tools.

docs.title: BRANCH-DISCOVERY-02 — compact result inheritance
docs.text: Complete child with architecture map. Capture next parent model request and assert it contains the compact BranchResult/stable refs but not the entire child transcript.

docs.title: BRANCH-DISCOVERY-03 — durable child details
docs.text: Reopen session/client and prove full child operation/tool history remains separately inspectable despite not being replayed to parent.

docs.title: BRANCH-DISCOVERY-04 — cancellation isolation
docs.text: Cancel child during discovery and assert project/current snapshot/parent durable state is not mutated unexpectedly.

docs.title: TUI-SEMANTIC-DISCOVERY-01 — real PTY continuation
docs.text: Onboard through the previous real-PTY flow, submit a deterministic second instruction that triggers read-only architecture discovery, and verify nested branch/result is observable while active project remains P@S0.

docs.title: Deterministic Provider Behavior
docs.text:
Extend the existing scripted provider configuration, not production prompt branching.

For this test world, after receiving the second instruction it should:

  1. observe exact P@S0 context;
  2. request capability discovery as needed;
  3. find/render project guidance semantically;
  4. start the read-only child branch through normal branch tool/operation if that is provider-visible, or follow existing orchestrator policy that creates it from provider request;
  5. child finds/inspects/render relevant architecture objects;
  6. child returns compact architecture result;
  7. parent produces a concise terminal response or proceeds to the next scripted stage in later tasks.

Capture trace evidence for exact scope and catalog.

No external model service is required.

docs.title: Likely Areas to Change
docs.text:
Inspect actual owners first. Likely:

crates/scriberig-agent-core/**
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/**
crates/scriberig-session/**
crates/scriberig-app/**
crates/scriberig-query/**
crates/scriberig-projection/**
crates/scriberig-protocol/**
crates/scriberig-client/**
crates/scriberig-conformance/**
TUI session/agent views under the current native product owner
agent deterministic provider fixtures/tests
capabilities.toml

Do not add semantic-source parsing logic to the TUI/provider fixture.

docs.title: Required Verification
docs.text:
Run focused branch/context/query/projection/session tests, existing agent branch isolation conformance, and native PTY continuation coverage.

Then at least:

cargo check --workspace --all-targets

plus repository-standard affected test targets.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Post-onboarding continuation carries structured exact P@S0 and root context.
  • [x] Context compiler treats project/snapshot/selection as authoritative scope.
  • [x] Cached model requests cannot cross semantic snapshot/tool-catalog boundaries incorrectly.
  • [x] Authorized agent can discover shared semantic read tools progressively.
  • [x] Repository guidance can be found/rendered through imported semantic project state.
  • [x] Representative language adapter/scanner/import targets can be discovered without hard-coded entity IDs.
  • [x] Nested architecture discovery branch receives exact P@S0.
  • [x] Discovery child is demonstrably read-only/capability-bounded.
  • [x] Child operations are durably branch-associated.
  • [x] Child returns compact stable-reference BranchResult.
  • [x] Parent continuation inherits result, not complete child transcript.
  • [x] Full child detail remains separately inspectable after restart/client recreation.
  • [x] Stale discovery refs remain explicitly bound to their base snapshot.
  • [x] SEMANTIC-CONTEXT-01 and SEMANTIC-CONTEXT-02 pass.
  • [x] SEMANTIC-DISCOVERY-01 and SEMANTIC-DISCOVERY-02 pass.
  • [x] BRANCH-DISCOVERY-01 through BRANCH-DISCOVERY-04 pass.
  • [x] TUI-SEMANTIC-DISCOVERY-01 passes in a real PTY.
  • [x] No external model provider is required.
  • [x] Affected repository quality gates pass.

Do not begin project-wide candidate work in task 125 by bypassing these exact semantic context rules.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Extend the normal candidate/migration path so one exact-base candidate can create, update, and delete multiple project source files as one coherent reviewed change.

The required self-hosting shape is conceptually:

P@S0
-> Candidate C1
   Create crates/domains/scriberig-domain-php/Cargo.toml
   Create crates/domains/scriberig-domain-php/src/lib.rs
   Update workspace Cargo.toml
   Update project scan/import source
   Add tests/fixtures
   Update lock/registry metadata as needed
-> inspect/render/review C1

Before Apply:

P.current == S0
live checkout bytes == base checkout bytes
created candidate files do not exist in the live checkout

This task creates/reviews the candidate only. Isolated whole-project validation and multi-file Apply/materialization are completed by task 126.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md
design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
design/level-1/014. agent native semantic self hosting.md
design/level-2/027. project wide candidate workspaces validation and materialization.md
design/level-3/036. implement migration operations and provenance.md
design/level-3/049. implement branches workspaces and promotion.md
design/level-3/050. implement candidate promotion and approval pipeline.md
design/level-3/062. implement universal semantic diff.md
design/level-3/075. implement change queries and summaries.md
design/level-3/078. implement projection specifications rendering and adapter api.md
design/level-3/079. implement change subsystem conformance suite.md
design/level-3/080. implement filesystem projection ownership hashing and atomic io.md
design/level-3/119. implement projection edit candidate review and validation.md
design/level-3/120. implement migration apply filesystem materialization refresh and conflict recovery.md
design/level-3/121. implement semantically scoped agent candidate through shared change path.md

Inspect current migration operation types, proposal/candidate snapshot construction, source projection ownership, candidate diff APIs, protocol/client representations, and agent change tool adapters before inventing new types.

docs.title: Reuse the Canonical Change Type
docs.text:
Do not introduce a canonical AgentRepositoryPatch, TuiPatch, or GitPatchCandidate that bypasses existing migration/proposal semantics.

Extend the normal change representation so one migration/candidate can contain the source effects required by a coherent project change.

A transient provider-facing text patch is acceptable only if it is converted into the shared candidate representation before it becomes durable/reviewable.

docs.title: Source Effect Semantics
docs.text:
Support shared source effects equivalent to:

Create {
  relative_path,
  expected_absence,
  new_content/projection,
  metadata
}

Update {
  relative_path,
  expected_base_source/digest,
  new_content/projection,
  metadata
}

Delete {
  relative_path,
  expected_base_source/digest,
  metadata
}

Fit these concepts into existing migration operations where possible.

Do not accept authoritative client-provided absolute target paths.

Every effect belongs to:

project_id
exact base snapshot
candidate/migration id

docs.title: Exact Base and Per-Path Preconditions
docs.text:
The aggregate candidate must name one exact project base snapshot.

For update/delete, retain the exact source identity/digest expected by the candidate.

For create, retain expected absence/conflict semantics.

Do not defer all source preconditions until filesystem write time if candidate construction can already prove the request is mismatched to its base.

A client request that says "update path X" without sufficient exact base/source context must either be enriched from the exact selected candidate base by trusted application code or rejected as ambiguous.

docs.title: Project-Relative Path Safety
docs.text:
Normalize/validate project-relative paths through shared project/projection/filesystem helpers.

Candidate creation must reject obvious invalid targets such as:

../outside
absolute paths
empty/invalid paths
paths associated with a different project context

Final symlink/external filesystem checks still happen through task 126/existing apply infrastructure.

Do not duplicate path policy independently in agent runtime and TUI.

docs.title: Create-New-File Candidate Projection
docs.text:
A proposed new source file must be renderable/reviewable even though it is absent from the live checkout.

Add or extend candidate projection APIs so callers can request conceptually:

candidate C / changed path -> proposed source text

The response includes:

candidate/base context
relative path
effect kind = create
new source text/content identity
semantic mapping when candidate reconciliation provides one

Do not create the live file early merely to reuse the existing file renderer.

docs.title: Update Existing File Candidate Projection
docs.text:
For an update effect, review/render must expose:

relative path
base source identity/text
candidate source identity/text
diff
semantic context when available

The base content comes from exact project/candidate base state, not from an unchecked fresh read presented as historical truth.

docs.title: Delete Candidate Projection
docs.text:
For delete effects, review must show:

relative path
effect kind = delete
base source/content identity
candidate absence

The live source remains present before acceptance.

docs.title: Aggregate Candidate Result
docs.text:
Candidate creation returns one durable identity and exact context equivalent to:

candidate/migration id
project id
base snapshot
candidate/result snapshot if constructed
provenance
changed path count
create/update/delete counts

If candidate semantic reconciliation creates a candidate snapshot, all source effects must be represented coherently in that candidate state.

Do not make each file its own independently applicable migration when the user's one feature requires all files together.

docs.title: Candidate Snapshot and New Source Entities
docs.text:
Where the repository's projection/import/reconciliation model supports representing the candidate source semantically before apply, new source files may create candidate-only source/domain entities.

These entities must be reachable only in candidate/result state and must not become current project ownership merely because candidate construction succeeded.

If full semantic reconciliation for a new path is not yet available generically, retain truthful source-level candidate effects and allow validators to operate on the candidate workspace in task 126. Do not fabricate semantic entities.

docs.title: Multi-File Request Shape
docs.text:
Extend the public application operation used by human/agent callers to accept a bounded set of source effects or an equivalent structured project edit.

The request must include/resolve:

project id
exact base snapshot
ordered effects
provenance/initiating surface

Order should be deterministic for hashing/review even when semantic meaning is set-like.

Enforce reasonable request/result size limits and use content/blob references if existing infrastructure supports large payloads.

docs.title: Agent Tool Contract
docs.text:
Extend the existing agent change tool rather than adding a privileged write tool.

The provider-facing tool may expose a coarse shape equivalent to:

propose_project_change {
  base project/snapshot,
  files: [create/update/delete ...]
}

but it must delegate to the shared application/migration operation.

The tool result returns stable CandidateId/migration identity, not merely "patch applied" text.

The implementation branch in the golden scenario does not receive normal Apply authority.

docs.title: Human/Agent Equivalence
docs.text:
Add conformance proving a project-wide candidate produced through an agent adapter and an equivalent candidate produced directly through public application APIs have the same canonical change meaning.

Random IDs/timestamps/provenance initiator may differ.

Both must be consumable by the same:

change detail
changed path listing
source diff/render
validation
apply
history

interfaces.

docs.title: Aggregate Diff Contract
docs.text:
Extend existing diff/change-summary output to list all changed paths and effect kinds.

Required structure is equivalent to:

Candidate C
Base S0
Changes:
  A path/to/new-file
  M Cargo.toml
  M crates/scriberig-project/src/...
  D optional/old-file

Per-path detail exposes old/new text or another faithful source diff representation.

Semantic diff may supplement source diff where reconciliation supports it.

Do not generate semantic claims solely by parsing UI diff strings.

docs.title: TUI Review Scaling
docs.text:
Extend/reuse the normal TUI change review so it can display a candidate with many changed paths.

Required interaction:

  • show candidate/base/provenance summary;
  • show changed path list with create/update/delete markers;
  • select a path;
  • inspect old/new or unified source diff;
  • return to path list without losing candidate context;
  • show validation placeholder/state from shared candidate even before task 126 adds full project profile;
  • no Apply success behavior implemented privately here.

Keep large file content bounded/scrollable.

docs.title: Protocol and Clients
docs.text:
Extend canonical protocol/client types once so remote/web/TUI adapters can inspect the same project-wide candidate.

Do not serialize a Rust internal enum differently for every surface without a shared protocol contract.

Required public capabilities include conceptual equivalents of:

create project candidate
get candidate detail
list/page candidate changed paths
get candidate path diff/render

Preserve backward compatibility/versioning according to existing protocol rules.

docs.title: Durability and Restart
docs.text:
After candidate creation, close/reopen application/client/session views and prove:

  • candidate identity remains valid;
  • exact base snapshot remains visible;
  • changed paths/effect kinds remain inspectable;
  • candidate-only new file content can still be rendered;
  • live project root/tree remain base.

Do not rely on an in-memory provider response to reconstruct the patch.

docs.title: Negative Cases
docs.text:
Cover at least:

  • duplicate conflicting effects for the same path in one request -> reject/normalize deterministically, never ambiguous apply;
  • create path already represented in exact base when expected absent -> reject;
  • update/delete path missing from exact base -> reject unless operation semantics explicitly support that state;
  • path escape -> reject;
  • project/base mismatch -> reject;
  • stale base at review -> mark stale according to existing change rules;
  • candidate request cancellation/failure -> no current snapshot/live filesystem mutation;
  • oversized source effect -> structured limit/error rather than uncontrolled memory use.

docs.title: PROJECT-CANDIDATE-01 — create + update
docs.text: Against a temporary project, create one candidate that adds a new Rust source file and updates an existing config/source file. Assert one candidate identity, exact base, live files unchanged, and candidate render contains both effects.

docs.title: PROJECT-CANDIDATE-02 — create multiple files
docs.text: Add a small new crate (Cargo.toml + src/lib.rs) plus workspace registration in one candidate. Assert created files are candidate-renderable but absent live.

docs.title: PROJECT-CANDIDATE-03 — delete
docs.text: Propose deletion of an owned file. Assert candidate review shows delete and live file still exists.

docs.title: PROJECT-DIFF-01 — aggregate and per-path review
docs.text: Inspect through public APIs; assert effect list/order/types and representative old/new content.

docs.title: PROJECT-DURABLE-01 — restart/reopen
docs.text: Reopen database/application/client and recover candidate plus new-file content from durable state.

docs.title: PROJECT-AGENT-01 — agent uses shared candidate
docs.text: Script deterministic provider to request a two-file project change. Assert normal candidate returned and no direct file write/current-root advance.

docs.title: PROJECT-EQUIV-01 — direct vs agent initiation
docs.text: Compare equivalent direct/agent candidates semantically and prove both use normal review APIs.

docs.title: TUI-PROJECT-REVIEW-01 — real PTY
docs.text: Open a pre-created project-wide candidate through normal TUI UI, browse create/update path diffs, and assert live tree unchanged.

docs.text:
Locate actual owners. Likely:

crates/scriberig-migration/**
crates/scriberig-projection/**
crates/scriberig-app/**
crates/scriberig-project/**
