TUI change review/application adapter
web shared model/client packages if canonical protocol types require update
capabilities.toml

Use repository search to identify current candidate/migration owner names rather than creating duplicate crates.

docs.title: Required Verification
docs.text:
Run focused change/migration/projection/protocol/client/agent/TUI tests and existing change conformance.

Then at least:

cargo check --workspace --all-targets

plus normal formatting/lint/test gates for affected code.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Normal canonical candidate can contain multiple project source effects.
  • [x] Create/update/delete semantics retain exact project/base/path preconditions.
  • [x] No authoritative absolute target path is accepted from clients.
  • [x] Invalid/path-escape effects are rejected structurally.
  • [x] New files are renderable from candidate state without live creation.
  • [x] Updated files expose exact-base old/new source review.
  • [x] Deleted files remain live until acceptance and are reviewable as deletion.
  • [x] One coherent feature remains one candidate/migration.
  • [x] Candidate creation does not advance project current snapshot.
  • [x] Candidate creation does not mutate live filesystem.
  • [x] Agent project-change tool delegates to shared application candidate operation.
  • [x] Agent result returns normal stable candidate identity.
  • [x] Public protocol/client can list and inspect all changed paths/effect kinds.
  • [x] TUI normal change review can browse multi-file candidate diffs.
  • [x] Candidate survives restart/client recreation with exact new-file content.
  • [x] Direct and agent initiated candidates are canonically equivalent in meaning.
  • [x] PROJECT-CANDIDATE-01 through PROJECT-CANDIDATE-03 pass.
  • [x] PROJECT-DIFF-01 passes.
  • [x] PROJECT-DURABLE-01 passes.
  • [x] PROJECT-AGENT-01 and PROJECT-EQUIV-01 pass.
  • [x] TUI-PROJECT-REVIEW-01 passes in a real PTY.
  • [x] Existing single-projection candidate behavior remains compatible.
  • [x] Affected repository quality gates pass.

Task 126 must use this canonical representation; do not introduce a separate multi-file apply path there.

docs.title: Validate and Apply Project-Wide Candidates Safely
Objective
docs.text:
Complete the project-wide candidate path from task 125: materialize the exact aggregate candidate in isolation for validation, then apply an accepted candidate through exact-base canonical promotion and safe multi-file filesystem effects with truthful conflict/recovery state.

Required successful path:

P@S0
+ project-wide Candidate C1
-> isolated candidate workspace
-> focused/workspace/E2E validation bound to C1
-> normal review enables Apply
-> exact-base/preflight checks
-> canonical successor S1
-> safe create/update/delete effects
-> effect receipts/status
-> active workspace refreshes to P@S1

Required invariant before user Apply:

P.current == S0
live checkout == base checkout
candidate workspace may differ

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

design/level-1/014. agent native semantic self hosting.md
design/level-2/027. project wide candidate workspaces validation and materialization.md
design/level-3/047. implement validation evidence and exact input binding.md
design/level-3/064. implement external effect receipts and reconciliation.md
design/level-3/080. implement filesystem projection ownership hashing and atomic io.md
design/level-3/083. implement filesystem observation synchronization and recovery.md
design/level-3/119. implement projection edit candidate review and validation.md
design/level-3/120. implement migration apply filesystem materialization refresh and conflict recovery.md
design/level-3/125. implement project wide source change candidates.md

Reuse the exact-base/candidate validation/apply/effect semantics already proven for focused Rust edits. Do not invent a second repository checkout or transaction model unless the existing abstractions cannot be extended.

docs.title: Candidate Workspace Contract
docs.text:
Provide a reusable way to materialize the exact source state represented by a project-wide candidate without changing the user's live checkout.

Conceptually:

CandidateWorkspace(C) = BaseProjectSource(C.base) + C.source_effects

It must correctly implement:

  • create: candidate path exists with new bytes;
  • update: candidate path contains proposed bytes;
  • delete: candidate path is absent;
  • unaffected tracked/required files reflect the chosen exact base/source policy;
  • workspace root is isolated from the live project root;
  • build outputs/temp state remain outside canonical project knowledge.

Prefer existing candidate materialization/staging helpers from task 119 and projection infrastructure.

docs.title: Exact Candidate Validation
docs.text:
Every validator result must bind to stable candidate identity/content and exact base according to existing validation evidence rules.

If candidate effects change, previous validation is stale and must not keep Apply enabled.

Structured result includes at least:

validation id
candidate id
base/candidate state identity
profile
status
bounded diagnostics
operation/process result category

Do not decide success by UI strings or shell-output substring matching.

docs.title: Validation Profile Registry
docs.text:
Add/reuse application-level validation profile registration/composition suitable for repository self-hosting.

Profiles are policy identifiers such as:

focused domain tests
project import tests
rust workspace quality checks
fresh-database ingestion E2E

The TUI/provider requests a profile; application/validation infrastructure owns which commands/checks it entails.

Do not encode raw shell pipelines in provider prompts or React/TUI widgets as canonical policy.

docs.title: Process Execution Boundary
docs.text:
Repository validation commands execute through the existing bounded operation/process capability owner.

Requirements:

  • cancellable/bounded according to current operation conventions;
  • working directory is the isolated candidate workspace;
  • environment is controlled/filtered according to validation policy;
  • stdout/stderr retained in bounded structured form/artifact references;
  • timeout/start failure are structured validation failures;
  • child processes are cleaned on cancellation;
  • no command runs in the live project root if it could rewrite source/lock/config as part of validation.

If existing validation invokes cargo check directly in a safe abstraction, extend that abstraction rather than spawning Cargo from agent/TUI code.

docs.title: Dependency Acquisition Capability
docs.text:
A project-wide candidate may add a new declared dependency.

If validation cannot proceed from already available Cargo cache/vendor state, dependency acquisition must be explicit and bounded.

Model it as validation/dependency-resolution capability, not generic agent internet access.

Required evidence includes the resulting locked dependency state that becomes candidate source (Cargo.lock where applicable).

Tests may prewarm/cache dependencies for deterministic CI, but must not fake parser functionality merely to avoid dependency resolution.

No external model-provider network access is required for the deterministic golden suite.

docs.title: PHP Self-Hosting Validation Profiles
docs.text: The final golden scenario will request profiles equivalent to:

docs.title: php-domain-focused
docs.text: Run candidate's PHP adapter tests covering declarations, comments, nested syntax, inline HTML, malformed PHP, and deterministic parse structure.

docs.title: project-import-focused
docs.text: Run candidate's scanner/import/ownership/navigation/projection/regression tests for PHP.

docs.title: rust-workspace
docs.text: Run repository-standard compile/format/lint/test policy appropriate to affected Rust workspace.

docs.title: project-ingestion-e2e
docs.text:
Against the candidate build/workspace, create a fresh Scriberig database and small PHP fixture project; use public scan/import/workspace/semantic operations and prove the new adapter composes.

These are target profiles for the later test fixture. Keep the validation machinery generic.

docs.title: Fresh-Database E2E From Candidate Code
docs.text:
The project-ingestion-e2e profile must test the candidate implementation, not the baseline executable that lacks PHP.

Choose an architecture-consistent approach, for example:

  • build/run a candidate-workspace test/binary through Cargo;
  • run an integration test compiled from candidate source;
  • invoke a candidate-built srig/test harness when appropriate.

The proof must establish:

candidate PHP adapter is actually compiled
.php scan selects PHP
project import creates expected semantic PHP data
public find/inspect/render succeed

A test that only reads the candidate source files and searches for the word php is insufficient.

docs.title: Validation Must Preserve Live Checkout
docs.text:
Add an explicit test that snapshots live relevant files/directories before validation and verifies byte/existence equality afterward.

For the self-hosting shape this includes proving candidate-only created crate files are still absent live before Apply.

Build tooling that writes target/ or caches should be directed to candidate/temp locations so it does not pollute assertions or user checkout unnecessarily.

docs.title: Apply Preconditions
docs.text:
Before accepted project-wide materialization, perform all feasible aggregate preflight checks.

At minimum:

candidate is validated/applicable
project current snapshot == candidate exact base
all relative paths are project-contained and authorized
update/delete expected source digests match live observed base state
create targets satisfy expected absence/conflict policy
ownership/projection identity matches where applicable
symlink escape rules pass

Evaluate the full effect set before performing avoidable writes.

If one path already conflicts, do not knowingly materialize unrelated paths and then report candidate success.

docs.title: Exact-Base Canonical Promotion
docs.text:
Reuse existing migration/project compare-and-swap semantics.

Do not silently rebase a project-wide candidate to a new current snapshot.

A stale candidate may remain inspectable, but normal Apply rejects it until an explicit merge/rebase/reconciliation produces a newly reviewed candidate.

The canonical transition records one migration/change linking base and successor.

docs.title: Multi-File Filesystem Effects
docs.text:
Extend shared filesystem materialization to execute the accepted set of create/update/delete effects safely.

For create/update, use existing atomic sibling/staging write + replace semantics where applicable.

For delete, verify expected source state immediately before destructive effect according to existing ownership/digest policy.

Do not let the agent/TUI execute std::fs::write, rm, or equivalent as the product Apply implementation.

docs.title: Aggregate and Per-Effect Receipts
docs.text:
Application result must make external effect state inspectable.

At aggregate level expose at least:

candidate/migration id
base snapshot
successor snapshot if canonical promotion occurred
project id
overall materialization/effect state

Per path/effect expose enough to distinguish:

created/updated/deleted successfully
not attempted due to preflight conflict
failed during I/O
already satisfied/idempotent recovery
requires reconciliation

Reuse/extend existing external effect receipt types.

Do not collapse partial failure into a misleading single success boolean.

docs.title: Ordering and Partial Failure
docs.text:
SQLite canonical state and multiple filesystem writes cannot be one physical transaction.

Inspect and preserve the ordering architecture established by task 120/external-effect receipts.

Extend it so recovery knows every intended source effect and its state.

If canonical promotion succeeds and effect N fails after some effects succeeded, persist durable recovery evidence sufficient to:

  • tell the product canonical and filesystem states differ;
  • identify completed/incomplete paths;
  • retry safely/idempotently where allowed;
  • avoid rewriting externally changed paths during recovery;
  • avoid claiming full materialization success.

docs.title: Create Conflict Rule
docs.text:
If a candidate proposes creating a path that was absent at base, but an external actor creates that live path before Apply, default behavior is conflict.

Do not silently overwrite the externally created file with candidate content.

A future explicit reconcile/merge can decide how to combine it.

docs.title: Update/Delete Conflict Rule
docs.text:
If live digest/content for an update/delete target no longer matches the candidate's expected base, reject unsafe materialization for that candidate.

Preserve the external bytes.

The UI/result should identify the specific path and expected/observed state in bounded form.

docs.title: TUI Validation and Apply
docs.text:
Extend/reuse normal change review from task 125.

Required behavior:

  1. candidate review shows required validation profiles/progress;
  2. Apply disabled until required policy succeeds;
  3. validation can be started/observed through public application operation;
  4. user can inspect bounded diagnostics;
  5. before Apply, live tree remains base;
  6. Apply invokes shared application operation;
  7. terminal state distinguishes canonical/materialization outcome;
  8. on full success, TUI refreshes authoritative project workspace;
  9. on conflict/effect failure, persistent inspectable state remains available.

No optimistic local snapshot switching before authoritative result.

docs.title: Post-Apply Refresh and History
docs.text:
On successful full path:

P.current = S1
S1 != S0

The TUI/client refreshes project workspace from the application.

History/diff remains able to render base and successor source states and list the complete accepted project-wide change.

Candidate/session provenance remains linked.

docs.title: Multi-Project Isolation
docs.text:
With projects A and B in one database, a project-wide candidate for A:

  • validates/materializes A workspace/path only;
  • advances only A current root;
  • writes only A owned/authorized checkout;
  • cannot use relative-path collisions to modify B;
  • emits project-scoped events so B clients do not adopt A state.

Add conformance coverage.

docs.title: PROJECT-WORKSPACE-VALIDATE-01
docs.text: Candidate creates a small crate and updates workspace metadata. Validator compiles/checks the aggregate candidate successfully only because created files and manifest update coexist in isolated workspace.

docs.title: PROJECT-WORKSPACE-VALIDATE-02
docs.text: Snapshot live tree before/after validation. Assert exact equality for intended source paths and absence of candidate-created paths.

docs.title: PROJECT-WORKSPACE-VALIDATE-03
docs.text: Modify candidate after validation or create superseding candidate. Assert old validation cannot enable Apply for changed candidate.

docs.title: PROJECT-APPLY-01
docs.text: Apply validated create+update candidate. Assert canonical successor and intended live files only after acceptance.

docs.title: PROJECT-APPLY-DELETE-01
docs.text: Apply validated delete effect and verify historical/base source remains renderable while live target is removed only after acceptance.

docs.title: PROJECT-APPLY-STALE-01
docs.text: Advance project snapshot after candidate creation. Assert exact-base rejection and no candidate source effects.

docs.title: PROJECT-CONFLICT-UPDATE-01
docs.text: Externally modify one update target before Apply. Assert external content survives and full-success is not reported.

docs.title: PROJECT-CONFLICT-CREATE-01
docs.text: Externally create candidate's proposed new path. Assert no overwrite and explicit conflict.

docs.title: PROJECT-EFFECT-FAIL-01
docs.text: Inject deterministic I/O failure in middle of multiple effects. Assert durable per-path receipt/recovery status and truthful aggregate result.

docs.title: PROJECT-RECOVERY-01
docs.text: Retry/reconcile deterministic incomplete effect according to existing recovery architecture; assert already-completed effects are handled idempotently and unrelated files untouched.

docs.title: MULTIPROJECT-PROJECT-APPLY-01
docs.text: Apply candidate to A; assert B semantic root/files unchanged.

docs.title: TUI-PROJECT-APPLY-01
docs.text: Real PTY: open multi-file candidate, run/observe validation, assert live base, invoke Apply, verify explicit success, refreshed snapshot, and resulting files.

docs.title: TUI-PROJECT-CONFLICT-01
docs.text: Real PTY: external edit/create conflict before Apply, assert visible conflict and external bytes survive.

docs.title: Likely Areas to Change
docs.text:
Inspect current owners. Likely:

crates/scriberig-migration/**
crates/scriberig-projection/**
crates/scriberig-project/**
crates/scriberig-app/**
crates/scriberig-protocol/**
crates/scriberig-client/**
crates/scriberig-conformance/**
validation/process operation owner
TUI migration/change review and workspace state
existing filesystem effect receipt/recovery code
capabilities.toml

Avoid introducing production global fault flags solely for tests when dependency injection/faultable I/O boundaries already exist.

docs.title: Required Verification
docs.text:
Run focused project-wide validation/apply/effect tests, existing single-file candidate/apply regression suites, protocol/client conformance, native PTY Apply/conflict tests, and multi-project isolation.

Then repository-standard quality gates including at least:

cargo check --workspace --all-targets

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Exact project-wide candidate can be materialized in an isolated workspace.
  • [x] Create/update/delete effects are reflected correctly in candidate workspace.
  • [x] Validators execute against candidate workspace, never live source checkout.
  • [x] Validation evidence binds to exact aggregate candidate content.
  • [x] Changed candidate cannot reuse stale validation evidence.
  • [x] Validation profiles are application policy, not UI/provider shell strings.
  • [x] Process execution is bounded/cancellable and diagnostics structured.
  • [x] Dependency acquisition, when needed, is explicit and bounded.
  • [x] PHP-target validation profiles can be expressed without PHP being preinstalled in baseline.
  • [x] Fresh-database ingestion E2E can execute candidate code/build.
  • [x] Apply performs full feasible preflight before unsafe multi-file writes.
  • [x] Apply uses exact project base compare-and-swap.
  • [x] Create conflicts never silently overwrite external files.
  • [x] Update/delete digest conflicts preserve external content.
  • [x] Shared filesystem infrastructure owns all live source effects.
  • [x] Aggregate and per-path effect receipts are durable/inspectable.
  • [x] Partial I/O failure is never presented as full materialization success.
  • [x] Recovery is bounded/idempotent according to existing effect architecture.
  • [x] TUI validation/review/apply uses public shared operations.
  • [x] Successful Apply refreshes authoritative P@S1 and history.
  • [x] Multi-project isolation is proven.
  • [x] PROJECT-WORKSPACE-VALIDATE-01 through -03 pass.
  • [x] PROJECT-APPLY-01 and PROJECT-APPLY-DELETE-01 pass.
  • [x] PROJECT-APPLY-STALE-01 passes.
  • [x] PROJECT-CONFLICT-UPDATE-01 and PROJECT-CONFLICT-CREATE-01 pass.
  • [x] PROJECT-EFFECT-FAIL-01 and PROJECT-RECOVERY-01 pass.
  • [x] MULTIPROJECT-PROJECT-APPLY-01 passes.
  • [x] TUI-PROJECT-APPLY-01 and TUI-PROJECT-CONFLICT-01 pass in real PTY.
  • [x] Existing focused candidate/apply behavior remains compatible.
  • [x] Affected repository quality gates pass.

Do not begin the full self-hosting product proof while project-wide validation or effect recovery is only simulated.

docs.title: Define PHP Self-Extension Contract and Golden Candidate Fixture
Objective
docs.text:
Create the checked-in reference/test material that defines exactly what the self-hosting agent must add for first-class PHP ingestion, while preserving a production baseline that does not already register PHP as a first-class adapter.

This task translates design/level-2/028. php code domain source adapter target.md into executable fixtures, expected candidate structure, and candidate-workspace validation assertions.

It must not satisfy the golden prompt in advance by wiring PHP into normal production scan/import dispatch.

Required baseline invariant after this task:

normal baseline Scriberig runtime:
  .php -> current generic/unsupported policy

golden candidate fixture/spec:
  describes/builds proposed .php -> PHP adapter implementation

Task 128 will make the deterministic self-hosting provider construct this candidate through normal agent/change tools.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

design/level-1/003. domain modeling and adapters.md
design/level-1/014. agent native semantic self hosting.md
design/level-2/002. domain adapters and versioning.md
design/level-2/028. php code domain source adapter target.md
design/level-3/059. implement language independent code domain.md
design/level-3/067. implement rust syntax domain adapter.md
design/level-3/086. implement domain conformance test support.md
design/level-3/089. implement domain schema and adapter version metadata.md
design/level-3/125. implement project wide source change candidates.md
design/level-3/126. validate and apply project wide candidates safely.md

Inspect current language adapters under crates/domains/, especially the Python Tree-sitter adapter; project scanner classification and adapter dispatch in crates/scriberig-project; workspace Cargo configuration; domain test conventions; and licensing/third-party notice rules.

docs.title: Do Not Pre-Install PHP
docs.text:
This is the most important requirement of this task.

Do not add normal production wiring equivalent to:

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-php as a normal workspace member used by baseline
.php -> php in production scanner
php branch in baseline project importer

if doing so would make the exact golden user instruction "Add support for ingesting PHP source files" already complete before the agent runs.

The starting checkout used by tasks 129/130 must still lack first-class PHP ingestion.

Test-only files may contain complete expected PHP adapter source so a deterministic provider can propose it into a temporary candidate workspace.

Keep that fixture outside normal production compilation/registration unless a test explicitly materializes it as candidate content.

docs.title: Fixture Ownership
docs.text:
Create one obvious test/reference area owned by the self-hosting golden suite, for example repository-idiomatic equivalents of:

tests/self-hosting/php-extension/
  README.md
  manifest/expected-files...
  sources/... candidate file contents or templates
  php-project/... input fixture
  invalid-php-project/... input fixture

If existing golden product fixture infrastructure has a better location, extend it rather than creating another test framework.

The README must explain:

  • baseline deliberately lacks production PHP adapter;
  • fixture represents the candidate the agent is expected to construct;
  • source content is test/reference data, not active production registration;
  • candidate validation compiles/runs the fixture only after it has been proposed into an isolated candidate workspace.

docs.title: Expected Candidate File Set
docs.text:
Encode a deterministic expected set of effects appropriate to the actual repository after inspecting current owners.

The expected shape should include the real equivalents of:

Create crates/domains/scriberig-domain-php/Cargo.toml
Create crates/domains/scriberig-domain-php/src/lib.rs
possibly Create additional module/test files under that crate
Update root Cargo.toml workspace/dependency metadata
Update Cargo.lock when dependency resolution produces a change
Update crates/scriberig-project/Cargo.toml
Update crates/scriberig-project/src/scan.rs classification
Update crates/scriberig-project/src/adapters.rs import dispatch
Add/update project/domain integration tests/fixtures
Update authoritative capability/format metadata if required

Do not hard-code paths that do not match current repository ownership. The fixture should evolve with real structure.

Use a manifest/declarative description so tests can assert no unexpected production areas are modified by the golden candidate.

docs.title: PHP Domain Candidate Source
docs.text:
The fixture's proposed scriberig-domain-php implementation must follow actual domain crate conventions.

At minimum its public/testable behavior implements:

adapter/schema id/version metadata
parse exact UTF-8 PHP source
Tree-sitter PHP parser initialization
complete deterministic syntax serialization
ordered syntax-node records
byte ranges
row/column ranges
named/missing/error flags
field names where available
leaf text where appropriate
comment preservation
important named declaration metadata
structured parse/decode errors

Use the actual tree-sitter-php Rust API/version selected for the candidate and normal workspace dependency conventions.

Do not write pseudocode that only passes source-text assertions. Candidate validation must compile and execute it.

docs.title: Parser Dependency and Licensing
docs.text:
Select an exact compatible tree-sitter-php dependency version by inspecting current Tree-sitter versions in the workspace.

Record in fixture/readme:

crate/version
license
why compatible with current tree-sitter runtime
whether lockfile update is expected

Follow repository third-party notice/licensing policy.

If dependency acquisition is required during golden validation, task 126's explicit dependency-resolution capability/policy applies.

Do not vendor third-party parser source into the fixture merely to avoid normal dependency policy unless repository licensing/build policy explicitly chooses vendoring.

docs.title: Complete Syntax Fixture Expectations
docs.text:
Provide representative valid PHP source containing at least:

<?php

namespace App;

class Greeter
{
    public function greet(string $name): string
    {
        // greeting comment
        return "Hello, " . $name;
    }
}

function helper(int $value): int
{
    return $value + 1;
}

Also provide a mixed inline-HTML/PHP fixture.

Golden domain assertions must prove complete/nested syntax retention rather than only detecting declaration names.

Use normalized deterministic assertions suitable for Tree-sitter version behavior; do not make tests depend on unstable debug formatting when a structured tree model exists.

docs.title: Named Declaration Target
docs.text:
The candidate must expose enough shared code-domain metadata that public semantic discovery can identify at least:

namespace App
class Greeter
method greet
function helper

Use current language-independent code domain concepts/relationships/property conventions.

If existing adapters expose declaration entities through project import rather than inside the parser crate directly, mirror that architecture.

Do not create a separate php_find_symbol production API.

docs.title: Inline HTML Target
docs.text:
Add fixture source where HTML surrounds a PHP block and ensure candidate parser tests expect a valid complete tree according to the selected grammar.

The proposed adapter must not reject the file solely because it does not start with a pure PHP-only document.

The public project import test should still discover the named PHP declaration within that file.

docs.title: Malformed PHP Fixture
docs.text:
Provide deterministic malformed input that the selected parser reports as syntax error/error node according to its API.

Candidate adapter logic must translate that state into the repository's structured adapter diagnostic and refuse to return a trusted successful semantic PHP document for project promotion.

Assertions include useful source position/range where parser data permits it.

docs.title: Candidate Domain Tests
docs.text:
Encode expected candidate tests equivalent to:

PHP-DOMAIN-01 declarations
PHP-DOMAIN-02 comments
PHP-DOMAIN-03 nested syntax
PHP-DOMAIN-04 inline HTML
PHP-DOMAIN-05 malformed source
PHP-DOMAIN-06 deterministic output

These tests should live in the source that the candidate adds, or in golden validation harness code that executes only against the candidate workspace. Prefer candidate-owned tests where they naturally belong so the accepted project retains its own regression coverage.

docs.title: Candidate Project Integration Tests
docs.text:
The expected candidate also includes tests equivalent to:

PHP-IMPORT-01 .php classification
PHP-IMPORT-02 exact source bytes/digest
PHP-IMPORT-03 project ownership
PHP-IMPORT-04 semantic find Greeter/greet
PHP-IMPORT-05 source projection
PHP-IMPORT-06 malformed import keeps prior snapshot
PHP-IMPORT-07 unchanged re-import stability
PHP-IMPORT-08 deleted PHP source reconciliation
classification regression matrix

Use public/project service APIs rather than querying SQLite tables to fake success.

docs.title: Fresh PHP Project Fixture
docs.text:
Provide a small project fixture suitable for project-ingestion-e2e, for example:

php-golden/
  README.md
  src/Greeter.php

Initialize/copy it as Git-tracked when the validation profile uses Git-tracked scan selection.

The expected public flow is:

fresh DB
project scan
manifest verifies src/Greeter.php -> PHP
project import
workspace resolve
semantic find Greeter
semantic find greet
inspect/render

This fixture is external input to candidate validation, not a production PHP adapter.

docs.title: Expected Candidate Assertions
docs.text:
Add helper/test code able to validate a produced candidate structurally before running expensive validation.

At minimum assert:

  • required create/update effects exist;
  • no unexpected direct DB/TUI/web implementation path was added solely for PHP;
  • scanner and importer refer to the same PHP adapter identity;
  • workspace/dependency integration exists;
  • candidate includes required PHP tests;
  • candidate base is exact expected project snapshot;
  • live baseline still lacks the proposed created files/first-class registration before Apply.

Do not require byte-for-byte equality to one fixture implementation if multiple correct implementations satisfy the semantic contract, unless deterministic provider golden tests intentionally use one exact fixture. Separate semantic acceptance from scripted fixture exactness.

docs.title: Two Layers of Test Data
docs.text: Keep these concepts distinct:

docs.title: Scripted-provider fixture
docs.text: May contain exact source texts/edits used by the deterministic provider to exercise the normal tool loop reproducibly.

docs.title: Product acceptance assertions
docs.text:
Must verify semantic behavior of the resulting candidate/build, not merely equality to the scripted texts.

This prevents the final gate from becoming a tautology where a stored patch is copied and considered successful without running PHP ingestion.

docs.title: Baseline Guard Test
docs.text:
Add a focused test that runs against the normal repository baseline before applying the golden candidate and proves first-class PHP ingestion is absent.

The exact assertion should match current policy, for example:

scan fixture with example.php
adapter != php / currently generic text

The purpose is not to freeze generic text forever; it protects the meaning of this specific self-hosting milestone.

If this guard starts failing because production gains PHP for another reason, do not simply delete it and leave the golden prompt unchanged. Revisit the golden absent-format choice/design.

docs.title: No Production Prompt Special Case
docs.text:
Nothing in normal runtime should recognize the literal text:

Add support for ingesting PHP source files.

and load this fixture directly as a magic patch.

The fixture is consumed only by deterministic test-provider configuration/harness code. Production agent runtime still sees ordinary provider tool requests and shared change operations.

docs.title: PHP-GOLDEN-BASELINE-01
docs.text: Against baseline project service, scan a PHP fixture and prove first-class php adapter is not already active.

docs.title: PHP-GOLDEN-FIXTURE-01
docs.text: Validate fixture manifest lists all required candidate integration areas and no impossible/nonexistent owners.

docs.title: PHP-GOLDEN-COMPILE-01
docs.text: Materialize the exact scripted PHP candidate into an isolated candidate workspace and compile focused PHP domain/project tests. This may use task 126 validation helpers.

docs.title: PHP-GOLDEN-DOMAIN-01
docs.text: Run PHP-DOMAIN-01 through -06 against candidate workspace and assert semantic requirements.

docs.title: PHP-GOLDEN-IMPORT-01
docs.text: Run PHP-IMPORT-01 through -08/regression matrix against candidate workspace.

docs.title: PHP-GOLDEN-E2E-01
docs.text: Use fresh DB + small PHP project + candidate build/public operations; assert Greeter and greet semantic discovery and source render.

docs.title: PHP-GOLDEN-LIVE-01
docs.text: Before candidate Apply, assert baseline checkout still lacks candidate-created production PHP crate/registration and remains byte-identical for expected update paths.

docs.title: Likely Areas to Add Test Data
docs.text:
Follow existing test fixture conventions. Possible owners:

tests/**
crates/scriberig-conformance/**
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/** deterministic provider fixtures
crates/scriberig-project/** test fixtures
product-golden fixture infrastructure from task 122

Avoid adding test fixture crates to normal workspace members if that would make baseline PHP support active or materially change production behavior.

docs.title: Required Verification
docs.text:
Run baseline guard, fixture compile/domain/import/E2E tests through isolated candidate workspace, plus repository quality gates for any new test harness code.

The test suite may resolve Cargo dependencies through explicit CI/validation policy, but must not call an external model provider.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Baseline production runtime still lacks first-class registered PHP ingestion.
  • [x] Golden fixture/reference area clearly documents the baseline invariant.
  • [x] Expected project-wide candidate effect set matches current repository ownership.
  • [x] Fixture contains compilable PHP domain implementation source, not pseudocode.
  • [x] Exact compatible Tree-sitter PHP dependency/version/licensing is documented.
  • [x] Proposed adapter preserves complete deterministic syntax, ranges, comments, and error state.
  • [x] Proposed adapter exposes named namespace/class/method/function metadata through shared code-domain conventions.
  • [x] Inline HTML/PHP fixture is present.
  • [x] Malformed PHP yields structured failure semantics.
  • [x] Candidate source includes PHP-DOMAIN-01 through -06 coverage.
  • [x] Candidate integration source includes PHP-IMPORT-01 through -08 and classification regression coverage.
  • [x] Fresh PHP project fixture exists for candidate E2E.
  • [x] Scripted exact source data is separated conceptually from semantic acceptance assertions.
  • [x] No production runtime branch on the literal PHP golden prompt exists.
  • [x] PHP-GOLDEN-BASELINE-01 passes.
  • [x] PHP-GOLDEN-FIXTURE-01 passes.
  • [x] PHP-GOLDEN-COMPILE-01 passes against isolated candidate workspace.
  • [x] PHP-GOLDEN-DOMAIN-01 passes against the fixture adapter crate.
  • [x] PHP-GOLDEN-IMPORT-01 passes.
  • [x] PHP-GOLDEN-E2E-01 passes using public project/semantic operations.
  • [x] PHP-GOLDEN-LIVE-01 proves live baseline remains unchanged before Apply.
  • [x] No external model provider is required.
  • [x] Affected repository quality gates pass.

Do not implement production PHP registration in this task merely to make fixture tests easier.

docs.title: Implement Deterministic Self-Hosting Provider Scenario for PHP Ingestion
Objective
docs.text:
Extend the existing deterministic/scripted agent provider and golden harness so, through normal provider-neutral tool requests, it can perform the semantic discovery and project-wide candidate construction required by the PHP self-hosting scenario.

The scripted provider is test configuration. Production runtime must not contain a literal-prompt shortcut or a privileged PHP patch path.

Required provider behavior after onboarding P@S0 and receiving:

Add support for ingesting PHP source files.

is conceptually:

observe exact P@S0
-> discover semantic tools
-> read project/design guidance semantically
-> run read-only architecture child branch B1
-> receive compact architecture BranchResult
-> run implementation child branch B2
-> inspect exact targets @ S0
-> propose one normal project-wide candidate C1
-> validate C1 through shared profiles
-> inspect C1
-> return terminal result with CandidateId C1

No Apply is performed by the agent in this task.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

design/level-1/014. agent native semantic self hosting.md
design/level-2/026. agent native self hosting golden workflow.md
design/level-2/028. php code domain source adapter target.md
design/level-3/109. implement branch context compiler and model request cache.md
design/level-3/110. implement nested branch orchestrator and trusted tool loop.md
design/level-3/115. verify agent branch isolation and cross surface conformance.md
design/level-3/121. implement semantically scoped agent candidate through shared change path.md
design/level-3/123. enable agent bootstrap and project onboarding from empty database.md
design/level-3/124. make onboarded project semantic context primary for agent discovery.md
design/level-3/125. implement project wide source change candidates.md
design/level-3/126. validate and apply project wide candidates safely.md
design/level-3/127. define php self extension contract and golden candidate fixture.md

Inspect the existing fake/scripted provider architecture and test scenario configuration. Extend it; do not build a second agent runtime or a provider that writes directly into migration/storage internals.

docs.title: Provider-Neutral Requirement
docs.text:
The deterministic provider must communicate only through the same normalized model/provider request/response contracts used by real providers.

It may be scripted based on:

  • normalized semantic context;
  • available tool definitions;
  • prior tool results;
  • test scenario state.

It must not invoke application Rust internals directly from the provider fixture.

Production agent runtime must not contain code equivalent to:

if prompt == "Add support for ingesting PHP source files." {
    install_fixture_patch();
}

The deterministic behavior belongs in test/provider configuration.

docs.title: Exact Scope Assertion
docs.text:
At the first model turn for the PHP command, capture normalized request evidence and assert:

project_id == onboarded P
snapshot_id == S0
root/selection context corresponds to active project

The provider should refuse or fail its scripted test if exact project/snapshot context is missing.

A prompt containing the word scriberig is not sufficient evidence.

docs.title: Initial Tool Discovery
docs.text:
The provider requests trusted capability discovery and verifies it can reach semantic read/branch/change/validation tools appropriate to its current scope.

Expected conceptual catalog includes:

inspect
find
query
render
follow/list as useful
branch.start or normal nested-branch request mechanism
change.propose for implementation branch
change.inspect
validate

change.apply must be absent from or unused by the implementation branch golden policy.

Direct database/live filesystem mutation tools must not be used.

docs.title: Semantic Project Guidance Reads
docs.text:
Before proposing source edits, the provider must use imported project semantics to retrieve governing guidance and relevant design/source precedent.

At minimum the scripted sequence should semantically locate/render:

AGENTS.md
design/AGENTS.md
relevant domain adapter/code-domain design
representative language adapter source
project scan/classification source
project adapter/import dispatch source
workspace Cargo metadata

Exact entity IDs are discovered at runtime from P@S0; do not bake database-generated IDs into the script.

Source-relative path/name expectations may be used as deterministic search anchors.

docs.title: Architecture Discovery Child B1
docs.text:
The provider/orchestrator starts B1 with:

purpose = determine minimal extension points for PHP source ingestion
base = P@S0
capabilities = read-only semantic set
expected result = architecture map

B1 performs normal semantic find/inspect/render operations.

The test captures tool invocation evidence proving B1 lacks/does not use mutation tools.

B1 returns a compact result including stable refs for actual current owners such as:

language domain precedent
project scan classifier
project adapter importer
workspace manifest
relevant conformance/test owner

The parent receives the BranchResult, not the complete transcript.

docs.title: Implementation Child B2
docs.text:
After B1, the parent starts B2 with:

base = P@S0
architecture result refs
capabilities = semantic read + project-wide propose + candidate inspect + validate
no normal apply capability
expected result = validated CandidateId

B2 re-inspects/renders exact edit targets at S0 before constructing its candidate.

This proves the architecture result is guidance, not a stale unchecked patch coordinate.

docs.title: Candidate Source Construction
docs.text:
Use the exact scripted PHP candidate source fixture from task 127 as deterministic model output data.

The provider should still construct the change through ordinary tool arguments/effects:

Create new PHP domain crate files
Update root workspace/dependency metadata
Update project crate dependency metadata
Update scan classification
Update import adapter dispatch
Add/update tests/fixtures/metadata as defined by fixture manifest

The agent tool receives project-relative source effects anchored to S0 and returns normal candidate C1.

Do not let the provider fixture call std::fs::write, Git apply, SQLite, or migration repositories directly.

docs.title: Candidate Baseline Guards
docs.text:
Before/after change.propose, assert through test harness/public state:

baseline production did not already have first-class PHP adapter
P.current == S0
candidate-created PHP crate path absent from live checkout
updated live files retain base bytes

The candidate must be inspectable/renderable independently.

docs.title: Candidate Structural Inspection
docs.text:
B2 calls normal candidate inspection and verifies the expected project-wide shape:

one CandidateId
base S0
required create/update effects present
no unexpected unrelated paths
candidate not current

If the tool result exposes source diff/path pages separately, the script follows the public pagination/detail operations rather than accessing internal migration tables.

docs.title: Validation Tool Sequence
docs.text:
The scripted implementation branch requests shared validation profiles in a sensible order:

php-domain-focused
project-import-focused
rust-workspace
project-ingestion-e2e

The exact names may match implementation policy from task 126.

Observe operations/results through normal application tool path.

On success, retain stable ValidationId/operation refs in branch result.

No validation step may write the live project checkout.

docs.title: Scripted Validation Failure Path
docs.text:
Add a second deterministic scenario that intentionally proposes one known-bad candidate variation or causes a controlled validation failure.

The provider must:

  1. receive structured failure;
  2. inspect bounded diagnostics;
  3. revise/supersede candidate through normal shared change operation;
  4. rerun focused validation;
  5. continue only after success.

This proves the provider/runtime supports iterative candidate repair without a hidden direct-edit loop.

The failure can be a deterministic source/API mismatch designed solely for test configuration, but production runtime must remain generic.

docs.title: Implementation Branch Result
docs.text:
On successful validation, B2 returns compact durable data equivalent to:

purpose = implement PHP ingestion
base = P@S0
candidate = C1
candidate/result snapshot if available
validation refs = [...]
changed areas = [...]
outcome = validated_candidate

The parent receives this result and calls normal change.inspect(C1) before terminal response.

docs.title: Parent Terminal Result
docs.text:
The root agent operation returns concise text plus structured durable result linking to C1.

Expected semantics:

PHP ingestion support is implemented as a validated candidate.
Review candidate.

The durable operation/session result exposes:

operation/session/branch ids
selected project/base snapshot
CandidateId C1
validation refs
result status

Do not make the candidate discoverable only by parsing assistant prose.

docs.title: No Auto-Apply
docs.text:
The deterministic provider must not request Apply in this scenario.

The final state before user review is:

P.current == S0
live checkout == base
C1 exists
required validation succeeded

Task 129 drives user Review/Apply through the TUI.

docs.title: Trace Evidence
docs.text:
Persist/capture enough evidence to assert the expected semantic tool path without depending on fragile exact token text.

Required evidence includes:

initial exact P@S0 context
capability discovery
semantic project/design/source reads
B1 branch creation + read-only catalog
B1 compact result
B2 exact base context
B2 source target inspections
normal project-wide candidate tool call
CandidateId C1
validation tool calls/results
final durable candidate link

Do not assert a provider implementation must make an exact number of benign inspect/find calls if the semantic behavior is equivalent.

docs.title: Context Size and Branch Isolation Evidence
docs.text:
Capture normalized requests to prove:

  • B1 receives only intended parent/project context;
  • parent after B1 receives compact result rather than complete B1 history;
  • B2 receives architecture result refs and exact base;
  • root parent after B2 receives compact validated-candidate result rather than entire B2 transcript.

Add bounded-size assertions if existing context compiler tests expose appropriate metrics, but avoid brittle byte-perfect thresholds.

docs.title: Cancellation and Tool Failure
docs.text:
Script focused cases for:

  • cancel B1: no candidate/project mutation;
  • cancel B2 before candidate: no candidate/current/file mutation;
  • fail candidate tool: operation/branch fails structurally;
  • validation failure without successful repair: root result must not claim validated candidate;
  • stale S0 before proposal: shared change tool rejects or marks stale according to task 125; provider must not silently retarget;
  • tool capability denied: provider cannot bypass catalog through raw database/filesystem mutation.

docs.title: No External Model Provider
docs.text:
All tests in this task run with network access to external model providers unavailable/disabled.

If candidate Cargo dependency resolution requires network/cache, that is validation infrastructure and must be independently capability-controlled; it is not a model-provider call.

Add explicit evidence/configuration that no OpenAI/Anthropic/etc. provider credentials are required for this suite.

docs.title: SELFHOST-PROVIDER-01 — exact semantic scope
docs.text: After task 123 onboarding, start PHP continuation and assert normalized provider request contains exact P@S0.

docs.title: SELFHOST-PROVIDER-02 — semantic architecture discovery
docs.text: Run through B1. Assert guidance/source objects are found/rendered semantically and child catalog is read-only.

docs.title: SELFHOST-PROVIDER-03 — compact branch result
docs.text: Assert parent request after B1 contains architecture BranchResult refs but not full child transcript.

docs.title: SELFHOST-PROVIDER-04 — normal project candidate
docs.text: Run B2 proposal. Assert returned C1 is normal canonical project-wide candidate based on S0, and live tree/current remain base.

docs.title: SELFHOST-PROVIDER-05 — candidate validation
docs.text: Run all required profiles against C1; assert durable successful evidence and candidate E2E actually imports/finds/renders PHP.

docs.title: SELFHOST-PROVIDER-06 — repair loop
docs.text: Trigger controlled candidate validation failure, observe structured diagnostic, create corrected candidate through normal change path, and reach success without live write.

docs.title: SELFHOST-PROVIDER-07 — durable result
docs.text: Recreate client/session view after operation completion and recover C1/validation refs from durable operation/branch state.

docs.title: SELFHOST-PROVIDER-FAIL-01
docs.text: Provider/tool failure before candidate success cannot change project current snapshot or live checkout.

docs.title: SELFHOST-PROVIDER-CANCEL-01
docs.text: Cancel nested/implementation operation and assert same no-mutation guarantees.

docs.title: Likely Areas to Change
docs.text:
Inspect actual deterministic provider/test ownership. Likely:

crates/scriberig-agent-core/**
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/**
crates/scriberig-session/**
crates/scriberig-conformance/**
agent deterministic fake/scripted provider fixtures
self-hosting/php-extension test fixtures from task 127
application/protocol test harnesses for candidate/validation operations

Production project/domain code should not gain PHP support in this task.

docs.title: Required Verification
docs.text:
Run all focused deterministic provider/branch/candidate/validation tests with external model-provider network unavailable.

Then repository-standard affected checks including:

cargo check --workspace --all-targets

The PHP candidate itself is compiled/tested only in isolated candidate validation as defined by task 127/126.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Existing provider-neutral deterministic provider is reused/extended.
  • [x] Production runtime has no literal PHP-prompt patch shortcut.
  • [x] Initial PHP continuation request proves exact P@S0 scope.
  • [x] Provider discovers/uses trusted semantic tools, not direct DB mutation.
  • [x] Project/design guidance is read through semantic imported project state.
  • [x] B1 is a real nested read-only branch with exact base and bounded catalog.
  • [x] B1 returns compact architecture result with stable refs.
  • [x] Parent does not automatically inherit B1 full transcript.
  • [x] B2 receives exact P@S0, architecture refs, propose/validate but no Apply.
  • [x] B2 re-inspects exact source targets before proposal.
  • [x] Scripted fixture source is submitted through normal project-wide candidate tool.
  • [x] Returned C1 is a normal candidate/migration.
  • [x] P.current and live checkout remain base after proposal/validation.
  • [x] B2 runs focused/project/workspace/E2E validation through shared profiles.
  • [x] Candidate E2E executes real proposed PHP implementation behavior.
  • [x] Controlled validation failure can be repaired through normal candidate path.
  • [x] B2 returns compact validated-candidate BranchResult.
  • [x] Parent terminal durable result exposes C1 and validation refs.
  • [x] No agent auto-Apply occurs.
  • [x] Trace evidence covers exact scope, branches, semantic tools, candidate, validation.
  • [x] Cancellation/tool failure cannot mutate current project/live checkout.
  • [x] SELFHOST-PROVIDER-01 through -07 pass.
  • [x] SELFHOST-PROVIDER-FAIL-01 and CANCEL-01 pass.
  • [x] External model-provider network/credentials are not required.
  • [x] Baseline production still lacks first-class PHP ingestion.
  • [x] Affected repository quality gates pass.

Task 129 should consume this provider scenario through the real TUI, not reimplement it in terminal test code.

docs.title: Deliver Native TUI Agent Self-Extension Workflow for PHP Ingestion
Objective
docs.text:
Compose tasks 123 through 128 into the exact native-TUI two-command workflow that the user will experience:

fresh DB, no project
> Onboard the current project.

active Scriberig project P@S0
> Add support for ingesting PHP source files.

validated normal project-wide candidate C1
-> Review candidate
-> user Apply
-> authoritative P@S1

This task owns the product integration and real-PTY interaction for the workflow. It must not add a TUI-only onboarding, patching, validation, or filesystem-write implementation.

Task 130 turns this flow into the final strict product gate.

Read:

design/level-1/014. agent native semantic self hosting.md

docs.title: Golden Launch
docs.text:
The primary focused PTY scenario launches the real built executable from a temporary copy of the Scriberig repository:

cd <temp-scriberig-copy>
srig tui --db <fresh-db>

Do not pass:

--project
--import
precomputed ProjectId
precomputed EntityId

The test must begin with no active project and prove the agent can bootstrap it.

Use the deterministic self-hosting provider configuration from task 128 through normal provider selection/runtime configuration.

docs.title: Initial TUI State
docs.text:
The TUI must clearly support agent input before a project is active.

Required observable state is equivalent to:

Agent
No active project
> _

Exact layout/copy may follow current native UI conventions.

Do not block the entire agent/session surface behind ActiveProjectWorkspace::Some.

Project-specific semantic/editor actions may remain disabled until onboarding completes.

docs.title: First Command Interaction
docs.text:
The PTY/user types exactly:

Onboard the current project.

The TUI starts the shared agent application operation and observes normal status/events.

Useful progress may include summaries such as:

scanning project
reviewing manifest
importing project
resolving workspace
semantic verification

These are display states derived from operation/tool activity. The TUI must not duplicate the business logic.

docs.title: Onboarding Completion UX
docs.text:
After successful deterministic agent onboarding, the TUI must visibly transition to an active workspace containing at least:

project display name = scriberig or fixture name
non-empty current snapshot representation
semantic/project navigation enabled

The session/agent result remains inspectable.

The user should not need to restart or manually open/import the project again.

If onboarding fails, the UI remains without a fake successful active project and shows inspectable structured failure.

docs.title: Second Command Interaction
docs.text:
Without restarting the TUI, the user types exactly:

Add support for ingesting PHP source files.

The operation continues from exact active P@S0 through the deterministic provider scenario from task 128.

The TUI may show nested branch/operation activity, but does not need to stream every child branch token inline.

At minimum the user can tell that work is proceeding and later inspect the relevant child results.

docs.title: Nested Branch Presentation
docs.text:
Represent architecture discovery and implementation branches through existing session/operation UI concepts.

Required observable semantics:

parent PHP request
  child: architecture discovery -> completed result
  child: implementation/validation -> completed result containing candidate

The user should be able to inspect branch status/purpose and resulting candidate references.

Do not flatten child transcripts into an enormous single terminal log as the only usable representation.

Do not invent a second TUI-only branch tree that is not backed by durable session/branch records.

docs.title: Candidate Result Action
docs.text:
When the root agent operation finishes successfully, its normal durable result exposes CandidateId C1.

The TUI presents an action equivalent to:

Review candidate

Activating it navigates to the existing/shared migration/change review using C1.

Do not render a fake diff from assistant text.

docs.title: Project-Wide Candidate Review UX
docs.text:
The review view must handle the multi-file candidate from task 125.

Required visible data includes:

candidate id/reference
base snapshot S0
validation status
stale/conflict status
changed paths with effect kind

The user can navigate representative paths such as:

new PHP domain Cargo.toml
new PHP domain src/lib.rs
workspace Cargo.toml
project scanner/import source
PHP tests/fixtures
Cargo.lock when changed

For selected path, show old/new or unified source diff appropriate to create/update/delete.

Large diffs may be paginated/scrollable.

docs.title: Validation UX
docs.text:
The deterministic provider will normally already have run required validation before returning C1.

The TUI review must display authoritative validation evidence/status, not infer success from agent prose.

At minimum show the equivalent of:

PHP domain focused      passed
project import focused  passed
Rust workspace          passed
PHP ingestion E2E       passed

Exact labels may reflect profile registry names.

The user can inspect bounded failure diagnostics in negative tests.

Apply remains unavailable when required validation failed/stale according to shared policy.

docs.title: Pre-Acceptance Live-Tree Proof
docs.text:
Before invoking Apply, the real PTY harness must inspect the temporary Scriberig checkout externally and prove:

  • candidate-created PHP domain production path is absent live;
  • expected updated source/config files still match baseline bytes;
  • current project snapshot remains S0 through public state;
  • candidate C1 remains separately inspectable.

This assertion is mandatory. It catches agent/TUI implementations that secretly wrote source before review.

docs.title: User Apply Interaction
docs.text:
The PTY/user invokes the normal review Apply action.

The TUI calls the shared application apply operation with exact candidate/base context and observes terminal result.

Do not run git apply, write files, update SQLite, or construct successor IDs in terminal UI code.

docs.title: Apply Progress and Result UX
docs.text:
During Apply, product may show states such as:

checking candidate base
checking filesystem preconditions
promoting canonical state
materializing source effects
refreshing workspace

On full success, the TUI displays enough authoritative result to establish:

new current snapshot S1
S1 != S0
required external materialization succeeded

If canonical/materialization states diverge, display explicit recovery/effect failure rather than generic success.

docs.title: Post-Apply Source Verification
docs.text:
After full success, external PTY harness verifies intended candidate-created/updated files now exist on disk.

The TUI refreshes project workspace through shared application/client state and can open history/diff showing the transition.

Stable semantic selections may be re-resolved to S1 according to existing workspace rules; stale S0 cached content must not be presented as current.

docs.title: History UX
docs.text:
Normal TUI History/Diff should make the accepted self-hosted change discoverable.

The user can inspect:

base S0
candidate/migration C1
successor S1
changed project paths
provenance/session when available

Historical source from S0 remains renderable according to existing history/projection design.

docs.title: Restart Persistence
docs.text:
The focused PTY flow exits cleanly and restarts:

srig tui --db <same-db>

against the same temporary checkout.

The product must recover/open existing project state according to current active-project/session policy and prove:

P current = S1
accepted change/history persists
session/branch/candidate/validation references are inspectable
materialized source remains present

If active workspace selection itself is intentionally session-local, the test may explicitly reopen the existing project through normal UI; it must not re-import it as a new unrelated project.

docs.title: Negative TUI Scenario — Validation Failure
docs.text:
Use deterministic provider failure variation from task 128 or a controlled invalid candidate.

Required outcome:

  • normal review shows validation failure/diagnostic;
  • Apply unavailable or shared operation rejects clearly;
  • P.current remains S0;
  • live checkout remains baseline;
  • TUI never reports full PHP support/materialization success.

docs.title: Negative TUI Scenario — External Conflict
docs.text:
After validated C1 exists but before Apply, externally modify one intended update target in the temporary Scriberig checkout.

Then invoke Apply.

Required outcome:

  • shared precondition detects conflict;
  • TUI displays stale/conflict/reconciliation-required state;
  • external marker/content remains on disk;
  • candidate does not silently overwrite it;
  • UI does not claim full successful materialization;
  • canonical/effect state is shown truthfully according to task 126 ordering.

docs.title: Negative TUI Scenario — Create Conflict
docs.text:
Before Apply, externally create one path that C1 expects to create, such as the candidate PHP crate path/file.

Required outcome:

  • explicit create-target conflict;
  • external file remains;
  • no silent replacement;
  • no misleading full success.

docs.title: Cancellation
docs.text:
Test cancelling:

  • initial onboarding agent operation;
  • architecture discovery child;
  • implementation branch before candidate completion;
  • validation operation where cancellable.

In all cases, TUI remains usable and durable operation state records cancellation.

No cancellation path may leave hidden live source writes or a fake current successor snapshot.

docs.title: No Network Model Requirement
docs.text:
The entire TUI scenario uses the deterministic provider and must run without external model-provider credentials/network.

If Cargo dependency resolution for the candidate is allowed/needed by validation, that remains an explicit separate validation capability and should be test-environment controlled.

The TUI must not prompt for an external model API key in the golden test configuration.

docs.title: TUI-SELFHOST-01 — empty DB onboarding
docs.text:
1. fresh temp Scriberig checkout and DB;
  2. launch real srig tui --db with deterministic provider;
  3. assert no active project;
  4. type exact onboarding command;
  5. wait for normal agent completion;
  6. assert active project and S0 visible/inspectable;
  7. assert semantic navigation works.

docs.title: TUI-SELFHOST-02 — PHP candidate generation
docs.text:
Continue from P@S0:

  1. type exact PHP command;
  2. observe nested branch completion;
  3. wait for terminal agent result;
  4. open Review candidate;
  5. assert multi-file PHP candidate paths/diffs;
  6. assert required validation success;
  7. externally assert live checkout remains baseline and project current is S0.

docs.title: TUI-SELFHOST-03 — Apply and successor
docs.text:
Continue/recreate validated candidate:

  1. invoke normal Apply;
  2. wait for explicit full canonical/materialization success;
  3. assert current snapshot becomes S1 != S0;
  4. external harness asserts PHP candidate files/updates on disk;
  5. open History/Diff and assert transition/candidate;
  6. ensure active workspace source/state reflects S1.

docs.title: TUI-SELFHOST-04 — restart
docs.text: Restart against same DB/checkout. Assert project/history/session result and S1 remain inspectable without rerunning onboarding/PHP agent commands.

docs.title: TUI-SELFHOST-05 — validation failure
docs.text: Run controlled failing candidate; assert diagnostic, no Apply-ready success, S0/live baseline unchanged.

docs.title: TUI-SELFHOST-06 — update conflict
docs.text: Externally edit update target before Apply; assert conflict and preservation.

docs.title: TUI-SELFHOST-07 — create conflict
docs.text: Externally create proposed new target before Apply; assert conflict and preservation.

docs.title: TUI-SELFHOST-CANCEL-01
docs.text: Cancel representative onboarding/implementation operation and assert no hidden project/file mutation.

docs.title: Failure Artifacts
docs.text:
Extend existing PTY harness failure reporting so failed self-hosting tests preserve enough safe evidence:

final PTY screen/transcript
process exit status
application/server stderr/logs when applicable
session/operation/branch ids
project/current snapshot ids
candidate id
validation status/diagnostics
fixture checkout git diff/current relevant files
effect receipt/conflict details

Do not dump secrets. Deterministic provider has no external provider secrets.

docs.title: Likely Areas to Change
docs.text:
Inspect actual TUI owners. Likely:

crates/scriberig-cli/** and/or apps/scriberig/** native TUI
TUI agent/session views
TUI project workspace state
TUI migration/change review
TUI history/diff
PTY golden test harness
crates/scriberig-client/**
crates/scriberig-protocol/** where result navigation data is missing
capabilities.toml only after truthful verification

Do not add PHP parsing/project scan logic to TUI code.

docs.title: Required Verification
docs.text:
Run the focused real PTY scenarios above plus existing native TUI golden tests from task 122 to guard regressions.

Run affected Rust quality gates including at least:

cargo check --workspace --all-targets

No test may pass by bypassing the real built srig process for the required PTY scenarios.

docs.text:

  • [x] Exact onboarding command runs through normal agent/application tools.
