Task 130 will harden this exact composition into the final mandatory product gate.

docs.title: Enforce Real-Process Self-Hosting PHP Golden Product Gate
Objective
docs.text:
Create the final executable product gate proving the complete Scriberig self-hosting scenario from a clean baseline:

fresh copied Scriberig checkout that does not have first-class PHP ingestion
+ fresh SQLite database
+ real built native TUI
+ deterministic provider

USER: Onboard the current project.
-> project becomes active semantic P@S0

USER: Add support for ingesting PHP source files.
-> semantic architecture discovery
-> nested implementation branch
-> normal validated project-wide Candidate C1
-> live checkout still base

USER: Review candidate / Apply
-> exact-base safe apply/materialization
-> P@S1
-> PHP support present in checkout
-> durable history/session/provenance
-> restart recovers state

This is a product-verification task. Do not weaken its assertions to accommodate missing implementation. Fix the owning task instead.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
All relevant existing first-use product-gate work through task 122 must remain passing.

Every checklist item in these new tasks must be complete:

123. enable agent bootstrap and project onboarding from empty database.md
124. make onboarded project semantic context primary for agent discovery.md
125. implement project wide source change candidates.md
126. validate and apply project wide candidates safely.md
127. define php self extension contract and golden candidate fixture.md
128. implement deterministic self hosting provider scenario for php ingestion.md
129. deliver native tui agent self extension workflow for php ingestion.md

If a prerequisite is incomplete, stop and finish the owning implementation task rather than adding test-only shortcuts here.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

AGENTS.md
design/AGENTS.md
design/level-1/014. agent native semantic self hosting.md
design/level-2/026. agent native self hosting golden workflow.md
design/level-2/027. project wide candidate workspaces validation and materialization.md
design/level-2/028. php code domain source adapter target.md
design/level-3/122. enforce real process golden path e2e product gate.md
design/level-3/123 through 129
existing product-golden/PTY harness documentation

Reuse the existing real-process golden harness from task 122. Extend it; do not create another unrelated E2E framework.

docs.title: Non-Negotiable Test Boundary
docs.text:
The main self-hosting scenario must use:

  • the real built srig executable;
  • an actual pseudo-terminal;
  • normal CLI/TUI startup arguments;
  • a fresh temporary SQLite/database path;
  • a copied temporary Scriberig checkout;
  • an actual Git repository/index when git_tracked scan is expected;
  • normal deterministic provider configuration through agent runtime;
  • public/shared application/project/query/change/validation operations;
  • real filesystem assertions performed by the harness;
  • restart of the real process.

Do not satisfy the gate with:

  • reducer/state-machine unit tests only;
  • mocked TUI widgets;
  • direct private database inserts;
  • direct migration repository inserts from the scripted provider;
  • pre-created active project IDs injected into the TUI;
  • pre-applying the expected PHP patch to the fixture;
  • HTTP/request mocks standing in for the native composition;
  • a source-text assertion that never compiles/runs the candidate PHP adapter.

docs.title: Baseline Checkout Rule
docs.text:
The temporary Scriberig checkout copied for the test must begin without first-class PHP ingestion.

Before launching the TUI, assert the baseline using task 127 guard logic:

normal project scan/import policy does not select registered PHP adapter
production PHP domain crate/registration from the golden candidate is absent

If production Scriberig later gains PHP support independently, this exact gate can no longer prove the requested self-extension. Update the absent-format scenario deliberately rather than deleting the guard and pretending the same prompt remains meaningful.

For this milestone, PHP remains the required target.

docs.title: Fixture Lifecycle
docs.text:
For every independent scenario unless persistence/restart is intentionally under test:

  1. create a fresh temp directory;
  2. copy the Scriberig repository fixture/checkout into it;
  3. ensure required Git metadata/index state exists for git_tracked scan;
  4. record baseline hashes/bytes for paths expected to change;
  5. create a fresh database path;
  6. configure deterministic self-hosting provider and required validation/dependency policy;
  7. launch real srig tui --db <fresh-db> from the temp checkout root;
  8. drive PTY interaction;
  9. on failure preserve bounded diagnostics/artifacts;
  10. terminate child processes cleanly;
  11. clean temporary data after success according to existing harness policy.

Never run write-back self-hosting tests against the developer's real Scriberig checkout.

docs.title: Stable Golden Inputs
docs.text:
The main scenario uses these exact user prompts:

Onboard the current project.

and:

Add support for ingesting PHP source files.

The PHP candidate behavior is defined by Level 2 document 028 and task 127 fixtures.

Representative semantic anchors include:

PHP fixture class: Greeter
PHP fixture method: greet
candidate PHP domain crate path from current fixture manifest
project Scriberig
base snapshot S0
candidate C1
successor snapshot S1

Do not hard-code random entity/snapshot/candidate IDs; capture them from public product/test-observable results.

docs.title: GOLDEN-SELFHOST-01 — Empty-Database Agent Onboarding
docs.text:
Required steps:

  1. launch real TUI from temp Scriberig checkout with fresh DB and no --project/--import;
  2. assert no active project is visible;
  3. assert agent input is usable;
  4. type exact onboarding command;
  5. wait on operation lifecycle, not arbitrary sleeps;
  6. inspect deterministic trace/session evidence and assert capability discovery occurred;
  7. assert scan tool used trusted current checkout context and Git-tracked policy as designed;
  8. assert persisted manifest was inspected/reviewed before import;
  9. assert import consumed the exact manifest reference;
  10. assert project workspace resolves to non-empty ProjectId P, SnapshotId S0, root;
  11. assert TUI visibly activates project without restart;
  12. assert agent performed semantic smoke check before terminal success;
  13. assert no direct SQLite/project-root mutation tool was used;
  14. assert process/browser-independent terminal diagnostics are clean.

Failure conditions include:

  • agent cannot start without a project;
  • test pre-injects a project ID;
  • scan is replaced by one model-visible file read per repository file;
  • import silently rescans different filesystem state;
  • TUI stops at status=imported without active semantic workspace;
  • agent claims success without semantic workspace resolution.

docs.title: GOLDEN-SELFHOST-02 — Semantic Architecture Discovery and Branch Isolation
docs.text:
Continue from exact P@S0.

  1. type exact PHP command;
  2. capture normalized root provider request and assert exact P/S0;
  3. assert provider uses semantic find/inspect/render to read project guidance/source precedent;
  4. assert architecture discovery child B1 is created with exact base and read-only catalog;
  5. assert B1 discovers actual current language adapter, scanner, importer, workspace/test owners without hard-coded EntityIds;
  6. let B1 complete;
  7. assert parent receives compact architecture BranchResult with stable refs;
  8. assert captured parent request does not include entire B1 transcript;
  9. assert full B1 detail remains durably inspectable separately;
  10. assert project remains P@S0 and checkout unchanged.

Failure conditions include using unrestricted filesystem grep/read as the sole architecture model while semantic project state is ignored.

docs.title: GOLDEN-SELFHOST-03 — Agent Creates Normal Project-Wide PHP Candidate
docs.text:
Continue from B1 result.

  1. implementation child B2 starts with exact P@S0 and architecture refs;
  2. assert B2 has read/propose/inspect/validate capabilities and no normal Apply capability;
  3. assert exact target source projections are re-inspected/rendered at S0;
  4. provider submits the task-127 PHP candidate edits through normal project-wide change tool;
  5. capture returned CandidateId C1;
  6. inspect C1 through public shared review API;
  7. assert expected create/update path classes are present;
  8. assert one coherent candidate/base S0, not independent applied file edits;
  9. externally read live temp checkout and assert candidate-created production PHP paths are still absent;
  10. assert expected updated files are byte-identical to baseline;
  11. assert public project workspace still reports current S0.

This scenario fails any direct agent write-through implementation.

docs.title: GOLDEN-SELFHOST-04 — Candidate Validation Proves Real PHP Ingestion
docs.text:
Run/observe required shared validation profiles for C1.

Required assertions:

php-domain-focused = success
project-import-focused = success
rust-workspace = success
project-ingestion-e2e = success

The gate must inspect evidence establishing that candidate code was actually compiled/executed.

The PHP ingestion E2E must use a fresh database and PHP fixture project against candidate code/build, and must prove through public semantic/project operations:

  • .php manifest classification selects PHP;
  • exact source bytes/digest are retained;
  • PHP document/syntax/code entities are imported;
  • Greeter is semantically discoverable;
  • greet is semantically discoverable;
  • source projection renders correctly;
  • malformed PHP negative test preserves prior valid snapshot;
  • unrelated adapter classification regression remains correct.

The gate fails if validation only checks that candidate source contains expected strings.

After validation, live Scriberig checkout and P.current must still be base S0.

docs.title: GOLDEN-SELFHOST-05 — Durable Agent Result Opens Normal Review
docs.text:
1. let B2 complete and return compact validated-candidate result;
  2. assert root parent receives compact result, not complete B2 transcript;
  3. root agent operation finishes with durable C1 link and validation refs;
  4. through TUI, activate Review candidate;
  5. assert normal shared project-wide migration review opens;
  6. assert candidate/base/validation/stale state visible;
  7. browse representative created PHP crate path and updated project/workspace path;
  8. assert real old/new/create diffs are visible;
  9. reconnect/recreate session/client view if harness supports it and recover C1 from durable result;
  10. reassert live checkout/current remain base before Apply.

Do not parse assistant prose to discover a hidden patch.

docs.title: GOLDEN-SELFHOST-06 — User Apply Produces S1 and Safe Multi-File Materialization
docs.text:
1. record displayed/public S0 and baseline relevant file bytes;
  2. invoke normal TUI Apply action;
  3. wait for terminal shared apply operation state;
  4. assert exact-base acceptance succeeded;
  5. assert result explicitly reports required external materialization/effect success;
  6. resolve authoritative project workspace and capture S1;
  7. assert S1 != S0 and P.current == S1;
  8. externally inspect checkout and assert candidate-created PHP domain files now exist with expected source;
  9. assert intended updated workspace/project files reflect accepted candidate;
  10. assert unrelated files are unchanged according to fixture expectations;
  11. open History/Diff and assert one transition/migration contains the project-wide PHP change;
  12. render/inspect historical S0 where appropriate and prove it remains addressable;
  13. assert operation/session/candidate/provenance links remain inspectable.

The TUI itself must not have written these files directly.

docs.title: GOLDEN-SELFHOST-07 — Restart Durability
docs.text:
After successful Apply:

  1. exit TUI cleanly;
  2. launch real srig tui --db <same-db> from same temp checkout;
  3. reopen existing project through normal product behavior if not automatically active;
  4. assert current authoritative snapshot remains S1;
  5. assert materialized PHP-support source remains on disk;
  6. assert history still exposes base/candidate/successor;
  7. reopen session/branch activity and recover onboarding result, B1 result, B2 validated candidate result, validation refs;
  8. no original provider token stream replay is needed to reconstruct these references.

docs.title: GOLDEN-SELFHOST-08 — Accepted Checkout Can Build and Ingest PHP
docs.text:
After Apply, build/test the now-modified temporary Scriberig checkout according to repository policy.

Then run a post-acceptance PHP ingestion proof using code from the accepted checkout, not the isolated pre-acceptance candidate workspace.

This may be a focused integration test or candidate/accepted srig invocation appropriate to current architecture.

Required result:

fresh PHP fixture DB
scan -> PHP adapter
import -> PHP semantic entities
find Greeter/greet
render source

This closes the loop: the accepted source on disk is capable of the feature the agent was asked to add.

docs.title: GOLDEN-SELFHOST-FAIL-01 — Validation Failure Does Not Mutate Current State
docs.text:
Use controlled bad candidate/provider variation.

Assert:

  • structured validation diagnostic visible/inspectable;
  • no validated-success result unless repair succeeds;
  • Apply disabled/unavailable or shared operation rejects;
  • P.current == S0;
  • live checkout remains baseline;
  • no candidate-created PHP production file leaked live.

docs.title: GOLDEN-SELFHOST-CONFLICT-01 — External Update Is Protected
docs.text:
Fresh scenario or recreate validated C1.

  1. externally modify one update target after validation and before Apply with known marker;
  2. invoke TUI Apply;
  3. assert explicit conflict/stale/effect state;
  4. read disk and assert external marker remains;
  5. assert stale candidate did not silently overwrite it;
  6. assert UI does not report full materialization success;
  7. assert canonical/effect state is truthful according to chosen ordering.

docs.title: GOLDEN-SELFHOST-CONFLICT-02 — External Create Target Is Protected
docs.text:
1. before Apply, externally create a file/path that candidate expects absent/create;
  2. invoke Apply;
  3. assert explicit create-target conflict;
  4. external content remains;
  5. no silent replacement/full success.

docs.title: GOLDEN-SELFHOST-STALE-01 — Canonical Base Advance Is Protected
docs.text:
1. create validated C1 from S0;
  2. advance project current state through another legitimate operation to Sx;
  3. attempt Apply C1;
  4. assert exact-base stale rejection;
  5. assert project remains Sx;
  6. assert no silent rebase and no stale PHP source effects materialized.

docs.title: GOLDEN-SELFHOST-CANCEL-01 — Cancellation Is Safe
docs.text:
Cover cancellation at representative phases:

onboarding before import completion
B1 discovery
B2 before candidate completion
validation

Assert durable cancelled state and no hidden live source/current-root mutation beyond any explicitly completed onboarding state appropriate to the phase.

docs.title: Cross-Surface Conformance
docs.text:
Although the main gate is TUI-native, add/extend shared conformance so the resulting stable identities remain usable outside TUI.

Required programmatic checks equivalent to:

docs.title: SELFHOST-CONFORMANCE-01 — project workspace
docs.text: Embedded application and public server/client (where normal test harness supports it) resolve same P@S0/P@S1 semantics.

docs.title: SELFHOST-CONFORMANCE-02 — branch result durability
docs.text: Architecture/implementation BranchResult references resolve equivalently through public session/application APIs.

docs.title: SELFHOST-CONFORMANCE-03 — project-wide candidate
docs.text: C1 changed paths/diffs/validation/apply detail are consumable through canonical client APIs, not TUI-private state.

docs.title: SELFHOST-CONFORMANCE-04 — provenance/history
docs.text:
Accepted change links user/session/branch/candidate/validation/successor through public history/result models.

Do not require the web product to reproduce the entire self-hosting UX in this milestone if canonical APIs/models remain reusable by it.

docs.title: Trace Assertions
docs.text:
The final golden trace should contain evidence equivalent to:

agent_start with no project
capabilities
project.scan(current trusted cwd)
manifest inspect/list
project.import(exact manifest)
project.workspace -> P@S0
semantic smoke check

second user input at P@S0
semantic guidance/source find/render
B1 read-only discovery
B1 BranchResult
B2 implementation at P@S0
normal project-wide change.propose -> C1
change.inspect C1
validate profiles
B2 BranchResult -> validated C1
root durable result -> C1

user Review
user Apply
shared exact-base/effect operation
project.workspace -> P@S1
history/restart

Do not make assertions depend on a fragile exact count of benign semantic reads.

docs.title: No-Shortcut Assertions
docs.text:
Add explicit tests/guards proving the scenario did not use:

direct SQLite mutation by provider/TUI
direct live filesystem writes by provider before Apply
preinstalled production PHP adapter in baseline
agent-only canonical patch type
hard-coded EntityId for architecture targets
hidden auto-Apply
full child transcript injection as the only branch communication
test-only source mutation to fake post-Apply result
external model provider

Where practical, assert catalogs/traces lack these forbidden paths rather than relying only on code review.

docs.title: Timing and Synchronization
docs.text:
Do not use arbitrary long sleeps.

PTY tests wait on stable observable tokens/states and operation lifecycle with bounded timeout.

Candidate validation waits on operation terminal result.

Filesystem assertions occur only after authoritative state says the relevant phase completed, except deliberate pre-Apply/conflict checks.

Keep failure messages specific to the phase/expected token to reduce debugging cost.

docs.title: Failure Artifacts
docs.text:
On failure preserve/report safe bounded evidence equivalent to:

PTY transcript/final screen
process exit code
server/application stderr logs
normalized deterministic provider/tool trace
session/branch/operation ids
project/current snapshot ids
candidate id + changed path summary
validation profile results/diagnostics
filesystem git diff or relevant file hashes/content markers
external-effect receipts/conflicts
candidate validation workspace path/artifacts when repository test policy permits

Never dump secrets. The deterministic provider requires none.

docs.title: Stable Product Gate Command
docs.text:
Add one repository-idiomatic command that runs the complete self-hosting gate, for example:

make test-self-hosting-golden

or the current build system's equivalent.

It must compose at least:

real PTY self-hosting golden scenarios
PHP candidate domain/import/E2E validation
shared self-hosting conformance
baseline no-PHP guard
no-external-model-provider guard

Do not silently skip an unavailable component and exit success.

Document exact invocation in the existing product-golden testing documentation or a focused self-hosting README referenced by it.

docs.title: CI Integration
docs.text:
Integrate the self-hosting golden gate into mandatory CI/release verification according to repository policy.

If the gate is too expensive/environment-specific for every local tools/check.sh, give it a distinct mandatory CI job/target rather than omitting it.

Do not remove existing task-122 product golden checks.

Pin/cache ordinary Rust dependencies as appropriate for CI stability while preserving explicit dependency-resolution semantics.

External model-provider credentials must not be required.

docs.title: Capability Matrix
docs.text:
Only after this gate passes, update truthful capability metadata for concepts equivalent to:

agent_empty_db_project_onboarding
agent_semantic_project_discovery
nested_branch_compact_results
project_wide_candidate
project_wide_candidate_validation
project_wide_materialization
self_hosting_agent_change

Do not mark PHP as a permanently baseline-supported capability merely because a temporary golden checkout's accepted candidate adds it, unless production main subsequently intentionally accepts that PHP implementation through normal development policy.

Distinguish product ability to self-extend from the set of adapters shipped in the baseline release.

docs.title: Required Verification
docs.text:
Run the stable self-hosting gate command from a clean checkout/environment matching CI.

Then run repository quality gates including at least:

cargo check --workspace --all-targets

and any existing task-122 product-golden command.

Review failure artifacts for accidental hidden network/model dependence and ensure all checked checklist items are backed by executable evidence.

docs.title: Implement Shared Agent Console, Model/Thinking Controls, and Trace Presentation
docs.text: Status: [ ] In Progress

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement one shared Agent Console capability across Scriberig's application, protocol, TUI, reusable web packages, and integrated web application.

The completed feature must provide:

  • a persistent free-text agent composer in the normal TUI/session surface, not only a modal overlay;
  • the equivalent persistent composer in the reusable web agent UI;
  • a user-visible model library and session-scoped active model selection;
  • model-declared available thinking levels and a user-selectable current thinking level;
  • a structured, causal activity view for model execution, reasoning summaries/status, tool calls, tool results, nested branches, validation, and final output;
  • colored nesting rails: a narrow terminal rail in TUI and a literal 2px rail in web;
  • independent presentation controls for reasoning visibility, tool invocation detail, tool output verbosity, and prompt/model-request visibility;
  • synchronized execution semantics between TUI, web, server/client, and other future clients;
  • durable provenance for execution-affecting configuration without polluting session semantics with presentation-only preferences;
  • deterministic cross-surface tests proving that the same underlying activity/model state is rendered with different verbosity without re-executing work.

This task integrates and extends the completed work in tasks 103, 107, 111, 113, 114, and 115. Do not create a parallel agent/session implementation.

docs.title: Instructions for the Implementation Agent
docs.text:
This plan is intentionally written for a smaller implementation agent such as Luna. Follow it literally and in order. Do not assume architectural details that are not verified in the repository.

Before modifying any subsystem:

  1. read the repository root AGENTS.md;
  2. read the nearest AGENTS.md for every directory you will modify;
  3. read the referenced Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3 design documents;
  4. inspect the current implementation before choosing a file or type name;
  5. extend the existing owner of a concept rather than creating a competing abstraction.

docs.title: Checklist discipline
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this file open while implementing.
  • [ ] Tick a checkbox from [ ] to [x] immediately after that exact item is implemented and its targeted verification passes.
  • [ ] Never tick an item because nearby work is complete.
  • [ ] Never bulk-tick the checklist at the end.
  • [ ] If the repository has moved since this plan was written, update this document with the actual file/type owner before implementing the changed step.
  • [ ] Before declaring the task complete, re-read every checked item and confirm the code and tests still prove it.

docs.title: Mandatory test discipline
docs.text:
During implementation, run only targeted tests/checks for the crate, package, module, or behavior just changed.

Do not run any of the following while implementation checkboxes remain incomplete:

cargo test --workspace
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
pnpm --dir web test
pnpm --dir web typecheck
pnpm --dir web build
python3 tools/lint_repo.py           # repository-wide mode

Use narrow commands instead, for example:

cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime <focused_test_filter>
cargo test -p scriberig-app <focused_test_filter>
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol <focused_test_filter>
cargo test -p scriberig-tui <focused_test_filter>
cargo test -p scriberig-server <focused_test_filter>
cargo test -p scriberig-client <focused_test_filter>

pnpm --dir web --filter @scriberig/protocol test
pnpm --dir web --filter @scriberig/model test
pnpm --dir web --filter @scriberig/agent-ui test
pnpm --dir web --filter @scriberig/agent-ui typecheck

It is acceptable to run a targeted formatter/check for files or the one changed crate/package. Do not use a workspace-wide command merely "to be safe" during implementation.

Only after every implementation and targeted-verification checkbox in this plan is complete may the Final Full-Suite Gate be run.

If a targeted test exposes a dependency-layer failure, fix that failure and run the smallest tests that prove the fix. Do not escalate to the full suite early.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read these documents before coding:

  1. design/level-1/009. agent interaction and sessions.md;
  2. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md;
  3. design/level-1/016. model driven agent execution and branch isolation.md;
  4. design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md;
  5. design/level-2/012. capability matrix and cross surface conformance.md;
  6. design/level-2/017. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md;
  7. design/level-2/021. terminal ui runtime and state architecture.md;
  8. design/level-2/022. terminal ui views interaction and conformance.md;
  9. design/level-2/023. agent runtime model provider and branch orchestration.md;
  10. design/level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md;
  11. design/level-3/103. implement tui sessions agent interaction and operation observation.md;
  12. design/level-3/107. extend session records for model execution and branch results.md;
  13. design/level-3/111. expose agent execution through application protocol server and clients.md;
  14. design/level-3/113. implement branch aware web agent experience.md;
  15. design/level-3/114. implement http protocol and event transport for remote clients.md;
  16. design/level-3/115. verify agent branch isolation and cross surface conformance.md;
  17. design/level-3/131. implement secure secrets management.md.

Current implementation facts to verify before changing them:

  • crates/scriberig-tui/src/overlay/mod.rs currently owns a multiline ComposerState, but it is an Overlay::Composer rather than persistent session-surface state;
  • crates/scriberig-tui/src/view/session.rs already projects branch depth and generic tool rows, but it does not expose the richer causal execution activity required here;
  • crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/events.rs currently emits bounded runtime events such as phase, model delta, and tool start/completion, but not the complete structured activity contract required here;
  • crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/config.rs currently has a provider profile with one model string and provider capabilities, but no model library or model-specific thinking-level descriptors;
  • crates/scriberig-app/src/event.rs currently reduces public agent observation mostly to output produced/delta plus generic operation events;
  • crates/scriberig-protocol/src/agent.rs currently exposes provider-neutral start/continue/result structures but no public model library, thinking selection, or activity projection;
  • crates/scriberig-protocol/src/event.rs has a monotonic public event sequence which can be reused rather than replaced;
  • web/packages/agent-ui already exists and is the reusable web owner; AgentComposer and BranchActivityView are currently intentionally simple and must be extended rather than replaced by app-local semantics.

Baseline inventory verified for this task:

  • The shared application model library now belongs to scriberig-app::agent_console::model; the integrated runtime's ProviderConfig remains the provider connection owner and still selects a single provider model until adapter-library integration is implemented.
  • Runtime provider/model configuration is owned by ProviderConfig in crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/config.rs; ProviderModel in src/model_provider.rs binds one provider adapter to one model string.
  • Durable execution records are owned by scriberig-session: Branch aggregates ordered ExecutionActivity, ModelInvocation, ModelOutput, ToolInvocation, and ToolResult; ModelInvocation records safe provider, model, profile, thinking, and request/context fingerprint provenance.
  • Session.execution now owns the persistent session-scoped profile/model/ thinking selection and independent mutation revision; the protocol session read projection carries the same fields for clients.
  • Shared application entry points currently accept agent commands through SessionBackend and ApplicationService; runtime events are projected through scriberig-app::ApplicationEvent and the public event sequence.
  • Server event streaming and Rust/TypeScript clients already exist. Safe model library and session selection APIs now cross the app, protocol, server, and client boundaries; causal activity query/mutation APIs do not yet exist.
  • TUI prompt submission already routes through SessionBackend; multiline editing is currently available only through Overlay::Composer.
  • Web protocol and client already expose branch pages and agent operation events; @scriberig/model owns durable branch/activity state plus transient output, and @scriberig/agent-ui owns reusable composer/activity rendering.
  • Deterministic runtime coverage exists in separate fixtures (FakeProvider model tests and nested branch tests), but no single shared fixture currently spans model response, tool result, and nested child causality. Extend the existing runtime fixtures as the owning behavior is implemented.

The focused baseline cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime --test nested_branches recursive_children_preserve_depth_and_hide_child_history initially exposed a duplicate RequestFingerprintInput definition in context.rs, left behind after extraction to context/fingerprint.rs. The duplicate was removed and the same focused fixture now passes. The runtime fixture inventory remains split across model_provider.rs, named_tools.rs, and nested_branches.rs; no single combined fixture has been identified yet.

If any of those statements are no longer true, update this section before continuing.

docs.title: Architectural Invariants
docs.text: These rules are not optional.

docs.title: 1. Execution configuration and presentation preferences are different
docs.text:
Execution configuration changes what the model does:

model
thinking level
generation parameters when exposed later
branch/invocation overrides

Presentation preferences change only what a client renders:

reasoning visibility
tool invocation simple/detailed
tool output hidden/summary/full
prompt/model-request hidden/shown

Do not store presentation-only changes as semantic session turns or model invocations.

docs.title: 2. Capture once, render many ways
docs.text:
The runtime/session/application layers must capture enough safe structured activity that the user can change presentation mode without rerunning the model or tool.

Changing:

tool output: hidden -> full
reasoning: hidden -> shown
prompt: hidden -> shown
tool invocation: simple -> detailed

must not execute anything again.

docs.title: 3. Never expose private chain-of-thought
docs.text:
"Show thinking" means:

  • Scriberig-generated runtime status such as Thinking, Planning, Waiting for tool, or equivalent safe phase information;
  • provider/model content explicitly intended to be shown to the user, represented as a reasoning summary when available.

It does not mean capturing, persisting, requesting, or displaying hidden/private chain-of-thought.

docs.title: 4. Persist causality, not UI indentation
docs.text:
The canonical/shared activity representation stores parent/correlation relationships. TUI/web derive visual depth.

Do not persist fields such as indent_pixels, terminal_depth, or a color index as semantic state.

docs.title: 5. Branch tree and activity tree remain distinct
docs.text:
The session graph owns branch ancestry.

The activity projection owns immediate execution causality such as:

model invocation
  reasoning summary
  tool invocation
    tool result
  child branch start
    child activity

Do not replace the existing session branch graph with an arbitrary UI activity tree.

docs.title: 6. Credentials never enter public/session activity
docs.text:
Credentials remain references resolved at the runtime/provider boundary.

Never place these into session records, protocol DTOs, prompt-display payloads, TUI state, web state, logs, test snapshots, or model profiles:

API key value
Authorization header value
secret environment value
resolved credential value

docs.title: 7. Running invocations are immutable with respect to later selection changes
docs.text:
Changing model or thinking level while an invocation is running affects the next invocation only.

The running invocation keeps the resolved model/thinking configuration it started with.

docs.title: 8. Observation ordering and mutation concurrency are separate
docs.text:
Reuse monotonic event/activity cursor semantics for observation/replay.

Use session/config revision or equivalent optimistic-concurrency data for mutations where simultaneous TUI/web changes can conflict.

Do not use an event cursor as a mutation revision.

docs.title: Required Conceptual Data Model
docs.text: Use existing repository naming/owners when equivalents already exist. The following shapes define semantics, not mandatory exact Rust names.

docs.title: Model descriptor
docs.text:
A model known to the system must expose safe capabilities:

struct ModelDescriptor {
    id: ModelId,
    display_name: String,
    provider_profile: ProviderProfileId,
    provider_model_id: String,
    capabilities: ModelCapabilities,
    thinking_levels: Vec<ThinkingLevelDescriptor>,
    default_thinking_level: Option<ThinkingLevelId>,
}

struct ThinkingLevelDescriptor {
    id: ThinkingLevelId,
    label: String,
    description: Option<String>,
    order: u32,
}

Do not define one global Low/Medium/High enum. The available levels belong to the model/provider capability declaration.

docs.title: Model profile/library entry
docs.text:
User/project configuration should be able to describe a curated model entry without containing a resolved secret:

struct ModelProfile {
    id: ModelProfileId,
    display_name: String,
    model: ModelId,
    connection: ConnectionRef,
    credential: Option<CredentialRef>,
    default_thinking_level: Option<ThinkingLevelId>,
    enabled: bool,
}

Adapt this to existing provider/profile configuration rather than duplicating it.

docs.title: Execution selection
docs.text:
Interactive resolution order must be explicit and tested:

invocation override
  -> branch override
  -> session active selection
  -> project default
  -> user/model-profile default
  -> runtime/provider fallback

The session-level selection is the ordinary interactive default.

docs.title: Resolved invocation provenance
docs.text:
Every actual invocation records safe resolved provenance sufficient to explain history later:

provider profile/display id
provider model id/model descriptor id
model profile id when used
thinking level actually used
safe generation parameters when applicable
context/request fingerprint already supported by session/runtime design

Editing/deleting a model profile later must not make old invocation provenance ambiguous.

docs.title: Presentation preferences
docs.text:
Use independent fields equivalent to:

enum ReasoningVisibility { Hidden, Shown }
enum ToolInvocationPresentation { Simple, Detailed }
enum ToolOutputVisibility { Hidden, Summary, Full }
enum PromptVisibility { Hidden, Shown }

struct AgentPresentationPreferences {
    reasoning: ReasoningVisibility,
    tool_invocation: ToolInvocationPresentation,
    tool_output: ToolOutputVisibility,
    prompt: PromptVisibility,
}

Optional presets may map to those fields:

Minimal -> hidden / simple / hidden / hidden
Normal  -> shown  / simple / summary / hidden
Verbose -> shown  / detailed / full / hidden
Debug   -> shown  / detailed / full / shown

Presets are shortcuts only. Do not replace the independent fields with one trace_level enum.

docs.title: Structured model request for prompt display
docs.text:
Do not model "prompt" as one flat string if the runtime already compiles multiple sections/messages/tools.

Expose a safe structured representation equivalent to:

ModelRequestRecord
  invocation
  instruction sections
  conversation/messages
  semantic/context references or safe rendered context
  tool definitions/references
  resolved model configuration
  optional token estimate

The visible representation is the canonical Scriberig request immediately before provider-specific serialization, not raw outbound HTTP JSON.

Secret values, authorization information, and sensitive tool parameters must be redacted/omitted before this structure reaches a public/application activity stream.

docs.title: Shared session activity item
docs.text:
Create or extend a UI-neutral projection equivalent to:

struct SessionActivityItem {
    id: ActivityId,
    sequence: ActivitySequence,
    session: SessionRef,
    branch: BranchRef,
    parent: Option<ActivityId>,
    kind: ActivityKind,
    state: ActivityState,
    content: ActivityContent,
    durable_ref: Option<SemanticRef>,
}

Required kinds include semantic equivalents of:

HumanInput
AssistantOutput
ReasoningSummary
RuntimeStatus
ModelInvocation
ModelRequest
ToolInvocation
ToolResult
BranchStarted
BranchCompleted
OperationProgress
Validation
ModelSelectionChanged
ThinkingLevelChanged
Error

Do not add an activity kind for raw hidden chain-of-thought.

Model and thinking selection changes are retained in the session execution selection's bounded history (latest 100 records), keyed by mutation revision. They are replayed with the session read and are not conversation turns.

Safe reasoning summaries and runtime status currently use the typed transient operation event stream. They remain available for local hidden/shown rerenders while that client retains its live tail. Disconnect discards that tail; session refresh restores durable execution activity, current selection, selection history, and final results. Visibility changes do not request new execution.

docs.title: Implementation Phases
docs.text: Work in this order. Do not begin a later surface until the shared owner it depends on is implemented and targeted tests pass.

docs.title: Phase A - Baseline Inventory and Test Fixtures
docs.text:
• [x] Re-read root, crate, TUI, web, and package AGENTS.md files for every planned modification.
  • [x] Inspect current model/provider types and record in this plan which existing type owns provider/model configuration.
  • [x] Inspect current session ModelInvocation, ToolInvocation, and ToolResult records and reuse them where possible.
  • [x] Inspect current application agent start/continue/event APIs and identify the exact owner for model selection and activity observation.
  • [x] Inspect current server/Rust-client/TypeScript-client event transport before adding any endpoint or stream.
  • [x] Inspect TUI reducer/effect/keymap/rendering files and identify the existing composer submit path; do not create a second submit path.
  • [x] Inspect @scriberig/protocol, @scriberig/client, @scriberig/model, @scriberig/react, and @scriberig/agent-ui before adding web state.
  • [x] Identify existing deterministic fake-provider tests in the runtime and inspect task 115's shared-fixture requirements.
  • [x] Add or identify a minimal fixture capable of a model response, a tool call/result, and a nested child branch; use it throughout later targeted tests.

Targeted verification only:

Run the smallest existing fixture/unit test that proves the inspected agent path is healthy.
Do not run a whole workspace/package family in this phase.

docs.title: Phase B - Provider-Neutral Model Library and Thinking Capabilities
docs.text:
Architectural owner: provider-neutral model identity/capability types at the lowest appropriate agent layer; runtime owns provider translation; application owns user-facing selection policy.

  • [x] Add provider-neutral ModelId/descriptor/profile concepts only if equivalent types do not already exist.
  • [x] Add ordered ThinkingLevelDescriptor support to model capabilities.
  • [x] Allow a model descriptor/profile to declare a default thinking level.
  • [x] Validate that configured default/current thinking ids are members of the selected model's supported levels.
  • [x] Extend provider adapter configuration so one provider connection can expose/select model entries without embedding credentials into public descriptors.
  • [x] Add provider-adapter translation from Scriberig thinking-level id to the provider-specific request setting.
  • [x] Keep provider-specific wire names/values inside the provider adapter.
  • [x] Add deterministic fake-provider support for asserting which model and thinking level were resolved.
  • [x] Add tests proving two models may advertise different thinking-level lists.
  • [x] Add tests proving the code does not assume low/medium/high globally.
  • [x] Add tests proving credential values are absent from model descriptor/profile serialization/debug output.

Targeted verification examples:

cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime thinking
cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime model

Use a narrower filter if available.

docs.title: Phase C - Session-Scoped Model and Thinking Selection
docs.text:
Application semantics own this behavior. TUI/web must not mutate provider config directly.

  • [x] Add/extend session execution configuration with active model profile/model and thinking level.
  • [x] Implement documented resolution order: invocation -> branch -> session -> project -> profile/user -> runtime fallback.
  • [x] Implement deterministic fallback when a model change makes the current thinking level unsupported.
  • [x] Emit/record a safe visible selection-change activity when a user changes model.
  • [x] Persist/replay safe visible model/thinking selection-change activity, including automatic fallback caused by model change.
  • [x] Ensure a running invocation snapshots its already-resolved model/thinking and does not change when session selection changes.
  • [x] Ensure the next invocation uses the newly selected model/thinking.
  • [x] Extend ModelInvocation provenance with the resolved safe model/thinking identifiers required for historical inspection.
  • [x] Ensure deleting/editing a model profile cannot erase historical resolved invocation provenance.
  • [x] Add optimistic concurrency/revision validation for session execution-setting mutations if the existing app mutation contract supports concurrent clients.
  • [x] Add application operations for listing model library entries, reading current selection, setting model, and setting thinking level.
  • [x] Keep provider credentials/configuration resolution inside runtime/server composition rather than exposing it through session operations.

Targeted tests must prove at least:

  • [x] model change affects next invocation only;
  • [x] thinking-level change affects next invocation only;
  • [x] model change falls back from an unsupported thinking level deterministically;
  • [x] concurrent/stale selection mutation is rejected rather than silently overwriting when revision checking is available;
  • [x] historical invocation retains exact model/thinking provenance.

Targeted verification examples:

cargo test -p scriberig-app model_selection
cargo test -p scriberig-app thinking
cargo test -p scriberig-session model_invocation

Run only the owning tests, not every crate together.

docs.title: Phase D - Safe Structured Model Request and Prompt Visibility Source
docs.text:
The runtime compiles the request. The public/application layer receives only a safe structured projection.

  • [x] Identify the existing provider-neutral compiled request type from task 109/provider runtime and extend/reuse it rather than creating a second prompt builder.
  • [x] Add a safe inspectable model-request record/projection containing instructions/messages/context/tool definitions/resolved execution settings as appropriate.
  • [x] Capture the safe request at the point immediately before provider-specific serialization.
  • [x] Add redaction/omission rules for credentials, authorization headers, secret values, sensitive tool parameters, and transport-only metadata.
  • [x] Do not store raw provider HTTP request JSON as the canonical prompt-display source.
  • [x] Associate the request projection with the exact model invocation/activity id.
  • [x] Make the projection retrievable after the invocation so toggling prompt visibility later does not rerun the model.
  • [x] Bound very large sections and retain canonical references/expand handles where needed instead of forcing huge payloads into live event frames.
  • [x] Add a fake unmistakable secret marker test and prove the marker cannot appear in the public request projection.
  • [x] Add a test proving prompt hidden -> shown uses already captured request data and performs zero additional provider calls.

Targeted verification examples:

cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime model_request
cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime redaction

docs.title: Phase E - Structured Tool Invocation and Tool Result Presentation Metadata
docs.text:
Do not make React or Ratatui guess how arbitrary tool JSON should be summarized.

  • [x] Extend/reuse trusted tool descriptors so a tool can provide a compact human-readable invocation presentation where appropriate.
  • [x] Preserve structured invocation arguments for detailed rendering.
  • [x] Mark/redact sensitive parameters through tool schema/metadata rather than string matching in individual UIs.
  • [x] Extend/reuse tool result representation with deterministic presentation metadata equivalent to summary and bounded preview.
  • [x] Keep the canonical/full result addressable through a durable result/reference even when UI output mode is hidden or summary.
  • [x] Ensure summary is preferably produced by the tool/result boundary, not by an extra LLM call.
  • [x] Add a safe generic fallback summary when a tool does not supply one.
  • [x] Ensure full mode remains bounded in the immediate list view; huge results expose expansion/retrieval rather than dumping unbounded text.
  • [x] Add tests proving simple and detailed invocation modes reference the same invocation id and arguments.
  • [x] Add tests proving hidden, summary, and full result modes reference the same captured result and do not rerun the tool.
  • [x] Add a sensitive argument test proving detailed mode renders a redacted value.

Targeted verification examples:

cargo test -p scriberig-agent-core tool
cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime tool
cargo test -p scriberig-session tool

Only run the crate/filter that owns the changed behavior.

docs.title: Phase F - Shared Causal Session Activity Projection
docs.text:
This phase is the central contract between execution and presentation.

  • [x] Add/extend a provider-neutral SessionActivityItem projection with stable id, sequence, session, branch, causal parent, kind, state/content, and optional durable reference.
  • [x] Derive causal parent relationships from explicit runtime/session correlations; do not infer causality from timestamps or current screen order.
  • [x] Map durable session inputs/outputs/model/tool/branch/result records into activity items.
  • [x] Map safe runtime status/progress events into transient/live activity items.
  • [x] Represent user-displayable reasoning summaries distinctly from runtime status and assistant output.
  • [x] Never generate an activity containing hidden chain-of-thought.
  • [x] Associate tool result activity with its exact tool invocation parent.
  • [x] Associate child branch activity/start with the activity that spawned the child where that relation is known.
  • [x] Preserve the existing session branch tree independently from activity causality.
  • [x] Give activity observation a monotonic cursor/sequence suitable for replay/deduplication.
  • [x] Merge durable history with a live tail so reconnect can reconstruct durable activity and then resume observation.
  • [x] Ensure duplicate/out-of-order live events cannot regress a newer activity state.
  • [x] Ensure a committed durable output/result replaces or settles corresponding transient activity instead of creating duplicate fake history.
  • [x] Keep large tool/model-request bodies behind bounded summaries plus durable expansion references.

Targeted tests must cover:

  • [x] model invocation -> tool invocation -> tool result parent chain;
  • [x] nested child branch activity causality;
  • [x] duplicate/out-of-order event handling;
  • [x] durable reload after losing all transient events;
  • [x] one activity sequence renders with multiple presentation modes without semantic changes.

Targeted verification examples:

cargo test -p scriberig-app activity
cargo test -p scriberig-session activity

Use the exact owning crate after inspection.

docs.title: Phase G - Public Protocol, Server, Rust Client, and Web Protocol/Client
docs.text:
Expose the shared concepts without leaking runtime/provider internals.

  • [x] Add protocol DTOs for model descriptors/profiles safe for clients.
  • [x] Add protocol DTOs for available thinking levels and current resolved/session selection.
  • [x] Add protocol DTOs for execution-setting mutations.
  • [x] Add protocol DTOs for causal session activity and activity cursor/replay.
  • [x] Add protocol DTOs/references for safe model-request inspection.
  • [x] Add protocol DTOs/references for bounded tool presentation metadata where not already part of activity content.
  • [x] Confirm protocol DTOs contain no credential source values, secret material, provider raw request bodies, or hidden reasoning.
  • [x] Extend server dispatch for model library/query, model/thinking selection, activity observation/replay, and safe request/result detail retrieval.
  • [x] Reuse the existing event transport/SSE boundary from task 114 rather than adding a second streaming stack.
  • [x] Keep mutations as ordinary request/response operations and observation as the existing resumable event/activity flow unless current transport architecture requires another existing abstraction.
  • [x] Extend the Rust client with semantic methods rather than exposing envelopes.
  • [x] Update generated/authoritative TypeScript protocol exports.
  • [x] Extend @scriberig/client with the same semantic methods.
  • [x] Test cursor resume and authoritative refresh after a missed/transient event window.
  • [x] Test stale concurrent model/thinking mutation behavior across two clients when revision protection is implemented.

Targeted verification examples:

cargo test -p scriberig-protocol agent
cargo test -p scriberig-server agent
cargo test -p scriberig-client agent
pnpm --dir web --filter @scriberig/protocol test
pnpm --dir web --filter @scriberig/client test

Run these one at a time as each owner changes. Do not run the complete web test command.

docs.title: Phase H - Presentation Preferences and Presets
docs.text:
Presentation preferences are not semantic session history.

  • [x] Add a shared/user-preference representation for reasoning visibility.
  • [x] Add tool invocation Simple | Detailed preference.
  • [x] Add tool output Hidden | Summary | Full preference.
  • [x] Add prompt Hidden | Shown preference.
  • [x] Implement optional Minimal, Normal, Verbose, and Debug presets strictly as setters over the independent fields.
  • [x] Allow a client-local override layer so TUI and web may intentionally use different presentation verbosity while observing the same session execution state.
  • [x] Define and test preference resolution order: client-local override -> shared/user preference -> built-in default.
  • [x] Ensure changing any presentation preference emits no semantic session turn, no model-selection activity, and no provider/tool invocation.
  • [x] Ensure presentation preferences can be applied to already-loaded activity immediately.
  • [x] Keep execution selection (model, thinking level) out of this presentation-preference structure.

If the repository does not yet have a general user-preference persistence boundary, implement the smallest reusable owner consistent with application architecture; do not bury these settings in TUI-only or web/apps/scriberig-only state.

Targeted tests:

  • [x] preference resolution order;
  • [x] preset expansion into individual fields;
  • [x] client-local override does not mutate shared session execution configuration;
  • [x] changing view settings produces zero model/tool calls.

docs.title: Phase I - Persistent TUI Agent Console
docs.text: scriberig-tui remains a renderer/controller over shared application semantics.

docs.title: Persistent composer
docs.text:
• [x] Extract/reuse the existing multiline composer editing behavior from Overlay::Composer so the normal Agent/Session surface owns a persistent composer state.
  • [x] Keep modal input behavior available where it is still useful, but do not require opening a modal before every agent message.
  • [x] Route submit through the existing shared agent submission effect/service path; do not create a second provider/runtime path.
  • [x] When no active session exists, shared application semantics start work; when a session/branch is active, shared application semantics continue it according to existing policy.
  • [x] Keep the composer usable while an agent operation is running.
  • [x] Keep submit/send separate from stop/cancel.
  • [x] Do not reinterpret a second submit as cancellation.
  • [x] Support multiline input without depending only on Shift+Enter; preserve terminal-compatible newline bindings such as Ctrl+J/configured equivalent if current keymap uses them.
  • [x] Paste must remain literal input data rather than command replay.

docs.title: Model and thinking controls
docs.text:
• [x] Show current model in the Agent/Session header/status area.
  • [x] Show current thinking level beside the model.
  • [x] Add a model picker backed by the shared model library.
  • [x] Add a thinking picker whose entries come only from the selected model's advertised thinking levels.
  • [x] Reflect model/thinking changes made by another client after authoritative refresh/event observation.
  • [x] If a model change forces thinking fallback, display the resulting shared activity/status rather than silently hiding it.
  • [x] Add /model, /thinking, and /view composer commands only as convenience adapters to shared application operations/preferences.
  • [x] Do not implement slash commands as TUI-local canonical state changes.

docs.title: Activity renderer
docs.text:
• [x] Render causal activity items rather than formatting generic runtime strings ad hoc.
  • [x] Render depth using a narrow vertical rail glyph, preferably ▏ with │ fallback where necessary.
  • [x] Give each nesting level a distinct theme color and cycle safely after a finite palette.
  • [x] Preserve indent/rail structure when color is unavailable so hierarchy never relies on color alone.
  • [x] Prefer drawing all active ancestor rails for deep nesting when terminal width permits.
  • [x] Keep branch nesting usable at narrow terminal widths.
  • [x] Show runtime/reasoning rows only when reasoning visibility is Shown.
  • [x] In Simple tool invocation mode, render a command-like compact line.
  • [x] In Detailed mode, render one parameter per line with nested structured indentation and redaction.
  • [x] In tool output Hidden, show invocation/status but no output body.
  • [x] In Summary, show deterministic result summary only.
  • [x] In Full, show bounded preview/full detail with expansion/navigation for large results.
  • [x] When prompt visibility is Shown, render grouped safe model-request sections; when hidden, omit them entirely.
  • [x] Toggling any of these modes must re-render already captured data without rerunning work.

docs.title: TUI targeted tests
docs.text:
Use reducer/service tests and Ratatui test backend only for the affected behaviors.

  • [x] persistent composer submits start/continue through existing service boundary;
  • [x] multiline typing and paste remain correct;
  • [x] composer remains editable during active operation;
  • [x] cancel invokes shared cancellation and submit does not cancel;
  • [x] model picker shows shared model library;
  • [x] thinking picker changes when selected model changes;
  • [x] nested activity renders rails with depth structure;
  • [x] reasoning hidden/shown changes only rendered rows;
  • [x] simple/detailed tool calls are two renderings of one activity;
  • [x] hidden/summary/full outputs are three renderings of one result;
  • [x] prompt hidden/shown uses one captured request;
  • [x] sensitive values never appear in detailed tool/prompt frames.

Targeted verification example:

cargo test -p scriberig-tui composer
cargo test -p scriberig-tui activity
cargo test -p scriberig-tui model

Use the smallest relevant filter after inspecting the test names.

docs.title: Phase J - Reusable Web Agent Console and Integrated App
docs.text: Do not put the semantic implementation only in web/apps/scriberig.

docs.title: Web model/react state
docs.text:
• [x] Extend @scriberig/model with model library, current execution selection, activity cursor/state, and presentation preferences without duplicating Rust/server semantics.
  • [x] Keep durable activity separate from transient live tail.
  • [x] Extend reducer logic for duplicate/out-of-order activity events and reconnect refresh.
  • [x] Add reusable hooks/controllers in @scriberig/react only where generic bindings are needed.

docs.title: @scriberig/agent-ui
docs.text:
• [x] Extend the existing AgentComposer rather than replacing it with an app-local composer.
  • [x] Keep composer available while execution is running and expose separate cancel/stop controls.
  • [x] Add reusable model picker.
  • [x] Add reusable thinking-level picker whose options derive from active model capabilities.
  • [x] Add reusable view/trace controls for reasoning, invocation detail, tool output, and prompt visibility.
  • [x] Extend/replace the simple BranchActivityView rendering with the shared causal activity projection.
  • [x] Render a literal CSS 2px vertical depth rail per visible nesting level.
  • [x] Use distinct depth colors but retain indentation/borders/text so hierarchy is accessible without color.
  • [x] Render simple tool invocation as a compact command-like line.
  • [x] Render detailed invocation with one parameter per line and nested structured values.
  • [x] Render tool output hidden/summary/full according to preference without new server execution.
  • [x] Render safe prompt/model-request sections only when enabled.
  • [x] Render reasoning summaries/status only when enabled.
  • [x] Ensure screen-reader/live-region behavior does not announce every token/status update noisily.
  • [x] Ensure all controls are keyboard operable and expose accessible labels/state.

docs.title: Integrated app
docs.text:
• [x] Compose the reusable controls/activity renderer in the official Scriberig app.
  • [x] MUI-specific styling may live in components-mui/integrated app, but model/thinking/activity semantics remain in public packages.
  • [x] Confirm the integrated app imports no provider SDK/config secret and does not contact model providers directly.

docs.title: Web targeted tests
docs.text:
• [x] composer submit/continue and cancel are separate actions;
  • [x] model and thinking selectors use shared client/model state;
  • [x] TUI-originated model/thinking change can be reflected after event/refresh;
  • [x] 2px rails represent nested activity depth;
  • [x] visibility/detail controls rerender existing activity without network execution;
  • [x] prompt/tool sensitive markers are absent from rendered DOM/text;
  • [x] reconnect reconstructs durable activity and attaches the live tail;
  • [x] keyboard/accessibility behavior for selectors, activity expansion, and controls is covered.

Targeted verification examples:

pnpm --dir web --filter @scriberig/model test
pnpm --dir web --filter @scriberig/react test
pnpm --dir web --filter @scriberig/agent-ui test
pnpm --dir web --filter @scriberig/agent-ui typecheck

Do not run pnpm --dir web test, typecheck, or build for the entire workspace yet.

docs.title: Phase K - Cross-Surface Conformance Scenarios
docs.text:
Extend the existing deterministic conformance fixture set from task 115. Semantic conformance compares shared state/results, not terminal cells versus React markup.

  • [x] Scenario: TUI selects model B; web refresh/event observation sees model B for the same session.
  • [x] Scenario: web selects model A; TUI refresh/event observation sees model A.
  • [x] Scenario: a running invocation on model A remains on A after session switches to B; the next invocation uses B.
  • [x] Scenario: a running invocation at thinking medium remains medium; next invocation uses newly selected high or equivalent model-advertised id.
  • [x] Scenario: switching to a model that does not support the current thinking id resolves the documented fallback and emits visible safe change activity.
  • [x] Scenario: TUI and web may use different presentation preferences while observing the exact same underlying activity ids/results.
  • [x] Scenario: reasoning hidden versus shown changes no semantic session/activity source data and performs no extra model call.
  • [x] Scenario: tool output hidden/summary/full performs no extra tool call.
  • [x] Scenario: tool invocation simple/detailed performs no extra tool call.
  • [x] Scenario: prompt hidden/shown performs no extra provider call.
  • [x] Scenario: nested model -> tool -> child branch -> tool result has stable parent relationships independent of renderer.
  • [x] Scenario: disconnect/reconnect loses transient events but reconstructs durable activity and final result.
  • [x] Scenario: huge tool result stays bounded in primary activity UI and remains retrievable by stable reference.
  • [x] Scenario: an unmistakable fake provider secret is absent from protocol/activity/TUI/web/model-request presentation.
  • [x] Scenario: an unmistakable fake sensitive tool parameter is redacted in detailed tool invocation on both surfaces.
  • [x] Scenario: no fixture/assertion depends on private chain-of-thought.
  • [x] Scenario: cancel semantics remain shared and are not triggered by submit, navigation, closing a panel, or changing view preferences.

During this phase run only the specific conformance test/scenario being added or fixed.

Example:

cargo test -p scriberig-conformance <specific_scenario_name>
pnpm --dir web --filter <owning-package> test -- <specific-test-filter-if-supported>

Do not run the complete conformance/full suite until the final gate.

docs.text:
