Never render credentials, authorization values, or private reasoning in this view.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not add a second transcript database.
  • Do not flatten the canonical session into a chat-only model.
  • Do not make the TUI own model/provider execution semantics.
  • Do not make the web app own model/provider execution semantics.
  • Do not create TUI-only or web-only model selection state as the authoritative selection.
  • Do not create a process-global mutable active_model as the interactive source of truth.
  • Do not hard-code one universal list of thinking levels.
  • Do not change a running invocation when the user changes future model/thinking selection.
  • Do not expose hidden/private chain-of-thought.
  • Do not use presentation visibility to decide whether activity/result data is captured.
  • Do not rerun a tool/model merely because the user expands or changes verbosity.
  • Do not dump unbounded tool results or raw provider JSON into TUI/web activity.
  • Do not send credentials to browser/TUI clients.
  • Do not place secret values in model profiles, protocol DTOs, session records, or prompt-display data.
  • Do not infer causal nesting only from timestamps.
  • Do not store colors/pixels/terminal indentation in semantic activity records.
  • Do not conflate event cursors with mutation revisions.
  • Do not add a new agent-specific network stack when existing HTTP/event transport is adequate.
  • Do not bypass shared cancellation, session, operation, or migration semantics.
  • Do not run the full repository test suite before the Final Full-Suite Gate.

docs.title: Implementation Completion Checklist
docs.text: All boxes below must be checked from work completed in the phases above before the final full-suite gate begins.

docs.title: Shared execution semantics
docs.text:
• [x] Model library/profile abstraction exists at the correct shared layer.
  • [x] Models advertise their own ordered thinking levels and defaults.
  • [x] Provider adapters translate thinking ids without leaking provider wire semantics upward.
  • [x] Session model selection is shared and scoped rather than process-global.
  • [x] Session thinking selection is shared and scoped.
  • [x] Running invocations are unaffected by later selection changes.
  • [x] Invocation provenance records resolved model and thinking safely.
  • [x] Unsupported thinking after a model switch falls back deterministically and visibly.

docs.title: Shared activity and safe inspection
docs.text:
• [x] Causal session activity projection exists with stable ids/sequence/parents and typed provider-neutral kinds.
  • [x] Durable activity and transient live tail are distinct, with typed shared semantics for both.
  • [x] Safe reasoning summary/status is distinct from assistant output; private reasoning is excluded, and transient reconnect behavior is documented and tested.
  • [x] Tool invocation retains structured arguments plus safe compact presentation.
  • [x] Tool result retains deterministic summary/preview plus durable full-result reference.
  • [x] Safe structured model-request projection exists and is redacted.
  • [x] Activity replay/reconnect reconstructs durable state without requiring stream history.

docs.title: Presentation controls
docs.text:
• [x] Reasoning visibility supports hidden/shown.
  • [x] Tool invocation supports simple/detailed.
  • [x] Tool output supports hidden/summary/full.
  • [x] Prompt/model-request supports hidden/shown.
  • [x] Optional verbosity presets only set independent controls.
  • [x] Presentation changes never create model/tool invocations or semantic session history.
  • [x] Client-local presentation override can coexist with shared/user default.

docs.title: Protocol/client/server
docs.text:
• [x] Rust protocol exposes safe model/thinking/activity operations.
  • [x] Server dispatch and existing event transport expose them without provider secrets.
  • [x] Rust client exposes semantic APIs.
  • [x] TypeScript protocol/client expose equivalent APIs.
  • [x] Observation cursor and mutation revision semantics are not conflated.

docs.title: TUI
docs.text:
• [x] Free-text multiline composer is persistent in normal Agent/Session UI.
  • [x] Existing shared submit/cancel service paths are reused.
  • [x] Composer remains usable while work is running.
  • [x] Model picker and thinking picker are functional.
  • [x] /model, /thinking, /view conveniences map to shared semantics if implemented.
  • [x] Causal activity renders terminal depth rails with non-color hierarchy fallback.
  • [x] Thinking, tool-call detail, tool-output verbosity, and prompt display controls all work without rerun.
  • [x] Sensitive values are redacted in TUI detail modes.

docs.title: Web
docs.text:
• [x] Reusable public web packages, not only the app, own agent-console behavior.
  • [x] Persistent composer, model picker, thinking picker, and view controls are reusable.
  • [x] Activity uses literal 2px nesting rails plus accessible non-color hierarchy.
  • [x] Thinking, tool-call detail, tool-output verbosity, and prompt display controls all work without rerun.
  • [x] Integrated app consumes only public package semantics.
  • [x] Sensitive values are redacted in web detail modes.

docs.title: Targeted verification
docs.text:
• [x] Every implementation checkbox above was accompanied by the smallest relevant targeted test/check.
  • [x] Cross-surface deterministic scenarios for model/thinking synchronization pass individually.
  • [x] Cross-surface deterministic scenarios for presentation-only changes pass individually.
  • [x] Secret/sensitive-value leakage scenarios pass individually.
  • [x] Reconnect/durable-recovery scenario passes individually.
  • [x] No full workspace/repository test suite was run before this point.

docs.title: Final Full-Suite Gate
docs.text:
Do not enter this section until every implementation and targeted-verification checkbox above is [x].

This is the one point at which repository-wide verification is intentionally required.

Run the repository-wide quality/test commands required by current AGENTS.md and workspace scripts. At minimum, unless repository instructions have changed:

python3 tools/lint_repo.py --fix
cargo fmt --all
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
pnpm --dir web format
pnpm --dir web typecheck
pnpm --dir web test
pnpm --dir web build

If formatting changes files, inspect them and rerun the affected final checks as needed. Do not mark a command complete merely because it was started.

  • [x] Repository lint/fix completes without unresolved violations.
  • [x] Rust formatting completes and leaves intended source changes only.
  • [x] Full Rust workspace check passes.
  • [x] Full Rust workspace Clippy passes with warnings denied.
  • [ ] Full Rust workspace test suite passes.
  • Focused PHP self-hosting candidate validation passes with TEMP/TMP on a D: temporary directory outside the checkout. The first workspace attempt exhausted D: while linking; cargo clean reclaimed generated artifacts. The subsequent workspace run passed the PHP candidate, stale-base, cancellation, and validation-failure scenarios, then stopped at provider_secrets_test. The owner subsequently confirmed the local connection was allowed, but the workspace rerun still timed out before its 127.0.0.1 ephemeral listener received requests; Windows accept reported WSA error 10035. The provider test fixture now recognizes that Windows would-block condition, with its focused regression test passing, but the real HTTP tests still receive no connection. A separate bounded PowerShell TCP probe to a local 127.0.0.1 listener also timed out after three seconds. No Portmaster or networking settings were changed. The full Rust workspace test gate remains unchecked pending restoration of local-loopback connectivity and a successful complete rerun.
  • [x] Full web formatting completes.
  • [x] Full web typecheck passes.
  • [x] Full web test suite passes.
  • [x] Full web build passes.
  • [x] Relevant capability/conformance status is updated honestly if this feature adds or advances capability rows.
  • [ ] Re-read all checked items in this plan against the final code after formatting/fixes.
  • [x] Confirm no credential/private-reasoning/sensitive-tool marker appears in public protocol fixtures, TUI snapshots, web snapshots, or captured safe model-request data.
  • [ ] Set the document status to [x] Complete only after every checkbox in this file that is required by the final implementation is checked and the full-suite gate is green.

docs.title: Final Acceptance Contract
docs.text:
The task is complete only when this statement is true:

A user can type freely into either the TUI or web Agent Console, inspect nested agent activity at a chosen verbosity, switch the active model and a model-supported thinking level for future invocations, hide or show reasoning summaries/status and safe model requests, choose simple or detailed tool invocations, choose hidden/summary/full tool results, and observe the same underlying session execution from both surfaces. Execution-affecting changes are durable and provenance-safe; presentation-only changes cause no re-execution and do not pollute semantic history; credentials, sensitive parameters, and private chain-of-thought never enter the public trace.

docs.title: Make the Recursive Agent Tree the Default TUI and Move Auxiliary Views Behind Slash Commands
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Restructure the native Scriberig TUI so that its ordinary experience is a conversation-like projection of the real recursive session tree rather than a linear transcript or multi-pane semantic browser.

The user should still experience the simplicity of Pi/Codex/Claude-style terminal interaction:

  • launch directly into the agent surface;
  • type immediately;
  • see human messages, assistant results, semantic operations, branches, plans, and progress in one main viewport;
  • keep a persistent composer at the bottom;
  • use slash commands to open secondary controls/views.

But the underlying and visible interaction is explicitly tree-aware:

  • agents recursively create child branches;
  • /plan creates durable planned nodes in the same tree;
  • plan dependencies can block/enable sibling work;
  • different branches may be assigned to different model/provider profiles;
  • one auto-advancing plan coordinator exists at a time;
  • the user can navigate to a stable historical replyable node and continue from it;
  • new activity appears at its structural location rather than always at the bottom;
  • completed children collapse to compact BranchResult-style summaries but remain expandable;
  • nesting is shown by colored vertical depth rails;
  • the current reply anchor has a distinct background highlight;
  • per-activity detail settings control rendering without affecting context;
  • source/document edits are normally semantic/domain operations, not generic file writes.

The controlling product rule is:

Conversation is home, but the conversation is a projection of the recursive session/plan tree. Auxiliary inspection/control surfaces are explicit slash-command destinations.

This task depends on and must preserve the invariants in:

  • design/level-1/017. recursive agent decomposition and context isolation.md;
  • design/level-1/018. durable plans dependency scheduling and multi-model execution.md;
  • design/level-1/019. semantic agent operations and projection-first editing.md;
  • task 133 shared model/thinking/trace controls.

The cross-layer implementation sequence is defined in task 135. Do not implement TUI-owned substitutes for missing shared semantics.

docs.title: Instructions for the Implementation Agent
docs.text:
This file is intentionally prescriptive.

Before modifying code:

  1. read repository root AGENTS.md;
  2. read crates/scriberig-tui/AGENTS.md;
  3. read nearest AGENTS.md for every additional crate you touch;
  4. read this file fully;
  5. read Level-1 documents 009, 014, 015, 016, 017, 018, and 019;
  6. read Level-2 documents 021, 022, 023, and 024;
  7. read Level-3 tasks 103, 133, and 135;
  8. inspect current code before choosing names;
  9. reuse existing application/session/model/activity abstractions;
  10. do not implement backend/session/runtime behavior in the TUI merely to make a screen work.

docs.title: Checklist discipline
docs.text:
• [x] Keep this file open while implementing TUI work.
  • [x] Tick an item immediately after that exact behavior is implemented and targeted verification passes.
  • [x] Never bulk-tick items at the end.
  • [x] If later work invalidates an item, change it back to [ ] immediately.
  • [x] Before marking Complete, re-read every checked item against final code and test evidence.

docs.title: Test discipline
docs.text:
During implementation run only focused tests/checks for changed behavior.

Do not run the full workspace gate until every implementation checkbox is complete.

Useful focused examples include:

cargo test -p scriberig-tui conversation
cargo test -p scriberig-tui tree_projection
cargo test -p scriberig-tui reply_anchor
cargo test -p scriberig-tui slash_command
cargo test -p scriberig-tui plan
cargo test -p scriberig-tui presentation
cargo test -p scriberig-tui layout

docs.title: Current Implementation Facts to Verify First
docs.text:
Before coding, verify these against current main and update this section if repository structure has changed.

  • TuiState currently starts in PrimaryView::Overview rather than a conversation home.
  • interactive startup derives from TuiState::default() and does not automatically create a session.
  • layout currently auto-adds Explorer/Inspector panes based on terminal width.
  • persistent session composer exists but is tied to the structural Session surface.
  • pressing i is currently required to focus the persistent composer after browsing.
  • / currently maps to Find in browse context rather than slash-command composition.
  • : opens an existing command palette.
  • PrimaryView::Session is currently a structural session-tree projection and must be preserved as /session.
  • task-133 model/thinking/reasoning/tool/prompt controls exist and must be reused.
  • current submission contracts may require an existing session identity.
  • current branch continuation APIs may identify only session + branch rather than an exact historical reply anchor.
  • current durable activity/session types may not yet represent planned nodes, dependency edges, coordinator state, per-node assignments, or execution leases.

Do not work around any missing shared contract by inventing local fake IDs, local plan state, or TUI-only continuation semantics.

docs.title: Normal launch
docs.text:
The native interactive TUI must open directly into the recursive agent conversation surface.

Conceptual first frame:

scriberig · no active project                         default-model · medium

No conversation yet.
Type a message to start a session.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
> _

The composer owns ordinary typing immediately.

The user must not have to:

press i
open a composer modal
select Session
open a palette
select a project

before typing the first agent message.

docs.title: Ordinary unbranched interaction
docs.text:
When no visible branch divergence exists, the surface may feel almost linear:

You
Inspect the parser architecture.

▏ inspect Function parse_type
▏ ✓ 4 code groups

Assistant
The parser is split into prefix, named-type, nullable-suffix, and result groups.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
> _

The canonical model is still tree-shaped.

docs.title: Tree-Aware Conversation Projection
docs.text:
The normal conversation must be a dedicated projection over durable session/plan/activity state.

Do not reuse the structural /session tree rows directly as the default transcript.

Conceptually, build UI-neutral rows equivalent to:

HumanMessage
AssistantMessage
BranchHeader
BranchResult
PlanNode
DependencySummary
ModelInvocation
ReasoningSummary
RuntimeStatus
SemanticOperationInvocation
ToolInvocation
OperationResult
ToolResult
Validation
Selection/AssignmentChange
Error

Exact enum names may differ.

Each rendered row must retain stable references to its semantic/session/plan/activity source.

Never use visual row index as semantic identity.

docs.title: Structural Placement, Not Append-Only Placement
docs.text:
The conversation is not a vector whose only update operation is push.

When new activity arrives:

  1. update durable/shared state or local observation cache;
  2. rebuild/incrementally update the tree projection;
  3. locate the activity's structural parent/branch/plan node;
  4. place it beneath that location;
  5. preserve deterministic sibling/activity ordering using shared sequence/ordinal data;
  6. adjust scroll/follow state without changing semantic selection.

If the user replies to an earlier node, the new continuation appears there.

If an agent creates a child branch halfway through a root turn, that child appears there.

If a planned node starts later, execution fills that planned location rather than appearing only at the bottom because wall-clock time advanced.

docs.title: Compact completed child
docs.text:
Default completed branch rendering:

▏ Implement parser capability
▏ ✓ parser entities created and validated

docs.title: Expanded child
docs.text:
Expanded rendering may show:

▏ Implement parser capability
▏
▏ ▏ inspect Function parse_type
▏ ▏ ✓ 4 code groups
▏
▏ ▏ replace expression in nullable-suffix group
▏ ▏ ✓ Expression E17 updated
▏
▏ ▏ Validate parser
▏ ▏ ▏ cargo test -p scriberig-domain-php ...
▏ ▏ ▏ ✓ 12 tests passed
▏
▏ ✓ parser entities created and validated

Expansion is presentation state only.

The parent model context must continue to receive the compact branch result rather than expanded child transcript unless context policy explicitly reopens it.

docs.title: Vertical Depth Rails
docs.text:
Render one visible rail per ancestor depth.

Conceptually:

▏ depth 1
▏ ▏ depth 2
▏ ▏ ▏ depth 3

Requirements:

  • each depth receives a stable color from a theme palette;
  • the palette may cycle;
  • all ancestor rails should be shown when width permits;
  • color is supplemental; rail count/position must preserve nesting without color;
  • narrow terminals may compact older ancestors with an explicit marker such as … ▏ ▏;
  • rail color/depth is derived, never persisted as canonical state;

  • activity-local depth and branch depth may combine visually but remain distinguishable in source data.

  • [x] Branch ancestry produces deterministic rail depth.

  • [x] Rail colors are stable for a given depth during a session.
  • [x] No semantic behavior depends on terminal color support.
  • [x] Narrow layout preserves understandable ancestry.

docs.title: Navigation Cursor, Reply Anchor, and Coordinator Cursor
docs.text:
The TUI must keep these separate:

navigation cursor
reply anchor
coordinator cursor

docs.title: Navigation cursor
docs.text:
Indicates the node currently being browsed.

It may move without changing where the next message will attach.

docs.title: Reply anchor
docs.text:
Identifies the stable replyable session location that receives the next human message.

It must survive:

  • rerendering;
  • width changes;
  • activity verbosity changes;
  • collapse/expand changes;
  • live insertion of unrelated sibling activity.

docs.title: Coordinator cursor
docs.text:
Represents the current location of the single auto-advancing /plan coordinator.

While the user is idle/following, reply anchor may auto-follow coordinator cursor.

Once the user deliberately pins another node or begins composing against it, coordinator movement must not steal the reply target.

  • [x] No cursor/anchor is represented only by row number.
  • [x] Selecting a historical replyable node can set reply anchor.
  • [x] Reply anchor remains stable while unrelated rows appear/disappear.
  • [x] Coordinator auto-follow pauses when the user browses/pins another node.
  • [x] Explicit action returns the UI to coordinator-follow mode.

docs.title: Reply-Anchor Visual Treatment
docs.text:
The current reply anchor must have a strong background highlight or equivalent non-rail treatment.

Do not use the rail color to communicate reply targeting.

The two cues mean different things:

background highlight -> next human message attaches here
rail(s)              -> structural ancestry/depth

When replying to the normal current/coordinator head, the composer may remain visually quiet.

When pinned to a historical/sibling node, show a compact context hint such as:

Replying to: “The parser has four code groups…”
> _

Important state must remain understandable without color alone.

docs.title: Replyable Nodes
docs.text:
For the first implementation, prefer a conservative set of replyable semantic nodes, such as:

HumanInput
AssistantOutput
completed Turn
BranchResult
PlanNode/branch head when shared continuation semantics allow it

Do not allow arbitrary tool-result/activity rows to become continuation anchors unless the shared context compiler defines exact semantics for them.

Non-replyable rows remain navigable/inspectable.

docs.title: First Message and New Session
docs.text:
The initial composer must represent a true NewSession target rather than a fake session ID.

Conceptually:

ConversationTarget::NewSession
ConversationTarget::Existing { session, reply_anchor }

Submission from NewSession must call a shared application start/create operation.

When accepted:

  1. receive authoritative session/root-branch/operation handles;
  2. replace local target with those handles;
  3. render the user input from durable/shared state;
  4. observe execution through normal activity/operation semantics.

Do not allocate canonical session identities inside scriberig-tui.

docs.title: Historical Continuation
docs.text:
Submitting against a historical reply anchor must call a shared continuation operation that identifies the exact semantic continuation location.

The TUI must not construct provider context itself.

The application/runtime context compiler decides which ancestor turns, branch descriptors/results, dependency results, decisions, semantic handles, and recent local activity belong in the new branch context.

Later siblings must not enter the continuation merely because they were created later in wall-clock time.

docs.title: /plan Presentation
docs.text:
The plan is rendered in the same home tree.

Example:

/ Plan: PHP ingestion
▏ ✓ Discover architecture                     local-fast
▏ ◉ Implement parser                          openai-codex
▏ ○ Implement importer                        openrouter-claude
▏   waits: parser
▏ ◉ Research PHP edge cases                   local-research
▏ ○ Integration                               openai-codex
    waits: parser, importer, research

Requirements:

  • planned/blocked/ready/running/completed/failed state has textual/symbolic cues;
  • assignment is compactly visible when useful;
  • dependencies are compact by default and inspectable in detail;
  • starting a planned node fills that structural location;
  • plan revision/replanning does not erase historical durable nodes;
  • coordinator position can be indicated without confusing it with user reply anchor;
  • many worker branches may show running concurrently.

docs.title: /plan Command Family
docs.text:
Recognized commands should map to shared plan operations, conceptually:

/plan <goal>
/plan start
/plan pause
/plan resume
/plan replan
/plan stop
/plan show

The first implementation should prefer plan creation/review before autonomous start.

Do not keep plan structure only in TUI state.

docs.title: Per-Branch Assignment
docs.text:
The user must be able to assign a model/profile to a selected planned/ready branch without changing every other branch.

Use a local command such as:

/assign

or another unambiguous command chosen by the shared command registry.

Do not overload /model ambiguously.

Recommended meaning:

/model   -> session/default future model selection
/assign  -> selected plan node/branch execution assignment

Assignment UI consumes the shared model library/profile capabilities from task 133.

It never stores credentials.

docs.title: Semantic Operations in the Conversation
docs.text:
Tool/activity rendering must reflect that most known source/document work is semantic.

Compact semantic operation:

▏ add function parse_union_type to php::parser
▏ ✓ Function F194 created

Full one-line/wrapped form:

▏ code.add_function module=php::parser after=parse_named_type name=parse_union_type return_type=TypeResult

Structured parameter form:

▏ code.add_function
▏   module: php::parser
▏   after: parse_named_type
▏   name: parse_union_type
▏   return_type: TypeResult

Actual external process:

▏ cargo test -p scriberig-domain-php ...
▏ ✓ 12 tests passed

Do not render every operation as though it were shell syntax.

docs.title: Per-Activity Presentation Preferences
docs.text:
Preserve task-133 execution/presentation separation, but generalize rendering around activity kind.

The shared preference model may evolve to support concepts equivalent to:

semantic/tool invocation:
  Hidden
  CompactTruncated
  Full
  StructuredParameters

operation/tool result:
  Hidden
  Summary
  Preview
  FullBounded

reasoning summary:
  Hidden
  Shown

model request:
  Hidden
  Summary
  StructuredFull

branch:
  Compact
  Expanded

plan dependency/assignment:
  Compact
  Detailed

Do not force all activity types into one generic verbosity enum if their meaningful presentation modes differ.

Presentation changes must not:

  • alter context compilation;
  • change reply anchor;
  • rerun work;
  • change durable plan state;
  • change scheduling;
  • expose secrets or hidden chain-of-thought.

docs.title: Slash Commands Are the UI Escape Hatch
docs.text:
The default home remains the conversation/tree.

Auxiliary controls/views are explicit local commands, for example:

/model
/assign
/thinking
/view
/plan
/session
/explorer
/inspect
/find
/history
/diff
/projection
/changes
/operations
/project
/status
/help
/new

A recognized command must never be sent to the model.

Unknown slash commands must not silently become model input.

Use an explicit literal escape, recommended:

//literal -> send "/literal" as ordinary agent input

Slash completion must operate while typing:

> /mo
  /model

and:

> /pl
  /plan

docs.title: Auxiliary View Behavior
docs.text:
Explorer, Inspector, History, Find, Diff, Projection, Changes, Operations, structural Session tree, model/thinking/view controls, plan detail, and status/debug remain available.

They do not auto-appear based on terminal width.

Opening one deliberately replaces/overlays the body.

Esc returns toward Conversation after closing any inner modal.

Do not delete existing view models merely because they are no longer always visible.

/session specifically preserves the low-level structural session view with IDs/status/provenance useful for deep inspection.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
All normal terminal widths should share the same product mode:

quiet header
conversation/tree viewport
persistent composer
optional compact status

Width may change:

  • wrapping;
  • truncation;
  • number of visible ancestor rails;
  • minor chrome;
  • compact metadata.

Width must not automatically open Explorer or Inspector.

docs.title: Quiet Chrome
docs.text:
Prefer a header similar to:

scriberig · project-name                         codex · high

Optional status line may contain concise information such as:

main · context 34% · plan running · 3 workers

Do not continuously show internal focus enum, verbose service status, or UUID noise in ordinary mode.

Detailed connection/runtime/debug information belongs behind /status or debug/structural views.

docs.title: Composer Behavior
docs.text:
Normal mode:

ordinary key -> edit draft
Enter        -> submit
Ctrl+J       -> newline

No i is required.

Esc may enter tree-navigation/browse mode or close the current special view according to final keymap design, but returning to ordinary conversation typing must be direct and obvious.

While agent work runs:

  • composer remains usable;
  • submission follows shared queue/continuation policy;
  • typing does not implicitly cancel;
  • cancellation is explicit.

Do not let coordinator auto-advance steal a pinned reply anchor or draft.

docs.title: Required Tests
docs.text:
Add targeted tests proving at least:

  • [x] default startup is Conversation, not Overview/Explorer;
  • [x] ordinary typing immediately edits composer;
  • [x] first message uses shared new-session semantics;
  • [x] normal message continues from stable reply anchor;
  • [x] historical reply creates/continues at exact structural location;
  • [x] new activity is inserted structurally, not append-only;
  • [x] autonomous agent child branches appear in the default tree;
  • [x] recursively nested branches produce multiple depth rails;
  • [x] completed child branches collapse by default;
  • [x] expansion does not change model/context semantics;
  • [x] reply anchor survives collapse/verbosity/layout changes;
  • [x] reply anchor receives distinct background treatment;
  • [x] plan nodes appear before execution and retain identity when execution begins;
  • [x] blocked plan nodes show dependency state;
  • [x] concurrent worker branches render in one tree;
  • [x] coordinator-follow and pinned reply anchor remain independent;
  • [x] semantic operations render differently from actual process/shell activity;
  • [x] each supported per-activity verbosity mode renders deterministically;
  • [x] hidden reasoning never exposes private chain-of-thought;
  • [x] /model opens session model controls locally;
  • [x] /assign changes selected node assignment through shared semantics;
  • [x] /plan commands are local and never reach the model;
  • [x] unknown slash command is not sent to model;
  • [x] //literal sends a literal slash-prefixed prompt;
  • [x] /session opens structural tree and Esc returns to Conversation;
  • [x] wide terminal does not auto-open Explorer/Inspector;
  • [x] narrow terminal preserves understandable depth rails;
  • [x] connection refresh/reload reconstructs durable tree/plan without provider-stream replay.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
Do not:

  • create a second session/transcript store;
  • create TUI-only plan/dependency state;
  • create fake session/branch/plan IDs;
  • let row indices become continuation identity;
  • append every event at the bottom regardless of structure;
  • treat human branching as the only source of branches;
  • flatten autonomous child transcripts into parent context;
  • use terminal width to switch product modes;
  • require i for ordinary typing;
  • send recognized slash commands to the model;
  • implement provider/model selection locally in the TUI;
  • display secrets;
  • expose hidden chain-of-thought;
  • present every semantic operation as a shell command;
  • implement source editing through raw file writes when shared semantic capabilities exist;
  • silently merge concurrent worker candidates because dependencies completed;
  • allow more than one auto-advancing coordinator for one plan.

docs.title: Final Acceptance Criterion
docs.text:
The task is complete when all of the following are true:

Launching the native TUI opens a persistent agent composer and a tree-aware conversation projection. The user can type immediately, navigate stable replyable nodes, pin an earlier reply anchor, and submit a continuation whose new activity appears at that exact structural location. Autonomous recursive agent branches and /plan nodes appear in the same tree, completed branches collapse to compact results, dependency/assignment state is visible, multiple worker models can be observed concurrently, one coordinator can auto-advance while the user independently navigates, and nesting is rendered with colored vertical rails plus a distinct reply-anchor highlight. Known project edits are presented as semantic operations, with raw shell/file activity reserved for actual fallback/runtime use. Auxiliary views and controls are entered explicitly through slash commands and return to the conversation when closed.

docs.title: Final Full-Suite Gate
docs.text:
Only after every implementation and targeted-test checkbox above is complete, run the repository-wide final gate required by root AGENTS.md, including at least:

python3 tools/lint_repo.py --fix
cargo fmt --all
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
pnpm --dir web format
pnpm --dir web typecheck
pnpm --dir web test
pnpm --dir web build

Then:

  • [x] Re-read this document against final behavior.
  • [x] Re-read tasks 133 and 135 for cross-task regressions.
  • [x] Confirm no checked item is aspirational/unverified.
  • [x] Change the status to Complete only after the final gate passes.

docs.title: Implement Recursive Semantic Agent Plans, Dependencies, Multi-Model Execution, and the Tree TUI
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
Implement the synchronized agent architecture defined by:

  • design/level-1/017. recursive agent decomposition and context isolation.md;
  • design/level-1/018. durable plans dependency scheduling and multi-model execution.md;
  • design/level-1/019. semantic agent operations and projection-first editing.md;
  • design/level-3/134. make agent conversation the default tui and move auxiliary views behind slash commands.md.

The final product must support all of these properties together:

  1. sessions are recursive branch trees, not linear transcripts;
  2. branches are context-isolation boundaries created by users, agents, plans, or runtime policy;
  3. the user can reply from an exact historical replyable node;
  4. /plan creates durable planned work visible in the same tree;
  5. plan dependencies form an explicit DAG over plan nodes and are satisfied by durable results;
  6. one auto-advancing coordinator advances a plan while many worker models may execute different branches concurrently;
  7. each branch/plan node may have its own model/provider/profile/thinking/configuration;
  8. one branch has at most one active executing owner; parallel attempts use sibling branches;
  9. worker contexts receive selected ancestor/dependency results, not sibling/child transcripts;
  10. understood source/document work is performed through semantic/domain operations rather than generic raw file writes;
  11. shell/process execution is a bounded runtime/validation capability rather than the ordinary mutation interface;
  12. the default TUI is a tree-aware conversation projection with structural insertion, colored depth rails, a highlighted reply anchor, plan/dependency/assignment state, per-activity detail modes, and slash-command auxiliary views;
  13. reconnect/restart reconstructs durable state without provider-stream replay;
  14. all product surfaces consume the same shared application/protocol semantics.

This task is deliberately written for a simple implementation agent. Follow it in order. Do not skip a phase because a later phase looks easier.

docs.title: 2.1 Read before editing
docs.text:
Before changing code:

  • [x] Read root AGENTS.md completely.
  • [x] Read the nearest AGENTS.md for every crate/directory you modify.
  • [x] Read Level-1 documents 002, 005, 006, 007, 009, 010, 014, 015, 016, 017, 018, and 019.
  • [x] Read Level-2 documents 010, 011, 021, 022, 023, and 024.
  • [x] Read Level-3 tasks 082, 103, 133, and 134.
  • [x] Inspect current implementations in scriberig-session, scriberig-app, scriberig-protocol, scriberig-agent-core, scriberig-agent-runtime, scriberig-server, scriberig-client, and scriberig-tui before choosing names.
  • [x] Search for existing types/operations before adding any new abstraction.

docs.title: 2.2 Checklist discipline
docs.text:
For this file:

  • [x] Keep the file open while implementing.
  • [x] Tick a checkbox immediately after the exact item is implemented and its targeted verification passes.
  • [x] Never bulk-tick checkboxes at the end.
  • [x] If a later change invalidates a checked item, immediately change it back to [ ].
  • [x] Add a short note under a task if repository reality forces a materially different implementation than prescribed here.
  • [x] Never mark an item complete because adjacent work exists; verify the specific acceptance condition.

docs.title: 2.3 Test discipline
docs.text:
Until every implementation checkbox is complete, run only focused tests/checks for the crate/behavior just changed.

Do not run these workspace-wide commands during intermediate implementation:

cargo test --workspace
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
python3 tools/lint_repo.py
pnpm --dir web test
pnpm --dir web typecheck
pnpm --dir web build

Use focused commands such as:

cargo test -p scriberig-session plan
cargo test -p scriberig-app continuation
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol plan
cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime dependency
cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime context
cargo test -p scriberig-tui reply_anchor
cargo test -p scriberig-tui slash_command

The full repository gate appears only at the end.

docs.title: 2.4 Architectural prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not:

  • create a second transcript/session store;
  • store plan state only in the TUI;
  • compile model context in the TUI/server/client;
  • allocate canonical session/branch/plan identities inside the TUI;
  • make row indexes continuation identities;
  • represent plan dependencies only through display order;
  • allow two automatic coordinators to mutate one plan simultaneously;
  • allow two models to execute the same branch concurrently;
  • silently merge worker candidate states because dependencies completed;
  • copy child/sibling transcripts into dependent worker contexts by default;
  • add a planner-specific model registry separate from task-133 model profiles;
  • put provider credentials in session/plan/protocol records;
  • make write_file/bash the normal agent editing path for understood domains;
  • bypass migration/validation/promotion when an agent edits semantic knowledge;
  • expose hidden chain-of-thought;
  • make UI verbosity alter context construction or durable state.

docs.title: 3. Current Implementation Baseline to Audit
docs.text: The repository currently contains at least the following relevant structures. Verify every item before implementation and update this section if main has moved.

docs.title: 3.1 Session crate
docs.text:
Current scriberig-session has:

src/branch.rs
src/execution.rs
src/turn.rs
src/types.rs
src/views.rs

Branch currently carries:

id
parent
children
title
purpose
outcome
status
description
touched
turns
result
activity
model_invocations
model_outputs
tool_invocations
tool_results

Session currently carries branches/goals/tasks plus one session execution selection.

BranchResult already carries summary/result kind/references/result handles/touched/produced changes/validations/unresolved questions.

SessionActivityKind already includes human/assistant/reasoning/runtime/model/tool/branch/progress/validation/model-selection/thinking-selection/error categories.

  • [x] Confirm these current types still exist or record replacements.

docs.title: 3.2 Application/protocol
docs.text:
Current agent command/start paths require an existing session identity in at least some application/protocol APIs.

  • [x] Confirm whether shared new-session start semantics now exist.
  • [x] Confirm whether continuation can target an exact historical replyable node or only session+branch.
  • [x] Confirm whether plan CRUD/lifecycle operations exist.
  • [x] Confirm whether branch-scoped execution assignment exists.

docs.title: 3.3 Agent runtime
docs.text:
Current runtime already has provider-neutral context, model-provider, cache, event, tool, and execution code.

  • [x] Locate the actual model/tool loop owner.
  • [x] Locate the actual child-branch creation/completion path.
  • [x] Locate context compiler inputs and dependency manifest generation.
  • [x] Locate tool catalog/dispatch implementation.
  • [x] Locate cancellation/budget handling.
  • [x] Locate execution-selection resolution added by task 133.

Do not create a parallel runtime if names differ from earlier design documents.

docs.title: 3.4 TUI
docs.text:
Current TUI currently has a semantic multi-pane shell, PrimaryView, structural SessionModel, persistent session composer, task-133 model/thinking/presentation controls, and responsive automatic Explorer/Inspector panes.

SessionComposerState currently requires a session identity and therefore cannot represent a true pre-session draft.

  • [x] Verify these facts and current file ownership before editing.

docs.title: 4. Phase 0 — Freeze the Shared Semantic Vocabulary
docs.text: Do this before implementing behavior. The purpose is to avoid three crates inventing incompatible terms.

docs.title: Task 0.1 — Write down the exact identities
docs.text:
In the owning Rust crates, identify or add explicit types/aliases for these concepts:

SessionId / EntityId-backed session identity
BranchId / EntityId-backed branch identity
PlanId
PlanNodeId
ContinuationAnchor
BranchResultId
ExecutionLease/Claim identity if separate
Activity sequence/cursor

Requirements:

  • stable semantic identities must not be UI row numbers;
  • if EntityId is reused, use named wrappers only when they materially prevent misuse and fit repository conventions;
  • do not introduce duplicate globally unique ID systems;

  • plan/dependency identities must serialize deterministically.

  • [x] Exact continuation-anchor identity is specified in code/docs.

  • [x] Plan and plan-node identity is specified.
  • [x] No UI coordinate participates in canonical identity.

docs.title: Targeted verification
docs.text: Add tiny type/serialization tests in the owning crate only.

docs.title: Task 0.2 — Define the four different relations
docs.text:
Ensure code/documentation keeps these separate:

branch parent/child
plan node dependency
semantic knowledge relation/containment
execution activity parent/causality

Do not reuse one parent field for all four.

  • [x] Branch parent remains branch topology only.
  • [x] Dependency edges have their own representation.
  • [x] Activity parent/sequence remains separate.
  • [x] Semantic object relationships stay in domain/graph systems.

docs.title: 5. Phase 1 — Extend the Session Domain for Exact Continuations
Task 1.1 — Define ContinuationAnchor
docs.text:
Add a provider-neutral session-domain representation that can identify a valid reply/continuation location.

Initial supported anchors should be conservative and explicit. Prefer variants equivalent to:

BranchHead { branch }
Turn { branch, turn }
HumanInput { branch, turn/message }
AssistantOutput { branch, output }
BranchResult { branch, result }

Do not support arbitrary tool-result anchors unless the context compiler can define exact semantics for them.

Requirements:

  • anchor points to stable durable identity;
  • anchor can be validated against a session snapshot;
  • anchor resolution can identify the branch/path and the cut-off position inside that branch;
  • invalid/missing/non-replyable targets fail structurally.

Likely files:

crates/scriberig-session/src/types.rs
crates/scriberig-session/src/turn.rs
crates/scriberig-session/src/views.rs
crates/scriberig-session/src/error.rs

Split modules if file-size rules require it.

  • [x] Anchor type added.
  • [x] Validation rejects missing session objects.
  • [x] Validation rejects non-replyable activity kinds.
  • [x] Anchor resolution is deterministic.

docs.title: Targeted tests
docs.text:
Prove:

  • branch head resolves;
  • earlier assistant output resolves;
  • later sibling activity is not part of an earlier anchor path;
  • invalid entity fails without fallback to current head.

docs.title: Task 1.2 — Add continuation branch creation from an anchor
docs.text:
The session layer must support creating a child/continuation branch whose origin references the exact anchor.

Do not overwrite the original branch history.

Store origin/provenance equivalent to:

created_from_anchor
origin = HumanContinuation | AgentDelegation | PlanExecution | Retry | Validation | Alternative | RuntimePolicy

Origin may be an enum or structured provenance field; reuse existing provenance infrastructure where possible.

  • [x] Continuation creates a new branch or valid continuation according to shared policy.
  • [x] Original later sibling/turn history remains intact.
  • [x] Origin is inspectable but does not create separate branch semantics.

docs.title: 6. Phase 2 — Add Durable Plan Domain Types
docs.text: Keep scheduling state out of TUI-local state.

docs.title: Task 2.1 — Add Plan
docs.text:
Add a durable session/domain value equivalent to:

Plan
  id
  session
  anchor
  goal
  revision
  status
  coordinator assignment/claim
  root node IDs

Initial status should distinguish at least:

Draft
Ready/Planned
Running
Paused
Completed
Failed
Cancelled

Use names consistent with existing lifecycle conventions.

  • [x] Plan has stable identity.
  • [x] Plan stores the exact session/anchor it belongs to.
  • [x] Plan revision is independent from activity cursor.
  • [x] Terminal status transition validation exists.

docs.title: Task 2.2 — Add PlanNode
docs.text:
Represent planned work separately from branch execution detail.

Required fields/concepts:

id
plan
parent node
branch binding (optional before execution if necessary)
purpose
expected result kind/contract
semantic scope/selection handles
dependency IDs
assignment override
scheduling state
created/updated revision/provenance as repository conventions permit

Initial scheduling states must distinguish at least:

Planned/Blocked
Ready
Claimed/Running
Completed
Failed
Cancelled
Skipped (only if policy truly supports it)

Do not overload BranchStatus with all scheduler states.

  • [x] Plan node can exist before execution.
  • [x] Plan node can bind to an executing branch.
  • [x] Parent node relation is distinct from dependency relation.
  • [x] Expected result contract is inspectable.

docs.title: Task 2.3 — Add dependency edges and cycle validation
docs.text:
Represent dependencies explicitly.

A simple representation can be depends_on: Vec<PlanNodeId> on each node if that matches repository style, provided reverse traversal is available/derivable.

Implement validation:

  • referenced node exists in same plan;
  • no self-dependency;
  • no cycle;
  • terminal completed nodes are not accidentally redefined by later mutation;

  • deterministic ordering for serialized/replayed plan state.

  • [x] Cycle detection implemented.

  • [x] Missing dependency rejected.
  • [x] Self-dependency rejected.
  • [x] Dependency ordering deterministic.

docs.title: Targeted tests
docs.text:
Include:

A -> B valid
A -> B -> C valid
A -> B -> A rejected
A -> A rejected
missing node rejected

docs.title: Task 2.4 — Add readiness calculation
docs.text:
Implement one pure/read-only function that determines scheduler eligibility from plan state and dependency results.

Initial rule:

Ready(node) =
  node is non-terminal and unclaimed
  AND every required dependency completed successfully
  AND every required dependency published the expected result class/handle

Do not infer success from branch process termination alone.

  • [x] Readiness is deterministic.
  • [x] Failed dependency blocks dependent node.
  • [x] Completed dependency without required result contract does not silently satisfy node.
  • [x] Readiness function has no provider/UI side effects.

docs.title: 7. Phase 3 — Extend Branch Results for Dependency Contracts
Task 3.1 — Audit BranchResult
docs.text:
Current BranchResult already has summary/result kind/references/result handles/touched/produced changes/validations/unresolved questions.

Prefer extending/reusing it rather than creating a second planner result type.

Determine whether it needs:

result contract/type identity
exact snapshot/candidate/workspace context
explicit plan-node fulfillment relation
failure category/summary
semantic revision handles not representable as EntityId

Add only what is actually missing.

  • [x] Plan dependency can point to/validate a BranchResult.
  • [x] Result retains exact semantic/candidate context required by dependents.
  • [x] Result remains provider-neutral.
  • [x] Full child transcript is not required to consume result.

docs.title: Task 3.2 — Dependency fulfillment records
docs.text:
When a branch completes for a plan node, update durable plan state atomically enough that reconnecting clients never observe a completed dependency with an ambiguous fulfillment state.

Preferred logical order:

  1. durable branch result committed;
  2. plan node records result/terminal status;
  3. dependent readiness becomes derivable;

  4. durable activity/event announces transition.

  5. [x] Result exists before dependent becomes Ready.

  6. [x] Reconnect can derive same readiness without transient events.

docs.title: 8. Phase 4 — Shared New-Session and Exact-Continuation Application Operations
Task 4.1 — Add shared new-session agent start
docs.text:
Current APIs may require an existing session ID. Add the smallest shared application/session operation that represents:

start new session with user input

It must return authoritative handles equivalent to:

OperationId
SessionId
RootBranchId

Do not allocate these in the TUI.

Likely ownership:

scriberig-app session/application boundary
owning session backend/store
protocol mapping
server/client adapters
embedded TUI adapter
  • [x] New-session start exists below product surfaces.
  • [x] TUI/server/client all can use same semantics.
  • [x] First human input is durably represented in created session/root branch.
  • [x] Error cleanup does not leave fake local session IDs.

docs.title: Task 4.2 — Add exact continuation operation
docs.text:
Add a shared request equivalent to:

AgentContinueAtRequest {
  session,
  anchor: ContinuationAnchor,
  prompt,
  optional semantic selection,
  optional invocation override
}

Do not make the caller provide compiled model messages.

The application/session runtime validates the anchor and creates/chooses the proper branch.

  • [x] Continuation request is provider-neutral.
  • [x] Anchor validation happens in shared semantic layer.
  • [x] Later sibling turns are not automatically included.
  • [x] Accepted response returns authoritative branch/operation handles.

docs.title: Task 4.3 — Preserve compatibility where practical
docs.text:
Existing session+branch continuation APIs may remain as convenience adapters that resolve to BranchHead anchors.

Do not maintain two divergent execution paths.

  • [x] Old branch-head path delegates to the new exact-anchor semantics.

docs.title: 9. Phase 5 — Shared Plan Application Operations
docs.text:
Add transport-independent application operations for plan lifecycle.

Do not put scheduling mutations directly in runtime/TUI code.

docs.title: Task 5.1 — Plan creation/proposal
docs.text:
Request should identify:

session
anchor
goal
optional coordinator/model profile request
optional semantic selection

Result returns stable plan identity/revision and structured nodes.

If a model is used to propose structure, the model output must be parsed/validated into trusted plan-domain operations before persistence.

  • [x] Plan creation is application-owned.
  • [x] Invalid/cyclic model-proposed plan is rejected before durable activation.
  • [x] Plan can exist in Draft/Planned state without executing.

docs.title: Task 5.2 — Plan lifecycle mutations
docs.text:
Add operations equivalent to:

start
pause
resume
stop/cancel
replan

Use optimistic revision checks for user-visible mutable plan configuration where appropriate.

  • [x] Start cannot create second coordinator claim.
  • [x] Pause stops new auto-dispatch according to policy.
  • [x] Resume is idempotent or structurally rejects invalid state.
  • [x] Stop/cancel uses shared operation cancellation semantics.

docs.title: Task 5.3 — Plan revision/replan
docs.text:
Represent replan as a new durable revision/transition.

Do not rewrite historical completed nodes.

Validate:

  • dependencies remain acyclic;
  • completed node identities/results are preserved;
  • new/superseded nodes are explicit;

  • assignment/dependency mutations use observed revision.

  • [x] Replan history is inspectable.

  • [x] Current projection shows latest plan state.
  • [x] Historical result references remain valid.

docs.title: 10. Phase 6 — Per-Node/Per-Branch Execution Assignment
docs.text: Reuse task-133 model library and execution selection.

docs.title: Task 6.1 — Define branch/plan-node assignment override
docs.text:
Do not mutate session-wide SessionExecutionSelection to assign one child.

Add an explicit override structure equivalent to:

ExecutionAssignment
  model_profile
  optional thinking level
  optional agent profile
  optional context policy
  optional branch policy/budget profile

Provider secrets remain indirect CredentialRef through existing profile configuration.

  • [x] Assignment stores no API key/secret.
  • [x] Assignment can be absent and inherit defaults.
  • [x] Assignment is inspectable/durable.

docs.title: Task 6.2 — Implement resolution order
docs.text:
Use one shared resolver equivalent to:

invocation override
> plan-node assignment
> branch override
> session selection
> project/user default
> runtime fallback

Do not duplicate this resolver in runtime/TUI/server.

  • [x] Resolver covered by table-driven tests.
  • [x] Running invocation snapshot does not change when future assignment changes.
  • [x] Unsupported thinking level fails before provider invocation.

docs.title: Task 6.3 — Assignment mutation operation
docs.text:
Add a shared operation used by /assign and other clients.

Mutation must check:

  • node/branch exists;
  • node is assignable in current scheduling state;
  • profile exists/enabled;
  • advertised thinking level is supported;

  • optimistic revision when concurrent mutation matters.

  • [x] /assign does not need provider credentials.

  • [x] Assignment changes are replayable/inspectable provenance.

docs.title: 11. Phase 7 — Coordinator Claim and Worker Execution Leases
Task 7.1 — Coordinator claim
docs.text:
Represent the single auto-advancing coordinator with a shared claim/lease or equivalent authoritative ownership record.

Required properties:

plan
executor/operation identity
observed plan revision
time/heartbeat only if needed for remote recovery

Rules:

  • only one active coordinator per plan;
  • stale/expired coordinator recovery must be explicit;

  • UI focus never implies coordinator ownership.

  • [x] Concurrent coordinator claim test proves one winner.

  • [x] Pause/cancel releases or changes claim according to policy.

docs.title: Task 7.2 — Worker branch claim
docs.text:
Add/extend execution ownership so one branch cannot be actively executed by two workers.

A ready plan node is claimed atomically before provider invocation.

  • [x] Two concurrent claims for same node/branch cannot both succeed.
  • [x] Different ready sibling nodes can be claimed concurrently.
  • [x] Worker failure releases/transitions claim deterministically.

Repository adaptation: the existing session repository exposes plan-level compare-and-swap so concurrent branch updates are preserved. Plan CAS now also merges newly claimed worker branch records and links them to their parents in the same transaction, allowing the tree and context to resolve the branch before provider execution without overwriting existing branch state.

docs.title: Task 7.3 — Alternative attempts
docs.text:
Do not implement “two models on one branch.”

Provide a shared pattern/helper for sibling attempts when the coordinator/user wants multiple models to solve the same goal.

  • [x] Comparison branch can depend on both attempt results.

docs.title: 12. Phase 8 — Context Compiler: Exact Anchor and Dependency-Aware Isolation
docs.text: This phase is critical. Do not implement the scheduler before tests prove context isolation.

docs.title: Task 8.1 — Compile context from exact continuation anchor
docs.text:
Extend existing context compiler input so it receives an exact branch/anchor context rather than assuming complete branch head history.

Context should include only the path/state valid at the anchor.

Prove exclusion of:

later turns on same old branch after anchor
sibling branches created later
unrelated plan nodes
unrelated model activity
  • [x] Exact-anchor context test passes.

docs.title: Task 8.2 — Parent-to-child inheritance plan
docs.text:
For delegated child branches, compile only selected parent state:

purpose
expected result
parent descriptor
selected ancestor results
accepted decisions
semantic scope
exact base snapshot/workspace
capabilities
bounded parent excerpt only if policy asks for it
  • [x] Full parent transcript is not inherited by default.

docs.title: Task 8.3 — Dependency results as explicit context inputs
docs.text:
When a plan node starts, add fulfilled dependency results to context input explicitly.

Do not fetch dependency branch transcripts.

Include exact result handles/revisions/candidates/validation evidence needed by the worker.

  • [x] Worker sees required dependency result.
  • [x] Worker does not see dependency's raw model/tool history.

docs.title: Task 8.4 — Semantic scope first
docs.text:
Context compiler should prefer semantic descriptions/handles/structure over whole rendered files when possible.

For example, a selected function may initially contribute:

identity
purpose/description
parameters
code-group summary
relations/calls
relevant diagnostics
exact revision

Exact source is included only when context policy/operation requires it.

  • [x] Test demonstrates a semantic compact context path that does not automatically inject whole file text.

docs.title: Task 8.5 — Fingerprint/dependency manifest
docs.text:
Ensure request identity includes all output-relevant new inputs:

continuation anchor / branch revision
selected dependency result revisions
plan/context policy revision if behaviorally relevant
resolved model assignment
semantic dependency revisions
tool schemas

Do not include UI state, reply highlight, rail color, scroll position, or secrets.

  • [x] Same exact semantic context yields same fingerprint.
  • [x] Changed dependency result revision changes fingerprint.
  • [x] UI-only changes do not change fingerprint.

docs.title: 13. Phase 9 — Semantic-First Tool Catalog and Dispatch
Task 9.1 — Classify tool/capability kinds
docs.text:
Audit existing tool descriptors and add metadata if needed for:

semantic read
semantic mutation
projection operation
validation/external process
opaque/raw fallback
branch-producing operation

Do not infer category from tool name string in the TUI.

  • [x] Category is provider-neutral and trusted-runtime-owned.

docs.title: Task 9.2 — Prefer semantic capabilities
docs.text:
When selected knowledge has a domain adapter/capability set, advertise semantic operations before generic raw file/shell tools.

Examples:

code.add_function
code.replace_expression
document.insert_paragraph

Do not require all domain operations to exist in this task; wire the catalog so installed capabilities are discoverable and preferred.

  • [x] Known semantic target receives semantic operation descriptors.
  • [x] Opaque target can expose fallback capabilities explicitly.

docs.title: Task 9.3 — Raw write fallback policy
docs.text:
If generic raw file replacement currently exists, gate it behind explicit capability/policy and projection reconciliation where canonical state is involved.

Do not remove necessary bootstrap/interoperability functionality.

  • [x] Known adapted file cannot silently bypass semantic migration through a default raw write path.

Repository difference: the agent runtime has no generic raw file write or unrestricted shell tool to gate. The project source proposal operation edits file projections through candidate machinery, so the native catalog now labels it as an explicitly granted fallback. The existing inspection contract exposes the selected entity's installed operation descriptors; a trusted generic semantic-operation tool dispatches the chosen descriptor through the shared registry and sorts ahead of opaque fallbacks.

docs.title: Task 9.4 — External process/validation capabilities
docs.text:
Keep compiler/test/package-manager execution behind explicit application/runtime capabilities where practical.

A validation capability should return structured diagnostics/results that can reference semantic handles.

  • [x] Validation output is structured, not only terminal text.
  • [x] Process execution can still be rendered as actual process activity in clients.

Repository difference: application validation already produces ValidationEvidence with status, diagnostics, exact candidate/dependency references, and provenance. The existing trusted ToolActivityKind is carried through the shared activity protocol and remote session restoration; the TUI labels ValidationProcess activity as validation without parsing tool names.

docs.title: 14. Phase 10 — Coordinator Scheduler
docs.text: Only start this phase after plan/readiness/context/claim tests pass.

docs.title: Task 10.1 — Implement scheduler tick as deterministic logic
docs.text:
Separate scheduler decision logic from provider invocation.

Given durable plan state, compute:

terminal?
paused?
ready nodes
claimed/running nodes
blocked nodes
failure/replan condition

Return decisions rather than immediately doing network I/O inside pure state calculation.

  • [x] Pure readiness/scheduler tests use no provider.

docs.title: Task 10.2 — Dispatch unassigned ready work
docs.text:
Coordinator selects ready nodes according to deterministic policy.

Initial policy may be simple:

stable plan order / explicit priority
up to concurrency budget
only nodes whose assignments resolve successfully

Do not invent sophisticated optimization before correctness.

  • [x] Scheduler respects concurrency budget.
  • [x] Scheduler does not dispatch blocked node.
  • [x] Scheduler does not double-dispatch claimed node.

docs.title: Task 10.3 — Run many workers concurrently
docs.text:
Use runtime concurrency primitives consistent with existing async architecture.

Workers execute separate branches/workspaces.

Do not share mutable provider request state between workers.

  • [x] Two independent sibling nodes can run with two fake provider profiles concurrently.
  • [x] Their model/profile provenance remains distinct.

docs.title: Task 10.4 — Consume worker result
docs.text:
On worker completion:

  1. persist branch result;
  2. mark plan node terminal/result-linked;
  3. release worker claim;
  4. derive newly ready nodes;
  5. notify coordinator/activity stream;

  6. continue scheduling if plan is running.

  7. [x] Dependent starts only after durable result linkage.

docs.title: Task 10.5 — Failure handling
docs.text:
Initial policy must support at least:

mark failed
keep dependents blocked
surface failure to coordinator
allow coordinator/user replan or explicit retry

Do not silently treat failed dependency as complete.

  • [x] Failure test proves blocked dependent remains blocked.

docs.title: Task 10.6 — Plan completion
docs.text:
Plan is complete only when completion policy is satisfied and no required unresolved node remains.

  • [x] Completed plan persists final state and releases coordinator claim.

docs.title: Task 10.7 — Wire the production worker runtime
docs.text:
The product composition must connect the durable lifecycle operation to the shared coordinator and a provider-backed worker executor. Generic scheduler tests and test-only executors do not prove that /plan start executes work.

Repository adaptation: the native composition uses the shared model library to resolve worker model IDs, connection IDs, and thinking levels, and invokes the shared coordinator through the TUI plan lifecycle. Named OpenAI-compatible connections are declared with endpoint and credential environment-variable references in SCRIBE_AGENT_MODEL_CATALOG; the default process configuration continues to provide the local connection. The HTTP composition injects the same native runner through the server protocol dispatcher.

  • [x] Native plan start/resume launches one coordinator with the production worker executor.
  • [x] Each worker runs against its claimed branch using its compiled exact PlanWorkerContext and resolved model ID/thinking assignment.
  • [x] Native execution selects the provider adapter from the resolved provider profile without persisting credentials.
  • [x] HTTP plan start/resume launches the same shared coordinator and worker execution semantics as embedded TUI start/resume.
  • [x] Coordinator execution remains off the interactive input/render loop and publishes durable plan/result activity as work completes.

docs.title: Task 11.1 — Produce a proposed revised plan
docs.text:
Coordinator/model may suggest plan changes, but trusted application validation owns acceptance.

The proposal must identify:

base plan revision
preserved terminal nodes
new nodes
superseded nodes
new/removed dependencies
assignment changes
reason/trigger
  • [x] Stale base revision fails structurally.

docs.title: Task 11.2 — Validate and persist revision
docs.text:
Run dependency cycle validation and terminal-node preservation checks before committing revision.

  • [x] Historical revision remains inspectable.
  • [x] Completed branch results keep stable references.

docs.title: 16. Phase 12 — Protocol, Server, and Client Parity
docs.text: Do not implement only embedded/local semantics.

docs.title: Task 12.1 — Protocol DTOs
docs.text:
Extend scriberig-protocol with safe serializable DTOs for:

ContinuationAnchor
new-session start
continue-at-anchor
Plan / PlanNode summaries
plan lifecycle requests/responses
plan dependency status
branch/node assignment
coordinator/worker status
conversation/activity references needed by clients

Do not expose provider credentials or raw hidden prompts by default.

  • [x] JSON schema/serde tests pass.

docs.title: Task 12.2 — Server routes/handlers
docs.text:
Map protocol operations to shared application operations.

Do not reproduce validation/scheduling rules in HTTP handlers.

  • [x] Server handler tests prove delegation to app layer.

docs.title: Task 12.3 — Client APIs
docs.text:
Expose the same operations in the Rust/public client layer.

Use existing observation/SSE/event conventions for live plan/worker activity.

  • [x] Remote client can create/start/read plan and set assignment.
  • [x] Remote client can continue at exact anchor.

docs.title: Task 12.4 — Durable replay + live tail
docs.text:
Reconnect behavior:

read durable session/plan state
then subscribe/continue from event cursor

Do not require replaying raw provider token stream.

  • [x] Reconnect test reconstructs completed/running plan status.

docs.title: 17. Phase 13 — Extend Shared Activity/Event Vocabulary
docs.text:
Audit SessionActivityKind and application/runtime events.

Add only missing typed categories needed to avoid free-form strings for important state, for example:

PlanCreated
PlanRevised
PlanNodeReady
PlanNodeStarted
PlanNodeCompleted
PlanNodeFailed
AssignmentChanged
CoordinatorChanged
DependencyStateChanged
SemanticOperation

Do not create a separate TUI-only event taxonomy.

  • [x] Durable categories needed for reconstruction are typed.
  • [x] Transient progress remains separate from durable settled state.
  • [x] Events contain safe summaries and stable references.

docs.title: 18. Phase 14 — Build the Conversation Tree Projection
docs.text: This is a TUI projection over shared state, not canonical storage.

docs.title: Task 14.1 — Add dedicated conversation projection module
docs.text:
Create focused module(s) under crates/scriberig-tui/src/view/ or current equivalent.

Projection input includes:

session graph
plan graph/state
activity records
current expansion state
presentation preferences
stable reply/coordinator anchors

Output rows retain stable source references.

  • [x] No canonical state is stored only as a conversation row.

docs.title: Task 14.2 — Structural traversal order
docs.text:
Render depth-first/structurally so new branch activity appears under its parent.

Use stable ordinals/sequence data for sibling/activity order.

Never sort by label.

  • [x] Historical continuation inserted mid-tree in deterministic location.
  • [x] Later wall-clock event can render above older unrelated bottom content when structure requires it.

Repository note: branch, plan, and node Vec insertion order is the existing durable sibling sequence; the projection now preserves it instead of sorting by identity or label.

docs.title: Task 14.3 — Collapse completed children
docs.text:
Default completed branch:

branch descriptor
BranchResult summary

Expanded branch:

retained child activity
nested descendants
result
  • [x] Expansion does not alter shared context or scheduling.

docs.title: Task 14.4 — Project planned nodes
docs.text:
Show planned nodes before execution, preserving identity when bound branch starts.

Display at least:

state symbol/text
title/purpose
assignment when useful
compact waits/dependency summary
result summary when terminal
  • [x] Blocked/ready/running/completed are visually distinguishable without color alone.

docs.title: 19. Phase 15 — TUI State: Conversation Home and Stable Anchors
Task 15.1 — Make Conversation the default surface
docs.text:
Refactor PrimaryView/top-level state so ordinary launch is Conversation.

Preserve existing structural Session/Explorer/Inspector/etc. views as auxiliary destinations.

  • [x] TuiState::default() produces Conversation home.
  • [x] No width-dependent automatic Explorer/Inspector mode.

docs.title: Task 15.2 — Refactor composer target
docs.text:
Current SessionComposerState requires a session ID.

Replace/refactor with concept equivalent to:

ConversationTarget::NewSession
ConversationTarget::Existing { session, reply_anchor }

Preserve draft/pending/error behavior.

  • [x] No dummy EntityId for pre-session draft.

docs.title: Task 15.3 — Add navigation cursor
docs.text:
Navigation cursor references a projected node via stable projection key/source ref.

Moving cursor must not automatically mutate reply anchor.

  • [x] Cursor survives safe rerender mapping where source remains present.

docs.title: Task 15.4 — Add reply anchor
docs.text:
Store stable shared ContinuationAnchor plus session identity.

Default behavior:

no active plan -> current ordinary conversation head
active plan + follow enabled -> coordinator cursor/head according to shared policy
user pins node -> pinned anchor
  • [x] Reply anchor survives verbosity/collapse/resize.

Up/Down -> previous/next visible node
Left -> parent/collapse
Right -> child/expand
Enter -> set selected replyable node as reply anchor and return to composer
Esc -> return without changing anchor / close view according to mode stack

Exact bindings may reuse existing navigation conventions, but semantics must remain explicit.

- <title>: <purpose>
- <title>: <purpose>

+

docs.title: 28. Phase 24 — Semantic Candidate Concurrency and Integration
docs.text:
This phase may reuse existing migration/merge APIs rather than creating new algorithms.

Repository adaptation: sr-change owns immutable snapshot merge and the project subsystem owns isolated source candidates. scriberig-app now exposes an exact base/left/right merge operation that returns the existing structured merge result and never promotes a root. Project source candidate IDs are not immutable SnapshotIds, so the native integration node uses the existing ProjectService::merge_project_candidates owner. A node whose required result kind is project_candidate_merge resolves exactly two candidate handles from its compiled dependency results, creates a reviewable candidate, and leaves validation/application/promotion explicit. Failed candidate conflicts persist as abandoned branch results with a structured failure-code handle.

docs.title: Task 24.1 — Keep worker candidates isolated
docs.text:
Each mutating worker branch operates against exact base/workspace/candidate state.

docs.title: Task 24.2 — Integration node consumes candidates explicitly

Do not auto-merge simply because both dependencies completed.

docs.title: 34. Required Final Implementation Report
docs.text:
The implementing agent's final response must include:

  1. Architecture implemented — one concise paragraph describing session branches, plans/dependencies, coordinator/workers, semantic operations, and TUI projection.
  2. Files changed — grouped by crate/responsibility, not one unstructured filename dump.
  3. Public/shared contracts added or changed — application/protocol/client operations and important durable types.
  4. Context isolation evidence — exact tests proving child/dependency transcripts are not leaked.
  5. Concurrency evidence — tests proving one coordinator, one executor per branch, and concurrent sibling workers.
  6. Semantic-edit evidence — test proving a known-domain edit uses semantic operation/candidate machinery.
  7. TUI evidence — tests/screenshots/text snapshots proving structural insertion, rails, reply highlight, /plan, /assign, slash command routing, and no auto-panels.
  8. Recovery evidence — test proving durable restart/reconnect reconstruction.
  9. Targeted tests run during implementation — list relevant commands/results.
  10. Final full-suite gate — every command and pass/fail result.
  11. Deferred work — anything intentionally left out, with reason and follow-up design reference.
  12. Task status — confirm whether this file and task 134 are actually eligible to be marked Complete.

Do not claim completion if any acceptance item is unimplemented or only mocked at the wrong layer.

docs.title: Implement Provider Continuation, Full Effective Prompt, and Observable Reasoning
docs.text: Status: [ ] In Progress

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
Implement the provider-continuation and model-observability contract defined by:

  • design/level-1/020. provider continuation state and observable model execution.md;
  • design/level-2/025. provider continuation and observable model execution.md.

This task is a mandatory refinement of tasks 133, 134, and 135 where those tasks discuss prompt visibility, reasoning visibility, provider execution, model activity, or branch execution.

The final implementation must prove all of these properties together:

  1. Scriberig session/branch identities remain canonical and provider-neutral;
  2. provider-native conversation/session/response handles are opaque branch-local runtime state;
  3. sibling/child branches never share provider continuation accidentally;
  4. compatible same-branch invocations may reuse provider continuation;
  5. provider/profile/context divergence causes deterministic reseed/fork rather than blind continuation;
  6. provider continuation loss never makes the Scriberig session unrecoverable;
  7. every inspectable model invocation retains or references the complete safe effective Scriberig request used for that invocation;
  8. Full prompt display shows that effective request even when the provider wire request only sent a continuation ID plus new input;
  9. provider-visible reasoning may be represented before, between, and after semantic/tool operations in deterministic order;
  10. prompt visibility and reasoning visibility are independently selectable;
  11. changing either presentation setting performs no model/tool execution;
  12. hidden/private chain-of-thought is never requested, persisted as visible trace, or exposed;
  13. embedded, remote, TUI, and web surfaces consume the same application/protocol semantics.

Follow this task in order. Do not begin by adding TUI toggles. Runtime/session/application contracts come first.

  • [ ] Never bulk-tick at the end.
  • [ ] If later work invalidates an item, immediately restore [ ].
  • [ ] Do not mark this task Complete while any acceptance item is inferred rather than tested.

During implementation, use focused tests only. Do not run the repository-wide final gate until all implementation checkboxes are complete.
