  shared presentation preferences

crates/scriberig-app/src/agent_console/model.rs
  shared model/profile library

Known gaps to verify:

  • [ ] Current ModelRequestProjection is bounded/truncatable and therefore is not by itself a guaranteed complete Full effective prompt record.
  • [ ] Current public reasoning representation is primarily summary/status oriented and does not yet prove multiple provider-visible reasoning segments interleaved around tool calls.
  • [ ] Current provider contract does not expose one provider-neutral continuation-state abstraction bound to branch/context lineage.
  • [ ] OpenAI-compatible execution does not yet prove one isolated provider conversation/response chain per branch.
  • [ ] Current prompt and reasoning preferences may still use binary Hidden/Shown modes rather than Hidden/Summary/Full semantics.
  • [ ] No current client may set arbitrary provider continuation IDs directly.

Do not assume a gap remains if current code already solved it. Reuse the implementation and add only missing conformance/tests.

docs.title: 4. Phase A — Define Provider-Neutral Continuation Types
docs.text:
Owner: scriberig-agent-runtime unless the repository already has an equivalent provider-neutral runtime crate/type.

Implement the minimum provider-neutral types needed to express:

provider/profile identity
branch identity
continuation strategy
opaque provider handle
context/lineage fingerprint
status
created/last-used invocation references
safe non-secret provider metadata

Requirements:

  • [ ] Provider continuation type does not reuse SessionId, BranchId, or any semantic entity ID as the provider handle.
  • [ ] Provider handle is opaque outside provider/runtime implementation.
  • [ ] Strategy can distinguish OpenAI Conversation-style state from previous-response-style chaining and future provider-specific/local sessions.
  • [ ] Status can distinguish reusable/stale/unavailable/expired-or-equivalent states.
  • [ ] No credentials are fields in continuation records.
  • [ ] No hidden/private reasoning is stored in continuation records.
  • [ ] Type documentation follows repository declaration-documentation rules.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] serialize/deserialize safe continuation metadata if durability requires serialization;
  • [ ] prove secret sentinel values are absent from debug/public projection;
  • [ ] prove two branches can carry distinct opaque handles for the same provider profile.

Do not implement OpenAI HTTP behavior yet.

docs.title: 5. Phase B — Add Continuation Storage/Lookup Boundary
docs.text:
Implement an explicit runtime/session persistence boundary rather than passing continuation handles ad hoc through provider call sites.

Required operations are conceptually:

load(branch, provider/profile)
store/update(successor state)
mark_stale
mark_unavailable
list safe provenance when needed

Requirements:

  • [ ] Storage lookup is keyed by canonical Scriberig branch plus resolved provider/profile identity.
  • [ ] Old provider state can remain historical after provider switch without becoming current automatically.
  • [ ] TUI/web cannot directly mutate opaque provider continuation handles.
  • [ ] Restart can recover whatever continuation metadata is intentionally durable.
  • [ ] Absence/unavailability is a normal state, not corruption.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] continuation survives configured durable round trip if persistence is intended;
  • [ ] missing continuation produces normal None/unavailable semantics;
  • [ ] provider A state is not returned for provider B;
  • [ ] branch A state is not returned for branch B.

docs.title: 6. Phase C — Formalize Context Lineage Compatibility
docs.text:
Extend current context fingerprinting rather than adding a second unrelated hash system.

Implement a deterministic decision that can answer:

Can provider continuation P represent the exact expected provider-visible predecessor context for invocation I?

Inputs should include as needed:

compiled context fingerprint
prior invocation/request fingerprint
resolved provider/profile/model
continuation strategy
branch identity

Requirements:

  • [ ] Fingerprint inputs contain no credentials.
  • [ ] Fingerprint is deterministic across equivalent reconstruction.
  • [ ] Same branch + unchanged compatible lineage is reusable.
  • [ ] Sibling branch is never reusable merely because text happens to match.
  • [ ] Provider/profile switch is not reusable by default.
  • [ ] An intervening canonical branch turn not represented by old provider state makes old state stale unless context compiler explicitly excludes it and fingerprint equivalence proves compatibility.
  • [ ] Historical continuation/fork semantics use exact anchors/lineage rather than current-head assumptions.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] same lineage -> reusable;
  • [ ] changed dependency result -> stale;
  • [ ] changed selected ancestor result -> stale;
  • [ ] sibling branch -> not reusable;
  • [ ] provider switch -> not reusable;
  • [ ] reconstructing identical canonical context after restart yields same fingerprint/compatibility decision.

docs.title: 7. Phase D — Introduce Complete Safe Canonical Model Request
docs.text:
Do not remove the existing bounded request projection if it serves ordinary activity rendering.

Add or extend a complete safe provider-neutral request record used for durable/on-demand inspection.

It must be able to represent:

invocation identity
session/branch/continuation anchor
context fingerprint
instruction sections
ordered messages/context sections
selected ancestor results
fulfilled dependency results
semantic context/projections
tool/semantic capability definitions
structured-output request when present
resolved model/provider/profile/thinking configuration
provider continuation strategy/reference
safe generation configuration
optional token estimate
explicit redaction records

Requirements:

  • [ ] The record is created after context compilation and before provider serialization.
  • [ ] It represents effective Scriberig context, not raw provider HTTP JSON.
  • [ ] It contains no API key/header/secret values.
  • [ ] Sensitive capability parameters are redacted according to existing security policy.
  • [ ] Redactions remain structurally visible rather than silently deleting context.
  • [ ] The complete record can be retrieved later without model re-execution.
  • [ ] Bounded activity projection references the complete record or invocation identity.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] all compiled safe context sections appear in complete request;
  • [ ] long request remains complete in full-detail storage while bounded projection reports truncation;
  • [ ] secret sentinel values absent;
  • [ ] dependency/ancestor result references are included when context compiler selected them;
  • [ ] excluded sibling transcript does not appear.

docs.title: 8. Phase E — Make Provider Serialization Consume Canonical Request
docs.text:
Refactor request construction so provider adapters serialize from the canonical provider-neutral request or an exact derived runtime structure rather than independently rebuilding context.

Requirements:

  • [ ] There is one authoritative compiled request before provider-specific mapping.
  • [ ] OpenAI adapter does not have a hidden second context compiler.
  • [ ] Provider-specific omissions caused by continuation optimization happen after canonical request capture.
  • [ ] Request fingerprint/provenance refers to canonical effective request.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] stateless fake provider sees exact canonical request mapping;
  • [ ] provider serializer can omit repeated wire context without altering stored effective request;
  • [ ] equivalent canonical requests produce expected fingerprint behavior.

docs.title: 9. Phase F — Implement Continuation Reuse/Reseed Decision
docs.text:
Before invoking a provider:

  1. resolve branch model/provider/profile assignment;
  2. compile canonical effective request;
  3. compute context lineage identity;
  4. load candidate provider continuation;
  5. ask provider capability/strategy whether state can be reused/forked;
  6. reuse only when lineage compatibility passes;
  7. otherwise mark stale/reseed or run stateless;
  8. after successful provider execution, persist successor provider state bound to the completed invocation.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Decision is explicit/testable and not scattered through request fields.
  • [ ] Provider continuation failure can fall back to canonical context when policy permits.
  • [ ] Failed provider continuation does not mutate canonical Scriberig session identity.
  • [ ] Cancellation does not incorrectly promote a half-established successor state.

Focused fake-provider tests:

  • [ ] first invocation initializes state;
  • [ ] second compatible same-branch invocation reuses it;
  • [ ] incompatible branch context reseeds;
  • [ ] provider-state error falls back or fails structurally according to policy;
  • [ ] cancelled invocation does not become reusable successor.

docs.title: 10. Phase G — Implement OpenAI Conversation Strategy
docs.text:
Use the OpenAI Responses/Conversations capability only behind the provider adapter.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Provider capability declares Conversation support separately from generic OpenAI compatibility.
  • [ ] A new isolated Scriberig branch receives a new OpenAI Conversation when this strategy is selected.
  • [ ] Conversation initialization reflects the branch's compiled selected context.
  • [ ] Same-branch compatible continuation reuses the branch Conversation.
  • [ ] Child/sibling branch never reuses the parent/sibling Conversation implicitly.
  • [ ] Conversation ID is retained only as opaque provider runtime/provenance state.
  • [ ] OpenAI Conversation ID is never exposed as canonical Scriberig session identity.

Tests must use an HTTP fake/mock adapter boundary; do not require live OpenAI credentials.

  • [ ] assert create-conversation request for first branch invocation;
  • [ ] assert reuse on compatible continuation;
  • [ ] assert separate conversations for siblings;
  • [ ] assert reseed/new conversation after incompatible provider switch/context divergence.

docs.title: 11. Phase H — Implement OpenAI previous_response_id Strategy
docs.text:
Support previous-response chaining/forking only as a separate explicit strategy.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Strategy is mutually exclusive with Conversation strategy on one request.
  • [ ] Stable/top-level Scriberig instructions required for the new invocation are resent rather than assumed inherited.
  • [ ] Previous response is reused only when exact lineage compatibility passes.
  • [ ] Historical fork uses the response corresponding to the exact anchor when retained and valid; otherwise recompile/reseed from canonical Scriberig state.
  • [ ] Provider response IDs are opaque safe provenance, not branch IDs.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] request with previous response contains required instructions;
  • [ ] request never contains both provider continuation mechanisms;
  • [ ] exact fork chooses correct predecessor;
  • [ ] unavailable predecessor falls back to canonical context.

docs.title: 12. Phase I — Prove Provider Switching and Multi-Model Behavior
docs.text:
Build deterministic tests around one branch and sibling branches using different provider profiles.

Scenario A:

branch B -> OpenAI invocation -> local invocation -> OpenAI invocation

Expected:

  • [ ] first OpenAI state retained as history;
  • [ ] local invocation uses no OpenAI opaque state;
  • [ ] switching back does not blindly resume stale OpenAI state;
  • [ ] runtime recompiles canonical context and reseeds/forks only if proven valid.

Scenario B:

root
  parser -> OpenAI
  research -> another provider/local
  integration -> OpenAI

Expected:

  • [ ] each branch receives its own state;
  • [ ] integration receives compact dependency results through context compiler, not provider transcripts;
  • [ ] no opaque provider state crosses branches/providers.

docs.title: 13. Phase J — Add Ordered Observable Reasoning Segments
docs.text:
Extend provider-neutral runtime/session activity so one model invocation may contain multiple provider-visible reasoning segments interleaved with operations.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Reasoning segment has stable invocation/branch association.
  • [ ] Reasoning segment participates in deterministic invocation-local ordering.
  • [ ] Distinguish runtime status, provider reasoning summary, and provider-visible reasoning where useful.
  • [ ] Record whether the available content is summary-only or full provider-visible content.
  • [ ] Do not add any hidden-chain-of-thought activity kind.
  • [ ] Encrypted/private reasoning items needed internally for continuation are never converted into visible reasoning text.

Build a fake provider producing exactly:

reasoning A
semantic/tool invocation 1
result 1
reasoning B
semantic/tool invocation 2
result 2
reasoning C
assistant output

Focused tests:

  • [ ] shared activity projection preserves exact order;
  • [ ] causality/parent relationships remain correct;
  • [ ] branch depth remains independent from activity order.

docs.title: 14. Phase K — Refine Prompt Presentation Preference
docs.text:
Extend shared preference ownership in scriberig-app::agent_console::preferences or current equivalent.

Implement semantic modes equivalent to:

Hidden
Summary
Full

Requirements:

  • [ ] Hidden renders no prompt detail.
  • [ ] Summary uses bounded metadata/summary without forcing full payload through live events.
  • [ ] Full fetches/resolves complete safe canonical request.
  • [ ] Changing preference does not call provider/runtime execution.
  • [ ] Presets remain projections over independent preference fields.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] Hidden -> Full changes only presentation/detail fetch behavior;
  • [ ] Full request is identical before/after preference toggling;
  • [ ] no operation/model invocation count changes.

docs.title: 15. Phase L — Refine Reasoning Presentation Preference
docs.text:
Implement modes equivalent to:

Hidden
Summary
FullAvailable

Requirements:

  • [ ] Hidden removes reasoning rows only.
  • [ ] Summary renders provider/runtime summaries where available.
  • [ ] FullAvailable renders all provider-visible reasoning content available through the safe contract.
  • [ ] Provider exposing only summaries reports that limitation rather than inventing fuller content.
  • [ ] Provider exposing no reasoning produces no fabricated reasoning.
  • [ ] Changing preference does not call provider/runtime execution.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] hiding reasoning preserves order of visible tool/result rows;
  • [ ] showing reasoning reinserts segments at original positions;
  • [ ] invocation count unchanged across preference changes.

docs.title: 16. Phase M — Prove Prompt and Reasoning Independence
docs.text:
Create focused application/model tests for at least:

prompt Full + reasoning Hidden
prompt Hidden + reasoning FullAvailable
prompt Summary + reasoning Summary
prompt Hidden + reasoning Hidden

Requirements:

  • [ ] Every combination is representable.
  • [ ] No global trace level is required to express the combinations.
  • [ ] Changing one field leaves the other unchanged.
  • [ ] Tool invocation/result preferences remain separately configurable.

docs.title: 17. Phase N — Add Shared Full-Detail Application Operations
docs.text:
Extend scriberig-app::agent_console::detail or equivalent shared owner.

Implement read-only operations equivalent to:

request detail summary by invocation
full canonical request by invocation
reasoning segments/detail by invocation
safe provider continuation provenance by invocation/branch when appropriate

Requirements:

  • [ ] Stable identity input; never UI row index.
  • [ ] Structured NotRetained/Unavailable/Redacted outcomes where relevant.
  • [ ] Full retrieval never re-executes provider/model/tool.
  • [ ] Application layer performs authorization/capability checks according to existing architecture.
  • [ ] TUI/web do not read session storage directly.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] full request retrievable after invocation settles;
  • [ ] unavailable detail produces structured result;
  • [ ] secret sentinel never appears.

docs.title: 18. Phase O — Extend Protocol DTOs
docs.text:
Expose provider-neutral structured DTOs for:

prompt presentation preference
reasoning presentation preference
request summary/full detail
ordered observable reasoning segments
safe provider continuation provenance/status where needed

Requirements:

  • [ ] No OpenAI wire types in public generic DTOs.
  • [ ] Full request remains structured into instructions/messages/tools/config rather than one untyped blob.
  • [ ] Redaction markers survive serialization.
  • [ ] Backward compatibility/versioning follows repository protocol conventions.

Focused protocol tests:

  • [ ] JSON/schema round trip;
  • [ ] independent preference values survive round trip;
  • [ ] secret sentinel absent.

docs.title: 19. Phase P — Extend Server and Rust/TypeScript Clients
docs.text:
Expose shared detail reads through existing server/client patterns.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Embedded and remote paths use same application semantics.
  • [ ] Client can fetch full request by stable invocation ID.
  • [ ] Client can fetch/render ordered reasoning segments.
  • [ ] No endpoint accepts arbitrary opaque provider continuation handle mutation.
  • [ ] Event stream remains bounded; large full details are fetched on demand.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] server route/action returns full structured request;
  • [ ] Rust client parity;
  • [ ] TypeScript client parity if web package is in scope/currently owns these calls;
  • [ ] no runtime execution triggered by detail fetch.

docs.title: 20. Phase Q — Integrate TUI Presentation
docs.text:
Only after shared/runtime/protocol work above passes.

Update recursive conversation projection from task 134/135.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Prompt and reasoning controls remain independently selectable.
  • [ ] Full prompt expands/fetches complete effective request.
  • [ ] Provider-visible reasoning segments render at exact structural/activity positions around semantic/tool calls.
  • [ ] Runtime status is visually distinguishable from provider-visible reasoning.
  • [ ] Hidden reasoning removes rows without changing tree structure/reply anchor/tool ordering.
  • [ ] Full prompt rendering does not display raw secrets/provider headers.
  • [ ] Provider continuation provenance is debug/detail information, not conversation identity.

Focused TUI tests:

  • [ ] full prompt with server-side provider continuation still shows full effective context;
  • [ ] prompt Full + reasoning Hidden;
  • [ ] prompt Hidden + reasoning FullAvailable;
  • [ ] interleaved reasoning/tool sequence;
  • [ ] row count changes do not move stable reply anchor identity.

docs.title: 21. Phase R — Integrate Web Presentation
docs.text:
Extend reusable web agent UI/model owners, not app-local one-offs.

Requirements mirror TUI:

  • [ ] independent prompt/reasoning controls;
  • [ ] on-demand full request fetch;
  • [ ] ordered interleaved provider-visible reasoning;
  • [ ] same redaction semantics;
  • [ ] no rerun on presentation changes;
  • [ ] branch/provider continuation remains provider-neutral in shared model.

Use focused package tests/typechecks only while implementing.

docs.title: 22. Phase S — Restart and Provider-State Loss Recovery
docs.text:
Construct a deterministic scenario:

  1. run branch invocation with provider continuation;
  2. persist settled Scriberig session/request/activity state;
  3. restart runtime;
  4. simulate provider continuation unavailable/deleted;
  5. inspect historical full prompt/reasoning successfully from Scriberig state;
  6. continue branch;
  7. runtime recompiles canonical context and establishes new provider state;

  8. verify semantic/session identity did not change incorrectly.

  9. [ ] Historical full prompt remains inspectable after provider-state loss.

  10. [ ] Settled observable reasoning remains inspectable according to retention policy.
  11. [ ] New continuation produces correct canonical successor activity.
  12. [ ] No provider stream replay is required.

docs.title: 23. Phase T — Security Audit
docs.text:
Use conspicuous sentinel values for:

API key
Authorization header
secret env var
sensitive tool parameter
provider-private/encrypted reasoning payload

Prove they are absent from:

  • [ ] ProviderContinuationState public/debug output;
  • [ ] canonical full prompt detail where policy requires redaction;
  • [ ] reasoning activity;
  • [ ] protocol JSON;
  • [ ] app/server errors;
  • [ ] TUI rendering;
  • [ ] web rendering/snapshots;
  • [ ] logs produced by focused tests.

If a secret must influence a request, preserve a redaction marker/reference, not the value.

docs.title: 24. Phase U — Cross-Surface Conformance Scenario
docs.text:
Use one deterministic fake-provider scenario with:

root branch
provider continuation
visible reasoning segment
semantic operation
result
visible reasoning segment
child branch with independent continuation
child result
final root output

Prove:

  • [ ] embedded application view;
  • [ ] protocol/server view;
  • [ ] Rust client view;
  • [ ] TUI projection;
  • [ ] web model/UI projection when web is in scope;

all agree on:

branch identity
invocation identity
activity order
full effective request identity
reasoning availability
provider continuation strategy/provenance

Presentation may differ, semantics may not.

docs.title: 25. Phase V — Negative Architecture Checks
docs.text:
Search changed code and verify all of these are false:

  • [ ] no OpenAI conversation ID used as Scriberig SessionId/BranchId;
  • [ ] no one provider conversation shared implicitly by whole session tree;
  • [ ] no client can set arbitrary provider continuation handle;
  • [ ] no Full prompt view is merely a larger truncation limit;
  • [ ] no prompt view dumps raw authorization/provider wire payload;
  • [ ] no reasoning setting requests/exposes private chain-of-thought;
  • [ ] no one global trace enum replaces independent prompt/reasoning/tool/result controls;
  • [ ] no presentation toggle invokes model/tool execution;
  • [ ] no provider-switch path blindly resumes stale continuation;
  • [ ] no sibling transcript appears through shared provider state;
  • [ ] no restart correctness depends on provider retention.

docs.title: 26. Phase W — Synchronization Audit
docs.text:
Re-read:

  • design/CONTEXT.md;
  • Level 1 016–020;
  • Level 2 023–025;
  • tasks 133–136.

Verify implementation uses the same meanings for:

canonical Scriberig session identity
provider continuation
context fingerprint/lineage
full effective request
provider-visible reasoning
hidden reasoning
presentation preferences
branch isolation

If implementation forced a material design refinement, update the relevant design document before completion rather than leaving code/design disagreement undocumented.

  • [ ] Architecture documents and code are synchronized.
  • [ ] Task 133 prompt/reasoning expectations are satisfied by the stronger 136 contract.
  • [ ] Task 134 rendering uses the shared detail/activity contract.
  • [ ] Task 135 branch/multi-model context behavior remains intact.

docs.title: 27. Final Full-Suite Gate
docs.text:
Run only after every implementation/targeted-test checkbox above is complete.

Run repository-mandated final commands from root AGENTS.md, including at least:

python3 tools/lint_repo.py --fix
cargo fmt --all
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
pnpm --dir web format
pnpm --dir web typecheck

If web behavior changed, also run the repository's relevant web test/build commands.

  • [ ] lint passes;
  • [ ] Rust formatting passes;
  • [ ] workspace check passes;
  • [ ] Clippy passes with warnings denied;
  • [ ] full Rust tests pass;
  • [ ] web formatting/typecheck pass;
  • [ ] required web tests/build pass;
  • [ ] every earlier checked acceptance criterion remains true after final fixes.

Only then set:

**Status: [x] Complete**

docs.title: 28. Final Report Requirements
docs.text:
The implementing agent's final report must state:

  1. provider-continuation types and owner;
  2. exact reuse/reseed/fork compatibility rules implemented;
  3. OpenAI Conversation and/or previous-response support implemented;
  4. evidence siblings/children are isolated;
  5. provider-switch behavior;
  6. where complete safe canonical requests are retained;
  7. how bounded request projection relates to full detail;
  8. reasoning segment representation and ordering;
  9. explicit proof hidden/private chain-of-thought is not exposed;
  10. independent prompt/reasoning presentation modes;
  11. application/protocol/server/client changes;
  12. TUI/web behavior;
  13. restart/provider-state-loss behavior;
  14. security/redaction results;
  15. focused tests run during implementation;
  16. final full-suite results;
  17. any deferred provider capabilities;
  18. whether task 136 is genuinely eligible for Complete status.

docs.title: Implement Agent Profiles, Branch Handoff Context Components, and Evidence-Driven Prompt Experiments
docs.text: Status: [ ] In Progress

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
Implement the architecture defined by:

  • design/level-1/021. agent profiles context composition and evidence driven optimization.md;
  • design/level-2/030. agent profile context component and prompt experiment runtime.md.

Also preserve the controlling contracts from:

  • design/level-1/016. model driven agent execution and branch isolation.md;
  • design/level-1/017. recursive agent decomposition and context isolation.md;
  • design/level-1/018. durable plans dependency scheduling and multi-model execution.md;
  • design/level-1/019. semantic agent operations and projection-first editing.md;
  • design/level-1/020. provider continuation state and observable model execution.md;
  • design/level-2/023. agent runtime model provider and branch orchestration.md;
  • design/level-2/025. provider continuation and observable model execution.md;
  • design/level-3/135. implement recursive semantic agent plans dependencies and tree tui.md;
  • design/level-3/136. implement provider continuation full prompt and observable reasoning.md.

The first visible behavior change is intentionally small:

Every model invocation receives the Scriberig core behavioral invariants, and every non-root branch receives an additional instruction to make its final response a compact one-paragraph parent handoff. Root branches do not receive that handoff instruction. Existing child completion continues to persist the final child output as BranchResult.summary; do not add another summarizer model call.

The complete task then makes those instructions versioned context components, records their exact provenance in effective requests, and establishes evidence-backed prompt experiments without making prompt files canonical state.

Follow phases in order. A simpler implementation agent should not jump directly to an autonomous optimizer.

docs.title: 2.1 Read before editing
docs.text:
Before changing code:

  • [ ] Read root AGENTS.md completely.
  • [ ] Read design/AGENTS.md completely.
  • [ ] Read the nearest AGENTS.md for every crate/directory modified.
  • [ ] Read Level-1 documents 009, 016, 017, 018, 019, 020, and 021.
  • [ ] Read Level-2 documents 023, 025, and 030.
  • [ ] Read Level-3 tasks 135 and 136, especially incomplete task-136 work that may own complete-request provenance.
  • [ ] Inspect current scriberig-agent-core, scriberig-agent-runtime, scriberig-session, scriberig-app, and apps/scriberig implementations before creating names.
  • [ ] Search for existing profile/context/branch-role/effective-request types before adding any new type.
  • [ ] Record any material difference from the baseline in this document before adapting the prescribed steps.

docs.title: 2.2 Checklist discipline
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this file open while implementing.
  • [ ] Tick a checkbox only after the exact criterion is implemented and focused verification passes.
  • [ ] Tick items immediately; do not bulk-check at the end.
  • [ ] If later work invalidates a checked item, return it to [ ] immediately.
  • [ ] Keep unfinished later phases unchecked even if scaffolding exists.
  • [ ] Before changing this status to Complete, review every checked item against code and test evidence.

docs.title: 2.3 Architectural prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not:

  • create a second session/branch store;
  • create a second model/tool execution loop;
  • equate child branch identity with a new agent identity;
  • add an AgentId that merely aliases branch identity;
  • copy the full parent transcript into a child by default;
  • copy the child transcript into its parent at completion;
  • add a second provider call solely to summarize every child branch;
  • force root user-facing output into a one-paragraph summary;
  • compile prompts independently in TUI/web/server code;
  • make Markdown/TOML/source prompt files canonical profile state;
  • automatically append every observed failure to always-on prose;
  • let prompt experiments overwrite the active base profile before validation/promotion;
  • use provider continuation IDs as Scriberig session/branch/profile identity;
  • expose hidden chain-of-thought as experiment evidence;
  • bypass ordinary semantic candidate/revision/validation/promotion because the edited knowledge happens to control prompts.

docs.title: 2.4 Test discipline
docs.text:
Until all implementation phases are complete, prefer focused tests such as:

cargo test -p scriberig-agent-core profile
cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime context
cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime fingerprint
cargo test -p scriberig-session model_invocation
cargo test -p scriberig-app child
cargo test -p scriberig-app prompt_experiment
cargo test -p scriberig -- child_runtime

Do not run the repository-wide final gate after every phase.

docs.title: 3. Verify the Current Baseline
docs.text: The following facts were true when this task was written. Verify them on current main.

docs.title: 3.1 Context compiler
docs.text:
Current files:

crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/context.rs
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/context/compiler.rs
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/context/fingerprint.rs

Current BranchExecutionContext contains, among other fields:

session
branch
continuation_anchor
purpose
instruction
parent_summary
ancestor_results
dependency_results
project_scope
activities

It does not yet carry an explicit root/non-root branch role.

Current compiler emits the system instruction:

You are operating within one isolated semantic branch.

before purpose/results/scope/instruction/activity.

Current CompiledContext contains:

messages
dependencies
omitted_handles
canonical

Current request fingerprint uses canonical compiled context plus provider/model/capabilities/tool identity.

  • [ ] Confirm these fields/owners remain accurate or document replacements.

docs.title: 3.2 Session model invocation provenance
docs.text:
Current scriberig-session::ModelInvocation already has fields including:

agent_profile: Option<String>
context_fingerprint: Option<String>
provider_profile
model
model_profile
thinking_level
request_fingerprint
request: Option<ModelRequestProjection>

Task 136 may add/replace complete effective request storage.

  • [ ] Confirm whether task 136 has introduced a complete canonical request type before extending provenance.
  • [ ] Reuse task-136 structures if present; do not create a competing full-prompt record.

docs.title: 3.3 Child completion
docs.text:
Current integrated child execution lives in/around:

apps/scriberig/src/child_runtime.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/service_local_sessions/operations_child.rs

Current child completion stores:

final child output
  -> child AgentOutput.text
  -> BranchResult.summary
  -> AgentResult.final_output
  -> ChildResult.summary returned to parent

No dedicated summarizer invocation is required by this path.

  • [ ] Confirm BranchResult.summary is still populated from child final output.
  • [ ] Confirm ChildResult.summary still returns the durable completed output/result.
  • [ ] Confirm result handles remain separate from summary prose.

docs.title: 3.4 Agent-core profile baseline
docs.text:
At task creation, crates/scriberig-agent-core/src/ contains tool/capability/inspect contracts but no full first-class profile/context-component implementation.

  • [ ] Confirm no equivalent profile/component types already exist elsewhere before creating them.

docs.title: 4. Phase A — Make Branch Role Explicit
docs.text: Do this before changing prompt text.

docs.title: Task A1 — Add a provider-neutral branch role
docs.text:
Add an explicit type in the lowest appropriate reusable owner. Prefer scriberig-agent-runtime::context if the role is currently only context-compilation input; move to scriberig-agent-core only if it is already useful across reusable agent APIs.

Use a shape equivalent to:

pub enum BranchRole {
    Root,
    NonRoot { parent: String },
}

Exact field types may follow existing stable branch-reference conventions.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Root/non-root is explicit and not inferred from titles.
  • [ ] Non-root can retain the parent branch reference when useful.
  • [ ] The type is documented according to repository rules.
  • [ ] Serialization is added only if the type crosses a durability/protocol boundary.
  • [ ] No new canonical branch identity system is created.

docs.title: Task A2 — Extend BranchExecutionContext
docs.text:
Add branch role to BranchExecutionContext or the current replacement type.

Prefer constructors/builders that make ordinary root behavior backward-safe, for example:

BranchExecutionContext::new(...) -> Root by default
.with_branch_role(...)

or distinct root/child constructors if current APIs make that clearer.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Existing root callers remain explicit or safely default to Root.
  • [ ] Child/delegation callers explicitly mark NonRoot.
  • [ ] Historical continuation that creates a new child uses the correct role from actual branch topology.
  • [ ] Plan workers use actual branch parentage rather than plan nesting heuristics.

docs.title: Focused tests
docs.text:
• [ ] default/root constructor yields Root;
  • [ ] child constructor/builder retains parent branch identity;
  • [ ] role equality/debug behavior is deterministic.

docs.title: 5. Phase B — Add Bootstrap Agent Profile and Context Components
docs.text: This phase should produce the immediate prompt-quality improvement while remaining small.

docs.title: Task B1 — Add reusable profile/component descriptors
docs.text:
In scriberig-agent-core, add focused files rather than overloading lib.rs.

A likely layout is:

crates/scriberig-agent-core/src/profile.rs
crates/scriberig-agent-core/src/context_component.rs

If repository naming conventions suggest one file initially, keep it under the source-size limit and split by responsibility when needed.

Define documented types equivalent to:

AgentProfileRevisionRef
  identity
  revision

ContextComponentRevisionRef
  identity
  revision

ContextComponentKind
  CoreInvariant
  BehaviorPolicy
  DomainGuidance
  ToolGuidance
  SkillTrigger
  ExecutionLesson

ContextActivationRule
  Always
  RootOnly
  NonRootOnly
  ...future narrow rules

ContextComponentDescriptor
  ref
  kind
  content
  activation
  priority

AgentProfileDescriptor
  ref
  name
  ordered component refs/descriptors

Keep the first implementation intentionally conservative.

  • [ ] IDs/revisions are deterministic/fingerprintable.
  • [ ] Display names are not used as the only identity.
  • [ ] Component kind and activation are typed, not parsed from prose.
  • [ ] Types contain no provider credential fields.
  • [ ] Types contain no hidden reasoning fields.
  • [ ] All declarations/fields/functions are documented.
  • [ ] lib.rs re-exports only the intended public surface.

docs.title: Task B2 — Define the bootstrap default profile
docs.text:
Add one deterministic bootstrap profile construction function in the shared agent/runtime layer.

It must contain separate components for:

  1. core Scriberig invariants — activation Always;
  2. non-root branch handoff — activation NonRootOnly.

Core component meaning must include:

operate inside the current Scriberig branch/context frame
semantic/domain operations first for understood domains
files are projections where understood
canonical changes use candidate/migration/validation/promotion
stable semantic handles and exact snapshots/revisions when exact state matters
child branches are focused context isolation and do not alone imply another agent
parents/dependencies consume compact durable results, not child transcripts
capabilities are used progressively

Non-root handoff meaning must include:

When about to finish this non-root branch, make the final response a compact
one-paragraph summary for the parent. Include important outcome,
decisions/discoveries, remaining issues, and durable semantic/result handles.
Do not reproduce the branch transcript or hidden reasoning.

The exact prose may be polished, but preserve the semantic requirements.

  • [ ] Core and handoff are separate components.
  • [ ] Profile identity/revision is stable for identical definitions.
  • [ ] Component identities/revisions are stable for identical definitions.
  • [ ] Changing a component's behaviorally relevant content changes its revision/fingerprint.
  • [ ] The bootstrap definition is short; no unrelated domain guidance is added.

docs.title: 6. Phase C — Resolve and Activate Context Components
Task C1 — Add deterministic component activation
docs.text:
Implement a small pure resolver, likely under scriberig-agent-runtime/src/context/.

Input:

exact AgentProfileDescriptor
BranchRole
later: domain/capability/tool applicability state

Output:

ordered Vec<ResolvedContextComponent>

Initial behavior:

Always       -> every invocation
RootOnly     -> root only
NonRootOnly  -> non-root only

Do not implement a scripting language.

Ordering must be deterministic by explicit priority plus stable tie-breaker identity.

  • [ ] Same exact inputs produce the same ordered component list.
  • [ ] Inactive components are absent, not emitted as comments.
  • [ ] Non-root handoff is never active for root.
  • [ ] Core invariant is active for both root and non-root.

docs.title: Task C2 — Integrate components into ContextCompiler
docs.text:
Replace the single hard-coded system sentence with compiled activated component sections.

Do not discard the existing branch purpose/result/scope/activity behavior.

Use a deterministic provider-neutral ordering equivalent to:

activated core/behavior components
continuation anchor where semantically required
branch purpose
selected parent/ancestor/dependency results
semantic project scope
current instruction
bounded branch-local activities

If task 136 has introduced typed complete-request sections, integrate there rather than flattening everything prematurely.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Root compiled context contains the core invariant component.
  • [ ] Root compiled context does not contain child-handoff guidance.
  • [ ] Non-root compiled context contains both core and handoff guidance.
  • [ ] Existing selected result handling still sorts deterministically.
  • [ ] Existing omitted-handle/budget behavior still works.
  • [ ] Context component identities/revisions contribute to dependencies/provenance, not only rendered text.
  • [ ] Context canonical representation changes when active component revision changes.

docs.title: Task C3 — Keep instructions compact
docs.text:
Review the generated default prompt after integration.

  • [ ] No duplicate statement appears in both core and handoff components.
  • [ ] No large generic coding-agent policy has been introduced.
  • [ ] Tool-specific guidance remains in tool/component activation rather than base prose where possible.
  • [ ] Domain-specific facts are not added to the global core component.

docs.title: Focused tests
docs.text:
Add/extend context compiler tests proving exact message/section order and activation.

  • [ ] core present in root;
  • [ ] core present in child;
  • [ ] handoff absent in root;
  • [ ] handoff present in child;
  • [ ] deterministic ordering;
  • [ ] inactive component absent;
  • [ ] canonical context differs when component revision/content differs;
  • [ ] unrelated parent/sibling transcript remains excluded.

docs.title: 7. Phase D — Wire Actual Root and Child Callers Correctly
Task D1 — Root execution uses BranchRole::Root
docs.text:
Trace every integrated root model execution path.

Likely owners include runtime composition in apps/scriberig and application start/continue paths.

  • [ ] New root session execution explicitly or safely resolves Root.
  • [ ] Continuing the current root branch remains Root if it has no parent.
  • [ ] User-facing final response receives no forced handoff component.

Do not decide this in the TUI.

docs.title: Task D2 — Child execution uses BranchRole::NonRoot
docs.text:
Update apps/scriberig/src/child_runtime.rs and any shared child execution construction to mark the child context as non-root using the actual parent branch identity.

Do not use the historical title delegated agent branch as the signal.

  • [ ] LocalChildExecutor or its current replacement passes actual branch role to context compilation.
  • [ ] Nested grandchildren also receive NonRoot with their immediate parent.
  • [ ] Same provider/model/profile in parent and child does not create a synthetic AgentId.
  • [ ] Different explicit branch assignments still work through existing execution-selection logic.

docs.title: Task D3 — Fix semantic context construction if it skips profile context
docs.text:
At task creation, with_child_context(...) returns the model unchanged when no semantic project scope exists.

That means any behavior placed only inside ContextCompiler risks being absent from such child requests.

Audit the actual provider-model construction carefully.

Required invariant:

Core profile/context behavior must apply to every integrated model invocation, not only invocations that happen to have a ProjectSemanticScope.

Possible correction:

  • compile branch/profile context regardless of whether semantic project scope is present;
  • add project scope conditionally inside that context.

Do not attach an empty fake project scope merely to trigger compilation.

  • [ ] Child without semantic project scope still gets core + non-root handoff components.
  • [ ] Root without semantic project scope still gets core component.
  • [ ] Project scope remains optional and exact when present.

docs.title: Focused tests
docs.text:
• [ ] child with semantic scope gets handoff;
  • [ ] child without semantic scope gets handoff;
  • [ ] root without semantic scope gets core but no handoff.

docs.title: 8. Phase E — Preserve Existing Branch Completion Semantics
docs.text: Do not redesign the successful child completion path unless a verified bug requires it.

docs.title: Task E1 — Verify final output becomes durable summary
docs.text:
In crates/scriberig-app/src/service_local_sessions/operations_child.rs or its current owner, preserve:

result.output/final_output
  -> AgentOutput.text
  -> BranchResult.summary
  -> returned AgentResult/ChildResult summary
  • [ ] Successful child result has non-empty summary when final output is non-empty.
  • [ ] result_handles are retained separately.
  • [ ] structured touched/change/validation/question fields remain available independently of prose.

docs.title: Task E2 — Do not add a summarizer invocation
docs.text:
Use a fake/counting provider in tests.

Construct a child that requires a known number of model steps and then completes.

  • [ ] Completion performs no extra provider invocation after the executor's final response solely for summarization.
  • [ ] No summarizer_model, hidden summary provider, or equivalent default path is introduced.

If an optional summarizer policy already exists by implementation time, prove it defaults off and is explicitly attributable.

docs.title: Task E3 — Parent receives compact result, not transcript
docs.text:
Verify the parent branch/session activity and context compiler behavior after child completion.

  • [ ] Parent can reference the child's BranchResult.
  • [ ] Parent context includes the selected compact result when policy selects it.
  • [ ] Child model invocations/tool calls are not copied into parent-local turns/activity merely because the child finished.
  • [ ] Full child history remains inspectable through the child branch reference.

docs.title: 9. Phase F — Record Exact Profile and Component Provenance
docs.text: Coordinate this phase with unfinished task 136.

docs.title: Task F1 — Resolve one exact profile revision per invocation
docs.text:
At invocation start, snapshot the effective profile revision.

  • [ ] The chosen profile cannot silently change halfway through one invocation.
  • [ ] Historical invocation keeps its resolved profile even if defaults later change.
  • [ ] Profile display name is not the only retained identity.

docs.title: Task F2 — Retain activated component revisions
docs.text:
Extend the complete provider-neutral request/provenance structure with an ordered list of exact activated component revision refs.

If task 136 adds CanonicalModelRequest, use that.

If task 136 is still incomplete, add the smallest compatible field in the current context/invocation provenance and leave a clear integration point; do not create a rival full-prompt subsystem.

  • [ ] Full effective prompt inspection can identify exact profile revision.
  • [ ] Full effective prompt inspection can identify exact active component revisions.
  • [ ] Root/non-root activation difference is observable without rerunning work.
  • [ ] Prompt visibility setting does not change captured provenance.

docs.title: Task F3 — Fill current ModelInvocation.agent_profile
docs.text:
At task creation, local persistence code currently writes agent_profile: None for captured model requests.

Trace the actual invocation persistence path.

  • [ ] Populate agent_profile with the exact safe profile revision reference or migrate to the task-136 canonical equivalent.
  • [ ] Populate context_fingerprint/request_fingerprint consistently where the runtime has them.
  • [ ] Do not store credentials.

docs.title: Task F4 — Update request fingerprinting
docs.text:
Current RequestFingerprintInput hashes provider profile, model, capabilities, canonical compiled context, and tool identity.

Ensure profile/component resolution affects identity explicitly or through an unambiguous canonical context representation.

Prefer explicit revision identities in the fingerprint input if task 136/Level-2 030 structures support it.

  • [ ] same task/context + different active component revision -> different fingerprint;
  • [ ] root vs non-root -> different fingerprint when handoff activation differs;
  • [ ] identical profile/component/context/tool inputs -> identical fingerprint;
  • [ ] credential sentinel never affects fingerprint.

docs.title: 10. Phase G — Make Profile/Component State Semantically Durable
docs.text:
Do this only after Phases A–F pass.

The bootstrap profile may initially be code-defined, but the architectural destination is stable semantic knowledge.

docs.title: Task G1 — Reuse the universal knowledge/revision model
docs.text:
Inspect current semantic-domain/application patterns before adding persistence.

Create or adapt the smallest appropriate semantic representation for:

AgentProfile
ContextComponent

Requirements:

  • [ ] stable identity and immutable revision are distinct;
  • [ ] exact component revisions can be referenced from a profile revision;
  • [ ] changing profile composition creates a new profile revision;
  • [ ] changing component content creates a new component revision;
  • [ ] historical model invocation remains bound to the old exact revisions;
  • [ ] storage is not a mutable prompt-file blob.

Do not put provider HTTP/runtime dependencies in the semantic/domain owner.

docs.title: Task G2 — Add application read operations first
docs.text:
Before mutation UI, expose shared read/resolve operations equivalent to:

list profiles
inspect profile exact revision
inspect component exact revision
resolve effective profile for branch/invocation
  • [ ] embedded and server paths can use the same application operation.
  • [ ] no TUI-specific profile database exists.
  • [ ] exact revision is returned where historical inspection matters.

docs.title: Task G3 — Add authorized candidate mutation path
docs.text:
Profile/component editing must enter the ordinary candidate/change model.

Implement operations equivalent to:

propose profile/component candidate
validate structural candidate
review/resolve conflict if needed
promote accepted candidate
  • [ ] no direct live-profile overwrite API is introduced for automated optimization;
  • [ ] candidate has exact base revision;
  • [ ] stale-base promotion conflicts rather than silently overwriting;
  • [ ] rejected candidate remains inspectable according to retention policy.

docs.title: Task G4 — Bootstrap migration
docs.text:
If the default profile was initially code-defined:

  • [ ] define deterministic bootstrap identity/revision mapping;
  • [ ] allow semantic stored profile to supersede bootstrap default without changing historical references ambiguously;
  • [ ] keep startup functional when no durable profile has yet been created;
  • [ ] document the transition in code/tests.

docs.title: 11. Phase H — Add Evidence and Execution Lessons
docs.text: Do not auto-inject learned behavior yet.

docs.title: Task H1 — Define evidence references
docs.text:
Reuse durable existing identities where possible:

ModelInvocation
ToolInvocation/ToolResult
BranchResult
ValidationResult
candidate/profile revisions
plan node/result

Do not copy whole transcripts into an evidence record.

  • [ ] Evidence references are stable and reopenable.
  • [ ] Exact candidate/profile/task context can be recovered.

docs.title: Task H2 — Define ExecutionLesson
docs.text:
Add semantic/application structures equivalent to:

identity
revision
cue
lesson/guidance
applicability scope
evidence refs
confidence
source experiment
producer provenance
status
  • [ ] Exact project facts are not silently generalized into reusable lessons.
  • [ ] Lesson retains provenance and evidence.
  • [ ] Candidate/rejected/superseded state is representable.
  • [ ] Lesson is not automatically active merely because it exists.

docs.title: Task H3 — Add deterministic accepted-lesson activation
docs.text:
Only accepted lessons whose applicability predicate matches exact invocation state may become ExecutionLesson context components.

Start with a narrow predicate vocabulary; do not create an arbitrary executable DSL.

  • [ ] accepted applicable lesson activates deterministically;
  • [ ] rejected/candidate/superseded lesson does not activate;
  • [ ] unrelated domain/project lesson does not activate;
  • [ ] activated lesson revision appears in full prompt provenance/fingerprint.

docs.title: 12. Phase I — Add Durable Prompt Experiments
Task I1 — Define experiment and attribution structures
docs.text:
Implement durable structures equivalent to:

PromptExperiment
  id
  base_profile_revision
  evaluation case/task refs
  candidate profile revisions
  probe branch/result refs
  validation refs
  behavioral contrast refs
  composition decision
  status

PromptAttribution
  candidate/component ref
  Helped | Hurt | NoObservedEffect | Confounded
  evidence refs
  note
  • [ ] KeepBase/no-change outcome is representable.
  • [ ] Confounded is representable.
  • [ ] Adoption does not automatically mark every component Helped.
  • [ ] Experiment is inspectable without parsing coordinator prose.

docs.title: Task I2 — Candidate proposals use normal profile candidates
docs.text:
The proposer may suggest changes to:

BehaviorPolicy
DomainGuidance
ToolGuidance
SkillTrigger
ExecutionLesson

but each proposal must become an exact candidate component/profile revision.

  • [ ] proposal records observed evidence/trajectory reference or explicit evaluation-case basis;
  • [ ] no evidence may validly yield KeepBase;
  • [ ] proposer cannot mutate active profile directly;
  • [ ] project-specific facts stay scoped rather than becoming global policy.

docs.title: Task I3 — Probe candidates in isolated branches
docs.text:
Use existing plan/branch orchestration.

For each experiment:

  • [ ] baseline probe binds the exact base profile revision;
  • [ ] each candidate probe binds the exact candidate profile revision;
  • [ ] probes use equivalent base semantic/task state where evaluation requires comparability;
  • [ ] each probe produces a durable BranchResult plus validation references;
  • [ ] probe transcripts remain in their branches and are not copied into the composer context.

docs.title: Task I4 — Compose from results/evidence
docs.text:
Create a compose/evaluate plan node that depends on required probe results.

The composer receives:

base/candidate profile identities
compact probe BranchResults
validation evidence
explicitly selected behavioral contrasts
known downside/failure evidence

not arbitrary hidden transcripts by default.

  • [ ] compose node cannot run before required dependencies are satisfied;
  • [ ] repeated baseline failure weighs more strongly than a single candidate anecdote where policy specifies;
  • [ ] deterministic validators are surfaced distinctly from model judgment;
  • [ ] KeepBase is allowed;
  • [ ] attribution is conservative when causality is unclear.

docs.title: Task I5 — Promote only validated selected candidate
docs.text:
Promotion uses ordinary profile candidate/revision semantics.

  • [ ] selection alone does not mutate current profile;
  • [ ] required validation/policy gate runs before promotion;
  • [ ] promotion creates a new current revision;
  • [ ] base/rejected candidates remain historically inspectable;
  • [ ] active sessions/invocations are not retroactively rewritten.

docs.title: 13. Phase J — Optional Automated Lesson Extraction
docs.text:
Only implement after PromptExperiment records are durable and tested.

At most one transferable lesson should be extracted from one experiment by default unless policy explicitly permits more.

Lesson extraction should capture:

cue
lesson
supporting evidence
confidence
applicability
source experiment
  • [ ] no lesson is created merely because a candidate won;
  • [ ] confounded experiments may produce no lesson;
  • [ ] task-specific facts remain scoped to the task/project/snapshot rather than global behavior;
  • [ ] accepted lesson requires explicit validation/promotion policy before future activation.

docs.title: 14. Phase K — Provider Continuation Conformance
docs.text:
Coordinate with task 136; do not duplicate its continuation implementation.

Add regression tests proving the new context/profile behavior interacts correctly with continuation.

  • [ ] child branch does not reuse parent provider continuation merely because executor/model/profile are the same;
  • [ ] returning from child does not attempt to "rewind" child continuation into parent;
  • [ ] compatible parent continuation may resume if task-136 lineage rules allow it;
  • [ ] changed profile/component revision makes incompatible continuation stale/reseeded as required;
  • [ ] loss of continuation still recompiles equivalent canonical profile/component context from Scriberig state.

docs.title: 15. Phase L — Product/Protocol Inspection Only After Shared Semantics Exist
docs.text:
Do not begin here.

If product exposure is in scope for this task, add only thin shared views/commands over completed lower-layer semantics.

Useful inspection may include:

resolved AgentProfile revision
active ContextComponent revisions
why branch role activated non-root handoff
experiment status
accepted ExecutionLessons

Requirements:

  • [ ] TUI/web do not assemble prompt text;
  • [ ] changing prompt visibility does not change activation;
  • [ ] profile/component historical inspection uses exact revisions;
  • [ ] no client can inject arbitrary provider continuation IDs or resolved credentials through profile APIs.

If no UI is required for acceptance, leave this phase unchecked for a follow-up task rather than adding speculative surface area.

docs.title: 16. Required Regression Tests
docs.text: Before final repository-wide validation, ensure focused tests cover all of the following.

docs.title: Branch semantics
docs.text:
• [ ] creating a child branch does not create a new canonical agent identity;
  • [ ] root/non-root role comes from branch topology/explicit construction;
  • [ ] nested child/grandchild role is correct;
  • [ ] parent context after child completion uses compact result, not child transcript.

docs.title: Prompt behavior
docs.text:
• [ ] root gets core behavior component;
  • [ ] root does not get non-root handoff component;
  • [ ] child gets core + handoff;
  • [ ] child without project semantic scope still gets both;
  • [ ] handoff wording instructs compact one-paragraph parent summary and durable handles;
  • [ ] no hidden-reasoning request is present.

docs.title: Completion behavior
docs.text:
• [ ] child final output persists as BranchResult.summary;
  • [ ] child result handles remain exact/separate;
  • [ ] no extra summarizer provider call occurs by default;
  • [ ] root final output remains ordinary user-facing output.

docs.title: Identity/provenance
docs.text:
• [ ] exact profile revision retained;
  • [ ] exact activated component revisions retained;
  • [ ] profile/component change affects fingerprint;
  • [ ] same exact inputs remain deterministic;
  • [ ] credentials do not enter fingerprint/provenance.

docs.title: Experiment behavior
docs.text:
When Phases H–J are implemented:

  • [ ] base profile is immutable during candidate probes;
  • [ ] candidate probes bind exact revisions;
  • [ ] experiment dependency scheduling uses durable results;
  • [ ] deterministic validations are retained;
  • [ ] KeepBase works;
  • [ ] Confounded works;
  • [ ] rejected candidate does not become active;
  • [ ] promoted candidate creates a new revision;
  • [ ] extracted lesson preserves evidence/provenance and activation scope.

docs.title: 17. Documentation Updates During Implementation
docs.text:
As code lands:

  • [ ] Update design/CONTEXT.md if implementation reveals a materially more precise invariant than the current architecture spine.
  • [ ] Update Level-2 030 if actual ownership differs from the initial crate split.
  • [ ] Update task 136 if the shared complete-request representation changes in a way that affects its checklist.
  • [ ] Update code/API docs to use child branch/branch executor where no distinct agent identity exists; do not perform meaningless mass renames that break public compatibility.
  • [ ] Keep historical names only where changing them would cause disproportionate churn; document semantic meaning at the boundary.

docs.title: 18. Final Repository Gate
docs.text:
Run this only after all implementation checkboxes intended for this task are complete.

python3 tools/lint_repo.py --fix
cargo fmt --all
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
pnpm --dir web format
pnpm --dir web typecheck

Run additional web tests/build if modified web packages require them under their nearest instructions.

  • [ ] Repository lint passes after fixes.
  • [ ] Rust formatting passes.
  • [ ] Workspace check passes.
  • [ ] Clippy passes with warnings denied.
  • [ ] Workspace tests pass.
  • [ ] Required web formatting/type checks pass when web was touched.
  • [ ] No source file violates the 400-line rule excluding allowed preamble.
  • [ ] Every new/modified declaration follows repository documentation rules.

docs.title: 19. Final Acceptance Checklist
docs.text: Do not mark the task Complete until every implemented scope item below is proven.

docs.title: Mandatory first slice
docs.text:
• [ ] Branch role is explicit in context compilation.
  • [ ] Bootstrap default profile has versioned/fingerprintable core and non-root-handoff components.
  • [ ] Core Scriberig behavior is present in every integrated model invocation.
  • [ ] Non-root handoff behavior is present in every non-root integrated model invocation.
  • [ ] Root requests never receive the non-root handoff instruction.
  • [ ] Child requests without project semantic scope still receive agent behavior context.
  • [ ] Child final output remains the source of BranchResult.summary.
  • [ ] Ordinary child completion performs no extra summarizer model call.
  • [ ] Parent consumes compact child result rather than child transcript.
  • [ ] Branch creation alone is not represented as creation of a new canonical agent identity.

docs.title: Versioned context/provenance slice
docs.text:
• [ ] Exact AgentProfile revision is resolved per invocation.
  • [ ] Exact activated ContextComponent revisions are retained/inspectable.
  • [ ] Profile/component revisions affect request identity.
  • [ ] Complete prompt integration follows task-136 architecture rather than creating a competing prompt store.
  • [ ] Provider continuation compatibility accounts for changed profile/component context.

docs.title: Semantic optimization slice
docs.text:
• [ ] Durable semantic profile/component revisions replace bootstrap-only authority for editable profiles.
  • [ ] Candidate profile changes use ordinary candidate/validation/promotion semantics.
  • [ ] ExecutionLesson carries cue, scope, evidence, confidence, and provenance.
  • [ ] PromptExperiment carries base/candidates/probes/results/validations/composition/attribution.
  • [ ] Propose-probe-compose uses branch/plan/result semantics, not transcript sharing.
  • [ ] KeepBase, Helped, Hurt, NoObservedEffect, and Confounded outcomes are representable where applicable.
  • [ ] Deterministic validators are preferred over model self-approval where available.
  • [ ] No prompt optimizer directly rewrites canonical prompt files or AGENTS.md.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• [ ] Files remain projections where their domain is understood.
  • [ ] Canonical semantic mutations still use shared migration/change semantics.
  • [ ] Session tree, plan dependency DAG, knowledge graph, and execution causality remain distinct.
  • [ ] Provider continuation remains secondary branch-local runtime state.
  • [ ] Product presentation state does not affect execution/context activation.
  • [ ] Hidden chain-of-thought is neither required nor exposed.

When every applicable checklist item is implemented, verified, and reviewed, change the status at the top from [ ] Not Started to [x] Complete.

docs.title: Pin, Vendor, and Wrap RPI TUI with Provenance and Dependency Isolation
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
Implement the first slice of design/level-2/031. rpi tui adoption and shared presentation migration plan.md.

This task does not replace the active Scriberig TUI yet. It establishes a reviewed, reproducible, isolated upstream intake and proves that generic rpi-tui primitives can be consumed without importing foreign agent/session semantics.

The required outcome is:

exact reviewed rpi-tui revision
        |
        v
provenance-preserving vendor boundary
        |
        v
scriberig-tui-kit generic facade
        |
        v
focused deterministic tests

Do not begin task 139 until this sheet is complete and every checked item has verification evidence.

docs.title: 2.1 Read before editing
docs.text:
Before changing code:

  • [x] Read root AGENTS.md completely.
  • [x] Read design/AGENTS.md completely.
  • [x] Read crates/scriberig-tui/AGENTS.md completely.
  • [x] Read the nearest AGENTS.md for every additional directory/crate modified.
  • [x] Read Level-1 documents 014, 015, and 022 completely.
  • [x] Read Level-2 documents 014, 021, 022, and 031 completely.
  • [x] Read Level-3 tasks 134 and 135 so the vendor intake does not redefine current session/TUI behavior.
  • [x] Inspect root workspace Cargo.toml, crates/scriberig-tui/Cargo.toml, current lockfile policy, LICENSES/, LICENSING.md, and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md if present.
  • [x] Inspect the exact upstream bigfish1913/pi-rust revision before copying code.
  • [x] Search the repository for an existing third-party/vendor convention before creating a new one.

docs.title: 2.2 Checklist discipline
docs.text:
• [x] Keep this file open while implementing.
  • [x] Tick a checkbox only after that exact criterion is implemented and focused verification passes.
  • [x] Tick items immediately; never bulk-tick at the end.

docs.title: 2.3 Architectural prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not:

  • add rpi-agent, rpi-harness, rpi-tools, rpi-extensions, or upstream provider/session crates;
  • map an upstream transcript/message/session identity onto Scriberig SessionId or BranchId;
  • add model/provider/tool execution to scriberig-tui-kit;
  • make the vendor tree depend on Scriberig semantic crates;
  • make Scriberig semantic/protocol types depend on rpi-tui types;
  • strip upstream license/copyright notices;
  • enable image terminal protocols as part of intake;
  • enable clipboard reads/writes without an explicit Scriberig-facing policy boundary;
  • ship two independently active Crossterm terminal runtimes;
  • silently copy only selected files without recording their exact upstream origin.

docs.title: Migrate Generic Terminal Primitives and Composer/Editor Infrastructure
docs.text: Status: [x] Complete

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
Continue design/level-2/031. rpi tui adoption and shared presentation migration plan.md after task 138 is complete.

Replace locally maintained commodity terminal behavior with the pinned rpi-tui-backed scriberig-tui-kit facade while preserving the existing Scriberig TUI state machine and semantic contracts.

This task migrates generic primitives only:

  • normalized terminal input;
  • editor/composer behavior;
  • safe text/Markdown rendering primitives;
  • generic selection/search helpers;
  • theme/style primitives;
  • width/wrapping helpers;

It does not yet replace the recursive conversation renderer or all auxiliary screens. Those are tasks 140 and 141.

Do not begin task 140 until this sheet is complete.

docs.title: 4. Task A — Define the Translation Boundary
docs.text:
scriberig-tui should consume Scriberig-owned facade types from scriberig-tui-kit, not scatter rpi_tui::* types through product code.

Add only the adapters required for the migration.

Conceptually:

rpi-tui input            -> TuiKitInput -> current Scriberig input/action mapping
rpi-tui editor           -> TuiKitEditor -> composer state/action bridge
rpi-tui text/markdown    -> SafeUiLine/Segment -> current render adapter
rpi-tui selection helper -> TuiKitSelection -> stable caller-owned row identity
rpi-tui theme            -> TuiKitTheme -> Scriberig semantic style roles

Exact type names should fit current code.

Backspace/Delete

docs.title: 6. Task C — Replace Composer Editing Internals
docs.text:
Adapt the pinned upstream editor through scriberig-tui-kit for the persistent composer.

Preserve the current product contract:

  • composer can own focus immediately on normal conversation home;
  • ordinary typing edits the draft;
  • Enter/submission behavior follows current TUI rules;
  • multiline behavior remains intentional and tested;
  • slash commands are recognized by Scriberig, not by an upstream agent command registry;
  • draft editing never changes durable session state until submit/command dispatch occurs.

Do not change session creation/continuation APIs in this task unless a currently failing interface adaptation requires a small shared fix already defined by tasks 134/135.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Composer draft uses the terminal-kit editor internally or through a clearly bounded adapter.
  • [x] Cursor movement works across Unicode text according to the adopted editor semantics.
  • [x] Insert/delete/backspace behavior has deterministic tests.

  • [x] Cancelling/clearing editor state does not cancel unrelated semantic work.

docs.text:
Move generic Markdown parsing/styling/wrapping to the terminal-kit wrapper where suitable.

Scriberig still decides what content means and which content to show. The kit decides how safe text/Markdown becomes terminal lines.

Requirements:

  • model output is data, not raw terminal escape code;
  • tool/validator diagnostics are data;
  • source/document projection text is data unless explicitly rendered through trusted style structures;
  • URLs/links must not inject OSC sequences;
  • code fences and long unbroken tokens must not panic narrow layouts.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Markdown headings/paragraphs/lists/code blocks render through the new primitive path.
  • [x] Existing conversation text remains readable at narrow widths.

  • [x] Width/wrapping tests cover Unicode and a long unbroken token.
  • [x] Rendering helpers remain presentation-only and perform no semantic/service calls.

docs.title: 14. Implementation Notes
docs.text:
The pinned upstream crate exposes editor and presentation components but no general terminal-event normalizer. Scriberig therefore retains its Crossterm-owned event decoder and action keymap, adding Home, End, and Delete translations for the shared composer editor. This keeps key help and slash command ownership in Scriberig while the kit owns editing, safe text and Markdown rendering, fuzzy selection mechanics, and semantic theme mapping.

The persistent conversation composer now wraps the kit editor; cursor state remains presentation-only and the existing draft/action submission contract is preserved. Palette filtering uses the upstream fuzzy selector and returns stable action IDs after filtering. The old case-insensitive substring helper was removed after its production path was replaced.

Focused verification passed: 15 tests in scriberig-tui-kit, 211 tests in scriberig-tui, cargo check -p scriberig-tui, and Clippy for both crates with warnings denied. Formatting passed with cargo fmt --all.

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:

docs.title: 5. Task B — Preserve Structural Placement

Task 139's reusable kit is used for palette filtering and stable selection, the Explorer list, external text, safe Markdown, main and overlay composer editing, and semantic theme colors. Scriberig continues to own key/event normalization, modal state, domain view models, action identifiers, capability availability, and effect execution. The former fabricated change-review diff and locally duplicated session hierarchy palette were removed from the renderer. Change review now retains the exact candidate snapshot and shared before/after revision deltas, and the rendered review exposes those identities instead of listing only entity IDs.

The public RenderedProjection result supplies projection identity, semantic scope/revision, base snapshot, style, renderer, and bytes, but has no universal source-path or synchronization fields. docs.title: Current implementation note
docs.text:
The audited owners in this checkout are:

Concern Current owner Recursive durable session, branch, activity, plan and dependency state scriberig-session (Session, branch/activity, plan types) Safe model library and shared presentation preferences scriberig-app::agent_console; wire values in scriberig-protocol Local application operations and operation lifecycle scriberig-app::ApplicationService and OperationRegistry Session/plan wire serialization scriberig-protocol::session Remote calls, event cursor and cursor-expiry refresh scriberig-client and scriberig-tui::RemoteAdapter Local TUI session projection scriberig-tui service adapter and session/conversation models Browser wire normalization web/packages/client/src/session-views.ts Browser durable/transient state and event reduction web/packages/model/src/agent-workspace.ts and agent-workspace/events.ts Reusable agent rendering web/packages/agent-ui; integrated composition

The protocol already carried plan revision, goal, status, anchor, coordinator claim, plan history, node expected result/scope/claim/supersession and branch result handles. The TypeScript contract/normalizer dropped those fields, and the browser workspace did not retain plans. This task extends those existing owners. A single JSON fixture under tests/fixtures/ is now consumed by Rust protocol and TypeScript client tests. Event sequences are transport cursors; Rust remote recovery already refreshes known sessions after CursorTooOld, and the browser reducer now marks its state stale when an established cursor skips a sequence. Rust and TypeScript clients do not automatically retry state-changing requests. Remote TUI reconnect only issues event subscriptions and authoritative session reads; a continuation is submitted only by an explicit user/application command. The protocol has no durable key for a caller that manually retries after an ambiguous command timeout, so this guarantee covers reconnect and automatic retry behavior only.

State-changing requests are not automatically retried by the Rust/TypeScript clients. Plan lifecycle/assignment/replan operations use the plan revision compare-and-swap contract; candidate promotion uses the expected base snapshot. The reconnect regression test records every remote request and asserts that recovery performs only Subscribe requests. A caller manually resubmitting after an ambiguous timeout remains a separate invocation and is not deduplicated by a durable command key.

The local/remote operation conformance test now compares completed operation records containing candidate and validation evidence through both TUI service adapters. It exposed that terminal transitions synthesized an empty local progress record, which the remote mapping did not report. The shared app lifecycle now preserves absent progress; its regression test verifies that a terminal status does not fabricate progress data.

Focused verification completed for the current implementation:

cargo test -p scriberig-tui local_and_remote_session_adapters_share_semantics
cargo test -p scriberig-tui local_and_remote_operation_adapters_share_lifecycle_semantics
cargo test -p scriberig-tui local_and_remote_agent_capability_denial_share_semantics
cargo test -p scriberig-app terminal_transition_preserves_absent_progress
cargo test -p scriberig-tui local_and_remote_operation_adapters_share_lifecycle_semantics
cargo test -p scriberig-app terminal_transition_preserves_absent_progress
cargo test -p scriberig-tui local_and_remote_presentation_preferences_share_semantics
cargo test -p scriberig-tui remote_session_mapping_preserves_plan_results_and_assignments
cargo test -p scriberig-tui expired_event_cursor_replays_and_refreshes_known_sessions
cargo test -p scriberig-tui remote_errors_remain_categorized
