The source split keeps session-views.ts and session-plan-views.ts under the 400-line implementation limit. cargo fmt --all, Prettier on the changed web files, and git diff --check pass. Full workspace verification remains deferred until all tasks in the migration sequence are complete.

docs.title: 4. Task A — Define Cross-Surface Semantic Fixture Set
docs.text:
Create deterministic fixtures representing shared semantic/application state rather than terminal rows.

The minimum fixture sequence should cover:

session/root branch exists
human input
model invocation starts
provider-visible text/reasoning activity appears where allowed
semantic operation/tool invocation
operation result
child branch starts and completes with BranchResult
plan node blocked then ready/completed after dependency result
candidate/change created
validation completes
model completes
presentation preference changes

Fixtures may be Rust builders/serialized protocol fixtures/test helpers according to current repository conventions.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Fixtures use stable Scriberig identities/handles.
  • [x] Fixtures do not use terminal row numbers as identity.
  • [x] Fixtures do not contain hidden chain-of-thought.
  • [x] Fixtures can be consumed without a real provider/network service.
  • [x] Fixtures are deterministic/offline.

docs.title: 5. Task B — Prove Embedded and Remote TUI Semantic Equivalence
docs.text:
Run the same logical fixture/workflow through:

embedded/local application adapter
remote/client/protocol adapter

Compare the resulting Scriberig TUI state/projection at the semantic level.

Allowed differences:

  • connection/loading metadata;
  • latency/progress timing;
  • transport-specific error wrapping that maps to the same public error class.

Not allowed:

  • different branch/reply identity;
  • different plan/dependency state;
  • different candidate/base/result meaning;
  • different capability availability solely because one path has privileged internal access;

  • missing model/reasoning/tool visibility metadata required by the shared contract.

  • [x] Session tree/projection state matches semantically.

  • [x] Reply anchors match semantically.
  • [x] Plan/dependency status matches semantically.
  • [x] Model/profile/presentation preferences match semantically.
  • [x] Change/validation status matches semantically.
  • [x] Operation lifecycle matches semantically.

If a mismatch is found, fix the shared application/protocol/client boundary rather than adding a remote-only TUI special case.

docs.title: 6. Task C — Audit Event Ordering, Replay, and Reconnect
docs.text:
Determine the current protocol guarantees for ordered activity/event delivery and reconnect.

If the existing system already exposes exact durable session/activity sequence data sufficient for deterministic reconstruction, reuse it.

If a transport cursor is missing and reconnect currently risks gaps/duplicates, add the smallest shared protocol/application capability needed.

A transport cursor/sequence:

  • is not a session/branch/activity semantic identity;
  • may be retained by clients for replay position;
  • must detect gaps/too-old replay conditions;
  • may require authoritative state refresh when replay cannot continue.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Remote reconnect can reconstruct/refresh current presentation state without provider stream replay.
  • [x] Duplicate delivered observations do not duplicate durable semantic activity.
  • [x] Missing replay range triggers explicit refresh/resync behavior.
  • [x] Transport cursor is not used as reply anchor or plan-node identity.
  • [x] Reconnect does not silently execute a model/tool/application command.

docs.title: 7. Task D — Audit State-Changing Command Idempotency
docs.text:
The Level-1 study recommended command UUIDs because reconnect/retry must not duplicate semantic effects. Do not add another idempotency system if shared application operations already have equivalent operation/request identities.

Inspect current write paths for:

session input/continue
plan lifecycle commands
cancel/start operation
candidate validate
candidate apply/promote
projection reconcile
other TUI/web state-changing operations touched by this migration

For any command that can be retried across transport failure, confirm one of:

  1. it is naturally idempotent under exact-base semantics;
  2. it uses an existing application operation/idempotency identity;
  3. add a shared application/protocol idempotency contract.

Acceptance:

  • [x] A reconnect/retry fixture cannot duplicate a canonical mutation.
  • [x] Candidate apply preserves expected-base/compare-and-swap semantics.
  • [x] Session continuation cannot accidentally create two sibling continuations from one retry unless that is explicitly requested.
  • [x] TUI does not invent a local-only deduplication map as the sole correctness mechanism.

docs.title: 8. Task E — Reuse/Extend Shared Presentation Models
docs.text:
Compare what the migrated TUI needs with current shared scriberig-app/protocol agent-console and session models.

When a new cross-surface field is needed, place it in the smallest appropriate existing owner.

Examples that may already exist and must be reused if present:

model/profile library
thinking level
prompt visibility
reasoning visibility
model invocation detail
branch result
plan assignment/status
operation state

Acceptance:

  • [x] No duplicate TUI-only model/profile registry exists.
  • [x] No duplicate web-only branch/plan truth exists.
  • [x] Shared presentation preferences serialize/transport only where product requirements need cross-process persistence/visibility.
  • [x] Pure local UI state such as scroll/focus/expanded rows remains local and is not pushed into canonical session state.

docs.title: 9. Task F — Cross-Check the Integrated Web Surface
docs.text:
Use the current reusable web package hierarchy and integrated app. Do not create a second React application.

For each shared fixture, verify the web surface/model can represent the same semantic state needed for the corresponding workflow.

This task does not require pixel parity with terminal output.

Compare at least:

recursive branch hierarchy
plan status/dependencies
model/profile/thinking display
prompt/reasoning visibility controls where exposed
operation status
candidate/change/validation state
stable semantic selection/labels

If the web surface intentionally lacks one product capability, record the capability-matrix status rather than silently duplicating backend logic in JavaScript.

  • [x] Recursive session state can be represented from shared/protocol data.
  • [x] Plan/dependency state uses shared identities.
  • [x] Agent-console preferences use shared contract where product-exposed.
  • [x] Candidate/change/validation state is not re-derived from raw source text.
  • [x] Web model does not gain knowledge of rpi-tui/terminal types.

docs.title: 10. Task G — Add Cross-Surface Conformance Tests
docs.text:
Add the smallest maintainable conformance harness compatible with current repository structure.

Preferred strategy:

  1. build one shared logical fixture;
  2. feed it through the local Rust/TUI model path;
  3. serialize/deserialize through protocol where relevant;
  4. feed corresponding data through reusable TypeScript/web model/reducer tests;
  5. compare normalized semantic outputs/expectations.

Do not compare terminal glyph output to DOM markup.

Acceptance:

  • [x] At least one recursive-session fixture is checked in both Rust and TypeScript paths.
  • [x] At least one plan/dependency fixture is checked in both paths.
  • [x] At least one model/presentation-preference fixture is checked in both paths when web exposes it.
  • [x] At least one candidate/validation fixture is checked in both paths when both surfaces expose it.
  • [x] Protocol round-trip preserves stable IDs and exact status values.

docs.title: 11. Task H — Verify Local/Remote Security Boundaries
docs.text:
The remote client is untrusted presentation from the server's perspective.

Confirm:

  • server/application performs authorization/capability checks;
  • no arbitrary internal Rust method invocation is exposed;
  • no generic database mutation command exists for UI convenience;
  • no provider credential is serialized to clients;
  • hidden reasoning is not serialized as presentation detail;

  • external text stays data all the way to each renderer.

  • [x] TUI remote path has no privileged hidden mutation route.

  • [x] Web path has no privileged hidden mutation route.
  • [x] Credentials remain server/runtime secrets.
  • [x] Hidden reasoning remains absent.
  • [x] Capability denial is consistent across local/remote surfaces, subject only to explicitly represented local-only capabilities.

docs.title: 12. Focused Verification
docs.text:
Use focused tests for changed layers, for example:

cargo test -p scriberig-app agent_console
cargo test -p scriberig-app continuation
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol session
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol plan
cargo test -p scriberig-client session
cargo test -p scriberig-tui remote
cargo test -p scriberig-tui reconnect
pnpm --dir web test -- <focused test/filter supported by repository>

Use current package scripts rather than inventing unsupported commands.

  • [x] Shared app focused tests pass.
  • [x] Protocol round-trip focused tests pass.
  • [x] Client focused tests pass.
  • [x] Embedded/remote TUI conformance tests pass.
  • [x] Reconnect/idempotency focused tests pass.
  • [x] Relevant focused web tests pass.

Do not run the full repository gate yet.

docs.title: 13. Completion Gate
docs.text:
Before Complete:

  • [x] Confirm no new parallel scriberig-ui/UI backend architecture was added without a documented necessity.
  • [x] Confirm every new shared field has one clear owner.
  • [x] Confirm local and remote TUI produce semantically equivalent state for the conformance fixtures.
  • [x] Confirm web consumes shared/protocol semantics rather than terminal-specific structures.
  • [x] Confirm reconnect cannot silently replay state-changing operations.
  • [x] Confirm cursors/sequences remain transport/ordering concepts rather than semantic identity.
  • [x] Re-review every checkbox against focused verification evidence.
  • [x] Leave task 143 Not Started until this sheet is complete.

Then set:

**Status: [x] Complete**

docs.title: Harden Terminal Recovery, Upstream Maintenance, Cleanup, and Release Gates
docs.text:
Superseded as final acceptance: Level-2 plan 032 supersedes the ownership target of Level-2 plan 031, and tasks 144–149 supersede this task's final migration acceptance. This document remains historical evidence for work completed during the earlier vendored rpi-tui adoption. Do not use its vendor-maintenance or terminal-kit criteria to preserve local commodity ownership; complete the corrective deletion and delegation work under tasks 144–149.

Status: [~] In Progress

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
Finish the rpi-tui adoption program after tasks 138 through 142 are complete.

This task removes temporary migration scaffolding, proves terminal lifecycle robustness and hostile-input handling, establishes a reproducible upstream-update process, and runs the final repository quality gate.

The implementation is not complete merely because the new UI looks correct in a normal terminal.

Final acceptance must prove:

  • one terminal lifecycle owner;
  • recovery on normal/error/panic/cancel paths;
  • safe rendering of untrusted content;
  • responsive resize/streaming behavior;
  • preserved Scriberig semantic ownership;
  • local/remote conformance;
  • reproducible vendor provenance;
  • no unexplained legacy renderer duplication;
  • complete repository validation.

docs.title: 2.1 Read before editing
docs.text:
• [x] Read root AGENTS.md.
  • [x] Read design/AGENTS.md.
  • [x] Read nearest instructions for every crate/tool/test directory modified.
  • [x] Read Level-1 documents 014, 015, and 022.
  • [x] Read Level-2 documents 012, 014, 021, 022, 031.
  • [x] Read all implementation notes and completed checklists in tasks 138 through 142.
  • [x] Inspect UPSTREAM.md, PATCHES.md, license/notices, Cargo dependency tree, and all temporary feature flags/compatibility modules introduced during migration.
  • [x] Inspect current repository final-gate commands in root AGENTS.md; use current commands if they changed.

docs.title: 2.2 Checklist discipline
docs.text:
• [x] Keep this file open through final validation.
  • [x] Tick only after exact criterion plus verification.
  • [x] Tick immediately, not in one final batch.
  • [x] If cleanup or final validation breaks an earlier criterion, uncheck it here and in the owning earlier sheet when appropriate; the final audit found no invalidated criterion.
  • [x] Record the retained Ratatui structural renderer with its reason, owner, and follow-up.
  • [x] Re-read all six adoption sheets before declaring the program complete.

docs.title: 2.3 Do not
docs.text:
• hide failing lifecycle tests behind ignored tests;
  • silence actionable compiler/Clippy warnings;
  • disable repository lint rules to land the migration;
  • remove attribution during cleanup;
  • leave two terminal runtime paths active without an explicit supported reason;
  • add unsafe raw ANSI shortcuts for performance;
  • broaden clipboard/image/plugin authority during hardening;
  • change semantic/session/change behavior merely to make a terminal golden test pass;
  • mark this task Complete while any final gate is failing.

docs.title: 3. Task A — Terminal Lifecycle Recovery
docs.text:
Exercise and harden the active terminal lifecycle implementation.

Verify restoration behavior for at least:

normal quit
Ctrl-C/requested shutdown
application error returned from event/effect loop
panic inside a controlled test harness where recovery hook/guard can run
remote disconnect causing UI error/recovery
resize during active rendering

The exact terminal modes depend on the adopted implementation, but restoration should include applicable state such as:

raw mode
alternate screen
cursor visibility
bracketed paste
keyboard enhancement modes
mouse capture if enabled

Acceptance:

  • [x] Normal exit restores terminal state.
  • [x] Error exit restores terminal state.
  • [x] Cancellation/shutdown restores terminal state.
  • [x] Panic recovery guard/hook is covered by the safest deterministic test possible without masking real panics.
  • [x] Recovery is idempotent enough that double-drop/double-cleanup does not panic.
  • [x] Terminal lifecycle code does not perform semantic mutations during cleanup.

docs.title: 4. Task B — Resize, Width, Unicode, and Large-Content Stress Fixtures
docs.text:
Create/extend deterministic rendering tests for:

very narrow terminal
very short terminal
repeated resize sequence
wide terminal
nested branch depth
CJK/wide characters
combining marks
emoji where supported by current width library
very long unbroken token
large Markdown block
large code block
long operation/tool diagnostic
large plan/session tree with bounded rendering

Acceptance:

  • [x] No arithmetic underflow/overflow/panic on minimum-size rectangles.
  • [x] Resize preserves semantic selection/reply anchor.
  • [x] Rendering remains bounded to requested viewport/visible rows.
  • [x] Unicode width handling is deterministic for tested fixtures.
  • [x] Long tokens/Markdown do not cause unbounded allocation in one frame beyond reasonable fixture expectations.
  • [x] Large tree tests exercise scrolling/virtual/bounded rendering rather than drawing the entire world unnecessarily.

docs.title: 5. Task C — Hostile Terminal-Content Test Corpus
docs.text:
Create one reusable test corpus for untrusted strings used across conversation and auxiliary renderers.

Include at least:

ANSI CSI color/control sequences
OSC hyperlinks
OSC clipboard sequences
BEL
ESC-only/incomplete escape strings
carriage-return/backspace tricks
NUL and other controls where Rust strings can represent them
malformed Markdown nesting
malformed/fenced code content
terminal-width edge strings

Normal renderer behavior may visibly escape, replace, or safely render these values as text according to the kit contract. The test must prove they are not passed through as trusted terminal commands.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Conversation renderer passes hostile corpus.
  • [x] Tool/operation result renderer passes hostile corpus.
  • [x] Projection/source renderer passes hostile corpus.
  • [x] Error/diagnostic renderer passes hostile corpus.
  • [x] Palette/help labels cannot inject terminal controls from external labels.
  • [x] No convenience raw_ansi(external_string)-style path remains reachable from untrusted data.

docs.title: 6. Task D — Clipboard, Image, and Privileged Presentation Audit
docs.text:
Audit final code for privileged terminal features.

Initial release policy from this plan remains:

clipboard: explicit user action + policy
images: disabled
native upstream plugins: not adopted
raw terminal control: trusted renderer code only

Acceptance:

  • [x] No OS clipboard read/write integration is wired. Bracketed paste enters as an explicit terminal paste event, and the TUI-kit policy rejects clipboard access unless an explicit user action is supplied; policy cases are covered by terminal_policy_disables_images_and_requires_clipboard_action.
  • [x] No rendering/focus/hover path reads the clipboard automatically.
  • [x] Image-support feature is disabled/not wired into production behavior.
  • [x] No upstream plugin loader was introduced.
  • [x] Any terminal title/hyperlink feature is produced from trusted structured data with escaping/validation.

docs.title: 7. Task E — Remove Temporary Migration Duplication
docs.text:
Inventory all compatibility code introduced by tasks 138 through 142:

legacy Ratatui renderer feature/path
old editor implementation
old Markdown renderer
old selection/fuzzy helper
old theme mapping
temporary conversion types
temporary dual event adapters
duplicate tests/fixtures

For each item choose one:

  1. remove because the new path fully replaces it;
  2. keep because another supported surface still needs it, with a comment/doc explaining the owner;
  3. defer removal with an explicit issue/task reference and non-default status.

Do not keep dead code solely for emotional rollback comfort; version control is the historical rollback mechanism once the new path passes acceptance.

Acceptance:

  • [x] No duplicate default terminal runtime exists.
  • [x] Superseded editor/Markdown/selection code is removed.
  • [x] Direct Ratatui dependency is removed if no supported final code requires it; otherwise its remaining role is explicitly documented.
  • [x] Direct Crossterm ownership is coherent with the TUI-kit/upstream lifecycle boundary.
  • [x] No temporary feature flag is left default-on accidentally.
  • [x] cargo tree -p scriberig-tui -d has no unexplained terminal-stack duplication.

Ratatui remains the integrated structural frame renderer and Crossterm backend because Scriberig still composes the complete application shell and semantic views through its existing render tree. The adopted rpi-tui code is reused through scriberig-tui-kit for generic terminal components and text safety; it does not own Scriberig layout, state, or event lifecycle.

There is no legacy migration renderer or compatibility adapter left. The remaining Ratatui renderer is owned by scriberig-tui because the current product shell still uses its structural frame API. No removal follow-up is scheduled; revisit that boundary only through a separate design task if the upstream presentation API later supports the complete Scriberig shell.

docs.title: 8. Task F — Upstream Update Procedure
docs.text:
Make vendor maintenance reproducible.

third_party/rpi-tui/UPSTREAM.md and/or repository tooling must explain the update process:

1. choose new exact upstream commit
2. inspect license/security/relevant release changes
3. compare old pinned tree to new tree
4. reapply documented Scriberig patches deliberately
5. update UPSTREAM.md SHA/date
6. update PATCHES.md
7. run TUI-kit focused tests
8. run TUI focused tests
9. review terminal dependency versions/Crossterm coherence
10. commit the vendor update separately where practical

Optionally add a small repository tool/check that verifies recorded provenance against a vendored manifest/hash inventory if that fits current tooling conventions. Do not require network access in ordinary CI merely to prove a pin exists.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Another engineer/agent can understand how to update the vendor from repository documentation alone.
  • [x] Exact old/new upstream revisions remain discoverable in Git history/provenance files.
  • [x] Local patches are not hidden in an undocumented copied source tree.
  • [x] Ordinary CI remains deterministic/offline with respect to the vendored source.

docs.title: 9. Task G — Architectural Drift Audit
docs.text:
Review final dependencies and code paths against Scriberig invariants.

Prove:

  • sessions remain recursive Scriberig session knowledge;
  • plans remain structured Scriberig plan knowledge with separate dependency DAG;
  • parent context uses BranchResults rather than child transcript display expansion;
  • provider continuation remains branch-local runtime state;
  • prompt/reasoning visibility remains presentation-only;
  • semantic/domain edits still use candidate/migration/validation/promotion;
  • TUI and web remain clients of shared application semantics;
  • upstream TUI code owns presentation mechanics only.

Acceptance:

  • [x] No upstream session identity is used as Scriberig identity; the scriberig-tui-kit public API exposes no upstream session type, and the rpi-tui dependency is presentation-only.
  • [x] No upstream agent/tool loop is in the dependency graph; cargo tree -p scriberig-tui -e normal -i rpi-tui shows only the TUI kit as its consumer, while upstream tool components are renderers and no agent runtime dependency exists in the vendored crate manifest.
  • [x] No TUI direct database mutation path exists; TUI service operations depend on application/service interfaces, with no SQLite crate in the TUI manifest or direct store calls in its implementation.
  • [x] No TUI direct file-write path was introduced for understood domains; the only filesystem writes in the TUI are the opt-in diagnostic log, while semantic candidate promotion is delegated to the shared application workflow.
  • [x] No presentation setting affects context/execution semantics; shared prompt and reasoning preferences are applied in the presentation reducer, and runtime context compilation consumes explicit branch/context inputs.
  • [x] No expanded transcript is implicitly fed back into parent context; runtime context compilation admits anchored activities and compact BranchResult values, and plan dependencies add results without branch transcripts.

docs.title: 10. Task H — Focused End-to-End Scenarios
docs.text:
Before the repository-wide gate, run focused native terminal scenarios/harnesses covering at least:

start TUI with no session -> type first prompt
stream response with interleaved operation/tool activity
create/observe nested branch -> collapse/expand
move historical reply anchor -> continue
open plan/session auxiliary view
open semantic explorer/inspect view
review candidate + validation without direct mutation
remote disconnect/reconnect if supported by current test harness
quit and verify terminal restoration

Use deterministic fake provider/application fixtures where the repository provides them. Do not require a paid/external provider for acceptance.

  • [x] New-session scenario passes (tui_pty_starts_fresh_after_abandoned_conversation_and_gets_answer).
  • [x] Streaming/interleaving scenario passes (tui_golden_05_agent_uses_exact_semantic_scope_and_returns_compact_result observes semantic_find and semantic_render before the final response).
  • [x] Recursive branch/reply scenario passes (tui_pty_continues_from_a_historical_reply_anchor creates a child from the exact historical assistant anchor and expands/collapses it).
  • [x] Auxiliary semantic-view scenario passes (tui_pty_shows_a_session_plan_in_the_conversation_tree, Explorer/projection golden PTY tests, and saved-session/history PTY tests).
  • [x] Candidate/review scenario passes (tui_golden_03_edits_reviews_applies_and_restarts).
  • [x] Remote reconnect scenario passes when supported (expired_event_cursor_replays_and_refreshes_known_sessions uses the deterministic remote service harness).
  • [x] Terminal restoration scenario passes (tui_pty_quits_with_ctrl_c verifies restoration after process exit; Task A also covers normal and error exits).

docs.title: 11. Task I — Final Repository Gate
docs.text:
Only after every implementation checkbox above and tasks 138 through 142 are complete, run the current repository-wide final gate from root AGENTS.md.

At the time this plan was written, the gate included commands equivalent to:

python3 tools/lint_repo.py --fix
cargo fmt --all
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

pnpm --dir web typecheck

Also run the repository's current full relevant tests according to CI/project conventions; do not invent or omit required commands because this list became stale.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Repository lint passes after its allowed fixes are reviewed.
  • [x] Rust formatting passes.
  • [x] Workspace Rust check passes.
  • [x] Workspace Clippy passes with warnings denied.
  • [ ] Relevant Rust tests pass.
  • [x] Web formatting passes.
  • [x] Web typecheck passes.
  • [x] Relevant web tests/build checks required by current CI pass.
  • [x] No generated/untracked accidental vendor artifacts remain; the temporary upstream intake checkout and migration helper directories were removed, while the reviewed vendor source and provenance files remain.

The isolated cargo test -p scriberig-tui suite passed (231 tests). The previously blocked localhost transport test also passed on retry. A later full workspace run exhausted C: while a validation-failure PTY tried to stage its temporary checkout. The two validation-failure PTYs then passed when their temporary files were redirected to E:. The next full workspace run used D: for Cargo artifacts and E: for PTY temporary files, but was stopped at the user's request while the 27-test native PTY suite was running; 35 application tests and 2 secrets CLI tests had passed. The full Rust test gate remains unverified, so keep this item and Level-2 final acceptance unchecked until a complete workspace test run is authorized and passes.

If a final gate exposes a real defect, fix it and uncheck any earlier criterion invalidated by the fix until reverified.

docs.title: Stop Local Commodity Ownership and Establish Upstream Contribution Gates
docs.text:
Status: [x] Complete

Historical upstream integration note (2026-10-21, superseded by §12.8): ScribeRig then pinned controlled fork commit b2fc63c78ae85044eb78e7ac9af184bd7fbfbc95, based on official bigfish1913/pi-rust 0.7.1 main 281dfddfa39ac063d86de57b75370974c4d75e6c. The upstream advancement since 0.7.0 adds the CLI web-startup guard and release metadata; the rpi libraries consumed by ScribeRig compile at the merged pin. The controlled fork retains its model-runtime, catalog, transactional config, stream lifecycle, TUI event/focus and keybinding extractions. The latest fork commits also expose TuiAltScreen::run_until_with_tick and upstream theme preset metadata so ScribeRig's application event/effect work and theme choices use upstream APIs. The 0.7.1 merge had one workspace dependency-version conflict, resolved by retaining the fork-only rpi-model-runtime workspace crate at the new workspace version. Revision-specific inventories below were inspected at earlier fork commits and are historical where APIs have moved. The provider ABI now lives in rpi-plugin-sdk; package lifecycle APIs live in rpi-extensions; rpi-model-runtime remains the model/configuration boundary. Earlier test-target compilation and app/agent-runtime checks were performed at prior pins. At that pin, focused cargo check -p scriberig-tui --lib --locked compiled rpi-tui but stopped on then-uncommitted task 151 calls to TreeList::items and TreeList::replace_items, which were not yet present at that revision. The TUI compile was therefore unverified there and no test binaries were executed. The later pin adds both APIs; §12.8 records the current state.

Begin the correction defined by design/level-2/032. upstream first agent runtime and terminal product ownership correction.md.

This task does not yet replace large production subsystems. It creates the authoritative ownership/deletion map, freezes further local duplication, and identifies every generic capability that must be consumed from or contributed to upstream before later tasks proceed.

docs.title: 12.1 Authority and classification key
docs.text:
Level 2 032 is the current target and supersedes the ownership target in 023, 025, 031, and older task notes where they assign generic provider, model, loop, or terminal framework ownership to ScribeRig. Level 1 semantic invariants remain controlling. No production subsystem is rewritten by task 144.

The classifications below expand the task sheet's U/S/A shorthand:

  • KEEP — ScribeRig semantic ownership (S): semantic contracts and durable ScribeRig state remain canonical.
  • ADAPTER — thin bridge from ScribeRig semantics to upstream (A): translate ScribeRig operation/context/capability values to upstream calls and results.
  • DELETE — duplicate commodity implementation (U): remove after the listed upstream consumer/API is available.
  • UPSTREAM GAP: generic capability is absent or trapped in a product binary; upstream work gates the consumer task.
  • TEMPORARY: bounded compatibility code with a named removal condition. No temporary exception is authorized by this audit.

Freeze: do not add a local model/provider/thinking catalog, provider auth registry, model property schema, generic provider transport, ordinary agent loop, plugin/package host, terminal lifecycle, generic widget/editor/Markdown/ selector/theme framework, or Ratatui shell. An upstream gap is not permission to implement a permanent ScribeRig substitute.

docs.text:
This detailed inventory was written against the previous fork pin bad1c5b4aa6f26cc231168d75a09165e990de39a. Its revision-specific entries are historical where APIs have since moved. The active pin is now b2fc63c78ae85044eb78e7ac9af184bd7fbfbc95; the focused source revalidation below is authoritative for present ownership.

Capability Status at pinned source Evidence and decision Model type and model-specific properties Typed model fields, extension option transport, and versioned applied-settings reporting are reusable; generic complete request provenance remains incomplete At baseline revision aab74de0737f4b7c454cd8c8c16ca66e4dfbf898, crates/rpi-ai/src/model.rs exposes typed cost/context/output, sampling, headers, compatibility, and thinking properties. Current ScribeRig pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5 carries ModelDefinition.provider_options into runtime Model; built-in provider behavior remains constrained by provider-declared support and validation. The extension ABI accepts an opt-in providerOptionsVersion: 1 declaration and sends {version: 1, values: ...} only to opted-in extensions; legacy extensions reject non-empty options. Its versioned applied-settings callback can report a provider's attested final settings; providers without that ABI path return an incomplete report. This is transport/reporting, not evidence that catalog metadata alone proves application. Malformed/unsupported versions reject registration. Runtime Model serialization omits options and its Debug output redacts them; config serialization retains them for round-trip. Current ScribeRig native extension activation fails closed, and the fork fingerprint excludes headers and provider_options, so it is not complete provenance. Provider implementations and streaming Reusable now, including protected request secrets and applied-settings callbacks for selected built-ins crates/rpi-ai/src/provider.rs exposes Provider, RequestSecret, SecretMaterial, AppliedRequestSettings, and combined secret/report methods. OpenAI Completions, Responses, and Anthropic prepare reports from their final transformed bodies and expose protected-secret forwarding in their provider modules. Reports contain an allowlisted projection and remain complete: false because transport headers, credentials, opaque options, prompts, tools, and other request categories are omitted. Provider package ABI runtime Reusable now for package execution, not catalog/auth Workspace package packages/provider-runtime (src/lib.rs) bridges provider packages through the plugin ABI and reuses rpi-ai providers. It does not implement provider discovery, credential resolution, model catalog refresh, or selector APIs. Ordinary agent/tool loop Reusable now crates/rpi-agent/src/agent_loop.rs, agent.rs, agent_tool.rs, public exports in lib.rs expose model/tool execution and tool schema/validation/stream/cancel behavior. It does not own ScribeRig session identity or branch semantics. rpi-tui runtime/components Reusable and consumed for lifecycle, event dispatch, rendering, editor, selectors, property editor, overlays, themes, and generic components At pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, crates/rpi-tui/src/lib.rs, component.rs, tui.rs, tui_alt_screen.rs, terminal.rs, and component modules expose Component::handle_event, typed InputEvent, TuiAltScreen::dispatch_input/note_resize/run_until, callback-based terminal input, editor, Markdown, selectors, overlays, themes, TreeList, PropertyEditor, ScrollView, HStack, VStack, and Container. ScribeRig's active terminal lifecycle and presentation use these APIs; only semantic projections/reducers and the thin input adapter remain local. Plugin ABI and extension host Reusable now, with limited UI seam and versioned applied-settings callback crates/rpi-plugin-sdk/src/lib.rs defines stable FFI/runtime actions and the versioned provider applied-settings callback; crates/rpi-extensions/src/provider.rs forwards protected credentials to opt-in providers, validates safe reports, and emits an incomplete v1 fallback after settlement. crates/rpi-extensions also provides host, registry, provider manifests and panel.rs structured text panels. UiComponent supports text lifecycle/content, not arbitrary native rpi-tui::Component registration. Model catalog storage/reconciliation Reusable upstream API exists; host discovery and refresh composition remain incomplete At current pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, rpi-model-runtime::ModelCatalog provides shared snapshots, provider replacement/reconciliation, subscriptions, ordered reconciliation, transactional configuration publication, and flat reconcile_models. ScribeRig wraps/shares this API through ApplicationService. The reviewed fork's host-neutral built-in provider factory binds provider/API/model identities and is consumed by configured root, plan-worker, one-shot, and doctor paths. CLI registry/configuration policy remains CLI-owned; ScribeRig separately composes explicitly trusted extensions. Package lifecycle, dynamic provider/catalog refresh, and runtime-factory reload remain open. Provider discovery/catalog refresh Built-in catalog/provider composition is reusable; native extensions are blocked pending isolation ScribeRig resolves configured built-in models through the upstream model catalog/factory. It currently rejects SCRIBE_AGENT_EXTENSION_DIRS and SCRIBE_AGENT_PACKAGE_ROOTS before loading native libraries; no provider manifests are merged and no PluggableProvider executes. Package install/update/link and atomic extension session/catalog reload remain upstream lifecycle work. Credential precedence, protected resolution, and readiness Reusable upstream API exists; host source access remains caller-owned At pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, rpi-model-runtime exposes credential source precedence, ProtectedCredentialResolver::{resolve, resolve_with_policy}, resolve_credential_protected_with_policy, and readiness_from_catalog. ScribeRig does not use upstream source precedence because it selects one host-authorized SecretRef; its protected bridge resolves only after the exact model endpoint is fixed and passes material through RequestSecret. Active built-in paths capture versioned applied-settings reports into durable request projections; reports remain incomplete and omit sensitive/opaque categories. Native extension provider reports are not active while the host rejects in-process plugin loading. Native readiness combines upstream catalog classification with host endpoint authorization and reports credential availability, not provider acceptance. rpi-cli::credentials::resolve continues to delegate CLI source precedence to rpi_model_runtime::resolve_credential; package and CLI settings policy remains composition-owned. Provider discovery and runtime construction CLI-coupled; extraction only if another host needs the full composition crates/rpi-cli/src/provider.rs resolves provider/model/auth using config.rs, settings.rs, extension manifests, and CLI runtime factories. rpi-model-runtime supplies reusable model catalog construction and credential/readiness policies, but this CLI path still binds flags/defaults, provider filtering, extension sessions, and concrete source resolvers. Do not classify credential precedence or safe readiness as missing upstream APIs. Provider/model/thinking selectors Generic selector widgets reusable now; CLI orchestration remains product-specific Pinned rpi-tui exposes SelectItem, SelectList, and SearchableSelectList. The rpi-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs and settings.rs functions are pub(super) because they combine CLI catalog matching, authentication/default persistence, and AgentLane updates; do not extract that policy as generic UI. ScribeRig adapts safe model rows to the upstream widgets and keeps assignment effects local. Selector focused-event integration is a Task147 migration detail, not a missing generic selector extraction. Thinking-level names and parsing Reusable from the selected fork commit rpi-ai::ThinkingLevel exposes canonical ORDERED, as_str(), and parse_name() at current fork pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5. Model::supported_thinking_levels() and clamp_thinking_level() provide model support and clamping. Provider serialization remains owned by upstream provider implementations. Package install/update/link/reload Registry and artifact operations are reusable; activation blocked on isolation and build/reload extraction ScribeRig currently rejects native extension roots before load_session. The pinned rpi-extensions package library supplies project registry and prebuilt-artifact operations, while rpi-cli/src/packages.rs retains Cargo build/update acquisition, command policy, and live session/catalog replacement. ScribeRig has no local duplicate package manager. Generic model-property configuration/editor Typed properties, schema-safe editor metadata, validated setter, and file-backed persistence are reusable; complete provenance remains incomplete The inspected fork API exposes ModelPropertyDescriptor, is_safe_for_generic_editor, set_model_property, update_model_config_property, ModelsConfigFile, and rpi_tui::PropertyEditor. ScribeRig's native settings flow uses these APIs and reconciles the shared model catalog after persisted edits. The host chooses the file path and authorizes the edit. Environment JSON and extension-only rows without a matching ModelsConfig entry remain read-only; undeclared/opaque options are not given a ScribeRig schema. Safe model fingerprints still do not establish complete effective-request provenance. Provider continuation Reusable upstream contract present; ScribeRig integration is partial At pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, rpi-ai::ProviderContinuation carries opaque provider/model-scoped state and provider extraction/consumption methods; rpi-agent exposes callbacks and a continuation setter. OpenAI Responses implements the provider path. ScribeRig consumes this for root turns with process-local cache and context checks; child/plan-worker scope and stale/reseed/cancel/expiry/restart/replay acceptance remain incomplete. Do not duplicate the wire-level handle contract locally. Generic tree/virtualized hierarchy/table/resizable split TreeList reusable; data-source table and interactive split remain upstream gaps if required At pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, rpi-tui::TreeList supplies stable caller IDs, parent/child hierarchy, selection, expansion, keyboard navigation, and bounded visible rows; ScrollView clips/scrolls and H/V composition is static. No generic data-source table, item virtualization API, controlled replacement/grouping-node support, or interactive resizable split component was found. Use existing upstream primitives for semantic projections; contribute the reusable missing primitives before considering a local substitute. Plugin-native arbitrary TUI component registration Conditional upstream feature Existing extension text panel API may suffice for textual plugin contributions. If third-party native panels are required, add registration/lifecycle seam between rpi-plugin-sdk/rpi-extensions and rpi-tui::Component; not needed for built-in ScribeRig semantic panels. rpi-harness session/task model Not needed by ScribeRig Do not adopt as canonical session, branch, plan, or identity model.

Current implementation note: the active upstream branch adapter now installs the pinned provider AppliedRequestSettingsCallback, serializes the safe upstream report without interpreting its schema, and stores it on the durable ModelRequestProjection. The existing authorized model-request detail operation carries that opaque report to clients. This supersedes earlier rows above that said ScribeRig did not consume the applied-settings callback. The report remains explicitly incomplete when upstream says so; it does not prove that all request-affecting settings were captured. The former native extension path consumed the versioned providerOptions ABI, but current ScribeRig activation fails closed before loading native code. The generic upstream model-property editor and validated persistence contract are now consumed by ScribeRig's settings flow; provider-specific support remains subject to upstream schemas and validation.

docs.title: 12.4 Upstream contribution and extraction gates
docs.text:
Upstream issues #67 and #68 and the associated fork drafts are contribution work in progress, not accepted upstream APIs. This gate audit was written at fork commit 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5; ScribeRig now pins b2fc63c78ae85044eb78e7ac9af184bd7fbfbc95. The audit-era gate descriptions below retain their original revision evidence. The active source revalidation in §12.7 is authoritative where path/API status or ownership has changed. The reviewed source provides rpi-model-runtime/src/provider_factory.rs with host-neutral built-in provider construction; rpi-ai protected request-secret and applied-settings forwarding for OpenAI Completions, Responses, Anthropic, and the extension ABI; versioned extension applied-settings attestation with an explicitly incomplete fallback; and rpi-tui::TuiAltScreen::run_until plus focused event/lifecycle APIs. The active CLI, root, and plan-worker paths use the upstream provider/agent boundary. ScribeRig rejects configured native provider-extension roots before the in-process rpi-extensions loader, so their manifests are not merged and PluggableProvider is not instantiated. Provider reports are captured as opaque data inside each durable ModelRequestProjection and exposed by the existing authorized detail operation. The report is intentionally partial: it projects approved values observed at the provider request boundary and excludes secrets, opaque options, and other request categories. Catalog/configuration metadata does not prove application. No ScribeRig-owned catalog authority or provider-property schema is authorized.

Gate Capability / upstream owner Required public boundary Current limitation Removal/consumer condition G1 Model catalog, provider discovery/configuration; rpi-model-runtime Host-configurable registry/catalog construction and provider resolution returning upstream Model/provider references, independent of CLI config ScribeRig pins 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5 (rpi-model-runtime/src/{models,catalog,live_catalog,selection,provider_factory}.rs). It consumes ModelsConfig, build_catalog, resolve_selection, and safe_model_snapshot; the latter supplies safe display projections, but copies configured provider/model/API identifiers and display names verbatim and is not a general secret scrubber. Treat those configured fields as public metadata and never put credentials in them. The pinned fork also provides provider_factory::{create_builtin_provider, create_builtin_provider_for_api, supports_builtin_provider_api}; configured built-in root, plan-worker, one-shot, and doctor paths bind exact resolved models to this factory. The factory does not select extension providers or apply CLI configuration/auth/package policy. safe_model_execution_configuration is explicitly partial (complete == false), omits endpoint/headers/opaque options, and is not a complete execution record or request-equivalence proof. Native extension activation is currently rejected before rpi-extensions::load_session; provider manifests and PluggableProvider are not consumed by ScribeRig until upstream supplies isolated worker execution. Package install/update/reload and provider/catalog refresh remain open upstream lifecycle work. Task 145 consumes pinned catalog/selection and built-in provider-factory APIs. Extension activation and provider/catalog refresh remain follow-up work. Do not treat partial model configuration or applied-settings reports as a complete effective-request fingerprint. G2 Credentials/auth/readiness and applied-settings reporting; rpi-model-runtime + rpi-ai request boundary ScribeRig resolves credentials only after destination authorization, keeps references/material host-owned, passes request-only secrets without exposing them through cloneable/string options, and records safe applied settings with truthful completeness; readiness remains a safe projection At the current pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, protected credential and readiness APIs are present. Configured one-shot, native root, plan-worker, and doctor built-in requests bind the exact resolved model endpoint to the host CredentialProvider adapter and pass material only through RequestSecret; catalog auth headers/credentials are rejected. The duplicate runtime ProviderConfig and CredentialSource wrappers are removed; app configuration carries upstream rpi_ai::Model, while the host credential adapter remains for ScribeRig's explicit SecretRef authorization policy. Upstream built-in providers expose versioned applied-settings callbacks on active paths; PluggableProvider support is currently unused because native extension activation fails closed. upstream_invocation.rs captures the callback's sanitized report in ModelRequestProjection.applied_settings; the existing durable invocation and authorized request-detail paths carry it to history consumers. The report is explicitly partial and omits credentials, headers, prompt, tools, and opaque fields. Native readiness combines upstream catalog classification with host endpoint authorization and reports credential availability, not provider acceptance. Distinct per-connection credential references and auth-response classification are not represented. ScribeRig consumes protected credential and applied-settings boundaries for active built-in paths. Keep complete effective-request fingerprinting, focused persistence/omission verification, distinct per-connection credential source support, and provider-auth acceptance/readiness refresh open. Never use ordinary-string AuthStore, SimpleStreamOptions.api_key, model headers, or plugin JSON for secret material. G3 Reusable model/provider/thinking controls; model identity selection in rpi-model-runtime, thinking conversion in rpi-ai Public selection accepts an upstream model catalog and request identity, returning the unique catalog index and upstream-supported/clamped thinking level. Canonical thinking parse/name/order lives on rpi-ai::ThinkingLevel. Generic terminal selection UI is reusable independently of CLI model/auth policy. At current pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, ScribeRig consumes resolve_selection and canonical thinking conversion. The prior 3ae8416ceaf2dcdbf853b03c7b4662ad832497cf reference is historical and is not the current dependency. rpi-tui exposes SelectItem, SelectList, and SearchableSelectList; rpi-cli selector orchestration additionally encodes CLI alias/auth/default and runtime mutation semantics and is not a generic UI API. Task 147 adapts ScribeRig safe rows to generic upstream selectors. No CLI selector extraction is required; only a concrete missing generic UI primitive found during migration should reopen this gate. Do not recreate a ScribeRig thinking catalog. G4 Package install/update/link/reload; rpi-extensions plus extraction from rpi-cli where needed Reusable project registry and artifact lifecycle functions, with project root and trust policy supplied by the host At the inspected fork pin, rpi-extensions/src/packages.rs owns project registry read/write, registered resource-dir resolution, activation of an already-built artifact, and uninstall. provider_reload.rs supplies reload predicates/provider composition only. rpi-cli/src/packages.rs still owns current-directory selection, Cargo metadata/build, link/update acquisition and rebuild orchestration, command policy, and live extension reload/session/catalog replacement. The former ScribeRig ProviderExtensions::from_environment path called package_resource_dirs and load_session, but this in-process activation is now rejected because no upstream isolation boundary protects canonical ScribeRig storage. It does not read or mutate the project package registry. Repository inspection found no ScribeRig package manager or duplicate registry/install/update/reload implementation to delete. Conditional on an explicit ScribeRig package-control product requirement. If added, authorize the exact project root in ScribeRig, use upstream read_project_registry/write_project_registry, project_package_resource_dirs, install_project_artifact, and uninstall_project_package; do not implement registry or artifact copying locally. Extract build/update acquisition and atomic isolated-session/catalog replacement from rpi-cli into a reusable upstream boundary before exposing those controls. No local package manager or lifecycle framework. G5 Generic model-specific property edit/config flow; upstream model/settings UI Property-preserving configuration API/editor over typed upstream model fields and provider-declared options, with upstream validation and path-parameterized persistence At current pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, rpi-model-runtime owns ModelsConfig/ModelDefinition, ModelPropertyDescriptor, is_safe_for_generic_editor, property setters, update_model_config_property, and ModelsConfigFile; pinned rpi-tui supplies PropertyEditor. ScribeRig's native settings flow consumes those APIs, projects safe descriptor fields into upstream editor items, validates and persists through upstream APIs, and reconciles the upstream ModelCatalog. It returns descriptors only for an exact model row in file-backed config, preventing read-only rows from opening the editor. The host selects the config path and authorizes the edit operation. Environment JSON and extension-only models without a matching config row remain read-only; arbitrary/undeclared options are not writable. Effective-request provenance for property changes remains incomplete. The reusable editor/persistence boundary is implemented and consumed. Keep this gate's effective-request fingerprint and unknown-property flow unchecked until canonical provenance and future-property semantics are verified. Do not add a ScribeRig property schema or validator. G6 Generic TreeView/virtualized hierarchy/table/split/panel; rpi-tui Reusable accessible/focusable component APIs with virtualization/selection as needed and interactive split resizing where required At active pin ebcf8d5e75d20fa3a6cc7cc76cbcdcec4cc36eb8, rpi_tui::TreeList supports stable caller IDs, parent links, selection, expansion, keyboard navigation, bounded visible rows, items(), and validated replace_items(). The API still has no grouping-node filtering, generic data-source table, or resizable split pane. Collapse hides every descendant. Current ScribeRig session and plan views construct upstream TreeList from ScribeRig semantic rows; activity-only collapse projection remains a ScribeRig view requirement. ScrollView clips/scrolls; H/V composition is static. Task 148 should continue adapting upstream TreeList to ScribeRig's semantic rows where stable IDs and reducer-owned expansion are preserved. Contribute any remaining reusable grouping/control or split/table capability upstream before adding generic local widgets. No ScribeRig widget fallback. G9 Focused-component input/event dispatch and resize forwarding; rpi-tui Public host callback/event receiver routes normalized events to the focused component and forwards resize notifications while upstream owns terminal setup and lifecycle. Preserve an explicit event type and host-facing dispatch method; Component::handle_input(&str) alone is insufficient for structured events. At current pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, Component::handle_event, TuiAltScreen::dispatch_input/note_resize, callback-based focused dispatch, reader shutdown/join handling, and TuiAltScreen::run_until are present and consumed by the active runtime. scriberig-tui-kit and vendored rpi-tui are absent. ScribeRig retains semantic reducers/projections and a Crossterm-backed event adapter; no production Ratatui renderer is present. Remaining task 147/149 work concerns semantic panels, theme/PTY/golden acceptance, and cleanup, not local terminal lifecycle or a retained widget kit. Keep upstream lifecycle and dispatch ownership. Review and remove any residual direct Crossterm/event adapter coupling only after the upstream event contract supports the current ScribeRig action semantics. Do not recreate local terminal lifecycle/rendering. G7 Provider continuation mechanics; rpi-ai and continuation-aware rpi-agent on the controlled TNick/pi-rust fork rpi_ai::ProviderContinuation carries in-memory opaque state scoped to provider/model without serialization or debug disclosure. Provider::continuation_from_response extracts it; stream_simple_with_continuation and stream_simple_with_continuation_and_applied_settings consume it. AgentBuilder::{cancellable_provider_continuation,on_provider_continuation} and Agent::set_provider_continuation provide the upstream loop seam. ScribeRig separately owns branch association, context-fingerprint validity, stale/reseed/cancel/expiry policy, and replay recovery. ScribeRig pins 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5 in Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock; this revision contains the rpi-ai contract in crates/rpi-ai/src/provider.rs, the rpi-agent seam in crates/rpi-agent/src/agent.rs and agent_loop.rs, and an OpenAI Responses implementation in crates/rpi-ai/src/providers/openai_responses.rs. ScribeRig wires the seam in crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/upstream_invocation.rs and provider_stream.rs. apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/runner.rs keeps opaque handles only in a process-local root-branch cache and checks provider/model/profile/thinking identity plus the completed root context fingerprint; upstream_execution/mod.rs rechecks the compiled context fingerprint and scope before use. No durable provider handle is stored, so restart naturally reseeds from ScribeRig context. This does not establish child/plan-worker continuation support, expiry/invalidation policy, or full replay-recovery behavior. The upstream API and one concrete provider path are present and consumed for root turns. Keep G7 and Task 146 continuation acceptance incomplete until branch-scope coverage, stale/reseed/cancel/expiry behavior, restart/replay semantics, and supported provider-route behavior are reviewed and verified. Upstream-main status and issue filing are not prerequisites. G8 Native plugin component registration; rpi-plugin-sdk + rpi-extensions + rpi-tui Optional dynamic Component registration/lifecycle API if native third-party panels are a product requirement Existing UiComponent and ExtensionPanel are structured text, not arbitrary TUI components Conditional: no issue filed; built-in ScribeRig views do not wait on this gate. File an upstream proposal only if third-party native panels become a requirement. G10 Isolated plugin execution and capability-scoped host API; rpi-extensions + rpi-plugin-sdk A reusable process boundary that prevents native extensions from inheriting host filesystem/database privileges and exposes only declared host capabilities At active pin ebcf8d5e75d20fa3a6cc7cc76cbcdcec4cc36eb8, rpi-extensions::isolated is committed and pinned: versioned worker frames, process-owning client with deadlines/cancellation/shutdown, worker-side plugin loading, host-call RPC, generic AllowlistedHostHandler, an injected WorkerLauncher, and LinuxBubblewrapLauncher; ISOLATED_WORKER_SANDBOX.md records platform gaps. The default HostProcessLauncher rejects sandboxed requests, and no built-in macOS or Windows sandbox exists. ScribeRig's plugin_worker module compiles against this pin and supplies ApplicationDomainDispatcher (snapshot-, capability-, and size-checked domain_operation only), PluginHostPolicy, and AuthorizedPluginWorker, which requires a sandboxed policy plus tool and operation allowlists. However, validate_isolated_plugin_configuration still rejects any configured worker or package root, so no dispatcher is composed into production, worker tools never enter ToolCatalog/build_tools, and there is no package lifecycle or atomic extension-session/catalog replacement. Launcher sandbox guarantees are self-reported and not independently verified; no seccomp or CPU/memory limits exist; cancellation remains cooperative inside native FFI; host capability calls are not cancellation-aware; and worker runtime-action coverage is partial. Compose an authorized worker into branch catalogs only after OS-enforced sandbox evidence, invocation-time branch capability/tool reauthorization, and lifecycle/cancellation validation. Keep extension activation and tools deny-by-default until then; do not create a ScribeRig plugin ABI/sandbox.

Historical G10 working-tree update (2026-10-21, superseded by the current G10 row and §12.8): the controlled fork then contained an uncommitted sandbox policy/launcher contract in rpi-extensions/src/isolated/client/launch.rs. HostProcessLauncher rejects sandboxed requests; LinuxBubblewrapLauncher constructs a namespace-based filesystem/network/environment restriction and fails closed when bwrap or required namespaces are unavailable. No built-in macOS or Windows sandbox exists. The worker client checks the injected launcher's self-reported guarantees against the requested policy, but does not independently verify the launcher. No seccomp or resource limits are provided, declared environment values may be visible in bwrap arguments, and broad host-granted roots can weaken isolation. This source is not committed or pinned, and the command has not been runtime-validated. G10 therefore remains open; do not claim proven OS containment or enable ScribeRig plugin execution.

Current security correction (2026-10-21): the native provider-extension path has been disabled. ProviderExtensions::from_environment rejects configured extension/package roots before calling the upstream in-process loader. The earlier extension-loading descriptions below are historical and must not be read as current behavior. Built-in provider construction, typed model/thinking resolution, protected credentials, and partial applied-settings capture remain active through upstream APIs. The report is nested in the invocation's durable request projection, not reconstructed from model metadata. ScribeRig still has no package install/update/link manager or live extension reload flow. G10 remains open: the worker protocol, host capability RPC, sandbox launcher contract, and allowlist wrapper are now committed and pinned, but ScribeRig does not activate them in production and no OS-enforced sandbox has been validated at runtime. In-process loading remains forbidden because no adapter can prevent native code from using ambient filesystem access to canonical storage.

Historical readiness note: extension manifest credential handling was present in the former in-process ProviderExtensions::provider_for adapter. That adapter cannot be reached now because native extension activation fails closed. The active readiness projection covers built-in catalog providers through upstream readiness_from_catalog plus host endpoint/credential authorization. It reports source availability only, not provider acceptance; G2 remains unchecked.

G4, G5's generic editor, G6, and G8 block only the corresponding product capability if that capability is required. G7 remains a required provider continuation gate. Its implementation belongs in the controlled TNick/pi-rust fork's rpi-ai provider boundary; no GitHub issue filing or upstream-main merge is required. Task 146 must leave continuation acceptance unchecked until the fork API/code is implemented, reviewed, and pinned. All follow-up tasks must use a reviewed fork commit and must not depend on uncommitted working-tree changes.

docs.title: 12.5 Target dependency direction and task handoff
docs.text:
rpi-ai / rpi-agent / rpi-tui / rpi-plugin-sdk / rpi-extensions
                         |
                         v
              thin ScribeRig product adapters
                         |
        +----------------+----------------+
        |                                 |
ScribeRig semantic/session/app       ScribeRig TUI Components

scriberig-knowledge, domain/schema/query foundations, and canonical ScribeRig session identity do not depend on rpi-tui, rpi-agent, or rpi-harness. ScribeRig must not pass canonical-store handles or private mutation APIs to an upstream extension. The pinned rpi-extensions loader uses libloading for native cdylib plugins in the host process; this does not sandbox arbitrary plugin code from process privileges or direct database/file access. Therefore host capability filtering can govern only host-mediated tool calls and is not proof that a loaded native extension cannot mutate canonical storage directly. Until upstream provides a process-isolated plugin boundary with a capability scoped host API, ScribeRig must treat loaded native plugins as explicitly trusted process code and must not claim the stronger non-mutation guarantee. Any authorized knowledge change still must use ScribeRig semantic operations and candidate → migration → validation → merge/conflict → promotion. The knowledge graph, session tree, plan dependency DAG, and execution causality remain distinct. Presentation settings never change execution. Provider-visible reasoning is surfaced only when explicitly available and safe; hidden chain-of-thought is not exposed.

Follow-up Inputs from this audit First blocking condition 145 model/catalog G1–G3, model rows, safe provenance rule Consume the pinned fork rpi-model-runtime APIs and rpi-ai::ThinkingLevel; finish auth/readiness integration and remove local catalog authority. Task 147 consumes generic rpi-tui selector widgets with safe ScribeRig rows; do not wait for upstream main or extract CLI selector orchestration. 146 agent loop/extensions provider/runtime/tool rows, G2, G4, G7 Consume upstream rpi-ai provider APIs and rpi-agent ordinary loop while ScribeRig branch/context orchestration stays. The pinned fork now provides a root continuation seam and OpenAI Responses implementation; finish branch-scope and lifecycle/replay coverage before checking continuation acceptance. 147 upstream TUI shell/runtime terminal/runtime, upstream component adoption, G9 The active runtime in crates/scriberig-tui/src/runtime/upstream.rs uses upstream TuiAltScreen, Editor, ScrollView, selectors, PropertyEditor, overlays, and Component; semantic reducers remain ScribeRig-owned. scriberig-tui-kit, vendored rpi-tui, and production Ratatui rendering are absent. Task 147's visible PTY acceptance remains unverified/failed in the recorded run; direct Crossterm coupling remains at crates/scriberig-tui/Cargo.toml and runtime/upstream/controls.rs. No ANSI/plain rendering bridge or Ratatui compatibility shell. 148 semantic component rebuild semantic view row and G3/G6/G8 where needed runtime/upstream/semantic_views.rs composes ScribeRig semantic projections through upstream TreeList, SelectList, and Markdown. Stable semantic identities and reducer actions remain ScribeRig-owned. Task 148 remains in progress for behavior, complete semantic action/focus/layout coverage, and PTY/golden acceptance. Generic missing tree/table APIs remain upstream gates; no local widget fallback. 149 cleanup/conformance verified DELETE ledger entries and task 145–148 outputs Remove only residual duplicated owners confirmed in the corrected ledger, review direct Crossterm and test-only event/keymap modules, and verify dependency boundaries. Keep provider continuation branch-scope and isolation gates open; no migration claim before required gates pass.

docs.title: 12.6 Verification record
docs.text:
• Inspected upstream checkout at exact SHA aab74de0737f4b7c454cd8c8c16ca66e4dfbf898; pinned source tree was cloned and detached at that commit for this audit.
  • Queried upstream main on 2026-10-20; it resolves to the same SHA. Verified issues #67 and #68 remain open, #68 links the selector draft branch, and no pull request exists for that branch. Issue search found no provider continuation proposal.
  • Inspected the public source paths named in §12.3, workspace package packages/provider-runtime, and searched for registry, credential, selector, package, continuation, tree/table, and plugin UI APIs.
  • The initial dependency audit ran cargo tree -p scriberig-agent-runtime and cargo tree -p scriberig-tui: the agent runtime tree contains reqwest and no rpi-ai/rpi-agent; the TUI tree has direct Ratatui/Crossterm dependencies and reaches vendored rpi-tui through scriberig-tui-kit. cargo tree -p scriberig-tui -i rpi-tui confirmed that vendored path. That audit predates the active upstream runtime slice recorded below.
  • Searched repository references for model/thinking descriptors, provider implementation, continuation handles, semantic branch/plan types, profiles, context components, plugin/package hosts and terminal framework dependencies.
  • No tests were run during this architecture inventory. A focused scriberig-tui cargo check after the current pin is recorded below; no test or PTY/golden verification is recorded for the active-root slice.

docs.title: 12.8.2 Reasoning-summary source and ordering
docs.text:
Confirmed at the active pin:

  • rpi-ai/src/types.rs defines ReasoningSummaryDelta separately from ThinkingStart/ThinkingDelta/ThinkingEnd. Its documentation states it is provider-supplied reasoning-summary text separate from raw thinking.
  • rpi-ai/src/providers/openai_responses.rs maps response.reasoning_summary_text.delta to ReasoningSummaryDelta, while response.reasoning_text.delta still maps to the hidden thinking slot.
  • rpi-agent/src/agent_loop.rs forwards the event through AgentEvent::MessageUpdate.

Implemented in this turn as a narrow adapter:

  • crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/lib.rs adds ReasoningSummaryCallback, carrying a per-invocation monotonic ordinal.
  • crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/upstream_invocation.rs forwards only ReasoningSummaryDelta to that callback; ThinkingDelta, ThinkingEnd, and their content are never forwarded.
  • apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/runner/summary_activity.rs accumulates bounded (256-character) cumulative summary text and publishes AgentActivityKind::ReasoningSummary with Running progress and a final Completed event.
  • crates/scriberig-app/src/{event.rs,operation_agent.rs} carry and bound the per-invocation ordinal; crates/scriberig-server/src/server_helpers_event.rs projects it as safe event metadata; scriberig-tui parses it and ignores stale summaries with a lower ordinal. TUI rendering, visibility controls, and layout were not changed.
  • Child/plan-worker invocations pass no summary callback, so a child summary cannot be misattributed to the root branch. The CLI one-shot path also leaves it unset.

This does not claim full observable-reasoning support: there is no separate ReasoningSummaryStart/End, no provider-visible/full reasoning distinction, no per-part identity, and no durable reasoning-segment representation. Those remain task 136/145 acceptance gaps.

docs.title: 12.8.3 Plugin worker guarantees and remaining gaps
docs.text:
Now present in the pinned dependency and ScribeRig:

  • Versioned worker protocol (rpi-plugin-worker-v1), worker process ownership, request correlation/deadlines, cancellation frames, shutdown, host-call RPC, and process-tree termination on host timeout.
  • WorkerLauncher injection, environment clearing by default, HostProcessLauncher failing closed for sandboxed requests, and LinuxBubblewrapLauncher reporting filesystem/network/secret guarantees.
  • ScribeRig AuthorizedPluginWorker requires WorkerSandboxPolicy::is_sandboxed, applies an upstream AllowlistedHostHandler over PluginHostPolicy, retains only host-authorized tool names, and rechecks tool authorization on call.
  • ApplicationDomainDispatcher permits only domain_operation, binds the exact host snapshot and branch context, performs capability/scope checks, rejects oversized arguments, and returns only a change handle; validation/apply/ promotion are not exposed through it.

Still absent or unvalidated:

  • validate_isolated_plugin_configuration rejects every configured worker or package root, so the worker is never started in production and worker tools never enter ToolCatalog/build_tools.
  • No atomic package/extension-session/catalog replacement and no package install/update/link path in ScribeRig.
  • Sandbox guarantees are launcher self-reports; the client does not verify them. macOS/Windows have no built-in launcher, and no seccomp or CPU/memory limits exist.
  • Cancellation is cooperative inside native FFI; a plugin that ignores its cancellation hook survives until the worker exits. Host capability calls are not cancellation-aware, and registration-time loading is not cancellable.
  • The bubblewrap launcher and sandbox policy have not been runtime-validated.

Therefore plugin activation remains deny-by-default and no OS containment is claimed.

docs.title: 12.8.4 Authentication note
docs.text: The fork now exposes typed AiError::Auth, but the provider stream still flattens provider failures into the assistant message error string at the pinned API. ScribeRig's UpstreamBranchError::Authentication therefore still depends on known upstream authentication display prefixes; HTTP 401/403 that the fork classifies internally are improved, but the ScribeRig boundary is not fully typed end-to-end. Replacing prefix detection would require a structured error event from the fork and is not part of this turn's change.

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
Implement the model/provider ownership correction from Level-2 plan 032 after task 144 is complete.

The goal is to remove ScribeRig as an authority for provider/model catalogs, thinking-level capability, provider authentication/readiness, and model-specific/custom execution properties.

The resulting system must treat upstream rpi model/provider machinery as the source of truth while preserving ScribeRig's own branch/plan assignment semantics and historical execution provenance.

Some open criteria in this sheet depend on Tasks 137, 146, 136, and 147. Keep Task 145 In Progress while those prerequisites run, following the ordered dependency gate in §16; return here afterward to reverify the affected criteria before completing this sheet.

docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this file open throughout implementation.
  • [ ] Tick exact criteria immediately after implementation plus focused verification.
  • [ ] Never bulk-tick.
  • [ ] Revert invalidated checks.
  • [ ] Do not solve a missing reusable upstream API by creating another ScribeRig catalog abstraction.
  • [ ] If blocked on upstream extraction/feature work, leave the affected criteria unchecked and record the upstream gate.

docs.title: 4. Preserve ScribeRig Assignment, Remove ScribeRig Catalog Authority
docs.text:
ScribeRig still owns the fact that one semantic execution location has one configured execution selection.

Examples:

branch -> execution selection
plan node -> execution selection
session default -> execution selection
agent profile preference -> execution selection
historical invocation -> resolved execution provenance

But ScribeRig must no longer decide what models exist or what capabilities/properties they expose.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Branch/plan assignment identity remains stable and ScribeRig-owned.
  • [x] Assignment resolution reads upstream catalog/runtime state.
  • [x] No branch/plan/session code depends on a ScribeRig-owned list of model capabilities.
  • [x] Historical assignment remains inspectable if the live upstream catalog later changes.

docs.title: 5. Replace ModelDescriptor and Local Model Library Authority
docs.text:
Current equivalents of these concepts are migration targets:

ModelDescriptor
ModelCapabilities
ThinkingLevelDescriptor
ModelLibrary as model/provider truth
local provider-profile metadata used as catalog truth

Use upstream model descriptors directly at the product/runtime integration boundary or a safe upstream-provided public snapshot/projection.

If upstream lacks a stable safe snapshot type suitable for protocol/history, contribute one upstream rather than defining a second capability schema in ScribeRig.

ScribeRig may define a narrow historical record containing:

provider public ID
model public ID
upstream catalog/version/fingerprint reference
safe resolved output-affecting selection fingerprint
safe display metadata needed for historical UI

That record is provenance, not a live catalog.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Selection resolves against the host-owned upstream catalog; authorized model reads return upstream SafeModelSnapshot rows directly, without an app-owned catalog/list representation.
  • [x] Live model metadata is queried from upstream.
  • [x] The ScribeRig JSON catalog parser, app ModelProfile/credential rows, and ModelLibrary validator/lookups are removed; exact source searches found no remaining app call sites.
  • [x] scriberig-app no longer defines or serializes ModelDescriptor, ModelId, or ModelLibrary; its authorized model-read operation returns upstream safe snapshots, while server/TUI project them into the versioned protocol DTO at the transport boundary.
  • [x] The app-owned ModelCapabilities type and ModelDescriptor.capabilities field are removed; ScribeRig no longer infers local streaming, tool_calls, or structured_output booleans. The reasoning boolean that remains in model metadata is copied from upstream's safe snapshot.
  • [ ] Tests prove an upstream catalog change is reflected without editing ScribeRig catalog code.

Catalog lifecycle evidence: ApplicationService stores a cloneable rpi_model_runtime::ModelCatalog handle. with_model_catalog installs a shared handle; the compatibility with_upstream_models(Vec<Model>) builder groups rows by Model.provider and seeds the service catalog. Model-library projection (service_agent_console.rs), session selection resolution (service_agent_console_selection.rs), and plan assignment validation (service_plans/authoring.rs) each capture one catalog snapshot per operation. The native runner seeds one catalog from its configured upstream models and shares its handle with the TUI service and server composition. The new crates/scriberig-app/tests/session_runtime.rs::model_library_projection_tracks_live_catalog_updates_and_removals fixture checks that one constructed service reflects a complete provider replacement and subsequent removal; it has not been run. This is source-level integration against the committed API at the pinned fork revision, not verified runtime evidence.

Upstream refresh extraction gate (historical note; current pin is documented above): the pinned fork now exposes rpi_model_runtime::ModelCatalog from rpi-model-runtime. Its shared handle provides provider-scoped rows, coherent revisioned snapshots, atomic complete reconciliation, and update notifications. Fork commit 6e2f83b1b26466a37bba7313b9f42c4cc6a595cf first added this API; an earlier ScribeRig pin was 714a778784bc99e982402114265bd99681857a10, superseded by the current pin recorded above. The catalog itself is a storage/update boundary; it does not load configuration, authenticate providers, discover packages, or decide filesystem policy.

That earlier fork revision also centralized project package registry/artifact operations in rpi-provider-runtime, exposed provider-reload predicates from rpi-extensions, and reconciled scoped provider catalog updates atomically. During the 0.7.0 upstream merge, provider package ABI moved to rpi-plugin-sdk, and package lifecycle APIs moved into rpi-extensions. These boundaries keep package-root authorization, configuration, trust, and credential policy in the host; ScribeRig has not yet adopted those runtime services.

At the earlier inspected CLI revision, rpi_cli::model_registry::ModelRegistry combined provider metadata with CLI config and filesystem-backed refresh policy, so moving that type unchanged would not make it reusable. The extraction should keep those policies in rpi-cli, feed complete resolved provider rows into ModelCatalog::reconcile_providers, and make the active CLI extension reload path use the shared catalog instead of ReloadContext.catalog: Arc<RwLock<Vec<Model>>>. The current pinned CLI now holds and reconciles an upstream ModelCatalog in its registry and reload context. ScribeRig already holds the shared handle and reads one snapshot per projection/selection/plan-validation operation; it does not need a second refresh loop or provider registry. The ScribeRig same-service replacement/removal fixture exists but has not been run. Keep catalog-refresh acceptance unchecked pending verification of the current CLI and ScribeRig consumers at the pinned revision. The native runner binds configured built-in models through the upstream factory. Native extensions are rejected before their in-process loader runs; deterministic test scenarios use upstream FauxProvider. Model and provider generations are still created at startup and are not hot-reloaded; catalog-refresh acceptance remains open until ScribeRig consumes a reusable reload lifecycle and verifies provider/model generation consistency.
