Consumer audit (source inspection, not runtime verification): main.rs passes the same runner catalog handle to server model projections and the plan lifecycle runner; local TUI composition in tui_command.rs installs the runner's same handle into ApplicationService. Remote TUI model rows arrive through the server's safe protocol projection and do not own a catalog. The app backend returns upstream SafeModelSnapshot rows from one ModelCatalog::snapshot() in service_agent_console.rs; the server converts those rows to the public protocol DTO. Session model resolution takes one snapshot in service_agent_console_selection.rs; plan creation, replanning, and assignment validation each take one snapshot in service_plans/authoring.rs. Native session selection and plan coordination also capture one upstream_models() vector per selection/coordination operation. Convenience server constructors without an injected catalog create an empty catalog; the executable's Serve path uses the injected shared handle. The native runner currently creates and shares its handle from upstream ModelsConfig at process startup. ScribeRig does not yet wire provider/package reload into that composition or refresh its provider-adapter map; keep end-to-end refresh and provider availability criteria unchecked pending the relevant integration and verification.

The app no longer defines ModelDescriptor, ModelId, or ModelLibrary. AgentConsoleBackend::agent_model_library returns a vector of upstream rpi_model_runtime::SafeModelSnapshot rows from one catalog snapshot. The server and local TUI convert those rows into the established protocol DTO at the transport boundary. The protocol DTO remains the versioned ScribeRig wire contract; catalog metadata and thinking support remain owned by upstream.

Protocol/client projection audit (2026-10-21): the server reads upstream safe model snapshots through agent_model_library, then projects ordered upstream thinking identifiers and allowlisted display metadata into the Rust DTO. The TypeScript selector consumes those advertised identifiers for the selected provider/model pair; it defines no supported-level list or custom property schema. The TypeScript protocol/client now also represents the Rust DTO's optional credential-safe provider-readiness rows. Presentation preferences remain a separate client display control and do not alter model selection or provider execution. Rust/TypeScript projection tests and live catalog replacement behavior remain unverified in this slice.

docs.title: 6. Delegate Thinking-Level Semantics Completely
docs.text:
Upstream owns thinking-level support, ordering, mapping, clamping, and provider serialization.

ScribeRig must not maintain a separate support table or validation list.

Required behavior:

selected model changes
  -> supported levels come from upstream model
  -> currently requested level is accepted/clamped/rejected according to upstream
  -> provider request receives upstream-mapped value

ScribeRig may persist the user-selected or resolved public level as execution configuration/provenance, but does not interpret its provider meaning.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Supported thinking values come from upstream API.
  • [x] Thinking-level mapping to provider effort comes from upstream.
  • [x] Unsupported-level fallback/clamping comes from upstream.
  • [x] TUI/web protocol projection does not invent an independent thinking enum/catalog.
  • [ ] Trusted app model rows carry upstream rpi_ai::ThinkingLevel values directly, and protocol/web rows expose only ordered scalar level IDs; focused Rust and TypeScript projection tests pass.
  • [ ] A model switch test proves levels update from the new model's upstream metadata.

The native path carries the exact upstream Model and typed effective ThinkingLevel from selection through UpstreamBranchInvocation to AgentBuilder::thinking_level and SimpleStreamOptions.reasoning. Provider crates own model-specific effort mapping and serialization. Durable request provenance converts the enum to its canonical scalar ID only at the projection boundary. Protocol projection and model-switch coverage remain unchecked.

docs.title: 7. Delegate Custom Model Properties
docs.text:
Use upstream model/provider metadata for custom and model-specific properties.

This includes current/future upstream equivalents of:

sampling parameters
reasoning maps
compatibility flags
strict-tool support
model input modalities
context window
max output
cost metadata
provider endpoint/public metadata
provider-specific request-shaping values
custom property maps

Do not introduce a ScribeRig enum/schema for these fields.

When ScribeRig needs to retain user overrides, store/forward them through an upstream-owned configuration type or an opaque serialized upstream value that upstream validates and resolves.

At the pinned fork revision, rpi_ai::Model in crates/rpi-ai/src/model.rs owns sampling_params and provider_options. rpi_model_runtime::models::build_catalog copies both from ModelDefinition into runtime models. The built-in OpenAI Completions and Responses adapters merge sampling_params into their request bodies in crates/rpi-ai/src/providers/openai_completions.rs and openai_responses.rs; this is upstream request shaping, but is specific to those adapters. provider_options is runtime-only and #[serde(skip)]. Built-in adapters fail closed on non-empty values. The extension ABI accepts an opt-in providerOptionsVersion: 1 declaration and sends a versioned providerOptions envelope only to opted-in providers; legacy providers fail closed. At ScribeRig's current pin, the envelope provides no provider- application acknowledgment. Fork commit 9f935d794053bccaf73737b5e2fb67cf3194a761 adds a closed, versioned JSON Schema for these values and validates them before creating the extension envelope; the extension still must attest which values it applied. ScribeRig's opt-in native extension path consumes the older envelope but does not yet consume the schema/setter API. Do not claim generic custom-option flow through built-in providers or copy arbitrary properties into ScribeRig DTOs.

rpi_model_runtime::safe_model_snapshot is a display projection. The separate safe_model_execution_configuration returns a versioned, partial execution snapshot: it copies allowlisted numeric sampling values (temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, seed, max_tokens, and max_completion_tokens) and only upstream schema-validated scalar provider_options; unknown, malformed, or unsafe entries are counted and omitted. It excludes endpoint, headers, opaque provider options, provider-specific thinking maps, and opaque compatibility values, and always reports complete: false. model_execution_fingerprint is a separate canonical SHA-256 identity over stable typed model metadata, including typed compatibility flags and output limits; it omits endpoint, headers, sampling parameters, provider options, thinking maps, and opaque compatibility, and always reports incomplete coverage because endpoint identity is omitted. Neither API alone establishes the complete configuration a provider actually applied.

ScribeRig's canonical request capture consumes both upstream-owned projections. It stores the SafeModelExecutionConfiguration JSON as ModelRequestProjection.model_execution_configuration, folds it into the request fingerprint, and then folds upstream's ModelExecutionFingerprint digest and coverage metadata into the same request fingerprint under a versioned domain separator. Neither value is redefined as a ScribeRig property schema. Endpoint URLs, headers, credentials, opaque provider options, and thinking-map labels never enter the durable record; upstream's omission metadata is retained. The combined identity records that upstream-reported safe model settings contributed to invocation provenance, but it still does not prove effective-request equivalence because upstream reports the fingerprint as incomplete. Source inspection confirms this capture path; the focused projection test covering sampling, typed compatibility, and secret exclusion was added but not run in this turn, so runtime parity remains unverified.

The pinned upstream boundary now reports versioned applied settings at the final provider request-preparation boundary, with explicit omitted categories and truthful completeness. ScribeRig's upstream invocation callback captures that report into ModelRequestProjection.applied_settings; the existing authorized model-request detail path carries the opaque report to history consumers. ScribeRig does not interpret the report or infer application from catalog metadata. Keep custom-property application, unknown-property flow, and canonical provenance gates open until persistence and omission semantics are verified; do not add a second ScribeRig property schema.

Provider-source review confirms that a complete applied-settings snapshot cannot be produced from rpi_ai::Model or rpi_model_runtime alone. The OpenAI Completions and Responses providers build different request bodies in rpi-ai/src/providers/openai_completions.rs::build_request and openai_responses.rs::build_request: they merge configured sampling values, apply protocol compatibility flags, map thinking levels, and choose output limits from both model metadata and SimpleStreamOptions. Anthropic instead builds RequestParams in rpi-ai/src/providers/anthropic/build_params.rs::build_params, where sampling metadata is not applied, temperature and thinking interact, thinking budgets can expand output limits, and the context-window estimate can clamp them. Extension providers receive a model and request options through rpi-extensions/src/provider.rs; the version-1 providerOptions envelope only transports opaque values to opted-in extensions and receives no provider-applied-settings acknowledgment. Providers may therefore ignore, transform, clamp, or reject configured values differently, and catalog metadata alone cannot state what a specific request used.

The upstream safe_model_execution_configuration and model_execution_fingerprint remain catalog-derived partial projections; their exclusion reports correctly leave complete false. The production callback captures upstream rpi_ai::Context, Model, and ThinkingLevel directly into ScribeRig's bounded historical ModelRequestProjection. The normalized local request DTO and model cache have been deleted. Before provider preparation, the canonical capture stores the upstream safe configuration JSON and folds both that snapshot and the upstream execution fingerprint digest into the request identity. The separate upstream callback then adds the provider-attested applied-settings report to the same per-request projection. The current adapter folds that safe report into the request fingerprint using a versioned domain separator, while retaining its separate report fingerprint. Since each upstream report is partial and the applied report omits opaque provider options and other request fields, the resulting identity still does not prove complete effective-request equivalence. The extension ABI's options-v1 envelope is not this report. Keep unknown-property and complete-configuration criteria unchecked until upstream attestation covers those values and focused persistence/omission verification is available.

The native root and plan-worker request paths use the upstream provider and agent boundary. Deterministic scenario fixtures use upstream FauxProvider and FauxScript; no production ProviderAdapter or normalized request DTO remains. The local OpenAI wire serializer and CompatibilityProfile were deleted. Do not copy provider_options or other arbitrary Model properties into a ScribeRig DTO. The applied-settings report is safe, provider-attested, and partial; it does not make the catalog execution fingerprint complete or establish a complete effective-request identity. Upstream provides schema-backed property descriptors and setters. ScribeRig's native model settings flow consumes them and persists validated edits through ModelsConfigFile when the catalog came from SCRIBE_AGENT_MODEL_CONFIG_PATH. Environment JSON and extension-only models remain read-only. The remaining property gaps are complete effective-request equivalence and unknown-future property flow, not a missing editor, persistence path, or fingerprint contribution from the safe values upstream currently reports.

Acceptance:

  • [x] ScribeRig does not define custom model property semantics.
  • [x] Runtime validation of model properties is upstream-owned.
  • [x] Output-affecting properties reported by upstream participate in ScribeRig invocation provenance and request fingerprinting through the canonical safe upstream snapshot/hash; this does not establish complete effective-request equivalence.
  • [x] Secret headers/credential material are excluded from ScribeRig durable records.
  • [ ] Unknown future upstream properties can flow through without a ScribeRig code change where the upstream public type supports that.

The pinned rpi_model_runtime::ModelsConfig and ModelDefinition are the configuration schema. Native built-in model requests pass the exact selected rpi_ai::Model to create_builtin_provider; ScribeRig does not define a parallel execution-property schema or editor. Fork commit 9f935d794053bccaf73737b5e2fb67cf3194a761 adds provider-owned ProviderOptionsSchema, ModelPropertyDescriptor, and validated setters in rpi-ai and rpi-model-runtime. Commit 46ea1250bd695540b7f0b395afd6e10518fc05ff adds upstream update_model_config_property and the reusable rpi-tui PropertyEditor. ScribeRig's local TUI/service adapter now uses those APIs: the host checks agent_model_config_edit, passes property values to upstream validation, and reconciles the live ModelCatalog for subsequent invocations. The current ScribeRig then pinned the combined fork at 714a778784bc99e982402114265bd99681857a10; the current pin is 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, which includes the typed label/value PropertyEditor API and ModelsConfigFile. Native configuration loaded from SCRIBE_AGENT_MODEL_CONFIG_PATH persists property changes with the upstream ModelsConfigFile writer after upstream schema validation, then refreshes the live ModelCatalog. Descriptor lookup requires both that file-backed path and an exact provider/model row in the upstream ModelsConfig, so the TUI does not open property editors for read-only rows. The environment JSON source SCRIBE_AGENT_MODEL_CATALOG remains read-only. Do not write it back or invent a ScribeRig model-file format. Extension-only models without a matching ModelsConfig provider/model row remain read-only. ScribeRig does not define a property schema; the only durable execution-property provenance is the upstream safe configuration snapshot and execution fingerprint captured by the request projection.

The upstream file writer persists only file-backed config selected by SCRIBE_AGENT_MODEL_CONFIG_PATH; environment-provided JSON and extension manifest-only rows are read-only. Keep complete effective-request equivalence and unknown-future-property flow unchecked. Complete provider-applied configuration remains a separate gate.

Unknown/future property boundary audit (2026-10-21, pinned fork b2fc63c78ae85044eb78e7ac9af184bd7fbfbc95): the generic settings path in apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/model_properties.rs enumerates upstream ModelPropertyDescriptor values, checks upstream's is_safe_for_generic_editor, and calls upstream update_model_config_property; it does not branch on property names or define a ScribeRig property type. rpi-model-runtime::ModelDefinition has a flattened provider_options map, and ModelsConfigFile writes that upstream config, so unrelated provider options survive an edit/save without ScribeRig interpreting them. Provider-declared scalar properties that appear in upstream schema descriptors are editable through the same path without a ScribeRig code change. The invocation path also passes the complete selected upstream rpi_ai::Model to the provider factory, so newly added typed model fields flow to upstream providers without a ScribeRig request DTO change.

This does not establish arbitrary future-property editing or provenance. model_property_descriptors exposes only declared schema properties, the generic editor deliberately excludes secret/read-only/composite descriptors, and update_model_config_property edits only the schema-backed provider_options map. The pinned safe_model_execution_configuration omits unknown/unsafe values, while its model fingerprint excludes sampling and provider options; the provider-applied settings report also remains partial and does not attest opaque provider options. Therefore the existing ScribeRig bridge is generic over properties the upstream schema/editor APIs expose, but unknown-property pass-through and complete canonical effective-request provenance are still unverified gates. Closing those gates requires upstream APIs: (1) a versioned opaque execution-configuration identity over every request-relevant typed model field and validated provider option, with explicit omission categories, and (2) a provider-preparation attestation that identifies which opaque options were applied or transformed. ScribeRig must consume those upstream results without adding a property catalog or interpreting option keys.

Durable-secret boundary evidence: SessionExecutionSelection and ModelAssignment retain only public provider/model/thinking identifiers. ModelInvocation and ModelRequestProjection contain bounded request content, safe identifiers, profile/component references, and fingerprints; they have no endpoint, header, credential-source, resolved-secret, or upstream Model fields. The SQLite session store serializes these session types. The native catalog loader clears and rejects configured provider/model credentials and headers before building its runtime catalog. Request-time credentials are held in SecretValue and passed only through SecretMaterial/RequestSecret; they are not part of session types. The old local HTTP credential fixture was removed with the local transport. Source inspection supports the storage boundary, but focused secret-omission verification remains outstanding; keep this criterion unchecked.

docs.title: 8. Delegate Provider Authentication and Readiness
docs.text:
Provider authentication, credential resolution, and readiness belong upstream.

ScribeRig may apply product trust/policy around whether a provider can be used, but it must not duplicate credential-source precedence or authentication status resolution.

Required behavior:

upstream provider package/catalog
  -> upstream auth/readiness
  -> safe status projection
  -> ScribeRig TUI/web/server display

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Provider authentication success/failure status comes from upstream runtime evidence. The current readiness response reports only credential source availability and must not be presented as a successful auth check.
  • [x] Upstream owns the generic protected credential-source APIs. Native ScribeRig configuration selects one SecretRef and uses upstream's HostSelected source without adding a parallel precedence chain.
  • [ ] Resolved credentials never enter ScribeRig session/protocol state.
  • [x] ScribeRig's explicit destination authorization can deny use while the upstream protected resolver preserves that denial as an error.
  • [ ] Provider reload/auth changes refresh ScribeRig-visible safe status from upstream.

Provider lifecycle refresh blocker (2026-10-21): the pinned rpi-model-runtime API ModelCatalog::refresh_from_configuration (and its transactional refresh_from_configuration_with_commit variant) rebuilds and publishes model rows from caller-supplied ModelsConfig; its documentation explicitly assigns configuration loading, credential policy, and refresh timing to the host. The native ScribeRig loader calls this only during startup or model-property save. provider_readiness::project re-resolves the selected host credential when invoked, so a credential change is reflected on the next projection, but the runtime exposes no auth-success/failure evidence or credential-change notification. The current host configuration loader rejects catalog-stored auth material and does not retain/reload a new source config. There is therefore no upstream-only event or safe API to refresh the catalog and readiness automatically when credentials/provider configuration change. Do not synthesize a local provider lifecycle/catalog authority; upstream needs to expose a provider reload/auth lifecycle event (including safe auth result evidence) or the host needs an explicit refresh invocation source before this criterion can be implemented.

Current upstream auth integration gate: fork commit 9f935d794053bccaf73737b5e2fb67cf3194a761 adds rpi_model_runtime::CredentialResolutionError, the policy-aware ProtectedCredentialResolver::resolve_with_policy, and resolve_credential_protected_with_policy. Source misses continue precedence; resolver errors stop it. A host that enforces policy must override resolve_with_policy; its default implementation adapts legacy resolve and cannot distinguish denial from a miss. The legacy resolve_credential_protected API maps an error to a credential-free Missing result and also stops precedence. The configured one-shot CLI, native root, and local-config plan-worker paths now create built-in providers through create_builtin_provider and execute through rpi-agent. They resolve the ScribeRig-selected credential only after the exact model endpoint is fixed, then pass it to the provider through RequestSecret. The bridge invokes upstream's ProtectedCredentialResolver through its CredentialRequestSource::HostSelected path, bound to the exact selected model endpoint. ScribeRig configuration selects one exact SecretRef, so the product must not invoke upstream's independent CLI override, stored auth, model-config, or environment precedence for that request. Fork commit 94c2a748f4acfd2211cff4e8d849270e2e7530a5 adds the generic CredentialRequestSource::HostSelected path, its policy-aware protected resolver, and path-parameterized auth-store read/write/upsert/delete APIs; these were included in the earlier 714a778784bc99e982402114265bd99681857a10 fork pin and remain present in current pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5. HostSelected allows a resolver already bound to ScribeRig's authorized SecretRef and exact endpoint to supply protected material without applying provider source precedence. It does not select ScribeRig's SecretRef or authorize the endpoint/SecretUseContext, so those product policy decisions remain ScribeRig-owned.

The same crate exposes readiness_from_catalog, which projects a resolved upstream source or model-header presence to a safe CredentialSource enum. The native provider_readiness::project uses it for catalog headers and uses credential_source_for_model for the same protected host-selected resolver used at request time. It maps only upstream's safe source/error classification to Available, Missing, Denied, NotRequired, or CatalogHeader; credential material is dropped before projection. Extension manifest requires_auth: false maps from upstream's Anonymous source to NotRequired. Catalog headers are rejected by the built-in loader. This reports whether a host credential can be resolved, not whether the provider accepted it. The projection is computed from the current catalog snapshot on demand, but no provider reload/refresh service or response-auth classification is exposed. For an extension manifest requiring authentication, an upstream Headers classification does not satisfy readiness: the ScribeRig extension binding requires the authorized host-selected RequestSecret, so readiness remains Missing without it. Keep upstream auth-status and refresh acceptance unchecked; do not treat Available as a successful provider authentication. The HTTP server now receives this projection through a host-injected ProviderReadinessHandler and refreshes it on each successful model-library read. The handler is composed from the same native runner as plan execution; server-side response mapping filters its rows to the exact provider/model IDs in that response. AuthorizedCredential reloads user/system policy before each source read, so policy and credential changes are visible on the next read without exposing source values. Package reload and response-auth evidence remain unavailable and are not represented by this status.

The ScribeRig host credential provider is request-scoped and authorizes the exact endpoint in scriberig-secrets::registry::AuthorizedCredential::credential. The upstream resolver receives provider/source descriptors but no endpoint or ScribeRig SecretUseContext; a request-scoped resolver can capture those host values while resolving the protected material. apps/scriberig/src/agent_config.rs selects one effective ScribeRig SecretRef. For native configured execution, there is no ScribeRig-side source precedence: the request-scoped host resolver asks upstream only for CredentialRequestSource::HostSelected, bound to the exact selected endpoint. Upstream's provider-keyed CLI/auth-store/environment precedence is deliberately not applied to this product-selected reference. The runtime's local CredentialSource enum and ProviderConfig aggregate have been removed. App composition passes the exact upstream Model together with an optional host Arc<dyn CredentialProvider>; the host adapter binds the selected reference to the endpoint and carries the resolved SecretValue only through upstream's protected request API. The bridge is used by the configured one-shot and built-in native root/plan paths; the host also fails closed on authorization or resolution errors. The native TUI exposes the safe readiness projection described above. The doctor command uses the pinned built-in OpenAI Completions provider with the exact configured endpoint and protected secret; it reports provider request failure generically and does not expose response-auth classification. Keep §8 auth-status and refresh acceptance unchecked; do not adapt via ordinary-string AuthStore or map authorization errors to source misses.

Native root and local-config plan-worker composition now tries exact upstream provider construction before consulting the compatibility adapter map. Plan preflight accepts upstream provider support without requiring a duplicate local adapter. The adapter lookup remains necessary only when upstream is disabled for the selected compatibility path; exact provider/auth failures still fail closed at execution.

The upstream protected request seam is sufficient for transporting a credential after host authorization: RequestSecret accepts opaque SecretMaterial, and built-in providers expose it only while constructing request headers. Endpoint and SecretUseContext are intentionally absent from that value because the host must authorize the secret before creating the request handle. ProtectedCredentialResolver also has no endpoint/context parameters; a host can bind those values in a request-scoped resolver instance without adding ScribeRig semantics upstream. Built-in providers expose the protected request transport; the current pin also implements protected credentials through versioned streaming extension callbacks. The legacy one-shot extension ABI has no protected credential input. Extension options_json serializes SimpleStreamOptions.api_key as apiKey; ScribeRig must not put an authorized credential in that ordinary JSON options field. Configured built-in execution uses upstream Provider implementations and the protected request boundary. The duplicate ScribeRig OpenAI-compatible transport and its tests have been deleted. Deterministic product scenarios remain local adapters and are wrapped as upstream providers for execution. The native extension composition uses the pinned upstream PluggableProvider; package registry, trust-root selection, and refresh policy remain separate host lifecycle gates.

Task 146's auth migration boundary is file-specific. Keep scriberig-secrets::{SecretRef, SecretUseContext, SecretValue} and scriberig-secrets::registry::AuthorizedCredential as ScribeRig's destination authorization and secret-storage owner. Keep the host-side configuration selection in apps/scriberig/src/agent_config.rs only where it chooses the authorized SecretRef and constructs the trusted use context. The configured one-shot, native root, plan-worker, doctor, and extension paths use the request-scoped request_secret_for_model bridge at the upstream provider boundary. It binds the exact selected model endpoint through AuthorizedCredential, returns authorization/resolution errors without fallthrough, and transports the resulting value only through SecretMaterial/RequestSecret. Do not route this one-reference product configuration through upstream's provider-keyed source-precedence resolver: the current upstream API lacks a host-selected source and exact endpoint/ SecretUseContext contract, and its generic source labels would not accurately describe every ScribeRig SecretRef. The local OpenAI-compatible secret resolution and HTTP-header construction were deleted with that commodity provider. Keep ScribeRig's authorization policy and secret registry. The doctor command uses the pinned built-in provider and reports safe generic failures; upstream response-auth classification and successful-auth readiness remain unavailable. Do not substitute catalog-source presence for successful authentication.

docs.title: Provider/auth ownership source audit and executable gate (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
Current source evidence does not identify a deletable ScribeRig duplicate in the credential path. apps/scriberig/src/agent_config.rs selects exactly one SecretRef, constructs SecretUseContext, and delegates the actual policy-checked lookup to scriberig-secrets::registry::AuthorizedCredential. crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/protected_credential.rs is the narrow adapter from that host authority to upstream resolve_host_selected_credential_with_policy: its resolver accepts only CredentialRequestSource::HostSelected, binds the exact Model.base_url, and maps denial/resolution failures to errors. Removing either layer would remove ScribeRig's required destination authorization or the upstream protected transport boundary; neither duplicates upstream source precedence.

Likewise, apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/provider_readiness.rs uses upstream readiness_from_catalog and the same protected resolver, drops secret material, and maps only safe classifications into the wire DTO. The DTO mapping is a transport projection, not auth resolution. The native loader in apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/provider_config/catalog.rs delegates generic endpoint resolution to resolve_model_endpoints; its remaining fallback insertion, config-path selection, rejection of catalog auth/header material, endpoint validation, and exact fallback override are host policy.

No owner-deletion change is justified by this audit. The remaining acceptance gap is specifically an upstream-produced provider response auth result and a change source that can invoke the existing host-injected catalog refresh after provider/credential configuration changes. The next executable gate is:

  1. At the pinned upstream API, expose a safe response-auth classification and a provider reload/auth lifecycle signal (or provide an explicit host refresh operation that is invoked by a real configuration change source).
  2. Wire that signal/operation through the existing shared ModelCatalog and readiness projection without moving SecretRef, SecretUseContext, endpoint authorization, or secret material into upstream catalog state.
  3. Run focused compile checks with cargo check -p scriberig-agent-runtime -p scriberig-app -p scriberig; then run the targeted Rust readiness, refresh, and secret-omission tests plus matching TypeScript protocol projection tests. Keep the §8 boxes unchecked until those behaviors and checks exist and pass.

docs.title: Provider response-auth classification boundary (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
Inspection of the current controlled fork pin b2fc63c78ae85044eb78e7ac9af184bd7fbfbc95 confirms that built-in providers represent non-success HTTP responses, including 401/403, as rpi-ai::AiError::Http { status: Some(..), .. }. rpi-ai::AiError::Auth is used for invalid protected-credential cases, not as the general response-auth classification. Neither distinction is a reusable runtime result at that pin. Provider stream adapters turn the error into AssistantMessage.error_message: Option<String> and a generic AssistantMessageEvent::Error; rpi-agent::AgentState retains only the error string. The ScribeRig invocation consequently receives a free-form message, not a typed auth outcome. Do not parse message text or infer auth status from generic failure strings.

The same fork's rpi-cli::ModelRegistry has AuthStatus and ModelRegistryEvent::AuthStatusChanged, but these are CLI-owned registry metadata. The inspected setter has no provider runtime producer and does not carry typed provider response evidence, so it cannot serve as a reusable authentication-result API. rpi-model-runtime::ModelCatalogEvent reports provider-model row changes only; catalog refresh remains an explicit host operation.

An earlier ScribeRig adapter briefly recognized the AiError::Auth display prefix. That heuristic has been removed. The controlled fork working tree now adds typed authentication classification for AiError::Auth and HTTP 401/403, preserves it as an internal AssistantMessageEvent::Error reason while keeping the existing serialized "error" reason, and retains it in rpi-agent state as provider_error_reason. ScribeRig maps that typed state to AgentError::Authentication without parsing diagnostic strings. These fork changes are uncommitted and absent from ScribeRig's pinned revision, and no compile/runtime verification has been run. The feature must remain unchecked until a reviewed fork revision is committed, pinned, and verified; it must not drive provider-readiness status until provider-result lifecycle policy is also implemented.

The reusable upstream extraction should preserve a typed, safe auth outcome from provider response handling through rpi-ai and rpi-agent (for example, a provider response classification callback/event containing only an outcome enum and provider/model identity). The host can then update its safe readiness projection without persisting provider response bodies, messages, headers, or credentials. ScribeRig must continue selecting the exact SecretRef, authorizing its endpoint, and projecting only non-secret status. Credential and policy availability is already re-resolved by the current ScribeRig adapter on each readiness query; provider-response success/failure and a live provider-configuration change source are still absent. No local status cache or message parser was added, and §8 acceptance remains unchecked.

docs.title: 9. Delegate Provider Packages and Catalog Refresh
docs.text:
Use upstream provider-package and catalog-refresh infrastructure.

If install/update/link/reload APIs are currently CLI-only, complete the upstream contribution gate from task 144 before implementing a local package manager.

Current fork API audit at ScribeRig's pin a40890741880838d02532fd57ec365ade16725d1: rpi_extensions::load_session in crates/rpi-extensions/src/loader.rs accepts host-selected cdylib directories, ExtensionSession exposes successfully registered ProviderManifest values through crates/rpi-extensions/src/registry.rs, and rpi_extensions::PluggableProvider::from_session in crates/rpi-extensions/src/provider.rs creates upstream rpi_ai::Provider adapters. rpi_model_runtime::build_catalog in crates/rpi-model-runtime/src/catalog.rs combines host ModelsConfig with those manifests. These are reusable loading, runtime-adapter, and one-shot catalog-composition APIs, not package lifecycle or refresh services. load_session scans caller-supplied directories; it does not select package roots from a package registry. The pinned commit does not expose ProjectPackage or ProjectPackageRegistry: those types exist only as uncommitted worktree changes and are not available to ScribeRig at this pin. In the pinned tree, rpi_cli::packages keeps ProjectPackage and PackageRegistry inside the CLI; it owns registry parsing/persistence and selects .rpi/packages roots. The pinned rpi_extensions::package_resource_dirs helper, added in commit 4ced7ab1a581fb6622e476f5fb4687dbe97f4eed and implemented in crates/rpi-extensions/src/package_roots.rs, joins a caller-provided resource string to caller-selected package roots, preserving order and retaining nonexistent paths. It does not constrain the resource to a relative child: Path::join allows an absolute resource to replace the root, and .. can escape it. The helper does not read or validate a package registry, authorize or canonicalize roots, check symlinks, load extensions, or reload a live catalog. In pinned rpi-cli/src/packages.rs, ProjectPackage and PackageRegistry are CLI-local, read_registry/write_registry own JSON persistence, and project_package_dirs chooses cwd/.rpi/packages/<name> before calling the resource-path helper. The pinned reusable boundary here is only package_resource_dirs. ScribeRig now calls it with process-configured package roots and the fixed extensions resource, then passes those paths to load_session after an explicit native-code trust opt-in. The current host does not canonicalize or authorize package roots against a package registry; that is a remaining trust-policy gap. Package installation and atomic session/catalog refresh still require separate host/upstream lifecycle APIs. rpi_cli::install::{run_async, installed_native_packages} in crates/rpi-cli/src/install.rs uses the CLI's global package registry and installation layout. The separate rpi_cli::provider::catalog_with_manifests in crates/rpi-cli/src/provider.rs reads CLI configuration. Reusable parsing and lexical root resolution do not provide package registry policy, install/update, or orchestration that atomically replaces a live extension session and model catalog.

Configured native extension paths are rejected before loading. The pinned upstream loader uses in-process native code and cannot enforce ScribeRig's canonical-knowledge invariant, so ScribeRig does not merge extension manifests or instantiate PluggableProvider. Built-in providers are created through the pinned upstream factory with the exact resolved model. Deterministic scenario fixtures use upstream FauxProvider; no local provider implementation or adapter map remains in production. Package install/reload and isolated extension execution remain blocked on upstream lifecycle and isolation APIs. The loaded extension session is retained for the runner lifetime, but there is no atomic session/catalog replacement or in-flight generation lifecycle. Native code loading still requires the explicit host trust switch; package registry, install/update, root authorization, and refresh remain separate host/upstream lifecycle gates.

Task 146's provider/catalog migration starts at these local call sites:

  • apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/provider_config/catalog.rs builds the upstream ModelsConfig catalog and provider_config/extensions.rs adds manifest models. Both retain exact upstream model identities.
  • apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent.rs::upstream_provider_for binds an exact selected model to the built-in factory or its registered PluggableProvider, and resolves only the host-authorized secret for that endpoint. The local provider map is limited to deterministic scenarios.
  • apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/runner.rs, plan_worker.rs, recursive-child execution, and apps/scriberig/src/main_agent_execution/upstream.rs use rpi-agent for model/tool sequencing. ScribeRig retains branch/session orchestration and authorized semantic tool execution. Remaining ProviderModel consumers serve deterministic/compatibility paths; removal is a Task 146 gate.

Provider loading through the upstream extension session is implemented for explicit process-configured directories and package roots, behind the native code trust opt-in. ScribeRig has no package registry, install/update policy, or live catalog refresh service. If package distribution is adopted, the host must authorize package roots against the intended registry and atomically publish replacement session/catalog generations while in-flight requests retain the old generation. Keep registry policy, install/update, and reload criteria unchecked until those lifecycle boundaries exist.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Provider package discovery/loading is upstream-owned.
  • [ ] Catalog refresh is upstream-owned.
  • [ ] Provider package reload updates available models without a ScribeRig restart where upstream supports it.
  • [ ] ScribeRig does not scan package/plugin directories independently for model providers.
  • [ ] ScribeRig does not maintain a second package manifest format for agent providers.

docs.title: 10. Refine AgentProfile Execution References
docs.text:
Keep ScribeRig AgentProfile semantics for context composition and branch behavior.

Replace local model-profile ownership with an upstream execution reference.

The final profile should conceptually contain:

ScribeRig profile id/revision
ScribeRig context-component policy
ScribeRig branch/tool policy
ScribeRig runtime budgets
preferred upstream execution selection/reference

It should not duplicate:

model capability table
thinking-level capability table
provider auth information
provider custom property schema

Acceptance:

  • [ ] AgentProfile remains revisioned ScribeRig semantic configuration.
  • [ ] Preferred execution selection resolves through upstream.
  • [ ] A profile revision changes when its profile-owned preferred upstream selection changes; an invocation-level override changes invocation provenance without mutating the profile revision.
  • [ ] Profile editing does not create a local shadow model catalog.

Current implementation gate: the design assigns reusable AgentProfile and context-component state to the shared semantic/application layer, with scriberig-agent-runtime resolving it for one invocation and scriberig-session retaining exact invocation provenance only. See Level-2 030 §§3, 6, and 7; Level-3 137 Stage 3 and Task G1. Task 137 Phase B now adds provider-neutral AgentProfileDescriptor and ContextComponentDescriptor types in scriberig-agent-core, plus a deterministic bootstrap profile in scriberig-agent-runtime. These are inline bootstrap descriptors, not a durable profile domain schema or store. scriberig-schema supplies generic schema vocabulary, and there is still no implemented profile domain adapter, shared application read/resolution API, or profile migration/projection path. The executable owner for selecting/adapting the semantic representation is Task 137 Phase G, especially G1–G4: reuse shared immutable semantic revisions, expose shared application operations, route edits through ordinary candidate/revision/validation/promotion, and define the bootstrap identity/import transition. Do not add a standalone profile store in Task 145; its profile integration depends on Task 137 establishing those semantics and the bootstrap-to-semantic path.

The profile-owned execution preference should contain only stable upstream provider/model identifiers and an optional canonical upstream thinking-level identifier. It is a ScribeRig semantic preference that must resolve against the host's current upstream catalog through rpi_model_runtime::ModelSelection and resolve_selection; it is not an upstream profile-reference type, a ScribeRig model-catalog entry, or a credential/configuration record. The pinned fork exposes catalog selection resolution but no reusable semantic profile reference API. Keep credentials, provider properties, and copied model capability metadata out of AgentProfile. When a branch, plan node, or invocation selection overrides the profile preference, the effective selection belongs to that invocation's safe provenance and request fingerprint; it must not rewrite the profile revision. Only changing the preference stored in the profile creates a new profile revision.

The selection bridge now exists, but the production semantic profile source does not. crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/profile/execution.rs accepts an exact AgentProfileDescriptor, projects only its provider/model/thinking IDs, and passes that selection to the shared application resolver. The resolver keeps invocation, plan-node, branch, session, project, and user-profile precedence and resolves the effective provider/model/thinking choice against the supplied upstream Model catalog via rpi_model_runtime::resolve_selection. This is a usable integration seam, not a complete profile flow: current ContextCompiler::new installs the code-defined bootstrap profile and with_profile is only an injection seam; there is no shared semantic profile read or candidate-promotion API, and the normal invocation/plan-worker paths do not obtain the active exact profile from one. Do not fabricate a profile lookup from display names, the retired catalog, or provider configuration. Task 137 Phase G remains gated on those shared semantic profile operations and wiring the resolved exact descriptor through normal invocation resolution. Keep profile identity and revision in context/request provenance; a narrower execution override changes the invocation's effective selection/fingerprint, not the profile revision.

The SQLite recovery importer in crates/scriberig-session-sqlite/src/payload.rs preserves allowlisted legacy session/plan profile and model identifiers in LegacyExecutionRecord, then clears unresolvable typed selections. It does not map a legacy profile/model name to an upstream provider/model pair. Keep the migration gate open until an archived profile/catalog supports unique exact resolution and a focused migration path preserves unresolved values for operator recovery. Do not recreate the retired ModelProfile or infer a provider from invocation history.

docs.title: 11. Preserve Historical Model Invocation Provenance
docs.text:
Historical ScribeRig model invocations still need safe explanation after upstream catalog updates.

Record exact safe execution facts used for each invocation without owning the live catalog.

At minimum preserve:

provider/model public ids
resolved thinking selection
safe output-affecting configuration fingerprint/snapshot
upstream runtime/catalog version reference when available
provider request/response public ids when safe
ScribeRig effective request id

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Historical invocation detail remains inspectable after live catalog mutation.
  • [ ] Historical provenance cannot expose credentials.
  • [ ] Historical safe snapshots are not re-used as a live catalog unless explicitly imported back through upstream resolution.

Current persistence gate: native catalog-backed execution carries the resolved provider/model pair from apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/model_selection.rs into ProviderModel::with_provider_id, through the bounded scriberig_session::ModelRequestProjection, and into the backward-compatible ModelInvocation.provider_id and provider_model_id fields in crates/scriberig-app/src/service_local_sessions.rs. The model id comes from the exact provider model string already used for that request; persistence does not perform a live catalog lookup or add a custom property schema. The CLI path separately carries its ScribeRig provider profile id through provider_profile; it does not mislabel that profile as an upstream provider_id. Both fields are optional/defaulted so prior serialized invocations and projections still load. Public ModelRequestDetailResponse carries the captured optional provider_id and the ScribeRig client normalizes its snake-case wire name to providerId; provider_profile remains internal provenance and is omitted from this DTO. The focused persistence/protocol/client fixtures were updated but not run, so §11 acceptance remains unchecked. The native root and recursive-child completion paths persist these projection fields. Native plan workers now return captured requests separately from the semantic BranchResult; the single coordinator persists those requests through the shared application invocation-history operation onto the exact claimed branch before saving the completed batch. Provider request projections are drained before propagating runtime errors, so a native worker that fails after preparing a request retains that bounded projection on its failed claimed branch. An invalid result naming another branch has its attached evidence dropped. Coordinator and runtime fixtures cover durable provider/model identity and capture across a provider error, but were not run. §11 acceptance remains unchecked pending focused runtime validation. Catalog/config snapshot identity and upstream request/model IDs remain absent. The applied-settings report is captured in the same durable request projection as a partial, provider-attested report; it is not a complete snapshot or fingerprint.

Root and recursive-child runtime failures now persist requests captured before the error onto the exact abandoned branch through the existing session save path. Durable failure summaries use fixed generic text, so provider diagnostics do not enter session state. A focused application fixture covers failed-child request persistence; it remains unrun, and §11 acceptance stays unchecked.

The available upstream safe_model_execution_configuration and model_execution_fingerprint are explicitly partial (complete == false) and do not say which values the provider applied. The canonical request projection stores the upstream safe configuration snapshot and folds both it and the upstream execution-fingerprint digest into the request identity, so the captured provenance retains the catalog-derived safe settings used at invocation time. The local adapter also discards provider response metadata before persist_execution_evidence. The captured request projection and its detail read are stable against later catalog mutation because service_agent_console_request::model_request_detail reads the persisted invocation projection and server_agent_console::project_model_request maps that record without consulting the live model library. This establishes stability only for captured request fields, the safe upstream model configuration, and ScribeRig context references; it is not a historical model/catalog snapshot or proof of applied settings. Therefore leave the complete effective-request identity, complete applied-configuration snapshot, catalog/runtime version, and provider request/response ID gates open. The upstream execution bridge carries the versioned partial applied-settings report into durable invocation details, and the request identity includes the safe model execution fingerprint, but their omissions do not provide a complete historical configuration identity. Credential references, endpoint URLs, headers, and opaque provider options must not be copied into that history.

docs.title: Current capture, persistence, and presentation safety audit
docs.text:
Static source review traced ordinary root execution from apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/runner.rs and recursive child execution from apps/scriberig/src/child_runtime.rs. Both pass the runtime's captured ModelRequestProjection values to the shared scriberig-app::persist_execution_evidence path in crates/scriberig-app/src/service_local_sessions.rs; it stores only that typed projection in ModelInvocation.request. The capture allowlist in crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/upstream_invocation/request_projection.rs copies model/provider/thinking identities, message role/content, bounded tool names/descriptions/schemas, the upstream safe execution-configuration snapshot, and the upstream execution-fingerprint digest folded into the request identity. A shared 15,000-character budget bounds message and tool content and sets truncated when content is omitted. It does not copy ModelRequest.metadata, resolved credentials, endpoint URLs, headers, arbitrary or opaque provider options, or provider response metadata. The separate upstream AppliedRequestSettings report carries provider-attested allowlisted values and explicit omissions with incomplete status. The budget is for prompt/tool content; model/provider identity strings, model configuration, and fingerprints are not included in that character budget.

SQLite's payload::encode stores the typed session graph as JSON; it is not a second secret scrubber. The boundary that excludes transport-only values is the capture projection before session persistence, so do not persist a raw upstream Model, host credential adapter, or wire request. The local OpenAI-compatible adapter and its direct-reflection tests were removed; configured model requests now use upstream providers and opaque RequestSecret material.

The durable request is pre-provider input plus upstream safe model configuration, its execution fingerprint, and a separate partial applied- settings report; it has no response or hidden-reasoning field. The removed local stream parser's hidden-reasoning behavior is historical; upstream providers own stream parsing. The separate ReasoningSummary activity is explicitly user-display content, bounded to 256 characters, and is not a hidden-reasoning capture. Server project_model_request maps only the typed projection fields to ModelRequestDetailResponse; it omits the internal safe provider_profile provenance field as well as transport credentials and configuration. The profile is not inserted into normalized provider request metadata (tests/provider_profile_provenance.rs covers this path). Web BranchActivityView loads detail only when the prompt presentation preference is shown, and the native TUI has the same opt-in prompt view. These paths do expose bounded model-visible prompt text when requested; they do not expose provider credentials, endpoint/header values, or hidden reasoning through the request projection.

No tests or builds were run for this audit. Existing focused source tests cover credential reflection at capture, request-content truncation, and streamed hidden-reasoning exclusion; the server fixture covers request-detail DTO projection, while the capture test owns the character-budget assertion. A deterministic fixture now extends the real HTTP credential case through request capture, SQLite-backed session persistence/reload, and the application request-detail read, checking the credential sentinel against both the loaded session and returned detail. A separate server fixture covers typed request detail DTO mapping; it does not combine SQLite reload with the server DTO dispatcher in one fixture. These fixtures were not run in this turn. Keep all §11 acceptance items unchecked until the new fixture and relevant runtime validation are run.

docs.title: 12. Protocol and Web Projection
docs.text:
The ScribeRig server/web client may need safe model information, but must not define another independent model schema.

Prefer one of:

  1. upstream public model snapshot serialized through a thin ScribeRig protocol wrapper;
  2. generated/versioned safe projection whose fields map directly to upstream public fields and preserve unknown extensible properties;
  3. stable upstream DTO contributed for remote presentation.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Web model/provider selectors consume server data derived from upstream state.
  • [x] Web thinking options come from upstream-derived state.
  • [x] Web exposes no custom-property editor; its model UI uses only the safe upstream model and thinking projections.
  • [ ] Rust protocol and TypeScript client fixtures cover the same current snake-case wire fields, including model IDs, scalar upstream thinking IDs, and nested pricing tiers; selector tests prove no ScribeRig-only capability inference is required. Source fixtures and decoder fields have been aligned, but this criterion remains unverified because no test/typecheck was run at the current pin.

docs.title: 13. TUI Model Controls
docs.text:
This task may prepare the data path, but task 147 performs the terminal-shell migration.

Do not spend this task building another ScribeRig model selector.

Reuse generic upstream selection widgets where suitable. CLI-specific model/provider/thinking selectors include CLI semantics and are not candidates for extraction as product controls. Task 147 should adapt ScribeRig's safe rows to generic upstream widgets.

Acceptance:

  • [x] No new local TUI selector is added.
  • [x] No new ScribeRig TUI selector framework is added.
  • [x] Generic upstream SelectItem, SelectList, and SearchableSelectList are reusable; CLI-specific model/provider selectors are not extraction candidates because they include CLI semantics.
  • [ ] ScribeRig TUI consumes generic upstream widgets with safe projected rows; task 147 owns this integration.
  • [ ] The native model-settings flow uses upstream property descriptors, validation, file-backed persistence, and transactional catalog publication. Source integration is present at the current pin; compile/runtime verification remains outstanding.

The pinned rpi-tui also exposes reusable SettingsList, Input, and Editor components. Fork commit 9f935d794053bccaf73737b5e2fb67cf3194a761 adds provider-owned property descriptors and validation/setter APIs in rpi-model-runtime; the current combined pin also includes the generic rpi_tui::PropertyEditor and ModelsConfigFile persistence API. ScribeRig's model-settings flow uses those upstream APIs. It must not add ScribeRig-owned property fields or arbitrary provider_options writes.

docs.title: 14. Focused Verification
docs.text:
Run focused tests for the changed ownership boundary, using current package/test names.

At minimum verify:

upstream catalog load -> ScribeRig selection resolution
provider package reload -> visible catalog refresh
thinking-level support changes by model
thinking clamp/map delegated upstream
custom model property passthrough/validation upstream
provider auth status safe projection
historical invocation provenance
protected credential sentinel absent from the actual provider request projection,
durable SQLite session, and reloaded model-request detail
agent profile execution reference
protocol round-trip
web model projection
  • [ ] Rust focused tests pass.
  • [ ] Protocol/client focused tests pass.
  • [ ] Web model/selector tests pass where affected.
  • [ ] No network-dependent test is required for deterministic catalog semantics.
  • [ ] Dependency review confirms ScribeRig is consuming upstream model/provider APIs rather than copied logic.

docs.title: 15. Deletion Gate
docs.text:
Before Complete, update task 144's deletion ledger.

The following should be Removed or explicitly Blocked on upstream:

local live model catalog authority
local thinking capability authority
local model capability authority — removed from runtime source: `ProviderCapabilities` and its fingerprint field are deleted; `RequestFingerprintInput` schema is now `model-request-v2` and hashes no provider capability descriptor. Upstream `ModelDefinition` remains the provider/model capability authority. Overall acceptance remains unchecked pending focused verification.
local provider auth/readiness authority — local `ProviderConfig` and `CredentialSource` aggregates are removed; catalog schema/configuration uses upstream `ModelsConfig`/`ProviderConfig`. ScribeRig retains destination authorization and its safe readiness projection because the upstream resolver cannot express the exact host `SecretRef`/endpoint policy. Provider acceptance and refresh remain open; overall acceptance remains unchecked.
local custom-property semantics
local provider package/catalog refresh machinery
  • [ ] No deleted owner still has a production call path.
  • [ ] Tests no longer instantiate the old catalog merely for convenience.
  • [ ] Compatibility DTOs, if retained, are clearly projections rather than authorities.

docs.title: 16. Completion Gate
docs.text:
• [ ] Re-read all checked criteria.
  • [ ] Confirm ScribeRig still owns branch/plan assignment semantics.
  • [ ] Confirm upstream owns provider/model/thinking/custom-property semantics.
  • [ ] Confirm no credential leakage was introduced.
  • [ ] Confirm task 144 deletion ledger is current.

docs.title: Dependency order
docs.text:
Task 145 cannot be completed before its dependent runtime, provenance, profile, and TUI work is verified. Keep this task In Progress while following this sequence; do not check blocked criteria or broaden the prerequisite work beyond the listed task slices:

The preflight gate for dependent implementation is satisfied only after the checked criteria have been re-read, the Task 144 ledger and pinned fork APIs have been rechecked, ScribeRig's ownership boundaries are confirmed, and every open criterion assigned to another task below has an explicit owner and evidence-based gate in this sheet. Unchecked downstream acceptance criteria remain unchecked during preflight.

  1. Complete Task 137 Phases A–F and verify their criteria before starting Phase G; Task 137 explicitly gates G1 on A–F passing. Reuse already-present behavior only after confirming it against that task's requirements, then complete G1–G4 to establish ScribeRig semantic profile ownership and the upstream-resolvable execution reference required by §10.
  2. After Task 145's ownership boundaries and upstream gates are documented, begin Task 146's provider/runtime/plugin integration. This prerequisite is required to verify §6–§9 and to provide the execution path needed by §11. Task 146 must allow this implementation after the Task 145 preflight gate while Task 145 remains In Progress; it must not require Task 145 completion.
  3. Complete the Task 136 work that captures continuation-aware effective requests and safe invocation provenance through the upstream execution path established by Task 146. Reverify §11 afterward.
  4. Begin Task 147 only after Task 146 is complete, as its own prerequisite requires. Verify §13's upstream widget consumption when Task 147 completes.
  5. Return to Task 145, re-read every checked criterion, reverify the criteria affected by Tasks 137, 146, 136, and 147, and refresh Task 144's ledger. Complete Task 145 only when every acceptance criterion is verified; keep each still-blocked item unchecked and the status In Progress until then.

Only Task 137 Phases A–G and the Task 146, 136, and 147 slices named above are authorized prerequisites to this gate. Do not start unrelated later phases.

Then set:

**Status: [ ] In Progress**

docs.title: 17.1 Upstream evidence and current gate
docs.text:
The prior audit inspected upstream commit aab74de0737f4b7c454cd8c8c16ca66e4dfbf898 (rpi 0.6.2). The user has selected the TNick/pi-rust fork as the intended source; missing APIs at upstream main are not a blocker. ScribeRig must consume a reviewed, committed fork revision and must never depend on fork working-tree changes.

  • rpi-ai/src/model.rs exposes upstream Model metadata and typed model properties, sampling/configuration fields, cost/context/output metadata, compatibility, and thinking maps. rpi-ai/src/types.rs defines ThinkingLevel and ThinkingLevelMap; model support, clamping, and provider-effort mapping are carried by the typed upstream value into the native built-in provider path.
  • rpi-ai/src/provider.rs and rpi-ai/src/providers/ expose provider traits, stream options, and provider implementations. Those APIs are the target for execution, but do not supply a product model registry/auth configuration service.
  • rpi-cli/src/model_registry.rs is public but is not a reusable catalog boundary: refresh_catalog reads CLI config directly, and no call site outside that module was found in the inspected rpi-cli tree.
  • The active product resolution path is rpi-cli/src/provider.rs: resolve_with_extensions, authenticated_catalog, catalog_with_manifests, and execution_catalog_with_manifests. It depends on CLI args/settings/config and rpi_extensions::ExtensionSession.
  • In the previously audited upstream-main revision, rpi-cli/src/credentials.rs was private and rpi-cli/src/auth.rs plus config.rs owned credential resolution and precedence. The selected fork extracts ordinary-string resolution/readiness APIs to rpi-model-runtime; ScribeRig consumes the protected request bridge and uses readiness_from_catalog only as one input to its safe host-authorized per-model readiness projection.
  • rpi-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs and settings.rs contain CLI-specific model/provider selection behavior and remain private to the CLI UI. Generic rpi-tui SelectList and SearchableSelectList widgets are already reusable; ScribeRig should adapt safe presentation rows to them rather than extracting the CLI-specific behavior.

The selected fork is TNick/pi-rust, branch codex/scriberig-integration. ScribeRig's package manifests and Cargo.lock now pin commit 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5. The earlier 714a778784bc99e982402114265bd99681857a10 pin included the previously reviewed a40890741880838d02532fd57ec365ade16725d1 catalog/config/auth APIs, canonical thinking-name parsing, model support/clamping, protected request-credential APIs with OpenAI Completions and Anthropic overrides, focused rpi-tui event-dispatch and terminal reader lifecycle changes, and a conservative model execution fingerprint and the error-bearing credential resolver described in §8. It also adds ordered live-catalog reconciliation, CLI registry/TUI catalog consumption, and the versioned fail-closed provider-options extension ABI. Focused upstream checks remain unverified and unchecked; no tests or builds were run.

The earlier 4a52baf41a19a889ca96c0f38369f7482f26973e commit is historical: it introduced the model-runtime catalog/config/auth APIs, thinking parsing and clamping, opaque provider_options, and the protected request seam before the built-in provider overrides and execution fingerprint were added. The prior d572c278 revision added those APIs; commit 2c69e8415e59dd1dbcbf035861ee1254b95f2828 adds the safe model snapshot and partial execution configuration APIs; commit 4ced7ab1a581fb6622e476f5fb4687dbe97f4eed adds the reusable package_resource_dirs extraction; a40890741880838d02532fd57ec365ade16725d1 adds the error-bearing credential resolver. At that fork commit (still present at the current 6e2f83b1 pin), Model.provider_options is skipped during ordinary serialization, built-in adapters reject non-empty values, and opted-in extension providers receive a versioned envelope. The local fork worktree now contains an uncommitted providerOptionsVersion: 1 opt-in and version-1 providerOptions envelope for extension calls, shared by one-shot and streaming providers. Legacy providers retain the original envelope when options are empty and fail closed when they lack v1 opt-in and options are non-empty. SDK contract documentation and manifest/envelope fixtures were added. The extension handoff forwards opaque values unchanged; it adds no built-in handling, validation, or safe applied-configuration provenance. It has only passed formatting and git diff --check; it is not yet a committed/pinned ScribeRig dependency. Built-in handling and safe applied-configuration provenance remain open. The earlier audit pins 24f79c15eafd25ca1fa29cea75ceae9436d1f94f and a15e8616e6d595b2d56d2199fbfd8386327d236d are historical only. The fork has reusable rpi-extensions::load_session and PluggableProvider::from_session plus rpi-model-runtime::build_catalog for caller-supplied package manifests; ScribeRig's opt-in native extension path composes the extension APIs. Package installation/update, package-directory policy, and CLI-specific model/provider selector orchestration remain in rpi-cli. The fork now has the reusable ModelCatalog snapshot/reconciliation store, but no provider configuration, package discovery, or refresh service. Generic rpi-tui SelectItem, SelectList, and SearchableSelectList are already reusable; ScribeRig can adapt safe rows without selector extraction.

The native catalog composition has moved to upstream ModelsConfig, build_catalog, and the fork's shared ModelCatalog. The app, native runner, TUI, and server share the same handle; each operation obtains an upstream snapshot. Selection uses resolve_selection, model-supported thinking levels, and upstream clamping for provider/model validation and plan assignment resolution. This covers selection support, clamping, and typed provider-effort mapping are upstream owned in the current execution path. Session and plan selection mutations now store and transmit explicit upstream provider_id + model_id; TUI and web pickers enumerate model descriptors and use local row IDs only as transient display handles. Protocol DTOs remain as a narrow server-boundary transport projection. The ScribeRig JSON catalog loader and app-owned ModelLibrary, ModelDescriptor, and model ID types have since been deleted; resolution.rs resolves from upstream models without a library parameter, and authorized app reads return SafeModelSnapshot rows directly. The server creates the public DTO from that safe upstream snapshot. Earlier references in this section to an application ModelLibrary or app-regenerated compatibility rows are superseded by this implementation. Old persisted model_profile/model session selections lose their model on deserialization, and old plan assignments using profile/model cannot deserialize into the new required provider/model pair. A safe persisted-data migration is still required; the IDs cannot be inferred without their old catalog. Provider package refresh/reload and upstream selector consumption remain later gates. Section 4 and selected criteria in sections 5–6 are checked; unchecked criteria remain in sections 5–12 and 15–16. Section 13's no-local-selector rule is met. Generic rpi-tui SelectItem, SelectList, and SearchableSelectList APIs are already reusable, so task 147 needs only to adapt ScribeRig's safe rows and consume them. CLI-specific model/provider orchestration remains private to rpi-cli and is not an extraction target. The native TUI consumes upstream model selectors, but safe protocol projection tests and a model-switch test remain unchecked. Upstream exposes provider-owned schema descriptors, validated setters, a generic PropertyEditor, and a ModelsConfigFile writer. ScribeRig consumes these APIs for file-backed configuration and leaves environment JSON and extension-only rows read-only. Task 147 still owns full TUI integration and visible-path verification; it must not invent ScribeRig property fields or store arbitrary option JSON. This is separate from request-property routing in §7.

The native catalog path composes upstream models. The app-owned model/library types have been deleted, and no app compatibility model rows remain. The versioned ModelLibraryResponse and its web/client types remain only as safe transport projections; they are generated at the server boundary from upstream snapshots. Native provider execution composition and session execution provenance remain separate migration concerns. The legacy JSON loader has been deleted; production resolution.rs resolves from upstream models without a library parameter.

The app-owned ModelLibrary, ModelCapabilities, and ModelDescriptor have since been removed. AgentConsoleBackend::agent_model_library returns Vec<rpi_model_runtime::SafeModelSnapshot> from the shared live catalog; selection resolves against that same upstream catalog. The server maps safe snapshots into the public protocol DTO only at the transport boundary. A live catalog replacement/removal fixture exists in crates/scriberig-app/tests/session_runtime.rs, but it has not been run, so criteria requiring focused runtime verification remain unchecked.

The protocol and web model-library projection has now dropped the permanently empty curated-profile field, its credential-reference DTO, and the capability booleans that the upstream model does not provide and ScribeRig always emitted as false. The application-side schema and default-false projection have also been deleted. Rust server and TUI projection plus TypeScript normalization now expose only safe model identifiers/display names and the upstream-derived thinking rows used by the selector. Legacy JSON profile/capability properties are ignored when received as unknown fields; they are no longer part of the typed response. This removes only unused compatibility claims: model selection still uses the provider/model pair, and no headers, credentials, or opaque provider options are projected. Focused protocol/client/web tests were not run, so the fixture changes remain unchecked as runtime evidence. Configured requests now use upstream provider construction and the protected request-secret bridge; the partial applied-settings report is captured, but focused persistence/omission verification remains outstanding. Provider authentication acceptance, host-authorized readiness projection, and dynamic refresh remain separate unchecked gates.

docs.title: 17.2 Native upstream catalog composition
docs.text:
apps/scriberig pins rpi-ai and rpi-model-runtime to fork revision 714a778784bc99e982402114265bd99681857a10 at that audit point; the current pin is recorded above. The native catalog loader parses SCRIBE_AGENT_MODEL_CATALOG as upstream ModelsConfig JSON and calls build_catalog with configured built-in models; registered extension models are merged from their upstream manifests. The former ScribeRig models/connections/thinking_levels schema is no longer consumed. When no provider model is configured, the host adds a minimal upstream OpenAI Completions model from SCRIBE_AGENT_MODEL.

The native runner seeds the shared ModelCatalog from the returned Vec<rpi_ai::Model> and passes the same handle to the TUI and HTTP application services. with_upstream_models remains a compatibility seeder for static callers. A credential-free ModelLibrary remains as a compatibility protocol/UI projection. Live session and plan assignments carry upstream provider/model IDs and resolve directly through rpi_model_runtime; local profile rows do not participate in that path. Its thinking list is derived from upstream model support. Configured built-in and extension routes use upstream providers; deterministic scenario execution retains a local compatibility adapter. The public model-library projection no longer includes capability booleans because the upstream Model does not provide the equivalent flags.

Session selection mutations and history, plan assignments, and Rust and TypeScript request/response mappings now carry provider/model pairs. The server's model-selection history projection returns that pair. Legacy single-model history cannot be mapped safely without the retired catalog and remains a migration concern.

Display model IDs and the temporary native selector identifier use a versioned provider/model composite with UTF-8 byte-length-prefixed components in the form rpi1:<provider-byte-length>:<provider><model-byte-length>:<model> for every catalog entry, even when the model ID is currently unique. This remains injective when either ID contains separators or Unicode text. Live assignment identity is the pair itself, not this composite. Provider construction binds the exact resolved Model; only deterministic scenario compatibility uses a local adapter lookup.

The host resolver supports literal values and simple $NAME/${NAME} references; it does not execute upstream command expressions. Before calling build_catalog, the loader strips provider/model typed api_key, auth_header, and header maps. It rejects catalog configuration that contains those typed fields with a generic error, so those values are neither resolved nor retained in rpi_ai::Model. Unknown model fields are retained in the upstream provider_options map and are not inspected for credential-like names; this map is neither serialized into ScribeRig records nor treated as safe durable provenance. Catalog-supplied auth and headers are rejected by the ScribeRig loader. The host resolves its selected credential only after the exact upstream model endpoint is fixed, and passes it through RequestSecret. ScribeRig does not use upstream's provider-keyed source precedence because the host selects a single authorized SecretRef. The legacy ConfigValueResolver and ordinary-string resolve_credential APIs cannot satisfy the destination-authorized SecretValue boundary. Fork commit 4a52baf41a19a889ca96c0f38369f7482f26973e adds a separate protected-material source resolver in rpi-model-runtime and request-only secret handle in rpi-ai; the ordinary CLI string APIs remain available. The former pin 4a52baf41a19a889ca96c0f38369f7482f26973e had only the default stream_simple_with_request_secret method, which fails closed. ScribeRig now pins 9f935d794053bccaf73737b5e2fb67cf3194a761, which includes commit a40890741880838d02532fd57ec365ade16725d1 where OpenAI Completions and Anthropic implement the protected method. The current fork also exposes protected streaming extension callbacks and an applied-settings report ABI. ScribeRig consumes these seams in configured built-in and opt-in native extension routes. Legacy extension callbacks fail closed when protected credentials or model headers are required. The upstream ProtectedCredentialResolver::resolve(CredentialRequestSource) still receives source descriptors but no destination endpoint. ScribeRig's scriberig-secrets::registry::AuthorizedCredential::credential(endpoint) in crates/scriberig-secrets/src/registry/authorized.rs rechecks live user and system policy against the exact endpoint; the policy is defined in crates/scriberig-secrets/src/policy.rs. The implemented request bridge is scoped to one exact upstream model and binds its endpoint before resolving the host credential. It returns errors without source fallthrough and passes material only as RequestSecret. It does not use ordinary-string AuthStore or weaken endpoint authorization.

At the pre-a408907 pin, there was a second fail-closed gap, now closed upstream: ProtectedCredentialResolver::resolve returns Option, and resolve_credential_protected continues to lower-priority sources when the resolver returns None. AuthorizedCredential::credential returns Result<Option<SecretValue>, SecretError>, so mapping an authorization or source error to None would erase the distinction between denied and missing and could allow fallback from an explicit source. The bridge must propagate a host authorization/resolution failure and stop source iteration before any provider call. Commit a408907 adds CredentialResolutionError, resolve_with_policy, and resolve_credential_protected_with_policy; the legacy resolver maps errors to credential-free Missing without fallback. The default resolve_with_policy implementation delegates to legacy resolve, so hosts must override it to report authorization denial or resolver failure instead of treating those conditions as a source miss. Its focused source test covers legacy fail-closed behavior; tests/builds were not run. This upstream API does not replace ScribeRig's host-selected credential contract: ScribeRig resolves one effective credential reference in apps/scriberig/src/agent_config.rs, not the upstream provider-keyed AuthStore, and the native catalog rejects model-configured credentials. The request bridge binds the selected model and exact endpoint to that host credential provider, and calls upstream's protected HostSelected resolver without applying unrelated upstream source precedence.
