The provider readiness projection uses that same upstream resolver and readiness_from_catalog, then reports the safe source classification; it does not claim provider acceptance or refresh catalog/provider state.

SecretValue::expose is wrapped by the existing rpi_ai::SecretMaterial adapter in crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/protected_credential.rs; the opaque RequestSecret carries it to the upstream async provider. Configured native built-in root/plan requests, one-shot CLI, and doctor use the upstream provider factory. NativeProvider::OpenAiCompatible and the app's local catalog-row adapter construction have been removed. Catalog credentials and headers are rejected. Built-in routes fail closed on non-empty opaque provider_options; the opt-in extension route forwards them only through the versioned extension ABI. Neither path turns these values into a ScribeRig property schema. The file-backed native model editor uses upstream descriptors, validation, and ModelsConfigFile persistence; environment JSON and extension-only rows remain read-only. Provider/package refresh and complete effective-request property provenance remain open. The generic server constructor does not load local catalog JSON; product composition passes host-loaded upstream models explicitly.

The pinned fork's rpi_model_runtime::ModelDefinition parses typed sampling, compatibility, reasoning, modality, limit, cost, and header fields, and carries unknown values in provider_options. provider_to_models copies these values to rpi_ai::Model. The configured built-in path passes the exact model to the upstream factory, which applies supported typed settings and fails closed on non-empty opaque provider_options. The opt-in extension path forwards opaque options only through the versioned ABI and captures provider-attested applied-settings reports. ScribeRig's native model-settings flow uses upstream property descriptors, safe-editor classification, PropertyEditor, schema validation, and ModelsConfigFile persistence for file-backed configuration. Environment JSON and extension-only rows remain read-only. ScribeRig has no local property schema or arbitrary-option validator. This remains a configuration boundary, not a local request-construction adapter gap.

At the historically inspected fork revision 4a52baf41a19a889ca96c0f38369f7482f26973e, rpi_model_runtime::ModelDefinition exposes typed reasoning, thinking_level_map, context_window, max_tokens, cost, sampling_params, input, headers, and compat fields, plus flattened unknown fields in provider_options. provider_to_models carries these into rpi_ai::Model. The upstream OpenAI Completions provider applies known sampling values, while model compatibility metadata shapes requests. The Model serializer includes baseUrl, headers, samplingParams, and compat; only provider_options is skipped. The typed compat enum also has an Other(Value) variant, and sampling values are arbitrary JSON. Therefore serializing Model for a public protocol projection could expose headers or endpoint secrets, and copying those arbitrary values into a ScribeRig-owned allowlist/bag would create a parallel property projection contract.

That historical revision's only reusable fingerprint is rpi_model_runtime::model_configuration_fingerprint. It serializes the model, removes headers, canonicalizes the remaining JSON, and hashes it. Its own documentation warns that the digest omits runtime-only provider_options and may omit output-affecting headers. It includes baseUrl, arbitrary sampling values, and opaque compatibility values, with no sensitivity classification or completeness/version marker. ScribeRig does not use this digest as a public snapshot or request-equivalence proof. Commit a40890741880838d02532fd57ec365ade16725d1 introduced the current execution fingerprint API, which remains available at ScribeRig pin 9f935d794053bccaf73737b5e2fb67cf3194a761 as conservative partial provenance: it partial provenance: it excludes endpoint unconditionally and reports conditional exclusions for headers, runtime provider_options, arbitrary sampling parameters, provider-specific thinking maps, and opaque compatibility values. Its complete flag is always false because endpoint is excluded. ScribeRig does not consume this fingerprint as applied-settings evidence. The active provider callback captures the separate report described in §17.3. Keep §7 and §11 unchecked until persisted reports, request fingerprints, and omission semantics are verified together. Any claim of complete execution identity still requires a separately defined, fully covered fingerprint. Opaque extension options use a separate versioned handoff and attestation path.

Fork commit 2c69e8415e59dd1dbcbf035861ee1254b95f2828 adds public rpi_model_runtime::safe_model_snapshot and rpi_model_runtime::safe_model_execution_configuration APIs on codex/model-runtime-extraction. The first returns schema rpi-safe-model-snapshot-v1 with provider/model/API identity, display name, reasoning, input modalities, typed costs and limits, upstream-supported thinking levels, and known typed compatibility flags. It excludes endpoint URLs, headers, sampling properties, provider options, provider-specific thinking mapping strings, and opaque compatibility JSON, and reports exclusion categories. The second returns schema rpi-safe-model-execution-v1; it allowlists numeric temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, and integer seed, max_tokens, and max_completion_tokens. It counts unknown or malformed sampling entries without exposing their names or values, reports excluded execution categories, and always sets complete to false. It does not establish which properties a provider ultimately applied. ScribeRig consumes the display snapshot for model rows; it does not attach the execution configuration projection to invocation history because the current provider path cannot prove those model values were applied to a request.

The display mapping is snapshot.provider_id -> protocol provider_id, snapshot.model_id -> provider_model_id, snapshot.display_name -> display_name, and snapshot.thinking_levels -> the existing ordered thinking display rows. The app's thin ModelMetadataSnapshot and protocol's PublicModelMetadataSnapshot carry only schema_version, api_id, reasoning, input, typed cost and cost_configured, context_window, and max_tokens. compatibility remains excluded because it is request-shaping metadata, and excluded_execution_fields is not copied to the public DTO. Generate the transient ScribeRig row ID from the provider/model pair as before. The old local default-thinking field was removed because the upstream safe snapshot has no model default; choosing a level remains an upstream resolution operation. Do not serialize rpi_ai::Model or treat either API as proof of effective-request equivalence. The protocol crate should not depend on rpi-model-runtime; map explicitly through the app and server/TUI protocol adapters, then normalize the versioned DTO in web/packages/client/src/model-views.ts. The upstream snapshot's camelCase serde representation differs from the existing Rust protocol's snake_case wire convention, so ScribeRig retains an explicit snake-case wrapper.

Static source review confirms the DTO omits every upstream-listed excluded category and does not copy headers, endpoints, sampling values, provider options, opaque compatibility data, or excluded-category names. The app now retains upstream rpi_ai::ThinkingLevel values directly; protocol and web types carry only their ordered scalar string identifiers. The old ScribeRig ThinkingLevelDescriptor type and public re-export are removed. The TypeScript normalizer accepts only scalar thinking-level IDs; it no longer reconstructs the retired object descriptor form. No supported compatibility consumer for that object form was found in the client or repository docs. The current fixture uses provider_id, provider_model_id, and scalar IDs. Rust omits empty pricing tiers, so the TypeScript wire type marks tiers optional; the normalizer materializes an empty array for consumers. Nested pricing tiers are also covered by the Rust protocol fixture. These focused tests were not run, and there is not yet one physical JSON fixture shared by the Rust and TypeScript test suites; leave the §6 projection and §12 cross-surface fixture criteria unchecked until focused tests pass.

The reusable package_resource_dirs extraction exists in commit 4ced7ab1a581fb6622e476f5fb4687dbe97f4eed and is used by the native extension loader for the fixed extensions resource under explicitly supplied package roots. Package registry authorization, installation, update, and reload policy remain outside that helper and are not implemented by ScribeRig. Safe projection acceptance remains unchecked until ScribeRig maps and validates every projected field, excluded values stay out of protocol/web fixtures, and focused Rust protocol/client and web projection checks are completed.

This slice does not complete the task: the remaining narrow protocol display DTOs are still ScribeRig wrappers rather than upstream public snapshot types, historical profile IDs cannot be recovered from the retired ScribeRig catalog format. Provider-auth status is a safe readiness projection only, and auth-status refresh remains incomplete. Property editing and file-backed persistence use upstream descriptors, validators, and config types; their transactional live-catalog publication awaits the fork API noted below. The public model_library_from_json helper, its JSON parser, and obsolete tests have been removed. The application has no caller-supplied model projection setter or cached model rows: each model-library response is projected from the complete upstream model vector held by the service. The app DTO has direct model-row construction only, with no local profile/credential rows, catalog validator, or model/profile lookup methods. Live execution selection remains provider/model-pair based. The protocol/web model-library contract no longer contains profile or credential-reference rows. Native-plan fixtures now configure only upstream models. This removes the local JSON catalog parser, cached app projection authority, and app-level profile/credential projection; the application/server/client/protocol model DTO flow remains a deletion target. Static source inspection verifies the app projection and retired wire fields are absent. No tests were run for this slice; the catalog-change criterion remains unchecked.

The local OpenAI-compatible provider's global and model-specific thinking translation maps, their request-writer mapping APIs, and the associated mapping tests have since been removed. The adapter no longer claims to map upstream thinking levels to provider effort: §6 provider mapping and serialization remain unchecked until the upstream provider integration owns that behavior. WireRequest.provider_parameters and its flattening path have also been removed, so the local adapter cannot forward arbitrary model custom properties. §7 custom-property routing, validation, unknown-property passthrough, and provenance criteria remain unchecked pending upstream integration. The unused RequestFingerprintInput::with_credential builder and its private credential String were removed as well; this local cleanup does not establish end-to-end credential isolation, so the broad §8 and §11 security/provenance criteria remain unchecked.

docs.title: Custom model-property execution and UI boundary
docs.text:
At the current ScribeRig pin, rpi_ai::Model carries typed sampling, compatibility, thinking-map, modality, cost, context/output-limit, endpoint, and header fields plus runtime-only provider_options. Built-in OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic providers consume the model at the request boundary and report allowlisted settings they actually prepared. Opaque provider_options are rejected by built-ins; opt-in extensions receive them through the versioned extension envelope and can attest applied settings.

The native root path retains the exact model from its selection snapshot; ResolvedPlanExecution retains the exact model used for plan selection. Both bind that value through rpi_model_runtime::create_builtin_provider and carry typed rpi_ai::ThinkingLevel through UpstreamBranchInvocation to the provider. Scalar names remain at storage, history, and protocol boundaries. The generic ModelRequest and ProviderAdapter were removed from production, and deterministic scenarios now use upstream test support. openai_request.rs and the local compatible HTTP provider were deleted. The remaining Task 146 gate is verifying end-to-end report persistence, not adding a ScribeRig property validator or serializer.

The public protocol DTO exposes only versioned safe display snapshot fields in scriberig-protocol/src/model.rs; scriberig-app returns upstream safe snapshots directly. web/packages/protocol/src/models.ts and web/packages/agent-ui/src/model-controls.tsx expose model and thinking selection, not custom-property editing. The native TUI picker selects model and thinking rows. A separate native model-settings flow uses upstream rpi_tui::PropertyEditor items created from upstream descriptors and writes only file-backed upstream configuration. ScribeRig adds no property schema or validator. Do not make the picker or public model DTO carry arbitrary property values.

docs.title: 17.3 Implemented consumer slice
docs.text:
scriberig-app consumes rpi-ai and rpi-model-runtime from the then-current fork commit 714a778784bc99e982402114265bd99681857a10; the current pin is recorded above. App selection and validation use rpi_ai::ThinkingLevel directly after parsing persisted scalar IDs through upstream ThinkingLevel::parse_name; no wrapper type or local supported-level authority remains. ScribeRig session and plan assignments retain provider/model pairs rather than local model-profile IDs. Application validation no longer accepts arbitrary thinking names or rejects a canonical upstream level because it is absent from the local presentation list. Model switching preserves a valid current thinking choice and lets upstream clamp it for the newly selected model; it does not choose the first entry in the display projection. The service stores a cloneable upstream ModelCatalog handle and captures coherent snapshots for each selection or projection operation. The native runner, TUI service, and server composition share that catalog handle.

Safe model-library presentation levels are rebuilt from each upstream model's supported_thinking_levels. App selection and plan assignment resolution use rpi_model_runtime::resolve_selection for provider/model matching and effective thinking-level clamping. The scheduler carries the host catalog to the assignment resolver. Unassigned runtime fallback models are matched in the upstream catalog and then passed through resolve_selection; missing or provider-ambiguous fallback IDs fail selection. Existing fixtures now inject explicit upstream models and use canonical thinking IDs.

ResolvedPlanExecution marks when resolution used the host runtime fallback and retains the exact upstream Model plus typed rpi_ai::ThinkingLevel from the catalog snapshot used for resolution. The native plan worker binds that same model directly to the provider and passes the typed thinking value; it does not re-resolve model identity or parse a thinking string. The native root path does the same. Scalar thinking IDs remain at storage, protocol, and historical provenance boundaries. The native plan worker selects the same configured local adapter used by ordinary unselected turns, while retaining the upstream provider/model pair for selection and provenance. Explicit provider/model selections continue to use their pair-keyed adapter.

Generated display model IDs and temporary native adapter lookup IDs are versioned, length-prefixed provider/model composites, so embedded separators cannot alias a different pair. Live assignments store the pair directly. Existing persisted local profile/model references cannot be mapped safely without their original catalog. scriberig-session-sqlite now imports the known legacy session and plan assignment shapes into a versioned recovery envelope. Typed execution is left unselected, while recognized legacy selection fields retain their exact values and source paths through legacy_execution_records; they survive session save and both compare-and-swap paths. Explicit operator reset can discard this recovery data with discard_legacy_execution_records. No provider/model ID is inferred from old names or ModelInvocation history. An archived exact catalog plus unique-match validation is still required before any legacy choice can be mapped to current upstream IDs.

The catalog loader strips provider/model typed API keys, auth headers, and request header maps before build_catalog, and rejects catalog configs containing those typed values. Opaque model provider_options are not inspected for credential-like names and must not be treated as safe for durable records. The loader does not resolve credential references or copy API-key references into local adapters. Configured provider credentials use the host-authorized request-secret bridge; catalog-specific credential references remain unsupported because upstream's source resolver cannot express the host's exact SecretRef/endpoint authorization contract. The ScribeRig-configured default provider endpoint and credential use that same host configuration boundary.

The local ThinkingLevelDescriptor has since been removed. The app carries upstream rpi_ai::ThinkingLevel values, while protocol and web model rows expose ordered scalar identifiers. ModelLibrary and model metadata DTOs remain thin presentation projections. Built-in provider request shaping and protected credential transport now use upstream. Provider acceptance/readiness status, custom-property editing/persistence, and persisted legacy assignment migration remain incomplete; scalar projection acceptance remains unchecked pending focused verification. For the present profile/provenance and persistence slice, no tests, builds, or workspace-wide checks were run. Static source inspection confirmed the fork selection/fingerprint limits. At the time of the earlier SQLite recovery audit, invocation provenance fields were unset; the later §11 slice now persists the resolved provider/model identity for native root and recursive-child requests, while complete request-configuration provenance remains open. Scoped rustfmt and git diff --check passed for the SQLite recovery changes. The legacy schema's typed selection/assignment values contain profile, model, and optional thinking identifiers; credential references belong to the separate retired catalog type and were not part of persisted session choices. The importer exposes only an allowlisted projection of those historical selection fields, dropping unknown credential-like properties. load and list now lazily rewrite any noncanonical legacy payload in an immediate SQLite transaction, preserving the recovery envelope while removing untyped extension fields from storage. Save and both compare-and-swap paths continue to carry the envelope forward. Focused fixtures inspect the stored payload after both load and list; they were not run, so task acceptance remains unchecked pending validation.

docs.title: Profile execution references and invocation provenance gate
docs.text:
The pinned fork exposes rpi_model_runtime::ModelSelection and resolve_selection for exact provider/model/thinking resolution. Its rpi_agent::AgentBuilder accepts an upstream rpi_ai::Model and thinking level, but the fork has no reusable profile-reference type or profile resolution API. Task 137 defines provider-neutral AgentProfileDescriptor and ContextComponentDescriptor types and a deterministic built-in bootstrap profile in scriberig-agent-core and scriberig-agent-runtime. Request capture now records the exact profile and active component identity/revision references used for context compilation, along with ScribeRig context and canonical request fingerprints. These captured references do not by themselves establish the shared semantic profile read, resolution, and candidate-promotion operations required by Task 137. Do not add a parallel model catalog to fill that gap; §10 acceptance remains unchecked pending its remaining shared semantic operations and verification.

The retired session and plan selection structs stored only profile/model/ thinking identifiers, not a resolved provider credential. The former catalog's CredentialRef was a reference value and was not part of Session or ModelAssignment. Recovery deliberately projects only those typed identifier fields (plus the selection revision) and drops unknown keys before exposing a record, so unexpected credential-like extension values are not returned by legacy_execution_records.

Historical invocation records now persist the resolved upstream provider id and provider model id for native root, recursive-child, and plan-worker requests. When available, the CLI ScribeRig provider_profile is captured separately from upstream provider_id. The projection and invocation retain the exact profile and active component identity/revision references, ScribeRig context fingerprint, and canonical request fingerprint. The bounded request projection includes the selected model and thinking level, messages, and tools. A provider-attested applied_settings report is captured after request preparation and stored in that projection; the report contains only upstream-allowlisted values and explicit omitted categories. The upstream model_execution_fingerprint is a versioned digest of a conservative model-metadata projection, not a complete effective-request fingerprint. It always excludes the endpoint and may also exclude headers, runtime provider_options, arbitrary sampling parameters, provider-specific thinking maps, and opaque compatibility data; complete is therefore false. The deprecated model_configuration_fingerprint compatibility API delegates to this digest but returns less coverage metadata. Neither API proves which configuration the provider applied. Do not persist the full upstream Model, Debug output, headers, credentials, or opaque provider options to paper over this gap.

ScribeRig's request fingerprint is a local identity for the canonical provider-neutral request projection. It covers provider identity/profile, model and thinking selection, exact profile/component revisions, compiled context fingerprint, messages, tools, and local request controls included in ModelRequest. Its context inputs remain ScribeRig-owned and must not be replaced by an upstream model-configuration digest. It does not include the upstream Model configuration or prove what provider fields were applied. The active local ModelCache key separately identifies the normalized ScribeRig ModelRequest and its cache namespace; neither fingerprint is output-affecting upstream model-property provenance.

The fork provides rpi_ai::AppliedRequestSettings. Built-in OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic providers report field-typed, allowlisted values from the final prepared request body. The report omits credentials, all headers, prompt/transcript, tools/schemas, and opaque fields, so it remains explicitly incomplete. Extension providers can attest through their versioned callback; providers without attestation use the explicitly-incomplete fallback. upstream_invocation.rs captures the callback into ModelRequestProjection.applied_settings; persistence and the existing authorized model-request detail response carry that value to history readers. This source path is implemented, but focused persistence/omission tests have not been run. The current rpi-ai provider response also has optional public request/model identifiers, but the runtime path must preserve them to the embedding application; ScribeRig's current ProviderMetadata is discarded before session persistence. The ScribeRig adapter can copy only declared-safe applied-configuration provenance alongside its resolved provider/model/thinking identity and effective-request identity. ScribeRig persists exact profile and component references, request/context fingerprints, and the partial report in ModelRequestProjection.applied_settings. The projection now also retains the upstream-defined SafeModelExecutionConfiguration and incorporates that versioned safe snapshot into its request fingerprint. It carries recognized sampling overrides plus explicit omission metadata; it does not prove those settings appeared in the final provider body. Current request projections exclude provider configuration credentials and headers, though they intentionally retain bounded model-visible messages and tool schemas. Model-property fingerprinting and complete-configuration criteria remain unchecked: the upstream snapshot and applied report still omit request-affecting categories. Focused persistence and omission verification remains outstanding.

docs.title: Thinking selection ownership audit (2026-10-21)
docs.text: The current native TUI presents ordered scalar thinking IDs from the safe ModelLibraryResponse projection in runtime/upstream/selector_factory.rs. That list is copied from rpi_model_runtime::SafeModelSnapshot; the TUI does not define supported levels, map provider effort, clamp, or choose a fallback. The selection intent reaches ApplicationService::set_session_thinking_level, which parses rpi_ai::ThinkingLevel and delegates support/clamping to rpi_model_runtime::resolve_selection. Native invocation resolution likewise uses resolve_execution_selection_typed with the upstream rpi_ai::Model catalog. Thus the scalar protocol IDs and selector rows are transport and presentation projections, not a second authority. The generic selectable widget is upstream rpi_tui::SelectList; a reusable model-control workflow would still need extraction from the CLI if more than row presentation or selection mechanics are to be shared. No supported-level list or independent clamping logic should be added to ScribeRig. Focused switch and selection verification remains outstanding, so related acceptance items stay unchecked.

docs.title: Generic property safety classification (2026-10-21)
docs.text: The TUI previously duplicated recursive JSON Schema checks for secret-like keys, password formats, writeOnly, readOnly, x-sensitive, nested properties, and composite values. This classification now lives on upstream rpi_model_runtime::ModelPropertyDescriptor::is_safe_for_generic_editor in fork commit 13b07a9. The ScribeRig adapter consumes that upstream decision and retains only conversion to upstream rpi_tui::PropertyEditorItem plus ScribeRig application callbacks. The upstream model-runtime crate and focused ScribeRig TUI/app dependency graph compile against the new pin. Tests remain unrun per the current instruction; no checklist verification item was checked.

docs.title: Safe model execution provenance (2026-10-21)
docs.text: Each upstream invocation stores the upstream SafeModelExecutionConfiguration snapshot in ModelRequestProjection.model_execution_configuration. The base request fingerprint includes this versioned snapshot, so changes to recognized safe sampling overrides or schema-safe provider properties alter the historical request identity. Fork commit cec3e986aacfb7768fae1b1468e8069a7146e5e2, included in the current ScribeRig pin, adds schema-screened boolean, integer, numeric, and enumerated string provider options to this upstream snapshot. Secret-like, composite, undeclared, and otherwise unrecognized options are omitted with counts, not names or values. The snapshot reports fields it omits; it still does not establish what the provider applied or provide complete request-configuration coverage. Targeted offline Cargo checks for the upstream model-runtime crate and ScribeRig agent-runtime/session persistence passed, along with workspace formatting and whitespace checks. No tests were run and acceptance checkboxes remain unchecked.

docs.title: Applied-settings fingerprint boundary (2026-10-21)
docs.text: The runtime stores a separately versioned digest of the upstream AppliedRequestSettings report when the provider callback arrives and folds the safe report into the request fingerprint with a versioned domain separator. Before persistence or forwarding, ScribeRig verifies the report schema and provider/model/API identity against the exact bound model. An incomplete report must name omitted categories; a complete report is accepted only when the producer marks it complete. The upstream report's allowlisted values remain opaque to ScribeRig. Durable projections carry the report and both digests through the existing invocation detail path. These source paths establish only a fingerprint of available provenance: endpoints, credentials/headers, prompt/tool payloads, provider-specific opaque transforms, and other omitted request effects mean there is still no canonical complete effective-request fingerprint. Keep §7/§11 acceptance unchecked pending focused persistence and omission verification.

docs.title: Upstream catalog endpoint resolution (2026-10-21)
docs.text: The generic provider/model endpoint expression loop was removed from apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/provider_config/catalog.rs. The host now delegates it to rpi_model_runtime::resolve_model_endpoints, which applies model-level precedence over provider-level configuration using the host's ConfigValueResolver and returns a non-sensitive unresolved-endpoint error. The API was added in fork commit 1d1d7cc7e74a5fc26c162d4aef754a5705f7f10f and was included in integration commit 714a778784bc99e982402114265bd99681857a10; all ScribeRig rpi-* dependencies now pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5. ScribeRig retains only its host-specific fallback-model insertion, destination authorization, and endpoint override policy. Offline checks passed for the runtime/session crates and the scriberig application. No tests were run; acceptance remains unchecked.

docs.title: Host-injected model catalog refresh boundary (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
The controlled TNick/pi-rust fork now has a host-injected refresh API in rpi-model-runtime::ModelCatalog::refresh_from_configuration. The host supplies the mutable ModelsConfig, package manifests, ConfigValueResolver, and a fallible preparation callback. The API builds from a cloned configuration, publishes only after preparation succeeds, returns the exact committed snapshot, and leaves caller configuration and catalog unchanged on preparation failure. It contains no CLI globals, credential reads, or filesystem policy. The upstream CLI registry continues reconciling its existing shared ModelCatalog; its refresh path does not create a second model catalog.

ScribeRig's native loader now uses this API and stores the same catalog handle in NativeTuiAgentRunner. Startup reads its published snapshot and shares the same handle with app/server/TUI projections without a second reconciliation. Configured in-process extension paths are rejected before any native plugin loads. Catalog configuration failures use HostConfigurationError, not the removed provider transport taxonomy. Catalog rows are no longer filtered by a ScribeRig built-in API allowlist; provider creation reports an unsupported selected API at the upstream provider boundary. The fork changes were published to the controlled codex/host-injected-catalog-refresh branch and are pinned by all ScribeRig rpi-* dependencies at 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5. Provider instance/package reload and refresh-aligned provider generations are still separate; do not treat this catalog publication seam as end-to-end hot reload. ScribeRig integration compile checks and fixture execution remain pending, so all refresh acceptance criteria stay unchecked.

docs.title: Provider readiness ownership review (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
Readiness has no missing reusable fork API at this boundary. Upstream owns the credential-source vocabulary and catalog-header detection through CredentialSource, resolve_host_selected_credential_with_policy, and readiness_from_catalog. The ScribeRig resolver binds the single selected SecretRef to the exact model endpoint and returns only a host-selected protected value; AccessDenied and resolver failure remain errors rather than falling through to another credential source. The native readiness adapter drops that value and maps upstream source/error results into the ScribeRig wire enum. Available, Missing, NotRequired, and CatalogHeader are safe transport/display projections, while Denied preserves host authorization failure. They do not claim provider acceptance or authenticated connectivity.

The Rust protocol enum and matching TypeScript union are transport schema, not credential-source or auth-resolution authorities. The browser client validates wire values and TUI presentation renders them; neither resolves credentials. Unsupported is currently accepted by the protocol/client and rendered by the TUI but is not produced by the native adapter or by an upstream CredentialSource; keep it documented as a legacy/future wire value rather than treating it as an upstream readiness result. No upstream contribution is needed for this projection. Focused Rust/TypeScript projection checks remain unrun, and the auth-status/reload acceptance items stay unchecked because the current status is an availability projection and no refresh/auth-response producer is wired to update it.

docs.title: App catalog removal and wire projection boundary (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
The app-owned ModelDescriptor, ModelId, and ModelLibrary types have been deleted. AgentConsoleBackend::agent_model_library now returns the published upstream SafeModelSnapshot rows directly; the app no longer creates a second model list or synthetic model identity. The server and local TUI adapt those rows into the versioned, allowlisted scriberig-protocol model response at their respective transport boundaries. The protocol row ID is a stable presentation key, not catalog identity or persisted ScribeRig model state.

The Rust protocol no longer accepts the retired provider_profile alias as a model provider identity. The TypeScript model-library contract now requires the current metadata snapshot, and the client decoder validates the Rust snake-case model, readiness, and nested pricing fields rather than silently defaulting missing model metadata or translating profile aliases. The existing client fixture still includes retired profile/capability data to verify that those values are ignored, and now includes the complete current upstream metadata shape; a focused assertion rejects a profile-only provider identity. The Rust protocol fixture similarly rejects that retired alias. Neither fixture has been run, so the §12 wire-fixture acceptance item remains unchecked.

The web client model decoder now rejects a malformed present cost-tier array, non-integral token thresholds, and unsafe integer context/output limits while continuing to accept the omitted empty tiers field that Rust deliberately omits. This mirrors the Rust field types without adding a ScribeRig model capability inference. The prettier and tsc launchers are present in this worktree, but no typecheck or tests were run for this documentation/audit pass. Keep §12 fixture/typecheck acceptance unchecked.

docs.title: Transactional model-property publication and credential boundary review (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
The native property editor obtains ModelPropertyDescriptor rows from the upstream catalog, and update_model_config_property performs schema validation and updates a candidate ModelsConfig. The host remains responsible for the chosen file path and serialization policy. The previous sequence saved the candidate and then separately reconciled a locally edited model vector, so a failed catalog preparation could leave disk and live state inconsistent.

A reusable upstream ModelCatalog::refresh_from_configuration_with_commit API has been added on local fork branch codex/transactional-model-config-publication, then combined into the pinned fork integration 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5. It builds and host-prepares a candidate model set, invokes a host persistence callback with the candidate config, and publishes the shared catalog and caller config only after that callback succeeds. Upstream regression coverage was added for persistence failure atomicity and successful publication but has not been run. The native file-backed property flow now uses this API, retaining resolved host endpoint overrides and stripping headers before publication. The upstream property descriptor drives the TUI filter, and the save command independently checks is_safe_for_generic_editor, so secret-like, write-only, read-only, and composite properties cannot be written through a direct command call that bypasses the UI filter. Persistence uses upstream ModelsConfigFile::save, which stages and atomically replaces the selected file. This fork contribution is included in the current pin. The property-settings checklist remains unchecked until the ScribeRig call site is compile- and runtime-verified.

The provider credential boundary is separate from model properties. The host selects one ScribeRig SecretRef, authorizes it for the exact upstream model endpoint, and supplies it through RequestSecret using upstream's HostSelected resolver. The ScribeRig path does not invoke upstream's provider-keyed CLI/auth-store/environment precedence. Catalog credential and header fields are rejected by the native loader, and the host readiness adapter projects only upstream's source category while dropping material. Upstream does not need a ScribeRig-specific per-model credential-reference schema: that reference selection and destination authorization are ScribeRig host policy. Auth-success status and refresh after credential/provider changes are still not available, so §8 auth-status/readiness acceptance remains unchecked. The fork's ModelCatalogEvent and ModelCatalog::subscribe notify consumers only after model-row or provider-order changes; refresh_from_configuration is an explicit caller operation and does not watch configuration sources. The CLI's separate ModelRegistryEvent::AuthStatusChanged and AuthStatus are CLI-owned compatibility metadata, and the status setter has no production callsites. ScribeRig readiness is recomputed on each query from the latest shared catalog snapshot and its authorized credential provider. That provider re-reads live user/system policy and the selected secret source, but ScribeRig currently has no in-process provider-auth mutation or catalog-file reload path that could request a new projection after an external change. A generic upstream auth event cannot identify or observe ScribeRig SecretRef or destination policy; adding an event without a host change source and subscriber would not close this lifecycle gap. Keep auth-status and hot-refresh criteria unchecked until ScribeRig defines an authorized live change operation and wires it to refresh the shared catalog/readiness projection.

docs.title: Replace Local Provider/Tool Loop and Extension Host with Upstream Agent and Plugin Runtime
docs.text:
Status: [ ] In Progress

Current dependency note (2026-10-21, late revalidation): all ScribeRig rpi-* dependencies now pin controlled fork commit ebcf8d5e75d20fa3a6cc7cc76cbcdcec4cc36eb8, based on official upstream 0.7.1 main 281dfddfa39ac063d86de57b75370974c4d75e6c. The fork now includes the isolated plugin worker protocol, host-call allowlist, and injected sandbox launcher contract, so the worker/IPC gate is no longer blocked on an uncommitted API. ScribeRig still does not activate workers in production and does not merge worker tools into branch catalogs. Older revision references below are historical implementation checkpoints.

The integration brings in canonical upstream 0.7.0 (bigfish1913/pi-rust commit 7a272ec). Its reusable provider ABI is in rpi-plugin-sdk; generic package lifecycle helpers are in rpi-extensions. The earlier fork-only rpi-provider-runtime wrapper was removed. Historical sections below that name earlier revisions or owners should be read as checkpoints.

Invocation adapter update (2026-10-21): ToolCatalog no longer performs generic argument-shape or required-field validation. Its authorize methods only resolve registered ScribeRig tool names and enforce branch capabilities; rpi-agent validates arguments against the supplied JSON Schema before calling SemanticAgentTool::execute, and owns call lookup, settlement, and late-update handling. The adapter still rechecks the trusted descriptor and branch capability before executing the semantic callback. It bounds provider-visible results by dropping images, structured details, and dynamic tool additions, and caps text at 16 KiB; those are ScribeRig result-projection safeguards, not generic call settlement. ScribeRig's semantic descriptors and scenario responses use upstream rpi_ai::types::Tool and ToolCall directly; the local field-for-field schema and call types and conversion code were deleted. The cargo check -p scriberig --bin srig passes at the active pin. Focused behavior verification is deferred, so the matching acceptance item remains unchecked.

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
After Task 145's §16 preflight gate authorizes prerequisite implementation, move commodity in-branch agent execution and integrated agent extensibility onto upstream rpi-agent, rpi-ai, rpi-plugin-sdk, and rpi-extensions while preserving ScribeRig's branch/context/semantic-operation architecture. Task 145 remains In Progress until it returns after Tasks 137, 146, 136, and 147 to reverify its dependent criteria.

The goal is not to make Scriberig use upstream session semantics. The goal is to stop maintaining a separate provider/tool-loop and agent plugin runtime when upstream already provides those capabilities.

Do not begin task 147 until this sheet is complete.

docs.title: 2. Read Before Editing
docs.text:
• [ ] Read root and design/AGENTS.md.
  • [ ] Read Level-1 documents 009, 010, 014, 016, 017, 018, 019, 020, 021.
  • [ ] Read Level-2 documents 010, 011, 023, 024, 030, 032.
  • [ ] Read completed Task 144 and Task 145's current ownership boundaries and §16 preflight gate; reread Task 145 after its dependent criteria are reverified.
  • [ ] Read nearest instructions for agent core/runtime, session, app, server, and any extension/plugin paths modified.
  • [ ] Read upstream rpi-agent, rpi-ai, rpi-plugin-sdk, rpi-extensions, and provider-package docs at the selected revision.

docs.title: 3. Checklist Discipline
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this file open during implementation.
  • [ ] Tick only after exact implementation plus focused verification.
  • [ ] Never bulk-tick.
  • [ ] Revert invalidated criteria immediately.
  • [ ] Do not adopt rpi-harness as canonical Scriberig session state.
  • [ ] Do not keep a local generic agent loop merely because existing tests are shaped around it.
  • [ ] Missing generic upstream features remain upstream contribution gates.

docs.title: 4. Define the Branch Execution Adapter
docs.text:
One active Scriberig branch/executor context should drive one upstream agent-loop instance or equivalent upstream execution context.

Scriberig supplies:

compiled effective context
resolved upstream model execution selection
allowed tool set
branch-local cancellation
runtime budget decisions that remain Scriberig-specific
semantic activity correlation

Upstream supplies:

provider invocation mechanics
assistant streaming
provider tool-call parsing
tool schema validation
ordinary tool-call settlement/order
loop continuation
cancellation mechanics
agent events

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Branch identity remains Scriberig identity.
  • [ ] Upstream agent instance/session identifiers are not used as Scriberig SessionId/BranchId.
  • [ ] One branch can select a different upstream provider/model than a sibling.
  • [ ] Parent/child context isolation is determined before upstream execution begins.

docs.title: 5. Preserve Scriberig Context Compilation
docs.text:
Do not let upstream transcript/session history become the source of Scriberig context.

The execution flow remains:

Scriberig branch state
  -> Scriberig context compiler
  -> canonical safe effective request/context
  -> upstream agent/provider execution

If upstream agent state internally retains current-branch messages for loop mechanics, treat that state as disposable branch-local execution state.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Scriberig context compiler remains authoritative.
  • [ ] Child context is selected from Scriberig state, not copied from upstream parent transcript.
  • [ ] Parent resumes from selected BranchResults, not child upstream transcript.
  • [ ] Full prompt/effective request inspection remains provider-neutral Scriberig state.

docs.title: 6. Adapt Scriberig Semantic Operations to AgentTool
docs.text:
Create a narrow tool adapter around public Scriberig semantic/application operations.

Each adapter maps:

Scriberig operation/capability descriptor
  -> upstream AgentTool schema/label
  -> validated upstream tool call
  -> Scriberig capability check
  -> shared Scriberig application operation
  -> bounded semantic result projection
  -> upstream AgentToolResult

Do not duplicate upstream generic tool-call validation or settlement.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Tool JSON-schema validation is upstream-owned where upstream provides it.
  • [ ] Unknown provider-returned tool names cannot bypass the advertised tool set.
  • [ ] Scriberig capability checks run before semantic execution.
  • [ ] Canonical mutations still use candidate/migration/validation/promotion.
  • [ ] Tool result projections retain stable Scriberig result handles where exact state matters.

docs.title: 7. Branch-Producing Tool Calls
docs.text:
Retain Scriberig's atomic-vs-child-branch distinction.

For branch-producing work:

upstream tool call
  -> Scriberig creates child branch
  -> compile selected child context
  -> run child through upstream agent loop
  -> finalize durable BranchResult
  -> return compact BranchResult projection as upstream tool result

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Child branch is durable before its first model invocation.
  • [ ] Child may use a different upstream execution selection.
  • [ ] Parent receives compact result rather than child transcript.
  • [ ] Nested recursion obeys Scriberig budgets/policy.
  • [ ] A failed/cancelled child returns structured Scriberig branch outcome.

docs.title: 8. Delegate Provider Wire Implementations
docs.text:
Remove or retire Scriberig-owned generic provider HTTP implementations when upstream covers the required protocols.

Scriberig should not maintain its own OpenAI-compatible/Anthropic request serialization in parallel with upstream.

If Scriberig needs a missing provider feature, implement it in the controlled TNick/pi-rust fork's rpi-ai provider API and consume it only after pinning the reviewed fork commit. Upstream-main merge status and GitHub issue filing are not prerequisites for this dependency direction.

docs.title: Provider composition and protected-auth gate
docs.text:
At the current fork pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, rpi-ai exposes reusable concrete provider implementations under rpi_ai::providers; this pin includes the earlier extraction commit 3ae8416ceaf2dcdbf853b03c7b4662ad832497cf. The current pin also exposes rpi-model-runtime/src/provider_factory.rs with create_builtin_provider/create_builtin_provider_for_api for resolved built-in provider/model sets. This removes the upstream factory extraction blocker for built-in APIs. It does not discover providers, resolve extension providers, or compose CLI configuration, auth-store policy, package manifests, and model rows; those remain in rpi-cli/src/provider/factories.rs and rpi-cli::provider::resolve_with_extensions. ScribeRig must not call that CLI resolver or recreate its auth/package policy in native_tui_agent/provider_config.rs. ScribeRig's native root and plan worker now use the upstream built-in factory after exact model resolution, while retaining host-owned authorization and provider-independent configuration policy. Keep package installation and CLI configuration policy in their existing owners.

At the pinned revision, built-in OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic implementations expose combined protected-request-secret and applied-settings forwarding. rpi-extensions::PluggableProvider also forwards protected credentials to extensions that opt into the versioned protected ABI; legacy providers fail closed. Its versioned applied-settings callback accepts safe provider attestation, while providers without attestation produce an explicitly incomplete report after the extension attempt settles. Built-in reports project allowlisted values from the post-transformation request body and remain incomplete because they omit request-affecting categories. These upstream APIs are available but ScribeRig has not yet routed its active provider calls through them or persisted the reports. Do not infer application from catalog metadata or providerOptions transport alone.

The ScribeRig host bridge must be created per invocation and bind the exact resolved provider/model, immutable catalog/config snapshot, effective endpoint, selected scriberig_secrets::SecretRef, and SecretUseContext. It must call AuthorizedCredential::credential only after binding that destination, wrap the resulting SecretValue as rpi_ai::SecretMaterial, and pass it only via RequestSecret. Override upstream ProtectedCredentialResolver::resolve_with_policy so authorization or resolution errors become CredentialResolutionError and stop precedence; never translate them to a source miss or route through ordinary-string AuthStore, SimpleStreamOptions.api_key, model headers, or plugin JSON.

The native TUI root, one-shot, and plan-worker paths create an upstream provider for the exact selected catalog model and run it through run_upstream_branch_invocation with the scoped ScribeRig semantic broker. The broker retains branch identity, compiled context, semantic authorization, recursive child creation, request projections, and tool evidence. Deterministic scenarios are being adapted as upstream FauxProvider scripts that produce upstream AssistantMessage values. Configured built-in providers use their upstream implementations and protected credentials. Native provider extensions are rejected at startup until upstream supplies an isolated worker/IPC boundary. The ScribeRig-local generic agent loop, provider decision bridge, response cache, and generic provider connection-check path have been removed. Every branch runs through the shared upstream loop and semantic broker. The previous runtime test files were broadly deleted during this migration, including nested_branches.rs, provider_profile_provenance.rs, and runtime_request_history.rs. App-level native_tui_agent_tests/decomposition.rs now exercises recursive durable branches, compact results, child context isolation, and request ordering through the upstream runner. Existing agent_context_tests.rs, native_tui_agent_tests_part1.rs, coordinator, and plan tests retain root/non-root context activation, exact continuation anchors, durable dependency scheduling, and result semantics. A focused upstream request-projection test now checks that a ScribeRig provider profile remains provenance and affects ScribeRig request identity without entering provider-visible content. The upstream-backed failure scenario now asserts that its prepared request is retained on the durable failed invocation. The provider fixtures now use upstream faux scripts, and request assertions read the durable ScribeRig model-invocation projections. Compilation is pending the shared model-catalog API integration; runtime verification remains deferred. Do not restore tests of the removed generic local loop.

The generic request/response DTOs, provider trait, fake provider, and local upstream translation bridge have been removed from production. ScribeRig's compiled context message representation now lives under context, and provider::HostConfigurationError is limited to host configuration and ScribeRig scenario diagnostics. The NativeScenario wrapper and bootstrap, arithmetic, PHP self-hosting, and app test scenarios consume upstream Context/Model and FauxProvider/AssistantMessage. Doctor diagnostics map stream failures to the upstream failure boundary without recreating provider transport/authentication classifications. Compilation of the integrated catalog path remains pending. Do not restore the deleted generic provider loop or DTOs to make these paths compile.

The CredentialSource::Authorized created by the shared provider configuration is now offered to each selected built-in model, including non-local catalog rows. The protected bridge resolves it only after the exact selected model endpoint is known and wraps it as RequestSecret; the live AuthorizedCredential policy rechecks its SecretRef, endpoint, project root, purpose, and execution mode before reading. A denied or failed resolution stops the upstream invocation and is not converted to an unauthenticated request. Catalog-supplied credentials and headers remain rejected. A catalog row that needs a distinct credential reference cannot yet supply one through the native model-selection path; that remains a TEMPORARY configuration gate. Remove it only after host-owned per-connection configuration binds a specific SecretRef and SecretUseContext to that selected model endpoint. Applied-settings callbacks are captured on the current request projection, but the report persistence/API boundary still needs focused verification. Upstream stream failures now remain at the upstream invocation boundary; doctor reports only distinguish host configuration from an upstream check failure rather than recreating provider transport/authentication classes. Focused behavior verification and distinct per-model credential-reference configuration remain open.

The inspect semantic operation still uses the non-cancellable Tool::invoke path. It addresses one entity at an exact or current snapshot and returns bounded compact/detailed output, but the synchronous application query boundary does not accept a cancellation token. Cancellation therefore stops the broker and provider loop but cannot interrupt an inspect query after that query has started. Add a cancellable query operation before claiming per-tool cancellation for inspect.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Active provider requests use upstream provider implementations.
  • [x] Scriberig runtime no longer owns generic provider HTTP request shaping for supported providers.
  • [ ] Provider errors are mapped into Scriberig public runtime error categories through a thin adapter.
  • [x] Credential handling stays upstream/runtime-secret and is never persisted in session state.

Provider-error adapter progress (2026-10-21): the controlled fork working tree now classifies AiError::Auth and HTTP 401/403 as an internal typed ErrorReason::Authentication, carries that through an rpi-agent provider error/state boundary, and ScribeRig maps the resulting typed state to AgentError::Authentication. The existing serialized provider event reason remains "error". This is not yet consumable at ScribeRig's pin, and no build or runtime verification has been run; leave the criterion unchecked until the fork changes are reviewed, committed, pinned, and verified.

docs.title: 9. Provider Continuation Split
docs.text:
Preserve Level-1 document 020.

Scriberig owns:

branch-to-continuation association
context fingerprint
stale/reseed decision
provider-neutral provenance

Upstream owns:

provider-specific continuation handles
wire request fields
provider continuation API mechanics
provider protocol errors

The pinned TNick/pi-rust revision 46ea1250bd695540b7f0b395afd6e10518fc05ff provides an opaque, non-serializable, debug-redacted rpi_ai::ProviderContinuation scoped to provider/model, plus Provider::continuation_from_response and stream_simple_with_continuation. rpi-agent exposes a continuation-aware stream callback, extraction callback, and Agent::set_provider_continuation. These APIs do not own ScribeRig branch identity or context validity. No concrete rpi-ai provider currently implements continuation extraction or consumption. The provider method also accepts no Context, protected RequestSecret, or applied-settings callback; it therefore cannot carry the next user message or preserve the current ScribeRig credential/report path. Deferred response polling IDs do not satisfy provider continuation.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Pin the fork commit containing the continuation API and rpi-agent AgentBuilder/Agent seam before ScribeRig consumes it.
  • [ ] At least one required provider implements extraction and continuation; unsupported providers fail closed and use ScribeRig replay/reseed behavior.
  • [ ] ScribeRig associates handles with canonical branch and context fingerprints, clears them on divergence, and never uses them as session identity.
  • [ ] Provider-specific continuation support is not reimplemented as ScribeRig HTTP code.
  • [ ] Losing upstream continuation does not make a ScribeRig branch unrecoverable.

The API pin criterion is satisfied. The preceding limitations describe the earlier 46ea125 snapshot. At ScribeRig's current 0f50101 pin, the audited continuation API accepts the current Context, optional protected RequestSecret, and required applied-settings callback. OpenAI Responses implements extraction and audited continuation, and advertises this support through Provider::supports_response_continuation(); the trait default is false. Its opaque provider/model-scoped handle is validated against the provider's private state type. The request builder supports a fresh context without the previous assistant response object and retains legacy anchor behavior when that object is present. The host must validate context/branch lineage because provider/model scope cannot prove it. ScribeRig has not yet implemented its in-memory branch/context handle store or verified stale, failure, and reseed behavior, so those continuation criteria remain unchecked. No upstream GitHub issue filing or upstream-main merge is a gate.

The long-lived native TUI root runner now keeps the opaque continuation in process memory under canonical root-branch identity. It checks provider, resolved model, connection profile, thinking level, provider/model scope, and a versioned fingerprint covering the compiled provider context, exact profile and active component revisions, dependency/omission identities, and effective semantic grants. Divergence removes the cached handle and replays from canonical ScribeRig branch state. The handle is not persisted or projected. Child branches, plan workers, one-shot CLI runs, and server-scoped invocations remain stateless. The continuation result is compiled, but no tests have been run; behavioral acceptance, including failure/reseed behavior, remains unchecked until the requested final validation phase.

docs.title: 10. Adopt Upstream Plugin ABI and Extension Host
docs.text:
Use rpi-plugin-sdk and rpi-extensions for integrated agent-product plugins.

Do not create or preserve a parallel Scriberig ABI for:

agent tools
providers
slash commands
agent event handlers
Markdown renderers
agent resources

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Upstream extension loader owns discovery/loading of configured provider extensions.
  • [ ] Upstream plugin version negotiation/ABI is used.
  • [ ] Registered provider plugins become selectable through the same extension session.
  • [ ] Scriberig does not re-load the same extension through another registry.

At the current ScribeRig fork pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, extension tool loading and invocation are reusable from rpi-extensions, not trapped in the CLI: RegistrySnapshot::tools() exposes ExtensionTool { tool, handle, origin }, ExtensionSession::keepalive() retains loaded libraries, and PluginToolAdapter implements upstream rpi_agent::AgentTool. The adapter offers a host-stamped origin and a pre-execution authorization callback. PluginToolAdapter::from_registered fails closed until a host policy is installed; from_registered_authorized preserves origin and policy together. These support host-mediated authorization, but do not provide process isolation or prevent native code from accessing ambient host resources.

ScribeRig currently fails closed before loading a configured native provider extension. apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/provider_config/extensions.rs checks SCRIBE_AGENT_EXTENSION_DIRS and SCRIBE_AGENT_PACKAGE_ROOTS and returns a configuration error when either selects native code. The pinned loader uses in-process libloading, so the former trusted-code opt-in could not enforce the canonical-knowledge invariant. The extension-consumption criteria above remain unchecked until an upstream isolated worker/IPC API is pinned and consumed; the no-duplicate-load criterion is also unchecked while ScribeRig has no active extension loader.

The same pin exposes reusable project-package operations from rpi-extensions: read_project_registry, write_project_registry, project_package_resource_dirs, install_project_artifact, and uninstall_project_package. The install API activates an already-built artifact under a host-selected project root; it does not build, download, or authorize the project root. Resource paths are lexically composed after registry/name validation, so the host still owns root authorization and any canonical-path or symlink policy. The library also exposes provider-reload predicates and provider-set composition, but not a complete extension-session swap with catalog reconciliation and active-provider handling. Build/link, update acquisition, and live extension reload/session swap remain in rpi-cli. ScribeRig should delegate registry and artifact operations to the library if it adds package controls; it must retain host root authorization and should not duplicate CLI build/update or session-swap orchestration.

docs.title: Package lifecycle boundary
docs.text:
The ScribeRig provider adapter at apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/provider_config/extensions.rs now rejects process-selected extension directories/package roots before loading any native code. It does not call package_resource_dirs or load_session, and it does not read or write a project registry, install/uninstall artifacts, build/update packages, or reload a live extension session. The one-shot path uses the same fail-closed gate. ScribeRig has no local package manager or duplicate registry/artifact lifecycle implementation to remove.

Do not add package controls as part of provider-extension discovery. If a product requirement later calls for project package management, ScribeRig must authorize the selected project root first and call the upstream registry, resource, install, and uninstall APIs. Upstream must expose reusable build and update acquisition plus an atomic extension-session/catalog replacement seam before ScribeRig offers build/update/reload controls. Until then, retain the current startup adapter and leave package controls absent; do not use rpi-cli command handlers as a library boundary or recreate them in ScribeRig.

docs.title: 11. Apply Scriberig Trust and Capability Policy to Plugins
docs.text:
Using the upstream plugin host does not mean granting unrestricted semantic authority.

Add a Scriberig host-policy adapter that can:

allow/deny a registered tool for the current branch
limit semantic scopes
require explicit approval for fallback filesystem/shell authority
prevent direct canonical semantic mutation outside public operations
hide unavailable capabilities from model context

Do not fork the loader to implement policy if upstream exposes hooks/filtering. If necessary, contribute generic host-policy hooks upstream.

At the current pin, ExtensionToolOrigin supplies host-stamped registration identity and PluginToolAdapter::with_pre_execute_authorizer can deny a host-mediated call before native execution. ScribeRig still does not pass registered extension tools to rpi-agent. This is an explicit deny-by-default boundary in product code: UpstreamBranchInvocation.tools accepts only SemanticAgentTool, and upstream_execution::build_tools constructs that vector only from capability-filtered ToolCatalog descriptors. An ExtensionTool or PluginToolAdapter cannot enter the branch tool list. Do not widen this type or merge extension schemas into the broker while plugins execute in process.

After upstream isolation exists, a bridge must bind the worker's host-stamped extension/tool identity to a ScribeRig capability, authorize against the immutable branch capability snapshot before dispatch, and route approved operations through the ScribeRig broker for activity/evidence. The worker must not receive database paths, canonical-store handles, or unrestricted runtime actions. The current authorization callback is only a host-mediated call gate; it cannot stop native code from opening canonical files or using other process APIs directly.

The pinned rpi-extensions/src/loader.rs still uses libloading to map cdylibs into the host process. Withholding ScribeRig store handles and omitting ToolCallContext or runtime-action bridges reduces host-mediated authority, but does not prevent trusted native code from opening canonical store files or calling other process APIs directly. The direct-mutation acceptance item requires an upstream isolated worker/IPC host with a capability-scoped host API. Until that API is implemented, pinned, and consumed, keep native extension loading disabled, keep plugin tools absent from ScribeRig agent tool sets, make no containment claim, and leave the direct-mutation item unchecked. This is a fork contribution gate, not a reason to create a second ScribeRig plugin ABI or loader.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Loaded does not imply authorized.
  • [ ] Plugin tools visible to the model match branch capability policy.
  • [ ] Plugin tools cannot directly mutate Scriberig database state through the integration API.
  • [ ] Raw file/shell tools remain fallback capabilities and are not automatically preferred for understood domains.

docs.title: 12. Keep Scriberig Domain Extensions Distinct
docs.text:
Do not collapse semantic domain adapters into the upstream agent plugin system.

Scriberig domain extensions may define:

schemas
parsers
semantic operations
projections
reconciliation
validation
derived knowledge

The upstream plugin system may expose agent-facing tools/resources that call those public domain capabilities.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Domain extension lifecycle remains compatible with Scriberig semantic APIs.
  • [ ] Agent plugins call public semantic capabilities rather than private storage.
  • [ ] The same domain capability can be used without the agent runtime.

docs.title: 13. Translate Upstream Agent Events into Scriberig Durable/Transient Activity
docs.text:
Use upstream events for execution observation, but keep Scriberig activity identity/provenance.

Map upstream events such as:

agent start/end
message start/update/end
tool start/update/end
provider error/cancel

into current Scriberig concepts without making upstream event sequence the semantic identity.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Streaming remains transient until Scriberig semantic boundaries are complete.
  • [ ] Final assistant output is recorded once.
  • [ ] Tool invocation/result ordering is preserved.
  • [ ] Scriberig ModelInvocationId, branch and operation correlations remain stable.
  • [ ] Duplicate/replayed observations cannot duplicate durable semantic activity.

docs.title: 14. Preserve Model Observability
docs.text:
The upstream loop may serialize requests differently, but Scriberig must still retain the canonical safe effective request before provider serialization.

Provider-applied settings are a separate observation from the canonical ScribeRig request projection. Consume upstream AppliedRequestSettings only from the final provider preparation callback; do not infer application from catalog/execution-configuration metadata or the providerOptions envelope. Persist the schema version, allowlisted values, omitted categories, and complete status with the canonical invocation. Built-in reports and extension fallbacks are intentionally incomplete; they do not replace the full safe ScribeRig prompt/context projection.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Full prompt means complete safe Scriberig effective context, not upstream HTTP body.
  • [ ] Any provider applied-settings report is captured from the final provider boundary and persisted with its explicit omissions and completeness; catalog metadata alone is never reported as applied.
  • [ ] Provider-visible reasoning is captured only when upstream/provider exposes it for user/application consumption.
  • [ ] Hidden chain-of-thought remains unavailable.
  • [ ] Prompt/reasoning presentation settings do not alter upstream execution.

Implementation in progress: UpstreamBranchInvocation now always installs the upstream AppliedRequestSettingsCallback on the provider stream. It stores the upstream report as opaque JSON on that request's durable ModelRequestProjection, while forwarding to any caller callback. The report is returned only through the existing authorized model-request detail operation and rendered as an upstream-owned report in the web activity view. Catalog values are not used to fabricate this report. The acceptance item remains unchecked until focused persistence/API verification is complete.

docs.title: 15. One-Shot, TUI, Server, and Web Use the Same Agent Operation
docs.text:
The product surfaces continue to start/observe shared Scriberig agent operations.

They do not instantiate their own upstream agent loop independently.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] One-shot CLI uses the shared Scriberig branch operation.
  • [ ] TUI uses the shared Scriberig branch operation.
  • [ ] Server/web uses the shared Scriberig branch operation.
  • [ ] Remote clients do not need provider credentials.

docs.title: 16. Focused Verification
docs.text:
Add/run deterministic tests covering:

Scriberig context -> upstream agent execution
semantic AgentTool adapter
capability denial before execution
ordinary upstream tool-call validation
child branch tool execution
multi-model siblings
provider error mapping
provider continuation stale/reseed
upstream plugin registration
plugin capability filtering
stream/event translation
cancellation
full prompt capture

Use upstream faux/test providers; no paid provider should be required.

  • [ ] Agent-runtime focused tests pass.
  • [ ] Session/branch focused tests pass.
  • [ ] Plugin integration tests pass.
  • [ ] Cancellation tests pass.
  • [ ] No real network is required for core conformance.

docs.title: 17. Deletion Gate
docs.text:
Update task 144's deletion ledger.

Current equivalents of these should be removed or explicitly blocked on upstream:

local generic provider HTTP implementation
local ordinary provider/model stream normalization duplicated upstream
local generic model/tool loop
local generic tool-call schema validation duplicated upstream
local agent plugin ABI/extension host/package loader duplicated upstream

Keep only Scriberig-specific adapters/orchestration.

  • [x] Production no longer routes through superseded local loop/provider code.
  • [ ] Deterministic branch/context/plan/provenance assertions are preserved or adapted to the upstream-backed path and verified.
  • [ ] No rpi-harness session identity leaked into Scriberig canonical state.

docs.title: 18. Completion Gate
docs.text:
• [ ] Re-read checked criteria.
  • [ ] Confirm Scriberig owns context/branch/plan/semantic mutation semantics.
  • [ ] Confirm upstream owns provider and ordinary agent-loop mechanics.
  • [ ] Confirm upstream plugin system is the integrated agent plugin mechanism.
  • [ ] Confirm task 144 deletion ledger is current.
  • [ ] Leave task 147 Not Started until this task is complete.

Then set:
