docs.title: 19. Implementation Notes
docs.text:
Record upstream versions/commits, upstream contribution references, and any deliberately retained adapter responsibilities.

The configured one-shot OpenAI-compatible CLI path now creates an upstream rpi-model-runtime provider and delegates the turn through the shared native_tui_agent::upstream_execution semantic broker. The CLI still owns credential-source resolution and endpoint authorization; the broker preserves the canonical session/branch, compiled ScribeRig context, semantic tool authorization, child results, bounded request projections, and streamed text callback. Deterministic local provider scenarios used by native root execution adapt to rpi_ai::Provider and run through the same upstream semantic broker. Plan-worker execution now uses execute_precompiled_branch, which invokes the same upstream semantic broker as root execution. Recursive delegate calls use that broker to create, execute, and finalize child branches with bounded request projections and tool evidence. The old LocalChildExecutor and local plan-worker executor are removed. Deterministic branch fixtures use the same upstream semantic broker as production, including recursive child finalization and bounded tool evidence. Configured OpenAI-compatible endpoints use the upstream built-in provider and the host-authorized protected request secret. The no-endpoint one-shot Echo provider uses the same scenario adapter and upstream semantic broker. No direct uses of the deleted ScribeRig AgentRuntime remain. The deterministic project-agent operations exposed by the server project route and TUI application adapter now use rpi_ai::FauxProvider with run_upstream_branch_invocation and ScribeRig SemanticAgentTool adapters. They preserve the shared project candidate/review operation and do not expose request projections as a transport transcript. They are public product flows and were migrated rather than removed as demo behavior. No production AgentRuntime construction remains in the ScribeRig app: child execution is owned by upstream_execution/delegation.rs, and plan workers use the shared upstream broker. The bootstrap fixture uses a thin test-only composition helper that invokes the upstream loop; it does not retain an alternate local loop. The one-shot failure path persists captured safe request projections and tool evidence with the canonical abandoned branch result, including cancellation. The one-shot CLI migration does not close the remaining non-local connection credential gate, provider-report persistence, continuation, plugin-host, or deletion criteria.

At the current pin 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, rpi-extensions exports ExtensionToolOrigin and a fail-closed registered adapter path. The callback can reject a host-mediated call before plugin arguments reach its native entry point, but the adapter still invokes in-process cdylib code. ScribeRig's UpstreamBranchInvocation.tools is typed as Vec<Arc<SemanticAgentTool>>, and upstream_execution::build_tools only adapts branch-visible ToolCatalog descriptors. This keeps plugin tools unrepresentable in the agent tool set by default. Do not widen that boundary until the fork supplies an isolated worker/IPC host with capability-scoped operations. The worker must keep canonical storage inaccessible and preserve the host-stamped tool identity used for branch authorization and ScribeRig broker evidence. Native provider loading now fails closed at the host boundary; plugin tool execution and direct-mutation criteria stay unchecked until the upstream worker/IPC boundary is pinned and consumed.

At the same pin, rpi-extensions provides registry read/write, validated project resource lookup, activation of a prebuilt artifact, and package uninstall in rpi-extensions/src/packages.rs. The host must still select and authorize the project root. Artifact build/download and an atomic isolated session/catalog swap remain absent from this library; reload predicates do not perform that swap.

The native TUI composition now rejects process-selected SCRIBE_AGENT_EXTENSION_DIRS and SCRIBE_AGENT_PACKAGE_ROOTS through reject_in_process_extensions before loading native code because the upstream loader uses in-process libloading and cannot enforce ScribeRig's canonical-knowledge invariant. ScribeRig does not merge provider manifests or instantiate PluggableProvider. The one-shot path uses the same fail-closed gate. Deterministic scenarios use upstream FauxProvider in tests; there is no local production provider adapter. The §10 extension-consumption checklist and §11 direct-mutation items remain unchecked. Any future package controls must authorize their project root and use upstream registry/artifact APIs; activation must wait for an upstream isolated worker/IPC boundary and an atomic session/catalog swap.

The configured one-shot srig run path uses the same fail-closed reject_in_process_extensions gate. Extension model selection is unavailable while native plugins would execute in-process. Configured built-in providers and deterministic scenarios use the upstream provider and agent paths, with ScribeRig semantic operations retained at the tool boundary. Package install/reload controls and extension tools/events remain unavailable pending upstream isolation and reusable lifecycle APIs.

Request provenance now reads rpi_ai::Context, rpi_ai::Model, and the upstream ThinkingLevel directly in crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/upstream_invocation/request_projection.rs. The production path no longer converts upstream context into the generic local ModelRequest DTO before recording ScribeRig's bounded historical projection. The DTO-based projection helper is compiled only for tests; persisted ModelRequestProjection remains ScribeRig-owned provenance and excludes non-text content and transport secrets.

docs.title: Runtime adapter ownership audit (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
The production branch loop is rpi_agent::Agent in crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/upstream_invocation.rs::build_agent; tool schema validation, ordinary tool sequencing/settlement, provider message parsing, and loop continuation are upstream-owned. ScribeRig's UpstreamBranchInvocation supplies its already compiled context, exact model, branch-scoped semantic tools, selected thinking level, and host-authorized request secret. The event subscription in run_upstream_branch_invocation forwards provider-visible text to the product callback and captures only ScribeRig's bounded request provenance.

The fork contribution for the remaining lifecycle gap is included in controlled-fork integration commit 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5. Its provider-stream change adds rpi_agent::CancellableContinuationStreamFn, which receives the active agent run cancellation token, and rpi_ai::stream_provider_cancellable, which owns provider method dispatch, protected secret/bearer forwarding, applied-settings reporting, continuation use, cancellation while provider startup or event consumption is pending, and terminal-event repair. ScribeRig's consumer now uses this upstream helper while retaining exact model binding, host-authorized credential resolution, canonical continuation validity, safe request projection, and ScribeRig cancellation/result mapping. Upstream regression coverage has been added but not executed. The combined pin has passed workspace compile checking. Extension isolation, provider-specific continuation implementations, and other unchecked criteria below remain independent open work.

The remaining app-side provider configuration is host policy or an upstream consumer: agent_config.rs uses rpi_cli::config::ConfigResolver for layered CLI configuration; provider_config/catalog.rs reads upstream ModelsConfig, resolves endpoints through rpi_model_runtime, and applies ScribeRig's endpoint/credential policy; protected_credential.rs binds the selected ScribeRig SecretRef to that endpoint through upstream's protected credential resolver; and model_properties.rs renders upstream property descriptors, validates edits through upstream setters, and persists through ModelsConfigFile. No ScribeRig provider-specific model-property schema, provider HTTP implementation, plugin loader, package registry, or generic tool-execution loop remains. provider_config/extensions.rs only rejects configured native extension roots before the upstream in-process loader can run. Keep extension activation blocked until the controlled fork has an isolated worker/IPC boundary and reusable package lifecycle APIs.

docs.title: Plugin/package ownership audit (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
The current pinned rpi-extensions API in fork commit 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5 supplies the rpi-plugin-sdk ABI, load_session/ExtensionSession, RegistrySnapshot/ExtensionTool, and PluginToolAdapter. The loader uses libloading::Library in the ScribeRig process. PluginToolAdapter::from_registered_authorized and with_pre_execute_authorizer can gate host-mediated calls, but cannot prevent plugin code from opening ScribeRig's database or using ambient process APIs. An ordinary child process is not enough: it needs OS-enforced access limits that keep canonical storage and secrets unavailable except through explicit host-mediated capabilities.

The same upstream crate exposes project-registry read/write, resource-root discovery, activation of a prebuilt artifact, and uninstall APIs. These are metadata/artifact operations, not a package build/download service or an atomic extension-session plus model-catalog generation swap. Root authorization, symlink/canonical-path policy, acquisition, and in-flight generation lifetime remain host/lifecycle concerns. ScribeRig has no local plugin ABI, loader, package registry, installer, or updater. apps/scriberig/Cargo.toml therefore no longer declares a direct rpi-extensions dependency while the production host deliberately does not load extensions. Cargo.lock retains the crate as an upstream transitive dependency of rpi-agent at the same fork revision.

The exact upstream contribution gate is a reusable isolated plugin worker contract in rpi-extensions/rpi-plugin-sdk: a versioned serialized tool protocol, cancellation and worker-lifetime handling, a host capability RPC surface, and a host-injected OS sandbox launcher whose contract denies direct canonical-store and secret access. The rpi-agent adapter must expose only registered tools whose host-stamped identities can be authorized against the immutable ScribeRig branch capability snapshot and dispatched through the semantic broker. A later lifecycle contribution must atomically replace the extension session and catalog while active invocations retain the old generation. The current in-process ABI cannot safely meet these conditions; keep reject_in_process_extensions and do not create a ScribeRig loader or package manager as a substitute.

docs.title: Pinned extension activation/install/reload boundary audit (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
Rechecked the exact workspace pin bad1c5b4aa6f26cc231168d75a09165e990de39a (Cargo.toml entries for rpi-agent, rpi-ai, and rpi-model-runtime; Cargo.lock's rpi-extensions source). The cached fork source is crates/rpi-extensions at that revision. Its APIs support three distinct lifecycle stages; none makes native plugin execution isolated:

  • Activation/loading: rpi_extensions::load_session in crates/rpi-extensions/src/loader.rs builds an ExtensionSession and RegistrySnapshot; RegistrySnapshot::tools() exposes registered tools, and ExtensionSession::keepalive() retains loaded libraries. The loader maps cdylibs with libloading::Library in the host process. This is executable activation, not just manifest discovery, and is unsafe for ScribeRig's canonical-store boundary without OS-enforced isolation.
  • Project artifact install/uninstall: read_project_registry, write_project_registry, project_package_resource_dirs, install_project_artifact, and uninstall_project_package are reusable APIs in crates/rpi-extensions/src/packages.rs (re-exported by src/lib.rs; registry value types also live in src/project_packages.rs). Install copies/registers a prebuilt artifact under a caller-selected project root; it does not load the cdylib into an extension session. It does not build/download an artifact or authorize the root, nor establish symlink/canonical-path policy. Project package metadata and resource lookup are not a worker boundary.
  • Live reload: providers_for_reload, requires_provider_catalog_refresh, and active_provider_was_removed in src/provider_reload.rs are predicates and provider-set helpers. They do not load a replacement session or atomically swap its registry/catalog. ReloadMailbox and reload_callback_from_mailbox in src/actions.rs provide an action callback seam; the host callback is responsible for discovery/load/swap. The rpi-cli implementation owns package build/update acquisition and integrated reload orchestration. No reusable atomic session/catalog swap API is present at this pin.

ScribeRig's activation gate is apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/provider_config/extensions.rs::reject_in_process_extensions. It rejects nonempty SCRIBE_AGENT_EXTENSION_DIRS or SCRIBE_AGENT_PACKAGE_ROOTS; native TUI setup calls it in apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent.rs, and one-shot setup calls it in apps/scriberig/src/main_agent_execution/upstream.rs. The runtime branch adapter builds SemanticAgentTools only from ToolCatalog in apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/upstream_execution/execution.rs::build_tools. No configured extension root is passed to load_session; ScribeRig has no extension registry, artifact install/uninstall, package build/update, or live reload implementation. Its remaining package/loader references are the fail-closed gate and explanatory comments, not commodity package-manager or loader code. Workspace Cargo packages and application command arguments are unrelated uses of “package”.

The next executable upstream contribution gate is sequenced: first expose a versioned isolated worker in rpi-extensions/rpi-plugin-sdk with serialized tool IPC, cancellation and worker lifetime, host capability RPC, and an injected OS sandbox launcher that denies direct canonical-store and secret access. Then expose a replacement-session API that stages the worker set and registry/catalog as one generation, swaps atomically, and keeps the old generation alive for in-flight calls. Only after both APIs exist should ScribeRig consume them: authorize the project root, resolve/install artifacts with reusable package APIs, activate through the isolated session API, and adapt only host-stamped tool identities through branch capability checks and the semantic broker. Until then retain startup rejection and omit package controls; do not add a ScribeRig loader, installer, updater, or reload path.

This audit is documentation-only. No source files or tests were changed/run.

docs.title: Controlled-fork isolated worker progress (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
The controlled fork working tree now contains an uncommitted implementation in crates/rpi-extensions/src/isolated/: versioned tool/host-call IPC, worker startup and process-tree supervision, plugin loading inside the worker, a runtime-action bridge over host capability RPC, and a reusable AllowlistedHostHandler. ScribeRig's feature-gated crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/plugin_worker.rs now consumes that allowlist wrapper around its semantic dispatcher. This is preparatory adapter work only: the API is absent from pinned commit b2fc63c78ae85044eb78e7ac9af184bd7fbfbc95, so the optional feature cannot build until a reviewed fork revision is committed and pinned. The application still fails closed on configured plugin roots, and the worker is not integrated into branch tool catalogs.

The worker protocol and process boundary do not establish an OS sandbox. The default launcher clears inherited environment and supervises process lifetime, but does not restrict filesystem, network, or secret access. Long-running plugin FFI calls do not cooperatively poll cancellation; host capability calls block worker runtime threads until reply timeout; several action hooks remain inert or unsupported; and session/catalog replacement is not atomic. These are explicit fork contribution and review gates. Keep plugin activation, package controls, and model-visible extension tools disabled until sandboxing, branch-scoped broker authorization, lifecycle behavior, and runtime evidence are implemented against a pinned upstream API.

docs.title: Isolated worker boundary implementation (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
The controlled fork now carries a versioned worker boundary in crates/rpi-extensions/src/isolated/:

  • protocol.rs defines rpi-plugin-worker-v1 frames for hello, tool_call, tool_result, tool_error, cancel, host_call, host_result, host_error, and shutdown.
  • client/mod.rs + client/reader.rs start a caller-selected executable, clear the host environment unless the host opts into inheritance, supervise the process tree through rpi-plugin-sdk::process::ProcessTree, enforce startup/request deadlines, correlate responses, route host-capability calls, cancel in-flight requests, and kill the tree on drop or failure.
  • client/launch.rs exposes the injected WorkerLauncher seam and the default HostProcessLauncher.
  • worker.rs serves the protocol from the worker process and executes each tool_call on a worker thread so cancellation and shutdown can still be processed.
  • plugin.rs loads plugins with load_session_mixed only inside the worker, advertises registered tools, and drives PluginToolAdapter in that process. run_worker is the worker entrypoint; rpi-extensions/Cargo.toml enables the upstream SDK's process feature for process-tree supervision.

The controlled fork working tree now contains isolated-worker protocol and runtime source, but it is uncommitted and absent from ScribeRig's current pin b2fc63c78ae85044eb78e7ac9af184bd7fbfbc95. The upstream module under crates/rpi-extensions/src/isolated/ defines a versioned JSON-lines protocol, worker startup/request deadlines, cancellation, shutdown, process-tree supervision, worker-side plugin loading, and execution through PluginToolAdapter. ScribeRig's uncommitted crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/plugin_worker.rs, behind the opt-in isolated-plugin-worker feature, adds a host-policy seam with tool/capability allowlists and PluginSemanticDispatcher; the executable recognizes --scriberig-plugin-worker before normal CLI/database startup. provider_config/extensions.rs::validate_isolated_plugin_configuration checks worker configuration through that adapter when the feature is enabled. The default build rejects configured plugin roots, and feature-enabled builds still reject them because production does not yet compose worker tools into branch tool catalogs. Package roots remain rejected. The feature cannot compile until the upstream isolated-worker API is committed and pinned.

Remaining gates: commit and pin the fork API; provide a WorkerLauncher with filesystem/network/secret OS sandboxing; compose an authorized PluginSemanticDispatcher; register worker tools in each branch's upstream Agent; route plugin runtime actions through host capability RPC; add cancellation polling for long-running plugin FFI calls; and replace extension/package catalogs atomically on reload. The default launcher only clears environment and supervises process lifetime. No tests, builds, or runtime isolation evidence were produced.

Sandbox launcher update (2026-10-21): the fork working tree now contains WorkerSandboxPolicy, launcher-reported WorkerSandboxGuarantees, fail-closed HostProcessLauncher behavior for sandboxed requests, and LinuxBubblewrapLauncher. The Linux command uses namespaces, explicit root binds, network isolation/opt-in sharing, cleared environment, capability drops, private /tmp, and parent-death behavior. macOS and Windows have no built-in sandbox launcher and fail closed unless the host injects one. The contract checks self-reported guarantees but cannot validate the launcher; there is no seccomp or resource limiting, and the bubblewrap invocation has not been runtime-tested. These changes are uncommitted and absent from the pin, so they reduce the remaining upstream source work but do not change ScribeRig's fail-closed activation gate or establish verified isolation. Host-mediated runtime-action RPC is also present in the fork worktree; ScribeRig still has no authorized dispatcher or branch tool-catalog integration.

docs.title: Isolated worker cancellation and shutdown update (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
The current fork working tree now passes a CancellationToken into each PluginToolAdapter::execute call. A host Cancel frame cancels the matching token, and worker shutdown or input closure cancels all active tokens. The worker joins calls that finish during a two-second settlement window and joins its input-reader thread after the loop. This provides a cooperative cancellation signal; it cannot safely preempt native plugin FFI that ignores the signal. Such work may remain detached after the grace window, and the worker process must exit to terminate it. Embedding serve_worker in a long-lived host process would therefore risk retaining unfinished plugin threads.

The host request deadline is a hard fallback: it kills the supervised process tree, marks the connection closed, and fails pending requests. Graceful host shutdown waits about 500 ms before killing the tree, shorter than the worker's two-second cooperative settlement window; in that path the process kill can preempt the worker's own grace period. Cancellation has no worker acknowledgement that a plugin call has stopped. Host capability RPC can block a plugin action for up to its 60-second reply timeout, and shutdown frames cannot be handled while synchronous plugin registration is still running. These are source-level claims only: no build, tests, or runtime lifecycle verification has been run. The fork changes are uncommitted and not in ScribeRig's pinned revision. Keep plugin activation disabled until the fork API is reviewed, pinned, and verified under runtime cancellation, timeout, and shutdown scenarios.

docs.title: Tool ownership and capability audit (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
The production semantic tool path in upstream_tool.rs delegates schema validation, provider-selected call parsing, ordinary execution sequencing, settlement, and late-update suppression to rpi-agent. Its adapter rechecks the immutable ScribeRig branch tool catalog/capability snapshot before calling the semantic operation and applies ScribeRig's bounded provider-visible result projection. tools.rs owns only the semantic descriptor/category and branch capability policy; the scheduler's concurrent worker claim and BranchResult settlement remain plan-DAG semantics, not a duplicate in-branch model/tool loop.

The exposure and final invocation checks now share tools.rs::descriptor_visible, so an OpaqueFallback descriptor without an explicit granted capability is neither advertised nor authorizable. Generic JSON-schema validation remains upstream-owned. Focused capability behavior verification has not been run, so the related §6 criteria remain unchecked.

docs.title: Task 146 runtime and extension boundary audit (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
Inspected the active pin 6e65635a2ac2336a86847d85e2c3bb771a945c87 and the corresponding cached source tree. The production ordinary branch loop is already rpi_agent::Agent; provider invocation, parsing, schema validation, tool settlement, continuation, and cancellation mechanics are delegated to the upstream rpi-agent/rpi-ai APIs. upstream_tool.rs remains a narrow ScribeRig adapter: it checks the immutable branch catalog/capabilities before semantic execution and bounds provider-visible results. Removing it would remove ScribeRig authorization and projection safeguards, not duplicate upstream behavior. provider.rs now defines only HostConfigurationError, which is still consumed by app composition and is not a local provider implementation.

The active upstream rpi-extensions API includes load_session, ExtensionSession, RegistrySnapshot, ExtensionToolOrigin, and PluginToolAdapter. Its loader uses libloading in the host process. The registered-tool authorization callback gates host-mediated execution but does not prevent loaded plugin code from accessing canonical storage or ambient process capabilities. Therefore the production host continues to reject configured in-process extension roots, and plugin tools remain unrepresentable in UpstreamBranchInvocation.tools.

The remaining upstream contribution gate is an OS-isolated worker contract in rpi-extensions/rpi-plugin-sdk: versioned serialized tool IPC, cancellation and worker lifetime management, host-mediated capability RPC, and an injected sandbox launcher that denies direct canonical-store and secret access. The uncommitted worker protocol code in the fork does not yet provide that sandbox or atomic extension/catalog generation replacement. The rpi-agent bridge must preserve host-stamped tool identity so ScribeRig can authorize each call against its branch capability snapshot and record broker evidence. Until those APIs are pinned and consumed, startup rejects configured roots and extension-host, plugin execution, and lifecycle acceptance remain unchecked. No tests or long checks were run for this audit.

docs.title: Provider continuation and context binding audit (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
Compared ScribeRig's root continuation cache and fingerprint checks with the active upstream ProviderContinuation contract. Upstream handles are opaque, non-serialized, and scoped to provider/model; rpi-agent exposes them through its continuation extractor/callback and Agent::set_provider_continuation. ScribeRig adds the separate branch and context validity binding in apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/runner.rs and upstream_execution/lineage.rs. Cache entries are held only in the runner's process-local map, keyed by root branch, and contain provider/model/profile, thinking identity, a ScribeRig context fingerprint, and the opaque handle. They are removed before each attempted turn, rejected on identity/fingerprint/ upstream-scope mismatch, and only reinserted after successful completion when not cancelled. No provider handle is written into session, request projection, or durable execution state; restart therefore reseeds from canonical ScribeRig context.

The fingerprint is ScribeRig-owned rather than an upstream duplicate: it binds compiled profile and active component revisions, dependencies, omitted handles, provider context, and sorted capability/grant identity under the provider-continuation-v1 domain. The request projection separately fingerprints the canonical compiled context for request identity. The root runner computes its pre-use candidate fingerprint from the completed branch with the submitted human turn omitted, while execute_root_branch_with_continuation recompiles with the actual prompt and independently rechecks the supplied fingerprint before passing the upstream handle. That is consistent with the prompt being sent as the next upstream user message rather than baked into the prior continuation context; provider/model scope itself remains guarded by upstream and rechecked locally.

No concrete persistence or validation defect was established, so this audit changes no runtime code and checks no acceptance items. The next executable gate is focused lifecycle coverage at the owning runtime/app boundary: verify same-root reuse, provider/model/profile/thinking and context divergence reseed, cancelled or failed-turn non-reinsertion, branch isolation for child/plan workers, and restart reseed. Then verify each advertised provider route either extracts and consumes the opaque handle or cleanly remains stateless. Keep the continuation acceptance criteria and Task 144 G7 unchecked until that evidence exists; no tests or long checks were run for this audit.

docs.title: Branch-scoped continuation follow-up (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
The current transient continuation implementation is intentionally root-only. NativeTuiAgentRunner::execute_accepted removes and validates a cache entry keyed by the accepted root branch, and reinserts the opaque upstream handle only after successful completion. execute_root_branch_with_continuation recompiles the root context and independently validates its ScribeRig fingerprint before handing the handle to rpi-agent. The runner cache is the only lifecycle owner for these handles.

Child executions are dispatched recursively by upstream_execution/delegation.rs through the active branch broker and inherit the current upstream invocation. They do not enter the root runner, and their context is a context-isolation frame rather than a distinct executor identity per Level-1 021. Reusing or capturing a handle there would require defining which exact child context/provider selection it is bound to and how a later turn re-enters that child identity. The current branch/tool execution request does not expose a corresponding child-turn lifecycle.

Plan workers have a separate invocation lifecycle. plan_worker/execution.rs builds a precompiled UpstreamBranchInvocation from PlanWorkerContext and calls execute_precompiled_branch; that path neither accepts nor returns a continuation. Plan context includes exact ContinuationAnchor, ancestor and dependency results, local branch history, and resolved assignment. Those inputs differ from the root runner's completed-root fingerprint. Applying a root handle to that invocation would cross branch/context boundaries, while blindly associating handles with durable worker branches would be unsafe for retries, changed claims, plan edits, or changed dependencies.

No code change is made in this slice: the allowed runtime paths lack a shared transient cache lifecycle and exact reusable lineage key for child/worker executions. Adding a map keyed only by branch would not prove equivalence of anchor, plan claim, provider/model/profile/thinking assignment, and compiled context; adding persistence would violate the opaque-handle non-persistence invariant. A safe continuation extension needs an explicit in-memory owner scoped to the execution tree plus context fingerprints derived from each exact child/worker context, and lifecycle rules for child re-entry and plan retries. The focused lifecycle coverage requested by the preceding audit (same-scope reuse, divergence reseed, failure/cancellation non-reinsertion, branch isolation, and restart reseed) remains unrun. No acceptance criteria are checked by this follow-up.

docs.title: Child and durable plan continuation implementation gate (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
Do not add child-branch or plan-worker continuation reuse until the execution owner can prove exact semantic validity for every handle. The current root cache is not that owner: it is keyed only by root branch and its root lineage fingerprint cannot identify a nested child invocation or durable plan claim. Do not treat a branch-only map, provider/model match, or a smaller context cache key as sufficient.

The present lifecycle lacks a single ScribeRig-owned continuation identity and handoff spanning child execution and plan-worker execution. The child delegation request does not expose a re-entry identity/lifecycle for a later turn. PlanWorkerContext provides compiled inputs but does not itself bind a continuation record to the full durable execution tuple. In particular, PlanWorkerExecutor::execute_bound_upstream_worker has the exact PlanNode, WorkerClaim, ResolvedPlanExecution, and compiled context at dispatch, but the upstream precompiled execution API accepts no continuation and returns no extracted continuation. Any later reuse also needs the authoritative current plan revision and anchor resolution; a retry must distinguish claim identity and generation, and dependencies must bind their exact fulfilled result IDs.

The next implementation must first introduce an explicit ephemeral ScribeRig-owned continuation owner for the execution tree and establish a canonical validity value before passing a handle upstream. For child work, that requires a stable child execution identity and a defined re-entry point. For a plan worker, the validity value must include session and plan identity plus plan revision, node identity, ContinuationAnchor and its resolved location/result, worker branch, WorkerClaim ID and generation, claim assignment, resolved provider/model/profile/thinking identity, the complete canonical compiled-context fingerprint, and ordered ancestor/dependency result identities (including each dependency's fulfilled result ID). Resolve and compile from the authoritative snapshot for use, then recompute/compare that same ScribeRig value immediately before upstream handle application.

Preserve ScribeRig BranchResult, ContinuationAnchor, profile/context fingerprint, plan assignment, and branch identity as the source of validity and durable semantics. Keep upstream ProviderContinuation completely opaque provider-owned process state: never serialize it, include it in BranchResult/session identity, or let its provider response ID stand in for the ScribeRig key. Consume a candidate handle before an attempted execution; reinsert only after successful, non-cancelled completion whose returned ScribeRig lineage still matches. Any missing/stale plan, changed anchor or dependency, assignment/profile/context divergence, failed attempt, or cancellation must discard the handle and seed from canonical ScribeRig context. Process restart always reseeds.

Only after the child re-entry API and plan snapshot/claim inputs above are available, and focused lifecycle evidence covers same-key reuse, every-key component divergence, sibling/branch isolation, failed/cancelled non-reinsertion, and restart reseed, may child/plan continuation acceptance be marked complete. Until then retain stateless child and plan execution; this gate does not authorize a smaller cache or persistence of provider handles. No runtime code changed and no tests or long checks were run.

docs.title: Plan worker execution boundary and claim preflight (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
The scheduler is the ScribeRig coordinator for durable plan-node claims, assignment resolution, exact PlanWorkerContext compilation, concurrent node dispatch, and BranchResult settlement. Its scoped worker threads call PlanWorkerExecutor; the production NativePlanWorkerExecutor resolves the provider/model and invokes execute_precompiled_branch, which enters run_branch_with_semantic_broker and delegates the ordinary provider/tool loop to rpi-agent through run_upstream_branch_invocation_with_continuation. The thread scope in scheduler_execution_helpers.rs is plan-DAG dispatch concurrency, not a second model/tool loop. Keep it with the ScribeRig plan coordinator.

Claim setup previously mutated the caller's Plan before compiling all worker contexts and before durable claim persistence. A context compilation or persistence error could therefore return without execution while leaving the caller's in-memory plan in Running state. claim_workers now stages claims on a cloned plan, compiles every exact context against that staged plan, persists the staged claims, and only then replaces the caller's plan. Thus preflight or persistence failure leaves the caller's plan unchanged, while successful persistence and returned worker snapshots share the same claims. This preserves ScribeRig ownership of plan claims and assignment while keeping provider streaming, tool-call validation/settlement, and loop cancellation in upstream rpi-agent. No checklist item is checked by this source change; focused failure-path verification remains required. No tests or long checks were run.

Plugin semantic host-policy adapter (2026-10-21): the feature-gated scriberig-agent-runtime::plugin_worker::ApplicationDomainDispatcher now admits only the domain_operation host capability. It derives the exact base snapshot and branch from trusted host state, checks ScribeRig named/scoped domain grants, invokes the shared ApplicationService semantic operation, and returns only its bounded change handle. The plugin cannot supply trusted branch/snapshot identity or call validation, apply, merge, or promotion through this dispatcher; all other runtime-action capabilities remain denied unless separately implemented and allowlisted. This is adapter source only: it is uncommitted, no production worker/tool-catalog composition invokes it, and no tests/builds were run. Keep activation and the related acceptance criteria unchecked.

docs.title: Replace the Ratatui Shell and TUI-Kit Bridge with the Upstream TUI Runtime and Native Model Controls
docs.text:
Status: [ ] In Progress

Current dependency note (2026-10-21, late revalidation): all ScribeRig rpi-* dependencies now pin controlled fork commit ebcf8d5e75d20fa3a6cc7cc76cbcdcec4cc36eb8, based on official upstream 0.7.1 main 281dfddfa39ac063d86de57b75370974c4d75e6c. The fork additionally exports upstream key types, caches visible rows, adds validated TreeList item replacement, exposes a host tick callback on the TUI lifecycle, publishes theme preset metadata, and adds typed AssistantMessageEvent::ReasoningSummaryDelta plus the isolated worker boundary. Earlier focused checks passed at a previous pin; checks have not been rerun after this pin change. Older revision references below are historical implementation checkpoints.

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
After task 146 completes, make upstream rpi-tui the actual terminal product framework rather than a hidden primitive source underneath the existing ScribeRig Ratatui shell.

This task replaces the normal terminal lifecycle/render/input/focus/overlay/composer/model-control path with upstream TUI/component machinery.

It intentionally creates a visibly different implementation boundary. Passing tests while retaining the old Ratatui shell is not completion.

Do not begin task 148 until this sheet is complete.

docs.title: 2. Read Before Editing
docs.text:
• [ ] Read root and design/AGENTS.md.
  • [ ] Read crates/scriberig-tui/AGENTS.md and nearest instructions for all terminal/product code changed.
  • [ ] Read Level-1 documents 015, 020, 022.
  • [ ] Read Level-2 documents 021, 022, 032.

  • [ ] Inspect upstream model/provider/thinking selector code and task 145's upstream extraction gates.

docs.title: 3. Checklist Discipline
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this file open during implementation.
  • [ ] Tick exact criteria after focused verification.
  • [ ] Never bulk-tick.
  • [ ] Revert invalidated criteria.
  • [ ] Do not preserve the current Ratatui shell as the default compatibility path.
  • [ ] Do not convert upstream ANSI/component output back into Ratatui widgets.
  • [ ] Missing generic upstream UI primitives must be contributed upstream rather than recreated as a new ScribeRig widget framework.

docs.title: 4. Select Upstream Terminal Mode and Lifecycle
docs.text:
Use upstream terminal/runtime ownership for the active srig tui process.

Select the appropriate upstream regular/fullscreen mode according to the desired product behavior, but let upstream own:

terminal setup/restore
raw mode
alternate/main screen behavior
cursor
input loop
render scheduling
resize
focus routing
overlay routing

Acceptance:

  • [x] Active srig tui starts through upstream TUI runtime.
  • [x] ScribeRig's direct terminal guard is no longer the active lifecycle owner.
  • [x] Exactly one terminal lifecycle owner exists.
  • [ ] Normal exit, Ctrl-C, panic/error restoration remain covered.

docs.title: 5. Remove the Double-Rendering Bridge
docs.text:
The current path that uses upstream components internally and then strips/reconstructs their output through Ratatui must be removed from the normal product path.

Forbidden final pattern:

rpi-tui component.render()
  -> strip ANSI / flatten lines
  -> Ratatui Text/Paragraph/Block

Required final pattern:

ScribeRig semantic component
  + upstream components
  -> upstream TUI child/overlay composition
  -> upstream render/runtime

Static baseline audit (2026-10-20): crates/scriberig-tui/src/render_conversation.rs::conversation_text calls scriberig_tui_kit::render_markdown; that wrapper sanitizes the row text, renders it with upstream rpi_tui::Markdown, strips ANSI styling, and returns plain lines that conversation_text converts into Ratatui spans. The Markdown parser is already upstream-owned. The remaining duplicate is the flattening bridge into the active Ratatui shell. Do not remove the wrapper in isolation: it is currently the sanitization boundary, and its consumer still requires Ratatui text. Replace this entire path when the semantic conversation component is composed directly into the upstream TUI runtime. No acceptance item below is satisfied by this inventory alone.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Composer renders directly as an upstream component.
  • [x] Markdown/message rendering remains upstream-rendered through the final terminal path.
  • [x] Selection/list components render directly through upstream.
  • [x] Upstream theme/style output is not flattened and recreated in Ratatui.
  • [x] No normal render frame is built with Ratatui widgets.

docs.title: 6. Move the Composer to the Upstream Product Path
docs.text:
Use the upstream editor/composer directly as the active input component.

Preserve ScribeRig submission semantics:

ordinary prompt -> shared ScribeRig branch operation
recognized slash command -> local/upstream command dispatch
historical reply target -> stable ScribeRig ContinuationAnchor
multiline draft -> local UI state until submit

Acceptance:

  • [x] Startup composer is an upstream component.
  • [ ] Cursor/IME/Unicode behavior comes from upstream.
  • [ ] Paste goes through upstream terminal/editor behavior and ScribeRig safety policy.
  • [ ] ScribeRig stable reply anchor remains independent of editor cursor/focus.
  • [x] Submission does not bypass shared ScribeRig application operations.

docs.title: 7. Use Upstream Provider/Model/Thinking Controls
docs.text:
Provider/model/thinking selection must use upstream product/UI machinery rather than ScribeRig selectors built from upstream data.

rpi-tui already exposes reusable generic SelectItem, SelectList, and SearchableSelectList components. Adapt the ScribeRig credential-safe model library rows to those generic selector APIs; keep selection effects and ScribeRig assignment semantics in ScribeRig.

Do not extract the rpi-cli model/provider/thinking selector orchestration into rpi-tui. That code includes CLI catalog matching and ambiguity rules, provider authentication/default persistence, and AgentLane updates. Those behaviors are not generic UI responsibilities. A task-144/145 upstream contribution is warranted only if migration demonstrates a missing reusable UI primitive beyond the existing generic selector components.

Earlier pinned API integration checkpoint (superseded by the current pin): ScribeRig pinned the controlled pi-rust fork at 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, which includes the current bigfish1913/pi-rust upstream commit 7d019f85cde614a6aa267a7d2e816e04a7e6abbe and exposes typed rpi_tui::InputEvent, Component::handle_event(&InputEvent), native SelectList/SearchableSelectList components, and TuiAltScreen::{run_until, dispatch_input, note_resize}. The active conversation and selector paths use upstream Markdown, Editor, list, and fullscreen lifecycle APIs. At that checkpoint, run_until owned startup, input reading, and restoration; ScribeRig's synchronous application loop ran inside its stop predicate. The then-pinned Editor and selector lists did not implement typed event handling, so thin adapters forward normalized events to their upstream key and paste handlers. TuiAltScreen::set_focus owns the active component for composer, help, and selector paths. Because the pinned TuiAltScreen dispatches only to the focused component and has no global key hook, every ScribeRig focused adapter recognizes normalized Ctrl-C before forwarding input to upstream selectors, editors, and overlays. This keeps quit global while terminal input, focus, and lifecycle remain upstream-owned. Model-library selections still pass through the existing revision-checked ScribeRig reducers/effects. The scriberig-tui target has no Ratatui or scriberig-tui-kit dependency. The legacy renderer's semantic assertions were moved to model/projection tests; renderer-specific layout and style assertions were retired with that renderer. These test targets have compile-checked, but the tests have not been run.

The active command palette opens upstream SearchableSelectList on Ctrl+P. Its selected stable action ID returns to ScribeRig's existing reducer/effect path. Palette state no longer stores an upstream-backed stable selector.

Model and plan-node assignment selection now share the upstream selector path. The old ScribeRig palette-backed model/thinking picker implementation and its model-library-loaded overlay side effect were removed. /model, /thinking, the provider/model/thinking controls, command-palette actions, and /assign open upstream selector components; chosen IDs continue through the existing revision-checked ScribeRig session or plan operations. cargo fmt --all, the repository convention linter, and cargo check -p scriberig-tui --all-targets --locked pass after this change. Runtime interaction was not run; the user can verify the TUI behavior directly.

At the current fork pin, SelectList and SearchableSelectList both implement Component::handle_event, while SearchableSelectList also implements Focusable. Upstream selectors own filtering and row navigation; their callbacks return stable IDs to ScribeRig, whose reducers retain assignment and command semantics. Plain SelectList lacks a hardware-cursor focus contract, but this does not require a ScribeRig selector adapter. Use the upstream TuiAltScreen dispatch and resize APIs rather than adding a second generic dispatch framework.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Model selector is upstream UI.
  • [x] Provider selector is upstream UI where product-exposed.
  • [x] Thinking selector is upstream UI and shows levels from upstream selected-model metadata.
  • [x] Model switch updates thinking options using upstream behavior.
  • [x] Provider authentication/readiness is rendered from upstream state.
  • [x] No ScribeRig-local model selector/picker remains on the normal terminal path.

The source audit and package all-target compile verified this criterion. /model, /thinking, provider/model/thinking controls, command-palette actions, and /assign all open upstream selector components. The removed ScribeRig palette-backed model/thinking picker code has no production module or runtime call site. Interactive behavior remains for user verification.

The active root invocation resolves its selected upstream model and thinking assignment from one catalog snapshot. Provider construction receives that exact model value, avoiding a second catalog lookup between selection and binding. Plan workers now retain the exact upstream Model in the ephemeral ResolvedPlanExecution produced from the catalog snapshot used for selection; provider construction receives that model without a second catalog lookup. The resolved value is not serialized or debug-formatted. Custom model-property settings use upstream PropertyEditor and schema descriptors through the ScribeRig host adapter; Task 145 retains the remaining provenance and request-shaping verification gates.

Provider controls now display per-model credential readiness derived with upstream readiness_from_catalog and ScribeRig's destination-authorized secret provider. The projection is limited to available, missing, denied, unsupported, or catalog-header states. It never includes source names, endpoint URLs, or credential values. The local TUI obtains the projection from its configured agent runner; remote model-library responses may omit it when their host does not supply an authorized readiness resolver. This status describes credential availability only and does not claim that the provider endpoint has passed a live request health check.

The assignment and readiness strip adapts the current ScribeRig session selection, provider credential status, and shell message into upstream FooterComponent status/model/thinking fields. ScribeRig supplies semantic content and key hints; the upstream component owns footer layout and rendering.

docs.title: 8. Use Upstream Custom Model Property UI
docs.text:
When upstream supports editable model/provider custom properties, use upstream UI/config components.

Do not implement a ScribeRig-specific editor for:

sampling parameters
reasoning effort maps
compatibility flags
provider-specific model properties
custom model fields

If upstream lacks a generic custom-property editor needed by ScribeRig, complete the upstream contribution before checking this section.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Custom-property editing uses the upstream PropertyEditor component.
  • [x] Upstream model-runtime APIs validate property values before updating config and runtime models.
  • [x] ScribeRig applies local authorization policy and live-catalog refresh around upstream configuration.
  • [ ] A deterministic test exercises a property through upstream UI/config and into a resolved provider request.

Fork commit 46ea1250bd695540b7f0b395afd6e10518fc05ff adds rpi-tui::PropertyEditor and the schema-validated ModelsConfig update API. ScribeRig has a local TUI/service adapter that passes submitted values to upstream validation, checks the local agent_model_config_edit capability, and refreshes the live ModelCatalog. Secret-like, write-only, read-only, password-format, nested sensitive, and opaque compound properties are omitted before display. This does not create a ScribeRig property schema or expose schemas through protocol.

The upstream PropertyEditor supports distinct choice labels and opaque values. The cited b4b8739a5c0b6dab42293f70006222327be01845 revision was an earlier integration checkpoint, not the active pin. The current controlled fork pin at that checkpoint was bad1c5b4aa6f26cc231168d75a09165e990de39a; its model-runtime source includes ModelsConfigFile. When SCRIBE_AGENT_MODEL_CONFIG_PATH selects a file, edits are validated by upstream and atomically persisted through that API before the live catalog is refreshed. SCRIBE_AGENT_MODEL_CATALOG environment JSON remains read-only. Extension manifest-only models without a corresponding ModelsConfig row remain read-only. Source inspection of runtime/upstream/property_editor.rs, runtime/upstream/event_loop/input/model_properties.rs, service_operation_adapter.rs, and apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/model_properties.rs confirms that the UI uses upstream PropertyEditor, edits pass through upstream schema validation, and the embedded host requires agent_model_config_edit before publishing a transactionally persisted catalog refresh. These source-level criteria are checked; the end-to-end request-shaping criterion remains unchecked.

The active scriberig-tui shell depends on rpi-tui for keybinding key types. The controlled fork's rpi-tui root did not re-export the KeyCode and KeyModifiers types used by its public KeyCombo API, so ScribeRig had a redundant direct production dependency on Crossterm. A focused fork API contribution now re-exports those key types; ScribeRig imports them from rpi_tui and keeps Crossterm only as a test dependency for the test-only input translator. This does not move terminal input ownership back into ScribeRig; TuiAltScreen::run_until continues to own the live input reader and lifecycle.

docs.title: 9. Move Palette, Help, Status, Focus, and Overlays Upstream
docs.text:
Adopt upstream mechanics for:

command palette/search
help overlay
modal focus
confirmation/input overlays
status/footer
scroll/navigation primitives

ScribeRig may supply command/action rows and semantic content, but not another generic overlay framework.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Palette is an upstream component.
  • [x] Help is composed through upstream overlay/component APIs.
  • [x] Focus is managed by upstream TUI focus APIs.
  • [x] Confirmation and input dialogs are upstream overlays/components.
  • [x] Status/footer structure is upstream-owned.
  • [x] Important ScribeRig status remains visible through content supplied to upstream components.

The reachable /edit input flow now mounts an upstream Editor inside an upstream overlay and forwards changed, submitted, and cancelled values into the existing ScribeRig reducers. Confirmation state also has an upstream Dialog adapter: it renders the stored action, target, base, and summary, then emits only accept/cancel intents carrying the exact ConfirmedCommit shown. The existing CommitConfirmed reducer revalidates the review against that payload before issuing the shared commit operation; stale acceptance or cancellation events cannot act on a newer confirmation. Task 148 still needs to expose the review route through its semantic review surface.

docs.title: 10. Theme and Styling
docs.text:
Use upstream theme/style ownership.

ScribeRig may define semantic roles or map branch depth/status into upstream style tokens, but it must not maintain a second concrete color/theme framework.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Theme selection/application is upstream-owned.
  • [x] ScribeRig semantic roles map into upstream styles.
  • [x] Branch depth/status styling still has non-color structural/text cues.
  • [x] Theme changes do not alter semantic/execution state.

The ScribeRig-owned Tone/PaletteColor/StyleToken mapping and the scriberig-tui-kit crate have been removed. The active upstream conversation uses indentation and labels for hierarchy/status and leaves concrete styling to upstream component defaults. F6, /theme, and the command palette now expose the upstream dark/light/monochrome presets through upstream SelectList and apply_theme_preset; ScribeRig stores no concrete palette or theme state. Theme selection opens an upstream SelectList; the selection handler invokes only upstream apply_theme_preset. Source tracing confirms this branch does not write ScribeRig state, alter model resolution or request construction, or call application operations. Focused scriberig-tui Clippy and all-target compile checks pass. Semantic failure, warning, success, and neutral plan statuses map through rpi_tui::theme::theme() to the current upstream error, warning, success, and text colors. Durable plan and node lifecycle, candidate validation and conflict, operation lifecycle and failure, and stale-load notices use the same role bridge; ScribeRig stores no concrete colors. Focused all-target compile, Clippy, and repository lint pass; behavior tests remain unrun.

Theme preset catalogue follow-up (2026-10-21): upstream ThemePreset now exports its available presets, stable IDs, display labels, descriptions, and ID resolution. ScribeRig builds the upstream SelectList from that metadata and passes the selected ID back through the upstream preset resolver; it no longer maintains a second list of theme names or maps those names to upstream enum variants. The ScribeRig compile remains blocked by the separate uncommitted task 151 TreeList API calls described above; no tests were run.

docs.title: 11. Generic Layout Gaps Go Upstream
docs.text:
If ScribeRig requires generic layout behavior not currently exposed upstream, such as:

split panes
resizable regions
hierarchical viewport
table
virtualized list/tree
persistent status slot

contribute the generic primitive upstream.

A temporary local semantic component may compose existing upstream primitives, but do not build a parallel general-purpose layout system.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Every generic layout helper added during this task is either upstream code/API or explicitly ScribeRig-semantic.
  • [x] No new local widget/layout framework is introduced.

Source audit (2026-10-21): the active composition uses upstream VStack, Editor, Dialog, TreeList, SelectList, Markdown, FooterComponent, and TuiAltScreen overlay/focus APIs. ComposerAdapter, SemanticViewPanel, SelectionStatusPanel, and InputModalHeading carry ScribeRig conversation, semantic navigation, assignment/status projection, and input-purpose semantics; they do not provide generic layout, editor, selection, focus, or overlay mechanics. The retired scriberig-tui-kit crate and Ratatui dependency remain absent. Focused compile/lint checks pass.

docs.title: 12. Keep ScribeRig State Machine Only Where It Owns Product Semantics
docs.text:
The current event/action/reducer/effect architecture may retain semantic product state if useful, but it must no longer duplicate upstream terminal state.

Candidates to remain ScribeRig-owned:

current semantic selection
current branch/reply anchor
plan coordinator cursor
expanded semantic branch IDs

operation correlation
presentation preferences tied to ScribeRig activity

Candidates to delegate/remove:

terminal focus engine
editor cursor state outside upstream component
raw terminal event parsing
resize mechanics
widget selection internals
overlay stack mechanics
terminal theme internals

Acceptance:

  • [x] Remaining ScribeRig reducer state is semantic/product state, not a duplicate terminal engine.
  • [x] Upstream input/focus/component events are translated only where a ScribeRig intent is produced.

Source audit (2026-10-21): production runtime input is dispatched by upstream TuiAltScreen to upstream Component implementations. ComposerAdapter, SemanticViewPanel, and product overlays translate normalized upstream events only into ScribeRig reducer intents. The former backend-neutral event.rs, keymap.rs, and TuiState::apply_event are gated under cfg(test) and have no production callers; they are legacy unit-test scaffolding, not a second runtime input or focus engine. The live reducer retains session, branch, plan, semantic selection, and operation presentation state. Focused all-target compile, Clippy, and repository-lint checks pass; behavior tests remain unrun.

It now also asserts the startup composer hint, opens the upstream searchable command palette and help overlay, and returns to the composer.
