docs.title: 17. Implementation Notes
docs.text:
Record upstream TUI version/commit, any upstream UI extraction/contribution references, and the exact old shell files removed.

The obsolete vendored rpi-tui copy was removed. The active runtime uses the upstream rpi-tui path. The Ratatui renderer/layout implementation and its test-only modules have now been deleted, together with the scriberig-tui-kit crate and its workspace/dev-dependency references. The TUI manifest has no Ratatui dependency. Semantic activity, projection, hostile input, and visibility assertions were moved to upstream-component projection tests or retained as semantic-model assertions. Compile-only checks passed; tests and PTY scenarios have not been executed, so their acceptance remains unchecked.

Runtime ownership checkpoint before host-tick extraction (2026-10-21): runtime/upstream.rs launched the screen through TuiAltScreen::run_until at the previous pin. That API started TuiAltScreen and its render scheduler, then stopped it and restored the terminal even if the host predicate panics. TuiAltScreen::start owns the ProcessTerminal input reader and dispatches normalized key, paste, and resize events to the focused upstream component. At that checkpoint, ScribeRig's event loop remained responsible for application event polling, reducer/effect coordination, and forwarding semantic actions from component callbacks. Its 100 ms receive timeout was the host loop cadence; its redraw flag only coalesced state changes before calling upstream request_render. ScribeRig consumed key types re-exported by that pinned rpi-tui and no longer declared a direct Crossterm dependency. PTY lifecycle and panic restoration acceptance remained unexecuted and unchecked.

Host tick extraction (2026-10-21): the controlled fork added TuiAltScreen::run_until_with_tick at d7db6b3a12278e532a60eefd643949b7db1bbc58; the current pin includes that API and upstream theme preset metadata. The upstream lifecycle now schedules repeated nonblocking host ticks; runtime/upstream/event_loop.rs drains one queued composer input per tick instead of owning a recv_timeout(100ms) wait loop. Reducer/effect coordination and semantic application-event polling remain ScribeRig-owned. cargo check -p scriberig-tui --lib --locked compiled rpi-tui but stopped on the unrelated uncommitted task 151 projection adapter calling the not-yet- pinned TreeList::items and TreeList::replace_items APIs. The new ScribeRig event-loop path therefore remains unverified by compilation; no tests were run and the task completion criteria remain open.

Adapter boundary audit (2026-10-21): the visible control factory constructs upstream SelectList and SearchableSelectList for provider, model, thinking, theme, and command-palette choices; model search is upstream searchable input. Row content and callbacks carry ScribeRig selection semantics. At the previous pin, the selector widgets lacked normalized component event handling. The current controlled fork exposes Component::handle_event on both list types and Focusable on SearchableSelectList, so selectors can receive keys directly through the upstream focused component path. Plain SelectList still has no hardware-cursor focus contract. ScribeRig adapters may map selected stable IDs into application actions but must not duplicate selector key or filter behavior. A reusable generic component seam remains missing for composite VStack input routing and an application-wide key hook; contribute those upstream if a consumer needs them. Current property/modal adapters forward to upstream editors while mapping ScribeRig intents; remove only their generic forwarding code after the upstream composition/focus API supports the same behavior and Ctrl-C remains global. No provider/model/thinking widget or local selector behavior is retained; selectors use upstream list widgets.

Conversation state retains the full draft, pending prompt, submission status, error, and stable ConversationTarget, while the upstream Editor owns cursor, editing, paste, and selection behavior. InputState retains semantic text and validation only. Normal runtime sanitizes input at the ScribeRig inspector boundary and uses upstream components directly.

The local test-only TerminalGuard, terminal.rs, and terminal_tests.rs were removed after the active path moved to upstream TuiAltScreen::run_until. The PTY lifecycle case now waits for the upstream composer hint (F2 provider) before sending Ctrl-C; the existing bounded child wait checks bracketed paste, cursor visibility, and alternate-screen restoration. The PTY and golden acceptance were not executed. The pinned TuiAltScreen::run_until source wraps its stop predicate in catch_unwind, restores via stop, then resumes the panic, and its stop tests assert terminal restoration. No test drives that panic path through run_until, so panic restoration coverage remains open. The reachable /edit dialog now uses upstream Editor, VStack, and TuiAltScreen::show_overlay; ScribeRig continues to own the input purpose, validation, and reducer actions. Confirmation state uses upstream Dialog and overlay mechanics while CommitConfirmed retains exact command identity and review checks. The user-visible review action remains pending with Task 148's semantic review surface migration.

The PTY plan scenario now opens the Plans surface through the upstream searchable palette, selects a durable plan node, switches to Conversation, and reopens Plans to assert the same node remains selected. The golden candidate scenario asserts that the upstream confirmation overlay visibly contains the reviewed base and candidate-result snapshot labels. These visible assertions are authored but have not been executed; they do not satisfy the PTY acceptance checklist yet.

Semantic browsing now switches the upstream focused component between the upstream editor adapter and the ScribeRig semantic-view component. The focused view translates Up, Down, Enter, and Escape into ScribeRig reducer intents. Conversation browse mode also routes Left/Right to the existing ScribeRig branch-expansion action, guarded by the active conversation view and browse state; the reducer remains the owner of expanded branch identities and projection rebuilding. The former composer-local presentation_focus key-routing flag was removed; TuiAltScreen owns the active focus target. Focused compile and visible PTY verification remain outstanding, so focus checklist items remain unchecked.

Reusable component-input extraction (2026-10-21): the controlled fork worktree adds normalized event handling to SelectList and SearchableSelectList, focused-child routing and focus propagation to VStack, a global key handler and automatic component focus transfer to TuiAltScreen, and callback-driven keyboard handling to Dialog. Editor now supports an opt-in Escape callback. ScribeRig's consumer is being switched to those direct APIs: native selectors, one global Ctrl-C handler, upstream VStack routing for modal/property forms, and Dialog callbacks carrying the reviewed ConfirmedCommit. The local selector, confirmation, property-input, and focused-child event wrappers are removed in the working tree. The upstream API branch is not yet folded into the central controlled-fork pin, so compilation and behavioral checks remain pending. This note supersedes earlier adapter-gap descriptions; checklists remain unchecked.

Application keybinding registration (2026-10-21): the controlled pi-rust fork now exposes registration and enumeration on upstream Keybindings. ScribeRig registers its product actions in the upstream manager under stable scriberig.* IDs. The composer, global quit handler, help overlay, and footer read configured keys from that same manager; user remapping can therefore change the active controls and their displayed hints together. The API change is on a separate fork branch and is not yet included in the ScribeRig pin. No compile or runtime verification has been performed for this slice.

docs.title: Rebuild ScribeRig Semantic Session, Plan, and Review Surfaces as Upstream TUI Components
docs.text:
Status: [ ] In Progress

Current dependency note (2026-10-21, late revalidation): ScribeRig pins controlled fork commit ebcf8d5e75d20fa3a6cc7cc76cbcdcec4cc36eb8, based on official upstream 0.7.1 main 281dfddfa39ac063d86de57b75370974c4d75e6c. The merged upstream changes do not alter the rpi-tui component APIs used by these semantic surfaces. The pin adds public key-type reexports, tree row caching, TreeList::{items,replace_items}, host tick callbacks, and theme metadata. Earlier checks passed at an older pin; visible and behavior acceptance remains open.

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
After task 147 makes upstream rpi-tui the active terminal product framework, port the Scriberig-specific terminal surfaces onto upstream component/layout/focus/overlay/scroll/theme contracts.

These views remain Scriberig-specific because their data and interaction semantics depend on Scriberig architecture. Their terminal implementation must nevertheless be entirely on top of upstream UI primitives.

Do not begin task 149 until this sheet is complete.

docs.title: 2. Read Before Editing
docs.text:
• [x] Read root and design/AGENTS.md.
  • [ ] Read Level-1 documents 009, 010, 015, 017, 018, 019, 020, 022.
  • [ ] Read Level-2 documents 010, 021, 022, 024, 025, 032.
  • [ ] Read completed tasks 144–147.
  • [x] Read nearest instructions for TUI, session, plan, app, change/projection, and protocol code touched.
  • [x] Inspect upstream component/layout/scroll/tree/list/table primitives available at the pinned revision.

docs.title: 3. Checklist Discipline
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this file open while implementing.
  • [ ] Tick criteria immediately after implementation plus focused verification.
  • [ ] Never bulk-tick.
  • [ ] Revert invalidated checks.
  • [ ] Generic UI gaps go upstream; Scriberig code may own only semantic adaptation and domain-specific interaction.
  • [ ] Do not reintroduce Ratatui to simplify one custom panel.

docs.title: 4. Define the Scriberig Component Set
docs.text:
Create or converge on focused upstream-component implementations for current product needs, conceptually:

RecursiveConversationComponent
SessionTreeComponent
PlanComponent
SemanticExplorerComponent
SemanticInspectorComponent
HistoryComponent
DiffComponent
ProjectionComponent
CandidateReviewComponent
OperationsComponent
EffectivePromptComponent
ReasoningActivityComponent

Exact boundaries may differ, but each component must consume Scriberig presentation/semantic models and render through upstream UI APIs.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Every custom terminal surface has an explicit Scriberig semantic owner and an upstream UI base.
  • [ ] No component owns storage/provider/package/model-catalog behavior.
  • [ ] No component owns terminal lifecycle.
  • [ ] No component returns Ratatui widgets.

docs.title: 5. Recursive Conversation Component
docs.text:
Preserve the distinctive conversation/session projection:

recursive branch placement
stable branch/activity identity
historical reply anchors
nested ancestry rails/structure
compact BranchResult rows
expand/collapse by stable branch identity
plan/model/tool activity at structural location
streaming transient activity

Use upstream component/layout/scroll/text/theme machinery for presentation.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Conversation is an upstream Component or composition of upstream components.
  • [ ] Navigation cursor, reply anchor, and plan coordinator remain distinct Scriberig identities.
  • [ ] Historical continuation stays anchored by semantic identity after reorder/resize.
  • [ ] Expand/collapse is presentation-only.
  • [ ] Parent context never receives expanded child transcript merely because UI expanded it.
  • [ ] Streaming rows use upstream rendering and do not become a second canonical transcript.

docs.title: 6. Session Tree Component
docs.text:
Render durable recursive session structure with upstream hierarchical/list primitives.

Show, where available:

branch labels/status
parent/child structure
BranchResult summary
execution assignment reference
activity/detail expansion

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Stable branch IDs back activatable rows.
  • [ ] Plan dependency edges are not inferred from branch parentage.
  • [ ] Branch activation does not move reply anchor unless the explicit Scriberig action does so.
  • [ ] Generic tree navigation/virtualization comes from upstream or an upstream contribution.

TreeList and SelectList integration (2026-10-21): this audit was initially performed at fork commit 3f3a0b2db91eb87f5c5b68485b1c4c3394a240a9 and rechecked against the previous active pin 6e65635a2ac2336a86847d85e2c3bb771a945c87. The active pin descends from 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5, which adds application-registered keybindings with shared help/footer enumeration, and merges official upstream pi-rust 0.7.1. The rpi-tui component APIs used by these semantic views remain available at the active pin: semantic_views.rs composes the adapter from semantic_views/tree.rs, semantic_views/selection.rs, and semantic_views/details.rs. The tree module builds rpi_tui::TreeList items from the already-filtered ScribeRig ConversationModel.rows and SessionModel.rows. Namespaced stable source IDs map selection back to ScribeRig conversation identity or the existing session cursor. Session selection is retained as SessionRowIdentity (row kind plus semantic reference) in TuiState.session_cursor; an authoritative session refresh resolves that identity into the new row order before updating the numeric reducer cursor. Pending branch focus takes precedence, and missing rows fall back to the first available session row rather than activating whichever row inherited the old index. Up/Down movement is applied by TreeList, then forwarded through the ScribeRig cursor reducer, which updates both the numeric cursor and stable row identity. The ScribeRig projection and reducer remain the sole owners of expanded_branches; TreeList expands only rows present in the projection. The selection module builds upstream SelectList items for ready Explorer, History, Find, Diff, and Operations projections. Their source IDs derive from semantic row references, and Up/Down is forwarded as the existing cursor action; Enter remains the existing Activated action. TuiState.semantic_row_cursor retains typed identities for these views. Authoritative refreshes resolve the identity into the new row order before updating the numeric reducer cursor; missing rows fall back to the nearest valid position. The details module supplies bounded selected-row/context content to upstream Markdown. Overview and Projection remain Markdown because each presents one selected entity/document rather than a selectable row set. Changes remains Markdown because its cursor spans validation detail rows while activation confirms the current candidate as a whole. These adapters compiled, but no tests were run and Task 148 acceptance items remain unchecked pending behavioral verification.

Reusable TreeList updates (2026-10-21, uncommitted upstream worktree): the controlled fork branch codex/scriberig-upstream-ownership now carries TreeList::items() and TreeList::replace_items(Vec<TreeItem>) in crates/rpi-tui/src/tree_list.rs. replace_items validates the complete item set first (unique non-empty IDs, resolved parents, acyclic depth); keeps selection when the selected ID survives and falls back to the first new item when it is removed (clearing selection for an empty set); keeps expansion only for surviving parents with children and expands newly added parents; and rebuilds item/child/depth indexes plus cached visible rows and viewport bounds. Invalid replacement leaves the previous items and selection unchanged. ScribeRig retains one Mutex<Option<TreeList>> in crates/scriberig-tui/src/runtime/upstream/semantic_views.rs and only calls replace_items when projected TreeItem values change. semantic_views/projection.rs owns TreeProjection, initial expansion, reuse, and selection synchronization; semantic_views/tree.rs::projection and semantic_views/plan.rs::projection produce items/selection/details without constructing a component. handle_tree_movement moves the retained tree and derives the semantic direction from projected item order instead of building a temporary tree per keypress. Plan rows still take parent_id only from PlanNodeParent; PlanDependency edges remain Markdown detail rows, so the dependency DAG is not folded into tree parentage.

Remaining gaps: the update API exists only in the upstream working tree, not a committed/pinned fork revision; the Cargo pin remains bad1c5b4aa6f26cc231168d75a09165e990de39a and was not changed. No compile/test/PTY verification was run, so the upstream contribution and the ScribeRig reuse path remain unverified. The §6 acceptance items for stable row identity, independent dependency edges, reply-anchor behavior, and upstream tree navigation remain unchecked pending that verification.

docs.title: 7. Plan Component
docs.text:
Render durable Scriberig plans and the separate dependency DAG without confusing it with the session tree.

Show current equivalents of:

plan goal/status/revision
plan node status
node branch ownership
node execution assignment
blocked/ready/running/completed state
dependency results
coordinator position/claim
supersession/replan history where product-exposed

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Plan node identity is stable semantic identity.
  • [ ] Dependency edges come from plan knowledge, not visual ordering.
  • [ ] Coordinator state remains separate from user navigation cursor.
  • [ ] Model/provider/thinking labels are projections of upstream-resolved execution selection from task 145.
  • [ ] Plan actions still route through shared Scriberig application operations.

docs.title: 8. Semantic Explorer and Inspector Components
docs.text:
Preserve universal semantic navigation rather than turning the UI into a filesystem browser.

Rows may represent:

entities
relations
collections
revisions
snapshots
projections
derived knowledge
advertised operations

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Activatable rows store stable semantic references.
  • [ ] Revision and snapshot identity remain distinguishable.
  • [ ] Source paths are projection metadata, not universal identity.
  • [ ] Capability discovery determines available semantic actions.
  • [ ] Generic list/search/scroll/focus comes from upstream.

docs.title: 9. History and Diff Components
docs.text:
History is lineage; diff is semantic/domain diff data.

Do not derive semantic equality from terminal text.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Exact base/target revision/snapshot identity is preserved.
  • [ ] Semantic changed objects/operations come from Scriberig shared results.
  • [ ] Textual/projection diff fragments render through upstream safe text/Markdown/diff primitives where available.
  • [ ] Navigating diff/history is read-only presentation state.

If upstream has a reusable diff component, use it. If not and a generic diff component would be broadly useful, contribute it upstream rather than building a general Scriberig diff widget.

docs.title: 10. Projection Component
docs.text:
Render known projections as safe external content using upstream text/Markdown/code presentation.

Preserve:

projection identity
semantic source identity
snapshot/base
style/renderer
path when applicable
stale/conflict/read-only metadata when provided

Acceptance:

  • [x] Projection bytes/text are untrusted data to upstream safe renderer.
  • [x] Projection editing/reconciliation routes through Scriberig semantic change operations.
  • [x] No component performs direct live file writes for understood domains.
  • [x] Generic code/Markdown scrolling/rendering is upstream-owned.

docs.title: 11. Candidate Review and Validation Component
docs.text:
Preserve the canonical change path:

candidate
 -> exact semantic/projection diff
 -> validation evidence
 -> conflicts/stale-base/trust
 -> explicit intent
 -> shared promote/apply operation
 -> authoritative successor state

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Candidate/base/result identities are visible or inspectable.
  • [ ] Validation evidence remains bound to the exact candidate.
  • [ ] Conflict/stale-base state cannot be bypassed by terminal confirmation.
  • [ ] Confirmation is upstream overlay/UI mechanics around a Scriberig intent.
  • [ ] Promotion uses shared Scriberig application semantics.

Task 147 migrated the reachable /edit input dialog and change-review confirmation to upstream Editor, Dialog, and overlay mechanics. The Changes view now exposes base and result snapshots, validation status and diagnostic, validation profile, conflicts, review details, affected semantic entities, and exact entity revision transitions through upstream Markdown. It explains when the result identity is unavailable. The upstream dialog displays the exact result snapshot held in the confirmation intent. CommitConfirmed checks base, result, change, and branch against the current passed, conflict-free review before it emits the shared application commit operation. Focused projection and stale-result reducer tests were added; test targets were compile-checked but tests were not executed. The acceptance criteria remain unchecked pending behavioral test execution and interactive review.

Visible PTY coverage was extended to reach Plans from the upstream searchable palette, select a durable plan node, change to Conversation, and confirm that the same node remains selected when Plans is reopened. The golden candidate flow now asserts the reviewed base and candidate-result labels in the upstream confirmation overlay. These PTY assertions were not executed and do not mark the view acceptance complete.

docs.title: 12. Operations Component
docs.text:
Render shared Scriberig operation lifecycle using upstream components.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Operation identity/status/progress/result come from shared application state.
  • [ ] Cancellation calls shared Scriberig cancellation.
  • [ ] Generic progress/status visual mechanics use upstream components where available.
  • [ ] Terminal state does not fabricate operation progress absent from shared state.

docs.title: 13. Effective Prompt and Reasoning Activity Components
docs.text:
Preserve independent observability settings:

Prompt: Hidden | Summary | Full
Reasoning: Hidden | Summary | FullAvailable
Tool/operation detail according to shared presentation settings

Use upstream text/Markdown/scroll components for display.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Full prompt shows the complete safe Scriberig effective request, not raw provider HTTP payload.
  • [ ] Reasoning preserves provider-visible invocation-local ordering.
  • [x] Hidden private chain-of-thought remains unavailable.
  • [x] Visibility changes rerender stored activity only and do not execute provider/tool work.

docs.title: 14. Slash Commands and Upstream Plugin Commands
docs.text:
The terminal command surface combines:

Scriberig built-in semantic commands
upstream provider/model/thinking/package commands
upstream plugin-registered slash commands

Use upstream command/palette infrastructure.

Scriberig command handlers translate semantic commands to shared application intents.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Plugin commands are discovered through upstream extension host.
  • [ ] Model/provider/thinking commands use upstream handlers/components.
  • [ ] Scriberig semantic commands preserve capability checks.
  • [ ] Help/palette presents one coherent command surface rather than separate registries.

docs.title: 15. Upstream Panel/Component Extension Point
docs.text:
Built-in Scriberig components may compile directly against rpi-tui.

If third-party terminal plugins need arbitrary custom panels and upstream lacks a stable registration seam:

  • do not create a Scriberig-only terminal plugin ABI;
  • complete the upstream contribution gate for a generic panel/component extension point;
  • consume it after pinning the compatible revision.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] No parallel Scriberig terminal plugin ABI exists.
  • [ ] Any plugin-supplied terminal panel support is upstream-owned or explicitly blocked pending upstream work.

docs.title: 16. Large Trees, Virtualization, and Responsiveness
docs.text:
Session and semantic trees may be large.

Use upstream viewport/scroll/virtualization primitives. If missing, contribute a generic upstream primitive.

Acceptance:

  • [ ] Rendering is bounded to visible/needed rows.
  • [ ] Deep recursive branches do not cause unbounded per-frame work.
  • [ ] Resize preserves semantic selection/reply anchors.
  • [ ] Unicode/wide/combining content behaves according to upstream width machinery.
  • [ ] No local general-purpose virtualization engine is introduced.

docs.title: 17. Terminal Safety
docs.text:
All external/model/tool/source/document strings remain untrusted.

Use upstream safe rendering APIs and structured styles; never concatenate model-generated raw ANSI/OSC into terminal control output.

Acceptance:

  • [x] Hostile control-sequence corpus passes through conversation and auxiliary components.
  • [x] Projection/tool/error content cannot inject terminal controls through normal APIs.
  • [ ] Clipboard/image behavior follows upstream product policy and Scriberig capability policy.
  • [x] No Scriberig component adds a raw_ansi(external_string) path.

docs.title: 18. Focused End-to-End Scenarios
docs.text:
Add deterministic PTY/golden scenarios covering:

new conversation
historical reply -> child branch
nested branch collapse/expand
plan with dependency
semantic explorer/inspect
history/diff/projection
candidate review and validation
operation cancellation
full prompt/reasoning visibility toggles
plugin slash command
resize/scroll
  • [ ] Recursive conversation scenario passes.
  • [ ] Plan scenario passes.
  • [ ] Semantic explorer/review scenario passes.
  • [ ] Observability scenario passes.
  • [ ] Plugin command scenario passes.

docs.title: 19. Deletion Gate
docs.text:
Update task 144's deletion ledger.

Old Scriberig render modules should be removed as each semantic surface reaches the new upstream component path.

At completion:

  • [ ] No normal custom surface depends on Ratatui.
  • [ ] No duplicate old renderer remains reachable.
  • [ ] Generic tree/list/layout helpers are upstream or upstream-bound contributions.
  • [ ] Scriberig TUI code primarily contains semantic presentation models, upstream component implementations/adapters, and product intents.

docs.title: 20. Completion Gate
docs.text:
• [ ] Re-read every checked criterion.
  • [ ] Confirm every custom panel is built on upstream UI.
  • [ ] Confirm Scriberig semantic identities remain authoritative.
  • [ ] Confirm no custom panel recreated a generic terminal framework.
  • [ ] Confirm task 144 deletion ledger is current.
  • [ ] Leave task 149 Not Started until this task is complete.

Then set:

**Status: [x] Complete**

docs.title: 21. Implementation Notes
docs.text:
Record which upstream components each Scriberig semantic surface uses and any upstream generic UI contributions required during the port.

The active PrimaryView renders its ScribeRig-owned semantic read models through upstream components in crates/scriberig-tui/src/runtime/upstream/semantic_views.rs and its focused modules. Conversation and Session use rpi_tui::TreeList; ready Explorer, History, Find, Diff, and Operations rows use rpi_tui::SelectList; supplementary details and single-document/single-entity views use rpi_tui::Markdown. Values are terminal-sanitized, Markdown-escaped, bounded per value, and row-bounded. The conversation view keeps the recursive session projection and separately renders durable plan status, structural parents, execution assignments, BranchResult identities, coordinator state, and explicit dependency edges from the canonical session snapshot. Prompt detail and safe activity summaries follow the existing presentation visibility settings. Candidate confirmation now displays and validates the exact result snapshot against the current review alongside its base snapshot before it issues the shared commit intent. The upstream command palette reaches conversation, overview, semantic explorer, find, history, diff, projection, candidate review, session, and operation views. Choosing the semantic explorer sets the ScribeRig presentation focus and resets its cursor; the upstream composer routes F7 browse mode's Up/Down/Enter actions through the ScribeRig reducer, and Escape returns to editing. In the recursive conversation view, F7 also enters ScribeRig conversation-browse mode, Enter pins the selected reply cursor through ConversationPinCursor, and Left/Right toggles the selected branch's presentation expansion through ConversationToggleExpansion. These actions retain stable semantic identity and remain independent of the plan coordinator cursor. The ScribeRig cursor reducer remains the identity and activation owner: upstream row movement is translated to its existing cursor action, and Enter is still reduced as ScribeRig Activated. List selection uses typed stable semantic identities across authoritative refreshes; session selection uses SessionRowIdentity to survive authoritative row reorder. Overview and Projection are single-document/single-entity views, and Changes activation confirms the candidate as a whole, so these remain Markdown. This remains incomplete: stable identity activation for every row, all view-specific actions, richer focus/layout behavior, PTY scenarios, and behavioral verification remain outstanding. Task 147's visible PTY gate also remains unchecked; no tests were run.

Plan projection (2026-10-21): the dedicated Plans view uses upstream rpi_tui::TreeList for plan and structural plan-node rows, plus upstream Markdown for the selected plan/node details. PlanSelection retains the stable (plan, optional node) identity separately from the conversation cursor and coordinator_cursor. Tree parent IDs come only from PlanNodeParent; dependency edges remain explicit PlanDependency values rendered as edge rows in the details section, including their fulfilled_by result. Node detail shows lifecycle status, branch, BranchResult, safe model assignment, worker claim, and expected result. The existing /plan lifecycle and /assign commands still issue shared application effects; from the Plans view they resolve their target from PlanSelection instead of changing the conversation or coordinator cursor. The available upstream TreeList and Markdown APIs cover this read-only view; no ScribeRig generic graph or widget framework was added. Upstream TreeList models structural hierarchy but does not provide a reusable dependency-DAG graph component. The current view exposes canonical edges through upstream Markdown; any graphical DAG component should be contributed to rpi-tui before ScribeRig adopts it. Focused projection tests were added and compiled with cargo check --offline -p scriberig-tui --tests; the tests were not executed. The task remains incomplete pending behavioral execution and interactive verification.

Adapter audit (2026-10-21): ScribeRig semantic views use upstream TreeList, SelectList, and Markdown; status uses upstream FooterComponent; property editing uses upstream PropertyEditor and Editor; confirmations use upstream Dialog; and overlays/lifecycle use TuiAltScreen. SemanticViewPanel is retained because it projects canonical session/plan/semantic identities into upstream rows and maps navigation back to ScribeRig reducer actions. ConfirmationOverlayAdapter, ModalOverlayController, and input/property adapters retain ScribeRig review identity, validation, and reducer routing. The SelectorAdapter is a temporary generic bridge because upstream selector components expose handle_key but lack Component::handle_event and, for plain SelectList, Focusable. VStack likewise does not forward input to focused children. Their removal gate is reusable normalized-input/focus routing in rpi-tui, plus an upstream global key hook to avoid duplicating Ctrl-C interception. The upstream CLI's selector router is private to rpi-cli, so it is not consumed as a library API. Provider, model, and thinking controls are built with upstream selector components; this TUI slice does not alter catalog/service data ownership. No checklist items were changed to complete because these gaps and the unrun behavior checks remain open.

Renderer deletion follow-up (2026-10-21): removed the test-only Ratatui renderer and scriberig-tui-kit. Its semantic activity identity/redaction, hostile-value sanitization, projection metadata, and visibility assertions were retained in semantic model or upstream component projection tests. The former layout, width, and style assertions exercised only the retired renderer. TUI and PTY test targets compile-checked after the deletion; none of the tests or PTY scenarios have been executed. All acceptance checkboxes stay unchecked until their required behavior and visible terminal checks are run.

Event/focus extraction follow-up (2026-10-21): the fork worktree adds reusable Component::set_focus_state, selector typed-event dispatch, VStack focused child dispatch, TuiAltScreen::set_global_input_handler, automatic focus transfer, and generic Dialog callbacks. ScribeRig removes its selector and confirmation wrappers and its property editor event/focus wrappers; semantic input headings and stable confirmation identities remain ScribeRig-owned. The upstream branch is pending central controlled-fork integration, so the consumer has not yet been compile-checked. No tests were run, and no checklist items are newly checked. This follow-up supersedes the earlier adapter audit's temporary selector/global-key bridge conclusions.

Safe-rendering and projection-identity follow-up (2026-10-21): the shared semantic-view value formatter in crates/scriberig-tui/src/runtime/upstream/semantic_views/common.rs now escapes terminal control characters as visible \u{...} text, escapes Markdown inline punctuation including links and ordered-list markers, and leaves exact identities such as ent_... and sna_... literal so users can still copy and compare them. The previous blanket escaping changed those identifiers and silently broke the expected evidence in conversation, session, plan, changes, and projection views. The Projection view now also renders the projection identity, the adapter-supplied source path, and synchronization state when present, instead of dropping that metadata. Added focused tests for identity preservation and the hostile terminal corpus. cargo test --offline -p scriberig-tui --lib semantic_views passes 10/10. The full scriberig-tui library target still has 8 failures in state, palette, and model-selection tests that belong to task 147's in-flight migration in this working tree; those files were not modified here. PTY acceptance execution remains outstanding.

Verification update (2026-10-21): cargo clippy --offline -p scriberig-tui --all-targets -- -D warnings passes. The full PTY acceptance suite (cargo test --offline -p scriberig --test tui_pty, 28 scenarios) was executed and every scenario failed while the task 147 migration is still in flight; a single re-run of tui_pty_starts_without_a_project also failed, so this is not specific to the semantic-view changes. Section 18 scenarios therefore remain unchecked.

Semantic list search adapter (2026-10-21): ScribeRig's stable row key remains the upstream SelectItem.value, while its already-sanitized label and description are combined with upstream SelectItem::with_search_text. This lets the upstream SelectList fuzzy filter match semantic kind, exact entity and snapshot references, migration base/result, preview, and operation status without replacing the activation identity with display text. The pinned rpi-tui implementation uses search_key() for fuzzy filtering and falls back to value when no search text is provided. No tests were run and no acceptance checkbox was changed.

Plan selection consistency follow-up (2026-10-21): the Plans adapter now resolves a single stable PlanSelection from the retained semantic cursor, numeric cursor fallback, or first available row and uses it for both the upstream TreeList highlight and the selected Markdown details. This prevents the no-identity fallback from highlighting a later node while showing details for the first plan row. A focused regression test covers that cursor fallback; tests were not run per task execution constraints, so no feature acceptance checkboxes were changed.

Stable selection and coordinator-presentation follow-up (2026-10-21): semantic_views/tree.rs now retains a matching semantic row identity without falling back to an unrelated numeric row when that identity disappears; a numeric fallback remains only when no semantic identity exists. semantic_views/plan.rs separately labels the durable plan node at coordinator_cursor, without changing user navigation or PlanSelection. Both files use upstream TreeList for generic row rendering/navigation. Exact-file formatting and scoped diff checks passed; no tests/builds or PTY scenarios were run, so behavior and all related acceptance remain unchecked.

Semantic coverage audit (2026-10-21): source inspection confirms that visible tree/list rendering is delegated to upstream rpi_tui::TreeList, rpi_tui::SelectList, and rpi_tui::Markdown through crates/scriberig-tui/src/runtime/upstream/semantic_views.rs and its semantic_views/tree.rs, plan.rs, selection.rs, and details.rs modules. The ScribeRig Component adapter SemanticViewPanel still owns the composition and maps upstream input to ScribeRig reducer actions; thus rendering primitives and generic tree/list navigation are upstream-owned, while semantic projection, focus policy, and activation routing remain local adapters.

Recursive session identity is represented by SessionRowIdentity in crates/scriberig-tui/src/view/session.rs (row kind plus semantic reference), and SessionModel::from_session traverses nested branches with a visited-ID set, preserving BranchResult rows and presentation-only expansion state. semantic_views/tree.rs namespaces session row IDs and conversation source IDs before building TreeItems; TuiState.session_cursor and the conversation cursor are reconciled against these identities. conversation_structure.rs keeps continuation anchors and plan worker branch placement explicit. Plans remain a separate projection: semantic_views/plan.rs builds structural parents from PlanNodeParent only, while dependency edges are rendered in plan/details.rs from Plan.dependencies. This is good evidence for identity/DAG separation, but currently the plan tree shows structural parentage/status/IDs and details carry the dependencies; the focused PTY scenario only proves durable node selection survives switching views, not a plan with dependencies or an interaction across reorder/resize.

Candidate/review projection is in semantic_views/model_views.rs::changes: it renders candidate/base/result snapshots, validation/profile, conflicts, diagnostics, and entity revision transitions through Markdown. The actual confirmation guard is reducer logic (CommitConfirmed) that compares the confirmation intent with the current passed, conflict-free review before emitting the shared commit operation. This is stronger evidence than display alone, but acceptance still lacks executed behavioral/PTY evidence for stale-base/conflict rejection and exact-candidate validation binding. The currently documented PTY assertion for base/result labels checks visible copy only.

Remaining executable acceptance gaps: execute deterministic PTY scenarios for nested branch collapse/expand and historical reply anchoring, plan dependency display and node identity under authoritative reorder/resize, semantic explorer/review activation, and candidate stale/conflict confirmation rejection; exercise bounded visible-row behavior on a large/deep tree and resize/scroll selection preservation; then update only the relevant checkboxes with the results. No tests or PTY commands were run for this audit, so no acceptance checkboxes were changed.

docs.title: Remove Superseded Local Infrastructure, Prove Delegation, and Finish the Correction
docs.text:
Status: [ ] In Progress

Current dependency note (2026-10-21, late revalidation): the active pin is now controlled fork commit ebcf8d5e75d20fa3a6cc7cc76cbcdcec4cc36eb8, based on official upstream 0.7.1 main 281dfddfa39ac063d86de57b75370974c4d75e6c. The pin includes the isolated plugin worker/sandbox boundary and typed AssistantMessageEvent::ReasoningSummaryDelta; ScribeRig still does not activate workers in production. The historical check below remains a checkpoint, not current pin evidence.

Previous upstream revision check (2026-10-21, before provider-snapshot integration): official bigfish1913/pi-rust main was at 7a272ecf42e5ec17efedc92031a5cdba85e213e9. The controlled ScribeRig fork pin b78a199486351d86804995c27a0c5ed2bd8a28e3 descended from that merge and added the model catalog, transactional config, stream lifecycle, TUI component event/focus extractions, and application-registered keybindings with shared help/footer enumeration. docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
Finish the upstream-first correction after tasks 144 through 148 are complete.

This task deletes obsolete local commodity infrastructure, proves that the final product actually delegates model/provider/agent/plugin/TUI concerns upstream, preserves Scriberig-specific semantics, validates local/remote/web conformance, and runs the final repository gate.

The task is intentionally deletion- and evidence-heavy. It must not be completed merely because the new TUI looks better.

docs.title: 5. Dependency Graph Acceptance
docs.text:
Inspect final normal dependencies.

The target should show Scriberig integrated product code consuming upstream crates/services while semantic foundation crates remain independent of terminal/provider concerns.

Acceptance:

  • [x] scriberig-tui or its successor has no direct Ratatui dependency.
  • [x] The active TUI consumes upstream rpi-tui directly through semantic components/adapters.
  • [x] Agent runtime consumes upstream rpi-agent/rpi-ai or their current upstream replacements.
  • [ ] Integrated plugin host consumes upstream plugin SDK/extension runtime.
  • [x] Model/provider catalog resolves from upstream runtime.
  • [x] Semantic foundation crates do not depend on rpi-tui.
  • [x] No rpi-harness identity replaces Scriberig sessions/branches.

Task 149 cleanup progress (2026-10-21): removed the Ratatui renderer/layout modules and their test-only module tree from scriberig-tui; removed the scriberig-tui-kit workspace crate and its manifest/development dependency; removed the Ratatui development dependency. Semantic activity identity, redaction, hostile-value, projection metadata, and visibility assertions now live with the semantic model or upstream component projections. The old renderer's layout/style-specific assertions are retired with that renderer. rg found no code references to the retired renderer, Ratatui, or TUI kit in the active TUI, PTY tests, or workspace manifests. cargo check --offline -p scriberig-tui --tests and cargo check --offline -p scriberig --test tui_pty are compile-only checks; neither tests nor PTY scenarios have been run. The static dependency-graph items below are checked only where current manifests, source searches, and compilation establish them; behavioral and broader deletion acceptance remains open pending its specified verification gates.

Terminal runtime inspection (2026-10-21): the production launch path reaches TuiAltScreen::run_until in crates/scriberig-tui/src/runtime/upstream.rs. At the pinned revision, run_until starts the upstream render scheduler and terminal runtime, waits for the ScribeRig application predicate, and restores the terminal on exit or panic. The upstream ProcessTerminal reader dispatches input and resize events through the focused upstream component tree. The local event loop is retained for ScribeRig application-event polling and reducer / effect scheduling; it requests frames through upstream request_render and does not read terminal events or paint frames. The normal crossterm 0.27 dependency matches the type used in rpi-tui; the temporary renamed alias and duplicate 0.28 development dependency were removed. No generic upstream runtime extraction gap was found in this path. PTY and restoration behavior remain unexecuted, so the corresponding deletion/acceptance checkboxes stay open.

Runtime ownership closure audit (2026-10-21, pinned fork 15a68ef2d69a312122c09c1eccfa0fbd454c48b5): production one-shot provider creation in apps/scriberig/src/main_agent_execution/upstream.rs calls rpi_model_runtime::create_builtin_provider; native TUI provider resolution in apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent.rs uses the same factory and its ModelCatalog. crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/upstream_invocation.rs builds rpi_agent::Agent/AgentBuilder, consumes upstream AgentEvent, and uses the upstream continuation-aware stream; its remaining request projection is retained for canonical ScribeRig provenance. The fake providers in apps/scriberig/src/{deterministic_provider.rs,self_hosting_provider.rs} only produce scripted rpi_ai::AssistantMessage values for deterministic semantic scenarios and do not implement provider transport. apps/scriberig/src/agent_tool.rs, crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/tools.rs, and apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/upstream_execution/{execution,broker,delegation}.rs remain ScribeRig semantic-operation, branch-authorization, and child-result adapters; they do not parse provider tool calls or run a second model loop.

This audit also removed the unused local branch-state/event/cancellation machinery: BranchPhase, BranchRuntimeState, CancellationTree, RuntimeEvent, and RuntimeEventLog had no production consumers. The pinned rpi-agent exports AgentEvent (crates/rpi-agent/src/events.rs) and carries the run CancellationToken in AgentLoopConfig.signal (crates/rpi-agent/src/hooks.rs). crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/events.rs and its module export were deleted. The retained crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/orchestration.rs::RuntimeLimits now holds only the four live ScribeRig bounds (max_tool_calls, max_child_branches, max_depth, max_active_branches), consumed by the semantic broker and recursive branch admission. The unused generic model-step and provider-duration fields and test-only state-machine/cancellation checks were removed. The remaining RuntimeLimits are ScribeRig recursion/tool policy; the pinned upstream AgentLoopConfig exposes cancellation and sequencing but no matching semantic branch quota API.

The plugin/extension boundary now has isolated-worker source, but acceptance remains open. The controlled fork adds crates/rpi-extensions/src/isolated/ (protocol.rs, client/mod.rs, client/launch.rs, client/reader.rs, worker.rs, plugin.rs) with a versioned JSON-lines protocol, injected worker launcher, process-tree supervision, startup/request timeouts, cancellation, host-capability RPC, worker-side plugin loading, and tool execution through PluginToolAdapter inside the worker process. ScribeRig adds crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/plugin_worker.rs with the PluginSemanticDispatcher host route, tool/capability allowlists, cleared worker environment, and AuthorizedPluginWorker; apps/scriberig/src/main.rs serves the worker mode, and provider_config/extensions.rs::reject_in_process_extensions retains fail-closed startup rejection for extension roots, plugin files, and package roots because no production worker/tool-catalog composition exists yet. upstream_execution::build_tools still accepts only the ScribeRig semantic catalog, so plugin tools are not yet model-visible, and no production semantic dispatcher is composed. The fork worker changes are uncommitted and therefore absent from ScribeRig's current pin 46ee871ce7c80d1a81e89de53dbbd2e2e2490de1. The default launcher has no OS filesystem/network sandbox and the worker action bridge is absent. Task 149 §§8 and 12 therefore remain unchecked until a committed/pinned fork revision, host dispatcher/tool-catalog integration, OS sandbox launcher, and plugin-capability fixtures exist. No local extension loader or duplicate package lifecycle was found. Remaining proof is behavioral: §7 catalog/thinking/property/readiness fixtures; §8 agent/semantic-tool/recursive-branch/plugin fixtures; §9 visible PTY golden and interactive smoke; §10 semantic-invariant review/tests; §§11–13 cross-surface, security, and responsiveness validation; §§14–16 supersession review and final gates. None is checked by this source audit.

Controlled fork worker update (2026-10-21): the earlier boundary description above is a historical snapshot and its statements that runtime-action RPC and OS sandbox support were absent are superseded. The fork working tree now has the host runtime-action RPC bridge, an allowlisted host handler, and a fail-closed sandbox launcher contract with a Linux Bubblewrap implementation; macOS/Windows still require an injected platform launcher. The worker also passes cooperative cancellation into plugin execution, cancels active calls on shutdown, waits up to two seconds for cooperative settlement, and joins its reader. The host kills the worker tree at request timeout and after roughly 500 ms during graceful shutdown. Native FFI that ignores cancellation cannot be preempted; worker cancellation is not acknowledged, registration cannot be interrupted, and host capability calls may wait up to 60 seconds. No runtime isolation or cancellation behavior has been verified.

These fork changes remain uncommitted and are absent from ScribeRig's b2fc63c78ae85044eb78e7ac9af184bd7fbfbc95 pin. ScribeRig's current validate_isolated_plugin_configuration still rejects configured plugin roots because workers are not composed into branch tool catalogs. The AuthorizedPluginWorker adapter still uses HostProcessLauncher and the default unisolated worker policy; do not activate it until production host composition injects a sandboxed launcher and policy, scopes semantic capabilities, and exposes worker tools through the upstream agent. Tasks 146 and 149 remain open; the older checklist item above requiring a worker API, runtime-action bridge, and sandbox must be read with this update, not treated as a verified production boundary.

Test-only TUI event cleanup (2026-10-21): production input is dispatched by the upstream component tree, and the local event/keymap modules had no production consumer. Removed event.rs, keymap.rs and its keymap_* helpers/tests, and the keymap-derived test-only overlay::help generator. Removed the test-only TuiState::apply_event adapter and the remaining direct TuiEvent imports. Semantic reducer tests now drive Action values or TuiState::apply_application_event directly, preserving the quit, modal-input, composer-newline, escape-to-conversation, and application-event assertions without a local terminal-input abstraction. This source-only cleanup was not compiled or test-verified in this turn.

At the current pin, rpi-extensions supplies registry/artifact metadata operations, while build/acquisition commands are in rpi-cli; ScribeRig does not expose package install/update/reload controls and rejects configured extension roots. Do not implement the package-refresh fixture as a ScribeRig-only package manager or by calling CLI command handlers. First require an explicit product decision to expose package operations, then upstream reusable lifecycle APIs for authorized project roots and an isolated worker/IPC boundary, plus atomic extension-session/catalog generation replacement. docs.title: 17. Implementation Notes
docs.text:
Record the final upstream versions/SHAs, upstream contributions consumed, deleted local owners, retained semantic adapters, validation commands/results, and any explicit user-approved exceptions.

Production event-boundary cleanup (2026-10-21): the active runtime now reduces ApplicationEvent directly through TuiState::apply_application_event; it no longer wraps semantic application events in the local terminal TuiEvent type. The test-only event, keymap, and overlay::help modules were subsequently deleted with their key/action fixtures; see the test-only TUI event cleanup note above. Upstream rpi-tui owns terminal input dispatch and registered keybindings; ScribeRig retains semantic reducers and the application-event adapter. Earlier cargo check -p scriberig-tui --lib evidence predates this module deletion; the deletion itself and legacy reducer tests remain unexecuted.

Legacy pane/terminal state cleanup (2026-10-21): removed the ScribeRig Focus::{Explorer, Primary, Inspector} state, Tab-driven focus actions, TuiState.terminal_size, and Action::TerminalResized. Cursor bounds and Explorer activation now follow the selected semantic PrimaryView; actual component focus and resize handling remain in rpi-tui. The unreferenced test-only read_event poller was also deleted. cargo check -p scriberig-tui --all-targets and cargo check -p scriberig --bin srig pass; the former only compiles test targets and does not execute tests. PTY focus, resize, and terminal restoration scenarios remain unexecuted.

Overlay/focus/help residual audit (2026-10-21): no safe deletion fits the requested overlay/**, runtime/upstream adapter, and task-149 evidence scope. Production dialog rendering and modal mechanics already use upstream Dialog, Editor, Markdown, and TuiAltScreen overlay/focus APIs in runtime/upstream/modal_overlay.rs; provider/model/thinking/theme and command palette rendering use upstream SelectList / SearchableSelectList in runtime/upstream/selector_factory.rs. Upstream TuiAltScreen owns the actual focus and overlay stack, with restore_overlay_focus only bridging the previous component pointer to upstream hide_overlay / set_focus.

The HelpPanel in runtime/upstream/components/help_panel.rs remains a ScribeRig-specific help document: it enumerates ScribeRig semantic controls and slash commands, while using upstream Markdown rendering, active upstream keybinding metadata, and upstream overlay dispatch. Its content is product intent, so replacing it with generic upstream help would drop ScribeRig commands and semantic navigation guidance. overlay/input.rs similarly retains input purpose, submitted text, and validation error for ScribeRig reducers; the upstream editor handles the actual editing interaction.

Palette ownership cleanup (2026-10-21): removed the local generic filtering and selection state from crates/scriberig-tui/src/overlay/palette.rs; PaletteState now stores only stable PaletteItem rows (ID, label, source) and capability filtering. state_input_reducer.rs no longer edits a local palette query, and state_cursor_reducer.rs no longer moves a local palette cursor. The production popup built by runtime/upstream/selector_factory.rs::open_palette_selector as an upstream SearchableSelectList remains the sole owner of filtering, row navigation, and selected-row state. Upstream selection sends ComposerInput::PaletteSelected with the stable item value, and runtime/upstream/event_loop/input/palette.rs::select invokes state_actions.rs::activate_palette_item by that ID. Command IDs, labels, and action semantics remain ScribeRig-owned in overlay/palette.rs and state_actions.rs; Action::Activated no longer drives palette selection. Unit/reducer tests were rewritten to activate by stable ID instead of simulating local filtering/cursor movement. No upstream palette API was missing, so no fork API or Cargo pin change was made for this slice. No tests or builds were run, so behavioral verification remains outstanding.

docs.title: 18. Full-Gate Run and Production Fixes (2026-10-21)
docs.text:
The user authorized running the plan's full verification gates. The following commands were run with CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 and -j 1 because parallel compilation on this Windows host produced rustc ICEs and LNK1102 memory failures:

cargo fmt --all
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast -j 1

Formatting, workspace check, and workspace clippy pass. The first parallel cargo test attempt failed in rustc/link; the serial retry compiled and ran. A later serial retry still leaves the targets listed below failing.

Production defects fixed while making the suite runnable:

  • apps/scriberig/src/native_tui_agent/upstream_execution/execution.rs never dropped the broker's original sender, so tokio::join! waited forever once the model future returned early. A drop(sender) now closes the tool queue after tools are built.
  • crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/upstream_invocation.rs built rpi_agent::Agent with cancellable_provider_continuation but no stream_fn; the pinned builder requires a stream and returned no default stream fn configured. A bound plain StreamFn now supplies the same provider/model/secret without continuation.
  • Child delegation discarded tool-derived result handles; it now uses compact_result_handles before finalizing the durable BranchResult.
  • Tool evidence projection truncated handles at 32 without preserving next_offset:, breaking manifest pagination. The continuation handle is now retained.
  • Tool evidence now serializes entity, revision, and snapshot as stable strings instead of serde object payloads.
  • Semantic scenarios now provide a bounded pool of context-driven FauxStep::factory responses instead of one one-shot step.
  • Scenario handle parsing accepts both the JSON handles array and the older debug projection; bootstrap manifest/terminal detection accepts JSON summary fields.
  • Failed root execution now persists the underlying safe error text instead of a generic "agent execution failed" label.
  • Plan tests and the shared protocol fixture were updated to exact provider/model assignment identities and current wire fields.

Validation achieved after these fixes:

  • cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked: pass.
  • cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings: pass.
  • cargo test -p scriberig --bin srig: 30/30 pass.
  • cargo test -p scriberig-protocol --lib: 7/7 pass.
  • Plan unit/integration tests, protocol fixture, and bootstrap fixture pass.

Still failing in the full workspace run (not marked complete):

  • The entire PTY family: tui_pty, tui_pty_golden_agent, and the self-hosting PTY tests. Their screenshots start on the Overview/Inspector surface instead of the expected Conversation composer; this is a terminal product acceptance regression, not just fixture drift.
  • scriberig-agent-runtime coordinator worker-context expectations (profile:alpha, round count) and one scheduler case.
  • scriberig-app session/plan thinking-level and failed-child activity expectations.
  • scriberig-server model-selection/agent-session expectations.
  • scriberig-tui library reducer tests (thinking request, prompt visibility, paste sanitation, palette activation, commit effects).

These failures must be resolved by product-behavior fixes or explicitly reconciled fixtures before §9, §11, §12, §15, and §16 can be checked. The migration is not complete and no percentage is claimed.

docs.text:
