Explicit /inspect, explorer activation, history, find, diff, and command paths still request the Overview view. scriberig-tui lib tests remain at 183 passed / 8 failed after this change.
  • Paste handling now escapes terminal control characters before insertion into any composer or input overlay (state.rs::sanitize_paste). This closes the raw-escape paste path.
  • A representative golden PTY run now reaches the Conversation view, but the typed /explorer arrives as /eexxpplloorreerr and stale scenario output is visible. The doubling is consistent with the Windows ConPTY line discipline echoing input because rpi-tui ProcessTerminal::enter_raw_mode ignores a failed crossterm raw-mode request. That is an upstream terminal-lifecycle gap, not a Scriberig shell defect; fixing it requires a reviewed upstream terminal raw-mode/console-mode change, not a local terminal owner.
  • Remaining non-PTY blockers are the same categories listed above: TUI reducer expectations, app/server thinking/selection expectations, and agent-runtime coordinator context/round expectations.

docs.title: 18.2 Round-2/3 status: non-PTY suites now green
docs.text:
The later reconciliation pass updated stale expectations to current upstream semantics and fixed the remaining reducer/runtime defects:

  • TUI reducer expectations now follow upstream validation and selector ownership: unsupported thinking levels are delegated upstream, the prompt and tool-output toggles are driven by stable palette control IDs, confirmed commits require the reviewed candidate snapshot, /model and /thinking are intercepted by the runtime and routed to upstream OpenControl selectors instead of local model-library reads, and /assign prepares the plan target consumed by the upstream selector.
  • Plan assignment now defaults to the model's first advertised thinking level when the caller does not choose one.
  • Initial model selection now chooses an explicitly mapped supported thinking level (or Medium/first supported) instead of leaving thinking empty.
  • Failed child completion now records the durable BranchResult activity, not only the abandoned branch result.
  • Paste input escapes terminal control characters before every composer path.
  • Startup auto-inspection no longer forces Overview; Conversation remains the initial product surface.

Verified after those changes:

cargo test --workspace --exclude scriberig --locked --no-fail-fast -j 1   pass
cargo test -p scriberig --bin srig                                    30/30 pass
cargo test -p scriberig-tui --lib                                    191/191 pass
cargo test -p scriberig-app --test session_runtime                    17/17 pass
cargo test -p scriberig-server --test agent_session                  11/11 pass
cargo test -p scriberig-server --test agent_console_concurrency        1/1 pass
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol --lib                                 7/7 pass
cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime --test coordinator               2/2 pass
cargo test -p scriberig-agent-runtime --test scheduler                 7/7 pass

Workspace check, workspace clippy with -D warnings, formatting, repository lint, web formatting, web typecheck, and the full pnpm --dir web test suite pass. A repeat of cargo test --workspace --exclude scriberig --locked --no-fail-fast after the app/server fixes also passes.

The terminal input duplication was fixed upstream: controlled-fork commit 79673db makes rpi-tui's ProcessTerminal reader ignore ordinary KeyEventKind::Release events, and ebcf8d5 preserves Enter release events so ConPTY submissions are not dropped. ScribeRig now pins ebcf8d5. The footer component is invalidated each render so status changes are not served from a stale frame, and its key hints are truncated when a status row is present so the status is not pushed past the terminal width. The PTY harness now answers split ESC[6n cursor-position queries and sends input byte-by-byte for reliable delivery. Golden PTY 01/02, project-context startup, and resize pass. The remaining PTY failures are stale test expectations for the pre-migration shell labels and explorer workflow (Message [ACTIVE], scriberig ·, Conversation [ACTIVE], root-only explorer rows) plus self-hosting scenario timing; they are test/acceptance modernization work, not model/runtime delegation defects. Instrumentation confirmed ComposerInput::Submit and slash-command dispatch are correct; the PTY harness intermittently delivers a partial command because it writes the whole burst before the upstream reader consumes it. §9 visible product acceptance and the final §15/§16 gates remain open.

docs.title: Migrate Durable Plans to Semantic Entities, Gates, Evidence, Rollups, and Recoverable Failure
docs.text:
Status: [ ] In Progress

Implementation note (2026-10-22): task 150 was authored on a commit chain not present in the active design/adopt-rpi-tui tree. Its governing Level-1 023 and Level-2 033 documents were restored from that same chain alongside this task. Task 148/TUI implementation remains deferred until its upstream-first component path is available in this implementation branch.

Baseline inventory (2026-10-22): scriberig-session/src/planning.rs and its planning/ modules own aggregate Plan, PlanNode, dependency, claim, and plan-history domain behavior. scriberig-session::SessionStore exposes a whole-session save plus plan-local CAS. scriberig-session-sqlite currently encodes complete plans inside the session_records.payload and performs plan CAS by replacing that nested plan in a transaction. scriberig-app owns plan operations and delegates CAS to the session repository. scriberig-agent-runtime owns scheduling/coordinator orchestration. scriberig-protocol, server, client, web, and TUI expose plan projections; none is an authority for canonical plan mutation. Universal immutable revision/snapshot APIs live in scriberig-store and its backends, but plan writes do not currently use them.

Implementation update (2026-10-22): scriberig-session::PlanSemanticSnapshot now encodes Plan, PlanNode, membership, structural, dependency, and mutation metadata as independent universal revisions. SqliteSessionStore stores each plan under a deterministic session/plan root in scriberig-store-sqlite; plan-local CAS promotes that root and reads hydrate the aggregate compatibility projection from the root. Snapshot ancestry reconstructs historical plan states, while separate revision metadata retains safe mutation reasons. Legacy aggregate plans are imported as an ordered snapshot chain on first read. The SQLite session JSON still carries a compatibility projection and branch/session records; it no longer accepts plan mutations when a semantic root exists.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): exact plan snapshot reads now reject snapshots outside the plan root's ancestry and preserve historical membership. Plan-attempt outcomes are independently revisioned semantic objects. Plan semantic promotion and compatibility session/branch projection updates now use one SQLite connection and one transaction, so a failed root CAS rolls back the projection write as well. The regression plan_cas_rolls_back_session_projection_on_semantic_conflict proves rollback; plan_dependencies_and_assignments_survive_reopen proves stale callers still receive a structured revision conflict. Structural cycle validation now runs before semantic promotion. Focused session and SQLite tests pass, including 20 consecutive runs of execution_selection_compare_and_swap_is_atomic after its competing proposals were made to carry consistent history.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): the session store now exposes a compact snapshot-bound PlanView read. SQLite selects plan, node, membership, and structure revisions using revision type metadata and does not load detailed evidence, gate, summary, attempt, or history payloads. A corruption regression proves compact inspection remains available while the full read correctly reports a damaged evidence object. The TypeScript protocol/client now preserve the shared plan/node view fields and call the shared semantic-mutation and retry operations. Focused Rust semantic/SQLite tests and the web client tests pass; pnpm --dir web typecheck passes.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): root promotion now starts with an immediate SQLite transaction so independent connections serialize before reading and promoting the named root. The regression independent_handles_serialize_root_compare_and_swap verifies exactly one writer succeeds and the other receives a structured root conflict. The focused store suite and the plan-related Rust suites pass across session, SQLite, application, agent runtime, protocol, client, and server packages; web client tests and full web typecheck pass.

Remaining implementation gaps: server session projections consume snapshot-validated SQLite rollup rows through the shared application read boundary, with canonical plan evaluation as fallback for missing, stale, or invalid cache data. Plan CAS stages sparse SQLite direct-node and rollup-row updates from their validated prior indexes and advances per-plan snapshot and completeness metadata in the root-promotion transaction. Missing/stale caches use a canonical reference rebuild. Ordinary reads rebuild indexes only after migration or pending claim recovery changes the canonical root. Migration coverage for stale runtime claims and some coordinator fields is incomplete; and web product surfaces do not yet present or invoke every plan operation. Task 148's upstream TUI implementation is still In Progress, so task 150's TUI integration remains deferred under the dependency rule below. These gaps must be resolved or explicitly deferred by the governing design before task 150 can be completed.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): scheduler settlement now sends successful and failed branch results, execution activity, evidence, and terminal Plan state through one plan CAS. SQLite derives newly settled worker branches from the prior and proposed semantic Plan and applies their result projections in the same transaction as root promotion. The application fallback performs the equivalent projection under its session lock. The regression plan_cas_rolls_back_session_projection_on_semantic_conflict injects a root promotion failure after projection work and proves neither the branch result nor terminal node state is visible; plan_settlement_commits_existing_branch_result_with_semantic_state proves both views appear after one successful CAS. Durable retry coverage proves failure outcomes survive reload and a later retry can complete. Focused session, SQLite, application, and runtime suites, Clippy, formatting, and repository lint pass. SQLite still stores the compatibility session and branch projection together, so this does not satisfy the independent disjoint-node storage requirement in Task 8.6.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): scheduler readiness and claiming criteria were re-audited against focused regressions. plan_dependencies_require_results_and_remain_acyclic and contradictory_validation_evidence_fails_entry_gate cover exact dependency results and failed entry gates; incremental_rollup_rejects_a_stale_base_snapshot covers stale derived-index rejection. concurrent_plan_coordinator_claims_have_one_winner proves CAS permits one competing claim, while sibling_workers_execute_concurrently_with_distinct_assignments proves independent ready siblings remain concurrent. The separate mutation-cost criterion remains unverified.

semantic_worker_claim_preserves_unrelated_node_and_relation_revisions verifies a worker claim advances the plan-local mutation revision while preserving the sibling node and membership, structure, and dependency revisions. The test passes in the session semantic-plan suite.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): the browser agent view now includes a reusable plan panel that renders server-projected direct/effective status, blockers, bounded exact-snapshot gates/evidence/attempts, and invokes shared retry, gate-waiver, and evidence-attach client operations. Successful writes reload the authoritative session projection. The panel test, agent-ui tests, and full web build/typecheck pass. The web does not derive rollups locally.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): durable SQLite coverage now opens two independent repository handles, settles disjoint sibling claims from the same base revision, verifies the second writer receives an exact revision conflict, then retries it against the latest projection and verifies both worker results survive. The regression passes. This validates serialized conflict/retry semantics; storage still promotes a shared plan root and rewrites the session compatibility projection, so independent per-node settlement storage remains unimplemented.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): legacy-plan migration equivalence now includes a provider/model assignment, worker branch and exact result, a superseded node and replacement, parent topology, dependency, and root membership. The migrated node projection equals the legacy node sequence, and the focused migration regression passes.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): incremental rollup validation no longer scans all Plan nodes to confirm unchanged membership or resolve an existing parent. It uses the indexed parent map and node-count invariant; propagation still recomputes changed nodes and their ancestor paths only. The session rollup tests, Clippy, and repository lint pass. Sparse staged updates no longer clone the full in-memory rollup, parent, or child maps. A cycle regression proves a rejected update leaves the index and snapshot unchanged.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): SQLite now persists effective status, ignored/abandoned flags, direct-child status counts, unsatisfied completion gate count, evaluator version, and source snapshot in a separate session-owned rollup table. The reference evaluator supplies values; root promotion and compatibility projection update these rows in the same transaction, and the index rebuild helper reconstructs both direct-node and rollup rows. A durable regression compares stored rollups with reference evaluation, checks snapshot refresh, incomplete-cache rejection, and rebuild. SqliteSessionStore exposes a cache read that verifies root snapshot, source snapshots, evaluator version, and row completeness before returning normalized values. Server session projection now requests these rollups through the shared application service and uses them to build plan views. Unavailable or invalid cache data falls back to canonical evaluation at the exact plan snapshot. An application regression compares cache-backed and canonical fallback results. Plan CAS writes only changed rollup values and advances a per-plan snapshot/evaluator/node-count record; it uses full replacement when the cache is absent/stale or plan membership changes. Direct-node index rows are still replaced as a complete set on plan CAS.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): SessionStore now has a default snapshot-bound rollup read, and SQLite overrides it with the validated normalized cache plus canonical fallback. The shared application read operation applies session authorization and resolves each plan at its exact snapshot. Server session responses use these values for direct and effective plan projection. Focused app, server, and SQLite suites, Clippy, formatting, and repository lint pass.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): first-time migration of a legacy plan now imports its current in-flight claim snapshot, then applies the existing stale claim recovery policy before promoting the recovered current snapshot. Historical state retains the original running claim state; the current worker becomes Failed with its branch identity preserved, and the old coordinator claim is released. A durable per-plan pending marker lets a later read finish recovery if the process stops after importing historical snapshots but before the recovered snapshot is promoted. The durable regression legacy_plan_migration_recovers_stale_worker_and_coordinator_claims passes. Claims imported at this boundary are treated as stale because legacy owner labels do not provide a process-liveness identity for safe validation.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): the durable retry regression now includes a dependent node. It verifies a failed attempt leaves the dependency unfulfilled and the later successful attempt binds the edge to its exact result after reload (semantic_retry_keeps_attempt_outcomes_across_reload). It also records the root-selected immutable PlanNode revision through Planned, Ready, Running, Failed, Ready, Running, and Completed, verifying each direct transition selects a distinct revision. The focused SQLite regression passes.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): gate coverage now verifies exact supporting validation evidence satisfies entry readiness, contradictory validation evidence fails the gate, and an explicitly waived gate remains visibly waived. A new completion regression confirms a pending completion gate keeps the plan Running and waiver allows completion. The plan_semantic target passes all 22 tests.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): required decomposition coverage now proves the generated RequiredChildCompleted gate keeps plan completion blocked while the child is unfinished, then permits completion after the child has an accepted result. The focused plan_semantic target passes.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): a scheduler regression forces a node's direct status to stale Ready after adding a pending canonical entry gate and proves the scheduler re-evaluates the gate before dispatch. The focused scheduler test passes. The separate rollup-cache-corruption dispatch scenario remains open because the scheduler currently receives canonical Plan state and does not consume the rollup cache.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): a focused session regression now isolates stale coordinator recovery from worker-claim recovery. After recovery releases the coordinator claim, attempting to dispatch a still-ready node fails without advancing the plan revision. The focused session-structure test passes.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): SQLite session branches now have a normalized per-branch compatibility projection. Legacy aggregate branches seed it once; subsequent reads hydrate branch views from those rows. Plan CAS updates only new or settled branch rows in its existing atomic root-promotion transaction and no longer rewrites session_records.payload. The disjoint settlement regression installs a trigger rejecting any session-payload update, then proves both sibling results survive conflict and retry. The complete scriberig-session-sqlite test target passes.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): incremental rollup conformance now compares the cache against reference evaluation across all direct statuses, failed and running siblings, ignored and other abandoned descendants, completion-gate blocking, and explicit waiver. Existing deep-tree and reparenting regressions cover those structural cases. The plan_semantic test target passes.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): plan lifecycle, assignment, replan, retry, next-step, decomposition, summary, evidence, gate, and waiver mutations are exposed by shared application operations and mapped by the protocol server to those same operations. Rust client methods preserve the typed request and plan response. The reconnect regression mutates a gate through the client, creates a fresh client over the same dispatcher, then verifies an authoritative session read returns the gate and updated node view without event replay. Focused app, server, and client operation coverage passes.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): SessionStore now exposes an exact- snapshot, per-node paged attempt-history read. SQLite filters the snapshot by semantic type and loads PlanAttempt records without decoding node evidence, gates, or full Plan projections. The durable retry regression verifies two pages preserve failed and successful attempt outcomes after reload. The page read is available through the authorized application session boundary, which validates page size. The application regression verifies the read and rejects an unbounded limit. A typed protocol request/response, HTTP route, server dispatcher, and Rust client method now expose the same page. Protocol round-trip, client field-preservation, and HTTP route-decoding tests cover the transport mapping. TypeScript protocol and client types now expose the same page; the web client test verifies exact snapshot/page fields and normalized attempt revisions. Web operation coverage and TUI surfaces remain incomplete.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): bounded exact-snapshot node detail reads now return gate definitions and evidence attached to the node or those gates. The SQLite repository selects only PlanGate and PlanEvidence revisions, decodes those records, and applies stable per-category offset/limit pages; the API caps each page at 256. The application enforces session read authorization. The typed protocol, HTTP route, server dispatch, Rust client, and TypeScript client expose the same DTO without SQL/index fields. Semantic, durable reload, application authorization/page-limit, protocol round-trip, HTTP route decode, Rust client, and web client tests pass; web typecheck passes. The storage read still loads all PlanGate and PlanEvidence revisions in the selected snapshot before filtering and paging by owner. Owner-indexed storage selection remains a performance follow-up rather than a bounded response contract gap.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): SQLite now maintains a session-specific plan_node_index with exact node revision, direct status, structural parent, and source snapshot columns. Plan CAS replaces these derived rows inside the same SQLite transaction as root promotion and compatibility projection writes; legacy semantic migration rebuilds the current index. The public repository helper rebuild_plan_node_index repairs missing rows from canonical semantic state. The sqlite_plan_node_index_tracks_snapshot_and_rebuilds regression checks node status, parent, revision, snapshot refresh after a plan CAS, and recovery after deleting index rows. The full session-sqlite test suite, Clippy, and repository lint pass. This indexes direct node state; effective rollup counters remain unmaterialized.

Implementation update (2026-10-22): focused SQLite recovery coverage exposed that a node's retained latest failure reference was incorrectly copied onto a later successful attempt. Attempt-history projection now associates failure evidence only with the exact branch named by that reference. A persistence regression exercises failure, retry, successful completion, and reload through the semantic snapshot ancestry (cargo test -p scriberig-session-sqlite --test durable semantic_retry_keeps_attempt_outcomes_across_reload). The PlanRetryRequest application operation now reloads exact branch results, validates the expected plan revision, routes through the plan domain retry, and persists with plan CAS. Its focused stale-revision and retained-failure regression passes (cargo test -p scriberig-app --test session_runtime application_retry_is_revision_checked_and_preserves_failure). A session domain regression also proves a failed prerequisite and pending entry gate block retry, exact successful prerequisite evidence plus supporting gate evidence permit retry, and an attached stale worker claim blocks retry (cargo test -p scriberig-session --test plan_recovery retry_requires_satisfied_dependencies_gates_and_no_claim). Retry is also available through a typed protocol request, the HTTP route, and Rust client method. These focused checks pass:

cargo test -p scriberig-protocol --lib references_and_requests_round_trip
cargo test -p scriberig-client --lib plan_client_methods_send_shared_application_requests
cargo test -p scriberig-server --lib typed_plan_retry_route_dispatches_shared_operation

Implementation update (2026-10-22): ordinary next-step insertion is now a separate revision-checked application operation, distinct from replan replacement. It requires a Running plan, creates one structurally anchored node, and commits one plan revision while preserving prior nodes. The typed protocol, HTTP operation, and Rust client expose the same request. Focused checks confirm that the mutation adds exactly one revision, records the ordinary next step added history reason, and leaves a completed earlier node and exact result intact. They pass:

cargo test -p scriberig-app --test session_runtime application_next_step_requires_running_plan_and_current_revision
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol --lib references_and_requests_round_trip
cargo test -p scriberig-client --lib plan_client_methods_send_shared_application_requests
cargo test -p scriberig-server --lib typed_plan_next_step_route_dispatches_shared_operation

Implementation update (2026-10-22): node decomposition is now a revision-checked application operation and typed protocol/client/HTTP route. Required children become structural descendants with RequiredChildCompleted completion gates; decomposition creates no dependency edges. The focused app, protocol, client, and server route checks pass:

cargo test -p scriberig-app --test session_runtime application_decomposition_creates_required_child_gates_once
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol --lib references_and_requests_round_trip
cargo test -p scriberig-client --lib plan_client_methods_send_shared_application_requests
cargo test -p scriberig-server --lib typed_plan_decompose_route_dispatches_shared_operation

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
Migrate durable planning from aggregate session-plan persistence to independently revisioned semantic plan objects while preserving the existing coordinator, scheduler, dependency-result, branch-isolation, and cross-surface behavior.

The finished implementation must provide:

independent Plan semantic entity
independent PlanNode semantic entities
semantic structural relations
independent dependency state
first-class Summary links
first-class evidence associations
first-class typed gates
recoverable Failed nodes and plans
preserved retry/attempt provenance
derived incremental parent/subtree status rollups
legacy aggregate-plan migration/compatibility
shared app/protocol/client/web/TUI projections

Do not introduce PlanNodeWorkState or another parallel lifecycle enum.

Do not replace Scriberig plan semantics with an upstream task-list model.

docs.title: 2. Read Before Editing
docs.text:
• [ ] Read root AGENTS.md.
  • [ ] Read design/AGENTS.md.
  • [ ] Read nearest AGENTS.md for every crate/package touched.
  • [ ] Read Level-1 documents 002, 003, 005, 008, 009, 010, 017, 018, 023.
  • [ ] Read Level-2 documents 010, 011, 013, 016, 023, 024, 032, 033.
  • [ ] Re-read task 135 current completed planning checklist before changing behavior it already verified.
  • [ ] Inspect current crates/scriberig-session/src/planning.rs and its planning submodules.
  • [ ] Inspect current scriberig-session store/repository contracts.
  • [ ] Inspect crates/scriberig-session-sqlite aggregate persistence and tests.
  • [ ] Inspect universal store/revision/snapshot/graph/change APIs before adding any new persistence abstraction.
  • [ ] Inspect scriberig-app plan operations and validation.
  • [ ] Inspect scriberig-agent-runtime coordinator/scheduler plan usage.
  • [ ] Inspect protocol/server/client/web plan DTO/view mapping.
  • [ ] Inspect current branch state of tasks 144–149 before touching TUI code.

docs.title: 3. Active RPI TUI Branch Rule
docs.text:
This task is authored on design/adopt-rpi-tui-plan because that branch contains the intended future terminal ownership model.

Core semantic/storage phases may be implemented independently of whether tasks 144–149 have finished.

However:

Do not implement or preserve plan presentation against the superseded local Ratatui shell merely to finish this task sooner.

TUI-specific work in this task must happen only after the relevant upstream-first component architecture from Level-2 document 032 and task 148 is available in the implementation branch.

If the RPI branch has merged before implementation begins, use the merged design/code as baseline.

If task 148 is still incomplete, leave the TUI integration checklist in this task unchecked and complete the semantic/protocol work first.

docs.title: 4. Checklist Discipline
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this file synchronized with implementation progress.
  • [ ] Tick a criterion only after code plus focused verification exists.
  • [ ] Never bulk-tick unverified criteria.
  • [ ] Revert checked items when later changes invalidate their evidence.
  • [ ] Record final validation commands/results in the implementation report.
  • [ ] Do not mark this task complete while legacy aggregate storage remains an uncontrolled second write authority.

docs.title: 5. Phase 0 — Baseline Inventory and Compatibility Map
Task 0.1 — Record current plan ownership
docs.text:
Identify current owners for:

Plan / PlanNode types
PlanStatus / PlanNodeStatus
PlanRevision history
parent structure
root node list
dependencies
worker claims
coordinator claims
readiness
worker settlement
replan
session persistence
plan CAS
application operations
protocol DTOs
web/TUI views
  • [x] Current owners are documented in implementation notes.
  • [ ] No design path is inferred solely from stale filenames in older tasks.

docs.title: Task 0.2 — Record current persistence boundary
docs.text:
Prove where complete session/plan aggregates are encoded today and which APIs perform plan-local compare-and-swap.

  • [x] Current aggregate write path is identified.
  • [x] Current plan mutation revision/CAS behavior is covered by tests.
  • [x] Restart/reload behavior has focused coverage.

docs.title: Task 0.3 — Audit reusable universal semantic infrastructure
docs.text:
Locate existing APIs for:

EntityId
Revision
TypeId/schema registration
Snapshot resolve/apply/diff
relations/collections
derived indexes/cache
change/migration/promotion
root compare-and-set
provenance
  • [x] Implementation reuses existing architectural owners where possible.
  • [x] No duplicate revision/snapshot/graph store is created for planning.

docs.title: 6. Phase 1 — Define Semantic Plan Object Encoding
Task 1.1 — Define stable object/relation type identities
docs.text:
Add/register semantic types equivalent to:

session.plan
session.plan-node
session.plan-dependency
session.plan-gate

Add session.plan-attempt only if Phase 6 proves existing branch/execution records cannot safely represent attempt history.

  • [x] Type identities are stable and documented.
  • [x] Canonical encoding uses the existing revision identity mechanism.
  • [x] Encoding is deterministic.

docs.title: Task 1.2 — Define Plan revision payload
docs.text:
Represent only plan-local state equivalent to:

session/anchor
goal
PlanStatus
mutation_revision
coordinator/coordinator_cursor
coordinator generation/claim or safe canonical references
plan-level policy/assignment references where applicable

Do not embed node/dependency/history vectors.

  • [x] Plan revision is independently addressable.
  • [x] Plan mutation revision survives round-trip.
  • [x] Coordinator state survives round-trip.
  • [x] Canonical Plan payload contains no complete node graph.

docs.title: Task 1.3 — Define PlanNode revision payload
docs.text:
Represent node-local state equivalent to:

plan reference
title
purpose
PlanNodeStatus
expected result
semantic scope
assignment
current branch/result references
superseded_by
claim generation/current claim
abandon reason
last failure reference when canonical

Do not embed derived rollup data.

  • [x] PlanNode has stable independent EntityId.
  • [x] Status transition creates a new node revision without changing node identity.
  • [x] Derived effective status/counters are absent from revision identity.

docs.title: Task 1.4 — Preserve one lifecycle enum
docs.text:
Keep the existing single plan-node status vocabulary:

Planned
Ready
Running
Completed
Failed
Abandoned
  • [x] No PlanNodeWorkState or equivalent second lifecycle is introduced.
  • [x] Existing public status naming compatibility is preserved or migrated explicitly.

docs.title: 7. Phase 2 — Structural and Dependency Graph Storage
Task 2.1 — Plan membership relation
docs.text:
Represent plan membership with semantic collection/relation state rather than a Plan-owned node vector.

  • [x] Query can list root/all plan nodes without deserializing a full plan payload.
  • [x] Historical snapshot can answer plan membership exactly.

docs.title: Task 2.2 — Structural parent/child relation
docs.text:
Represent decomposition independently from dependency scheduling.

  • [x] Direct parent lookup exists.
  • [x] Direct child lookup exists.
  • [x] Reparenting does not create unnecessary child content revision when relation infrastructure permits it.
  • [x] Structural cycles are rejected if the plan structural model requires a tree.

docs.title: Task 2.3 — Independent dependency state
docs.text:
Represent dependency state as first-class relation/entity state with at least:

prerequisite
dependent
fulfilled_by
result contract/policy as currently supported
  • [x] Dependency cycle detection still passes.
  • [x] Failed prerequisite does not satisfy dependent.
  • [x] Fulfillment references exact accepted result.
  • [x] Removing/superseding dependency preserves history/provenance.

docs.title: Task 2.4 — Root-node view is derived from structure
docs.text:
Stop treating an embedded root_nodes vector as the only canonical source if structure relations can derive roots.

A cached root list is permitted as a projection/index.

  • [x] Root-node order/semantics are deterministic.
  • [x] Root query works after restart from semantic storage.

docs.title: 8. Phase 3 — Plan Graph Read Repository and Views
Task 3.1 — Build exact snapshot-bound plan loader
docs.text:
Add a session/domain read service that assembles a Plan semantic view from:

Plan revision
PlanNode revisions
membership/parent relations
dependencies
gates/evidence/summary refs when requested
derived rollup cache when valid
  • [x] Read requires or resolves an exact snapshot.
  • [x] View exposes exact Plan/PlanNode revision IDs.
  • [x] View does not depend on legacy aggregate JSON after semantic migration.

docs.title: Task 3.2 — Build compact PlanView
docs.text:
Expose at least:

id
exact revision
mutation revision
goal/status
coordinator
root node identities
compact status counts
  • [x] Large plans can be inspected without loading all detailed evidence/history.

docs.title: Task 3.3 — Build PlanNodeView
docs.text:
Expose at least:

id/exact revision
parent/title/purpose
direct status
effective status
contains ignored/abandoned
summary preview/ref
assignment/current branch/result
blockers/dependency summary
gate summary
evidence summary
retry capability
  • [ ] Product surfaces can consume this view without knowing physical storage.

docs.title: 9. Phase 4 — Semantic Mutation Batch and Plan CAS
Task 4.1 — Preserve plan-local mutation revision
docs.text:

docs.title: Task 7.5 — SQLite normalized plan index
docs.text:
If SQLite acceleration is implemented in this task, add session-specific normalized derived rows in the appropriate architectural owner.

Do not add scriberig-session dependencies to generic foundation store crates.

  • [x] Current node status/parent/revision can be indexed without parsing opaque revision bytes in triggers.
  • [x] Index rows identify source snapshot.
  • [x] Index rebuild command/helper exists for tests/recovery.
  • [x] Effective status and direct-child counts are persisted as rebuildable derived rows with evaluator and snapshot identity.
  • [x] Exact-snapshot rollup reads reject stale or incomplete cache rows.
  • [x] Plan CAS writes changed rollup values and advances plan-level cache metadata without rewriting unrelated rows. Verified 2026-10-30 by cargo test --locked --offline -p scriberig-session-sqlite --test durable plan_cas_keeps_unrelated_sqlite_rollup_rows_untouched; SQLite triggers reject unrelated direct-node and rollup row updates/deletes while a leaf failure advances exact cache snapshots and remains equivalent to reference evaluation.

docs.title: Task 7.6 — Optional SQLite triggers
docs.text:
Use triggers only if they simplify and harden transactional ancestor counter maintenance.

  • [ ] Trigger implementation, if used, has equivalence tests against reference rollup.
  • [ ] Trigger SQL is not the only specification of status semantics.
  • [x] Memory/reference backend passes the same conformance without triggers.

If triggers are not used initially:

  • [x] Document why application/session-layer transactional propagation is preferable for the first implementation.

Implementation decision: reference evaluation in scriberig-session remains the only specification of rollup semantics. SQLite stores its results as rebuildable, snapshot- and evaluator-version-bound rows in the session crate's architectural owner. Triggers would duplicate Rust gate/rollup semantics in SQL and complicate cache invalidation. When the exact prior cache is valid and membership is unchanged, Plan CAS stages only affected rollup and adjacency values and persists changed rows with plan-level snapshot metadata. Missing or stale caches and membership changes use a reference rebuild.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): application coverage proves authorized running-plan evolution through both next-step addition and required decomposition. The next-step test preserves completed work and rejects a stale revision; decomposition creates structural children and a completion gate without adding dependency edges. Session semantic and application operation regressions pass.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): a session semantic regression verifies a child summary remains separately addressable and is not mechanically folded into its parent's canonical summary (child_summary_remains_distinct_from_parent_summary). The plan_semantic target passes all 23 tests.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): restart/reconnect criteria are covered by durable reopen, index rebuild, and fresh-client regressions. The SQLite plan reopen test restores plan nodes and fulfilled dependencies; the node-index test rebuilds the derived index; a new Rust client reloads the authoritative gate-mutated PlanView without event replay. Focused app, server, and SQLite tests pass.

Implementation update (2026-10-30): SQLite plan CAS now stages sparse direct node-index writes alongside rollup writes. A plan-level snapshot/count marker tracks index completeness while unchanged node rows retain their prior materialization snapshot. The durable sparse-write regression installs SQLite triggers that reject updates and deletes of an unrelated direct-node or rollup row, then verifies the changed plan, metadata, and reference rollups after CAS. The focused durable test passes.

docs.title: 19. Architecture Drift Rejections
docs.text:
Reject an implementation that does any of the following:

  • [ ] Treats serialized Plan JSON as the new canonical storage after migration.
  • [ ] Stores PlanNode only as a nested field of Plan.
  • [ ] Introduces PlanNodeWorkState or a second lifecycle enum.
  • [ ] Makes parent rollup counters part of PlanNode revision identity.
  • [ ] Requires a full descendant scan every time top-level status is read.
  • [ ] Defines rollup semantics only inside SQLite trigger SQL.
  • [ ] Makes generic foundation store crates depend on scriberig-session plan types.
  • [ ] Copies validation/result payloads into opaque evidence strings instead of referencing exact semantic objects.
  • [ ] Treats gates and dependencies as the same relation.
  • [ ] Treats failed node as permanently terminal.
  • [ ] Deletes failed attempt provenance during retry.
  • [ ] Allows ignored/abandoned work to satisfy dependencies implicitly.
  • [ ] Requires replan merely to append ordinary newly discovered work to a running plan.
  • [ ] Lets TUI/web mutate plan state directly.
  • [ ] Implements new TUI plan widgets against the superseded local Ratatui shell instead of task 148/upstream components.

Every item above must remain unchecked because each describes forbidden behavior.

docs.title: Implement Resolved Projection Style and Style Resolution Contracts
Status
docs.text:
Planned.

All completion items remain unchecked until implemented and verified.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Implement the generic and shared-application foundation from:

  • level-1/024. projection styles personalized representations and materialization policy.md;
  • level-2/034. projection style resolution loss-aware reconciliation and cross-surface contracts.md.

This task establishes exact renderer-consumable resolved styles, domain style-schema/discovery seams, purpose-aware style resolution, provenance, and exact-style fidelity queries.

It does not implement the full Rust/ECMAScript renderers or TUI/web controls. Those belong to tasks 152 and 153.

docs.title: 2. Required Reading Before Editing
docs.text:
Read, in order:

  1. repository AGENTS.md;
  2. nearest AGENTS.md for every crate modified;
  3. design/CONTEXT.md;
  4. Level-1 006, 007, 011, 019, and 024;
  5. Level-2 007, 008, 011, 012, 024, 032, and 034;
  6. current sr-projection source and projection conformance tests;
  7. current application projection/configuration/capability owners before introducing any new public service type.

Do not rely on historical crate names when the current repository has moved an owner. Reuse the current owner and public boundary.

docs.title: 3. Architectural Constraints
docs.text:
Preserve these invariants:

canonical semantic code != source projection bytes

StyleRef = exact identity/provenance boundary
ResolvedStyle = exact renderer-consumable value

domain adapter owns style meaning
shared application layer owns selection/resolution semantics
product surfaces do not own formatting rules

InteractiveView resolution != SharedMaterialization resolution

style change alone != semantic source migration

Do not:

  • make sr-projection know TypeScript/Rust style properties;
  • let renderers read ambient user settings;
  • create a TUI-only style store/resolver;
  • use terminal theme types as source projection styles;
  • make filesystem/project source bytes canonical;
  • bypass candidate/migration/change semantics for project configuration that is canonical knowledge.

docs.title: 4. Audit the Existing Style Path
docs.text:
Before changing public types, document in the task implementation/commit notes the current owners for:

StyleRef / StyleValue
ProjectionSpec
RenderRequest
RenderCacheKey
RenderedProjection
ProjectionAdapter
ReconciliationContext
projection application operations
configuration/user preference persistence
protocol/client projection models

Confirm whether scriberig-projection is only a compatibility/re-export layer and edit the true owner rather than duplicating types.

docs.title: 5. Add an Exact ResolvedStyle Contract
docs.text:
Add a generic domain-neutral type equivalent in responsibility to:

ResolvedStyle {
    reference: StyleRef,
    value: StyleValue,
    schema: Option<StyleSchemaRef>,
}

Exact names/field arrangement may change to fit the existing public API.

Requirements:

  • preserves exact StyleRef provenance;
  • carries exact canonical adapter-owned style bytes;
  • can identify the schema/version when required for validation;
  • is immutable after construction;
  • participates in equality/hash/cache identity as required;
  • supports deterministic construction for inline style values;
  • does not depend on any domain crate;
  • does not contain mutable application/user-setting handles.

If resolving a revision reference requires storage/application access, perform that resolution before the domain renderer is invoked.

Do not give projection renderers hidden store access merely to resolve style preferences.

docs.title: 6. Refine Render Identity
docs.text:
Update the render contract so the exact canonical resolved style consumed by a renderer is part of the declared render input.

A compatibility transition is acceptable, but the resulting API must make it impossible for a migrated renderer to receive a StyleRef::Revision while lacking the exact value it is supposed to apply.

Ensure render/cache identity changes when the canonical resolved style value changes.

Detect inconsistent reference/value pairs where the current storage/identity model makes such validation possible.

Keep renderer version and rendering context separate from style.

docs.title: 7. Add Domain Style-Schema Seams
docs.text:
Add or refine a narrow extension seam through which a domain projection adapter can describe and validate style.

It must support responsibility equivalent to:

schema for projection kind
normalize style input
merge style values according to domain rules
provide exact defaults
classify fidelity for exact resolved style/purpose

Do not require one universal schema property enum across all domains.

Generic schema descriptors may include stable keys/value kinds/allowed values/defaults/documentation/purpose applicability, but domain code remains authoritative for validation and interpretation.

Use structured diagnostics for invalid/unsupported properties.

docs.title: 8. Add Projection Purpose and Fidelity
docs.text:
Introduce shared domain-neutral types equivalent to:

ProjectionPurpose
  InteractiveView
  SharedMaterialization
  ExplicitExport

ProjectionFidelity
  LosslessEditable
  LossAwareEditable
  ReadOnlyLossy

Names may vary, but callers must be able to distinguish these cases without inferring them from style bytes.

Fidelity is evaluated for the exact resolved style/projection/purpose, not only for the projection kind.

Do not make Editable on a generic projection specification override an adapter's determination that one resolved style is too lossy to edit safely.

docs.title: 9. Implement Shared Purpose-Aware Resolution
docs.text:
Place style selection/resolution in the current shared application/configuration owner after inspecting existing code.

Implement deterministic source resolution equivalent to:

docs.title: Interactive view
docs.text:
DomainDefault
< RepositoryConvention / ProjectPolicy
< UserPreference
< ViewOverride

docs.title: Shared materialization
docs.text:
DomainDefault
< RepositoryConvention / ProjectPolicy
< WorkspaceMaterializationPolicy

UserPreference must not enter shared materialization by default.

docs.title: Explicit export
docs.text:
Require explicit selection of any personal/view override used for the export; do not borrow it from ambient UI state invisibly.

Use domain-defined merge/normalization rather than generic last-write-wins JSON merging.

docs.title: 10. Preserve Style Provenance
docs.text:
Return enough provenance from resolution to explain effective choices.

At minimum preserve ordered exact source identities/revisions/values used to derive the result.

Per-property winning-source provenance may be added if it fits cleanly and deterministically.

Do not include secrets or unrelated user configuration.

Provenance is inspectable derived/configuration evidence, not semantic source-code content.

docs.title: 11. Add Shared Application Operations
docs.text:
Extend current application capability/operation owners with operations equivalent in responsibility to:

query style schema
query available profiles
query effective style + provenance
query exact fidelity/editability
set/clear user preference
set/clear view override
set materialization policy

Follow existing operation/capability naming and result conventions rather than introducing a parallel API family solely because the Level-2 document uses conceptual names.

Ensure local embedded callers can use the same semantics later exposed remotely.

A view override is presentation/user configuration and must not create a source-code migration.

docs.title: 12. Repository Convention Boundary
docs.text:
This task only establishes a pluggable source/provenance boundary for repository/project conventions.

Do not attempt to fully implement every .editorconfig, rustfmt, Prettier, or Biome option in this task.

If an existing configuration reader already owns relevant behavior, adapt it into the shared resolver rather than duplicating parsing.

Use deterministic fixtures for at least one synthetic repository-convention source so precedence can be tested.

docs.title: 13. Compatibility Strategy
docs.text:
Migrate incrementally.

Existing adapters that do not yet expose a style schema may resolve to one fixed canonical default style and conservative fidelity.

Do not break unrelated Markdown/filesystem projection workflows merely to force all adapters to implement rich style discovery immediately.

Task 152 will migrate Rust and ECMAScript source rendering to the new contract.

docs.title: 14. Tests
docs.text: Add tests at the lowest layer that owns each behavior.

docs.title: Generic projection tests
docs.text:
Prove:

  • resolved style retains reference and exact value;
  • different canonical style values produce different render/cache identity;
  • deterministic repeated style resolution produces equal exact values;
  • projection fidelity variants remain distinguishable;
  • no domain-specific property names leak into generic projection tests/types.

docs.title: Application resolution tests
docs.text:
Prove:

  • interactive view includes user preference;
  • shared materialization excludes user preference;
  • explicit view override wins only in the intended view scope;
  • two users may resolve different interactive styles for the same semantic scope;
  • those users resolve the same shared materialization style under one workspace policy;
  • invalid domain merge produces a structured diagnostic;
  • effective provenance identifies applied sources.

docs.title: Regression test
docs.text: Add a test demonstrating that changing a user preference does not create or request a semantic source-code migration.

docs.title: 15. Validation
docs.text:
Run the narrowest relevant tests during implementation, then at minimum:

cargo fmt --all
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
python3 tools/lint_repo.py

If web/protocol TypeScript is touched in this task, also run the repository-prescribed web format/typecheck/test commands for affected packages.

Record any validation that cannot run and why; do not mark its checklist item complete.

docs.title: Core exact-style contract
docs.text:
• [ ] ResolvedStyle or an equivalent exact generic type exists in the current projection owner.
  • [ ] The type preserves exact style reference/provenance and exact canonical adapter-owned value.
  • [ ] Migrated render contracts receive exact renderer-consumable style data without hidden storage/global lookup.
  • [ ] Exact resolved style participates correctly in render/cache identity.
  • [ ] Generic projection code contains no Rust/TypeScript/Markdown style-property semantics.

docs.title: Style schema and fidelity
docs.text:
• [ ] A domain extension seam exists for schema/default/normalize/merge/fidelity behavior.
  • [ ] Generic schema discovery supports structured client presentation without becoming the formatter.
  • [ ] Projection purpose distinguishes interactive view, shared materialization, and explicit export.
  • [ ] Fidelity distinguishes lossless editable, loss-aware editable, and read-only lossy behavior or equivalent states.
  • [ ] Fidelity is evaluated after exact style resolution.

docs.title: Shared resolution
docs.text:
• [ ] Interactive resolution supports domain/project/user/view precedence.
  • [ ] Shared materialization excludes personal user preference by default.
  • [ ] Explicit export does not borrow ambient personal style invisibly.
  • [ ] Domain-defined merging/normalization is used.
  • [ ] Effective style provenance is inspectable.

docs.title: Application integration
docs.text:
• [ ] Existing shared application owners expose effective style/schema/fidelity semantics.
  • [ ] User/view style changes do not create semantic source migrations.
  • [ ] No TUI-only/web-only resolver or formatter semantics were added.
  • [ ] Compatibility behavior exists for adapters not yet migrated.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• [ ] Generic projection tests pass.
  • [ ] Application style-resolution tests pass.
  • [ ] User-preference/materialization isolation regression test passes.
  • [ ] cargo fmt --all passes.
  • [ ] cargo check --workspace --all-targets passes.
  • [ ] cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings passes.
  • [ ] python3 tools/lint_repo.py passes.

docs.title: 17. Handoff to Task 152
docs.text: At completion, task 152 must be able to ask the shared/domain style layer for an exact validated ResolvedStyle and render the same semantic source under at least two different exact styles without changing semantic identity.

docs.title: Implement Style-Aware Rust and ECMAScript Source Projection Rendering
Status
docs.text:
Planned.

All completion items remain unchecked until implemented and verified.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Prove the projection-style architecture in real source-code domains by making Rust and ECMAScript/TypeScript rendering consume exact resolved style inputs.

This task depends on task 151.

The required architectural sources are:

  • level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md;
  • level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md;
  • level-1/024. projection styles personalized representations and materialization policy.md;
  • level-2/007. projection crate boundaries and core model.md;
  • level-2/034. projection style resolution loss-aware reconciliation and cross-surface contracts.md.

The task establishes source rendering and style fidelity. Full loss-aware reverse editing and product controls belong to task 153.

docs.title: 2. Required Reading Before Editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. repository AGENTS.md;
  2. nearest AGENTS.md for each domain/projection crate modified;
  3. design/CONTEXT.md;
  4. task 151 and its implemented code/current completion status;
  5. current Rust domain parser/syntax/render code and tests;
  6. current ECMAScript domain parser/AST model and tests;
  7. current projection adapter registration/application path;
  8. current dependency/license policy before adding any formatting/codegen dependency.

Do not assume filenames from this task still identify the implementation owner if task 151 or concurrent work has moved them.

docs.title: 3. Architectural Constraints
docs.text:
Preserve:

semantic source model
  + exact resolved domain style
  -> deterministic source projection

Do not:

  • make rendered source text canonical state;
  • put Rust/ECMAScript properties into sr-projection;
  • read ambient formatter configuration from the renderer;
  • interpret a style-only byte difference as a semantic program change;
  • make the TUI/web own source formatting;
  • use raw file editing as the normal semantic source mutation path.

The renderer may delegate formatting/code generation to a suitable library, but the Scriberig domain adapter remains responsible for exact input declaration, semantic safety, style normalization, and fidelity classification.

docs.title: 4. Rust: Establish a Domain Style Schema
docs.text:
Add a Rust source-projection style type/schema in the Rust domain owner.

The first required property is indentation.

Support at least an exact normalized distinction equivalent to:

spaces(width = 2)
spaces(width = 4)

The schema may also include line width or another already-supported representational property if doing so is small and naturally supported, but do not inflate this task by implementing a complete rustfmt configuration model.

Requirements:

  • deterministic canonical encoding into the style value used by task 151;
  • structured validation for invalid widths/values;
  • documented defaults;
  • purpose applicability compatible with shared style resolution;
  • fidelity classification for the styles actually supported.

docs.title: 5. Rust: Remove Hard-Coded Indentation
docs.text:
The current renderer emits a literal four-space prefix for function-body statements.

Replace hard-coded indentation with the exact resolved Rust style.

The renderer must accept the resolved style through the projection/domain render path rather than by reading a process-global/user-global setting.

Preserve deterministic behavior for the default style so existing tests/fixtures change only where intentionally required.

Add tests proving:

same RustFile + 2-space style -> bytes A
same RustFile + 4-space style -> bytes B
A != B
semantic RustFile unchanged

Also prove repeated rendering under one exact style is byte-identical.

docs.title: 6. Rust: Do Not Confuse Attributes, Docs, and Comments
docs.text:
Before adding any Rust comment-visibility control, audit how the current Rust semantic/syntax model represents:

ordinary comments
doc comments
attributes/tool directives
raw token-preserved items

If the current semantic model cannot reliably distinguish safely hideable comments from behavior/documentation-affecting forms, do not implement a generic strip_comments switch.

Instead:

  • document the unsupported capability through the style schema/fidelity result;
  • preserve all currently representable content;
  • leave comment-hiding support for a model that can classify it safely.

Task success does not require lossy Rust comment projection if the semantic model is not ready.

docs.title: 7. ECMAScript: Audit Rendering Options Before Selecting an Engine
docs.text:
The existing ECMAScript domain uses Oxc for parsing JavaScript/TypeScript/JSX/TSX.

Before adding a dependency or custom printer, evaluate the current viable code-generation/formatting options against:

JS/TS/JSX/TSX syntax coverage
integration as a Rust/library dependency
explicit configuration control
deterministic output
comment and directive preservation
source range/source-map support
ability to avoid undeclared ambient config
round-trip/parser compatibility
license compatibility
maintenance cost

Prefer reusing an established renderer/formatter over implementing a large handwritten JavaScript pretty-printer.

If current Oxc crates provide a suitable code generator/formatter at the pinned ecosystem version, prefer the smallest coherent Oxc-based path unless evidence favors another existing dependency.

Record the chosen engine and why in code/module documentation or the task/commit notes.

docs.title: 8. ECMAScript: Add Source Projection Rendering
docs.text:
Add a domain-owned rendering path for JavaScript/TypeScript/JSX/TSX semantic/syntax structures supported by the current adapter.

It must consume the exact resolved ECMAScript style from task 151.

At minimum support one visible style dimension with two exact variants, preferably indentation width if the chosen engine exposes it deterministically.

Where the chosen engine supports them safely and cheaply, additional properties may include:

line width
quote preference
semicolon preference
trailing comma preference

Do not promise a style property through discovery unless the renderer actually honors it for the supported syntax set.

docs.title: 9. ECMAScript Comment and Directive Classification
docs.text:
Audit how Oxc/current AST data exposes comments/trivia/directives.

Create a domain-level classification boundary capable of distinguishing, where supported:

ordinary comments
documentation/JSDoc
license/header comments
TypeScript compiler/type-check directives
lint directives
formatter directives
source-map/tooling directives

Do not assume all comment-syntax content is safely hideable.

A first implementation may expose only:

PreserveAll
HideOrdinaryCommentsInView

if and only if the adapter can prove that the second option preserves mandatory/directive categories.

If that proof is not practical in this task, keep comments preserved and expose the limitation explicitly. Do not implement unsafe stripping to satisfy a checkbox.

docs.title: 10. Fidelity Classification
docs.text:
For each implemented Rust/ECMAScript style, return the exact fidelity state defined by task 151.

Examples:

indentation-only style
  -> LosslessEditable, assuming existing parse/reconcile capabilities support it

hide ordinary comments
  -> LossAwareEditable only after task 153 implements and proves loss-aware reconciliation
  -> otherwise ReadOnlyLossy

Task 152 must not claim loss-aware editability merely because rendering can omit content.

A lossy renderer may land before loss-aware editing as long as the projection is conservatively read-only.

docs.title: 11. Repository Convention Mapping
docs.text:
Add only narrowly justified mappings required to prove the style-resolution path.

For example, if .editorconfig support already exists or is small and owned in a suitable configuration/domain layer, map indentation settings into the Rust/ECMAScript domain style input.

Do not implement full Prettier/Biome/rustfmt configuration parsing in this task unless an existing library/current owner already provides it with little duplication.

The important proof is:

external/project convention
  -> typed style source
  -> task-151 resolver
  -> exact resolved domain style
  -> renderer output

not exhaustive ecosystem compatibility.

docs.title: 12. Adapter and Projection Integration
docs.text:
Ensure normal application projection rendering can reach the new domain renderers through the existing adapter/registry path.

Do not leave the style-aware renderer as an isolated helper tested only directly.

A render request through the public/shared projection boundary must:

  1. resolve/receive an exact style;
  2. dispatch to the correct domain renderer;
  3. return RenderedProjection or current equivalent with exact style/renderer metadata;
  4. produce cache identity that differs for different exact styles;
  5. preserve semantic scope/snapshot identity.

docs.title: Rust
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  • default style reproduces expected deterministic source;
  • 2-space and 4-space styles produce expected distinct bytes;
  • repeated render is deterministic;
  • invalid style input returns structured diagnostics;
  • style-only difference does not alter semantic source identity/state.

docs.title: ECMAScript
docs.text:
Add tests for at least JavaScript and TypeScript, and JSX/TSX when the renderer claims those kinds:

  • parse supported source into the current semantic/syntax model;
  • render deterministically;
  • render the same semantic structure with two styles into different expected bytes;
  • parse rendered output successfully;
  • preserve behavior-significant directives/comments supported by the adapter;
  • invalid/unsupported style input produces structured diagnostics.

docs.title: Projection integration
docs.text:
Add tests proving:

  • public render path carries exact style metadata;
  • render/cache keys differ by style;
  • same semantic snapshot is reused across style variants;
  • unsupported lossy editing is classified read-only.

docs.title: 14. Dependency and Licensing Discipline
docs.text:
If adding a new formatter/codegen crate or external library:

  • follow the repository licensing design and notices process;
  • verify license compatibility;
  • prefer maintained library APIs over subprocess-only integration when practical;
  • keep the dependency in the domain layer rather than generic projection/application/TUI layers;
  • avoid a dependency that implicitly reads the filesystem/global config during deterministic rendering unless that behavior can be disabled and exact inputs supplied.

Do not vendor a large formatter into Scriberig merely to avoid declaring a normal compatible dependency.

docs.title: 15. Validation
docs.text:
Run targeted domain tests first, then at minimum:

cargo fmt --all
cargo test -p <affected projection/domain crates>
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
python3 tools/lint_repo.py

Also run relevant projection/application integration tests from task 151.

If a formatter dependency has dedicated conformance fixtures, include deterministic fixtures in the repository rather than relying on network access.

docs.title: Rust
docs.text:
• [ ] Rust owns a domain style schema/value with deterministic canonical encoding.
  • [ ] Rust renderer consumes exact resolved style.
  • [ ] Hard-coded four-space statement indentation is removed from the normal style-aware path.
  • [ ] Two-space and four-space render tests produce distinct expected bytes from one semantic source.
  • [ ] Repeated Rust rendering is deterministic.
  • [ ] Invalid Rust style input produces structured diagnostics.
  • [ ] Unsafe generic comment stripping was not introduced.

docs.title: ECMAScript
docs.text:
• [ ] Rendering/codegen options were audited against the criteria in this task.
  • [ ] The selected implementation and ownership boundary are documented.
  • [ ] JavaScript/TypeScript source rendering exists through the domain projection path.
  • [ ] Claimed JSX/TSX support has tests, or unsupported kinds are diagnosed explicitly.
  • [ ] At least one exact style dimension produces two deterministic renderings from one semantic structure.
  • [ ] Rendered output reparses successfully for supported kinds.
  • [ ] Comment/directive preservation/classification is conservative and tested.
  • [ ] Any lossy style is read-only until task 153 proves loss-aware editing.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
• [ ] Shared projection rendering reaches the style-aware domain renderers.
  • [ ] RenderedProjection/current equivalent records the exact style used.
  • [ ] Render/cache identity differs across exact style variants.
  • [ ] Style-only rendering does not create semantic source migrations.
  • [ ] Repository-convention mapping, if added, goes through the shared resolver rather than renderer globals.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• [ ] Targeted Rust domain tests pass.
  • [ ] Targeted ECMAScript domain tests pass.
  • [ ] Projection integration tests pass.
  • [ ] cargo fmt --all passes.
  • [ ] cargo check --workspace --all-targets passes.
  • [ ] cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings passes.
  • [ ] python3 tools/lint_repo.py passes.

docs.title: 17. Handoff to Task 153
docs.text: At completion, task 153 must have at least one style-capable code projection whose lossless editing remains valid and, if a safely classified lossy style exists, a conservative ReadOnlyLossy baseline that can be upgraded only after exact loss-aware reconciliation is implemented and tested.

docs.title: Implement Loss-Aware Reconciliation and Shared Projection Style Controls
Status
docs.text:
Planned.

All completion items remain unchecked until implemented and verified.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Complete the projection-style vertical slice by:

  1. binding editable projections to an exact typed reconciliation baseline;
  2. preserving canonical content intentionally omitted by a lossy style;
  3. exposing style schema/effective style/fidelity through shared application/protocol/client contracts;
  4. integrating source-style selection into the current RPI-based TUI and reusable web surfaces without creating product-local formatting semantics.

This task depends on tasks 151 and 152.

It is constrained by:

  • level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md;
  • level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md;
  • level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md;
  • level-1/019. semantic agent operations and projection-first editing.md;
  • level-1/024. projection styles personalized representations and materialization policy.md;
  • level-2/008. filesystem projection synchronization.md;
  • level-2/024. agent operations protocol and cross surface product contract.md;
  • level-2/032. upstream first agent runtime and terminal product ownership correction.md;
  • level-2/034. projection style resolution loss-aware reconciliation and cross-surface contracts.md.

docs.title: 2. Required Reading Before Editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. repository AGENTS.md;
  2. nearest AGENTS.md for every affected projection/application/protocol/TUI/web crate/package;
  3. design/CONTEXT.md;
  4. the design documents listed above;
  5. completion state and implementation from tasks 151 and 152;
  6. current ReconciliationContext, projection synchronization state, observation/import pipeline, and conflict types;
  7. current application operation/capability patterns;
  8. current RPI TUI migration state, especially Level-2 032 and the latest applicable Level-3 TUI task;
  9. reusable web protocol/client/model/react package boundaries.

The TUI branch is active work. Do not restore a superseded local Ratatui/TUI ownership model because older files or task 031 still exist.

docs.title: 3. Architectural Constraints
docs.text:
Preserve these rules:

lossy projection absence != semantic deletion

editable reconciliation
  = exact baseline semantic state
  + exact baseline representation
  + exact baseline style
  + current canonical state
  + edited representation

if loss-aware reconciliation is not proven
  -> lossy projection is read-only

TUI/web controls
  -> shared application intent
  -> shared style resolver
  -> exact projection render/reconcile

Do not:

  • hide baseline/style identity in an untyped metadata bag when correctness depends on it;
  • infer deletion of style-hidden entities from parser absence;
  • let a new user preference reinterpret an edit created under an old style;
  • create a TUI-specific source-style persistence/resolution system;
  • create a parallel web source-style semantics layer;
  • use rpi-tui theme/style objects as canonical source projection styles;
  • let UI edits bypass candidate/migration/validation/conflict/promotion semantics.

docs.title: 4. Introduce a Typed Exact Reconciliation Baseline
docs.text:
Refine the current reconciliation boundary with a typed baseline equivalent in responsibility to:

ReconciliationBaseline
  base semantic state/snapshot
  semantic scope
  projection specification
  exact resolved style
  renderer version
  adapter version
  exact rendered output reference/hash
  exact projection fidelity
  optional adapter mapping/loss evidence

Update ReconciliationContext or its current replacement to contain this baseline plus current canonical state and any truly auxiliary metadata.

Do not duplicate base/scope/specification fields indefinitely after callers are migrated unless compatibility requires a temporary transition.

The type must make it difficult to accidentally reconcile edited bytes without knowing the style/renderer/output that produced the edit baseline.

docs.title: 5. Retain Exact Baseline Output
docs.text:
For editable managed projections, synchronization state must identify an exact retrievable baseline representation, not only a hash when reconciliation needs content.

Prefer content-addressed projection artifact storage or an existing immutable blob/content facility if one already fits.

Requirements:

  • exact bytes can be retrieved for the baseline after canonical state advances;
  • baseline identity remains valid after user style preferences change;
  • baseline identity remains valid after materialization policy changes;
  • the stored reference is bound to style/renderer/adapter/base-state metadata;
  • hashes remain available for dirty/self-write detection;
  • old baseline content is retained according to existing reachability/GC policy rather than an ad-hoc permanent leak.

Do not make baseline bytes canonical semantic source knowledge merely because they are retained for synchronization evidence.

docs.title: 6. Add Optional Projection Mapping/Loss Evidence
docs.text:
Allow domain renderers/adapters to attach exact output-bound derived evidence where needed.

Examples:

rendered token/range -> semantic entity/revision
hidden semantic entity/category set
structural anchors used for reconciliation
adapter-specific source-map data

This evidence must be bound to the exact baseline state/style/renderer/output.

Use semantic handles for durable identity. Do not persist TUI rows, editor line numbers, parser pointers, or other unstable presentation identities as canonical mapping keys.

An adapter that does not need mapping metadata may omit it.

docs.title: 7. Implement Loss-Aware Reconciliation for One Proven Safe Style
docs.text:
Choose the narrowest domain/style combination from task 152 that can safely demonstrate loss-aware editing.

A preferred example is an ECMAScript/TypeScript style that hides only ordinary comments while preserving all compiler/tooling/license/directive categories the domain model can reliably identify.

If task 152 determined that no current domain model can distinguish safely hideable content, do not force a lossy editable implementation. In that case:

  • keep all lossy styles read-only;
  • implement the typed baseline/fidelity infrastructure;
  • add tests proving read-only enforcement;
  • leave the loss-aware-editable checklist items unchecked and record the blocking semantic-model gap.

Never implement unsafe comment stripping merely to complete this task.

docs.title: 8. Required Loss-Aware Behavior
docs.text:
For a safely supported lossy style, prove this scenario:

canonical base B
  ordinary comment C
  statement S = foo()

baseline style H
  hides C

baseline rendered bytes
  foo()

user edits visible representation
  bar()

current canonical state D
  still contains C

reconciliation result
  preserves C
  proposes semantic change S: foo() -> bar()

The adapter must identify that C was absent because the baseline style omitted it, not because the user deleted it.

Also distinguish a represented element that was visible in baseline output and is actually removed by the user.

When evidence is insufficient, return ambiguity/conflict rather than inventing lineage or deletion.

docs.title: 9. Preserve Three-Way Reconciliation
docs.text:
Loss-aware handling does not replace the existing three-way model.

Reconciliation still reasons over:

B = last synchronized semantic baseline
D = current canonical state
F = current edited external/view representation

with additional exact evidence:

B_rendered
B_style
B_renderer
B_mapping/loss metadata

Concurrent canonical changes between B and D must still participate in ordinary merge/conflict logic.

Do not special-case lossy styles by overwriting current canonical state with a candidate parsed from F.

docs.title: 10. Style Changes During an Active Edit
docs.text:
An active edit remains bound to its baseline style.

Implement safe behavior equivalent to one of:

reconcile under old baseline -> rerender new style

or a typed explicit rebase operation if the current editor/application architecture supports it safely.

Do not silently switch the baseline style while dirty edits exist.

For managed filesystem materialization, a deliberate materialization-style change must:

  1. render from canonical semantic state with the new resolved style;
  2. atomically write using the normal projection sync path;
  3. record exact new output/style/renderer metadata;
  4. establish a new synchronization baseline only after successful write.

Personal user preference changes must not trigger this shared-file path.

docs.title: 11. Expose Shared Protocol/Client Models
docs.text:
Where remote/web/TUI-remote behavior requires transport, extend the existing protocol/client models with the minimum shared data for:

style schema descriptors
style/profile identifiers
projection purpose
current effective style summary/provenance
projection fidelity/editability
style diagnostics
style selection/update intent

Follow existing request/result/event/versioning conventions.

Do not expose raw internal trait objects or arbitrary unvalidated style bytes to UI code when a structured descriptor/reference suffices.

Ensure embedded/local and remote paths produce equivalent semantic results.

docs.title: 12. TUI Integration Must Follow the Current RPI Target
docs.text:
Level-2 032 supersedes the old final ownership target from Level-2 031.

Implement the Scriberig-specific source-style UI as a custom semantic component/adapter on the current upstream rpi-tui component/runtime architecture.

Conceptual flow:

upstream rpi-tui setting/select/overlay primitives
  -> Scriberig source projection style intent
  -> shared application operation
  -> style resolver
  -> exact render/fidelity result
  -> Scriberig projection/source component renders result

Upstream remains owner of:

terminal lifecycle
input normalization
focus
overlays
selection/settings widgets
theme/colors/layout primitives
scrolling/editor primitives

Scriberig remains owner of:

which semantic scope is projected
which source style/profile is selected for that user/view
purpose-aware resolution
projection fidelity
semantic edit/reconciliation behavior
materialization policy

Do not add a new Ratatui shell, independent key/event framework, independent theme system, or local TypeScript/Rust formatter settings engine.

If generic settings UI is missing upstream, follow the upstream-first rule from Level-2 032.

docs.title: 13. Keep Terminal Theme and Source Style Distinct in UX/State
docs.text:
The UI must not conflate:

Terminal theme
  dark/light/colors/emphasis/chrome

with:

Source projection style
  indentation/wrapping/comment visibility/etc.

Changing the terminal theme must not alter rendered source bytes or projection cache identity.

Changing source projection style may alter source projection bytes/cache identity but must not change terminal theme state.

Add a regression test at the shared/TUI presentation boundary proving this independence.

docs.title: 14. TUI Personal View Behavior
docs.text:
Provide a way, using current product interaction conventions, to:

inspect effective source style
inspect provenance when practical
choose a user profile/preference
apply/clear a temporary view override
see whether the resulting projection is editable/read-only

Exact slash commands, overlays, palette actions, or settings placement must follow the current RPI product design at implementation time. Do not freeze obsolete task-031 UI shapes into this task.

Changing these personal view settings must not:

  • move reply/navigation/coordinator cursors;
  • alter branch/session topology;
  • rerun model invocations;
  • change plan scheduling;
  • rewrite shared files;
  • create semantic source migrations.

docs.title: 15. Web Reusable Package Integration
docs.text:
Expose the same semantics through existing reusable web layers.

Follow the current direction:

protocol -> client -> model -> react/editor/components -> app

Add reusable model/hooks/components only at the layer that owns them.

A third-party web client should be able to:

query style schema/effective style/fidelity
select a user/view style
request/render a projection
know whether editing is allowed

without importing web/apps/scriberig.

Opinionated MUI controls may wrap reusable semantics in the integrated app/library, but MUI must not own precedence or language-style meaning.

docs.title: 16. Shared Materialization Isolation
docs.text:
Add an end-to-end/application-level scenario with two users:

User A view style -> 2 spaces
User B view style -> 4 spaces
Workspace materialization policy -> repository style

Prove:

  • A and B receive different personal source projections when requested;
  • the same semantic snapshot underlies both;
