  • the managed shared file materializes identically regardless of which user is viewing;
  • changing A's personal preference does not dirty/rewrite the managed file;
  • changing the workspace materialization policy deliberately rerenders and establishes a new exact synchronization baseline.

docs.title: 17. Local/Remote Cross-Surface Conformance
docs.text:
Create deterministic fixtures covering at least:

schema
style sources
resolved effective style
provenance
fidelity
semantic scope/snapshot

Replay equivalent requests through local application access and remote client/protocol paths.

TUI and web should observe equal semantic effective-style/fidelity results even though their visual controls differ.

Do not compare terminal glyphs to browser pixels.

docs.title: 18. Agent and Model Context Safety
docs.text:
If any current agent inspection/context path includes rendered source projections, ensure it can carry exact projection identity/style metadata where required for reproducibility.

A personal UI style change must not mutate historical effective model requests.

If a new invocation intentionally includes a differently styled source projection, the resulting effective context is different and should participate in the normal context fingerprint/continuation validity logic.

Do not add style preferences to provider requests when no rendered styled projection or other execution-semantic input depends on them.

docs.title: Baseline/reconciliation tests
docs.text:
Prove:

  • exact baseline style/renderer/output survives later preference changes;
  • baseline bytes can be retrieved when required;
  • style-hidden canonical content is preserved during a supported lossy edit;
  • visible baseline content removed by the user is distinguishable from hidden content;
  • concurrent canonical changes retain correct conflict behavior;
  • unsupported lossy style cannot enter edit mode;
  • changing style while dirty does not silently reinterpret the old edit.

docs.title: Filesystem tests
docs.text:
Prove:

  • materialization style change creates a new baseline only after successful write;
  • personal preference change does not rewrite a managed shared file;
  • self-write/dirty detection still uses exact output hash correctly;
  • failed reconciliation does not advance the baseline.

docs.title: TUI tests
docs.text:
Using the current upstream TUI/component test strategy, prove:

  • source-style intent dispatches through shared application semantics;
  • changing personal source style updates the source projection presentation;
  • editability/read-only status reflects exact fidelity;
  • source-style change does not move session/reply/plan cursors;
  • source-style change does not trigger model execution;
  • terminal theme and source style are independent.

docs.title: Web/client tests
docs.text:
Prove:

  • schema/effective style/fidelity are available through reusable packages;
  • user/view changes round-trip through client/protocol correctly;
  • remote effective style matches embedded/local semantics;
  • integrated web controls do not duplicate precedence rules.

docs.title: 20. Validation
docs.text:
Run narrow tests throughout, then at minimum the repository-prescribed validation for all affected Rust and web packages:

cargo fmt --all
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
python3 tools/lint_repo.py
pnpm --dir web format
pnpm --dir web typecheck

Run relevant Rust tests, web package tests, TUI component/PTY tests, and remote/client conformance tests affected by the implementation.

Do not mark a checklist item complete unless its validation evidence exists.

docs.title: Exact reconciliation baseline
docs.text:
• [ ] Reconciliation uses a typed exact baseline containing semantic state, scope/specification, resolved style, renderer/adapter identity, output identity, and fidelity.
  • [ ] Editable synchronization retains/retrieves exact baseline output where reconciliation requires it.
  • [ ] Optional mapping/loss evidence is bound to exact baseline inputs/output.
  • [ ] Baseline style remains fixed even after user/materialization preferences change.
  • [ ] Failed reconciliation does not advance the synchronization baseline.

docs.title: Loss-aware behavior
docs.text:
• [ ] At least one safely classified lossy style is implemented as loss-aware editable, or the semantic-model blocker is recorded and all lossy styles remain correctly read-only.
  • [ ] Supported loss-aware editing preserves style-hidden canonical content.
  • [ ] Visible baseline deletion is distinguishable from style-hidden absence for the supported domain.
  • [ ] Concurrent canonical changes still use normal conflict/merge semantics.
  • [ ] Ambiguous cases return ambiguity/conflict rather than guessed deletion/identity.

docs.title: Materialization isolation
docs.text:
• [ ] Personal view preference changes do not rewrite shared managed files.
  • [ ] Workspace materialization policy determines shared file style independently of current viewer.
  • [ ] Deliberate materialization-style changes establish a new exact baseline only after successful render/write.
  • [ ] Two-user personal-style/shared-materialization scenario passes.

docs.title: Shared contracts
docs.text:
• [ ] Shared application semantics expose style schema/effective style/provenance/fidelity.
  • [ ] Protocol/client transport exists where required for remote/web/TUI use.
  • [ ] Local and remote style resolution are semantically equivalent.
  • [ ] Reusable web packages expose the semantics without depending on the integrated app.

docs.title: RPI TUI integration
docs.text:
• [ ] TUI style controls are implemented on the current upstream rpi-tui component/runtime boundary.
  • [ ] No new parallel Ratatui shell/theme/settings framework was introduced.
  • [ ] TUI dispatches source-style intent through shared application operations.
  • [ ] Personal source-style changes do not move session/reply/coordinator cursors.
  • [ ] Personal source-style changes do not trigger model execution or plan scheduling.
  • [ ] Source projection style and terminal theme remain independent.
  • [ ] Fidelity/read-only status is visible/enforced for the selected style.

docs.title: Web integration
docs.text:
• [ ] Web client/model/react/editor layers consume shared style semantics at appropriate boundaries.
  • [ ] Integrated/opinionated controls do not duplicate domain formatting or precedence logic.
  • [ ] Web and TUI observe equivalent effective style/fidelity for equivalent fixtures.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• [ ] Projection/reconciliation tests pass.
  • [ ] Filesystem synchronization tests pass.
  • [ ] Application/protocol/client conformance tests pass.
  • [ ] Current TUI component/PTY tests relevant to the feature pass.
  • [ ] Relevant web package tests pass.
  • [ ] cargo fmt --all passes.
  • [ ] cargo check --workspace --all-targets passes.
  • [ ] cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings passes.
  • [ ] python3 tools/lint_repo.py passes.
  • [ ] pnpm --dir web format passes when web code is changed.
  • [ ] pnpm --dir web typecheck passes when web code is changed.

docs.title: 22. Completion Result
docs.text:
When this task is complete, Scriberig should support the architectural scenario that motivated this design:

one canonical TypeScript/Rust semantic program
        |
        +-- User A personal source projection
        |     e.g. 2 spaces, comments shown
        |
        +-- User B personal source projection
        |     e.g. 4 spaces, safely hideable comments omitted
        |
        +-- shared repository materialization
              repository/workspace policy

All three representations remain tied to exact declared styles and one semantic source of truth. Personal representation changes remain presentation/configuration behavior, shared materialization remains deterministic, and any editable lossy representation preserves canonical content that its style intentionally did not show.

docs.title: Implement Compound Artifacts, Scalable Collections, Fidelity, and Atomic Materialization
Status
docs.text:
Planned.

All completion items remain unchecked until implemented and verified.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Implement the shared infrastructure required before XLSX, DOCX, CAD, or geospatial write support is added.

This task must deliver:

  1. logical artifacts that may have one, many, or container-internal physical members;
  2. exact source evidence and artifact/member manifests;
  3. explicit fidelity/editability and opaque-preservation capability;
  4. bounded scalable semantic collection access;
  5. typed support for non-text projection anchors where needed;
  6. staged multi-member materialization with failure/recovery evidence;
  7. shared application/protocol/client exposure sufficient for later domain tasks.

This task is constrained by:

  • level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md;
  • level-1/003. identity revisions and snapshots.md;
  • level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md;
  • level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md;
  • level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md;
  • level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md;
  • level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md;
  • level-1/019. semantic agent operations and projection-first editing.md;
  • level-1/024. projection styles personalized representations and materialization policy.md;
  • level-1/025. compound artifacts scalable collections and rich domain editing.md;
  • level-2/008. filesystem projection synchronization.md;
  • level-2/010. universal query and operation implementation.md;
  • level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md;
  • level-2/027. project wide candidate workspaces validation and materialization.md;
  • level-2/034. projection style resolution loss-aware reconciliation and cross-surface contracts.md;
  • level-2/035. rich project artifacts office cad and geospatial implementation plan.md.

docs.title: 2. Required Reading and Audit
docs.text:
Before editing:

  • [ ] Read root AGENTS.md completely.
  • [ ] Read design/AGENTS.md and design/CONTEXT.md.
  • [ ] Read every design document listed in section 1.
  • [ ] Read the nearest AGENTS.md for every crate modified.
  • [ ] Inspect current scriberig-project scan/import manifest types.
  • [ ] Inspect current exact source-byte/digest retention path used during project onboarding.
  • [ ] Inspect sr-projection model/capability/render/reconciliation types.
  • [ ] Inspect sr-projection-fs ownership, hashing, atomic I/O, observation, and effect-receipt behavior.
  • [ ] Inspect current universal query pagination/list contracts before adding scalable collection selectors.
  • [ ] Search for existing artifact/blob/member/fidelity types before adding new abstractions.
  • [ ] Record any material repository reality that differs from this task directly in this document before implementing around it.

Do not check an audit item until the relevant code/design has actually been read.

docs.title: 3. Checklist Discipline
docs.text:
While implementing this task:

  • [ ] Keep this task document open.
  • [ ] Tick each checkbox immediately after that exact behavior is implemented and its focused verification passes.
  • [ ] If later work invalidates a checked behavior, immediately restore [ ].
  • [ ] Do not bulk-check at the end.
  • [ ] Do not mark a behavior complete because a neighboring abstraction exists.

Until all implementation checkboxes are complete, run focused crate/tests only. Save workspace-wide final gates for section 14.

docs.title: 4. Architectural Prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not:

  • create a second project catalog;
  • create a second canonical blob/file database disconnected from the universal store/projection evidence model;
  • equate an artifact with exactly one filesystem path;
  • use absolute machine paths as semantic identity;
  • make parser-library object IDs canonical Scriberig identities;
  • make fidelity a UI-only flag;
  • silently drop unknown source-significant package members;
  • report successful multi-member materialization after only some required members were written;
  • bypass candidate/migration/validation/promotion for artifact edits;
  • add unrestricted ZIP/XML/SQLite mutation as the model-facing normal editing API;
  • eagerly serialize huge spreadsheet/GIS collections merely to satisfy inspect or list.

docs.title: 5. Phase A — Define Artifact and Member Contracts
docs.text:
Implement or reuse shared contracts equivalent in responsibility to:

ArtifactKind
ArtifactMemberKey
ArtifactMemberDescriptor
ArtifactSourceEvidence
ArtifactExternalReference
ArtifactManifest
ArtifactFidelity
ArtifactPreservationStatus

The owning crate must follow current dependency direction. Prefer existing project/core/projection owners over a new crate.

Requirements:

  • [ ] One artifact has stable semantic identity separate from paths/member names.
  • [ ] One artifact revision can reference one or more exact physical source members.
  • [ ] A member carries a logical key and exact digest.
  • [ ] Filesystem members carry project-relative paths, never absolute paths as canonical identity.
  • [ ] Container-internal members can use adapter-defined logical part names without pretending they are project files.
  • [ ] Artifact manifests serialize deterministically.
  • [ ] Exact evidence provenance identifies scan/import source and adapter/version where applicable.
  • [ ] External references are represented explicitly rather than hidden in arbitrary strings.
  • [ ] Public types contain no parser-native handles/pointers.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] one-file artifact manifest round trip;
  • [ ] four-member Shapefile-like manifest round trip;
  • [ ] container-member manifest with no extracted filesystem path;
  • [ ] deterministic equality/encoding for equivalent manifests;
  • [ ] absolute path changes do not redefine semantic artifact identity.

docs.title: 6. Phase B — Extend Project Scan Classification and Grouping
docs.text:
Extend persisted scan/import classification so adapters may group related paths deterministically.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Every selected regular file still has its own exact scan evidence and digest.
  • [ ] Classification may nominate a logical artifact/grouping key.
  • [ ] Grouping happens from the persisted scan manifest, not by a hidden fresh rescan.
  • [ ] Grouping rules are domain/adapter owned.
  • [ ] Ambiguous grouping returns structured diagnostics.
  • [ ] Unsupported files still use the existing binary fallback.
  • [ ] A grouped artifact retains each member's project-relative path and digest.
  • [ ] A single container file can classify as one compound artifact without exposing internal package parts as scanned project files.
  • [ ] Import produces stable artifact semantic handles usable by later operations.

Add a synthetic test adapter if necessary; do not wait for XLSX/Shapefile tasks to test the generic mechanism.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] group roads.shp, roads.dbf, roads.shx, roads.prj into one synthetic artifact;
  • [ ] leave unrelated roads.txt outside that group;
  • [ ] prove import uses the recorded manifest after the physical directory changes;
  • [ ] prove grouping ambiguity is diagnostic and not silently resolved.

docs.title: 7. Phase C — Add Fidelity and Preservation Capability
docs.text:
Build on current projection capabilities and Level-2 034.

Introduce an exact capability model able to represent at least the responsibilities of:

InspectOnly
ReadOnlyDerived
LosslessEditable
LossAwareEditable
EditableWithOpaquePreservation
RestrictedExternalProviderEdit
Unsupported

Exact enum names may differ if repository naming already exists.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Fidelity is available through shared domain/projection capability discovery.
  • [ ] Fidelity can depend on adapter/version and artifact-specific conditions.
  • [ ] Opaque-preservation guarantee/status is explicit.
  • [ ] A parser being available does not automatically imply write support.
  • [ ] Unsupported unknown content can downgrade editability deterministically.
  • [ ] Capability diagnostics explain why an artifact is read-only/restricted.
  • [ ] Fidelity participates in editable projection/reconciliation safety checks.
  • [ ] UI/agent code consumes capability rather than guessing from file extension.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] artifact without writer reports read-only;
  • [ ] artifact with unknown unpreservable extension reports restricted/read-only;
  • [ ] artifact with proven opaque preservation reports editable-preserving;
  • [ ] serialized protocol/client view preserves the same fidelity result.

docs.title: 8. Phase D — Add Opaque Preserved Content Boundary
docs.text:
Implement an adapter-owned preserved-content mechanism.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Opaque preserved content is bound to exact base artifact/member evidence.
  • [ ] Opaque content is not flattened into arbitrary universal property bags when it has no semantic interpretation.
  • [ ] Adapters can carry opaque preserved records through render/materialization.
  • [ ] Unrelated semantic edits can prove preserved records survived.
  • [ ] A requested operation that invalidates/removes the owner may explicitly discard affected opaque records with provenance.
  • [ ] Failure to preserve required opaque content blocks promotion/materialization or downgrades capability.
  • [ ] Opaque source evidence remains distinct from derived extraction.

Create a synthetic compound fixture containing one understood record and one opaque record and prove the understood record can change without losing the opaque record.

docs.title: 9. Phase E — Add Scalable Collection Access
docs.text:
Do not redesign the universal graph. Add the minimum contracts necessary for bounded semantic collections.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Collection reads support deterministic pagination/range selection.
  • [ ] Domain-specific selector/query extensions can be registered without a universal untyped Any payload.
  • [ ] Results retain exact snapshot/revision context.
  • [ ] Member results contain stable semantic handles.
  • [ ] A collection may report count/extent/summary without enumerating all members.
  • [ ] Large collection implementations may use indexes/backing blocks internally.
  • [ ] Derived indexes record provenance/dependencies through existing derivation infrastructure.
  • [ ] Semantic mutations identify the smallest changed member/range/collection structure rather than replacing an entire huge collection by default.

Add test-only scalable collection data with at least tens of thousands of logical members without building an enormous protocol response.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] request page 2 returns only bounded members;
  • [ ] range query touches only requested logical range plus required index data;
  • [ ] member handle resolves in the same snapshot without enumerating all siblings;
  • [ ] changing one member produces a local changed set;
  • [ ] stale snapshot member reads remain exact.

docs.title: 10. Phase F — Add Non-Text Projection Anchor Boundary
docs.text:
Use existing selection/projection architecture.

Requirements:

  • [ ] A projection may expose adapter/domain-owned typed anchor data.
  • [ ] Anchor schema/kind is discoverable.
  • [ ] Anchor resolves to semantic handle(s) plus exact snapshot/revision context.
  • [ ] Anchor itself is not canonical entity identity.
  • [ ] Existing textual source anchors continue to work unchanged.
  • [ ] Protocol/client transport can carry bounded anchor descriptors needed by remote/web clients.
  • [ ] UI-specific pixel/screen positions are not persisted as semantic identity.

Add generic test anchors equivalent to a cell/range and geometry/bounds without adding actual XLSX/GIS code in this task.

docs.title: 11. Phase G — Implement Artifact-Level Staged Materialization
docs.text:
Extend the current filesystem projection materialization owner rather than introducing a domain-private writer transaction.

Implement state equivalent to:

ArtifactMaterializationPlan
  artifact
  expected external baseline
  required output members
  optional output members
  staged bytes/digests

ArtifactMaterializationReceipt
  artifact
  per-member result/digest
  completion/recovery state
  new baseline identity

Requirements:

  • [ ] All required output members are rendered before final replacement starts.
  • [ ] Candidate validators can inspect the complete staged set.
  • [ ] Expected external baseline/digest is checked before destructive replacement.
  • [ ] Single-file artifacts continue to use existing safe atomic path.
  • [ ] Multi-file artifacts stage all required members.
  • [ ] If platform-level all-member atomic replacement is unavailable, a recovery journal/receipt records exactly what happened.
  • [ ] Partial failure is never reported as success.
  • [ ] Self-write observation suppression/hash tracking is updated only for members actually committed.
  • [ ] Successful completion establishes one new exact artifact synchronization baseline.
  • [ ] Failed completion does not advance canonical project snapshot a second time or invent success state.
  • [ ] Recovery path is idempotent or detects already-completed members safely.

Focused tests must inject failure after at least one staged/committed member.

  • [ ] failure leaves explicit recoverable/failed receipt;
  • [ ] success receipt contains every mandatory member;
  • [ ] external concurrent modification blocks replacement;
  • [ ] retry/recovery produces deterministic final state.

docs.title: 12. Phase H — Shared Application, Protocol, and Client Exposure
docs.text:
Add the minimum shared operations/views needed by tasks 155–160.

Conceptual reads:

artifact.inspect_source
artifact.list_members
artifact.fidelity
artifact.materialization_status

Requirements:

  • [ ] Application service owns operation semantics and capability enforcement.
  • [ ] Protocol DTOs contain stable semantic/public data only.
  • [ ] Client exposes local/remote-equivalent methods/views.
  • [ ] Large member content is referenced/bounded rather than embedded into every summary.
  • [ ] Agent capability discovery can advertise artifact reads but no raw mutation shortcut.
  • [ ] TUI/web can inspect fidelity/member summaries through the same application path.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] embedded application and remote client return equivalent artifact summary;
  • [ ] unauthorized/capability-scoped call is rejected consistently;
  • [ ] large member does not appear inline in bounded summary DTO.

docs.title: 13. Phase I — Conformance Fixtures and Test Support
docs.text:
Extend crates/domains/test-support and/or scriberig-conformance with reusable helpers.

  • [ ] Add synthetic one-file artifact fixture.
  • [ ] Add synthetic multi-file artifact fixture.
  • [ ] Add synthetic container-part fixture.
  • [ ] Add opaque-preservation fixture.
  • [ ] Add large paged collection fixture.
  • [ ] Add materialization failure injection helper.
  • [ ] Add assertions for exact source digest/provenance.
  • [ ] Add assertions for no partial-success materialization.
  • [ ] Document how later domain tasks reuse these helpers.

Do not add real XLSX/DOCX/DXF/GIS behavior here beyond what is necessary to test the generic layer.

docs.title: 14. Verification
docs.text:
Run focused checks while implementing, for example the exact current package names that own changed code:

cargo test -p scriberig-project artifact
cargo test -p sr-projection artifact
cargo test -p sr-projection-fs materialization
cargo test -p scriberig-app artifact
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol artifact
cargo test -p scriberig-client artifact
cargo test -p scriberig-conformance artifact

Adapt filters to actual test names.

Final gate after all preceding checkboxes are complete:

  • [ ] python3 tools/lint_repo.py --fix
  • [ ] cargo fmt --all
  • [ ] cargo check --workspace --all-targets
  • [ ] cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
  • [ ] relevant focused test suites pass after formatting/lint fixes;
  • [ ] no source file violates the repository size rule;
  • [ ] all new public/private functions/types follow declaration documentation rules;
  • [ ] third-party notices are updated if this task introduced any dependency.

docs.title: 15. Completion Gate
docs.text:
Do not mark this task complete until all are true:

  • [ ] logical artifacts can represent one, many, and container-internal members;
  • [ ] exact source evidence remains distinct from semantic interpretation;
  • [ ] fidelity/editability is shared and discoverable;
  • [ ] opaque preservation has a tested safe path;
  • [ ] large semantic collections support bounded exact reads;
  • [ ] non-text projection anchors can resolve to semantic handles;
  • [ ] staged multi-member materialization has tested failure/recovery behavior;
  • [ ] shared app/protocol/client exposure exists;
  • [ ] tasks 155–160 can build on these contracts without inventing competing infrastructure;
  • [ ] every checked item above has current verification evidence.

docs.title: Implement Spreadsheet Domain and Editable XLSX Vertical Slice
Status
docs.text:
Planned.

All completion items remain unchecked until implemented and verified.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Implement the first rich-artifact vertical slice: a format-independent spreadsheet domain plus an XLSX adapter that can safely inspect and edit a bounded workbook through normal Scriberig semantic change flow.

The minimum product scenario is:

onboard workbook.xlsx
inspect Workbook
list worksheets
inspect used range on sheet Budget
inspect B3
change B3 value or formula semantically
create candidate
validate candidate
review/apply
materialize workbook.xlsx
reopen workbook and prove the edit

This task depends on task 154.

It is constrained by:

  • level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md;
  • level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md;
  • level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md;
  • level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md;
  • level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md;
  • level-1/019. semantic agent operations and projection-first editing.md;
  • level-1/024. projection styles personalized representations and materialization policy.md;
  • level-1/025. compound artifacts scalable collections and rich domain editing.md;
  • level-2/035. rich project artifacts office cad and geospatial implementation plan.md.

docs.title: 2. Required Reading and Audit
docs.text:
Before editing:

  • [ ] Read root AGENTS.md, design/AGENTS.md, and design/CONTEXT.md.
  • [ ] Read every design document listed above.
  • [ ] Read completed implementation and tests from task 154.
  • [ ] Read crates/domains/AGENTS.md and nearest AGENTS.md for every modified crate.
  • [ ] Inspect current domain registration/capability patterns in Markdown, Rust, data, PDF, and binary domains.
  • [ ] Inspect current project scan classification and adapter-selection rules.
  • [ ] Inspect current semantic operation registration and candidate creation flow.
  • [ ] Inspect current projection render/reconciliation/style/fidelity contracts.
  • [ ] Inspect current third-party licensing/notices conventions before adding XLSX dependencies.
  • [ ] Record material deviations from this task in this document before implementing around them.

docs.title: 3. Checklist Discipline
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this task document open while implementing.
  • [ ] Tick each item immediately after focused verification passes.
  • [ ] Reopen a checkbox if later work invalidates it.
  • [ ] Do not bulk-tick at the end.
  • [ ] Use focused tests until section 15.

docs.title: 4. Architectural Prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not:

  • treat XLSX ZIP/XML/package parts as the canonical spreadsheet model;
  • make the external XLSX library's workbook structs public Scriberig semantic types;
  • eagerly create semantic records for every possible empty Excel cell;
  • treat cell display formatting as the same thing as cell value/formula semantics;
  • treat cached formula results as authoritative recalculation;
  • mutate xl/worksheets/*.xml directly from agent/UI code;
  • expose insert-row/ref-rewrite operations until their formula/reference semantics are correct;
  • silently drop macros, signatures, charts, relationships, unknown package parts, or other source-significant content;
  • claim write fidelity when the chosen library cannot preserve encountered workbook structures.

docs.title: 5. Phase A — Choose Package Layout and XLSX Dependency
docs.text:
Create a format-independent spreadsheet domain.

Preferred layout:

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-spreadsheet/

Place XLSX-specific code either in focused modules there initially or create:

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-xlsx/

Use a separate XLSX crate if external dependencies/package logic would otherwise leak into the generic domain.

Before adding a dependency:

  • [ ] Evaluate at least the practical current Rust XLSX read/write options available to the repository.
  • [ ] Record why the selected library is suitable for the first vertical slice.
  • [ ] Record known preservation/write limitations.
  • [ ] Verify license compatibility.
  • [ ] Update THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md if required.
  • [ ] Keep the library behind adapter-private modules.

Do not make library choice an architectural commitment.

docs.title: 6. Phase B — Define Spreadsheet Semantic Schema
docs.text:
Implement minimum semantic types/schema equivalent to:

Workbook
Worksheet
Cell
Range
Formula
DefinedName
Table
CellStyleRef

Requirements:

  • [ ] Workbook and Worksheet have stable semantic identities.
  • [ ] Worksheet ordering is represented by owning collection structure.
  • [ ] Cell identity is semantic and snapshot-aware, not merely a display string.
  • [ ] Empty cells are not eagerly materialized across the full Excel grid.
  • [ ] Cell values distinguish at least blank/string/number/boolean/error/formula where source safely supports them.
  • [ ] A formula preserves authored formula text/expression.
  • [ ] Formula references can be inspected or derived without making cached result authoritative.
  • [ ] Defined names are imported at least for inspection if supported by the selected adapter.
  • [ ] Tables are imported at least as semantic ranges/metadata if supported.
  • [ ] Cell style reference is separated from cell value/formula semantics.
  • [ ] Schema and adapter versions are registered using existing domain version conventions.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] create workbook semantic graph with two sheets;
  • [ ] stable cell handle resolves in exact snapshot;
  • [ ] one changed cell creates local revision/change set;
  • [ ] empty surrounding grid does not appear as thousands of semantic entities.

docs.title: 7. Phase C — Create Deterministic XLSX Fixture
docs.text:
Add a repository-controlled binary fixture under the rich-project fixture family.

Required semantic anchors:

Workbook
  sheet: Budget
  A3 = 10
  B3 = formula =A3*2
  C3 = "existing"

second sheet: Notes
  A1 = "preserve me"

Include at least one unrelated package feature that tests preservation, such as a style, defined name, simple chart, relationship, custom property, or unknown preserved part if the chosen library can round-trip it safely.

  • [ ] Add a reproducible generator script or clearly document how the binary fixture was produced.
  • [ ] Keep fixture small and deterministic.
  • [ ] Add expected semantic anchors to fixture README.
  • [ ] Prove the original fixture opens in the selected parser before implementing edits.

Do not make acceptance depend on Microsoft Excel being installed.

docs.title: 8. Phase D — Implement XLSX Import and Exact Evidence
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • [ ] Scanner classifies .xlsx into the XLSX adapter instead of generic binary.
  • [ ] Exact outer XLSX source digest/evidence is retained.
  • [ ] Package-part/member evidence integrates with task-154 artifact contracts where needed.
  • [ ] Import creates Workbook and Worksheet semantic entities.
  • [ ] Import exposes used-range summary without eagerly returning every cell.
  • [ ] Import maps non-empty cells in requested/known used areas to semantic cell handles.
  • [ ] Formula cell B3 preserves authored formula =A3*2 or the canonical adapter form that deterministically renders to it.
  • [ ] Unrelated sheet Notes remains independently addressable.
  • [ ] Unsupported source-significant package content is preserved or causes write capability downgrade.
  • [ ] Adapter diagnostics report unsupported workbook features affecting editability.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] import fixture from exact bytes;
  • [ ] list worksheets returns Budget and Notes;
  • [ ] used range for Budget is bounded;
  • [ ] inspect B3 returns formula semantics;
  • [ ] inspect source evidence returns exact original digest;
  • [ ] capability reports expected fidelity.

docs.title: 9. Phase E — Implement Bounded Range Reads
docs.text:
Add spreadsheet-specific range selector/query using task-154 scalable collection mechanics.

Required behavior:

read range Budget!A1:D20
list non-empty/used regions
inspect cell Budget!B3

Requirements:

  • [ ] Range request is snapshot-bound.
  • [ ] Response includes row/column coordinates and semantic handles.
  • [ ] Response size is bounded by requested range/page policy.
  • [ ] Large sheet does not serialize unrelated cells.
  • [ ] Cell/range selection can produce a typed spreadsheet projection anchor.
  • [ ] Agent capability discovery advertises range reads only when workbook selected.

Add a synthetic larger workbook/range test sufficient to prove bounded behavior.

docs.title: 10. Phase F — Implement Safe Spreadsheet Operations
docs.text:
Implement first operations:

spreadsheet.set_cell_value
spreadsheet.set_formula
spreadsheet.rename_sheet

spreadsheet.insert_rows is optional in this task unless formula/reference rewriting is fully correct.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Operations resolve Workbook/Worksheet/Cell semantic handles in exact base snapshot.
  • [ ] Operations produce candidate semantic state through shared change model.
  • [ ] No operation writes the live XLSX file directly.
  • [ ] set_cell_value rejects invalid target/kind changes cleanly.
  • [ ] set_formula preserves formula source semantics.
  • [ ] rename_sheet updates dependent formula/name references only if the implementation can do so correctly; otherwise block rename when dependencies exist and explain why.
  • [ ] Changed-set/diff identifies target sheet/cell/formula, not the whole workbook by default.
  • [ ] Provenance identifies user/agent/application operation.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] set B3 formula to =A3*3 creates candidate only;
  • [ ] canonical project snapshot remains unchanged before apply;
  • [ ] semantic diff reports B3/formula change;
  • [ ] invalid stale-base operation fails without mutation.

docs.title: 11. Phase G — Render/Materialize XLSX
docs.text:
Implement deterministic XLSX materialization through shared artifact/projection infrastructure.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Candidate workbook renders to staged XLSX bytes.
  • [ ] Rendering uses exact base/preservation evidence needed to retain unsupported preserved parts.
  • [ ] Output is written only by shared materialization path.
  • [ ] Expected external baseline is verified before replacement.
  • [ ] Successful apply/materialization records exact new digest/baseline.
  • [ ] Unrelated sheet Notes remains unchanged semantically.
  • [ ] Untargeted preserved package content remains present when adapter advertises preservation.
  • [ ] If preservation cannot be proven for a encountered feature, write capability is blocked/downgraded rather than silently dropping it.

Do not assert byte-for-byte equality for ZIP container output unless the adapter intentionally guarantees it. Assert semantic and preserved-content correctness.

docs.title: 12. Phase H — Validation
docs.text:
Create XLSX validation profile that at minimum:

reopens staged XLSX
verifies package parse
verifies expected workbook/sheet structure
verifies candidate target cell/formula
verifies required preserved content

Requirements:

  • [ ] Validation runs against staged candidate state, not live file.
  • [ ] Validation result binds to exact candidate/output digest.
  • [ ] Validation failure blocks promotion/materialization completion.
  • [ ] Reopen parser may be the same library initially, but add an independent structural ZIP/XML check if practical.
  • [ ] Cached formula result mismatch is not treated as semantic failure unless explicitly recalculated by a supported engine.

Focused test:

  • [ ] deliberately corrupt staged XLSX and prove validation rejects it without changing live artifact.

docs.title: 13. Phase I — Application, Protocol, Client, and Agent Capabilities
docs.text:
Expose shared semantic operations/views.

Required public concepts:

WorkbookSummary
WorksheetSummary
SpreadsheetRangeView
CellView
FormulaView
SpreadsheetOperationResult

Requirements:

  • [ ] Embedded app can inspect workbook/sheet/range/cell.
  • [ ] Remote protocol/client returns equivalent semantic data.
  • [ ] Agent tool catalog exposes semantic spreadsheet tools for selected workbook/sheet/cell.
  • [ ] No raw ZIP/XML mutation tool is added as normal spreadsheet capability.
  • [ ] Operation results expose candidate/change handles for review.
  • [ ] Fidelity diagnostics are visible through shared capability data.

Do not implement full web/TUI rich grid here; task 160 owns cross-surface presentation.

docs.title: 14. Golden End-to-End Test
docs.text:
Add one focused product/domain integration test proving:

import fixture
resolve workbook
resolve Budget sheet
read B3 = =A3*2
propose set_formula B3 = =A3*3
validate candidate
apply candidate
materialize
reopen output
read B3 = =A3*3
read Notes!A1 = "preserve me"
  • [ ] Test does not require network.
  • [ ] Test does not require Excel installed.
  • [ ] Test starts from a fresh copied fixture.
  • [ ] Test proves original checked-in fixture is untouched.
  • [ ] Test verifies history/provenance contains the spreadsheet operation.

docs.title: 15. Verification
docs.text:
Focused checks while implementing, adapting package names if the final crate split differs:

cargo test -p scriberig-domain-spreadsheet
cargo test -p scriberig-domain-xlsx
cargo test -p scriberig-project xlsx
cargo test -p scriberig-app spreadsheet
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol spreadsheet
cargo test -p scriberig-client spreadsheet

Final gates after implementation checkboxes are complete:

  • [ ] python3 tools/lint_repo.py --fix
  • [ ] cargo fmt --all
  • [ ] cargo check --workspace --all-targets
  • [ ] cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
  • [ ] relevant focused tests pass after final formatting;
  • [ ] new source files obey file-size/documentation rules;
  • [ ] third-party notices/license metadata are correct.

docs.title: 16. Completion Gate
docs.text:
Do not mark complete until:

  • [ ] XLSX imports as semantic Workbook/Worksheet/Cell/Formula knowledge;
  • [ ] used-range/range reads are bounded;
  • [ ] B3 can be changed through semantic candidate flow;
  • [ ] live XLSX is not touched before apply/materialization;
  • [ ] candidate validation reopens staged workbook;
  • [ ] materialized XLSX reopens with expected edit;
  • [ ] unrelated semantic content survives;
  • [ ] opaque/unsupported content is preserved or write support is explicitly restricted;
  • [ ] local/remote/application/agent semantic contracts agree;
  • [ ] every checked item has current verification evidence.

docs.title: Implement Rich Document Domain and Editable DOCX Vertical Slice
Status
docs.text:
Planned.

All completion items remain unchecked until implemented and verified.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Implement a reusable rich-document semantic domain plus a DOCX adapter that can safely inspect and edit document paragraphs/tables while preserving unrelated package content and using normal Scriberig candidate/change/materialization semantics.

Minimum scenario:

onboard report.docx
inspect Document
navigate section/paragraph/table
replace one paragraph or table cell semantically
create candidate
validate
review/apply
materialize DOCX
reopen and prove edit + preservation

This task depends on task 154. It may reuse generic document semantics from the Markdown domain where appropriate but must not force Markdown-specific representation onto DOCX.

docs.title: 2. Required Reading and Audit
docs.text:
Before editing:

  • [ ] Read root AGENTS.md, design/AGENTS.md, and design/CONTEXT.md.
  • [ ] Read Level-1 documents 002, 005, 006, 007, 019, 024, and 025.
  • [ ] Read Level-2 documents 009, 034, and 035.
  • [ ] Read task 154 implementation and tests.
  • [ ] Read crates/domains/AGENTS.md and nearest AGENTS.md for modified crates.
  • [ ] Inspect current Markdown schema to identify genuinely reusable document concepts.
  • [ ] Inspect current PDF imported-document handling for exact source/provenance precedent.
  • [ ] Inspect current projection fidelity/reconciliation contracts.
  • [ ] Inspect third-party notices/licensing conventions before adding DOCX/OpenXML dependencies.
  • [ ] Record any material deviation from this plan directly in this file before implementing around it.

docs.title: 3. Checklist Discipline
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this file open while implementing.
  • [ ] Tick each item immediately after focused verification.
  • [ ] Reopen items invalidated by later changes.
  • [ ] Do not bulk-tick.
  • [ ] Run focused checks until section 14.

docs.title: 4. Architectural Prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not:

  • make WordprocessingML XML trees the public canonical document model;
  • duplicate Paragraph/TableRow/TableCell concepts unnecessarily if existing shared semantics can be reused cleanly;
  • make rendered page number/line wrapping canonical paragraph identity;
  • silently discard unsupported DOCX parts, relationships, tracked changes, comments, bookmarks, fields, headers/footers, content controls, or embedded objects;
  • claim editable fidelity merely because paragraphs can be parsed;
  • mutate DOCX ZIP/XML directly from agent/UI code;
  • bypass shared candidate/change/materialization paths.

docs.title: 5. Phase A — Define Crate/Schema Ownership
docs.text:
Preferred structure:

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-document/
crates/domains/scriberig-domain-docx/

If repository audit proves current Markdown semantic types can serve as a generic document layer without pulling Markdown parser/renderer dependencies upward, reuse/refactor those types instead of creating duplicates.

  • [ ] Document final ownership decision in crate/module docs.
  • [ ] Keep generic document domain independent of DOCX libraries.
  • [ ] Keep DOCX parser/package types private to the adapter.
  • [ ] Register schema/adapter versions using existing conventions.

docs.title: 6. Phase B — Implement Rich Document Semantic Schema
docs.text:
Minimum types/concepts:

Document
Section
Paragraph
InlineRun
List
Table
TableRow
TableCell
ImageReference
Hyperlink

DOCX-specific extension concepts, at least inspectable when encountered:

DocumentStyle
HeaderFooter
Footnote
Endnote
Bookmark
Field
Comment
TrackedChange
ContentControl
DrawingObject

Requirements:

  • [ ] Paragraphs are independently addressable semantic objects.
  • [ ] Tables expose rows/cells semantically.
  • [ ] Inline runs preserve author-significant structure needed for round trip.
  • [ ] Formatting/style references are distinct from paragraph text semantics where appropriate.
  • [ ] Section/document ordering is explicit collection structure.
  • [ ] Images/links use explicit relations/references.
  • [ ] DOCX-specific extensions are not flattened into generic strings merely for convenience.
  • [ ] Layout/page facts are classified as derived unless exact canonical semantics require otherwise.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] construct document with two paragraphs and one table;
  • [ ] edit one paragraph produces local semantic change;
  • [ ] table cell has stable handle across unrelated paragraph edit;
  • [ ] style change alone can remain projection/configuration change where applicable.

docs.title: 7. Phase C — Choose DOCX Library and Create Fixture
docs.text:
Before dependency choice:

  • [ ] Evaluate practical current Rust DOCX/OpenXML read/write options.
  • [ ] Record selected library and known unsupported structures.
  • [ ] Verify license compatibility and update notices if needed.
  • [ ] Keep dependency types behind adapter-private modules.

Create deterministic fixture tests/fixtures/rich-project/report.docx with anchors:

paragraph: "Existing site area"
paragraph: "Preserve this paragraph"
table cell: parcel 124
header/footer text or another unrelated package structure
at least one style/relationship

Add one feature that tests opaque/unsupported preservation if feasible.

  • [ ] Provide generator/source description.
  • [ ] Document expected anchors in fixture README.
  • [ ] Prove original fixture reopens before editing logic is added.

docs.title: 8. Phase D — Implement DOCX Import
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • [ ] Scanner classifies .docx into DOCX adapter instead of generic binary.
  • [ ] Exact outer source digest/evidence is retained.
  • [ ] Package parts/relationships integrate with task-154 artifact member/evidence model.
  • [ ] Main document imports to Document/Section/Paragraph/Table semantic structure.
  • [ ] Paragraph Existing site area is independently discoverable.
  • [ ] Table cells are independently inspectable.
  • [ ] Headers/footers/comments/bookmarks/etc. are imported semantically when supported or preserved opaque when not.
  • [ ] Unknown source-significant package parts are preserved or editability is downgraded.
  • [ ] Adapter reports fidelity diagnostics for unsupported structures.
  • [ ] Import does not make pagination canonical.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] inspect Document summary;
  • [ ] list paragraphs without rendering entire package XML;
  • [ ] find paragraph by text;
  • [ ] inspect target table cell;
  • [ ] inspect exact source digest/fidelity.

docs.title: 9. Phase E — Implement Document Semantic Operations
docs.text:
Required first operations:

document.replace_paragraph
document.insert_paragraph
document.update_table_cell

Requirements:

  • [ ] Operations resolve exact base semantic handles.
  • [ ] Operations create candidate semantic state only.
  • [ ] Live DOCX is unchanged until apply/materialization.
  • [ ] Paragraph replacement preserves paragraph identity when continuity is clear.
  • [ ] Insert paragraph updates owning collection structure without revising unrelated paragraphs.
  • [ ] Table-cell update changes only relevant cell/content revisions where possible.
  • [ ] Operation provenance is recorded.
  • [ ] Stale-base operation fails/conflicts through shared change semantics.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] replace Existing site area with Proposed site area in candidate;
  • [ ] semantic diff identifies paragraph, not whole document blob;
  • [ ] Preserve this paragraph remains unchanged;
  • [ ] invalid target kind is rejected structurally.

docs.title: 10. Phase F — DOCX Rendering and Opaque Preservation
docs.text:
Materialize through shared artifact/projection infrastructure.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Render candidate semantic document into staged DOCX.
  • [ ] Preserve required package relationships and untargeted parts.
  • [ ] Carry task-154 opaque preserved records through output.
  • [ ] Preserve header/footer or chosen unrelated fixture structure.
  • [ ] Preserve styles referenced by unchanged content.
  • [ ] Expected external baseline is checked before replacement.
  • [ ] Successful output establishes exact new artifact baseline/digest.
  • [ ] Unsupported feature that cannot be preserved blocks/downgrades write capability.

Do not require byte-identical ZIP ordering/compression unless explicitly guaranteed. Validate semantic/package preservation.

docs.title: 11. Phase G — Reconciliation for External DOCX Edits
docs.text:
If first implementation can safely parse externally edited DOCX back into semantic structure, integrate reconciliation.

Requirements for editable external projection support:

  • [ ] Reconciliation is bound to exact prior artifact/source baseline.
  • [ ] Paragraph/table identity matching uses semantic/structural evidence, not ZIP member order alone.
  • [ ] Concurrent canonical change uses ordinary three-way conflict semantics.
  • [ ] Opaque preserved content absence from semantic parser is not interpreted as deletion.
  • [ ] Ambiguous moved/split/merged paragraph identity returns conflict/new-entity decision rather than invented continuity.

If safe reverse reconciliation cannot be proven in this task:

  • [ ] Keep direct external DOCX projection synchronization read-only while semantic operations/materialization remain editable.
  • [ ] Document exact blocking gap and leave unsafe reconciliation items unchecked.

docs.title: 12. Phase H — Validation
docs.text:
Validation profile must at minimum:

reopen staged DOCX
validate package relationships enough to parse
verify target paragraph/table cell
verify required preserved unrelated content
  • [ ] Validation binds to exact candidate/output digest.
  • [ ] Corrupt package is rejected before live replacement.
  • [ ] Missing required relationship/part is a structured diagnostic.
  • [ ] Layout differences are not semantic failures unless explicitly part of validation profile.
  • [ ] Validation evidence maps back to semantic Document/Paragraph/Table handles where possible.

docs.title: 13. Phase I — Shared Application/Protocol/Agent Exposure
docs.text:
Expose stable public views such as:

DocumentSummary
SectionSummary
ParagraphView
TableView/TableCellView
DocumentOperationResult

Requirements:

  • [ ] Embedded application supports inspect/list/find on document structure.
  • [ ] Remote protocol/client produces equivalent views.
  • [ ] Agent tools expose semantic paragraph/table operations progressively.
  • [ ] No raw OpenXML mutation tool is added as normal DOCX capability.
  • [ ] Candidate/change handles are returned for review.
  • [ ] Fidelity/opaque-preservation diagnostics are visible.

Task 160 owns rich interactive web/TUI presentation.

docs.title: 14. Golden End-to-End and Verification
docs.text:
Golden test:

import report.docx
find paragraph "Existing site area"
replace with "Proposed site area"
validate
apply/materialize
reopen
verify changed paragraph
verify "Preserve this paragraph"
verify chosen unrelated header/footer/style/package feature
  • [ ] Uses fresh copied fixture.
  • [ ] Requires no Word installation/network.
  • [ ] Checked-in fixture remains untouched.
  • [ ] History/provenance records document operation.

Focused commands, adapting crate names if needed:

cargo test -p scriberig-domain-document
cargo test -p scriberig-domain-docx
cargo test -p scriberig-app document
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol document
cargo test -p scriberig-client document

Final gate:

  • [ ] python3 tools/lint_repo.py --fix
  • [ ] cargo fmt --all
  • [ ] cargo check --workspace --all-targets
  • [ ] cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
  • [ ] focused tests pass after final formatting;
  • [ ] repository file-size/documentation rules pass;
  • [ ] third-party notices are correct.

docs.title: 15. Completion Gate
docs.text:
Do not mark complete until:

  • [ ] DOCX is represented as semantic document structure plus exact source evidence;
  • [ ] target paragraph/table cell can be edited through semantic candidate flow;
  • [ ] unrelated document content survives;
  • [ ] unsupported source-significant content is preserved or editability is explicitly restricted;
  • [ ] staged DOCX validation/reopen passes;
  • [ ] materialized DOCX reopens with expected edit;
  • [ ] no page/line coordinate became canonical document identity;
  • [ ] shared app/protocol/agent semantics exist;
  • [ ] every checked item has current verification evidence.

docs.title: Implement CAD Domain and Editable DXF Vertical Slice
Status
docs.text:
Planned.

All completion items remain unchecked until implemented and verified.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Implement a reusable CAD drawing semantic domain and an editable DXF adapter. DXF is the first required CAD materialization target; native DWG integration is handled separately by task 158.

Minimum scenario:

onboard drawing.dxf
inspect Drawing
list layers
inspect entity on layer PARCELS
change supported entity semantically
create candidate
validate
review/apply
materialize DXF
reopen and verify

This task depends on task 154.

docs.title: 2. Required Reading and Audit
docs.text:
Before editing:

  • [ ] Read root AGENTS.md, design/AGENTS.md, and design/CONTEXT.md.
  • [ ] Read Level-1 documents 002, 003, 005, 006, 007, 010, 019, 025.
  • [ ] Read Level-2 document 035.
  • [ ] Read task 154 implementation and tests.
  • [ ] Read crates/domains/AGENTS.md and nearest AGENTS.md for all modified crates.
  • [ ] Inspect current geometry/value representation in universal core/graph before inventing CAD-specific scalar encoding.
  • [ ] Inspect current projection anchor and fidelity contracts.
  • [ ] Inspect third-party licensing before adding DXF dependencies.
  • [ ] Record material deviations from this task directly in this file.

docs.title: 3. Checklist Discipline
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this task open during implementation.
  • [ ] Tick each item after focused verification passes.
  • [ ] Reopen invalidated items immediately.
  • [ ] Do not bulk-tick.
  • [ ] Run focused checks until section 14.

docs.title: 4. Architectural Prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not:

  • make DXF group-code records the canonical CAD domain model;
  • make native DXF handles equal Scriberig EntityId;
  • make screen/canvas pixels canonical geometry coordinates;
  • flatten all entity types into one generic string/property bag when meaningful CAD semantics are known;
  • discard unsupported DXF sections/entities merely because first vertical slice does not understand them;
  • write live DXF directly from agent/UI code;
  • couple generic CAD schema to task-158 DWG provider implementation.

docs.title: 5. Phase A — Create CAD Domain Crate and Schema
docs.text:
Add:

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-cad/

Minimum semantic concepts:

Drawing
DrawingSpace
Layout
Viewport
Layer
BlockDefinition
BlockReference
Line
Polyline
Arc
Circle
Text
Dimension
EntityStyleRef
ExternalReference

Requirements:

  • [ ] Drawing/Layer/Block/Entity identities use Scriberig semantic identity.
  • [ ] Native CAD handles are stored as external identifiers/provenance/reconciliation evidence.
  • [ ] Entity geometry uses exact domain values with documented coordinate/unit semantics.
  • [ ] Layer membership is semantic structure/relation, not inferred only from display color/name.
  • [ ] Block definitions and references remain distinct.
  • [ ] Model/paper/layout space is represented explicitly where encountered.
  • [ ] Entity ordering is preserved when author/tool significance requires it.
  • [ ] Schema version is registered.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] construct drawing with two layers and supported entities;
  • [ ] edit one entity without revising unrelated entities;
  • [ ] move entity between layers changes relation/structure explicitly;
  • [ ] native external handle survives as provenance without becoming EntityId.

docs.title: 6. Phase B — Choose DXF Adapter and Fixture
docs.text:
Evaluate current Rust DXF parser/writer options or implement the required bounded parser/writer if dependencies are unsuitable.

  • [ ] Record chosen implementation and supported DXF versions/entity types.
  • [ ] Verify dependency license and notices.
  • [ ] Keep parser-native types private.
  • [ ] Document preservation behavior for unsupported sections/entities.

Create tests/fixtures/rich-project/drawing.dxf with anchors:

layer PARCELS
layer LABELS
one polyline on PARCELS
one text entity "Parcel 124"
known native handles if writer preserves them
one unrelated entity to preserve
  • [ ] Fixture is deterministic and small.
  • [ ] Expected anchors are documented.
  • [ ] Original fixture successfully parses before edit implementation.

docs.title: 7. Phase C — Implement DXF Import and Exact Evidence
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • [ ] .dxf classifies to CAD/DXF adapter rather than generic text/binary.
  • [ ] Exact source bytes/digest remain available as artifact evidence.
  • [ ] Drawing, layers, blocks, and supported entities import semantically.
  • [ ] Native handles are retained as external identifiers where present.
  • [ ] Unsupported sections/entities are preserved opaque when safe.
  • [ ] Unsupported content that cannot be preserved downgrades write fidelity.
  • [ ] Units/header metadata needed for geometry interpretation are imported or preserved.
  • [ ] Entity-to-source/projection mapping supports inspection/diagnostics where practical.
  • [ ] Import does not require rendering a full image/canvas.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] inspect drawing summary;
  • [ ] list layers shows PARCELS/LABELS;
  • [ ] find text Parcel 124;
  • [ ] inspect target polyline geometry;
  • [ ] fidelity/source digest matches expected.

docs.title: 8. Phase D — CAD Queries and Anchors
docs.text:
Implement bounded semantic navigation/query sufficient for large drawings.

Required capabilities:

list entities by layer
find by native handle/external id
query by entity kind
query/intersect geometric bounds when practical

Requirements:

  • [ ] Queries are snapshot-bound and paged.
  • [ ] Results return semantic handles.
  • [ ] Drawing projection can expose geometric bounds anchor separate from semantic identity.
  • [ ] Large layer does not serialize every entity by default.
  • [ ] Native handle lookup resolves through reconciliation/index evidence, not direct replacement for EntityId.

docs.title: 9. Phase E — Implement Safe CAD Operations
docs.text:
Implement at least two operations from:

cad.move_entity
cad.change_layer
cad.update_text
cad.insert_polyline

Minimum required for golden path: one existing-entity edit plus one structural/geometry edit.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Operations resolve exact semantic target/base snapshot.
  • [ ] Candidate state is created without live file mutation.
  • [ ] Geometry operation validates coordinate dimensionality/units.
  • [ ] Layer operation verifies destination layer exists or uses explicit layer-create operation.
  • [ ] Text operation preserves untargeted entity properties.
  • [ ] Native handle behavior for edited entities is deterministic and documented.
  • [ ] Operation provenance is recorded.
  • [ ] Semantic diff identifies affected entity/layer relation rather than whole file blob.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] move/update target creates candidate only;
  • [ ] stale base fails/conflicts;
  • [ ] unrelated entity revision stays unchanged;
  • [ ] invalid geometry is rejected before materialization.

docs.title: 10. Phase F — Deterministic DXF Rendering and Preservation
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • [ ] Candidate drawing renders through shared projection/artifact infrastructure.
  • [ ] Supported entity semantics render deterministically.
  • [ ] Untargeted supported entities survive.
  • [ ] Opaque preserved sections/entities survive when fidelity advertises preservation.
  • [ ] Native handles are preserved when safe or remapped with explicit provenance according to documented adapter rule.
  • [ ] Expected external baseline is checked before replacement.
  • [ ] Successful materialization records new artifact digest/baseline.
  • [ ] Unsupported nonpreservable records block editability instead of being silently lost.

Do not require byte-identical DXF formatting unless adapter deliberately guarantees it.

docs.title: 11. Phase G — DXF Reconciliation
docs.text:
If external DXF editing synchronization is enabled:

  • [ ] Reconciliation uses native handle as strong evidence but not sole identity authority.
  • [ ] Fallback matching may use entity kind/layer/geometry/text/structural context.
  • [ ] Ambiguous continuity creates conflict/new entity rather than invented identity.
  • [ ] Concurrent semantic change participates in normal three-way reconciliation.
  • [ ] Opaque preserved records absent from semantic parse are not automatically deleted.

If safe reconciliation is not ready:

  • [ ] Keep external DXF synchronization read-only while semantic operations/materialization remain editable.
  • [ ] Document the exact gap and do not fake completion.

docs.title: 12. Phase H — Validation
docs.text:
Validation must at minimum:

reopen staged DXF
verify drawing parses
verify target entity/layer/geometry/text
verify required unsupported preserved records when advertised
  • [ ] Validation binds to exact candidate/output digest.
  • [ ] Parse failure blocks materialization success.
  • [ ] Geometry diagnostics map to semantic entity where possible.
  • [ ] Unsupported content preservation failure is a structured validation error.
  • [ ] Validation does not mutate live project files.

docs.title: 13. Phase I — Shared Application/Protocol/Agent Exposure
docs.text:
Expose public views such as:

DrawingSummary
LayerSummary
CadEntitySummary
CadGeometrySummary
CadOperationResult

Requirements:

  • [ ] Embedded app supports inspect/list/find/query for drawing/layers/entities.
  • [ ] Remote protocol/client returns equivalent semantic data.
  • [ ] Agent tools expose CAD semantic operations progressively from selected drawing/entity.
  • [ ] Raw DXF record mutation is not normal agent capability.
  • [ ] Candidate handles/fidelity diagnostics are shared.
  • [ ] Task 160 can build presentation without parser-native types.

docs.title: 14. Golden Test and Verification
docs.text:
Golden test:

import drawing.dxf
resolve PARCELS layer
resolve target entity
perform semantic edit
validate
apply/materialize
reopen output
verify target change
verify unrelated entity
verify fidelity/preserved unsupported content expectation
  • [ ] Uses fresh copied fixture.
  • [ ] No AutoCAD/network required.
  • [ ] Checked-in fixture remains untouched.
  • [ ] History/provenance records CAD operation.

Focused commands:

cargo test -p scriberig-domain-cad
cargo test -p scriberig-app cad
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol cad
cargo test -p scriberig-client cad

Final gates:

  • [ ] python3 tools/lint_repo.py --fix
  • [ ] cargo fmt --all
  • [ ] cargo check --workspace --all-targets
  • [ ] cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
  • [ ] focused tests pass after final formatting;
  • [ ] file-size/documentation rules pass;
  • [ ] third-party notices are correct.

docs.title: 15. Completion Gate
docs.text:
Do not mark complete until:

  • [ ] CAD schema is format-independent;
  • [ ] DXF imports supported entities as semantic knowledge;
  • [ ] native handles remain external evidence, not EntityId;
  • [ ] at least one existing entity and one geometry/structural operation use candidate flow;
  • [ ] staged DXF reopens after validation/materialization;
  • [ ] unrelated/opaque content is preserved or editability is explicitly restricted;
  • [ ] shared app/protocol/agent semantics exist;
  • [ ] task 158 can attach DWG provider behavior without changing CAD semantic identity model;
  • [ ] every checked item has current verification evidence.

docs.title: Implement Optional DWG Provider Boundary and Licensing-Safe CAD Capability
Status
docs.text:
Planned.

All completion items remain unchecked until implemented and verified.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Add native DWG capability without coupling the reusable CAD semantic domain to one mandatory proprietary, copyleft-incompatible, native, or platform-specific implementation.

This task must establish a provider boundary that can support:

DWG inspect/read
optional DWG semantic import
optional DWG write/materialization
provider-specific validation
explicit fidelity/capability diagnostics

The CAD schema from task 157 remains canonical. A DWG provider maps to that schema; it does not create a second CAD model.

This task depends on tasks 154 and 157.

docs.title: 2. Required Reading and Audit
docs.text:
Before editing:

  • [ ] Read root AGENTS.md, design/AGENTS.md, design/CONTEXT.md.
  • [ ] Read Level-1 documents 007, 014, 025.
  • [ ] Read Level-2 documents 014 and 035.
  • [ ] Read tasks 154 and 157 implementations/tests.
  • [ ] Inspect current extension/provider/optional dependency conventions in the repository.
  • [ ] Inspect licensing files, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, package metadata, and any current native/system dependency handling.
  • [ ] Research the exact license/deployment terms of every DWG implementation considered before adding it.
  • [ ] Record the chosen provider strategy and rejected alternatives in this task file or adjacent design note before implementation.

Do not rely on vague statements such as “open source” or “commercial SDK”. Verify the exact dependency and distribution implications for the chosen integration.

docs.title: 3. Checklist Discipline
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this task open during implementation.
  • [ ] Tick each item only after focused verification.
  • [ ] Reopen invalidated items.
  • [ ] Do not bulk-tick.
  • [ ] Keep provider-specific work isolated from unrelated CAD functionality.

docs.title: 4. Architectural Prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not:

  • change scriberig-domain-cad semantic identity/types to match a provider's native object model;
  • make DWG support mandatory for using CAD/DXF support;
  • add a provider dependency with incompatible licensing to the reusable platform without explicit licensing approval reflected in repository metadata/design;
  • expose native provider pointers/handles through protocol or persistent semantic records;
  • store provider credentials/license keys as semantic project/session content;
  • silently downgrade a DWG write to DXF conversion unless the user explicitly requests/export policy permits it;
  • report write capability when provider only supports reading;
  • bypass Scriberig candidate/change/materialization semantics because a vendor SDK has its own save API.

docs.title: 5. Phase A — Define Provider-Neutral CAD Format Adapter Capability
docs.text:
Reuse existing domain adapter architecture where possible. Add only the minimum CAD-specific provider contract needed for native formats.

Conceptual contract:

CadExternalProvider
  provider_id/version
  supported_formats
  open/import capabilities
  render/export capabilities
  validation capabilities
  preservation/fidelity descriptors
  deployment requirements

Requirements:

  • [ ] Provider identity/version is explicit and safe for provenance.
  • [ ] Provider capability distinguishes read/write/validation separately.
  • [ ] Provider reports supported native object classes/features when relevant.
  • [ ] Provider fidelity maps to shared artifact fidelity from task 154.
  • [ ] Provider-native objects are converted to/from CAD semantic types at adapter boundary.
  • [ ] Absence of provider is a normal discoverable state.
  • [ ] Provider errors are structured and do not expose secret license material.
  • [ ] DXF adapter from task 157 remains usable with no DWG provider installed.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] fake read-only provider reports inspect capability but no write;
  • [ ] fake read/write provider advertises write only for supported feature set;
  • [ ] absent provider returns explicit unavailable capability;
  • [ ] provider A/B cannot leak native handles into semantic public model.

docs.title: 6. Phase B — Choose Integration Strategy
docs.text:
Pick one of these implementation forms based on licensing/deployment evidence:

optional in-process library
optional dynamically loaded/native bridge
out-of-process adapter service/tool
user-supplied provider plugin

Requirements:

  • [ ] Document why chosen strategy preserves the repository's platform/product licensing boundary.
  • [ ] Make native/system dependency optional at build/runtime when it cannot be assumed on all systems.
  • [ ] Provide a deterministic fake provider for CI.
  • [ ] Do not require proprietary SDK/license in ordinary workspace tests.
  • [ ] Update license/notice/package docs for any shipped dependency/bridge code.

If no acceptable real DWG provider can be shipped under current project constraints:

  • [ ] Implement the provider boundary and fake/conformance provider only.
  • [ ] Expose real DWG as provider required/unavailable rather than weakening licensing rules.
  • [ ] Leave real-provider-specific checkboxes unchecked and document the blocker.

docs.title: 7. Phase C — DWG Import/Inspect Mapping
docs.text:
When a real provider is available, implement import for the subset that maps safely to task-157 CAD semantics.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Exact DWG source evidence/digest is retained.
  • [ ] Drawing/layers/blocks/supported entities map to existing CAD schema.
  • [ ] Native object handles/IDs remain external identifiers/provenance.
  • [ ] Unsupported native object classes are represented as preserved opaque/provider-owned evidence or cause read/write fidelity downgrade.
  • [ ] Provider version is recorded in import provenance.
  • [ ] Re-import through a different provider does not silently redefine semantic entity identity without reconciliation.
  • [ ] Inspect/list/find use shared CAD application operations.

Focused tests may use fake provider records if redistribution of native DWG fixtures is problematic; if a legal deterministic DWG fixture is included, document its provenance.

docs.title: 8. Phase D — Optional DWG Write/Materialization
docs.text:
Only implement if chosen provider supplies safe write capability.

Requirements:

  • [ ] DWG output is generated from exact candidate CAD semantic state plus required preserved provider evidence.
  • [ ] Provider save/export occurs in candidate staging, not directly against live project file.
  • [ ] Shared expected-baseline verification runs before replacement.
  • [ ] Provider-reported unsupported semantic operation blocks output rather than dropping data.
  • [ ] Resulting DWG is reopened/validated through provider before live replacement.
  • [ ] Materialization records provider/version and exact new digest.
  • [ ] Failure leaves canonical/project external state recoverable under task-154 materialization rules.

If write is unavailable:

  • [ ] Capability is read-only/provider-inspect.
  • [ ] Explicit DXF export may be offered as a separate operation, never as hidden DWG overwrite.

docs.title: 9. Phase E — Application/Protocol/Configuration
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • [ ] Shared capability view identifies DWG provider availability/version/fidelity.
  • [ ] Product configuration selects/enables provider through existing configuration/plugin boundaries.
  • [ ] Protocol contains provider-neutral capability/result DTOs only.
  • [ ] Remote server may have DWG provider even when client machine does not.
  • [ ] Client/TUI/web do not need native provider libraries to inspect remote semantic CAD state.
  • [ ] Agent tools receive CAD semantic operations, not vendor SDK calls.
  • [ ] Provider credentials/license paths/keys are not serialized into session/project semantic state.

docs.title: 10. Phase F — Validation and Failure Modes
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  • [ ] provider unavailable;
  • [ ] provider load/init failure;
  • [ ] read-only provider;
  • [ ] unsupported entity class;
  • [ ] stale external DWG baseline;
  • [ ] provider write failure before staged output complete;
  • [ ] provider reopen validation failure;
  • [ ] optional provider absent while DXF tests continue to pass.

Every failure must be structured and must not corrupt canonical state or live external artifact.

docs.title: 11. Verification
docs.text:
Focused checks depend on final module/package placement. At minimum run:

cargo test -p scriberig-domain-cad dwg
cargo test -p scriberig-app cad_provider
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol cad_provider
cargo test -p scriberig-client cad_provider

Final gates:

  • [ ] python3 tools/lint_repo.py --fix
  • [ ] cargo fmt --all
  • [ ] cargo check --workspace --all-targets succeeds without optional proprietary provider installed;
  • [ ] cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings succeeds without optional provider;
  • [ ] optional-provider-specific build/test instructions are documented if applicable;
  • [ ] third-party/licensing notices are correct;
  • [ ] no secret/provider license material is present in repository fixtures/logs/tests.

docs.title: 12. Completion Gate
docs.text:
Do not mark complete until:

  • [ ] CAD semantic schema remains provider-neutral;
  • [ ] provider capability boundary is tested with deterministic fake provider;
  • [ ] absence of DWG provider is safe and explicit;
  • [ ] DXF remains independently usable;
  • [ ] licensing/deployment implications of chosen real provider are documented and compliant;
  • [ ] real DWG read/write items are checked only if actually implemented and verified;
  • [ ] no provider-native identity became canonical Scriberig identity;
  • [ ] no provider save path bypasses candidate/validation/materialization semantics;
  • [ ] every checked item has current verification evidence.

docs.title: Implement Geospatial Datasets, Spatial Query, and QGIS Project Integration
Status
docs.text:
Planned.

All completion items remain unchecked until implemented and verified.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Implement geospatial dataset semantics, bounded spatial/attribute query, editable vector-layer operations, and a distinct QGIS project domain that references those datasets rather than absorbing them.

Minimum scenario:

onboard QGIS project + parcels.gpkg
inspect QGIS project
resolve referenced parcels layer
find parcel_id=124
inspect feature
change area attribute or geometry semantically
create candidate
validate
review/apply
materialize dataset
reopen dataset
refresh QGIS project view/reference without rewriting unrelated project configuration

This task depends on task 154. It may use optional system/native geospatial libraries, but universal/public semantic contracts must remain provider-neutral.

docs.title: 2. Required Reading and Audit
docs.text:
Before editing:

  • [ ] Read root AGENTS.md, design/AGENTS.md, and design/CONTEXT.md.
  • [ ] Read Level-1 documents 002, 005, 006, 007, 010, 013, 014, 019, 025.
  • [ ] Read Level-2 document 035.
  • [ ] Read task 154 implementation/tests.
  • [ ] Read crates/domains/AGENTS.md and nearest AGENTS.md for every modified crate.
  • [ ] Inspect current query AST/extension mechanism before adding spatial query forms.
  • [ ] Inspect current project external-reference/path semantics.
  • [ ] Inspect current optional/native dependency conventions before adding GDAL or equivalent provider.
  • [ ] Inspect third-party licensing/notices for GDAL/bindings or any chosen geospatial library.
  • [ ] Record material deviations from this plan directly in this file.

docs.title: 3. Checklist Discipline
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this task document open during implementation.
  • [ ] Tick each checkbox immediately after focused verification.
  • [ ] Reopen invalidated items.
  • [ ] Do not bulk-tick.
  • [ ] Use focused tests until section 16.

docs.title: 4. Architectural Prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not:

  • make QGIS project XML the canonical GIS dataset model;
  • copy every feature from referenced datasets into the QGIS project entity;
  • make GDAL/QGIS/native library types public protocol/domain types;
  • make provider feature IDs equal Scriberig EntityId;
  • use screen/map pixel coordinates as canonical geometry;
  • serialize an entire large layer into one inspect/list response;
  • mutate GeoPackage SQLite tables directly from agent/UI code as the normal semantic write path;
  • treat Shapefile component files as unrelated independent artifacts when the adapter understands them as one dataset;
  • require a remote network service for acceptance tests;
  • bypass candidate/validation/materialization because a geospatial library has an update API.

docs.title: 5. Phase A — Create Geospatial Domain Crate
docs.text:
Add:

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-geo/

Minimum semantic concepts:

GeoDataset
GeoLayer
Feature
Geometry
Field
CoordinateReferenceSystem

Optional/derived concepts may include:

SpatialIndex
LayerExtent
GeometryValidity
RasterResource

Requirements:

  • [ ] Dataset and Layer identities are stable semantic identities.
  • [ ] Feature identity is Scriberig-owned and separate from provider/native feature ID.
  • [ ] Native feature ID is stored as external reconciliation/provenance evidence when useful.
  • [ ] Field/schema definitions are semantic and revisioned.
  • [ ] CRS identity/definition is explicit and not a display-only string.
  • [ ] Geometry has deterministic canonical representation sufficient for exact revision identity.
  • [ ] Coordinate dimensionality and CRS context are explicit.
  • [ ] Layer ordering/schema/ownership are modeled deliberately.
  • [ ] Spatial indexes are derived/rebuildable unless source format requires otherwise.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] construct dataset/layer with two features;
  • [ ] change one feature attribute without revising unrelated feature;
  • [ ] change geometry creates new exact feature revision;
  • [ ] native feature ID remains external evidence.

docs.title: 6. Phase B — Choose Geospatial Provider Strategy
docs.text:
Prefer a provider capable of GeoPackage/Shapefile read/write and spatial metadata. GDAL-compatible integration is expected when practical, but keep it adapter-private.

  • [ ] Evaluate selected Rust/system geospatial dependency.
  • [ ] Document required system libraries and CI strategy.
  • [ ] Verify licenses/notices.
  • [ ] Keep provider/native types behind adapter modules.
  • [ ] Provide deterministic behavior/tests when optional system provider is unavailable, or make CI install explicit and repository-supported.
  • [ ] Do not force unrelated Scriberig crates to depend on GDAL/native libraries.

docs.title: 7. Phase C — Create Deterministic GIS Fixtures
docs.text:
Create under tests/fixtures/rich-project/gis/:

parcels.gpkg
project.qgs or project.qgz
optional shapefile set for compound artifact test

GeoPackage anchors:

layer: parcels
fields: parcel_id, area, name
feature: parcel_id=124
known geometry
feature: parcel_id=125 (unrelated preservation check)
CRS: deterministic known CRS

QGIS anchors:

layer reference name: Parcels
reference to parcels.gpkg layer parcels
one group/layout/style/config element to preserve
  • [ ] Provide fixture generator/source description.
  • [ ] Do not require network data.
  • [ ] Document expected CRS/extent/feature anchors.
  • [ ] Original fixtures successfully open in chosen provider/parser before edit logic.

If Shapefile fixture is included:

  • [ ] Include required .shp/.shx/.dbf and CRS sidecar when applicable.
  • [ ] Prove task-154 grouping treats it as one logical artifact.

docs.title: 8. Phase D — Implement GeoPackage Import
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • [ ] .gpkg classifies to geospatial adapter instead of generic binary/database fallback.
  • [ ] Exact outer source digest/evidence is retained.
  • [ ] Dataset lists logical layers without loading all features.
  • [ ] parcels layer imports schema, CRS, extent/count summary.
  • [ ] Feature rows are addressable through scalable collection mechanics.
  • [ ] Native feature IDs are retained as evidence when stable/useful.
