  • [ ] Geometry/attributes map to semantic Feature revisions.
  • [ ] Unsupported tables/extensions are preserved or write fidelity is downgraded.
  • [ ] Provider/version is recorded in import provenance.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] inspect dataset summary;
  • [ ] list layer parcels;
  • [ ] inspect schema/CRS/count without serializing all features;
  • [ ] find parcel_id=124;
  • [ ] source digest/fidelity is correct.

docs.title: 9. Phase E — Implement Shapefile Compound Import/Materialization Coverage
docs.text:
This phase verifies the shared compound-artifact model with a real format.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Scanner groups matching .shp/.shx/.dbf and optional .prj into one logical dataset artifact.
  • [ ] Missing mandatory sidecar produces structured diagnostic/capability downgrade.
  • [ ] Dataset/layer semantics match the same geo domain used for GeoPackage.
  • [ ] Materialization stages all mandatory sidecar files as one artifact operation.
  • [ ] Injected failure after one member replacement is not reported as success.
  • [ ] Recovery/receipt behavior follows task 154.

If provider cannot safely write Shapefile in the first implementation:

  • [ ] Implement read/grouping conformance and explicitly expose read-only fidelity.
  • [ ] Do not fake multi-file write support.

docs.title: 10. Phase F — Add Spatial and Attribute Query Extensions
docs.text:
Implement geospatial query forms using shared query extension mechanics.

Minimum queries:

attribute equality/predicate
bbox intersection
geometry intersection or within (if provider supports robustly)
nearest with explicit max results/distance policy
layer extent

Requirements:

  • [ ] Every query is snapshot-bound.
  • [ ] Results are paged/bounded.
  • [ ] Results return semantic Feature handles plus requested summaries.
  • [ ] Query execution may use derived/provider indexes without making those indexes canonical identity.
  • [ ] CRS of query geometry is explicit; transform/reject mismatched CRS deterministically.
  • [ ] No hidden use of UI map CRS as semantic query CRS.
  • [ ] Query provenance/diagnostics identify transformation/provider where relevant.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] find parcel_id=124 by attribute;
  • [ ] bbox returns known bounded feature set;
  • [ ] wrong/unknown CRS returns structured error or explicit transform path;
  • [ ] page size prevents full-layer serialization.

docs.title: 11. Phase G — Implement Geo Semantic Operations
docs.text:
Required first operations:

geo.set_attribute
geo.replace_geometry

Add geo.insert_feature and geo.delete_feature when safe within task scope.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Operation resolves exact layer/feature/base snapshot.
  • [ ] Candidate semantic state is created without live dataset mutation.
  • [ ] Attribute operation validates field type/nullability/domain constraints available from schema.
  • [ ] Geometry operation validates geometry kind/dimensionality and CRS assumptions.
  • [ ] Changed set identifies target feature/schema relation only as needed.
  • [ ] Unrelated feature parcel_id=125 remains unchanged.
  • [ ] Provenance records semantic operation.
  • [ ] Stale-base change follows shared conflict semantics.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] set area for parcel_id=124 in candidate;
  • [ ] replace geometry in candidate;
  • [ ] invalid field/geometry rejected;
  • [ ] live GeoPackage unchanged before apply.

docs.title: 12. Phase H — GeoPackage Materialization and Validation
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • [ ] Candidate dataset renders/writes to staged GeoPackage through domain adapter.
  • [ ] Do not update live SQLite file directly during candidate creation/validation.
  • [ ] Expected external baseline is checked before replacement.
  • [ ] Output preserves schema/CRS/unrelated feature.
  • [ ] Unsupported extensions required for fidelity are preserved or write is blocked.
  • [ ] Reopen staged output before live replacement.
  • [ ] Validation checks target feature attribute/geometry and layer metadata.
  • [ ] Successful materialization records new digest/baseline/provider version.
  • [ ] Failed validation leaves live dataset unchanged.

docs.title: 13. Phase I — Create QGIS Project Domain
docs.text:
Add:

crates/domains/scriberig-domain-qgis/

Minimum concepts:

QgisProject
LayerGroup
LayerReference
ProjectCrs
RendererConfiguration
LabelingConfiguration
Join
Relation
Layout
MapItem
ProjectSetting

Requirements:

  • [ ] .qgs import supported at least for deterministic fixture.
  • [ ] .qgz package import supported at least for inspection if included.
  • [ ] Exact project source evidence retained.
  • [ ] Layer tree/group/order imported semantically.
  • [ ] LayerReference stores external/project-relative data-source reference explicitly.
  • [ ] Reference resolution can link Parcels to imported GeoLayer without copying feature contents.
  • [ ] Unresolved/remote references remain explicit unresolved external references with diagnostics.
  • [ ] Renderer/labeling/layout structures are imported semantically where supported or preserved opaque.
  • [ ] QGIS plugin/unknown project content is preserved or project write capability downgraded.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] inspect project/layer tree;
  • [ ] resolve Parcels reference to GeoLayer;
  • [ ] removing GeoPackage from project produces unresolved reference diagnostic rather than deleting project layer entity.

docs.title: 14. Phase J — QGIS Semantic Operations and Materialization
docs.text:
Implement a small safe subset such as:

qgis.reorder_layer
qgis.rename_layer_reference
qgis.update_project_setting

Requirements:

  • [ ] Operations modify QGIS project semantic candidate only.
  • [ ] Editing referenced GeoLayer remains a geo-domain operation, not QGIS XML mutation.
  • [ ] Project materialization preserves unrelated configuration/opaque content or restricts writes.
  • [ ] .qgz uses task-154 compound/container output handling.
  • [ ] Reopen validation verifies project parses and layer reference remains resolvable.

The golden feature-edit scenario may leave QGIS project bytes unchanged when only GeoPackage feature data changes.

docs.title: 15. Phase K — Shared Application, Protocol, Client, and Agent Exposure
docs.text:
Expose stable public views/operations:

GeoDatasetSummary
GeoLayerSummary
FeatureSummary
GeometrySummary
CrsSummary
SpatialQueryResult
QgisProjectSummary
QgisLayerReferenceSummary
GeoOperationResult

Requirements:

  • [ ] Embedded app and remote client return equivalent layer/feature/query semantics.
  • [ ] Protocol does not expose GDAL/QGIS-native structs.
  • [ ] Geometry transfer is bounded/typed and suitable for web client use.
  • [ ] Agent capability discovery exposes geo.* only in relevant selection/scope.
  • [ ] QGIS selection exposes reference/navigation tools to linked GeoLayer.
  • [ ] Candidate/change handles returned from writes.
  • [ ] Fidelity/provider/unresolved-reference diagnostics are shared.

Task 160 owns map/editor presentation.

docs.title: 16. Golden Tests and Verification
docs.text:
Primary golden test:

import project + parcels.gpkg
resolve QGIS Parcels LayerReference -> GeoLayer parcels
query parcel_id=124
set area attribute to deterministic new value
validate candidate
apply/materialize parcels.gpkg
reopen
verify parcel 124 changed
verify parcel 125 unchanged
verify CRS/schema unchanged
verify QGIS project reference still resolves
  • [ ] Fresh copied fixtures only.
  • [ ] No network/QGIS desktop required.
  • [ ] Checked-in fixtures untouched.
  • [ ] History/provenance records geo operation.

Focused commands, adapting names/provider features:

cargo test -p scriberig-domain-geo
cargo test -p scriberig-domain-qgis
cargo test -p scriberig-project shapefile
cargo test -p scriberig-app geo
cargo test -p scriberig-protocol geo
cargo test -p scriberig-client geo

Final gates:

  • [ ] python3 tools/lint_repo.py --fix
  • [ ] cargo fmt --all
  • [ ] cargo check --workspace --all-targets
  • [ ] cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
  • [ ] focused tests pass after formatting;
  • [ ] optional/native provider build expectations documented;
  • [ ] file-size/documentation rules pass;
  • [ ] third-party notices are correct.

docs.title: 17. Completion Gate
docs.text:
Do not mark complete until:

  • [ ] GeoDataset/GeoLayer/Feature/Geometry/CRS semantics exist independently of QGIS;
  • [ ] large feature collections are bounded/paged;
  • [ ] attribute and spatial query return snapshot-bound semantic handles;
  • [ ] parcel feature can be changed through candidate flow;
  • [ ] staged GeoPackage reopens after validation/materialization;
  • [ ] QGIS project domain references GeoLayer rather than copying it;
  • [ ] Shapefile grouping/materialization behavior is real or explicitly read-only;
  • [ ] provider/native types do not leak through public contracts;
  • [ ] local/remote/agent semantics agree;
  • [ ] every checked item has current verification evidence.

docs.title: Implement Reusable Rich-Artifact Web and RPI-TUI Semantic Surfaces
Status
docs.text:
Planned.

All completion items remain unchecked until implemented and verified.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Expose the spreadsheet, document, CAD, geospatial, QGIS, and generic artifact capabilities implemented by tasks 154–159 through reusable web packages and the current RPI-based TUI without duplicating domain semantics in product code.

The surfaces must support:

semantic navigation
bounded rich projections
semantic selection
shared semantic operations
candidate review
fidelity/diagnostic inspection
history/diff/materialization status

The web editor should provide the richer interactive grid/document/canvas/map experiences. The TUI must provide useful semantic navigation and operation/review workflows, but is not required to recreate Excel, Word, AutoCAD, or QGIS in a terminal.

This task depends on tasks 154–159 to the extent each domain is implemented. It is constrained by the active RPI adoption work, especially Level-2 032.

docs.title: 2. Required Reading and Audit
docs.text:
Before editing:

  • [ ] Read root AGENTS.md, design/AGENTS.md, and design/CONTEXT.md.
  • [ ] Read Level-1 documents 010, 011, 012, 015, 019, 024, 025.
  • [ ] Read Level-2 documents 011, 012, 017, 021, 022, 024, 032, 034, 035.
  • [ ] Read current completion state of RPI migration tasks 138–149 and projection-style tasks 151–153.
  • [ ] Read implementations/public contracts from tasks 154–159.
  • [ ] Read nearest AGENTS.md in all modified web/TUI/app directories.
  • [ ] Inspect current reusable web package boundaries and existing semantic selection model.
  • [ ] Inspect current TUI semantic explorer/selection/operation/review views after RPI migration state.
  • [ ] Inspect remote-client mapping before adding product-local DTOs.
  • [ ] Record material deviations from this plan directly in this file.

Do not restore superseded local Ratatui/TUI infrastructure because older code/tasks still exist.

docs.title: 3. Checklist Discipline
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this task open during implementation.
  • [ ] Tick each item immediately after focused verification.
  • [ ] Reopen invalidated items.
  • [ ] Do not bulk-tick.
  • [ ] Run focused package/crate tests until section 14.

docs.title: 4. Architectural Prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not:

  • parse XLSX/DOCX/DXF/QGIS/GeoPackage directly in TypeScript/React or TUI code to recover semantics already available through application APIs;
  • implement a web-only or TUI-only mutation path;
  • make grid row, DOM node, canvas object ID, map feature layer index, or terminal row canonical identity;
  • duplicate domain operation semantics in reducers/components;
  • put huge layer/workbook contents into one client model snapshot;
  • make personal UI projection style rewrite shared materialized artifacts;
  • equate RPI-TUI theme/style with Scriberig document/source/domain projection style;
  • require the TUI to support direct graphical manipulation before the semantic workflow is usable;
  • bypass shared candidate/change review because a rich editor can locally modify a visual model.

docs.title: 5. Phase A — Extend Shared Client/Model Selection for Rich Anchors
docs.text:
Build on existing semantic selection contracts.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Selection always carries semantic handle plus exact snapshot/revision context where applicable.
  • [ ] Spreadsheet selection can represent cell/range anchors without using UI grid row objects as identity.
  • [ ] Document selection can identify paragraph/table cell semantics independent of DOM nodes.
  • [ ] CAD selection can carry entity plus projection-space bounds/anchor as presentation metadata.
  • [ ] Map selection can carry feature plus CRS-aware geometry/bounds anchor as presentation metadata.
  • [ ] QGIS layer selection can resolve to QGIS LayerReference and linked GeoLayer separately.
  • [ ] Switching projection/view does not silently change the selected semantic entity.
  • [ ] Remote and embedded clients normalize equivalent selections the same way.

Focused tests:

  • [ ] serialize/normalize spreadsheet cell selection;
  • [ ] serialize/normalize feature selection with CRS anchor;
  • [ ] view-local anchor changes do not mutate semantic selection identity;
  • [ ] stale snapshot selection refresh preserves EntityId when still present or clears meaningfully when absent.

docs.title: 6. Phase B — Generic Artifact Inspector
docs.text:
Implement reusable artifact inspection UI before domain-specific editors.

Required data shown through shared APIs:

artifact kind
source evidence digest/summary
physical/logical members
adapter/schema/provider version
fidelity/editability
opaque-preservation status
external references
current synchronization/materialization baseline/status
diagnostics

Web:

  • [ ] Add reusable headless/model component for artifact inspection.
  • [ ] Add neutral reusable visual component.
  • [ ] Integrate into reference web app without app-private data access.

TUI:

  • [ ] Add an artifact details view/panel/command using current RPI components.
  • [ ] Page member lists rather than rendering unbounded output.
  • [ ] Surface fidelity/read-only reason prominently before edit commands.

Cross-surface:

  • [ ] Embedded/remote modes show equivalent core artifact facts.
  • [ ] No surface derives fidelity from extension alone.

docs.title: 7. Phase C — Spreadsheet Web Grid and TUI Range View
Web
docs.text:
Implement a reusable spreadsheet grid/controller.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Grid requests bounded ranges/pages from shared client APIs.
  • [ ] Scrolling/viewport changes fetch only required ranges with bounded prefetch.
  • [ ] Cell selection resolves to semantic Cell handle.
  • [ ] Formula/value inspector shows semantic value and formula distinctly.
  • [ ] Edit commit invokes spreadsheet.set_cell_value or spreadsheet.set_formula shared operation.
  • [ ] Dirty local editor state is distinguishable from candidate/canonical state.
  • [ ] Candidate result opens existing shared review workflow.
  • [ ] Read-only/fidelity state disables edit affordances with diagnostic reason.
  • [ ] Changing personal display settings does not materialize the XLSX.

docs.title: TUI
docs.text:
Provide a bounded range/table projection.

  • [ ] User can choose worksheet and range/page.
  • [ ] Cells are rendered in bounded table/text form using RPI-TUI primitives.
  • [ ] Selected cell semantic details/formula are inspectable.
  • [ ] User can invoke shared set-value/set-formula operation through command/prompt flow.
  • [ ] No custom full spreadsheet widget is required if bounded range interaction is usable.

Tests:

  • [ ] web scrolling does not request entire worksheet;
  • [ ] cell edit creates candidate, not immediate materialization;
  • [ ] TUI and web target same semantic cell in fixture.

docs.title: 8. Phase D — Rich Document Web Editor and TUI Document View
Web
docs.text:
Implement reusable document outline/content controller.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Section/paragraph/table structure comes from semantic client model.
  • [ ] Paragraph selection resolves to Paragraph EntityId.
  • [ ] Table cell selection resolves to TableCell EntityId.
  • [ ] Paragraph/table edits call shared document operations.
  • [ ] Inline rendering does not expose DOCX XML/package structure as editing model.
  • [ ] Unsupported/read-only structures are visually marked and preserved.
  • [ ] Candidate review remains shared change review.
  • [ ] Page-like preview, if provided, is a projection and not semantic identity.

docs.title: TUI
docs.text:
• [ ] Outline lists sections/paragraph summaries/tables progressively.
  • [ ] Paragraph/table cell details are inspectable.
  • [ ] Replace paragraph/update table cell operation can be invoked through shared command path.
  • [ ] TUI does not need pixel-perfect Word pagination.

Tests:

  • [ ] selecting paragraph survives view rerender;
  • [ ] DOM recreation does not change semantic target;
  • [ ] web/TUI create equivalent candidate for same paragraph fixture edit.

docs.title: 9. Phase E — CAD Web Canvas/Explorer and TUI Entity View
Web
docs.text:
Implement a bounded vector drawing projection sufficient for supported fixture entities.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Layer explorer loads semantic layer summaries.
  • [ ] Canvas projection uses domain-provided geometry/projection data.
  • [ ] Clicking supported entity resolves to CAD semantic entity handle.
  • [ ] Pan/zoom/view matrix remains presentation state only.
  • [ ] Entity property edits invoke shared cad.* operations.
  • [ ] Geometry edit affordances are enabled only for supported semantic operations/fidelity.
  • [ ] Unsupported entities may render as placeholders/bounds if adapter provides them, without pretending editability.
  • [ ] Candidate changes appear in shared review/diff flow.

docs.title: TUI
docs.text:
• [ ] Layer list and paged entity list are usable.
  • [ ] Entity kind/layer/geometry/text properties are inspectable.
  • [ ] User can invoke safe CAD operation through shared command flow.
  • [ ] Optional textual/vector preview does not become a separate CAD model.

Tests:

  • [ ] canvas selection resolves exact entity;
  • [ ] pan/zoom does not alter semantic state;
  • [ ] web/TUI operation targets same fixture entity.

docs.title: 10. Phase F — Map/Layer/Feature Web View and TUI Geo View
Web
docs.text:
Implement reusable map/layer controller using domain-provided feature/geometry queries.

Requirements:

  • [ ] View requests features by spatial window/bbox with explicit CRS and paging.
  • [ ] Map does not fetch entire large layer by default.
  • [ ] Layer list distinguishes QGIS LayerReference from resolved GeoLayer.
  • [ ] Feature click resolves semantic Feature handle.
  • [ ] Attribute inspector uses semantic schema/values.
  • [ ] Attribute/geometry edits invoke shared geo.* operations.
  • [ ] QGIS renderer/labeling configuration may influence projection when supported but remains project semantics separate from feature data.
  • [ ] Map screen coordinates convert through explicit projection/CRS logic before semantic geometry operations.
  • [ ] Read-only remote/provider layers disable edit operations with shared diagnostics.

docs.title: TUI
docs.text:
• [ ] Project/layer tree is navigable.
  • [ ] GeoLayer summary shows CRS/schema/count/extent.
  • [ ] User can run attribute/spatial query with bounded results.
  • [ ] Feature attributes/geometry summary are inspectable.
  • [ ] User can invoke geo.set_attribute and other supported operations via shared command path.
  • [ ] Full graphical map is not required for completion.

Tests:

  • [ ] viewport query includes explicit CRS/bounds;
  • [ ] changing map zoom does not mutate semantic state;
  • [ ] web/TUI resolve parcel_id=124 to same Feature handle;
  • [ ] remote read-only layer behavior matches embedded behavior.

docs.title: 11. Phase G — Candidate Review for Rich Domains
docs.text:
Extend existing review components rather than creating per-domain approval systems.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Spreadsheet diff shows target cell/range value/formula changes semantically.
  • [ ] Document diff shows paragraph/table cell changes semantically.
  • [ ] CAD diff shows entity property/geometry/layer changes semantically.
  • [ ] Geo diff shows feature attribute/geometry changes semantically.
  • [ ] QGIS diff shows layer/order/project configuration changes semantically.
  • [ ] Raw/projected artifact bytes may be inspectable as secondary evidence but are not the only diff.
  • [ ] Validation status/evidence is visible.
  • [ ] Apply uses existing expected-base promotion path.
  • [ ] Materialization failure/recovery status is visible after promotion attempt.

TUI and web may render these differently but must consume the same semantic review model.

docs.title: 12. Phase H — Agent/Conversation Integration
docs.text:
Rich artifact operations must fit current recursive session/plan architecture.

Requirements:

  • [ ] Selected rich semantic object can be attached to branch context by stable handle.
  • [ ] Agent capability catalog exposes domain operations based on semantic selection/fidelity.
  • [ ] Tool results return compact semantic summaries and handles rather than complete workbook/layer/document payloads.
  • [ ] Child branches receive selected semantic scope, not rich UI state.
  • [ ] Provider/model continuation is unaffected by personal view-only pan/zoom/grid/format changes unless exact projection is deliberately included in model context.
  • [ ] Agent-produced rich artifact edits create normal candidate handles visible to user review.

Do not add domain-specific transcript/session architecture.

docs.title: 13. Phase I — Reusable Package Boundaries
docs.text:
Preserve web dependency direction:

protocol -> client -> model -> editor/react -> reusable components -> web app
  • [ ] Protocol package contains transport DTOs only.
  • [ ] Client package owns transport normalization.
  • [ ] Model/editor packages own semantic selection/query/edit orchestration.
  • [ ] Reusable components accept models/controllers rather than direct server internals.
  • [ ] Integrated web app composes reusable packages only.
  • [ ] No public package depends on web/apps/.
  • [ ] TUI consumes shared app/client semantics rather than TypeScript/web packages.

docs.title: 14. Verification
docs.text:
Focused web commands as appropriate:

pnpm --dir web test -- <rich-artifact filters>
pnpm --dir web typecheck

Focused Rust/TUI commands:

cargo test -p scriberig-tui rich_artifact
cargo test -p scriberig-client rich_artifact
cargo test -p scriberig-app rich_artifact

Use actual repository-supported focused commands; do not run all final gates after every small edit.

Final gates after implementation items complete:

  • [ ] python3 tools/lint_repo.py --fix
  • [ ] cargo fmt --all
  • [ ] cargo check --workspace --all-targets
  • [ ] cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
  • [ ] pnpm --dir web format
  • [ ] pnpm --dir web typecheck
  • [ ] relevant web tests pass;
  • [ ] relevant TUI tests pass;
  • [ ] file-size/documentation rules pass.

docs.title: 15. Completion Gate
docs.text:
Do not mark complete until:

  • [ ] generic artifact fidelity/source/member view is available in web and TUI;
  • [ ] spreadsheet range/cell navigation and semantic edit path works across web/TUI;
  • [ ] document paragraph/table navigation and semantic edit path works across web/TUI;
  • [ ] CAD layer/entity navigation and semantic operation path works across web/TUI;
  • [ ] QGIS/Geo layer/feature navigation and semantic operation path works across web/TUI;
  • [ ] large collection views are bounded/paged;
  • [ ] no UI coordinate/index became canonical identity;
  • [ ] all writes create shared candidates and use shared review/apply;
  • [ ] RPI-TUI ownership boundary is preserved;
  • [ ] embedded and remote core semantics are equivalent;
  • [ ] every checked item has current verification evidence.

docs.title: Verify Mixed Rich-Project Conformance, Recovery, and Product Gates
Status
docs.text:
Planned.

All completion items remain unchecked until implemented and verified.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Finish the rich-artifact work as one coherent product capability rather than a set of isolated parser demos.

This task verifies that one mixed project containing source code plus spreadsheet, rich document, CAD, QGIS project, and GIS datasets can be onboarded and edited through the same Scriberig semantic/change/session/product architecture.

It depends on tasks 154–160. If task 158 has no real DWG provider because of licensing/deployment constraints, the conformance suite must verify the provider-unavailable/read-only behavior rather than pretending native DWG support exists.

docs.title: 2. Required Reading and Audit
docs.text:
Before editing:

  • [ ] Read root AGENTS.md, design/AGENTS.md, and design/CONTEXT.md.
  • [ ] Read Level-1 documents 001, 005, 006, 007, 010, 011, 013, 019, 024, 025.
  • [ ] Read Level-2 documents 012, 025, 027, 032, 034, 035.
  • [ ] Read every task 154–160 and inspect actual checked/unchecked state.
  • [ ] Do not infer completion of a dependency from code presence; verify its task checklist and tests.
  • [ ] Read nearest AGENTS.md for tests/conformance/apps/web directories modified.
  • [ ] Inspect existing real-process Rust project and PHP self-hosting E2E harnesses before creating another parallel harness.
  • [ ] Record any dependency task that remains partial and adjust only the relevant gate; do not falsely mark it complete here.

docs.title: 3. Checklist Discipline
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep this task open throughout integration.
  • [ ] Tick each item immediately after its exact integration test/gate passes.
  • [ ] Reopen items when later fixes invalidate them.
  • [ ] Never bulk-tick.
  • [ ] Preserve failure evidence when a gate exposes a real product gap.

docs.title: 4. Architectural Prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not:

  • special-case the golden fixtures with test-only production paths;
  • bypass project scan/import by constructing semantic entities directly in the product E2E test;
  • edit fixture files directly to simulate semantic operations;
  • accept a parser-unit test as proof of application/protocol/product completion;
  • flatten rich artifacts into binary fallback just to make onboarding pass;
  • skip validation/review/promotion/materialization in golden edits;
  • make web/TUI tests use private application internals unavailable to remote clients;
  • require external network/model/provider services for deterministic acceptance;
  • make test ordering hide persistent-state/restart defects.

docs.title: 5. Phase A — Assemble Canonical Mixed Project Fixture
docs.text:
Create/finish:

tests/fixtures/rich-project/
  README.md
  source/ or small existing source/config files as useful
  workbook.xlsx
  report.docx
  drawing.dxf
  gis/
    project.qgs or project.qgz
    parcels.gpkg
    optional Shapefile members

Requirements:

  • [ ] Fixture README documents every semantic anchor expected by tests.
  • [ ] Binary fixtures have reproducible generators or documented deterministic provenance.
  • [ ] Fixture contains no network dependencies.
  • [ ] Fixture contains no secrets or proprietary copyrighted sample data that cannot be redistributed.
  • [ ] Every E2E run copies fixture to fresh temporary directory.
  • [ ] Checked-in fixture is never mutated.
  • [ ] Git initialization is performed on the copied project if required by onboarding policy.

Expected anchors include at least:

XLSX: Budget!B3 formula
DOCX: paragraph "Existing site area"
DXF: layer PARCELS and one target entity
QGIS: Parcels layer reference
GPKG: layer parcels, parcel_id=124 and parcel_id=125

docs.title: 6. Phase B — Mixed Project Scan and Import Conformance
docs.text:
Start from an empty Scriberig database/application state.

  • [ ] project.scan discovers every authored fixture member according to normal selection policy.
  • [ ] XLSX is classified to spreadsheet/XLSX adapter.
  • [ ] DOCX is classified to document/DOCX adapter.
  • [ ] DXF is classified to CAD/DXF adapter.
  • [ ] GeoPackage is classified to geo adapter.
  • [ ] QGS/QGZ is classified to QGIS adapter.
  • [ ] Shapefile members, when present, group into one logical artifact.
  • [ ] Unrecognized binary remains binary fallback without blocking project import.
  • [ ] Persisted scan manifest contains exact path/digest/classification evidence.
  • [ ] Import uses that exact manifest and creates one project workspace/current snapshot.
  • [ ] Product does not require restart/manual EntityId copying after import.
  • [ ] Semantic navigation reaches each artifact from the active project.

Add conformance assertions that the same project/snapshot/root identity is used by application, protocol, web, and TUI views.

docs.title: 7. Phase C — Universal Operation Conformance Across Domains
docs.text:
For each rich domain, prove the universal grammar works where applicable:

inspect
list
find
query
render
history
diff
  • [ ] Workbook inspect/list/find returns stable semantic handles.
  • [ ] Document inspect/list/find returns paragraph/table handles.
  • [ ] CAD inspect/list/find returns layer/entity handles.
  • [ ] Geo inspect/list/query returns layer/feature handles.
  • [ ] QGIS inspect/list/follow resolves layer reference to GeoLayer.
  • [ ] Results identify exact snapshot/revision context.
  • [ ] Large/bounded collections use paging/ranges and do not serialize complete artifact contents.
  • [ ] History after edits remains semantic, not merely file timestamp history.

docs.title: 8. Phase D — XLSX Golden Edit
docs.text:
Execute only through shared semantic operations:

Budget!B3
=A3*2 -> =A3*3
  • [ ] Agent/application operation targets exact Cell semantic handle.
  • [ ] Candidate created; live workbook unchanged.
  • [ ] Semantic diff identifies formula/cell change.
  • [ ] XLSX validator reopens staged candidate.
  • [ ] Apply uses expected base snapshot.
  • [ ] Materialization produces reopenable XLSX.
  • [ ] Notes!A1 or equivalent unrelated anchor remains unchanged.
  • [ ] Exact new artifact digest/baseline recorded.
  • [ ] History/provenance identifies spreadsheet operation.

docs.title: 9. Phase E — DOCX Golden Edit
docs.text:
Execute:

"Existing site area" -> "Proposed site area"
  • [ ] Operation targets exact Paragraph handle.
  • [ ] Candidate leaves live DOCX untouched.
  • [ ] Semantic diff identifies paragraph change.
  • [ ] Validation reopens staged DOCX.
  • [ ] Apply/materialize succeeds through shared path.
  • [ ] Unrelated paragraph/table/header/style/package preservation anchor remains unchanged.
  • [ ] Exact new digest/baseline recorded.
  • [ ] History/provenance identifies document operation.

docs.title: 10. Phase F — CAD Golden Edit
docs.text:
Execute one supported deterministic edit defined by task 157, for example text/layer/geometry change.

  • [ ] Operation targets exact CAD entity handle.
  • [ ] Candidate leaves live DXF untouched.
  • [ ] Semantic diff identifies entity/property/layer/geometry change.
  • [ ] Validation reopens staged DXF.
  • [ ] Apply/materialize succeeds.
  • [ ] Unrelated entity remains unchanged.
  • [ ] Native handle behavior matches documented adapter rule.
  • [ ] Opaque/unsupported preservation rule is verified.
  • [ ] History/provenance identifies CAD operation.

DWG conformance:

  • [ ] When real provider exists, run provider-specific supported golden read/write gate.
  • [ ] When real provider does not exist, verify explicit provider-unavailable/read-only capability and ensure unrelated CAD/DXF workflow remains unaffected.

Only check the applicable DWG item; leave impossible/unimplemented provider-specific item unchecked and document why.

docs.title: 11. Phase G — QGIS/Geo Golden Edit
docs.text:
Execute:

QGIS Parcels LayerReference
  -> GeoLayer parcels
  -> Feature parcel_id=124
  -> geo.set_attribute(area, deterministic new value)
  • [ ] QGIS reference resolves to GeoLayer through explicit relation/reference.
  • [ ] Feature found by bounded attribute query.
  • [ ] Candidate leaves live GeoPackage untouched.
  • [ ] Semantic diff identifies feature attribute change.
  • [ ] Validation reopens staged GeoPackage and verifies schema/CRS/feature.
  • [ ] Apply/materialize succeeds.
  • [ ] parcel_id=125 remains unchanged.
  • [ ] QGIS project bytes remain unchanged when only dataset changed, unless explicit project operation requires otherwise.
  • [ ] QGIS LayerReference still resolves after dataset refresh.
  • [ ] History/provenance identifies geo operation.

If Shapefile write is supported:

  • [ ] Run one multi-member materialization success test.
  • [ ] Run one injected partial-failure/recovery test.

If Shapefile is read-only:

  • [ ] Verify explicit read-only fidelity and grouping instead of write tests.

docs.title: 12. Phase H — Cross-Domain References and Isolation
docs.text:
Add at least one cross-domain reference in fixture or test setup using normal semantic operations where available, for example:

Document paragraph -> references Spreadsheet range
or
Project decision/session branch -> touches GeoFeature
  • [ ] Reference uses universal graph relation, not copied content.
  • [ ] Editing referenced spreadsheet/feature does not rewrite referencing document/session entity unless relation semantics require it.
  • [ ] Derived summaries depending on changed target invalidate through declared dependencies only.
  • [ ] Unrelated artifact revisions remain stable.
  • [ ] Global snapshot advances while local unchanged revisions remain reusable.

docs.title: 13. Phase I — Large Collection and Performance Conformance
docs.text:
Create/generated larger deterministic test data without making repository fixtures enormous.

Spreadsheet:

  • [ ] Workbook with at least tens of thousands of logical populated cells can report sheets/used ranges without returning all cells.
  • [ ] Small range request returns bounded DTO size.
  • [ ] Editing one cell does not reconstruct protocol payload for entire sheet.

Geo:

  • [ ] Layer with at least tens of thousands of features can report count/extent/schema without returning all features.
  • [ ] Bounded bbox/attribute query returns bounded page.
  • [ ] Editing one feature produces local semantic changed set.

Agent/context:

  • [ ] Compiled model context for one cell/feature does not include entire workbook/layer.
  • [ ] Branch result returns compact handles/summaries.

Record performance assertions in deterministic structural terms where wall-clock timing would be flaky.

docs.title: 14. Phase J — Fidelity and Preservation Negative Tests
docs.text:
For each domain, add a fixture/condition that cannot be safely edited with current adapter.

  • [ ] XLSX unsupported/nonpreservable feature downgrades write capability.
  • [ ] DOCX unsupported/nonpreservable feature downgrades write capability.
  • [ ] CAD unsupported/nonpreservable object downgrades write capability.
  • [ ] Geo/provider read-only layer disables edits.
  • [ ] QGIS unresolved/unsupported project extension reports diagnostics.
  • [ ] UI and agent tool catalog honor those restrictions.
  • [ ] Raw fallback remains inspectable where policy permits but cannot silently promote unsafe writes.

docs.title: 15. Phase K — Concurrent Change and Reconciliation Tests
docs.text:
Use exact baselines and shared change semantics.

  • [ ] Candidate based on stale workbook snapshot is rejected/rebased/conflicted correctly.
  • [ ] Concurrent DOCX paragraph semantic change does not get overwritten by stale materialization.
  • [ ] Concurrent external DXF modification is detected by baseline digest.
  • [ ] Concurrent GeoPackage modification is detected before replacement.
  • [ ] Loss-aware/opaque-preserved content is not interpreted as deletion merely because projection/parser omitted it.
  • [ ] Conflict records contain enough semantic/artifact evidence for review.
  • [ ] Recovery does not advance canonical state twice.

docs.title: 16. Phase L — Local/Remote/Web/TUI Conformance
docs.text:
For representative read and write operation in each implemented domain:

  • [ ] Embedded application result is canonical reference behavior.
  • [ ] Remote server/client result normalizes to equivalent semantic view.
  • [ ] Web uses remote/public client path without private server shortcuts.
  • [ ] TUI local mode uses shared application semantics.
  • [ ] TUI remote mode uses client/protocol semantics.
  • [ ] Agent tool dispatch uses same application operation owner.
  • [ ] Candidate identity/change result agrees across surfaces.
  • [ ] Fidelity/read-only diagnostics agree across surfaces.
  • [ ] Presentation-only changes do not mutate semantic/project/session state.

Do not require identical visual rendering; require semantic contract equivalence.

docs.title: 17. Phase M — Restart and Durability
docs.text:
After successful imports/edits:

  • [ ] Restart server/application and reopen project.
  • [ ] Current project snapshot/root remains correct.
  • [ ] Artifact source evidence/manifests remain resolvable.
  • [ ] Workbook/document/CAD/geo semantic handles that should remain stable still resolve.
  • [ ] History/migrations remain inspectable.
  • [ ] Projection/materialization baseline/recovery receipts remain durable as designed.
  • [ ] QGIS external layer reference resolution reconstructs correctly.
  • [ ] Session/branch results referencing rich entities remain inspectable without provider continuation.

docs.title: 18. Phase N — Failure and Recovery Product Tests
docs.text:
Inject failures at meaningful boundaries:

  • [ ] XLSX validation failure before live replacement.
  • [ ] DOCX staged package corruption.
  • [ ] DXF staged reopen failure.
  • [ ] GeoPackage staged provider error.
  • [ ] Shapefile multi-member partial replacement when write supported.
  • [ ] server/client disconnect during operation observation.
  • [ ] process restart with recoverable materialization receipt when supported.

For every case prove:

  • [ ] canonical state is not silently corrupted;
  • [ ] live artifact is either unchanged or recovery state is explicit;
  • [ ] operation/result status is durable and inspectable;
  • [ ] retry/recovery behavior is deterministic;
  • [ ] no success is reported prematurely.

docs.title: 19. Phase O — Documentation and Capability Matrix
docs.text:
Update shared capability/conformance documentation.

  • [ ] Add spreadsheet/XLSX support matrix.
  • [ ] Add rich-document/DOCX support matrix.
  • [ ] Add CAD/DXF and optional DWG provider matrix.
  • [ ] Add GeoPackage/Shapefile/QGIS support matrix.
  • [ ] For each, distinguish inspect/import/query/edit/reconcile/validate/materialize capability.
  • [ ] Document known fidelity limitations.
  • [ ] Document optional native/system dependencies.
  • [ ] Document that unsupported formats fall back to binary/raw evidence rather than semantic edits.
  • [ ] Document rich-domain agent examples using semantic operations rather than raw writes.

docs.title: 20. Focused Verification During Integration
docs.text:
Use focused tests first, including actual package names from tasks 154–160:

cargo test -p scriberig-conformance rich_project
cargo test -p scriberig-app rich_project
cargo test -p scriberig-project rich_project
cargo test -p scriberig-tui rich_project
pnpm --dir web test -- rich-project

Also run domain-specific golden tests when fixing integration defects.

Every defect found during this task must gain a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after it, following repository rules.

docs.title: 21. Final Repository Gate
docs.text:
Only after all applicable implementation/conformance checkboxes are complete:

  • [ ] python3 tools/lint_repo.py --fix
  • [ ] cargo fmt --all
  • [ ] cargo test --workspace
  • [ ] cargo check --workspace --all-targets
  • [ ] cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
  • [ ] pnpm --dir web format
  • [ ] pnpm --dir web typecheck
  • [ ] pnpm --dir web test
  • [ ] pnpm --dir web build if this is part of the repository's current final gate;
  • [ ] real-process/native TUI E2E rich-project scenario passes;
  • [ ] browser/web E2E rich-project scenario passes where current harness supports it;
  • [ ] all optional-provider absence tests pass on baseline CI environment;
  • [ ] repository license/notice checks pass;
  • [ ] no source file violates repository size/documentation rules.

Do not suppress warnings or skip failing gates merely to complete the checklist.

docs.title: 22. Completion Gate
docs.text:
Do not mark this task complete until all applicable statements are proven:

  • [ ] one mixed project onboards all supported rich artifacts through normal scan/import;
  • [ ] XLSX semantic edit validates/applies/materializes/reopens;
  • [ ] DOCX semantic edit validates/applies/materializes/reopens;
  • [ ] DXF semantic edit validates/applies/materializes/reopens;
  • [ ] GeoPackage feature semantic edit validates/applies/materializes/reopens;
  • [ ] QGIS project resolves referenced GeoLayer separately from project composition;
  • [ ] Shapefile grouping and write/recovery behavior is proven or explicitly read-only;
  • [ ] DWG provider behavior is truthful and licensing-safe whether available or unavailable;
  • [ ] large collections remain bounded/paged;
  • [ ] opaque/unsupported content is preserved or editability is restricted;
  • [ ] concurrent/external changes use exact baseline/conflict semantics;
  • [ ] web/TUI/local/remote/agent use shared application semantics;
  • [ ] restart preserves canonical semantic/history/materialization state;
  • [ ] failure/recovery paths never silently report partial success;
  • [ ] final repository gates pass;
  • [ ] every checked item above has current verification evidence.
